# 1761 Pochaiv Menaion — Vol. 4: December (Pochaiv Lavra, 1761) <a id="1761-pochaiv-menaion-vol-4-december-pochaiv-lavra-1761"></a>

[Title Page with typographical ornament border printed in cinnabar and black ink]

THE BOOK OF THE MENAION
Month of December

To the glory of the Holy, Consubstantial, Life-Creating, and Undivided Trinity: of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit; under the reign of the Great King Augustus the Third;[^1] by the blessing of His Grace, Lord Sylvester Lubieniecki-Rudnytskyi,[^2] Exarch of the Metropolitanate of Kyiv, Halych, and all Rus', Bishop of Lutsk and Ostroh; by the volition of the Most Reverend Lord Father Hieromonk Hypatius Bilynskyi,[^3] Protoarchimandrite of the Order of Saint Basil the Great; through the zeal and at the expense of the monks of the same Order; in the Holy Wonderworking Lavra of Pochaiv, printed with types: Published. In the year from the Creation of the world according to the Greek chronographs 7269,[^4] and of the Nativity of Christ 1761.

*(Vacat — Blank page)* [Fol. 1r]

# MONTH OF DECEMBER

[Woodcut headpiece depicting the Nativity of Christ]

*Having 31 days.*

*December 1: Holy Prophet Nahum:*

*Alleluia, or Troparion: Stichera, Tone 3.*[^5]
*Tone 3, Podoben: "Great is the power of Thy Cross, O Lord" (Ве́лїя крⷭ҇та́ твоегѡ̀):*

The grace of the Holy Spirit dwelt in thee, O prophet of God, and by His ray made thee a most radiant lamp; and through thee He proclaims things to come unto Nineveh the great.

A light-bearing cloud wast thou revealed to be, O Nahum, prophet of God, pouring forth the shower of the knowledge of God; and thou didst give to drink the potion of the divine judgment[^6] unto the city of Nineveh, which had forthwith fallen sick with impiety.

Having become a partaker of incorruptible blessing, O Nahum, prophet of God, and of ineffable glory, unutterable joy, and divine sweetness: pray unto the Master of all on our behalf, O God-inspired one.

*Other Stichera to the Theotokos, same Tone and Podoben (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже).*
*(If Alleluia is sung, the Stichera to the Theotokos are sung first, then those of the Saint.)*

Wounded am I by the weapon of the serpent, and scarcely alive, O Maiden; lying upon the bed of despair, heal me swiftly by the medicine of thy maternal prayer, and make me a servant of Thy Son and God.

Knowing my bodily weakness and the affliction of my soul, and the malice of my heart: vouchsafe me divine visitation, O all-immaculate Virgin; and save me, I pray thee, by thy fervent prayer.

I have surpassed all men in sins, O gracious Lady; yet having cleansed the multitude of these, O pure Virgin Mother, vouchsafe me on account of thy maternal supplication to obtain forgiveness at the future judgment of Thy Son and God.

[Fol. 1v]
...supplicating Him.

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

Entreat Him Who was born of thee to preserve thy flock unharmed from every temptation of the adversary devil; and strengthen us, O Maiden, to fulfill all the will of Thy Son.

*Stavrotheotokion:*

A sword pierced thy heart, O all-pure one, when thou didst behold Thy Son upon the Cross, and thou didst cry out: Show me not childless, O my Son and my God, Who didst preserve me a virgin after childbirth.

*At the Aposticha, the Octoechos.*

*Troparion, Tone 2:*

Celebrating the memory of Thy prophet Nahum, O Lord, therefore we pray Thee: Save our souls.

*At Matins, the Canon: A composition of Theophanes.[^7] Tone 5.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

The horse and his rider into the Red Sea, He Who crushes warfare with a high arm, Christ shook out; but Israel He saved as they sang a song of victory.

Having been anointed with the Holy Spirit of God, O God-receiver, and enlightened by His grace: honoring therefore the divine foresight of thy mind, we call thee blessed, O most excellent one.

The grace of the Spirit having resounded from on high upon thy soul, O prophet, worthily inspired the prophetic operation, and fashioned thy God-inspired tongue, O worthy of all wonder.

Thou wast revealed as an instrument struck by the plectrum of the Spirit, chanting of God the Jealous One, and proclaiming unto all the impartiality of the divine judgment, O much-lauded one.

*Theotokion:*

O most blessed and all-pure Virgin, save from tribulations those who with faith and love sing of thee as the honorable Mother of God, loosening untamed savagery.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

Thou Who didst establish the earth upon nothing by Thy command, and didst suspend what gravitates without restraint: establish Thy Church upon the immovable rock of Thy commandments, O Christ, Who alone art good and the Lover of mankind.

By participation in the Life-Creating and Divine Spirit, thou wast most God-like in soul; therefore by divine beckoning thou wast prepared to foretell distant things openly unto all, O God-inspired one.

Thou didst foresee the judgment of vengeance upon the enemies, O blessed and most God-seeing one, when the impious despised the forbearance and mercy of God [Fol. 2r]
...and His loving-kindness, on account of their incurable malice.

*Theotokion:*

He Who of old fashioned all things out of nothingness passes forth from thy holy womb, having become man, O pure Virgin, through His exceedingly great love for mankind, the Lover of mankind, that He might deliver mankind.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 5, Podoben: "The Word co-unoriginate" (Собезнача́лное сло́во):*

Having acquired a mind unmingled with earthly figures, O glorious one, thou didst become a most pure receptacle of the Divine Spirit, O Nahum, receiving His radiance brightly and shining forth unto all; therefore we pray thee: Intercede for the peace of the world.

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

Beseech God and Lord Who was incarnate from thee for the sake of us who have perished through transgressions, O pure one, fervently to show mercy upon us, and to turn away His wrath and anger from those who with faith honor and unceasingly praise His power and dominion.

*Stavrotheotokion:*

Beholding Thee, O Christ, hanging voluntarily upon the Cross in the midst of thieves, Thy Mother, maternal sorrow tearing at her heart, cried: O sinless Son, how art Thou unjustly nailed to the Cross like an evildoer, desiring to quicken the human race as the Compassionate One?

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

Perceiving Thy divine emptying clairvoyantly, O Christ, Habakkuk cried out to Thee with trembling: For the salvation of Thy people, to save Thine anointed art Thou come.[^8]

Illumined by the dawn of the Spirit, thou didst foretell unto the Ninevites the threat of the decree, revealing the inescapable power of God, O God-manifested one.

Thou dost proclaim the righteous judgment of the Creator, dire total ruin unto the hostile people, as thou didst utter in prophecies, O Nahum, prophet of God, all-blessed one.

Adorned with humility of mind, the soul of Thy prophet was supernaturally lifted up unto the vision of Thee, O Good One, and unto the brightness of the divine contemplation.

*Theotokion:*

O Mother and Sovereign Lady of creation, having given birth to the King of all, only all-immaculate one: show me free from the tyranny of passions through thy prayers.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

Thou Who deckest Thyself with light as with a garment, unto Thee I rise early and unto Thee I cry: Enlighten my darkened soul, O Christ, as the only Compassionate One.

To acquire a blameless and pure life through the operation and illumination [Fol. 2v]
...by the illumination of the Holy Spirit thou wast vouchsafed, O marvelous prophet.

Thou didst subject the flesh unto the sovereign mind, eagerly placing ascents in thy heart; therefore thou didst receive divine manifestation.

Honored above visible things are they who have been honored with prophecy; for through them speaks the Holy Spirit, the All-Good.

*Theotokion:*

Not even a heavenly intellect can truly worthily hymn thee, O Mother of God; for thou didst bear the Creator, Who is hymned by the heavenly powers.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

Raging with a soul-corrupting tempest, O Master Christ: calm the sea of passions, and lead me up from corruption, as Thou art compassionate.

She who was revealed as the temple of divine grace, O ye faithful, and became a most pure receptacle beyond understanding: let us hymn her divine manifestation.

Having received the unsetting beam of the Divine Spirit and acquired a divine mind, he instructs the pious unto hymnody.

*Theotokion:*

The spiritual powers and all generations of men glorify thee as the Mother of God, O blessed, all-immaculate one.

*Kontakion, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared today" (Яви́лся є҆сѝ):*

Enlightened by the Spirit, thy pure heart became a receptacle of most radiant prophecy; for thou seest things far off as though they were present. Therefore we honor thee, O blessed and glorious prophet Nahum.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

The supremely exalted Lord of the fathers quenched the flame and bedewed the children, as with one accord they sang: Blessed art Thou, O God.

Having the most God-beholding prophet as the leader of our choirs, we celebrate honorably in divine manner, singing: Blessed art Thou, O God.

Knowing thee as a Spirit-moved instrument and a God-inspired pipe, we call upon thee as our defender, singing in hymns: Blessed art Thou, O God.

The Lord crowned thee, O marvelous prophet, and gave thee grace to foretell things to come; unto Whom we all sing: Blessed art Thou, O God.

*Theotokion:*

The prophet beheld thee, O all-pure Virgin, as the impassable gate through which He alone passed; unto Whom we all sing: Blessed art Thou, O God.

[Fol. 3r]
*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

Unto Thee, the Creator of all, the children in the furnace, weaving a universal choir, sang: All ye works of the Lord, hymn the Lord and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.

Deified by the immaterial beam of the Triune Principle, O prophet, thou singest rejoicing: All ye works of the Lord, hymn the Lord and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.

In sacred manner honoring thy sacred memory, O marvelous prophet, we sing: All ye works of the Lord, hymn the Lord and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.

*Theotokion:*

Strengthen my soul, O pure one, weakened by transgressions and passions, that I may hymn thy childbirth, O Virgin, most glorified unto all ages.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

Rejoice, O Isaiah: The Virgin had in womb, and bare a Son, Emmanuel, God and man, the Dayspring is His name; Whom we magnify, and call the Virgin blessed.

On earth thou truly hadst an angel-like life, and now in the heavens with the angelic choirs thou hast taken up dwelling near the Thrice-Radiant Light; filled with Whom, look down upon those who sing of thee.

Thee we bring unto God as an intercessor for peace, O blessed one; pray fervently, O prophet, as having boldness, to give unto the faithful beautifully abiding eternal deliverance.

*Theotokion:*

As having given birth to God, twofold and consubstantial, we the faithful name thee with God-inspired words the all-pure Theotokos by a most true calling, heralding thy honorable childbirth, O all-holy Bride of God.

*Exapostilarion of the day.*
*At the Aposticha, the Octoechos.*

*December 2: Holy Prophet Habakkuk:*

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Prophet, Tone 4.*[^9]
*Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant among martyrs" (Я́кѡ до́бля):*

The marvelous Habakkuk, having received the beam of the Spirit, became wholly divine; and beholding the impiety of judges and unrighteous judgment, he is indignant, showing forth the uprightness of Christ and Master, in God-loving manner and with warm intent, as one inflamed with comfort.

Standing upon his divine watch, the venerable Habakkuk [Fol. 3v]
...heard the ineffable mystery of Thy coming unto us, O Christ; and his preaching prophesies most clearly, foreseeing also the most wise Apostles as horses stirring up the sea of multi-tribal nations.

Rejoicing in the Lord, God Thy Savior, O glorious God-proclaimer, making glad; and receiving the beam of the radiance which is there, and spiritually enlightened by divine light: from afflictions and tribulations deliver by Thy prayers those who with faith celebrate Thy most festive memory.

*Other Stichera to the Theotokos, same Tone and Podoben (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже).*
*(If Alleluia is sung, these Stichera are sung first.)*

With showers of the Holy Spirit, O all-pure one, bedew my mind, who didst bear Christ, the boundless drop that washed away the iniquities of earthborn men by His mercies; dry up the fountain of my passions, and vouchsafe me the torrent of delight by thy prayer free from grief.

Cast down unto the earth, I am deadened by sins, by passions of soul and body; therefore am I covered by the darkness of despair; but raise me up now, guiding me unto the incorruptible life, unto the homeland on high, where is the pure voice of those who feast, and where is the light of Thy countenance, O Christ.

Thou who didst contain in thy womb the uncontainable God, Who became man in His love for mankind, and took our mixture from thee, and manifestly deified it: despise me not, O all-pure one, who am now in sorrow, but have compassion swiftly, and free me from every enmity and harm of the evil one.

*Glory... Both now... same Tone and Podoben (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*

Myriad times, O all-pure one, did I promise to make repentance for my sins, but my unseemly evil habit does not leave me. Therefore do I cry unto thee, and fervently pray: Deliver me, O gracious Lady, from such torment, guiding me unto better things and those near unto salvation.

*Stavrotheotokion, same Podoben (Подо́бенъ то́йже):*

When the Ewe-lamb who bare Thee beheld Thee upon the Wood, the Lamb and Shepherd, she wept and cried out to Thee in maternal sorrow: O Son greatly desired, how art Thou suspended upon the wood of the Cross, O Long-Suffering One? How are Thy hands and Thy feet nailed by the lawless, O Word, and Thou hast poured out Thy blood, O Master?

[Fol. 4r]
*Troparion, Tone 2:*

Celebrating the memory of Thy prophet Habakkuk, O Lord, therefore we pray Thee: Save our souls.

*Canon of the Prophet.*
*Whose acrostic is: I sing of thee, O blessed Prophet Habakkuk.[^10] A composition of Theophanes. Tone 4.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

I will open my mouth unto Thee, O Lord my God, for Thou didst lead Thy people out of Egyptian bondage, and didst cover the chariots of Pharaoh and his power.

Make me wise, O Lord my God, to hymn Thine inspired prophet Habakkuk, and by Thy grace, O Good One, enlighten my heart.

How long, O Lord, the prophet cries, shall I cry unto Thee and Thou wilt not hear?[^11] Why hast Thou shown me the impiety of judges?

Unto those who piously celebrate thy honorable memory, O prophet, deliver them from tribulations and cruel circumstances by thy supplications.

*Theotokion:*

The Holy God appeared when the time drew nigh, having become man from thee, O Theotokos, that He might save man.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

The bow of the mighty has become weak, and the powerless have girded themselves with strength; therefore my heart is established in the Lord.

Uplifted by gazing upon God, and enlightened by beams of light from Him, thou didst foresee the prefiguration of things to come, O God-manifested one.

Every virtue didst thou embrace, and every malice from thy mind didst thou hate; and justly didst thou turn away with loathing from the lawless, O all-blessed one.

By the utterance of the Holy Spirit, Thou as one pure wast most clearly entrusted to prophesy the fulfillment of things to come, O worthy of all wonder.

*Theotokion:*

A mountain overshadowed with virtues wast thou revealed to be, O all-honorable one, from which the Master came in the form of a servant, to deliver mankind from bondage.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up upon the Cross" (Вознесы́йся):*

Thou didst stand upon thy divine watch, O blessed one, and didst perceive the divine coming with prophetic eyes, O God-inspired one. Therefore didst thou cry aloud, O Habakkuk, with fear: O Lord, I have heard of Thy fearful coming, and I hymn Thee, Who didst desire to bear earthly flesh from the Virgin.

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

After God, unto thy divine protection do I, the humble one, flee, O Theotokos, and falling down I pray [Fol. 4v]
...unto me: Have mercy, O all-pure one, for my sins have risen above my head; and I fear torments, O Sovereign Lady, and I tremble. Make supplication, O pure one, unto Thy Son, to deliver me from them.

*Stavrotheotokion:*

She who in the latter days gave birth in the flesh unto Thee Who wast begotten of the unoriginate Father, seeing Thee hanging upon the Cross, O Christ, cried out: Woe is me, O most beloved Jesus! How art Thou, Who art glorified as God by angels, now voluntarily crucified by lawless men, O my Son? I hymn Thee, O Long-Suffering One.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

Proclaiming Thine appearance on earth, O Christ God, and Thy coming, the prophet cried out with gladness: Glory to Thy power, O Lord.

Light-like through virtue wast Thou revealed to be, O God-inspired one, and Thou didst herald the unwaning light, unto Whom we now cry with faith: Glory to Thy power, O Lord.

The all-radiant grace of the Spirit, having abundantly taken up dwelling in thee, O all-wise one, perfected thee as a prophet, proclaiming the Savior unto all.

Having received the report of the Almighty, thou didst reverently fear, O marvelous one; and understanding His works, thou wast filled with awe.

*Theotokion:*

The ark of testimony portrays thee, O Virgin, who didst truly receive the Bread of Life, O pure one, the Word co-eternal with the Father.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

Thou Who hast made the light to dawn and enlightened the morning, and shown forth the day: Glory to Thee, glory to Thee, O Jesus, Son of God.

Now the venerable Church sees the Sun lifted up upon the Wood, even as thou didst foretell, O most sacred Habakkuk.

Having winged thy mind, thou didst stand upon thy watch, O most rich one, and didst behold the coming of the Lord.

Loudly didst thou cry, O wise one: I will rejoice and be glad in God my Savior, O all-blessed Habakkuk.

*Theotokion:*

Weighed down by the bonds of my many transgressions, unto thee do I flee: Save me, O Sovereign Lady Theotokos, praise of the faithful.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

Prophet Jonah cried aloud, prefiguring the three-day burial, praying in the sea-monster: Deliver me from corruption, O Jesus, King of hosts.

God came, having become incarnate, even as thou didst foretell, enlightened brightly by Him, O most blessed Habakkuk, and He illuminated the world with light.

Illumine, O God, the souls of those who hymn Thee, by the prayers of Habakkuk [Fol. 5r]
...Habakkuk, the venerable and God-wise, whose mind was enlightened by divine inspiration.

Thy utterance and the power of divine words, O God-proclaimer, went forth into all the ends, prophesying unto us the divine coming of the Word.

*Theotokion:*

O Virgin, thou didst give birth in the end of times unto the Word Who is consubstantial with the Father, and co-understood as without beginning with Him Who begat Him, when He became flesh.

*Kontakion, Tone 8, Podoben: "In the highest" (Въ вы́шнихъ):*[^12]

Having proclaimed unto the universe the divine coming from the south from a Virgin, O God-proclaiming Habakkuk, and by standing upon the divine watch, hearing from the light-bearing angel, thou didst herald unto the world the Resurrection of Christ. Therefore with gladness we cry unto thee: Rejoice, radiant beauty of the prophets!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

The Hebrew children of old in Babylon trampled down the flame of the furnace, crying aloud in hymns: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou.

Having been taught knowledge surpassing speech, O blessed one, and prophesying as a most radiant lamp, thou criest aloud now: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou.

Christ gave thee communion of the Thrice-Radiant illumination and of the unwaning glory, Whom thou didst glorify, crying aloud: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou.

*Theotokion:*

Throughout generations of generations, O Virgin Mother, thou wast revealed to be blessed, having given birth beyond understanding to the incarnate Word. Therefore, O pure one, we hymn thee.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

All ye works of God and all creation, bless the Lord; ye venerable ones and humble in heart, sing of Him and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.

Enlightened by the Thrice-Radiant Light, thou wast vouchsafed, O most excellent one, divine and supernatural visions, crying: Supremely exalting God unto all ages.

Drinking from the torrent of delight and being filled with immaterial vision, and partaking of prophetic glory and presidency, rejoicing thou singest of God unto all ages.

O the divine and honorable beauties of the Prophet Habakkuk! For this one, making choir with the angelic hosts, rejoicing hymns Christ unto all ages.

*Theotokion:*

Truly wast thou revealed as the Mother of Him Who shone forth before all ages from the Father; for thou alone wast the wall [Fol. 5v]
...of all, and thee do we supremely exalt, O pure one, unto all ages.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

Thy childbirth was revealed as incorrupt; God came forth from thy womb, and appeared upon earth as a bearer of flesh, and dwelt among men. Therefore, O Theotokos, we all magnify thee.

Thy memory shines, O prophet, casting forth the radiant beam of thy God-proclamation, and of thy mystical teaching and prophecy, unto those who honor thee, O most blessed Habakkuk.

Having preached the Lord of glory, and foretold His coming from the holy Virgin which manifestly took place, and beholding that which was shown forth, rejoice, O God-blessed Habakkuk.

All the prophets rejoice on thy joyful day, being glad, O God-wise one, partaking of thy joy and of divine glory; with whom pray to save those who hymn thee.

*Theotokion:*

By the sprinkling of thy compassions, O pure one, wash away the defilement of my soul, and grant me to pour forth streams of tears continually, O Maiden, staying the torrents of my passions.

*December 3: Holy Prophet Zephaniah:*[^13]

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Prophet, Tone 4.*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "Being called from on high" (Зва́нный свы́ше):*

Receiving the beam of the most divinely originating radiance by purity of mind, and having become a herald and sign-giver of divine words and a divine prophet, thou wast revealed as the God-moved mouth of the Spirit, proclaiming and declaring unto all nations the things shown unto thee by Him, the salvation given, and the all-honorable Kingdom of Christ: Whom beseech to save and enlighten our souls.

Honored worthily with holy God-vision, O God-inspired one, and with prophetic presidency and grace, and vouchsafed divine blessedness, being held by boldness and compassion toward the Supremely Good One, pray without ceasing for those who with faith [Fol. 6r]
...praise thee, and honor thee as a God-proclaimer, venerable and God-pleasing, to deliver us from tribulations and save our souls.

Thou didst show forth Thy prophet as an animate cloud, O Immortal One, pouring out water truly unto eternal life; having sent him abundantly and granted the All-Holy Spirit, Who is consubstantial with Thee, O Almighty Father, and with Thy Son Who shone forth from Thy essence, through Whom he foretold the saving coming of Christ our God, and proclaimed salvation unto all nations.

*Other Stichera to the Theotokos, same Tone and Podoben (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*
*(If Alleluia is sung, these Stichera are sung first, then those of the saint.)*

From every hostile assault, O all-immaculate Mother of God, save those who piously bow before thy childbirth, as thou art the protectress of our whole race; for thee have we all now acquired as help, refuge, and establishment, and mediatress unto the Master, Christ and Lord; Whom beseech to grant peace unto the world, we pray, and remission of sins unto those who flee into thy shelter.

Behold, I lay bare unto thee the festering sores of my soul, and show forth the cruel wounds which robbers inflicted on me, the thoughts of malice, by demonic agitations, O all-immaculate Sovereign Lady. Having given birth to the Physician of souls and bodies, do thou grant me healing unto these, pouring out the oil of thy mercy and goodness, unto the well-tempered restoration of salvation and health.

I, the wretched one, will not hide my cruel deeds, for I have acquired all things that God hates: I have defiled my flesh and my spirit, and my mind with impure thoughts, and with defiled deeds and words. With my tongue I judge those who sin, while I myself do worse things, O Mother of God. Grant me correction of all these things, that I may rise up from my evil habit, falling down and weeping for the evils I have committed in the walking of my life.

*Glory... Both now... same Tone and Podoben (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*

For into the depth of many sins have I fallen, from my slothfulness and despondency, wretched and ignorant, and I am now held fast by despair. Be unto me a help, cleansing, and salvation, O all-pure one, granting me consolation with good transformation. Thee do I entreat, and unto thee do I cry for mercy, and fall down, and with faith call unto thee: [Fol. 6v]
...lest I appear utterly as a rejoicing unto the deceitful one.

*Stavrotheotokion, same Podoben (Подо́бенъ то́йже):*

Lament Me not, O Mother, seeing Thy Son and God suspended upon the Tree, Who hung the earth unrestrained upon the waters and created all creation; for I will arise and be glorified, and will crush the kingdoms of hades with power, and destroy his might, and deliver those who are bound from his malice, as I am compassionate, and will bring them unto My Father, as the Lover of mankind.

*At the Aposticha, the Octoechos.*
*Troparion, Tone 2:*

Celebrating the memory of Thy prophet Zephaniah, O Lord, therefore we pray Thee: Save our souls.

*At Matins, the Canon.*
*Whose acrostic is: May the glory of Zephaniah elucidate me.[^14] A composition of Theophanes. Tone 6.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

Traversing the deep on foot as through dry land, Israel, beholding the pursuer Pharaoh drowned, cried aloud: Let us sing unto God a song of victory!

We pray thee, O prophet, as thou standest before the throne of God, pray fervently to grant enlightenment unto us, who sing with faith of thy honorable memory.

Thou wast revealed as a divine instrument, containing the illuminations and gifts of the Divine Spirit, O all-wise Zephaniah. Therefore rejoicing, we the faithful call thee blessed.

*Theotokion:*

The Sun that shone forth from thy holy womb enlightens all the earth with most radiant beams, O Sovereign Lady; enlightened by which, we honor thee as the Mother of God.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

There is none holy as Thou, O Lord my God, Who hast exalted the horn of Thy faithful, O Good One, and established us upon the rock of Thy confession.

Beholding as God the knowledge of things to come and of those that are to be, He clearly reveals and shows forth understanding unto thee in God-befitting manner, O blessed and marvelous one.

Having made thy mind bold, O blessed one, with goodly daring, thou didst join thyself unto the Divine Spirit, and didst become receptive of the divine inspirations dwelling there.

*Theotokion:*

Behold, all generations bless thee in faith, who didst give birth supernaturally in time in the flesh unto the timeless Word, and remained a Virgin again.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 6, Podoben: "The doors of compassion" (Милосе́рдїя две́ри):* [Fol. 7r]
...Having cleansed thy mind from defilements, O all-wise one, thou didst make it a divine mirror, receptive of the beam of the Divine Spirit. And now rejoicing, thou hast departed unto the source of illuminations, O Prophet Zephaniah.

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

The groaning of my heart and from my inward parts do I bring unto thee, O all-immaculate one, asking thy well-abiding protection: Have mercy on my all-passionate soul. Entreat the Most Merciful God to deliver me from judgment and from the lake of fire, O thou who alone art blessed.

*Stavrotheotokion:*

Seeing Thee, O Christ, suspended upon the Cross for our sake, the Ever-Virgin Maiden who bare Thee was wounded in her heart and soul with the sword of sorrow, and wept, lamenting as a mother: By her prayers have mercy on us, O merciful Lord.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

Christ is my power, God and Lord, the venerable Church sings in God-befitting manner, crying out from a pure mind, feasting in the Lord.

The Lord, the Light, appeared unto us according to thy prophecy, O blessed one, calling all unto His knowledge, and delivered us from bondage.

Illumined by grace, thou didst proclaim, speaking unto those who have bowed their necks under the one yoke to labor, who follow the faith and serve the Lord.

*Theotokion:*

O all-venerable Mother, destroy the turmoil of passions of my mind and the tempest of calamities, having given birth to the Wellspring of dispassion, O Virgin Mother.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

With Thy divine light, O Good One, illumine with love the souls of those who rise early unto Thee, I pray, to know Thee, O Word of God, the true God, Who callest us out of the darkness of sin.

From unrighteousness unto virtue, and from captivity of the passions, turn me, O blessed one, by thy supplications, O glorious prophet, and guide me unto the light of the deeds of piety.

Having enlightened thy soul with the fair adornments of virtues, thou didst show it well-pleasing unto the illuminations of the Divine Spirit, by Whom thou wast also enriched with the grace of prophecy.

*Theotokion:*

The prophetic sayings, O all-pure one, proclaim thy childbirth in many figures; the fulfillment of which we now behold, and herald thee truly as the Theotokos.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

Beholding the sea of life surging with the tempest of temptations, fleeing unto Thy calm haven [Fol. 7v]
...fleeing unto Thy calm haven, I cry unto Thee: Lead up my life from corruption, O Most Merciful One.

Receiving the beam of the Spirit, O glorious one, by appearing as a mirror of prophecy of the divine radiance, thou didst shine forth upon the world, prophesying things to come as though present.

Thy King is come; rejoice, O Zion, and be glad beholding Him, and He illuminated the world with the radiants of His Divinity, and put to shame the demonic deceit.

*Theotokion:*

The Only-Begotten of the Father was united with mortal flesh in thy womb, and came forth as one from two without corruption, preserving thine immaculate virginity unharmed, O all-immaculate one.

*Kontakion, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared" (Ꙗ҆ви́лсѧ є҆сѝ):*

Thou wast revealed as light-radiant by the Divine Spirit, O Prophet Zephaniah, having proclaimed the manifestation of God: Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion of Jerusalem; preach: Behold, thy King comes saving![^15]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

The angel made the furnace bedewed for the venerable children, but the command of God burning the Chaldeans persuaded the tyrant to cry out: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.

Thy memory, O prophet, shone forth upon the world like the sun, illuminating it with the grace of thy prophecy, unto those who sing in concord with faith: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.

A most fertile cloud wast thou revealed to be; thou didst cause the shower of divine knowledge to dawn upon us from the saving springs, O blessed one, by which we are enlightened to cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.

*Theotokion:*

The Word, Who of old gave being unto all things by divine will, wishing to recall man, O pure one, took up dwelling in thy womb, O blessed one, who didst give birth unto God in the flesh.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

Out of the flame Thou didst pour forth dew for the venerable ones, and didst consume the sacrifice of the righteous one with water; for Thou doest all things, O Christ, merely by willing them: Thee do we supremely exalt unto all ages.

Surrendered wholly unto the Almighty, thou wast mystically instructed in the manners of providence, wisely instructing the nations. Therefore we hymn thee, O God-proclaiming prophet.

Bring prayerful hymnody unto God for those who hymn thee, O God-blessed one, and destroy the turmoil of temptations [Fol. 8r]
...destroy the turmoil of temptations, that we may hymn thee, O God-proclaiming prophet.

*Theotokion:*

Having given birth unto God and Lord, the Giver of life, O all-pure one, thou didst stay the unrestrained destruction of death, having put it to death. Therefore we hymn thee unto all ages.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

It is impossible for men to see God, upon Whom the ranks of angels dare not gaze; but through thee, O all-pure one, the incarnate Word was revealed unto men: Whom magnifying, with the heavenly hosts we call thee blessed.

Thou hast settled in the land of the meek, where after thy end thou beholdest the angelic brightness, O all-wise Zephaniah, prophet of God, having been meek, shining with grace. Therefore rejoicing, we the faithful call thee blessed.

Beholding brightly the fulfillment that has come of thy prophecies, O most glorious one, we marvel at the grace given unto thee, and we are in awe of the purity of thy mind and of thy God-beholding soul.

*Theotokion:*

For none other like unto thee was ever granted from ancient generations, O all-immaculate Mother of God; for thou alone of all didst possess holiness and purity incomparably. Therefore didst thou receive God incarnate within thee.

*Exapostilarion of the day.*

*December 4: Holy Great-Martyr Barbara and our Venerable Father John of Damascus:*[^16]

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Saint, Tone 2.*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*

When the all-blessed Juliana beheld the glorious martyr Barbara being scraped with wounds upon the fearful tribunal, and all her body being cut with diverse torments, she cried out with warm tears: O Word of God, Lover of mankind, vouchsafe me now to be a partaker of her suffering!

Truly possessing one disposition unto piety, holy Barbara and Juliana strove against the enemy, and having conquered him mightily, they were vouchsafed glory from Christ God. Therefore, having destroyed the harm of destructive passions, they grant healing unto all the faithful.

[Fol. 8v]
When sweet death was pronounced upon thee, O most honorable martyr Barbara, rejoicing and hastening thou didst finish thy course; and by the most lawless hands of an impious parent thou wast sacrificed, and didst offer thyself as a fruit unto God. Therefore, truly rejoicing with the wise virgins, thou beholdest the illumination of Christ thy Bridegroom.

*Other Stichera of the Venerable One, Tone 8.*
*Tone 8, Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (Ѽ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*

O most marvelous wonder! O all-wise Father John, thou didst elucidate the Church of Christ with hymns, sweetly singing the most divine songs, O all-glorious one. By the operation of the Spirit, striking thy lute, resembling diverse Davids, sounding thereon, thou didst draw all by divine hymns.

O glorious Father John, having departed from worldly turbulent noise, thou didst hasten unto the tranquility of Christ, O venerable one; and with divine visions and deeds, manifestly with all-rich splendors, thou wast truly enriched, and didst impart them unto the faithful, shining with a God-befitting life, O most blessed one.

Come, ye earthborn, let us piously hymn today the sacred and honorable festivity of Venerable John with songs; for this one was truly vouchsafed to receive the light of divine illumination. O Thine ineffable compassion, O Lord, through which we have come to know how to glorify Thee, the Supremely Good One!

*Glory, Tone 6:*

Having left homeland, family, and honorable estate, O Barbara, and hated thine impious father, thou didst love God, unto Whom thou wast betrothed, and wast named a Great-Martyr: Him beseech to save our souls.

*Both now, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having risen on the third day" (Трїдне́венъ):*

Seeing the most lawless people unjustly nailing Thee upon the Tree, O Savior, the Virgin and Thine immaculate Mother, even as Simeon foretold, was wounded in her maternal heart.

*At the Aposticha, the Octoechos.*
*Glory to the Saint, Tone 6:*

O venerable father, into all the earth went forth the proclamation of thy corrections; therefore hast thou found the reward of thy labors in the heavens. Thou didst destroy the demonic legions, and didst attain [Fol. 9r]
...unto the angelic ranks, whose life thou didst blamelessly emulate. As having boldness before Christ God, ask peace for our souls.

*Both now, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion:*

Seeing Thee crucified, O Christ, she who bare Thee cried aloud: What strange mystery is this which I behold, O my Son? How diest Thou in the flesh, suspended upon the Tree, O Giver of life?

*Troparion of the Saint, Tone 8:*

Let us honor the holy Barbara; for she broke the snares of the enemy, and like a bird was delivered from them, by the help and weapon of the Cross, the all-honorable one.

*Glory, Troparion of the Venerable One, Tone 8:*

O guide of Orthodoxy, teacher of piety and purity, luminary of the universe, God-inspired adornment of monks, O all-wise John, by thy teachings thou hast enlightened all, O spiritual pipe: Entreat Christ God that our souls may be saved.

*Both now, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion.*
*At Matins, at "God is the Lord," Troparion of the Saint twice. Glory to the Saint. Both now, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion.*
*One Canon of the Octoechos to 6, and two Canons of the Saints to 8.*[^17]

*Canon of the Saint to 4, Tone 2.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

The overdressed power of Pharaoh's whole host was of old laid low in the deep, but the incarnate Word destroyed all-wicked sin, the most glorified Lord, for gloriously is He glorified.

O most divine and honorable Trinity, Who bestowest gifts beyond understanding upon Thy servants, breathe a light-bearing beam into my darkened mind, that I may praise Thy martyr Barbara, ever to be remembered. *(Twice)*

The glory of Thy martyrs truly surpassed every boundary of praise, O Lover of mankind; but accepting praise according to our strength from faith, send down rich recompense, O Master.

From a thorny root grew forth a most beautiful rose, fragrancing the Church of Christ; and dyed red with the scarlet of suffering in blood, glorious Barbara, of whom we worthily sing.

*Another Canon of the Venerable One to 4, same Tone and Heirmos:*

As I desire to begin thy praises, grant me now thy honey-flowing voice, O venerable one, with which thou didst elucidate the Orthodox Church with hymns, O Father John, which honors thy memory. *(Twice)* [Fol. 9v]
As a wise and astute judge, looking most excellently upon the nature of things, thou didst discern eternal things above the present; for with transient things thou didst exchange abiding things, O Father John, where Christ now glorifies thee.

*Theotokion:*

Remaining ever-virgin, O pure one, thou wast revealed higher than all creation, visible and invisible; for thou didst bear the Creator, even as He was pleased to be incarnate in thy womb: Whom with boldness beseech to save those who hymn thee.

*Canon of Saint Barbara.*
*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

The wilderness, the barren Church of the Gentiles, blossomed like a lily at Thy coming, O Lord, wherein my heart is established.

Wounded with Thy love as with a bridegroom's, O Master, with unrestrained yearning the holy sufferer Barbara hated all paternal godlessness.

Neither the beauty of sweetness, nor the bloom of comeliness, nor wealth, nor the pleasures of youth delighted thee, O glorious Barbara, who wast betrothed unto Christ, O good maiden.

Unto perfect ascetical struggles neither the weakness of women nor the youth of age proved any hindrance, O Christ, being strengthened by Thine invisible power.

*Canon of the Venerable One:*

Thou didst disperse wealth, giving in loan unto God; therefore the Kingdom was prepared for thee in the heavens, and now, O John, thou hast received manifold recompense.

Having received the talent of wisdom, thou didst adorn it with deeds and elucidate the Church of Christ, O John, multiplying it manifoldly, having also abandoned this life.

*Theotokion:*

The angelic ranks marveled, O all-pure one, and the hearts of men were in awe at thy childbirth. Therefore in faith we honor thee as the Theotokos.

*Kontakion of the Venerable One, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up upon the Cross" (Вознесы́йсѧ на крⷭ҇тъ):*

Let us hymn the hymnographer and honorable God-proclaimer, the instructor and teacher of the Church, and the adversary of foes, John; for having taken up the Cross of the Lord as a weapon, he repelled all the deceit of heresies, and as a fervent intercessor before God, he grants unto all the forgiveness of transgressions.

*Ikos:*

Unto the instructor, teacher, and priest of the Church, as an initiate of ineffable mysteries, let us cry aloud in concord: By thy prayers unto God open our mouths, and account us worthy to speak the words [Fol. 10r]
...the words of thy teachings. For thou wast revealed as a communicant of the Trinity, shining in the world like a fair sun, radiant with wonders and teachings like Moses; having meditated upon the law of the Lord at all times, in word and deed thou wast a luminary, praying unceasingly to grant unto all the forgiveness of transgressions.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 3.*
*Tone 3, Podoben: "Beholding the beauty of thy virginity" (Красотѣ̀ дѣ́вства):*

At thy suffering thou didst astonish all, in that thou didst endure the wounds of the tormentors, bonds, tortures, and prisons, O most praised Barbara. Therefore Christ gave thee also a crown from heaven; and unto Him Whom thou didst desire thou didst fervently run, and He granted thee grace, O martyr, to pour forth healings unto men.

*Glory, of the Venerable One, the same Tone:*

Thou wast revealed unto us most sacredly as a sweet-sounding trumpet that was seen,[^18] singing figuratively the teachings of the Lord and Savior unto the ends of the earth. And by thy words thou didst enlighten the world, O venerable John: Entreat Christ God to grant us great mercy.

*Both now, Theotokion:*

Thou wast the divine tabernacle of the Word, O only all-pure Virgin Mother, who in purity didst surpass the angels; cleanse me, who beyond all others have become dust, defiled by carnal transgressions, by the divine waters of thy prayers, granting great mercy, O pure one.

*Stavrotheotokion:*

Beholding Him Who sprouted forth from her without travail hanging upon the Cross, the spotless ewe-lamb of the Word, the incorrupt Virgin Mother, weeping maternally, cried aloud: Woe is me, my Child! How sufferest Thou willingly, desiring to deliver man from the passions of dishonor?

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

Thou didst come from the Virgin, not an intercessor nor an angel, but Thou Thyself, O Lord, having become incarnate, and didst save me, whole man; therefore I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparia:*

Being born of the Virgin, Thou didst grant unto young maidens by deeds to cast down the haughtiness of the deceiver; therefore the fair-victorious Barbara mocked his pride.

Those seduced of old by the crafty wiles of the deceiver were driven out from the delight of Paradise; but Barbara, having mocked him, now takes up her abode in the heavenly bridal chamber.

By Thy Cross Thou didst destroy the power of death; therefore the maiden, not sparing her body, O Christ, endures most valiantly [Fol. 10v]
...most valiantly the wounds, O Barbara, with a firm mind.

*Of the Venerable One:*

Obeying the command of Christ, thou didst forsake worldly beauty, wealth, sweetness, and brilliance; therefore taking up thy cross, thou didst follow Him, O wise John.

Having shared with Christ Who became poor for the sake of human salvation, thou wast glorified together with Him, as He promised, and thou reignest with Him Who is co-eternal, O John.

*Theotokion:*

All we the faithful know thee as a haven of salvation and an insurmountable wall, O Birthgiver of God, Sovereign Lady; for by thy prayers thou deliverest our souls from afflictions.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

Thou wast a Mediator between God and men, O Christ God; for through Thee, O Master, we have access from the night of ignorance unto Thy Father, the Source of light.

*Troparia:*

Having commanded that the bathhouse be illuminated with three windows, thou didst mystically depict baptism, O Barbara, working a light-bearing cleansing of the soul by the light of the Trinity.

Kindled with zeal as with a coal of God, the all-praised maiden Barbara spat upon the defiled faces of the falsely-named gods, mocking the outward ruler of the world.

Fleeing from the frenzy of her fierce father, O Barbara, a mountain opened and received thee straightway; as of old Christ worked a miracle for Thecla the ever-memorable first martyr.

*Of the Venerable One:*

O father,[^19] being strengthened by the fear of Christ unto the divine life, thou didst subject all carnal wisdom unto the Spirit, cleansing thy senses, O John.

Having cleansed body, mind, and soul of all defilement, O God-wise one, thou didst receive the tri-radiant beam, O John, enriching thee with radiant gifts.

*Theotokion:*

Beseech Thy Son and Lord, O pure Virgin, to grant peaceful deliverance from adverse circumstances unto those who have taken refuge in thee.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

Held fast in the depth of sin, O Savior, and tempest-tossed in the surge of life: yet as Jonas from the whale, so also lead me up from the passions, and save me.

*Troparia:*

As Thou didst promise, O Savior, to grant God-taught wisdom unto those who stand before the tribunal of the tormentors for Thy sake: whereof the martyr Barbara was filled.

[Fol. 11r]
Thou didst refute the deceit of the godless by God-wise word, O glorious Barbara; and by the endurance of deeds thou didst astonish the haughty thoughts of the tormentors.

The blameless passion-bearer surrendered her body to be scraped mercilessly with wounds and firmly torn with iron claws for the sake of Christ.

*Of the Venerable One:*

Enlightened by the grace of the Spirit, and having clearly grown rich in the knowledge of divine and human things, thou didst ungrudgingly impart it unto those who ask, O John.

In likeness to the heavenly choirs, O wise one, thou didst adorn the Church most harmoniously, chanting choir-standing songs God-woven unto the Trinity.

*Theotokion:*

Without knowing a bridegroom, O Virgin, thou gavest birth, and thou remainest a Virgin forever, showing forth the images of the true Divinity of thy Son and God.

*Kontakion, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up upon the Cross" (Вознесы́йсѧ на крⷭ҇тъ):*

Having followed God Who is piously hymned in the Trinity, O passion-bearer, thou didst blunt the idol shrines; and striving in the midst of thy struggle, O Barbara, thou wast not afraid of the threats of the tormentors, O manly-minded one, ever crying aloud with a great voice: I honor the Trinity, the one Godhead!

*Ikos:*

Coming together, let us worthily honor Barbara who was betrothed unto Christ through martyrdom: that being delivered by her prayers from soul-destroying ruin, pestilence, earthquake, and downfall, we may pass our life in peace, being accounted worthy with all the saints who from the ages have been pleasing unto God to walk in the light and to sing with them: Thou hast shown marvelous mercy, O Savior, unto all men who confess with faith: We honor the Trinity, the one Godhead!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

The God-opposing decree of the lawless tormentor raised high the flame: but Christ extended the spiritual dew unto the pious children: He Who is blessed and supremely glorified.

*Troparia:*

The tormentor, brightly raging to destroy the earth and consume the sea, lies under the feet of the maiden Barbara as a plaything; for Christ, having trampled him, bound him like a paltry bird.

While all thy body was scraped with unbearable wounds, and crimsoned with drops of blood, thou didst endure being burned upon thy ribs with torches, O all-praised martyr, thanking Christ, O glorious Barbara [Fol. 11v]
...of the unchild-loving and unmerciful cruelty of the tormentors, and their exceedingly great godlessness! For the breasts of the martyr were severed with swords cruelly, as in a slaughterhouse, while she fixed her mind upon Christ the Umpire of the contest.

*Of the Venerable One:*

Kindled with zeal, thou didst refute every malice of God-fighting heresies with radiant writings, clearly revealing unto all what had been sown of old, finely written by the wise, O Father John.

Fervently thou didst refute the blasphemous impiety of the evil-named disciples of Manes, who attempted to subvert the Church of Christ, by thy words and dogmas which thou didst compose, O Father John.

*Theotokion:*

We know thee to be more holy than the saints, as the only one who didst give birth unto the immutable God, O undefiled Virgin, unmarried Mother; for unto all the faithful thou didst pour forth incorruption by thy divine childbirth.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

The fiery furnace of old in Babylon divided its operation by the divine command, burning the Chaldeans, but bedewing the faithful who sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparia:*

Christ appeared unto Thee in inaccessible light when thou wast shut up in prison, O Barbara, bidding Thee to be of good cheer, healing thy wounds, and granting joy; therefore thou wast winged with desire for thy Bridegroom.

Manifestly was Thy prophecy revealed as fulfilled, O Christ; for the father surrenders his child unto death, and the wretched father became the very slaughterer of Thy martyr; therefore was he destroyed by fire from heaven.

A radiant angel clothed thee, stripped naked for the sake of Christ, O pure Barbara, with a light-bearing garment, as a bride going forth unto suffering; for thou didst strip off garments, O martyr, having received the divine transformation.

*Of the Venerable One:*

Clearly, O thrice-blessed John, thou didst refute the division of Nestorius, the confusion of Severus, and the madness of the Monothelites;[^20] and thou didst radiate the single-energy faith, the brightness of Orthodoxy, unto all the ends of the earth.

The enemy, sowing his customary heretical tares in the Church of Christ to reject His worship in the venerable icons, found thee not slumbering, O all-blessed John, uprooting every evil seed.

*Theotokion:*

[Fol. 12r]
Thou, O all-pure Birthgiver of God, didst seedlessly conceive and ineffably give birth unto Him Who lived in a divine manner in thy womb without being separated from the Father: therefore do we confess thee as the salvation of us all.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

The Son of the unoriginate Begetter, God and Lord, incarnate of the Virgin, appeared unto us to enlighten the darkened, and to gather the scattered: therefore do we magnify the all-hymned Theotokos.

*Troparia:*

Destined to receive a glorious end of thy martyrdom by the sword, O Barbara, and being accounted worthy of the pouring forth of martyrs' crowns, thou didst hear the divine voice fulfilling thy supplications.

Now united unto Christ, the King of all, thy Bridegroom, radiant with the glory of the divine light in the heavenly bridal chambers, O Barbara, look down upon those who sing of thee, transforming their passions, and bringing them unto the living God.

Fulfilling thy petition, O passion-bearer Barbara, Christ grants healings unto those who celebrate thy annual memory with faith; truly, O blessed one, thy marvelous deeds have surpassed the sand of the sea.

*Of the Venerable One:*

Thou didst teach all sons of the Church to sing in an Orthodox manner unto the honorable Monad in Trinity, and to glorify the divine incarnation of the Word; clearly, O John, thou didst elucidate what was hard for many to understand in the sacred Scriptures.

Having hymned the choirs of the saints, O venerable one—the honorable Theotokos, the Forerunner of Christ, and also the Apostles, the Prophets with the fasters, the wise Teachers, the Righteous, and the Martyrs: in their tabernacles dost thou now take up thy dwelling.

*Theotokion:*

Thou wast the bridal chamber of the incarnation of the Word that surpasses the mind, O Virgin Birthgiver of God, clothed and adorned with the glory of virtues: therefore do we proclaim thee, O all-immaculate one, as the Theotokos.

*Exapostilarion of the Octoechos, and of the Saints.*
*Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Жены́ оу҆слы́шите):*

Like a most fair briar-rose from a thorny root didst thou grow forth, O virgin Barbara, crimsoned with blood through the sacrifice of thy sacred suffering as a martyr; and now save from perils those who celebrate thy divine memory with love.

*Glory, of the Venerable One:*

As a divine light, O our father, thou didst shine forth upon the Church, illuminating it with the brightness of thy hymns and with the light of thy disposition; wherewith [Fol. 12v]
...wherewith thou showest forth the dogmas of Christ adorned; unto Whom cease not to pray for us, O John.

*Both now, Theotokion:*

Truly do we confess thee as the Theotokos, O Sovereign Lady, who are saved through thee; for ineffably thou didst give birth unto God, Who destroyed death by the Cross and drew unto Himself the assemblies of the venerable ones: with whom we praise thee, O Virgin.

*At the Praises, Stichera of the Saint, 4, Tone 1. Idiomela. By Anatolius:*

Having despised the enjoyment of earthly food and her father's wealth, and having likewise hated glory, thou didst love the heavenly Bridegroom, O all-glorious Barbara; for having been beheaded with the sword, thou didst enter with the wise virgins unto Christ the Bridegroom. Therefore, driving away pestilential disease, thou healest the faithful by the operation of the Holy Spirit, praying unceasingly for our souls.

*Tone 2. By Byzantios:*

The crafty enemy was put to shame, being conquered by a woman, even as he possessed an operation toward sin through the foremother; for the Father's Word, incarnate of the Virgin immutably and unconfusedly, as He alone knows, destroyed the curse of Eve and Adam—Christ Who worthily crowned Barbara the martyr, and for her sake grants cleansing and great mercy unto the world.

The God-called martyr Barbara, suffering upon the tribunal, said: Severe indeed are the present tortures from the tormentors, but joyful is the receiving of eternal life; nor will I at all prefer earthly things above heavenly: therefore cut, scrape the flesh, and surrender me to the fire; rejoicing I shall depart unto Christ my Bridegroom. By her prayers, O Christ God, send down Thy mercies and save us who celebrate her sufferings with faith.

Come, ye people, let us sing the festival of the passion-bearer Barbara today; for neither sword, nor fire, nor other torture, nor the manifold snares of Belial conquered her; and unto her let us cry aloud with faith: Entreat Christ, O all-glorious fair-martyr, to grant us great mercy.

*Glory, Tone 6. By John the Monk:*

Having walked the path of suffering, thou didst escape the counsel of the forefather, O all-honorable Barbara; and as a wise virgin carrying a lamp, thou didst enter into the courts of thy Lord. And as a courageous martyr, thou hast received grace to heal [Fol. 13r]
...bodily passions; but also deliver us who hymn thee from soul-sicknesses, by thy prayers unto God.

*Both now, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion:*

When the pure one saw Thee hanging upon the Cross, she cried aloud, weeping maternally: O my Son and my God, my sweetest Child, how sufferest Thou an ignominious passion?

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos.*
*Glory, of the Venerable One, Tone 8:*

We honor thee, O our father John, as the instructor of multitudes of monks; for by thy path have we truly learned to walk uprightly. Blessed art thou, having worked for Christ, and having exposed the power of the enemy, O converser with the angels, communicant of the venerable and the righteous: with whom entreat the Lord that our souls may be saved.

*Both now, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion.*
*Tone 8, Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (Ѡ҆ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*

I cannot endure, O Child, seeing Thee asleep upon the Tree, Who bestowest wakefulness upon all, that Thou mayest grant divine and saving wakefulness unto those who of old fell asleep in the sleep of perdition through the fruit of transgression! cried the Virgin, weeping, whom we magnify.

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes from the Canon of the Martyr, Ode 3, and of the Venerable One, Ode 6.*
*Prokeimenon, Tone 4: God is marvelous in His saints, the God of Israel.*
*Verse: In the congregations bless ye God, the Lord from the springs of Israel.*
*Epistle to the Galatians, pericope 208 [Gal. 3:23-29].*
*Alleluia, Tone 4: With patience I waited for the Lord, and He gave ear unto me.*
*Gospel according to Mark, pericope 21 [Mark 5:24-34].*
*Communion Hymn: Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous.*

*Where there is a temple of the Holy Great-Martyr Barbara, or otherwise if the rector desires to celebrate an All-Night Vigil: see the service for the Holy Great-Martyr appointed at the end of the book of this month of December.*[^21]

[Fol. 13v]
*In the same month, on the 5th day: Our Venerable and God-bearing Father Sabbas the Sanctified:*
*At Small Vespers, Stichera on 4.*
*Tone 1, Podoben: "All-praised martyrs" (Всехва́льнїи мꙋ́ченницы):*

Thou wast a beholder of the spiritual hosts with thy mind, as one who didst practice the divine words, laying them in thy heart; wherein thou didst also establish ascents like a ladder, O venerable Sabbas, our father. And now pray that peace and great mercy be granted unto our souls. *(Twice)*

O most venerable Sabbas, from infancy thou didst commit thy life unto Christ our God; strengthened by Whom, thou didst subject carnal passions to reason, subordinating the worse to the better; therefore pray that peace and great mercy be granted unto our souls.

O God-wise father of ours, thou wast revealed as a most great luminary, enlightening the world beneath the sun with the rays of wonders and with divine deeds; therefore after thy dormition the unwaning light received thee. And now pray that peace and great mercy be granted unto our souls.

*Glory, Tone 2:*

O venerable father, having diligently trained thyself in virtues from infancy, thou wast an instrument of the Holy Spirit; and having received from Him the operation of wonders, thou didst persuade men to despise sweet things. And now, being most purely illumined by the divine light, enlighten also our thoughts, O Sabbas, our father.

*Both now, Theotokion:*

All my hope I place upon thee, O Mother of God; preserve me beneath thy shelter.

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O house of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*

Thou wast revealed from thy mother's swaddling bands, O our God-bearing father, as a consecrated vessel and a dwelling of the All-Holy Spirit.
*Verse: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones.*
Bearing the Cross of the Lord upon thy shoulders, O our father Sabbas, thou didst utterly destroy the demonic fantasies.
*Verse: Blessed is the man who fears the Lord, in His commandments he will* [Fol. 14r]
...greatly.

Having refuted the deceit of the crafty demons by the power of the Cross, thou didst also elucidate the glory of Christ, O Sabbas, our father.

*Glory, Both now, Theotokion, the same Podoben (Подо́бенъ то́йже):*

O good Sovereign Lady, lift up thine all-holy hands unto thy Son, the soul-loving Creator, to have compassion upon thy servants.

*Troparion, Tone 8:*

With the streams of thy tears thou didst cultivate the barren desert, and with sighings from the depths thou didst bring forth fruit in thy labors a hundredfold; and thou didst become a luminary to the universe, shining with wonders, O Sabbas, our father: Entreat Christ God that our souls may be saved.

*Tone 5, Podoben: "O venerable father" (Прпⷣбне ѻ҆́ч҃е):*

O God-wise Sabbas, peer of the angels, fellow-dweller with the venerable, converser with the prophets, co-heir with martyrs and apostles, now dwelling in the unwaning light, shining with its divine rays; standing before Him with utmost desire, enlightened with boldness, and enjoying His visions and feeding upon His beauties unceasingly: Praying unto Christ, entreat Christ, O venerable one, to grant unto the Church oneness of mind, peace, and great mercy.

O God-wise Sabbas, unquenchable luminary of abstinence, most radiant lamp of monastics, enlightened by the rays of love, unbending pillar of endurance, confirmation and strength of those who honor thee with faith, treasure-house of healings, dweller of the wilderness in truth, having shown it forth as a divine paradise bearing divine fruits of those who are saved: Praying unto Christ, entreat Christ, O venerable one, to grant unto the Church oneness of mind, peace, and great mercy.

O God-wise Sabbas, fiery pillar of virtues, lamp guiding men from the sea of this world unto the divine haven, who didst cast down the spirits of deceit, pure receptacle of the Holy Spirit, instructor of monastics, certain measure of abstinence, bright height of humility, fountain pouring forth an abyss of healings: Praying unto Christ, entreat Christ, O venerable one, to grant unto the Church oneness of mind, peace, and great [Fol. 14v]
...and great mercy.

*Glory, Tone 6:*

Having preserved that which is according to the image unharmed, having by fasting set the mind as master over destructive passions, thou didst ascend as far as possible unto that which is according to the likeness; for having manfully constrained thy nature, thou didst strive to subject the worse to the better, and to enslave the flesh to the Spirit. Therefore thou wast revealed as the summit of monastics, a dweller of the wilderness, an instructor of those who run well, a most exact rule of virtue. And now in the heavens, the mirrors being resolved,[^22] O our father Sabbas, thou purely beholdest the Holy Trinity, directly interceding for those who honor thee with faith and love.

*Who will not call thee blessed:*

*Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day.*
*Readings, 3.*

*The Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon. [Chapter 3:1-9]:*

The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment shall touch them. In the eyes of the foolish they seemed to die, and their departure was accounted an affliction, and their going from us to be destruction; but they are in peace. For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality. And having been a little chastened, they shall be greatly rewarded, for God tested them, and found them worthy for Himself. As gold in the furnace did He test them, and received them as a whole burnt offering. And in the time of their visitation they shall shine forth, and shall run to and fro like sparks among the stubble. They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the peoples, and the Lord shall reign in them forever. They that put their trust in Him shall understand the truth, and the faithful in love shall abide with Him; for grace and mercy are in His venerable ones, and visitation is among His elect.

*The Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon. [Chapter 5:15–6:3]:*

The righteous live forever, and their reward is in the Lord, and the care of them is with the Most High. Therefore shall they receive a kingdom of majesty, and a crown of beauty from the hand of the Lord; for with His right hand shall He cover them, and with His arm shall He shield them. He shall take His zeal for complete armor, and shall arm creation for vengeance upon enemies. He shall put on righteousness as a breastplate, and shall don unfeigned judgment as a helmet. He shall take holiness as an invincible shield; He shall sharpen fierce wrath for a sword; and the world shall fight with Him against the foolish. The right-aiming arrows of lightnings shall go forth; and as from [Fol. 15r]
...as from the well-drawn bow of the clouds they shall fly unto the mark; and from the stone-casting wrath hailstones full of fury shall fall; the water of the sea shall rage against them, and the rivers shall drown them sharply. Against them shall stand the spirit of power, and as a whirlwind it shall winnow them. And iniquity shall lay waste the whole earth, and evildoing shall overthrow the thrones of the mighty. Give ear therefore, O ye kings, and understand; learn, ye judges of the ends of the earth. Give ear, ye that rule multitudes, and that make your boast in peoples of nations: for dominion is given unto you from the Lord, and power from the Most High.

*The Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon. [Chapter 4:7–15]:*

The righteous man, though he happen to die early, shall be in rest. For honorable age is not that which stands in length of time, nor is it measured by number of years. But wisdom is gray hair unto men, and an unspotted life is ripe old age. Having been well-pleasing unto God, he was beloved, and living among sinners, he was translated. He was caught away, lest wickedness should alter his understanding, or deceit beguile his soul. For the bewitching of wickedness darkens good things, and the roving of desire undermines the innocent mind. Being made perfect in a short time, he fulfilled long years; for his soul was pleasing unto the Lord: therefore hastened He from the midst of wickedness. But the peoples saw, and understood not, neither laid they this in mind, that grace and mercy are in His venerable ones, and visitation is among His elect.

*At the Litiya, the Sticheron of the Temple:*
*And of the Saint, Idiomela, Tone 2:*

Having assembled an ascetic training upon the earth, O venerable Sabbas,[^23] and having blunted all the assaults of the passions by the stream of thy tears: as a divine and honorable ladder leading up unto heaven was thy God-pleasing life made known unto all; for having shown forth the fruits of piety therein, thou healest by them the infirmities of passions of those who cry aloud unto thee with faith: Rejoice, O radiant eastern golden-beaming star, bright lamp and shepherd of monastics! Rejoice, O ever-praised one, most excellent nurture of the wilderness, and unshakable confirmation of the Church! Rejoice, O great guide of the wandering! Rejoice, our boast, and the radiant joy of the universe!

An angel upon earth and a man of God in the heavens, the fair beauty of the world, the sweetness of good [Fol. 15v]
...things, and the praise of ascetic virtues: let us honor Sabbas. For planted in the house of God, he blossomed uprightly; and like a cedar in the wilderness, he multiplied the flock of Christ's noetic sheep, in holiness and righteousness.

God, Who alone rests among the saints, having found thy sanctified soul a pure dwelling-place, took up His abode therein and filled it with divine graces: wherewith thou guidest unto the light those who sing of thee, O sanctified and blessed Sabbas.

*Glory, Tone 2:*

Having received a desire for good things that surpasses the mind, thou didst despise all the fair things of the world, O God-pleasing one. For thence by fruit thou wast not tripped up like Adam; and having struck down the serpent by abstinence, thou didst live an angelic life. And now thou art tabernacled in the heavens, enjoying the tree of life, entreating God for us who faithfully celebrate thy memory, O sanctified Sabbas.

*Both now, Theotokion:*
*O wonder of new wonders!*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 5.*
*Tone 5, Podoben: "Rejoice" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ):*

Rejoice, O fragrant vessel of ascetic struggles in truth! For having taken the Cross upon thy shoulder and committed thyself unto Christ the Master, O all-blessed one, thou didst trample down the fleshly mind that drags downward; and with virtues thou didst enlighten thy soul, and didst soar unto divine longing. Therefore, encircling thine all-holy shrine, O all-praised Sabbas, we ask to obtain divine love for mankind through thy prayers, and that great mercy be granted unto the world.

*Verse: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones.*

A coal shining with God, having drawn near unto the fire of the Spirit, O God-bearer, wast thou revealed in the world, O Sabbas, enlightening the souls of those who faithfully approach thee, O God-wise one, guiding them unto the unwaning light, O venerable one; and being bedewed from above by divine grace, thou didst quench the coals of the wilderness.[^24] Therefore Christ, the Dispenser of divine righteousness, manifestly granted thee the crown of victory, O blessed one: Whom do thou entreat to grant unto our souls great mercy.

*Verse: Blessed is the man who fears the Lord, in His commandments he will desire greatly.*

A ladder reaching unto heaven in truth was thy life revealed to be, O God-wise one, whereby thou didst ascend unto the heights, and wast accounted worthy to converse with Christ the Master, O all-blessed one [Fol. 16r]
...having enlightened thy mind with the brightness that is there, and being illuminated by His rays, thou didst receive an angel-equal radiance. Standing now before Him, entreat Him, O venerable one, to present with thee those who celebrate thy divine and all-sacred memory, and to grant unto the world great mercy.

*Glory, Tone 8:*

Multitudes of monks honor thee as instructor, O our father Sabbas; for by thy path have we truly learned to walk uprightly. Blessed art thou, having worked for Christ, and having exposed the power of the enemy, O converser with the angels, communicant of the venerable and the righteous: with whom entreat the Lord that our souls may be saved.

*Canon of the Venerable One, on 8.*
*Whose acrostic is: I lovingly sing of Sabbas, the preeminent among fasters. The work of Theophanes. Tone 8.*

[Fol. 17r]
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

The charioteer Pharaoh did the wonderworking rod of Moses of old engulf, striking in the form of a cross and dividing the sea; but it saved the fleeing, pedestrian Israel, who sang a song unto God.

*Troparia:*

Illumine with the radiant beaming of the Holy Spirit, O Sabbas, those who praise thee with hymns in pious love: O boast of fasters, glory of monastics, adornment of the wilderness, teacher of piety.

Having placed all thy love upon God from thy youth, and having all thy longing joyfully toward Him, thou didst put to death the movements of the flesh and the assaults of the passions by abstinence, O all-praised God-bearing Sabbas.

Having overcome the serpent hidden beneath the fruit, thou didst trample him down, and didst lightly pass by his snares, having winged thyself with the wings of piety, O father; and rejoicing, thou didst find life from the strong Garden.

Illumined by the light of grace, thou didst enter into the fire, and like the three children thou didst remain unburnt, God having preserved thee, and revealing unto all thy future progress and perfection thereafter, O father.

*Theotokion:*

Death advanced with unrestrainable assaults against us;[^26] but drawing near unto thy childbearing it perished, and colliding with it was abolished, O Virgin Birthgiver of God: for in truth thou didst give birth unto the incarnate ever-existing Life.

*Katavasia: The Master Who wrought wonders saved a people:*[^27]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

The bow of the mighty has been broken by Thy power, O Christ, and the weak have girded themselves with power.

*Troparia:*

He Who is outside of all time, as Maker of times, was willingly formed as an infant of thee, O Virgin.

Let us hymn the womb that was more spacious than the heavens, through which Adam rejoices, dwelling in the heavens.

*Another Heirmos:*

Thou Who in the beginning didst establish the heavens in understanding, and didst found the earth upon the waters, confirm me, O Christ, upon the rock of Thy commandments; for there is none holy above Thee, O Thou Who alone lovest mankind.

*Troparion:*

Having set thy mind as master over passions, O all-rich one, thou wast revealed as a dispenser of righteousness, for clearly thou didst subject the worse unto the better. Therefore like a palm tree [Fol. 17v]
...didst thou blossom in the wildernesses, O father.

Understanding how to follow the divine footsteps, thou wast an exile from thy homeland; and dwelling in the wilderness, thou didst raise up a victory over adversaries, being strengthened by divine power.

Strengthened by firmness of understanding, O all-blessed one, thou didst wisely expose the diverse wiles of the enemy, and didst show them unto all, and didst cast down his exalted pride.

Seeing thee sanctified in soul and in choice of purity, adorned with virtues, the most radiant star Euthymius received thee, prophetically proclaiming thy brightness, O all-blessed one.

*Theotokion:*

Thou wast truly known to be the bright door of the saving dispensation of the Word for our sake, O Virgin Mother: for unto us thou didst introduce the noetic ray of the transcendent Godhead.

*Katavasia: Look down upon the hymns of thy servants, O Benefactor:*

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8.*
*Tone 8, Podoben: "Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*

Having left all earthly things, though being in the world bodily, in spirit thou wast a partaker with the angels; for having put to death the present bodily passions, thou didst show thyself a servant of the Trinity, O blessed one. Therefore thou healest the sufferings of the sick, and by a word thou drivest away spirits by grace, O our God-bearing father: Entreat Christ God to grant remission of offenses unto those who celebrate thy holy memory with love.

*Glory:*

Having left worldly turmoil, and taken thy cross upon thy shoulders, thou didst commit thy whole self unto God; and being outside of flesh and the world, thou wast a converser with the Holy Spirit. Therefore, stirring up people unto zeal, thou didst empty out cities, and didst make the wildernesses into cities, O our God-bearing father: Entreat Christ God to grant remission of offenses unto those who celebrate thy holy memory with love.

*Both now, Theotokion:*

As the all-immaculate bride of the Creator, as the unwedded Mother of the Redeemer, as the receptacle of the Comforter, O all-hymned one: hasten to deliver me from the malice of demons, who am a foul dwelling-place of iniquity and who through lack of understanding have become their plaything; and make me a radiant dwelling of virtues, O light-bearing and incorrupt one, drive away the cloud of passions, and a partaker of the higher good [Fol. 18r]
...vouchsafe me to be a partaker of the higher good and of the unwaning light, through thy prayers.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

I heard, O Lord, of Thy glorious dispensation, and I glorified Thine incomprehensible power, O Lover of mankind.

*Troparia:*

The divine mountain of the house of the Lord was exalted above the heavenly powers, clearly shown forth as the Mother of God.

Apart from the laws of nature, O Virgin, having alone given birth unto the Benefactor of creation, thou wast accounted worthy of the divine calling.

*Another Heirmos:*

Thou art my strength, O Lord, Thou art also my power, Thou art my God, Thou art my rejoicing, Who leftest not the Father's bosom and didst visit our poverty; therefore with the Prophet Habakkuk I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparia:*

Having purified the disposition of thy soul, and expanding it by divine visions, thou didst truly make it a receptive vessel of divine gifts, O God-blessed one. And by the laying on of thy hands thou didst heal the sick, having become an imitator of the Master.

He that raged fiercely against thee, O father, was swallowed up like wretched Dathan, and like Abiram was destroyed; for divine grace invisibly preserved thee, providing for the salvation of many, O all-blessed one, glorious Sabbas, wise in God!

Having disciplined thy senses by the law of God, O God-proclaimer, thou didst skillfully direct thy thought unto the understanding of bodiless and spiritual things: passing unfalteringly from glory to glory, from strength to strength, O father.

Having resolved to benefit thy kinsmen, thou didst build God-befitting and soul-profiting cities in the wilderness; and in a thirsty land thou didst bring forth fountains of waters, and didst marvelously bring down rain from heaven upon waterless regions, O God-wise one.

*Theotokion:*

A newly blossoming paradise of immortality and truly fair wast thou revealed to be, bearing in thy womb and giving birth most God-governingly unto the Tree of life planted within thee, dripping saving hope unto all who faithfully acknowledge thee as the Birthgiver of God.

*Another Heirmos:*

Why hast Thou cast me away from Thy face, O unwaning Light, and an alien darkness has covered me, a wretch? But turn me, and direct my paths unto the light of Thy commandments, I pray.

*Troparia:*

Reaching out with unwavering thought unto Him Whom thou didst desire, from Him thou didst receive the ineffable grace of greatest wonders, O father, and didst compassionately heal those who approach with faith, O venerable one.

Having put off the coarseness of fleshly heaviness, thou wast chosen as a God-fashioned vessel of the Holy Spirit, O marvelous one, adorned by the washing of tears,[^28] by prayer, and patience, and humility of mind.

Thou wast ordained a most loud-voiced preacher of divine dogmas, and wast a communicant of the holy councils, O father, instructing emperors; wherewith, manifestly protected by divine grace, thou wast revealed, O blessed one.

The grace given thee from God was proclaimed, O God-inspired one, and was dispensed unto all the ends of the universe, clearly showing forth in God-befitting manner the divine operation of wonders.

*Theotokion:*

O protectress of the faithful, unbreakable wall of those who hymn thee, as the salvation that appeared unto all the human race, having given birth in the flesh unto God Who appeared, save my soul, O all-pure one!

*Katavasia: From the night of the works of darkened delusion:*

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

Having heard the voice of suppliant words from an afflicted soul, O Master, deliver me from grievous things; for Thou alone art the cause of our salvation.

*Troparia:*

Human nature, enslaved unto sin, obtained freedom through thee, O pure Sovereign Lady; for thy Son, like a Lamb, is slain for all.

We all cry aloud unto thee, the true Mother of God: Deliver thy servants who have angered Him, for thou alone hast boldness toward the Son.

*Another Heirmos:*

*Troparia:*

Having acquired love toward God and neighbor, fulfilling the chief point of the Law and the Prophets: for thou didst uprightly perform the most wise virtue of all, without judging, O father.

Thou didst acquire an angel-equal life upon earth, and Christ granted thee angel-equal honor, having sent the holy ranks to accompany thy soul.

Having appeared as an offspring of wisdom, thou didst desire the fear of God, which is the beginning of wisdom, strengthened whereby, O father, thou didst reach the perfection possible for men.

*Theotokion:*

Having given birth unto the Savior and Redeemer, the God of all and Lord, Who partook of flesh unto us: save from perils those who call upon thee, O all-pure Sovereign Lady!
