*Tone 8, Podoben: "To thee, the Champion Leader" (Взбра́нной):*

As an immaculate sacrifice from infancy offered up unto God by virtue, O blessed Sabbas, thou wast a planter of piety. Therefore thou wast the adornment of the venerable, and a praiseworthy citizen of the wilderness. Therefore we cry aloud unto thee: Rejoice, O Sabbas most rich!

*Ikos:*

O supreme head of the fathers and beauty of the venerable, boldness of ascetics toward Christ, citizen and planter of the wilderness, how shall I hymn thy life, O venerable one? For thou shinest unto the ends of the earth like the sun. Therefore I cry aloud unto thee: Rejoice, fair boast of the Cappadocians! Rejoice, honorable sign of the universe! Rejoice, most fair shoot of the wilderness! Rejoice, divine plantation of the righteous! Rejoice, for thou didst despise fleeting and corruptible things! Rejoice, for thou dwellest in the heavens with the angels! Rejoice, correction and rule of monastics! Rejoice, awakening unto God for the slothful! Rejoice, God-flowing fountain of wonders! Rejoice, honorable organ of the Spirit! Rejoice, wherewith the East was adorned! Rejoice, wherewith the West shines! Rejoice, O Sabbas most rich!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

Holy did the most philosophic youths appear of old, for theologizing from a God-receiving soul with their lips, they sang: Blessed art Thou, O transcendent God of our fathers and our God!

[Fol. 19v]
*Troparia:*

Jacob indeed saw God in the night as in an enigma; but incarnate of thee, He appeared in brilliance unto those who sing: Blessed is the transcendent God of our fathers and exceedingly glorified!

Manifesting the tokens of the ineffable salvation in thee, He wrestled with Jacob: whereby He willingly united Himself unto men, O pure one: Blessed is the transcendent God of our fathers and exceedingly glorified!

Abominable is he who does not proclaim Thee, the Virgin's Son, as One of the all-hymned Trinity, and who cries not aloud with unwavering thought and tongue: Blessed is the transcendent God of our fathers and exceedingly glorified!

*Another Heirmos:*

The fire of the condescension of God was ashamed in Babylon of old; therefore the children in the furnace, dancing with joyful foot as in a meadow, sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparia:*

Having put off temporal things,[^29] rewarded with eternal things, thou rejoicest with the angels, having lived an angelic life, with whom thou didst also sing: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

Thy great and all-honorable Lavra cries aloud thankfully unto the Lord, offering thee as its dweller and builder and citizen, O wise one, and boasting calls: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

Unceasingly pray unto the Lord, O God-wise Sabbas, for thy flock, and diligently ask that those who continually bring forth fruit through thy labors may live forever, and who with love cry aloud: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*

An all-pure bridal chamber beyond words, of the incarnation of the Word, and palace, and throne, do we who hold right opinions name thee. And rejoicing in thy Son we cry: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Katavasia: Caught by love for the King of all, the children:*[^30]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

Disregarding the golden image, the thrice-blessed youths, seeing the immutable and living image of God, sang in the midst of the fire: Let all creation, being hallowed, bless the Lord, and exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparia:*

He Who is incomparable in goodness and in power was seen upon earth through thee, and dwelt with men. Singing unto Whom, all we the faithful cry aloud: Let all creation, being hallowed, bless the Lord, and exalt Him unto all ages!

Truly proclaiming thee pure, we glorify thee, O Birthgiver of God; for thou [Fol. 20r]
...for thou didst give birth unto One of the Trinity, incarnate. Unto Whom, together with the Father and the Spirit, all we sing: Let every creature bless the Lord, and exalt Him unto all ages!

*Another Heirmos:*

The Chaldean tormentor furiously kindled the furnace sevenfold for the godly; but seeing them saved by a higher power, he cried aloud unto the Creator and Deliverer: Ye children, bless; ye priests, sing praises; ye people, exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparia:*

With gladness, O venerable one, the ranks of the saints ran before thy most honorable soul unto a chosen place, into the radiant dwellings where the choirs of the righteous rejoice; with whom thou now singest: Ye priests, sing praises; ye people, exalt Christ unto ages!

Marvelous are thy wonders: for thou didst tame wild beasts, having calmed the waves of the passions; thou foretellest the future by a prophetic gift, driving away the demonic hosts, wounding them by all-powerful vigils, and by prayers and fastings, and by the invincible power of the Cross, O God-bearer.

He Who of old spake unto Moses from the pillar showed thee an all-radiant pillar stretched out from earth unto heaven, where now lies thy patient and much-suffering body: standing before which in faith, we piously sing: Ye people, exalt Christ unto ages!

Joyfully is thy memory celebrated, O all-praised one; for thou didst clothe thyself in joy-working virtue, the true robe of salvation, and the honorable and light-bearing garment of gladness; adorned in which, thou now singest unceasingly: Ye priests, sing praises; ye people, exalt Christ unto ages!

*Theotokion:*

Without knowing wedlock thou didst give birth, remaining a Virgin, and by thy marvelous childbearing thou didst unite all things, having destroyed the burdensome warfare[^31] and the distant estrangement, bearing in thy bosom Christ the Giver of peace: Whom we faithfully sing and exalt unto ages.

*Katavasia: The furnace moist with dew typified:*[^32]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

Thou art all desire, all sweetness, O Word of God, Son of the Virgin, God of gods, O Lord, all-holy One of the saints: therefore with her that bare Thee, all we magnify Thee.

*Troparia:*

The Word of God was given as a rod of strength unto corruptible nature, in thy womb, O pure one: and He raised up this nature that had slipped down toward hades: therefore we all [Fol. 20v]
...magnify thee, O pure one, as the Birthgiver of God.

Accept, O Master, Thy Mother as an intercessor praying for us, whom Thou wast well pleased to choose, and all things shall be filled with Thy goodness: that all we may magnify Thee as Benefactor.

*Another Heirmos:*

Heaven was astonished at this, and the ends of the earth were amazed, that God was manifested in the flesh unto men, and thy womb became more spacious than the heavens: therefore the hierarchies of angels and men magnify thee, O Birthgiver of God.

*Troparia:*

Thy shrine breathes forth a spiritual fragrance, richly gladdening thy sons who earnestly surround thee, remembering, O venerable one, thine angelic conversation, and the brightness and glory given unto thee, and the ever-existing beauty.

Water broke forth in the wilderness, and the thirsty land became a pool, transformed by thy prayers, O father; for ascetic hosts inhabit it as a well-watered river land; the country of the Jordan blossomed like a lily, watered by thy tears.

The brightness of the saints shone forth upon thee as a righteous man in the heavens, O father, for thou didst openly love Christ's true righteousness; following Whose manner of life, O all-blessed one, thou didst become conformed, in so far as it was possible, unto His life-bearing estate.[^33]

Shining with rich light, O God-bearer, and seeing the angelic choirs, light-bearing, surrounding the Light of the Trinity, and receiving by grace the rays of the vision of God: cease not to entreat that those who hymn thee be accounted worthy of remission of sins.

*Theotokion:*

As thou art higher than all the earthborn by incomparable preeminence, O pure one; for thou didst contain in thy womb God the Creator of all creation: entreat Him, as He is merciful, to grant unto the churches concord, peace, and quiet stability.

*Katavasia: It were easier for us to love silence:*[^34]

*Exapostilarion:*

Thou didst make the wilderness into a city by philosophic ways, O beauty of the fathers, Sabbas, our God-wise father, and didst make it a noetic paradise, blossoming with divine flowers, the multitudes of those of like mind who worthily celebrate thine honorable memory. *(Twice)*

*Glory, Both now, Theotokion:*

As thou hast compassion and great mercy, look down, O all-hymned Virgin Birthgiver of God, upon my lowliness, and dispel the turmoil of passions and the stumblings of life [Fol. 21r]
...and the stumblings of life, O Maiden, and deliver me from the fire of Gehenna through thy prayers.

*At the Praises, Stichera on 4, Tone 1. Podoben: "Joy of the ranks of heaven" (Нб҃ныхъ чинѡ́въ):*

The despiser of things below and stranger to them, the lover of things on high, and citizen of the wilderness, God-wise Sabbas, commands all of us faithfully to celebrate the saving day of his departure unto God. *(Twice)*

Having come to be outside flesh and the world through virtues, and by them in life upon earth thou didst glorify the Lord of glory, O wise father; and worthily wast thou glorified by Him, and wast shown forth as a divine fountain of healings, O God-received Sabbas.

Humble, guileless, meek, simple, silent wast thou, O father, truly surpassing man; and immaterial in matter, thou wast shown forth as an all-worthy house of God, prayerfully granting unto us the gifts that overflowed unto thee from Him.

*Glory, Tone 6:*

O venerable father, into all the earth went forth the report of thy correct deeds; therefore in the heavens thou hast found the reward of thy labors, thou didst destroy the demonic hosts, and didst reach the angelic ranks whose life thou didst blamelessly emulate. Having boldness toward Christ God, ask peace for our souls.

*Both now, Theotokion:*
*O Birthgiver of God, thou art the true vine:*

*Great Doxology and Dismissal.*
*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes from the Saint's Canon, Odes 3 and 6.*
*Prokeimenon, Tone 7: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones.*
*Verse: What shall I render unto the Lord for all that He hath rendered unto me?*
*The Epistle to the Galatians, pericope 213 [Galatians 5:22–6:2].*
*Alleluia, Tone 6: Blessed is the man who fears the Lord.*
*Verse: His seed shall be mighty upon the earth.*
*The Gospel according to Matthew, pericope 43 [Matthew 11:27–30].*
*Communion Hymn: In everlasting memory shall the righteous be.*

[Fol. 21v]
*In the same month, on the 6th day: Our Father among the Saints Nicholas, Archbishop of Myra in Lycia, Wonderworker:*

*If the rector desires, he celebrates an All-Night Vigil.*
*At Small Vespers, on "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 4, Tone 4. Podoben: "As one valiant among martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*

With divine myrrh the divine grace of the Spirit anointed thee, who didst preside over the people of Myra, and didst make the ends of the world fragrant with myrrh by thy virtues, most sacredly; and by thy sweet-breathing[^35] prayers thou ever drivest away foul-smelling passions. Therefore with faith we praise thee, and we celebrate thine all-holy memory, O Nicholas.

As an unwaning beacon, as a universal luminary that shone forth upon the firmament of the Church, O Nicholas, enlightening the world, driving away the mist[^36] of grievous perils, removing the winter of sorrows, and working a profound calm, we bless thee as is meet.

Being present here and appearing in dreams, O Nicholas, thou didst save those who were unjustly about to die, as one compassionate, as loving of good, as a most fervent deliverer, as a true defender of those who faithfully ask thy protection, O most sacred father, fellow citizen with the angels, equal in station unto the apostles and prophets.

Thy glorious life showed thee to be marvelous everywhere, O benefactor, most sacred, God-wise father, fair beauty of hierarchs, adornment of the venerable; and having spread out thy rays upon the earth like the sun, thou didst illumine the hearts of the faithful who celebrate thy light-bearing and divine memory, O all-blessed Nicholas.

*Glory, Tone 6:*

Thy holy memory shone forth like the sun, noetically enlightening the hearts of the faithful; which we also brightly celebrating today, prayerfully cry aloud unto thee: Rejoice, realm of chastity, who didst preserve the dignity of the soul unenslaved, girding thyself with the shield of abstinence! Rejoice, shepherd and teacher of thy people named after Christ! Rejoice, adornment of the Church, fair beauty of hierarchs [Fol. 22r]
...fair beauty of hierarchs, boast of monastics, O Nicholas most sacred, all-blessed father! Ceaselessly pray unto Christ God to grant peace unto the universe, and to save our souls.

*Both now, Theotokion:*
*No one that flees unto thee:*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 6. Podoben: "Having risen on the third day" (Трїдне́венъ воскре́слъ є҆сѝ):*

O blessed Nicholas, have compassion on me who fall down before thee, I pray thee, and O all-wise one, enlighten the eyes of my soul, that I may purely behold the Giver of light, Who is compassionate.

*Verse: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones.*

From enemies that seek to do me evil deliver me, O holy one, as thou hast boldness toward God, O all-blessed hierarch Nicholas, and save me from men of blood.

*Verse: Thy priests shall clothe themselves with righteousness, and Thy venerable ones shall rejoice.*

As a storm-free[^37] haven and an unconquerable wall have we the faithful acquired thee, O hierarch: a pillar of confirmation, a door of repentance, a guide of souls, and a defender.

*Glory, Both now, Theotokion:*

Having become envious against thy flock, O all-pure one, the adversary hungers each day, seeking deceitfully to make it his food: but do thou, O Birthgiver of God, deliver us from his harm.

*Troparion, Tone 4:*

A rule of faith and an image of meekness, a teacher of abstinence did the truth of things show thee forth unto thy flock. Therefore thou didst acquire high things by humility, rich things by poverty, O father and hierarch Nicholas: entreat Christ God that our souls may be saved.

*Glory, Both now, Theotokion:*
*The mystery hidden from the ages:*

*At Great Vespers, "Blessed is the man," the 1st Antiphon.*
*On "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 8, Tone 2. Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*

Having lived in Myra in the flesh, thou wast revealed truly as myrrh, being anointed with noetic myrrh, O holy Nicholas, hierarch of Christ; and thou makest fragrant the faces of those who ever celebrate thine all-praised memory with faith and love, delivering them from perils and assaults and these sorrows, O father, through thy prayers unto God.

Truly named after victory, thou wast revealed as mighty in perils unto the faithful people, O holy Nicholas, hierarch of Christ; for being invoked everywhere, thou swiftly anticipatest those who flee in love beneath thy protection; for appearing by day and by night unto the faithful, thou savest them [Fol. 22v]
...unto the faithful, thou savest them from perils and adversities.

Thou didst appear unto Emperor Constantine and unto Ablabius in sleep, and having cast fear into them, thou saidst thus unto them: Loose quickly those whom ye hold bound in prison, for they are guiltless of unlawful slaughter. But if thou disregardest me, I will make supplication against thee unto the King, praying unto the Lord.

A great and fervent defender art thou unto those who find themselves in perils, O glorious one, holy Nicholas, sacred preacher of Christ, unto those upon earth and those who sail, unto those who are far off and those near at hand, as most exceedingly merciful and a mighty intercessor. Therefore having assembled, we cry aloud: Pray unto the Lord, that we may be delivered from every adversity.

*Other Stichera, in the same Tone. Podoben: "With what crowns of praise" (Кі́ими похва́льными):*

With what crowns of praise shall we crown the hierarch? Who is in Myra in the flesh, yet spiritually reaches all who purely love him; the defender and protector of all, and consoler of all the sorrowful; the refuge of all that are in perils; the pillar of piety, champion of the faithful: for whose sake Christ, Who hath great mercy, cast down the arrogance of enemies. *(Twice)*

With what songs of praise shall we praise the hierarch? The adversary of impiety and champion of piety, the primate of the Church, great protector and teacher, putting to shame all the ill-believing, the destroyer of Arius and of his accomplices: for whose sake Christ, Who hath great mercy, cast down their arrogance.

With what prophetic hymns shall we praise the hierarch? Who foresees things that are far off, and unerringly prophesies things that are present as though near at hand, watching over all the universe and delivering all the wronged; who appeared in sleep unto the God-wise emperor, and of old delivered those bound from an unjust slaughter, and grants great mercy.

*Glory, Tone 6:*

The adornment of hierarchs and glory of the fathers, the fountain of wonders and great defender of the faithful: let us, O feast-lovers, assembling together, praise with hymns of praise, saying: Rejoice, guardian of the people of Myra, and honorable primate, and unshakeable pillar! Rejoice, all-radiant luminary, who by wonders enlightenest the ends of the world [Fol. 23r]
...who by wonders enlightenest the ends of the world! Rejoice, divine joy of the sorrowful, and fervent defender of the wronged! And now, O all-blessed Nicholas, cease not to pray unto Christ God for those who with faith and love honor thy ever-joyous and all-festal memory.

*Both now, of the Forefeast, in the same Tone:*

O cave, adorn thyself well; for the Ewe comes, bearing Christ in her womb; and ye mangers, receive Him Who by a word loosed us earthborn from irrational conduct. Ye shepherds, playing upon your pipes, bear witness unto the marvelous wonder; and ye magi from Persia, bring gold, frankincense, and myrrh unto the King: for the Lord was manifested of a Virgin Mother. Before Whom the Mother also, stooping as a handmaid, bowed down, and spake unto Him Whom she held in her arms: How wast Thou sown in me, or how didst Thou sprout forth within me, O my Deliverer and my God?

*Entrance. Prokeimenon of the Day. Three Readings.*
*The Reading from Proverbs. [Composite from Chapters 10, 3, 8]:*[^38]

The memory of the righteous is with praises, and the blessing of the Lord is upon his head. Blessed is the man that found wisdom, and mortal man that knew understanding. For it is better to traffic for her than for treasures of gold and silver. And she is more precious than costly stones, and nothing precious is worthy of her. For length of days and years of life are in her right hand, and in her left hand are riches and glory. Out of her mouth goes forth righteousness, and she bears law and mercy upon her tongue. Give ear therefore unto me, O children, for I will speak honorable things; and blessed is the man that shall keep my ways; for my issues are issues of life, and the will is prepared from the Lord. Therefore I pray you, and utter my voice unto the sons of men: For I, wisdom, built counsel, and understanding, and intellect have I called upon. Mine is counsel and confirmation, mine is understanding, and mine is strength. I love them that love me, and they that seek me shall find grace. Understand craftiness therefore, ye simple; and ye untaught, apply your hearts. Give ear unto me yet again, for I will speak honorable things, and I will open upright things from my lips; for my throat shall meditate truth, and lying lips are an abomination before me. With righteousness are all the words of my mouth: there is nothing crooked or perverse in them. They are all upright to them that understand, and straight to them that find knowledge. For I teach you truth, that your hope may be in the Lord, and that ye may be filled with the Spirit.

[Fol. 23v]
*The Reading from Proverbs. [Chapters 10:7, 6, 31–32; 11:1–12]:*

The mouth of the righteous drops wisdom, but the tongue of the unrighteous shall perish. The lips of righteous men drop graces, but the mouth of the ungodly is perverse. False balances are an abomination before the Lord, but a just weight is acceptable unto Him. Wheresoever insult enters, there also enters dishonor; but the mouth of the humble meditates wisdom. The perfection of the upright shall guide them, but the stumbling of them that deny shall spoil them. Possessions shall not profit in the day of wrath, but righteousness shall deliver from death. When a righteous man dies, he leaves regret; but the destruction of the ungodly is sudden and brings mockery. The righteousness of the blameless directs ways, but unrighteousness falls into impiety. The righteousness of upright men shall deliver them, but the lawless are caught in their lack of counsel. When a righteous man dies, hope perishes not; but the boast of the ungodly shall perish. A righteous man escapes from a snare, and in his stead the ungodly is delivered up. In the mouth of the ungodly is a snare for citizens, but the perception of the righteous is prosperous. In the good things of the righteous a city shall prosper, and at the destruction of the ungodly there is rejoicing. In the blessing of the upright a city shall be exalted, but by the mouth of the ungodly it shall be overthrown. He that is void of understanding mocks citizens, but a wise man keeps silence.

*The Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon. [Chapter 4:7–15]:*

The righteous man, though he happen to die early, shall be in rest. For honorable age is not that which stands in length of time, nor is it measured by number of years. But wisdom is gray hair unto men, and an unspotted life is ripe old age. Having been well-pleasing unto God, he was beloved, and living among sinners, he was translated. He was caught away, lest wickedness should alter his understanding, or deceit beguile his soul. For the bewitching of wickedness darkens good things, and the roving of desire undermines the innocent mind. Being made perfect in a short time, he fulfilled long years; for his soul was pleasing unto the Lord: therefore hastened He from the midst of wickedness. But the peoples saw, and understood not, neither laid they this in mind, that grace and mercy are in His venerable ones, and visitation is among His elect.

*At the Litiya, the Sticheron of the Temple:*
*Then the Stichera of Saint Nicholas, Tone 2. Idiomela.*
*By Byzantios:*

A rule of faith and an image of meekness did Christ God show thee forth unto thy flock [Fol. 24r]
...did Christ God show thee forth unto thy flock, O hierarch Nicholas: while thou indeed exhalest fragrance in Myra, everywhere brightly shine thy divine accomplishments, O defender of orphans and widows. Therefore pray unceasingly that our souls may be saved.

O father Nicholas, the repository of thy relics enriches Myra with myrrh, wherein having appeared in a vision in sleep unto the emperor, thou didst deliver from death, and from bonds, and from prison those who had been unjustly condemned. But even now, as then and always, appear in thy vision, praying for our souls.

O father Nicholas, though the land of Myra be silent, yet the whole world which was enlightened by thee, by the fragrances of myrrh and by multitudes of wonders, cries aloud with hymns of praise; and those condemned who were saved by thee, together with those in Myra, and we, singing cry aloud: Pray that our souls may be saved.

*Tone 4:*

O father Nicholas, being the repository of the myrrh of the All-Holy Spirit: as in Myra thou exhalest fragrance with divine aromas. For having become an imitator of Christ's apostles, thou compassest the universe with the accounts of thy wonders: therefore unto those far off as though near at hand, appearing in sleep thou deliverest from death those who were about to die by unjust judgment, marvelously saving from many perils those who invoke thee. Therefore also deliver us from incoming grievous things, through thy prayers who ever praise thee.

*Tone 8:*

The fruit of thy virtues, O venerable father, hath enlightened the hearts of the faithful. For who that heard of thy boundless humility was not amazed at thy patience? of thy gentleness toward the poor, of thy consolation toward the sorrowful? All things didst thou teach in God-befitting manner, O hierarch Nicholas. And now being crowned with an unfading crown, pray for our souls.

Unto the praise of the Lord didst thou run, O Nicholas, in temporal life, and He glorified thee in the heavens and in true life. Therefore having acquired boldness toward Him, entreat Him that our souls may be saved.

*Glory, Tone 6:*

O good and faithful servant, laborer of Christ's vineyard, thou didst both bear the burden of the day, and didst increase the talent given unto thee, and didst not envy those who came after thee. Therefore the heavenly gates opened unto thee; enter into the joy of thy Lord [Fol. 24v]
...enter into the joy of thy Lord, and pray for us, O holy Nicholas.

*Both now, in the same Tone:*

Triumph, O Zion; rejoice, O Jerusalem, city of Christ God; receive the Creator Who is contained in a cave and in mangers: open unto me the gates, and having entered in I shall see Him Who as an infant is wrapped in swaddling clothes, yet holds creation in His palm. Whom the angels sing with unceasing voice: the Lord and Giver of life, Who saves our race.

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 5. Podoben: "Rejoice" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ):*

Rejoice, O sacred head, pure home of virtues, rule of the most divine priesthood, great shepherd, all-radiant luminary, who bearest the name of victory, mercifully inclined unto them that pray, bending down unto the supplications of the weak, most ready deliverer, saving guardian unto all that faithfully honor thy most glorious memory: entreat Christ, O all-blessed one, to send down great mercy upon the world.

*Verse: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones.*

Rejoice, O most sacred mind, pure dwelling of the Trinity, pillar of the Church, confirmation of the faithful, help unto the overcome, O star that by the beams of thy acceptable prayers ever destroyest the darkness of perils and sorrows, O hierarch Nicholas: quiet haven, wherein those flee who are gripped by the billows of life and are saved: entreat Christ to grant unto our souls great mercy.

*Verse: Thy priests shall clothe themselves with righteousness, and Thy venerable ones shall rejoice.*

Rejoice, thou that wast filled with divine zeal, and by a fearful apparition and warnings in sleep didst deliver from an evil assault those who were unjustly about to die: O fountain that in Myra richly pourest forth myrrh, O Nicholas, watering souls and driving away the foul smells of passions: a sword cutting down the tares of delusion, a winnowing fan dispersing the chaff-like teachings of Arius: entreat Christ to send down great mercy upon our souls.

*Glory, Tone 6. By John the Monk:*

O man of God and faithful servant, minister of the Lord, man of desires, chosen vessel, pillar and confirmation of the Church, heir of the kingdom: keep not silence in crying aloud unto the Lord for us.

*Both now, in the same Tone. By Byzantios:*
*O unwedded Virgin:*[^39]

O unwedded Virgin, whence art thou come? Who is he that bare thee? Who also is thy mother? How bearest thou the Creator in thine arms? How hast thou not suffered corruption in thy womb? O the great, marvelous, and dread mysteries wrought upon thee on earth do we behold, O good maiden! And we prepare a worthy debt for thee: on earth, a cave; and from the heavens we ask that a star be granted; and the Magi come from the east of the earth unto the west, to see the salvation of mankind wrapped in swaddling clothes in a manger.

*At the blessing of the loaves, the Troparion is chanted twice, as written at Small Vespers; and "O Birthgiver of God and Virgin," once.*
