*"A rule of faith," twice; Glory, both now, Theotokion: "The mystery hidden from the ages."*

*After the first Kathisma, Sessional Hymns. Tone 1, Podoben: "Thy Tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й):*
Dwelling in Myra visibly in the flesh, O Hierarch, thou wast shown to be spiritually anointed with mystical myrrh, O father Nicholas. Therefore with the myrrh of thy wonders thou hast made the world fragrant, pouring forth ever-flowing myrrh through thy fragrant, myrrh-bearing words and through thy memory.

*Glory...*
Thou shinest upon the earth with the rays of thy wonders, O wise Nicholas, and thou movest every tongue unto the glory and praise of Him Who glorified thee on earth. Him do thou entreat that they who honor thy memory with faith and love may be delivered from every necessity, O chosen one of the fathers.

*Both now, Theotokion:*
O all-immaculate, pure Maiden, by the Divine Spirit thou hast conceived in thy womb the Creator, God, and Fashioner of all, and without corruption hast thou given birth to Him; glorifying Him, we sing thy praise, O Virgin, as the palace of the King of all and the defense of the world.

*After the second Kathisma, Sessional Hymns. Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared today" (Ꙗ҆ви́лсѧ є҆сѝ):*
Thou intercedest for the faithful, protecting and preserving them, O blessed one, manifestly delivering them from every sorrow, O fairest glory and boast of hierarchs, venerable Nicholas.

*Glory... Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom and Word" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
Having received a fountain of wonders from the Lord, O wise father, thou pourest forth honey-flowing waters unto all the faithful, O blessed one; for as a true shepherd and preacher of the faith, thou hast kept the words of the true Shepherd. Therefore, having boldness toward Him, thou didst save men from death, O blessed hierarch Nicholas. Pray to Christ God that He grant remission of sins unto them that honor thy holy memory with love.

*Both now, Theotokion:*
Having fallen into the mire of sins, and having no firm footing, the tempest of transgressions sorely drowns me; but as thou hast given birth unto the Word of the only Lover of mankind, look down upon me thy servant, and deliver me from every sin, and from soul-corrupting passions, and from every affliction of the deceitful murderer, O unwedded Birthgiver of God; pray to Christ God that He grant me remission of sins; for I, thy servant, have placed my hope in thee.

*After the Polyeleos, Sessional Hymns. Tone 5, Podoben: "Word Co-Beginningless" (Собезнача́льное сло́во):*
Let us all piously praise with faith the all-wise hierarch Nicholas, the God-bearer, as a fervent helper and protector from God in afflictions and sorrows; for he prays unto the Lord on behalf of them that keep and sing with faith his divine memory.

*Glory... Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily Anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*
Thou wast shown to be a most fervent protector of the Church of Christ, O Nicholas, and with boldness didst thou overthrow the godless doctrines of the heresies, and thou wast shown unto all to be a rule of orthodoxy; praying for all who follow thy divine teachings and admonition.

*Both now, Theotokion:*
Speedily receive our prayers, O Sovereign Lady, and bear them unto thy Son and God, O all-immaculate Lady; deliver from tribulations them that run to thee; crush the craftiness, and cast down the audacity of the godless who arm themselves against thy servants, O all-pure one.

*Gradual Hymns, the 1st Antiphon of Tone 4.*
*Prokeimenon, Tone 4: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His saints. Verse: What shall I render unto the Lord for all that He hath rendered unto me?*
*Let every breath praise the Lord.*
*Gospel according to John, Pericope 36.*[^40]

*After Psalm 50, Sticheron, Tone 6:*
O heir of God, companion of Christ, minister of the Lord, holy Nicholas: according to thy name, so also was thy life; for understanding blossomed forth with gray hair; the brightness of thy countenance bore witness to the simplicity of thy soul; the quietness of thy speech confirmed thy meekness; thy life was glorious, and thy dormition was with the saints; pray for our souls.

*The Canon of the Birthgiver of God with the Heirmos on 6; and two Canons of the Saint on 8.*
*The Canon of the Birthgiver of God, Tone 4. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Let us all sing a song of victory unto God, Who hath wrought marvelous wonders with a high arm, and saved Israel, for He hath been glorified.

*Troparion:*
O pure one, who hast given birth unto the Abyss of Wisdom, send down upon me drops of wisdom, a fountain pouring forth grace, that I may hymn the deep sea of thy graces.

*Troparion:*
I hymn thee, O all-hymned one, whom the ranks of angels hymn, as having given birth unto the all-hymned God, Whom all creation praises, for He hath been glorified.

*Another Canon of the Saint, whose acrostic is: "Unto thee, O Nicholas, do I sing a divine song." The composition of Theophanes.[^41] Tone 2. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
The overpowered army of Pharaoh did the armed might once cast down into the deep; and the incarnate Word destroyed all-wicked sin, the most glorified Lord, for He hath been gloriously glorified.

*Troparion:*
Standing crown-bearing before the throne of Christ, O all-wise Nicholas, with the angelic armies, grant me illumination brightening the darkness of my soul, that with joy I may praise thy most blessed memory.

*Troparion:*
The Lord, Who glorifies all them that glorify Him, hath given thee as a refuge unto the faithful, delivering from afflictions them that flee unto thy protection, O Nicholas, and call upon thee with faith and love, O most glorious one.

*Theotokion:*
Having cast into me the desire to be equal to the Fashioner, the all-crafty serpent snatched me away as a captive; but through thee, O all-pure one, have I been recalled, and most truly deified; for thou, O Mother of God, hast given birth unto Him Who deified me.

*Another Canon in alphabetical acrostic, excluding the Trinity hymns and Theotokia.[^42] Tone 1. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Christ is born, give ye glory; Christ from the heavens, go ye to meet Him; Christ on earth, be ye lifted up! Sing unto the Lord, all the earth; and in gladness chant, O ye people, for He hath been glorified.

*Troparion:*
With perplexed tongue and lips have I come, O Nicholas, to offer a small praise and supplication unto thine excellence that imitates God; but do thou, as a bountiful giver, grant me the Savior and God to be merciful.

Being an earthly man, thou wast shown to be equal unto the angels upon earth, a ready protector of widows, an avenger of the oppressed, and a helper unto all that are afflicted in misfortunes, O father Nicholas.

*Troparion:*
The whole universe declares, O thrice-blessed Nicholas, the ocean of the wonders of thy virtues: the poor proclaim thee their defender, the orphans and widows their nourisher, the blind their guide, and all their champion.

*Triadicon:*
I honor the uncreated Trinity, the Father and the Son with the Spirit: simple Essence, Godhead, undivided Nature in essence, dividing the three Hypostases personally and according to hypostasis.

*Theotokion:*
Seedlessly hast thou conceived the Word, One of the Trinity, O all-immaculate one, and in the flesh hast thou given birth unto Him, remaining a virgin after childbirth even as before; Him, as thy Son and God, do thou ever entreat for us.

*Katavasia: Christ is born...*

*The Canon of the Birthgiver of God, Tone 4. Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Let my heart be established in Thy will, O Christ God, Who didst establish the second heaven above the waters, and didst found the earth upon the waters, O All-powerful One.

*Troparion:*
A heaven most honorable, a dwelling-place of the Church, truly breathing with grace, and a fragrant paradise, the hope of Christians, do I praise as my Birthgiver of God.

*Troparion:*
By the word hast thou given birth unto the Word, Who by His word brought all rational together with irrational nature into being, delivering men from irrationality, O all-blessed one.

*Another Canon of the Saint, Tone 2. Ode 3. Heirmos:*
The wilderness hath blossomed as a lily, O Lord, the barren church of the Gentiles by Thy coming, wherein my heart hath been established.

*Troparion:*
O blessed Nicholas, having been a true disciple of the Master, thou savest them that flee unto thee from cruel tribulations and bitter death.

*Troparion:*
Cleanse Thy servants, granting remission of sins as Thou art good, through the intercessions of Nicholas Thy servant unto Thee, O Most Merciful One.

*Theotokion:*
Assuage the tumult of my soul, O all-pure one, and pilot my life, O good one who hast given birth unto God, in Whom my heart hath been established.

*Another Canon of the Saint, Tone 1. Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Unto the Son begotten of the Father without corruption before the ages, and in these latter days incarnate seedlessly of the Virgin, Christ God, let us cry aloud: Thou Who hast lifted up our horn, holy art Thou, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Having acquired in thy heart a tablet of many virtues, written by the immortal and all-pure finger of Christ God, O Nicholas: thou pourest forth sweetness from thy lips more than honey and the honeycomb.

*Troparion:*
Grace hath shown forth wonders most gloriously in thee, O Nicholas; for thy pure life, truly brighter than gold, illumines darkened souls with the radiance of the Divine Spirit.

*Troparion:*
Appearing even after death, manifestly showing thyself in dreams, thou didst gloriously deliver the youths from death, crying manifestly unto the king: Do no wrong unto the men slandered by counsel of envy!

*Triadicon:*
Be Thou my supplication, O all-holy Trinity, our God, unto me who have defiled my life by immeasurable transgressions: O living Father, Son, and Spirit, preserving me from every side, and ever unhurt by affliction.

*Theotokion:*
Thou givest the hope of salvation unto thy servants, O Birthgiver of God; stand forth to preserve and help in necessities and afflictions with swift-flowing prayers; for thou art our boast, O faithful, Ever-virgin.

*Katavasia: Unto the Son begotten of the Father...*

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom and Word" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
Having ascended unto the height of virtues, and from thence being illuminated with the divine rays of wonders, O father, thou wast truly shown to be a most radiant shepherd unto the world, being an invincible protector unto us in afflictions. Therefore having gloriously conquered the enemy, thou didst drive away falsehood, and saved men from death, O Nicholas; pray to Christ God that He grant remission of sins unto them that honor thy holy memory with love.

*Glory... Another Sessional Hymn, in the same Tone:*
The abyss of mercy hath shown thee, O Nicholas, to be a river abundantly pouring forth healings, and an inexhaustible fountain of wonders; for they who are bitterly crushed with heavy infirmities, and sorely tormented by life's misfortunes, truly find thy fervent protection to be a healing medicine for every sorrow. For this cause we cry unto thee: Pray to Christ God that He grant remission of sins unto them that celebrate thy holy memory with love.

*Both now, Theotokion:*
As a Virgin, and the only one among women, who hast seedlessly given birth unto God in the flesh, all generations of mankind call thee blessed; for the fire of the Godhead dwelt within thee, and as an infant thou sucklest the Fashioner and Lord. Therefore we, the angelic and human race, worthily glorify thy most holy childbearing, and with one accord cry unto thee: Pray to Christ God that He grant remission of sins unto them that with faith bow down before thy most holy childbearing.

*The Canon of the Birthgiver of God, Tone 4. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Foreseeing in the Spirit the incarnation of the Word, O Prophet Habbakuk, thou didst proclaim, crying aloud: When the years draw nigh, Thou shalt be known; when the time is come, Thou shalt be shown forth; glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Eve indeed became the cause of death unto mortals by the counsel of the serpent; but thou, O pure Virgin, having given birth by the word unto the Word, wast shown to be the mediatress of immortality and life. Therefore worthily do we hymn thee.

*Troparion:*
Foreseeing thee in the Spirit, O pure one, the prophets prefigured thee in riddles as a mountain, a gate, a table, a holy ark, a lampstand, a throne of life, an urn,[^43] and a couch, the Mother of God; the fulfillment whereof we now behold.

*Another Canon of the Saint, Tone 2. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Thou hast come forth from the Virgin, neither an ambassador nor an angel, but Thyself incarnate, O Lord, and hast saved all of me, a man; therefore I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Having purely drawn near unto the spiritual radiances, thou becamest a light-bearer, illuminating the ends of the world, interceding for all, and saving all who run with faith unto thee.

*Troparion:*
As thou didst formerly appear, O venerable Nicholas, delivering the youths from death, so also now save me from every distress, affliction, and calamity, O all-blessed one.

*Troparion:*
Thou hast shone forth with the radiances of virtues, O all-blessed one, having become an excellent imitator of thy Master, and thou savest them that call upon thee, who glorify thee with reverence and love.

*Theotokion:*
The Master of creation came upon thee, becoming incarnate, and saving all of me, a man, as He is tender-hearted; therefore, O faithful, we glorify thee as the Birthgiver of God.

*Another Canon of the Saint, Tone 1. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
A rod from the root of Jesse, and a blossom from him, O Christ, hast Thou budded forth from the Virgin; from the mountain overshadowed and dense, the Praised One, Thou hast come incarnate from her who knew not man, immaterial and God: glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Thy name alone, when truly called upon, speedily delivers from all the counsels of the enemy them that cry warmly unto thee:

warmly, O holy Nicholas: as thou didst formerly deliver the generals, save us also from every cruel affliction.

*Troparion:*
Standing before the throne of God, cease not, O wise one, to pray fervently on behalf of all of us thy faithful servants, O marvelous Nicholas, that we may be delivered from eternal fire, and from enemies, a deceitful tongue, and affliction.

*Troparion:*
Thou pourest forth healings everywhere unto them that flee unto thee with faith, and deliverest all from bonds; therefore turn our sorrow into joy by thy God-pleasing prayers, O most radiant Nicholas, casting down the pride of our enemies.

*Triadicon:*
I honor the Father as the Origin of the unoriginate Godhead, and the Son, and I revere the all-holy Spirit: the all-creating Cause of all things, single, undivided, ever divided in three characters and persons, one undivided Kingdom.

*Theotokion:*
Truly thou art more honorable than earthly and heavenly beings, thou alone, O Birthgiver of God; for thou hast conceived in thy womb the Creator of all, clad in material flesh, having given birth seedlessly. O newly-fashioned vision!

*Katavasia: A rod from the root of Jesse...*

*The Canon of the Birthgiver of God, Tone 4. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Shine forth unto us the bright, ever-existing Light, as we rise early unto the judgments of Thy commandments, O Master, Lover of mankind, Christ our God.

*Troparion:*
As an ark of honorable consecration, and as a holy fire-like throne, and as a consecrated palace, O Sovereign Lady, thou hast contained God the Ruler of all.

*Troparion:*
A Mother knowing not man among virgins, thou wast shown again to be a virgin among mothers, thou alone all-pure; for ineffably hast thou given birth unto God, Who created nature.

*Another Canon of the Saint, Tone 2. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Illumination of them that lie in darkness, salvation of the despairing, O Christ my Savior: early do I rise unto Thee, O King of peace; enlighten me with Thy brightness, for besides Thee I know no other God.

*Troparion:*
Illumined by a life worthy of God, O thrice-blessed one, thou didst stand forth and deliver them condemned to die by an unjust sentence, who cried unto the Master Christ: For besides Thee we know no other God.

*Troparion:*
Now beholding the ever-existing glory in the heavens, and enjoying the brightest splendors of the ineffable and divine radiances, shelter me with thy protection, O venerable one, all-honored servant of Christ.

*Theotokion:*
That Thou mightest seek out Thine image buried by passions, O Savior, being hidden from heavenly hosts and incarnate of the Virgin, Thou hast appeared unto them that cry unto Thee: For besides Thee we know no other God.

*Another Canon of the Saint, Tone 1. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
As Thou art the God of peace and Father of mercies, Thou hast sent unto us the Angel of Thy Great Counsel, granting peace; therefore guided unto the light of the knowledge of God, rising early out of the night, we glorify Thee, O Lover of mankind.

*Troparion:*
The most great metropolis of Myra, and the eparchy of Lycia, and all fatherlands now preach thy wonders, O father, thy marvelous deeds, whereby thou deliverest all from illnesses and sorrows, O God-blessed Nicholas.

*Troparion:*
Being the nourisher of widows, and the father of orphans, a most excellent helper unto them that are in sorrows, consolation unto the weeping, shepherd and guide unto all that go astray, O Nicholas: deliver us also from tribulations by thy prayers.

*Troparion:*
Thou hast passed away from earth unto the immaterial mansions, where thou beholdest the ineffable beauty of Christ, and wast shown to be a companion of the angelic hosts; therefore rejoicing with the apostles and with the martyrs, O father Nicholas, pray fervently unto the Master of all on our behalf.

*Triadicon:*
Co-beginningless Trinity, sharing the single throne of the one Godhead, I manifestly glorify Thy sovereign Persons, through Whom I was brought into being out of nothingness, crying with the angels: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O Lord!

*Theotokion:*
Salvation and hope of all men, who alone dost anticipate and save, help us also now who cry unto thee, O pure one, and call upon thee ever in cruel tribulations; for next to God, we have no other protector than thee.

*Katavasia: As Thou art the God of peace...*

*The Canon of the Birthgiver of God, Tone 4. Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Imitating the Prophet Jonah, I cry aloud: Deliver my life from corruption, O Good One, and save me, O Savior of the world, who cry: Glory to Thee!

*Troparion:*
Protection of the faithful, and joyful gladness of the sorrowful: enrich thy servants who desire thy defense with spiritual joy.

*Troparion:*
Rational heaven, all-pure temple, holy ark, most fair paradise of God, wherein is the Tree of my life, let her be hymned.

*Another Canon of the Saint, Tone 2. Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Wallowing in the abyss of sins, I call upon the unsearchable abyss of Thy mercy: bring me up from corruption, O God!

*Troparion:*
The crown of victory hath worthily been placed upon thy head, O Nicholas; therefore, as a most excellent victor, save them that call upon thee.

*Troparion:*
Slain as I am by transgressions, O blessed one, and engulfed by the billows of passions: appear and save me unto the haven of the divine will.

*Theotokion:*
And upon thee have I set the hopes of my salvation, O Mother, Ever-virgin, and thee do I place as a firm and unshakable protector of my life.

*Another Canon of the Saint, Tone 1. Ode 6. Heirmos:*
The monster of the deep disgorged Jonah unharmed from its womb, even as it had received him; and the Word, having dwelt within the Virgin and taken flesh, came forth preserving her incorrupt; for not having suffered corruption Himself, He kept her that bare Him uninjured.

*Troparion:*
Thou wast shown to be a new Abraham, O Nicholas, for thou hast now brought thine only-begotten son unto thy Master, ever offering unbloody sacrifices; therefore thou wast blessed as a lover of strangers, O father, and becamest a divine and blameless dwelling-place of the Trinity.

*Troparion:*
Strange and terrifying wonders dost thou work throughout the whole earth, O Nicholas, and for them in distress far off at sea, interceding with swift-running prayers: a physician unto the infirm, a nourisher unto the poor, shown forth as "victory of the people"[^44] unto the faithful people.

*Troparion:*
Foreseeing the future with the eye of the mind, thou hast filled all ends of the earth with right doctrines, proclaiming unto us the Son consubstantial with the Father; thou didst destroy the madness of Arius, setting forth thy venerable accomplishments as a pillar of the orthodox faith.

*Triadicon:*
I honor and revere the undivided Trinity, ever divided into three Persons, yet united in essence and nature: as one Principle, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, sovereignly ruling over all things and preserving all things according as It wills.

*Theotokion:*
Wholly incarnate in thy womb, O all-pure one, Christ God was born without seed; for He could not endure to behold the creation of His hands tormented by the deceiver; He came in the form of a servant to deliver mankind.

*Katavasia: The monster of the deep Kontakion, Tone 3, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дв҃а дне́сь):*
In Myra, O holy one, thou wast shown to be a priest; for having fulfilled the Gospel of Christ, O venerable one, thou didst lay down thy life for thy people, and didst save the innocent from death; therefore thou hast been sanctified as a great initiate of the grace of God.

*Ikos:*
Let us now praise with holy songs the shepherd and teacher of the people of Myra, that we may be enlightened by his prayers; for behold, he was shown to be wholly pure, incorrupt in spirit, offering unto Christ a sacrifice blameless, pure, and well-pleasing unto God, as a holy priest, purified both in soul and body; therefore being truly the protector and champion of this Church, as a great initiate of the grace of God.

*The Canon of the Birthgiver of God, Tone 4. Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The furnace, O Savior, was bedewed, and the youths rejoicing sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
The Most High hath shown thee forth, O pure one, as an animate heaven, a bridal chamber graced with beauty, a gold-like purple robe, and paradise.

*Troparion:*
Establish the tossing of my mind, and strengthen my troubled thoughts upon the immovable rock by thy protection, O Virgin Mother!

*Another Canon of the Saint, Tone 2. Ode 7. Heirmos:*
When the golden image was worshipped on the plain of Dura, Thy three youths disregarded the godless command; and cast into the midst of the fire, being bedewed, they sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
I have fallen into sharp temptation, and being sorely pierced, and having drawn nigh unto the gates of hades, smitten with sorrows: save me by thy prayers, O blessed one, and raise me up, who sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Shining with the immaterial rays of the unwaning Light, snatch away them that are afflicted in the darkness of sorrows, and guide unto the enlightenment of gladness them that sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
Pray to Christ thy Son and God, O Virgin Birthgiver of God, that they who were sold by cruel transgressions and the deceits of the serpent may be redeemed by His precious blood, who sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Another Canon of the Saint, Tone 1. Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The youths, brought up together in piety, disregarding the command of the ungodly, and not fearing the threatening of the fire, not fearing the threatening of the fire, but standing in the midst of the flame, they sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Shown forth as the most excellent physician of every cruel disease, O father Nicholas, heal the infirmity of my soul and grant me good health, to cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Having of old delivered the generals from death, O holy one, thou didst also raise them up to sing and glorify Christ the Savior with warm faith, who also cried: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Drawing near mystically unto the cup of wisdom, with thy lips, O father Nicholas, thou hast drawn forth drops of rain, sweeter than honey and the honeycomb, commanding the people to cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Triadicon:*
O Trinity, we sing of Thee, a Unity most radiant in three lights, consubstantial: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit; in Whom we all were baptized, we sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
As thou art higher than all creatures, O Birthgiver of God, pray to thy Son and God, that they who truly honor and glorify thee may be delivered from torment: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Katavasia: The youths, brought up together in piety...*

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Him Whom the angels and all the hosts dread as Creator and Lord, hymn, O priests; glorify, O youths; bless, O peoples, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
As an animate bridal chamber and divinely-inspired scarlet robe, a mantle dyed scarlet for the King of all, hast thou appeared, O Virgin, and a purple robe, from which the flesh of the God-man Word shone forth together.

*Troparion:*
Thou hast conceived, O all-pure one, Him Who holds all creation in His fist, as Maker and God, ineffably, incomprehensibly, Who for our sake became man like unto us, and departed not from that which He was.

*Another Canon, Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Unto God Who descended into the fiery furnace unto the Hebrew youths, and changed the flame into dew, hymn His works as the Lord, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
As thou art good and compassionate, deliver them that are cruelly held in the abyss of misfortunes, O blessed Nicholas, granting release by thy prayers from the cruel evils that hold them, which thou offerest unto Christ the Savior, O initiate of sacred mysteries, O initiate of sacred mysteries.

*Troparion:*
Mystic guide of things beyond understanding, minister of holy things, and being heavenly, O divinely-wise one, and a faithful high priest: ask remission of transgressions from our Savior, O consecrated revelator.

*Theotokion:*
My mind now fails, having fallen into the abyss of dishonor, for I am encompassed on all sides by diverse evils; but do thou heal me, O Virgin, clothing me with the light of dispassion.

*Another Canon, Ode 8. Heirmos:*
The furnace moist with dew prefigured the image of a supernatural wonder; for it burned not the youths whom it received, even as the fire of the Godhead consumed not the Virgin's womb into which It entered. Therefore in song let us sing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
The ranks of patriarchs, and apostles, and the assemblies of hieromartyrs, and the choir of prophets, the whole assembly of fasters bless thy divine life; with whom we also cry: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
O supreme Sovereign King, of great dominion, through the prayers of the venerable shepherd pacify the life of all Christians, O Word, fighting against the barbarians for our pious King,[^45] that with him we may cry unto Thee, O Christ: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Illumined with unapproachable Light, O father, thou enlightenest the souls of them that are in affliction, destroying all the gloomy darkness of temptations, and shining upon our hearts with gladness, whereby shining from afar we cry: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages!

*Triadicon:*
Life and lives, and One and three Lights, we faithfully sing of the Trinity, following the paternal, divine, true teachings: Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit; with Whom being pious let us sing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
A marvelous, strange wonder did the bush prefigure of old on Mount Sinai, burning without being consumed, O pure Maiden, portraying the mystery of thy childbearing; for the fire of the Godhead, having dwelt within thee, preserved thee unhurt; Whom we sing of unto all ages.

*Katavasia: The furnace moist with dew prefigured...*

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
The life-receiving, ever-flowing spring, the light-bearing lamp of grace, the animate temple, the all-pure tabernacle, more spacious than heaven and earth, the Birthgiver of God, do we the faithful magnify.

*Troparion:*
Pour forth upon me a stream of thy grace, O thou that pourest forth grace, for I am scorched by the flame of calamities and cruelly afflicted, O thou that didst give birth unto the River of goodness, whereof he that drinks shall never thirst.

*Troparion:*
As the fair bridal chamber of the Bridegroom, as the animate palace of the Master, as the divinely-woven purple, as the most beautiful dwelling-place of Christ, O Sovereign Lady of all, save me who implore thee.

*Another Canon, Ode 9. Heirmos:*
The Son of the unoriginate Father, God and Lord, incarnate of the Virgin, hath appeared unto us, to enlighten them that are in darkness, to gather the dispersed; therefore the all-hymned Birthgiver of God do we magnify.

*Troparion:*
Illumined with the torches of grace, O divinely-wise one, thou wast shown forth plainly to be a lamp of piety; thou savest them that are in misfortunes, and deliverest them that are in the depth of the sea, and feedest the hungry marvelously, O all-blessed one.

*Troparion:*
Dwelling now in the paradise of delight, and clearly beholding the ineffable glory, from the heavenly spheres thou lookest down upon thy singers, delivering them from passions, O all-blessed God-bearer.

*Theotokion:*
The Wisdom, and Power, and hypostatic Word of the Father, O pure Mother of God, hast thou borne, Who from thy most pure blood received His temple, and was united unto it in indivisible union.

*Another Canon, Ode 9. Heirmos:*
A strange and most marvelous mystery do I behold: the cave is heaven; the cherubic throne, the Virgin; the manger, the place wherein the uncontainable Christ God lay down; Whom singing, we magnify.

*Troparion:*
Let us rejoice spiritually, all ye that love the feast; let the heavens be glad, and the mountains and hills of the Church, and the choirs of virgins, and the splendor of fasters, in the memory of the all-blessed one; wherein having come together, we magnify the Savior.

*Troparion:*
Let all the ends of the earth sing unceasingly with hymns, adorning with crowns of praise the head of Nicholas, the servant of Christ God; by whose prayers may we be delivered from passions and calamities.

*Troparion:*
Accept, O Nicholas, this hymn of my small labor as worthy, even as Christ accepted the two mites of the widow; abhor not the wretched one passions; for not boasting, O thrice-blessed one, have I dared.

*Triadicon:*
The Trinity is united by consubstantial will, and is again divided hypostatically without division, ever preserving dominion: Father, Son, and living Spirit: one God in three Hypostases, Whom we magnify.

*Theotokion:*
All sorrow was done away with by thy childbearing, and the Lord hath taken away weeping and mourning, and every tear from every face of the earthborn, O pure Birthgiver of God that knewest not wedlock; concerning thee we also fulfill our debts.

*Katavasia: A strange and most marvelous mystery...*

*Exapostilarion, Tone 2, Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Жє́ны оу҆слы́шите):*
Let us all praise the great archpastor and hierarch, Nicholas the primate of Myra in Lycia; for he saved many men about to die unjustly, and appearing in a vision in sleep unto the emperor and Avlavius, he revoked the unjust sentence.

*Glory...*
Greatly did the Lord glorify thee in wonders, both in life and after thy demise, O hierarch Nicholas; for who that only calls upon thy holy name out of love of faith is not immediately heard? He finds thee a fervent defender.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
Having given birth unto the hypostatic Wisdom, and the superessential Word, and Christ the Physician of all, O Virgin: heal the cruel and long-enduring festerings and wounds of my soul, and put to death the passionate thoughts of my heart.

*At the Praises, Stichera on 6, Tone 1. Idiomela:*
Having looked steadfastly unto the height of understanding, and perceived the hidden depth of wisdom, thou didst enrich the world with thy teachings, O father; ever pray unto Christ God on our behalf, O hierarch Nicholas.

*Sticheron:*
O man of God and faithful servant, steward of His mysteries, and man of spiritual desires, animate pillar and divinely-inspired image: for as a divine treasure the church of Myra received thee with wonder, and as an intercessor for our souls.

*Other Stichera, Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Нбⷭныхъ чинѡ́въ):*
Flying about the flowers of the Church like a bird of the former angelic nest, O thrice-blessed Nicholas, ever crying unto God on behalf of all of us who are in pressing misfortunes and temptations, thou deliverest us by thy prayers.

*Sticheron:*
The beauty of the sacred vestments thou didst make most radiant by active virtues, O God-bearing father; therefore thou performest sacred wonders for us, O sacred performer of glorious miracles, delivering us from cruel afflictions.

*Sticheron:*
Passing through the beauties of things invisible, thou didst comprehend that awesome glory of the saints, O holy one; therefore thou revealest unto us heavenly words of those ever-living visions, O most sacred father.

*Sticheron:*
As thou didst appear in a dream unto the pious emperor, and didst deliver the prisoners from death, O father, pray unceasingly that now also through thy prayers we may be delivered from temptations and misfortunes and illnesses, who worthily praise thee.

*Glory... Tone 5:*
Let us sound the trumpet of song, let us leap for the feast, and dance with rejoicing in the prayerful solemnity of the God-bearing father! Let kings and princes come together, and let them hymn him who through an awesome apparition in a dream persuaded the emperor to release the three generals held innocently; pastors and teachers, let us come together and praise the shepherd who is a fellow-emulator of the Good Shepherd: the physician unto them that are in infirmities, the deliverer unto them that are in misfortunes, the defender of sinners, the treasury of the poor, the consoler of them that are in sorrows, the companion of travelers, the pilot of them at sea; and praising the great hierarch who everywhere warmly anticipates help, let us speak thus: O most holy Nicholas, come quickly, and deliver us from the present misfortune, and save thy flock by thy prayers!

*Now and ever, Theotokion, Tone 5, Podoben: "Let us sound the trumpet of song" (Вострꙋ́бимъ трꙋбо́ю пѣ́сней). The work of Patriarch Germanus:[^46]*
Let us sound the trumpet of song: for looking down from on high, the Queen of all, the Virgin Mother, crowns with blessings them that hymn her! Let kings and princes come together, and let them clap their hands in hymns unto the Queen that bare the King, Who of His love for mankind was well pleased to loose them that were formerly held by death; pastors and teachers, let us come together and praise the most pure Mother of the Good Shepherd: the golden lampstand, the light-bearing cloud, more spacious than the heavens, the animate ark, the fiery throne of the Master, the golden urn that received the manna, the closed gate of the Word, the refuge of all Christians; praising her with God-proclaiming hymns, let us speak thus: O palace of the Word, account us humble ones worthy of the heavenly kingdom; for nothing is impossible unto thine intercession.

*The Great Doxology, and the Dismissal.*
*Oil is also given to the brethren from the lamp of the saint, and the First Hour.*
*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes from the first canon, Ode 3; and from the second canon, Ode 6.*
*Prokeimenon, Tone 7:* The righteous man shall be glad in the Lord, and shall hope in Him. *Verse:* Hear my voice, O God...
*The Epistle to the Hebrews, Pericope 335 (Heb. 13:17–21).*[^47]
*Alleluia, Tone 4:* Thy priests shall be clothed with righteousness...
*The Gospel according to Luke, Pericope 24 (Luke 6:17–23).*[^48]
*Communion Hymn:* In everlasting remembrance...

*In the same month, on the 7th day: Our Father among the Saints Ambrose, Bishop of Milan. Alleluia, or Troparion:*
*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of Ambrose, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Нбⷭныхъ чинѡ́въ):*

*Sticheron:*
Adorning the throne of priesthood with virtues, through divine inspiration thou didst worthily receive the hierarchical office; therefore, having been a faithful steward of grace in both, O Ambrose, thou hast inherited a twofold crown.

*Sticheron:*
In abstinence and afflictions, and in many vigils and fervent prayers, thou didst purify soul and body, O divinely-wise one; therefore thou wast shown forth as a chosen vessel unto Christ God, and appearing equal unto the apostles, thou didst receive their gifts.

*Sticheron:*
When the pious emperor formerly sinned, thou didst boldly rebuke him as Nathan rebuked David, O all-blessed Ambrose; thou didst openly impose a holy excommunication, and having instructed him in God-befitting repentance, thou didst reunite him unto thy flock.[^49]

*Other Stichera of the Birthgiver of God (if Alleluia is sung, these stichera are sung first).*
*Tone and Podoben the same (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*
By the oil of thine intercession, O pure Birthgiver of God, drive away the bestial passions of my wretched soul, and guiding me peaceably from hence unto life and guiding me, reckon me unto the holy flock of thine elect sheep.

*Troparion:*
As thou art the helper of helpless men, as thou art the hope of all the hopeless, a release in cruel evils, O Birthgiver of God: be a helper unto me, delivering me from sins and misfortunes, as thou art merciful, O all-pure one.

*Troparion:*
Extinguish with divine dew, by thy willing raining, O Virgin, the fiery surges of my soul-destroying passions; that I also, like the youths, may give thanks unto God Who was born of thee, and glorify and bless thy grace, O Birthgiver of God.

*Glory... and now and ever, of the same, in the same tone and podoben (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*
Having slipped by corrupt ways, I lie prostrate, and flee unto thy calmness, O Virgin; from the adverse storm and manifold temptations deliver me, that I may unceasingly sing of thy grace, O Birthgiver of God, Ever-virgin Mother.

*Staurotheotokion, Podoben the same (Подо́бенъ то́йже):*
Standing by the Cross of thy Son and God, and beholding His long-suffering, the pure Mother said, weeping: Woe is me, O sweetest Child! Why dost Thou suffer these things unjustly, O Word of God, that Thou mayest save mankind?

*At the Aposticha, from the Octoechos.*

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
A rule of faith, an image of meekness, a teacher of abstinence did the truth of things show thee forth unto thy flock; therefore thou didst acquire high things by humility, rich things by poverty, O father Ambrose: entreat Christ God that our souls may be saved.

*At Matins, both canons from the Octoechos, and the canon of the saint on 4; whose acrostic is: "I will praise the great Ambrose." The work of Joseph. Tone 4.*[^50]

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Having traversed the Red Sea's deep with unwetted feet, ancient Israel of old, by the cross-shaped hands of Moses, conquered the power of Amalek in the wilderness.

*Troparion:*
Illumined with divine lightnings, O venerable one, with thy prayers enlighten them that piously honor thy radiant, light-bearing, and holy dormition.

*Troparion:*
The Word of God granted thee a word of wisdom adorned with true knowledge, O hierarch Ambrose, driving away the irrational malice of heretics.

*Troparion:*
Having pre-purified the contemplative part of thy mind from passionate gloom, thou didst make it receptive of the pure splendors of the All-Holy Spirit, O all-blessed one.

*Troparion:*
By thy most wise and sacred doctrines, driving away the Arian plague like a shepherd, on the pasture of orthodoxy hast thou pastured thy rational sheep in faith, O most wise one.

*Theotokion:*
Without seed, by the Father's will, from the divine Spirit of God hast thou conceived the Son, and in the flesh hast thou borne Him, Who is motherless from the Father, and for our sake fatherless from thee.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Not in wisdom, nor in power, nor in riches do we boast, but in Thee, the Father's hypostatic Wisdom, O Christ; for there is none holy save Thee, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
Having received great grace and power from God, by thy sensible touch thou didst heal diverse passions of them that came unto thee, O father Ambrose.

*Troparion:*
Instructed as a divine hierarch, O venerable one, every meaning of Scripture that was hard to understand hast thou clearly elucidated unto them that knew not, O father Ambrose.

*Troparion:*
When an unclean woman rushed forward foolishly and boldly to draw near unto thee who shinest with spiritual wisdom, thou didst speedily cause her to die by divine rebuke.[^51]

*Theotokion:*
Thou hast renewed the human race, having alone given birth unto the Maker and Lord of our nature; therefore we glorify thee, O full of God's grace.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom and Word" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
Emulating the zeal of the Prophet Elijah and likewise of John the Baptist, thou didst courageously rebuke the emperor who acted lawlessly, O hierarch; thou didst divinely adorn the throne, and didst enrich the world with a multitude of wonders; therefore also instructed by the divine Scriptures, thou didst confirm the faithful and convert the unbelieving, O hierarch Ambrose: pray to Christ God that He grant remission of transgressions unto them that celebrate thy holy memory with love.

*Glory... and now and ever, Theotokion:*
Having slipped by evil thoughts, I have fallen into the depth of sin; and groaning I cry unto thee from my heart, O all-pure one: make marvelous upon me thy rich mercy, and the unmeasurable deep of thy compassion, and the unsearchable riches of thy bounties; and grant me repentance, and forgiveness of transgressions, that with love I may cry unto thee: Pray to Christ God that He grant remission of transgressions unto me; for in thee do I thy servant have hope.

*Staurotheotokion:*
The ewe-lamb, beholding the Lamb and Shepherd and Deliverer upon the Cross, cried out weeping, and bitterly lamenting cried aloud: The world indeed rejoices, receiving redemption through Thee, but my womb burns, beholding Thy crucifixion, which Thou endurest through the tender compassion of mercy, O long-suffering Lord! O abyss of mercy and inexhaustible fountain, have compassion and grant remission of transgressions unto them that sing in faith of Thy divine passions!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
For the sake of the love of Thine image, O Bountiful One, Thou didst stand upon Thy Cross, and the nations melted away; for Thou, O Lover of mankind, art my strength and praise!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst show thyself to be a hierarch, anointed with the myrrh of priesthood, consecrating priests, granting unto all saving purification.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst preserve thy flock from all harm of the adversaries, O blessed one, and didst darken all the deceit of Arius by the radiance of thy words.

*Troparion:*
Fenced about with the power of Christ, O all-blessed one, thou drivest away evil spirits of malice, which cannot endure thy rebuke.

*Theotokion:*
He Who formed all things by His will is willingly fashioned from thy pure blood, saving them that acknowledge thee as the pure Mother of God.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Thou, my Lord, art come as a light into the world, a holy light, turning back from gloomy ignorance them that sing of Thee with faith.

*Troparion:*
Having acquired a mind shining with immaterial light, thou didst flash forth the rays of healings and wonders, O blessed Ambrose.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst build thyself up as a sacred dwelling of the Spirit, and didst demolish the temples of idols, O divinely-inspired Ambrose.

*Troparion:*
Emperors were put to shame before thee, who shinest with the light-beaming of greatest virtues, and they swayed not the boundaries of thy tongue.

*Theotokion:*
He Who wisely made all things by His will, desiring to renew mankind, O Virgin, dwelt within thy womb.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord, the Church cries unto Thee, having been cleansed from the blood of demons by the blood that flowed for mercy's sake from Thy side.

*Troparion:*
Rome praises thine honorable accomplishments; for as a light-beaming star, shedding everywhere the rays of thy wonders, O hierarch, thou art faithfully admired.

*Troparion:*
Having risen early unto Christ, Thou wast richly illumined with the brightnesses that are there, and wast filled with most divine light, and Thou ever enlightenest them that faithfully honor thee.

*Troparion:*
Sanctifying thy body and soul unto God,[^52] thou didst make thy heart receptive of gifts, O father, continually giving heed unto sweet desire.

*Theotokion:*
Heal the wounds of my soul, O Virgin, by thy divine overshadowing, and enlighten my mind darkened by slothfulness and by the malice of the enemy adversary.

*Kontakion, Tone 3, Podoben: "Of the divine faith" (Бж҃твенныѧ вѣ́ры):*
Having shone forth with divine doctrines, thou didst darken the Arian delusion, O sacred initiate and shepherd Ambrose; and working wonders by the power of the Spirit, thou didst openly heal diverse passions, O venerable father: entreat Christ God that our souls may be saved.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
In the Persian furnace, the Abrahamic youths, burning with love of piety rather than with flame, cried aloud: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
The divine utterance of thy doctrines, O all-wise father, hath gone forth like lightning into all the earth, and shone like light with manifestations of wonders, enlightening hearts that are in darkness.

*Troparion:*
Following the statutes of the Savior, O father, as a most blessed servant thou didst diligently multiply the talent given unto thee, being accounted worthy of the Master's joy.

*Troparion:*
Having sharpened thy theological mind, thou didst pour forth the stream of sacred doctrines like a river, watering the fulness of the faithful, O sacred initiate, father Ambrose.

*Theotokion:*
Behold, O Virgin, in thy womb thou hast conceived the Word co-unoriginate with the Father, and hast borne Him in the flesh, granting restoration unto all that are fallen of Adam, O all-immaculate one.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Daniel, having stretched forth his hands, shut the lions' gaping mouths in the pit; and the youths, lovers of piety, having girded themselves with virtue, quenched the power of fire, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Having put thy members to death, and made dead the fleshly mind, thou didst enliven thy soul, O venerable one : and thou hast poured forth a fountain of wonders unto those dead through passions, granting life unto them that cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Thou knewest thy departure from the body, O wise one, by the Divine Spirit; for prophetically thou didst tell this unto them that were with thee, and joyfully didst ascend into the heavens, crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Having pre-purified thy body, and heart, and mind from the mingling of passions, thou didst receive from on high the fiery beam of the Spirit, like the divine disciples, O Ambrose accepted of God: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst appear higher than the heavens, having given birth unto the heavenly God, Who united earthly things unto the heavenly, O all-pure one, and Who grants knowledge of Himself unto all that cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
A cornerstone was cut out without hands from thee, the unhewn mountain, O Virgin, even Christ, Who hath joined together the divided natures. Therefore, rejoicing, we magnify thee, O Birthgiver of God.

*Troparion:*
Being in ecstasy, thou didst behold the eternal honors prepared for the saints, unto which thou hast passed over, receiving with rejoicing the rewards of thy labors, O glorious one.

*Troparion:*
As a ripe cluster of grapes, O divinely-wise Ambrose, thou hast worthily been stored up in the winepresses on high, pouring forth the wine of immortality and gifts of healings unto them that have recourse unto thee with piety.

*Troparion:*
As a golden-beaming lamp of the Divine Spirit, O father, sending forth the light of pious doctrines and a healing ray, and enlightening the faithful, we bless thee with loud voice.

*Troparion:*
Having today acquired thee as a radiant star,[^53] the Church flees from the darkness of all deceit, O all-blessed one, and being illuminated by the brightness of thy sacred doctrines, she calls thee blessed.

*Theotokion:*
We cry aloud unto thee joyfully, O Virgin, the voice of the archangels: Rejoice, release from the curse, deliverance from all grievous evils; rejoice, thou who hast deified earthly beings beyond understanding by thy childbearing.

*In the same month, on the 8th day: Our Venerable Father Patapius. If the superior so wills, Alleluia, or Troparion; let it be chanted according to the Typikon.*

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera, Tone 1, Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Всехва́льнїи мꙋ́ченицы):*

*Sticheron:*
O father Patapius, having withered the burning of the flesh's impulses by temperance, thou didst settle in the wilderness like Elijah of old, purifying thy mind by unceasing prayers unto God. And now pray, that peace and great mercy may be granted unto our souls.

*Sticheron:*
O father Patapius, thou wast numbered with the ascetics' choirs,[^54] adorning thyself with dispassion, and didst settle in the mansions of the venerable, where the unsetting Light is, where the Tree of Life is. And now pray, that peace and great mercy may be granted unto our souls.

*Sticheron:*
O father Patapius, thou didst shine forth from Egypt as a luminary, enlightening the world beneath the sun with the brightness of wonders, driving away the gloom of soul-corrupting diseases, dispelling the darkness of demons. And now pray unto Christ, that peace and great mercy may be granted unto our souls.

*Other Stichera to the Most Holy Theotokos, Tone and Podoben the same (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*

*Theotokion:*
Incorruption didst thou bear God, Who destroyed corruption and poured forth incorruption, O incorrupt and immaculate one. Therefore I pray thee: by thy prayers, O pure one, renew me who am corrupted by grievous sins, that I may glorify thee, that with love I may magnify thee, who hast magnified our race.

*Theotokion:*
O extolled Sovereign Lady, hope and confirmation of the faithful, refuge and help, we pray thee: preserve thy servants from all tribulations, who in faith bow down before thy childbearing. Pray unto Christ, that peace and great mercy may be granted unto our souls.

*Theotokion:*
Woe is me, what shall become of me, having defiled mind and soul and body with transgressions? What shall I do? How shall I escape the unquenchable flame, and the everlasting bonds that cannot be loosed? But O all-immaculate one, before the end entreat thy Son to grant me remission.

*Glory, both now, Theotokion, Podoben (Подо́бенъ):*

*Podoben the same (Подо́бенъ то́йже):*
Thou didst bear the Fire of the Godhead, even Christ, in thy womb. Entreat Him now, O all-pure one, to quench all the easily-kindled matter of my passions, and deliver me from the eternal fire, and make me worthy of the brightness of the righteous, when He comes to judge all things.

*Stavrotheotokion:*
When the ewe-lamb and immaculate Sovereign Lady beheld her Lamb upon the Cross, having neither form nor comeliness, weeping she cried: Woe is me! Whither hath Thy comeliness set, O sweetest One? Whither Thy fair majesty? Whither the grace that shone from Thy face, O my most beloved Son?

*At the Aposticha, from the Octoechos.*

*Troparion, Tone 8:*
In thee, O father, was that which is according to the image preserved with certainty; for having taken up the Cross, thou didst follow Christ, and by deed didst teach to despise indeed the flesh, for it passes away, and to care for the soul, an immortal thing. Therefore together with the angels doth thy spirit rejoice, O venerable Patapius.

*Glory, both now, Theotokion.*

*At Matins, both Canons from the Octoechos, and the Venerable Father's, on 4. Tone 2.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
In the deep of old, the overwhelming power laid low the whole army of Pharaoh; and the incarnate Word destroyed all-wicked sin, even the most glorified Lord; for gloriously hath He been glorified.

*Troparion:*
Desiring to praise the radiant achievements of thy radiant life, I pray thee, O venerable Patapius: pray unto the Lord to grant me from heaven a beam endowed with grace, driving away the cloud of mine ignorance.

*Troparion:*
He Who of old covered the Egyptians in the deep by His divine bidding, having drawn thee up as from the deep of worldly confusion, enlightened thee with divine radiances, and showed thee forth as an all-radiant star, O venerable father.

*Troparion:*
Kindled like a spiritual coal by the warmth of the Spirit, thou didst melt the demonic frost, and didst quench the fiery darts of sin, O venerable one, and wast raised up most honorably unto the height of dispassion.

*Theotokion:*
Granting the world deliverance from the ancient curse, the Deliverer is born of thee, O Virgin, having become man, Who showed the venerable Patapius to be a fountain of healings unto all that with faith are reconciled unto Him.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
The wilderness, the barren church of the nations, hath blossomed forth like a lily at Thy coming, O Lord, wherein my heart hath been established.

*Troparion:*
Having excellently watered the furrow of thy soul with streams of tears, thou hast brought forth the divine wheat of deeds, preserved in the granaries on high.

*Troparion:*
Armed with love as with a sword, O venerable one, and shielded by thy divine humility, thou didst destroy the regiments of demons.

*Troparion:*
With the flower of temperance like a lily hast thou blossomed forth, O venerable one, making fragrant the hearts of them that praise thee, and who celebrate thy memory with faith.

*Theotokion:*
Borne in the arms of her that bare Thee, O Lord, by Thy power Thou didst shatter the idols of Egypt, from whence sprouted a multitude of venerable ones.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom and Word" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
By the ascetic sweats of temperance thou didst quench the flame of the passions, pouring forth unto all an abyss of wonders; and therein, like a second Moses, thou didst drown the deceitful assaults of the regiments of demons. Therefore, having come together, we dutifully honor thy most honorable memory in prayer, O venerable God-bearer Patapius: entreat Christ God that He grant remission of sins unto them that honor thy holy memory with love.

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*
As thou hast borne the merciful and compassionate Word, O Sovereign Lady of all, have mercy upon all that have recourse unto thee; and deliver them from temptations and diseases, and from every affliction and from the eternal flame: that we may thankfully glorify the wealth of thy manifold compassions and boundless mercy, and ever cry unto thee: Entreat Christ God that He grant remission of sins unto them that with faith bow down before thy childbearing.

*Stavrotheotokion:*
The Virgin and Mother of the Deliverer, standing before the Cross, painfully weeping with tears, maternally cried aloud: What is this strange and most glorious thing, O Son? He Who pours forth dispassion unto all men is crucified on the Cross between two condemned ones, pierced in the ribs, and given gall to drink by the hands of those whom He created. But arise, and grant remission of transgressions unto them that with faith hymn Thy divine sufferings!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Thou didst come from the Virgin, not an ambassador nor an angel, but Thyself incarnate, O Lord, and hast saved all of me, man. Therefore I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
The abyss of thy warm tears drowned the demonic hosts and the waves of sins; and an ocean of wonders was shown forth unto them that were in the deep of passions.

*Troparion:*
Having acquired humility, vigilance, prolonged prayer, unfeigned love, faith, and hope, thou wast a converser with the heavenly angels,[^55] O venerable father.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst lull to sleep the afflictions of manifold passions by divine ascents and unceasing purifications. Therefore unto the unsetting radiance, after thy dormition, hast thou departed.

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst shine forth from the Virgin as the sun from a cloud, showing forth Thy venerable ones as illumining stars, crucified unto the world and passions by Thy power, O Compassionate One.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
O Christ my Savior, Enlightenment of them that lie in darkness, Salvation of the despairing: early I awake unto Thee, O King of peace; enlighten me with Thy brightness, for besides Thee I know no other God.

*Troparion:*
Enlightenment of them that lie in darkness, shine forth a beam upon me by the divine prayers of Thy venerable one; disperse the clouds of my wretched soul;[^56] rain down upon me a stream of remission, for besides Thee I know no other God.

*Troparion:*
Having purified the eye of the mind from the defilements of the passions by temperance, O God-bearing father, by divine prayer thou didst open the pupils of the blind, and by the radiance of healings didst destroy the gloom of grievous afflictions.

*Troparion:*
Come, all ye, let us draw forth health of soul, health of body, an ungrudged grace, as from a fountain, from the divine shrine of the wise Patapius; for he pours forth wonders like waters unto them that have recourse unto him with undoubting faith.

*Theotokion:*
By ineffable childbearing, O Maiden, thou hast borne the Giver of life, Who holds all things, Who is glorified in the saints and rests upon the venerable: entreat Him for us, O Bride of God.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Wallowing in the abyss of sin, I call upon the unfathomable abyss of Thy compassion: bring me up from corruption, O God!

*Troparion:*
Enlightening thy mind with most radiant ascents, O father, as one bodiless thou didst live with the flesh, not stained by sins, O Patapius.

*Troparion:*
Emulating Elijah the Tishbite, and following John the Forerunner, thou didst first settle in the wilderness, having purified thy mind by silence.

*Troparion:*
A most God-radiant luminary from Egypt, in Constantine's city thou didst shine forth with the radiance of healings for enlightenment,[^57] O most bright father Patapius.

*Theotokion:*
Sitting upon a light cloud, Christ came into Egypt of old, and having cast down the idols, He gathered the choirs of the venerable.

*Kontakion, Tone 3, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дв҃а дне́сь):*
Having found thy temple, O holy one, to be a spiritual dispensary, the people coming unto it with diligence ask to receive healing of diseases and release from transgressions in life; for thou hast appeared as a protector of all that are in distress, O venerable Patapius.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
Unto the golden image worshipped in the plain of Dura, Thy three youths took no heed of the godless decree; but cast into the midst of the fire, being bedewed, they sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
With spiritual fire thou didst kindle the feelings of the soul, and didst burn up the fire of sin by the cooperation of the Spirit; and light-bearing didst thou appear, singing, O Patapius: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Having given sight unto the blind by divine cooperation,[^58] O divinely-blessed one, thou didst heal diverse passions, and by divine invocations didst drive away regiments of subtle demons, singing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
A depth of wonders, a river of healings, an unceasing fountain, a stream never failing, hath thy tomb appeared, O father, unto them that approach with faith and warmly cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
The transcendent God deifies me from thee, O Virgin, taking the form of a servant, and renews the paths of knowledge as well as the bounds of nature, having brought a multitude of monks and venerable ones who sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Unto God Who descended into the fiery furnace unto the Hebrew youths, and changed the flame into dew, hymn His works as the Lord, and exalt Him supreme unto all unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Having cleansed thyself from the mire of passions by heedfulness, O father, thou didst most brightly appear as a receptacle of God, crying: Hymn the Lord, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Having ordered thy life in a manner worthy of God, O venerable father, thou didst appear as a steward, having ministered well unto the needs of the saints, O venerable one, with whom thou wast accounted worthy of the heavenly inheritance.

*Troparion:*
By prayers unto the Lord cleanse us from every defilement; by thy warm prayer deliver from the surge of passions, and diseases, and sorrows us who worthily honor thee, O Patapius.

*Theotokion:*
Thou who hast made heavenly our earthly, corruptible, frail nature,[^59] the glory of angels and joy of the venerable, sole Sovereign Lady of creatures, as she that bare God, let her be hymned unto the ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
The Son of the unoriginate Begetter, God and Lord, incarnate of the Virgin hath appeared unto us, to enlighten them that are in darkness, and to gather the dispersed: therefore we magnify the all-hymned Birthgiver of God.

*Troparion:*
Thy memory hath shone forth as a saving day, enlightening hearts that are in darkness, and dispersing the gloom of passions, showing forth as sons of light them that now honor thee, O pleasing servant of the Lord.

*Troparion:*
The offshoot of the Thebaid, the praise of the wilderness, the glory and fair majesty of monastics, the luminary of Byzantium, who appeared on earth as an angel: Patapius let us all worthily bless.

*Troparion:*
Having been a converser with angels, an emulous champion of the venerable, a partaker with prophets, apostles, martyrs, and hierarchs, O venerable one, and serving the honorable Trinity in purity of mind: pray for us all!

*Theotokion:*
The great mystery of thy childbearing beyond understanding amazes the angels, O thou full of the grace of God; it sweetens the assemblies of the venerable, O pure one, and gladdens the sacred fathers, who divinely hymn thee, O unwedded Birthgiver of God.

*In the same month, on the 9th day: The Conception of Saint Anna, when she conceived the Most Holy Birthgiver of God.*

*At Small Vespers, at "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 4, Tone 2, Podoben: "With what crowns of praise" (Кї́ими похва́льными):*

*Sticheron:*
With what unworthy lips shall we now praise her that is conceived? Holier than creation, and being more honorable than the Cherubim and all the saints: the immovable royal throne; the house wherein the Most High took up His dwelling; salvation unto the world; the sanctification of God: granting unto the faithful in her divine conception peace and great mercy.

*Sticheron:*
What spiritual songs shall we now offer unto thee, O all-pure one? For by thy conception in a barren womb thou hast sanctified the whole world, and hast delivered Adam from bonds, and freed Eve from travail. Therefore do the angelic choirs feast together, heaven and earth rejoice, and the souls of the righteous clap their hands together, faithfully crying songs unto the glory of thy conception.

*Sticheron:*
What awe-inspiring songs did the maidens then offer unto thee, O Virgin, around thy conception, rejoicing and in wonder crying aloud: The palace of the King is conceived; the ark of sanctification shines forth; the barren doors are opened; for the door of God ushers in the fair offspring of virtues, granting unto the world peace and great mercy!

*Glory, both now, in the same Tone, Automelon:*
Today from the root of David the royal purple hath sprouted; from Jesse the mystical flower begins to grow, wherein Christ our God hath blossomed forth, Who saves our souls.

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O house of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*

*Sticheron:*
Rejoice, ye choir of prophets! For behold, Anna sprouts a fruit, concerning whom the prophecies that were[^60] shall go forth to be fulfilled.

*Verse: The Lord hath sworn in truth unto David, and He will not turn from it.*

*Sticheron:*
Rejoice together, all ye tribes, with barren Anna; for beyond hope she sprouts the fruit of her womb, the mediatress of our life.

*Verse: Of the fruit of thy loins will I set upon thy throne.*

*Sticheron:*
Be glad, ye ends of the earth! For behold, the Mother of the Creator of all sprouts today from a barren womb.

*Glory, both now, Podoben the same (Подо́бенъ то́йже):*
Rejoice, O Joachim, and rejoice, O Anna! For the mediatress of salvation and joy of the world do ye bear as fruit today.

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
Today the bonds of childlessness are loosed; for God, having heard Joachim and Anna, clearly promises unto them that beyond hope they shall give birth to the Maiden of God, from whom He Himself was born, the Uncircumscribed, having become man, commanding an angel to cry unto her: Rejoice, thou full of grace, the Lord is with thee!

*At Great Vespers,*
*We chant the kathisma "Blessed is the man," the 1st Stasis. At "Lord, I have cried," we set 8 Stichera, and we sing Stichera in Tone 4, Podoben: "Called from on high" (Свы́ше зва́нъ):*

*Sticheron:*
Bearing fruit beyond hope, the barren one shines with joy, about to bear the Virgin who is to bear God in the flesh, and rejoicing she leads the choir, with loud voice crying aloud: All ye tribes of Israel, rejoice with me! For behold, I bear in my womb and put away the reproach of childlessness, as the Creator was well-pleased, having heard my prayer and healed the pain of my heart in that which I desired! (Thrice)

*Sticheron:*
He Who poured forth water from the dry rock grants a fruit unto thy womb, O Anna, even the Ever-Virgin Sovereign Lady, from whom the water of salvation is to come forth. No longer shalt thou abide on earth as barren ground, for thou hast put away reproach; for having grown a land bearing the ear of life, which takes away reproaches from all men, as the Mother was well-pleased according to His compassion to take form in that which was alien.[^61] (Thrice)

*Sticheron:*
The prophetic utterances are fulfilled today: for the holy mountain is lodged in the womb; the divine ladder is planted; the great throne of the King is prepared beforehand; the place passable by God is adorned; the unburnt bush begins to sprout; the alabaster jar of holiness already flows forth, putting to flight the rivers of barrenness of the divinely-wise Anna, whom we bless in faith.

*Glory, both now, Tone 2, by Germanus:[^62]*
The great and most glorious mystery, incomprehensible to angels and hidden from the ages unto men, today is borne as an infant in the womb of the chaste Anna: Mary, the Maiden of God, being prepared for the habitation of Christ, the King of all the King of the ages, and for the renewal of our race. Her let us entreat with a pure conscience, crying unto her: Pray unto thy Son and God, as thou art the protectress of us Christians, that our souls may be saved.

*Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day. And three Readings:*

*Reading from Genesis (Chapter 28):*[^63]
Jacob went forth from the Well of the Oath,[^64] and went unto Haran. And he found a place, and slept there, for the sun had set; and he took of the stones of that place, and put them for his pillow, and slept in that place; and he dreamed a dream. And behold, a ladder established on the earth, whose top reached unto heaven; and the angels of God were ascending and descending on it. And the Lord leaned upon it, and said: I am the God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac; fear not: the land whereon thou sleepest, unto thee will I give it, and unto thy seed. And thy seed shall be as the sand of the earth, and shall spread abroad to the sea, and to the south, and to the north, and to the east. And in thee shall all the tribes of the earth be blessed, and in thy seed. And behold, I am with thee, preserving thee in all the way whithersoever thou goest; and I will bring thee back into this land; for I will not leave thee, until I have done all that I have spoken unto thee. And Jacob awoke from his sleep, and said: Surely the Lord is in this place, and I knew it not. And he was afraid, and said: How fearful is this place! This is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.

*Reading from the Prophecy of Ezekiel (Chapters 43 and 44):*[^65]
Thus says the Lord: It shall come to pass from the eighth day and forward, that the priests shall offer your whole-burnt-offerings upon the altar, and your peace-offerings; and I will accept you, says Adonai the Lord. And He turned me back by the way of the outer gate of the sanctuary, which looks toward the east; and it was shut. And the Lord said unto me: This gate shall be shut, it shall not be opened, and no man shall pass through it; for the Lord God of Israel shall enter by it, and it shall be shut. For the Leader, He shall sit in it to eat bread; He shall enter by the way of the porch of the gate, and shall go out by the way of the same. And He brought me in by the way of the north gate of the sanctuary, before the house; and I looked, and behold, the house of the Lord was full of glory.

*Reading from Proverbs (Chapter 9):*[^66]
Wisdom hath builded her house, and established seven pillars. She hath killed her beasts, and mingled her wine in the bowl, and prepared her table. She hath sent forth her servants, summoning with high proclamation unto the cup, saying: Whosoever is simple, let him turn aside unto me; and to them that lack understanding she says: Come, eat of my bread, and drink the wine which I have mingled for you. Leave foolishness, and ye shall live; and seek wisdom, that ye may live, and set aright understanding in knowledge. He that reproves evil men shall get unto himself dishonor; and he that rebukes the ungodly shall blame himself, for reproofs unto the ungodly are wounds unto him. Rebuke not evil men, lest they hate thee; rebuke a wise man, and he will love thee. Give an occasion unto a wise man, and he will be yet wiser; instruct a righteous man, and he will increase in receiving it. The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, and the counsel of the saints is understanding; for to understand the law is the sign of a good mind; for in this manner thou shalt live a long time, and years of thy life shall be added unto thee.

*At the Litiya, Stichera, Tone 1:*
*Idiomelon, by Malaxos:[^67]*

*Sticheron:*
Rejoice today, O righteous God-ancestors, Joachim and Anna! For ye were fore-named from among all generations to be the parents of her who according to the flesh bare the Only-begotten Son of God, Mary, the unwedded Mother of God; and for her sake an end is given unto all signs and unutterable corruption,[^68] and unto the prophetic foretellings, even the mystery of the Incarnation of the Word. Rejoice thou also, all the choir of prophets, with Adam and Abraham our forefather! For the glory of your proclamation hath come, and universal deliverance.

*Tone 2:[^69]*

*Sticheron:*
Today a radiant cloud is formed in a barren womb, from whom Christ our God, the Sun of righteousness, shines forth transcendent over nature, to enlighten them that sit in darkness and the shadow of death, and to grant great mercy unto all.

*Tone 6:*

*Sticheron:*
O the marvelous wonders! O the promises beyond nature! An angel from heaven foreannounces the childbearing of the Mother of God unto the all-honorable union; and the barren woman, not bearing, brings forth the Maiden of God; and the dried-up womb sprouts the door of Him Who was shut;[^70] and the appellation of childless spouses is changed into the namesake of God-ancestors, by grace for the sake of [grace]. Therefore let us cry aloud: O Thou Who hast made all things, and by Thine intention alone dost alter them, Lord, glory to Thee!

*Glory, both now, Tone 5:*

*Sticheron:*
Rejoice and be glad, O Anna, honored of God! For from promise thou dost bear fruit, having received joy from an angel; and from a non-bearing womb thou sproutest her that from a seedless womb sprouted the Planter of all. Blessed is the house from which she was born; blessed is the root in truth from which she came forth; blessed is the fruit of the parents, from whom she was brought forth with Joachim the God-wise. For by divine nodding ye were shown to be in truth the parents of the only Virgin blessed among women, and Mother of God.

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 5, Podoben: "Rejoice" (Ра́дуйся):*

*Sticheron:*
Anna, the divine grace, once praying for a child, cried aloud unto the God and Creator of all: Adonai Sabaoth, Thou knowest the reproach of childlessness! Do Thou Thyself loose the pain of my heart, and open the depths of my womb, and show me, who am barren, to be fruitful; that we may bring the newborn as a gift unto Thee, blessing, hymning, and with one mind glorifying Thy loving-kindness, whereby great mercy is given unto the world!

*Verse: The Lord hath sworn in truth unto David, and He will not turn from it.*

*Sticheron:*
Of old, praying faithfully, the chaste Anna, entreating God, heard an angelic voice assuring her of the divine fulfillment of what was asked. Unto whom the bodiless one plainly spoke: Thy supplication hath drawn near unto the Lord; mourn not, and cease from tears! For thou shalt be a fruitful olive tree, sprouting a fair branch, the Virgin, who shall blossom forth the Flower, Christ in the flesh, Who grants great mercy unto the world.

*Verse: Of the fruit of thy loins will I set upon thy throne.*

*Sticheron:*
The honorable couple bears fruit: a divine heifer, from whom shall come forth the calf fed in truth by the ineffable Word, slain for the whole world. Therefore, rejoicing, they offer unceasing thanksgiving in contrition unto the Lord, and they shall have her that profits in all things. Let us therefore bless them, and with faith dance in the divine conception of the Mother of our God born of them, through whom great mercy is richly given.

*Glory, both now, Tone 2:*
Today from the root of David the royal purple hath sprouted, from Jesse from Jesse begins to grow the mystical flower, wherein Christ our God hath blossomed forth, Who saves our souls.

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
Today the bonds of childlessness are loosed; for God, having heard Joachim and Anna, clearly promises unto them that beyond hope they shall give birth to the Maiden of God, from whom He Himself was born, the Uncircumscribed, having become man, commanding an angel to cry unto her: Rejoice, thou full of grace, the Lord is with thee! (Once)

*At Matins, after the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 1, Podoben: "The angelic choir" (Ли́къ а́ггельскїй):*
A new heaven is fashioned in Anna's womb by command of God the Creator of all, from whom shines forth the Unwaning Sun, enlightening all the world with the rays of His divinity, by the multitude of His loving-kindness, the only Lover of mankind.

*Glory, both now, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph was amazed" (Удиви́ся Ио́сифъ):*
The beginning of blessing, a sprouting from barrenness hast Thou granted, O Good One, unto Anna as she cried: By prayer Thou transformest natures toward childbearing; therefore, O Savior, make my deadened nature new again, as God, that I may bring fruit unto Thee, crying unto my Creator: Glory is due unto Thee, O God of all things, and only Lover of mankind!

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 1, Podoben: "The angelic choir" (Ли́къ а́ггельскїй):*
The prophetic choir of old preached the undefiled, pure, and Maiden of God, the Virgin, whom Anna conceived, being barren and childless: her today with gladness of heart let us bless, having been saved for her sake, as the only undefiled one.

*Glory, both now, Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́ро предвари́):*
Be renewed, O Adam, and leap for joy, O Eve! For the dry and barren earth hath sprouted a most blossoming fruit, having blossomed forth the ear of immortality unto all the world, and all reproach of childlessness is taken away. Rejoice ye together with them today!

*Selected Refrain and Psalm:*
*The same as on the Nativity of the Most Holy Birthgiver of God. Instead of "Nativity," we sing "Conception." After the Polyeleos, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph was amazed" (Удиви́ся Ио́сифъ):*
Cry aloud, O David: What did God swear unto thee? That which He swore unto me (he says) He hath already fulfilled: from the fruit of my womb a Virgin Maiden, from whom the Creator, Christ the new Adam, was born a King upon my throne; and He reigns today, having a kingdom immovable; the barren woman conceives the Birthgiver of God and nourisher of our life.

*Verse: Remember, O Lord, David and all his meekness.*

*Gospel according to Luke, pericope 4 [Luke 1:39–49, 56].[^71]*

*Glory, Tone 2:*
Rejoice, O human nature, which once wast barren of virtues; for the barren woman now conceives the loosedness of thy barrenness!
