*Have mercy on us, O God, according to Thy great mercy:*
*Sticheron, Tone 6:*
The beginning of our salvation, O ye peoples, hath come to pass today! For the Virgin Mary begins to be, and is fashioned in the womb of the barren woman, and the world is renewed with her. Joachim rejoices with Anna, the bonds of childlessness are loosed, and Adam is glad, being delivered from bonds. With them let us also cry aloud unto her with joy: Rejoice, thou full of grace, the Lord is with thee!

*Two Canons of Saint Anna: the first with the Heirmos on 8; the second on 6. A composition of Andrew.[^72]*
*Tone 4. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Let us all sing a triumphant song unto God Who hath wrought marvelous wonders with a high arm, and saved Israel, for He hath been glorified!

*Troparion:*
Today we celebrate thy conception, O God-wise Anna; for having been loosed from the bonds of childlessness, thou didst conceive her that contained Him Who cannot be contained anywhere.

*Troparion:*
Thou hast heard the prayer of the righteous, O Lord, and hast fulfilled the promise of Thy holy forefathers, and unto them hast given as fruit the pure one that bare Thee.

*Troparion:*
Anna the glorious now conceives the pure one, who conceived the incorporeal, all-good Lord; and she is about to give birth unto her that in the flesh is to give birth to Christ.

*Theotokion:*
From mortal loins thou hast shone forth, O Virgin; for in an incorrupt womb thou didst bear the Sun of glory, Who became as we are, without turning and without confusion.[^73]

*Another Canon, whose acrostic follows the alphabet.[^74]*
*Tone the same. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Christ is born, give ye glory! Christ from the heavens, meet ye Him! Christ on earth, be ye lifted up! Sing unto the Lord, all the earth, and with gladness sing, ye peoples, for He hath been glorified!

*Troparion:*
Having received in the womb the pure Virgin Maiden of God, who was to be the Mother of the Creator, Anna joyfully cried aloud: All ye tribes of Israel, rejoice with me, for behold, I also have conceived!

*Troparion:*
Holding in her womb the book foretold by the prophet, sealed by the divine Spirit, Anna cried aloud unto all: Her whom all the scriptures reveal, having sprouted today, let us magnify!

*Troparion:*
In the womb is contained and fashioned a divine and saving temple in maternal loins; the ladder is planted which leads all men on high: whose conception let us faithfully celebrate!

*Katavasia:*
*Christ is born:*

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Let my heart be established in Thy will, O Christ God, Who didst establish the second heaven above the waters, and didst found the earth upon the waters, O Almighty!

*Troparion:*
If Thou wilt grant me fruit of the womb, Anna cried unto the Lord, I shall be magnified, and shall bring this unto Thee. Therefore she conceives the pure Mother of God.

*Troparion:*
Having fulfilled the law, and blamelessly served God, thou in truth dost bear in the womb her that bare the Lawgiver, O all-honorable Anna: therefore do we the faithful bless thee.

*Theotokion:*
While praying in the garden, the Most High heard thy voice, O God-wise Anna, and grants fruit unto thy womb: the Mother of God, who by grace opened the door of paradise.

*Supplication to the Theotokos:*
Drive away all the barrenness of my barren thoughts, and show my soul to be fruitful in virtues, O all-holy Birthgiver of God, help of the faithful!

*Another. Heirmos:*
Unto the Son begotten of the Father without corruption before the ages, and in these latter days incarnate without seed of the Virgin, Christ God, let us cry aloud: Thou Who hast exalted our horn, holy art Thou, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Joachim praying unto the Lord receives from on high the longed-for utterance, when an angel stood before him and said: Go, the God of all hath fulfilled thy requests, O righteous one!

*Troparion:*
Anna, calling upon the God of all, while once standing in the garden, beheld an angel standing before her and saying: Mourn not, for thou shalt be the mother of the Mother of God!

*Troparion:*
Emulating Sarah of old before thee, O Anna, thou didst offer supplications unto God, and didst conceive in Thy pure womb her that received without seed the Uncontainable Word; having enriched all of us by Thy goodly childbearing O Anna, having been bestowed with grace.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up" (Вознесы́йся):*
The sacred Joachim and Anna brought gifts of old unto the priests, and were not accepted, being childless; they offered supplication unto the Giver of all things, and having heard their prayer, He grants unto them her that is the very gate of life: whose holy conception let us honor!

*Glory, both now, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph was amazed" (Удиви́ся Ио́сифъ):*
The unblemished ewe-lamb and all-pure bridal chamber, the divinely-adorned Mary, now begins to come forth gloriously from the righteous, O ye faithful! Rejoice therefore, heaven and earth, and all ye earthborn leap for joy together! For today God hath wrought marvelous things, having shown forth in the womb of the barren woman a fruit, the only Virgin: whom let us faithfully hymn.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Foreseeing in the Spirit the Incarnation of the Word, O prophet Habakkuk, thou didst proclaim, crying aloud: When the years draw near, Thou shalt be known; when the time is come, Thou shalt be shown forth. Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
O divine utterance! O strange saying! If I also shall conceive! an angel having been sent unto her, Anna in amazement cried with a loud voice: Glory to my God, Who does marvelous things!

*Troparion:*
Rejoice with me, all ye tribes of Israel: in my womb I have conceived a new heaven, from which after a little while the Star of salvation shall shine forth, Jesus the Light-giver! Anna crying aloud rejoiced.

*Troparion:*
God heard Anna's groaning, and the Lord gave ear unto her prayer; and having broken the cloud of childlessness, He illumines her gloriously with the light of goodly childbearing: therefore she conceives the only pure one.

*Theotokion:*
As the unblemished tabernacle of God, O Birthgiver of God, cleanse me now who am defiled with transgressions, by the most pure sprinklings of thy compassions; and give me a hand of help, that I may cry: Glory to thee, O pure one, glorified of God!

*Another. Heirmos:*
A rod from the root of Jesse, and a flower from it, O Christ, Thou hast budded from the Virgin; from the mountain overshadowed and densely forested, Thou hast come incarnate from her that knew not man, O Incorporeal One and God: glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Thy womb which before did not bear is opened, and thou receivest, O Anna, the heavenly cloud, from which the bright Sun hath shone forth upon us, enlightened all things with the light of truth, and deep dispersed the deep darkness of godlessness.

*Troparion:*
A fiery-formed divine throne was established in thy loins, whereon God sat and rested, taking away the toil of all the pious, and establishing pure knowledge of God upon the earth: O blessed Anna, acceptable unto God!

*Troparion:*
Behold, the bed of which Solomon prophesied thou hast received in the womb, preserved most truly for the true King, for the divine calling and restoration of the human race. Therefore with joy, O Anna, do we the faithful bless thee.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Grant us Thy peace, O Son of God, for we know no other God besides Thee; we call upon Thy name, for Thou art the God of the living and of the dead!

*Troparion:*
Having sprouted from the root of David and of Jesse, Anna now begins to grow the divine rod, which sprouted the mystical flower, Christ the Creator of all.

*Troparion:*
Seeing me become a mother, cried Anna, the peoples shall look and wonder; for behold, I give birth, as He Who loosed the bonds of my barrenness was well-pleased!

*Troparion:*
The Maiden whom I have conceived, prophetic voices foreannounced from afar as a mountain and an impassable gate, most joyfully cried Anna unto them that came unto her.

*Theotokion:*
A cloud, and paradise, and the gate of light, the table, and the fleece do we know thee to be, and the jar holding the manna within, the sweetness of the world, O pure Virgin Mother!

*Another. Heirmos:*
Being the God of peace and Father of compassions, Thou hast sent unto us the Angel of Thy great counsel, granting peace. Therefore, having been guided unto the light of the knowledge of God, watching early from the night, we glorify Thee, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
Joachim came down from the mountain, not having received the tablets of the law, but her whom the law prefigured and all the prophetic utterances revealed, the pure Mother of God; and leaping with joy he cried aloud: My heart is magnified!

*Troparion:*
When Anna once perceived in her loins the fruitful vine planted, from which blossomed forth for us the ripe cluster pouring forth abundantly the wine of immortality: What shall I render unto Thee, O compassionate Lord? she spoke.

*Troparion:*
Joachim, not enduring to see creation barren of piety, prayed that Anna's barrenness might be cut off, and that they might possess this Maiden, from whom the Son was given, Who made all sons unto His Father the Most High [Son] Who adopted all [men] unto His Father.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Imitating the prophet Jonah, I cry aloud: Deliver my life from corruption, O Good One, and save me, O Savior of the world, who cry: Glory to Thee!

*Troparion:*
How is she contained in the womb who contained God? How is she born who bare Christ in the flesh? And how is she nourished at the breast who suckled the Creator with milk?

*Troparion:*
Having heard your supplication, God now grants unto you a fruitful offspring, O all-praised Joachim and Anna today!

*Troparion:*
Having conceived the pure dove in her womb, Anna was in truth filled with spiritual joy, offering songs of thanksgiving unto God.

*Theotokion:*
The tempest of thoughts, and assaults of passions, and the depth of sins storm my wretched soul.[^75] Help me, O holy Birthgiver of God!

*Another. Heirmos:*
The sea beast spewed forth Jonah as an infant from its belly, such as it received him; and the Word, having dwelt in the Virgin and taken flesh, came forth, having preserved her incorrupt: for from Him Who suffered no corruption, He kept her that bare Him unharmed.

*Troparion:*
The shadows of the law plainly pass away: for behold, the ray of divine grace is shown forth, the cloud-like Virgin, from whom the radiant Sun of divinity shines forth in truth, Anna cried aloud rejoicing, magnifying the God of Israel.

*Troparion:*
A strange sight, if I also shall conceive! she that was before barren and not bearing, Anna, said; when she heard the angel speaking that an infant should be born. And she cried aloud: Good is the goodly hearing, if the fulfillment of the words shall come to pass!

*Troparion:*
Let mountains and hills, fields and sea, the angelic multitude and all human nature rejoice! For again a divine temple, the beginning of reconciliation, hath Anna received, when she perceived that she herself had conceived, she spoke.

*Kontakion, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared today" (Яви́лся еси́ дне́сь):*
Today the universe celebrates the conception of Anna, which came to pass from God; for she bare her that beyond words bare the Word.

*Ikos:*
The marvelous Joachim and the God-wise Anna, both living in all piety according to the law of Moses, were barren, and prayed unto God with all their soul, saying: O Lord Sabaoth, all-good One, Hope of all, Thou knowest the pain of childlessness and the reproach of all men all men and their sorrow: grant us therefore fruit from the womb, and we will bring it into Thy temple as a holy gift, and an offering complete: her that beyond words bare the Word!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
Unto Thy youths in the furnace, O Savior, the fire touched them not, nor troubled them. Then the three, as with one mouth, sang and blessed, saying: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Anna prayed unto the Good One of all to escape the reproach of childlessness; and having heard her prayerful voice, He gave unto her as fruit her that bare Him, as He was well-pleased.

*Troparion:*
The royal purple begins to be woven in thy womb, O Anna, which God the King of all, having put on, shall appear unto men, and humble the enemies that war against us.

*Troparion:*
A fragrant myrrh hast thou conceived in thy womb, O Anna, having supernaturally received the good one who received the myrrh of life, who by the breathings of grace hath perfumed our thoughts.

*Theotokion:*
As One of the Trinity do we glorify Thee, O Christ, for having become incarnate of the Virgin without turning,[^76] Thou didst endure all human things, without departing from the paternal nature, O Jesus, though Thou wast united unto us.

*Another. Heirmos:*
The youths brought up together in piety, having despised the ungodly decree, were not afraid of the threat of fire; but standing in the midst of the flame, they sang: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Troparion:*
The fiery bush of old which Moses saw on Sinai, Anna conceived in her womb, extinguishing the fire of childlessness like some impiety, as they sang: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Troparion:*
A drop was gloriously poured forth today in thy womb, O Anna, which received within all the Water of life, watering them that faithfully cry unto Him: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Troparion:*
When thou didst behold a bird's nest, thou wast winged by the Spirit and by prayer, O Anna, and didst receive the unblemished dove bearing Christ, the olive branch, delivering us from the spiritual flood!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Him of Whom angels and all hosts are in dread as Creator and Lord, sing, ye priests; glorify, ye youths; bless, ye peoples; and exalt Him supreme unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Her whom my forefather foretold unto the King, behold, I receive in the womb, Anna cried aloud; and I shall give birth unto the protectress of all the faithful, who is to give birth to Christ the King.

*Troparion:*
The earth wherein the Creator of the earth took up His dwelling, the holy sceptre, the new ark, the jar of manna in the loins of the mother: her that bare this she begins to sprout.

*Troparion:*
The unburnt bush, the golden lampstand, the animate bridal chamber of the Lord God, the pure rod, in the womb of the mother: her that bare this she begins to sprout.

*Theotokion:*
Raise me up who lie in the depth of evils; conquer now the enemies that war against me; wounded by unseemly pleasures, O good and pure one, despise me not, but take pity and save me!

*Another. Heirmos:*
The dew-bearing furnace portrayed the image of a wonder beyond nature: for it burns not the youths whom it received, even as the fire of the Godhead burned not the Virgin's womb into which it entered. Therefore let us sing and chant: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Why hast Thou made my womb childless and my breasts dry, as Thou didst foretell in the prophets, O Master? Anna once cried aloud: Loose the reproach of my childlessness, and grant me fruit, with which I will cry aloud: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
The lampstand came down into thy womb, O Anna, which mystically contained the divine Candle, enlightening every breath with the mystical rays of divine knowledge. Therefore rejoicing thou didst cry aloud: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
The couple now bears the divine heifer as most fair, from whom the fair Calf shone forth, slain for all. The glorious Joachim and Anna, singing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
The ever-flowing life-receiving fountain, the light-bearing lamp of grace, the animate temple, the all-pure tabernacle, more spacious than heaven and earth, the Birthgiver of God do we the faithful magnify.

*Troparion:*
Conceiving the life-receiving fountain, O God-wise Anna, receive now joy, receiving the holy temple within thy womb, and being illumined with the light of righteousness, magnifying the Creator!

*Troparion:*
Let the honorable and most glorious couple, the ancestors of the pre-eternal Son, who were sure guardians of the law and bare the beginning of joy, Joachim and Anna, be honored!

*Troparion:*
Her whom Daniel saw as a great mountain, and Joel beheld as the holy land, an impassable door; and another foretold as a sealed fountain and the divine fleece: the Virgin Birthgiver of God let us hymn!

*Theotokion:*
The purple that dyed the fleece of the ineffable Incarnation of the Word, the golden censer, the table whereon Christ the Bread was set: the Virgin Birthgiver of God is glorified.

*Another. Heirmos:*
A strange and most glorious mystery do I behold: heaven is the cave; the cherubic throne, the Virgin; the manger, the receptacle wherein reclined the Uncontainable Christ God, Whom chanting we magnify!

*Troparion:*
Dance for joy, all ye souls, and leap! Now the earth is created which shall bring forth the unsown, life-bearing ear of grain, whereof they that eat shall never hunger, magnifying His goodness!

*Troparion:*
Take up the psaltery with the harp, O David, and sing: Behold, the ark of God hath appeared, which thou didst foretell plainly shall be for building up, whereby we are raised up from the fall of sin!

*Troparion:*
As two most great luminaries, ye brought forth the universal dawn, which shall radiate the great Sun unto the world. Therefore do we praise and glorify you, O Joachim and Anna, as the Ancestors of God!

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "O Light immutable" (Свѣ́те неизмѣ́нный):*
Her that is to give birth to the Light that illumines all creation, Anna today begins to sprout forth from barren loins. Therefore let us all run together, for the deliverance from Eve's condemnation is come!

*Glory, both now, the same.*

*At the Praises, Stichera on 4, Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Небе́сныхъ чинѡ́въ):*
The nature of men that was formerly barren, the beginning of piety for hope toward God, sprouts forth the Virgin; through whom the abundant fruit of good things is proclaimed, in her conception upon earth, at the approaching of Christ's coming. *Twice.*

*Sticheron:*
The impassable door of Christ the King, by the divine counsel, receives conception in barren loins; through whom, when she is brought forth upon earth, the gates of heaven shall be lifted up and grant entrance unto the earthborn.

*Sticheron:*
Of the divine and fearful mysteries preached from God unto the earthborn ineffably before the ages, the conception of the pure Maiden of God is shown forth as the beginning of faith; through whom it is foreannounced that the works of darkness and passions shall cease.

*Glory, both now, Tone 8:*
*By Malaxos:*[^77]
Come, let every rank and age of mankind today with joy, together with the angelic choirs, brightly celebrate the most glorious conception of the Birthgiver of God! Ye patriarchs, the Mother of the King of all; ye prophets, her that was proclaimed by you; ye forefathers, the Mother of God who is from you; ye elders, the Ancestors of God; ye Ancestors of God, the Maiden of God; ye virgins, the Ever-Virgin; ye faithful, the root of faith; ye priests, the all-holy temple of God; ye choirs of all the saints, the cause of your assembly; and ye angelic hosts, her that bare the Master of all creation, the Savior of our souls!

*Great Doxology.*

*After the Trisagion, the Troparion once, and the Dismissal.*

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes from the first Canon, Ode 3, and from the second, Ode 6.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 4:*
God is marvelous in His saints, the God of Israel. *Verse:* In the congregations bless ye God...

*Epistle to the Galatians, section 210 from the half.*[^78]

*And Alleluia, Tone 4:*
The salvation of the righteous is from the Lord.

*Gospel of Luke, pericope 36.*[^79]

*Communion Hymn:*
Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous!

*In the same month, on the 10th day:*
*Of the holy Martyrs Menas, Hermogenes, and Eugraphus.*

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Octoechos, 3; and of the Saints, 3.*

*Tone 1, Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Всѧхва́льнїи):*
*Troparion:*
O most glorious Martyr Menas, beaten upon the soles of thy feet, having thine eyes gouged out, and having thy theologically speaking tongue cut out, thou didst endure most steadfastly, looking unto the divine recompenses; therefore pray thou that there may be granted unto our souls peace and great mercy!

*Troparion:*
The glorious Hermogenes welcomes the cutting off of hands and the severance of feet; and looking upon the fire, he showed forth a greater warmth of heart, cleaving unto God, Whom he now also implores that there may be granted unto our souls peace and great mercy.

*Troparion:*
Having your limbs crushed, O wise ones, ye were cast into the depth of the sea, O saints; but by a higher beckoning ye steered unto the calm haven of delight, having drowned the malice of the serpent. Therefore pray ye that there may be granted unto our souls peace and great mercy!

*Glory, both now, Theotokion, the same Tone and Podoben (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*
Incorruptibly didst thou bear God, Who abolished corruption and poured forth incorruption, O incorrupt and spotless one! Therefore I pray thee: me who am corrupted by grievous things, do thou renew by thy prayers, O pure one, that I may glorify thee, that with love I may magnify thee who hast magnified our race!

*Stavrotheotokion, the same Tone and Podoben (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*
When the spotless Ewe-lamb once beheld upon the Tree Him Whom she had borne from a seedless womb, not enduring the wounding of maternal bowels, tearing her hair, she said: Thou Who by Thy beckoning upholdest all creation, how art Thou lifted up upon the Cross like a condemned man, willing by all means to save mankind?

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos.*

*Troparion, Tone 8:*
Having through abstinence put to death the fiery forms and motions of the passions, the martyrs of Christ received grace to drive away the infirmities of the ailing, and both while living and after their end to work miracles. Truly a most glorious wonder, that bare bones pour forth healings! Glory to the only God and Creator!

*At Matins, both Canons of the Octoechos; and the Canon of the Saints on 4.*

*Whose acrostic is:* The steadfast crown-bearing martyrs will I hymn. Joseph.[^80]

*Tone 1. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Delivered from bitter bondage, Israel passed through the impassable deep as upon dry land; seeing the enemy drowned, they sing a hymn unto God as their Benefactor, Who works wonders with a high arm, for He hath been glorified!

*Troparion:*
Adorned with crowns of glory, standing before the throne of God, and filled with divine light, deliver from the darkening of passions, O martyrs, them that with love celebrate your light-bearing memory!

*Troparion:*
Loving divine blessing, desiring the beauty of God, ye cast aside the pleasant things of life and all deceitful power, and through death ye found endless life, O martyrs.

*Troparion:*
Kindled with divine zeal, they extinguished the fire of impiety; and radiating the light of piety unto all, the great-minded Hermogenes and Menas were shown forth most brightly as luminaries through faith.

*Theotokion:*
That thy servants may be delivered from the hold of passions, O all-spotless Maiden, entreat fervently thy Lord and Master, Whom thou didst incarnate from thy most pure blood, Who hath partaken of our nature.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Unto the Son born incorruptibly of the Father before the ages, and in the last times incarnate without seed of the Virgin, Christ God, let us cry aloud: Thou Who hast exalted our horn, holy art Thou, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Clearly enlightened with heavenly radiance, O martyrs, ye destroyed the darkness of the idols' deceit; and ye beamed forth upon us the brightness of healings, as we sing unto the God of all: Holy art Thou, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Following the dying of the living Master, O marvelous Menas, thou art crushed in the soles of thy feet, and thou crushest the head of the tormentor, the enemy, establishing thy feet upon the firm path of martyrdom, O most valiant martyr!

*Troparion:*
Hermogenes sings unto the Savior when his hands are cut off, having made the garment of priesthood brighter by the dipping of blood, and being shown forth by grace as an imitator of Him Who suffered in the flesh.

*Theotokion:*
Finding thee alone among women fair in beauty, Christ came forth flesh-bearing from thy womb, O Maiden, enlightening our race with divine beauties. Therefore do we honor thee.

*Kontakion, Tone 1, Podoben: "The angelic choir" (Ли́къ а҆́ггелскїй):*
Let us all honor together with sacred sweet singing the marvelous Menas, the divine Hermogenes, and Eugraphus, as those who honored the Lord and suffered for Him, and attained unto the choir of the bodiless hosts in the heavens, and pour forth miracles!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom and Word" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
Despising worldly glory, winged with divine glory, Menas, Hermogenes, and the glorious Eugraphus, with zealous disposition endured the burden of grievous torments, sparing not their flesh. Therefore after their end, being cast into the depth of the sea, they were directed unto the divine desire. Unto whom let us cry aloud with faith: Pray ye unto Christ God, that He grant remission of sins unto them that with love honor your holy memory!

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*
Fallen into manifold afflictions from visible and invisible enemies, held fast by the tempest of mine unnumbered transgressions, and as unto a fervent protection and my shelter, O pure one, unto the haven of thy goodness do I flee. Therefore, O most pure one, entreat Him Who was incarnate from thee without seed fervently on behalf of all thy servants who unceasingly pray unto thee, O all-pure Birthgiver of God: praying Him ever to grant remission of transgressions unto them that worthily hymn thy glory!

*Stavrotheotokion:*
Beholding the Lamb and Shepherd and Deliverer upon the Cross, the Ewe-lamb cried aloud weeping, and bitterly lamenting, exclaimed: The world indeed rejoices, receiving deliverance through Thee, but my womb burns, beholding Thy crucifixion which Thou endurest for the tenderness of Thy mercy, O long-suffering Lord, Abyss of mercy and inexhaustible Fountain of compunction; and grant remission of transgressions unto them that with faith sing of Thy divine passions!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
A rod from the root of Jesse, and a flower from it, O Christ, Thou hast budded from the Virgin; from the mountain praised, the densely shadowed forest, Thou hast come incarnate from her that knew not wedlock, O Immaterial One and God: glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Proclaiming radiant laws, thou didst unlawfully endure the gouging out of thine eyes, O Menas, having the eyes of thy heart gazing intently toward the unsetting Light, and singing with joy: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Thy tongue was shown forth sharpened by the fire of the Spirit most wisely when it was cut out; for it spoke clearly the wonders of God, turning the tormentor's speechlessness into the pious glory of Him Who made it manifest.

*Troparion:*
Having his shoulders bound, Hermogenes patiently endures having his feet cut off, trampling upon the serpent's head, and with an unyielding disposition preparing the path of martyrdom that leads unto the life of heavenly brightness.

*Troparion:*
Christ appears unto thee who didst keep thy soul unharmed, O Menas, healing thy wounds and bidding thee endure valiantly, that through thee the Desirer of mercy might work salvation for all that behold!

*Theotokion:*
Thou hast grown a rod from the root of Jesse, having blossomed forth the Sweetener of all creation, Who withered the gardens of barren knowledge, and piously planted in us the truest faith, O pure, all-hymned Virgin!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Being the God of peace and Father of compassions, Thou hast sent unto us the Angel of Thy great counsel, granting peace; therefore, guided unto the light of the knowledge of God, watching early from the night, we glorify Thee, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
Why dost thou rage altogether? the martyrs cried together unto the most lawless judge; grant strength, He stands by us, Who alone is invincible in might, for Whose sake we endure wounds most steadfastly!

*Troparion:*
Sudden was the turning of the marvelous Hermogenes unto the Lord; for he is cleansed by the bath, and by divine judgment receives the light of the hierarchal office, illuminating with his eyes them that are in the night of grievous evils.

*Troparion:*
Forsaking the unskilled mind of subtleties, ye were captured by the simple meshes of unlettered men, when the Spirit truly made you wise, O martyrs, and through faith made you mighty in strength against every tempest of torments.

*Theotokion:*
More exalted than the holy angels wast thou shown forth, O pure Virgin, having given birth unto the Angel of great counsel, God Emmanuel, Who through His descent became man, O Maiden, by His unsearchable loving-kindness.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
The sea beast spewed forth Jonah as an infant from its belly, such as it received him; and the Word, having dwelt in the Virgin and taken flesh, came forth, having preserved her incorrupt: for from Him Who suffered no corruption, He kept her that bare Him unharmed.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst save Jonah from the beast on the third day, prefiguring Thy burial, O Almighty One; and the bodies of the martyrs cast into the deep, Thou didst direct unto the calmest haven of burial, where Thy divine will appointed, for the preservation of us the faithful.

*Troparion:*
The deep yields up your bodies unharmed, O invincible martyrs, with heavenly angels leading the way, O blessed ones, and announcing unto all your resting-place, which is a common wellspring of healings and deliverance from passions of the soul.

*Troparion:*
The angelic ranks marveled at your endurance, how in the body ye conquered the bodiless serpent, O martyrs, and were entwined with crowns of victory, standing before the throne of God and illuminated with divine rays.

*Theotokion:*
Death was abolished through thee, O Virgin, for thou didst bear Christ our Life, Who grants immortality and divine rejoicing unto them that purely believe in Him; pray thou unto Him, O all-spotless one, to deliver thy servants from perils!

*Kontakion, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up" (Вознесы́йся):*
The melodious sound of thy words, having drawn Hermogenes up from the depth of perdition, set him upon the rock of life; whence also Eugraphus, having rebuked the emperor, rejoicing is struck down in his glorious head. But pray fervently, O Menas, that all who honor thee with love may be saved!

*Ikos:*
Divinely-becoming was thy life, and sweet thy word; great was thy boldness, O Menas, and thy teaching; and thy courage toward the lawless was marvelous, shown forth steadfast, fearing nothing; but instructing all, thou didst teach them to worship the one God in three Persons, and to serve with an undoubting mind; and again, that for our sake now in the last times the Son of God took flesh; confessing Whom, thou didst catch Hermogenes: therefore with him pray, that all who honor thee with love may be saved!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The youths brought up together in piety, having despised the ungodly decree, were not afraid of the threat of fire; but standing in the midst of the flame, they sang: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Troparion:*
Where the voice of them that feast purely and the sound is heard, with a joyful soul have ye taken up dwelling, O sufferers, filled with gladness and singing: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Troparion:*
Sweet unto me, cried Hermogenes, is the death by which I die: to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain boundless! Let my limbs be cut off as I sing with love: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Troparion:*
With most steadfast wisdom hast thou inscribed thy name in the book of the living of the heavenly One, O wise Eugraphus; for when thy head was severed, thou didst mount as upon a chariot by thy blood, and didst pass over unto the unsetting Light!

*Theotokion:*
Without burning thy womb, nor shaking the signs of virginity, the incarnate Word came forth from thee, granting incorruption and life unto us, O Maiden, who sing: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
The dew-bearing furnace portrayed the image of a wonder beyond nature: for it burns not the youths whom it received, even as the fire of the Godhead burned not the Virgin's womb into which it entered. Therefore let us sing and chant: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
The haughty one falls before thy feet, trampled upon, O God-wise Menas; for having deprived thee of eyes and tongue, he shook not the steadfastness of the better purpose of thy mind. Therefore with joy didst thou cry aloud: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
When by most cruel piercing the most senseless tormentor deprived thee of both hands and feet, then, O wise Hermogenes, desiring an intensification [of struggle],[^81] thou didst sing unto Christ, rejoicing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
I sing thy divine sufferings, O Menas; I honor the struggles of Hermogenes; I bow down before their relics; I hymn the wounds, the bonds, persecutions, and death, whereby they ascended unto life, crying aloud: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
We know thee to be the jar holding the manna of the Godhead, O Maiden, the ark, and table, and lampstand, the throne of God, and palace, and the bridge leading across unto divine life, for them that sing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
The unburnt bush showed forth an image of thy pure childbearing; and now we pray thee to extinguish the furnace of afflictions that rages against us, that we may unceasingly magnify thee, O Birthgiver of God!

*Troparion:*
Behold, the light-bearing solemnity of the radiant martyrs hath shone forth upon all, illuminating the ends of the universe and taking away blindness of souls; let us run together with great zeal and draw sanctification!

*Troparion:*
Ye who obtained the good things of heavenly glory, whereunto ye were accounted worthy, pray ye, as standing ever before God, that they who with faith honor your bright memory may obtain them, O great martyrs, by your beckoning![^82]

*Troparion:*
Ye brought body and soul as a spotless sacrifice unto the Creator of all, being consumed as a whole burnt-offering by the fire of torments, and were numbered among the choirs of martyrs, being enlightened with the purest light, O all-lauded ones!

*Troparion:*
The mansions were opened and ye took up dwelling therein, the radiant divine choir of martyrs; and it stands before the Father, the Son, and the Spirit, clearly enjoying deification: Menas with Hermogenes and Eugraphus, the God-wise!

*Theotokion:*
Our rejected nature beheld the shining brightness of thy childbearing, O all-spotless one, and was delivered from the night of ignorance and the dark turmoil of passions. Therefore do we honor thee as the cause of our salvation!

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "Thou Who didst adorn heaven with stars" (Не́бо ѕвѣзда́ми):*
By thy rhetorical words and divine miracles, O Menas, thou didst draw the sacred Hermogenes as a fellow sufferer; with whom, and with Eugraphus, we now most joyfully praise thee!

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast shown forth, O Virgin, as the mountain which the divine Habakkuk foresaw of old, densely shadowed and thickly wooded; and David names thee a rich and fertile mountain.

*At the Liturgy, Prokeimenon, Tone 4:*
Unto the saints that are in His earth, the Lord hath been marvelous; He hath wrought all His desires in them. *Verse:* I foresaw the Lord always before me...

*Epistle to the Ephesians, pericope 233.*[^83]

*Alleluia, Tone 4:*
The righteous cried, and the Lord heard them. *Verse:* Many are the afflictions of the righteous...

*Gospel of Luke, pericope 106.*[^84]

*Communion Hymn:*
Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous!

*In the same month, on the 11th day:*
*Of our venerable Father Daniel the Stylite.*

*Alleluia, or Troparion, Tone 8.*

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera, 3, Tone 8, Podoben: "What shall we call you, O holy ones" (Что́ вы̀ нарече́мъ):*
*Sticheron:*
What shall we proclaim thee, O Daniel? Rooter-out of passions and cultivator of virtues; true worker of miracles and intercessor for sinners; most valiant expeller of spirits; lamp radiating with piety; dwelling-place of the Spirit; champion of the Church! Pray that our souls may be saved!

*Sticheron:*
What shall we name thee, O Daniel? Fasting ascetic, for thou didst subdue the passions unto the mind; sufferer, for thou didst endure every harshness, lifted up upon the height of the pillar from the earth, planted upon the rock of truth; most zealous ascetic, and most skilled physician! Pray that our souls may be saved!

*Sticheron:*
What shall we call thee now, O Daniel? Pattern of monastics, and teacher of temperance; adornment of the faithful, and dispenser of healings; lamp shedding light upon them that are in darkness; fellow citizen and peer of the angels; dweller of paradise and heavenly man! Pray that our souls may be saved!

*Other Stichera of the most holy Birthgiver of God, the same Tone and Podoben (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже).*

*If Alleluia is chanted, these Stichera are sung first.*

*Sticheron:*
A strange mystery, O pure Virgin, and dreadful, is that of thy seedless childbearing, surpassing every human thought; for Him Whom the many-eyed cannot bear to gaze upon, and all the ranks of holy angels tremble before, thou hast borne for us in the flesh, without departing from the Father's essence. We glorify her that bare thee, O Bride of God!

*Sticheron:*
Unto whom art thou become like, O wretched soul,[^85] not looking up at all unto repentance, and not fearing the fire that awaits the wicked? Arise, and call upon the only speedy one for protection, and cry aloud: O Virgin Mother, pray Thy Son and our God, to deliver me from the snares of the deceiver!

*Sticheron:*
Having borne the intolerable Fire that consumes sins and bedews the faithful, burn up by thy prayers the material kindling of mine immeasurable transgressions, O all-spotless and pure one! And with dew refresh my soul corrupted by passions, that I, thy servant, may with a loud voice magnify thy mercy and power!

*Glory, both now, Theotokion, the same Tone and Podoben (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*
O Protection of all, Birthgiver of God, unto me who am burdened by the deep of darkness and ever submerged by the tempestuous waves of the grievous things of life, send down a drop of thy mercy, and give me a hand of help; and account me worthy of the portion of the elect and righteous, as having borne the Abyss of the Lover of mankind!

*If it be Wednesday or Friday, Both now, Stavrotheotokion, the same Tone and Podoben (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*
When the Ewe-lamb beheld the Lamb upon the Tree, stretched out willingly upon the Cross, she cried aloud maternally, grieving with weeping: O my Son, what is this strange sight? Giving life unto all as Lord, how art Thou put to death art put to death, O longsuffering One, Who grantest resurrection unto those on earth? I glorify Thy manifold condescension, O my God.

*If "God is the Lord" [be sung]: Glory..., Tone 1. Of the Studite:*[^86]

Having well traded with the talent entrusted unto thee by Christ, O venerable father, even after death thou hast been shown forth as an expeller of demons, and a physician of diverse diseases, a pillar and foundation, and a holy mountain of the Church of Christ; therefore we beseech thee, O Daniel the wonderworker: Entreat peace and great mercy for our souls.

*Both now, Theotokion.*

*At the Aposticha, of the Octoechos.*

*Troparion, Tone 1:*

A pillar of endurance hast thou been, rivaling the forebears, O venerable one: Job in sufferings, Joseph in temptations, and the life of the bodiless hosts, while in the flesh, O Daniel our father: Entreat Christ God that our souls may be saved.

*At Matins, both canons of the Octoechos, and that of the Venerable One unto 4, whose acrostic is:*

With songs I honor Daniel the Stylite. By Joseph. Tone 8.

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

Let us sing unto the Lord, Who led His people through the Red Sea, for He alone hath been gloriously glorified.

*Troparia:*

As I desire with songs to praise thy memory, O blessed one, send down unto me from heaven a light-bearing ray, O Daniel.

Truly as a great sun, O father, hast thou shone forth unto the ends [of the earth], illuminating the gatherings of the faithful with the radiance of virtues.

Having submitted to the laws of the Master, O father, thou hast put the flesh to death through abstinence, and hast made it subject unto the spirit.

*Theotokion:*

Having become wholly man, He remained that which He was even after the Incarnation: the unchangeable Lord Who was born of thee, O Birthgiver of God.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

O Lord, Maker of the celestial vault and Builder of the Church: Do Thou establish me in Thy love, O Summit of desires, Firm Foundation of the faithful, O only Lover of mankind.

*Troparia:*

Having parted the sea of passions with the rod of abstinence, O father, thou hast crossed over undrowned, and hast attained unto the mountain of true dispassion, and conversed with God in purity of mind.

Having ascended unto the height of virtues, thou wast made known unto the world; for standing elevated upon a pillar, thou didst illumine with the radiance of marvelous wonders those who flee unto thee with faith.

Established upon the rock of the knowledge of God, by all demonic machinations thou hast been shown forth as unshakable; for upon a pillar thou didst elevate thy body on earth, and didst give wings to thy soul toward heavenly things.

*Theotokion:*

Deliver me from the assault of passions, O Sovereign Lady, and overcome now the enemies that wage war against me; establish me upon the rock of God's will; illumine my soul, O portal of divine light.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "While the soldiers were guarding Thy tomb" (Гро́бъ тво́й):*[^87]

Ascending upon the pillar of the bodily [frame], O father, by abstinence, O Daniel, thou didst exhaust the flesh; therefore thou wast made a worthy vessel of the Spirit; and having received divine grace, O thrice-blessed one, thou drivest away every disease from those who honor thy memory with faith.

*Glory..., Both now, Theotokion:*

O Hope of Christians, O all-holy Virgin, Whom thou didst bear as God beyond understanding and word, entreat Him unceasingly for those who praise thee, to grant the remission of all our sins and amendment of life unto those who ever glorify thee with faith and love.

*Stavrotheotokion:*

The undefiled Ewe-lamb, beholding the Lamb and Shepherd suspended dead upon the Tree, weeping, cried aloud, maternally lamenting: How shall I endure Thine ineffable descent, O my Son, and Thy voluntary sufferings, O all-good God?

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

Thou art my strength, O Lord, Thou art also my power; Thou art my God, Thou art my rejoicing, Who hast not left the bosom of the Father, and hast visited our poverty; therefore with the Prophet Habakkuk I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparia:*

Truly as a radiant sun, O ever-memorable father, thou didst behold shining upon a pillar the servant of God, Symeon; and through the divine splendors flowing from him thou wast divinely illuminated, O Daniel, and didst walk following his way of life.

Thou didst conquer the demonic hosts with the weapon of faith, and didst drown them with the streams of thy prayers, driving away their ruin, O father, which they wrought against seafarers, and didst save those who sing unto God in faith: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

Thou didst mortify the [passions] of the body, O all-blessed one, and didst stand all night long as if bodiless, possessing a soul's eye that is not haughty, and receiving purely, as a mirror, the ray of the Spirit and divine manifestations with pure thoughts.

*Theotokion:*

The laws of nature are renewed in thee; for [thou didst bear] the Lawgiver for thou hast borne the Word, beyond cause and beyond word, truly most pure one, Who hath delivered the human race from irrationality, of those who faithfully sing: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

Why hast Thou cast me away from Thy face, O Light unwaning, and a strange darkness hath covered me, the wretched one? But turn me back, and guide my paths toward the light of Thy commandments, I pray Thee.

*Troparia:*

That thou mightest obtain immortal glory, thou didst mortify carnal desires, O father, and didst bridle the surges of passions through the labors of abstinence; and thou hast been shown forth as a river of wonders, and a fountain of healings, O ever-memorable one.

Walking upon that path, O father, which marvelous Symeon trod upon earth, when thou wast in awe, O blessed one, he appeared unto thee, shown unto thee with two angels, crying aloud: Come and stand by me, ascending toward God through grace.

Illumined with a celestial ray, O father, and with divine splendor, thou didst drive away demonic gloom and the mist of passions; and thou hast been shown forth as a light-radiant pillar, and truly a ladder leading the faithful upward unto God.

*Theotokion:*

Having borne the Master, thou hast been revealed as higher than the celestial hosts, and thou hast divinized the nature of earthly beings, O Maiden Bride of God; therefore, as the most true Birthgiver of God, with soul and tongue we, the faithful, glorify thee, O Virgin.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

Cleanse me, O Savior, for many are mine iniquities, and lead me up from the abyss of evils, I pray Thee; for unto Thee have I cried, and do Thou hear me, O God of my salvation.

*Troparia:*

Thy mind, illuminated through drawing near unto God, remained uncaptured by the fire of pleasures, O father, having become superior to passions and attachment unto the flesh.

Thy soul was filled with the living waters of the gifts of the Spirit, O divinely wise and all-blessed one; and truly it poured forth rivers of healings that dry up the torrents of passions.

*Theotokion:*

We, the faithful, have all acquired thee as an intercessor and a rampart, being ever in peril in the depth of evils and the tempest of afflictions: O Birthgiver of God, only refuge of earthly beings.

*Kontakion, Tone 8, Podoben: "As first-fruits of nature" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ нача́тки):*

As a star of manifold light, ascending upon the pillar, O blessed one, thou didst enlighten the world with thy venerable deeds and hast driven away the darkness of delusion, O father; therefore we beseech thee, even now cause the unwaning light of understanding to shine in the hearts of thy servants.

*Ikos:*

An unclean song is offered for the praise of thy struggles, O father, for I have not a clean heart, since I have shamefully defiled it; but do thou grant me speech, O holy one, cleanly to hymn thy life, at which the angels also were truly astonished; for thou wast as if bodiless, having received the unwaning light of understanding.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

The Hebrew youths in the furnace boldly trampled upon the flame, and turned the fire into dew, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages!

*Troparia:*

The angelic ranks were astonished at thy standing, O all-blessed God-bearer; for having embraced their way of life while in the body, thou didst cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages!

Through the height of immaterial life, and shining with the radiance of prophecy, thou didst make the rays of healings to shine upon us who piously honor thee, O Daniel, bearer of wonders.

Dispel the mist of my passions through the brightness of thy prayer, O all-blessed one, and guide me onto the path of life as I cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages!

*Theotokion:*

Be merciful unto me, O Virgin, and heal me who am wounded by the weapon of sin through the medicine of thy prayer, as I cry aloud: Blessed is the Fruit of thy womb!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

Sevenfold did the Chaldean tormentor furiously kindle the furnace for the pious ones; but seeing them saved by a higher power, he cried aloud unto the Creator and Redeemer: Youths, bless; priests, hymn; people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparia:*

The ultimate end of desires, the supreme summit of good things, O God-bearing father, thou hast assuredly attained, clad with the wings of virtuous deeds; and together with the bodiless hosts, O Daniel, thou criest aloud: Youths, bless; priests, hymn; people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

The power of God, manifestly strengthening Thee, caused Thee to endure the bitter cold of winter, and the scorching heat of the sun, and the corruption of thy flesh, and the affliction of worms that came forth from it, as thou didst cry aloud: Youths, bless; priests, hymn; people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

A new Job hast thou appeared, O right marvelous Daniel, beset by a multitude of temptations and afflictions: thou didst emulate the meekness of David, the guilelessness of Jacob, and the chastity of Joseph, crying aloud with thanksgiving: Youths, bless; priests, hymn; people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*

Holding the orthodox mind of the Fathers, O all-holy Sovereign Lady, and following thy words, O all-undefiled one, we now call thee blessed, for thou didst bear for us the blessed God; Whom we hymn in two natures and in one Hypostasis, crying aloud: Youths, bless; priests, hymn; people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

Every hearing was awestruck at the ineffable condescension of God, how the Most High willingly came down even unto the flesh, being made man from a virginal womb; therefore, O most pure Birthgiver of God, we, the faithful, magnify thee.

*Troparia:*

Behold, the heavenly gates were opened unto thee when thou didst repose and finish thy course, O father, and the ranks of angels received thee; and Christ the Crowngiver crowned thee with the glory of righteousness. Hymning Him, we, the faithful, magnify Him.

Like a lily of the field, O father, thou didst blossom in the paradise of abstinence, and like a cypress thou didst rise unto the height of perfection; like an olive tree, according to the psalm, thou didst appear, anointing our faces and hearts with the oil of thy labors.

Creation recognized thee as a pillar established upon the foundation of virtues, an unshakable mirror, a fountain of wonders, a tranquil haven, a treasure of healings, a receptacle of the Spirit; therefore today, O Daniel, we celebrate thy memory.

Brighter than the sun hath thy divine memory shone forth unto us today, O venerable one, illuminating the hearts of the faithful with the light of righteousness, and driving away the gloom of soul-corrupting passions; celebrating it, we piously hymn thee.

*Theotokion:*

Spare me, O Savior Who wast born, and Who didst preserve her that bare Thee incorrupt after childbirth, when Thou shalt sit to judge my deeds; overlook mine iniquities and my sins, as Thou art sinless, as God merciful and the Lover of mankind.

*Exapostilarion of the Octoechos. Glory... of the Saint, Podoben: "O Light unchangeable" (Свѣ́те неизмѣ́нный):*[^88]

The pillar cries aloud thy struggles with ineffable voices, as thou didst suffer unsheltered from contrary elements; whence like a light-bearing luminary thou didst shine forth, O father, illuminating all creation.

*Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:*

With unceasing songs we call thee blessed, O Virgin, for thou didst bear One of the Trinity, O Birthgiver of God, and dost hold in thy divine hands the super-essential Word, unconfusedly and unchangeably.

*At the Aposticha, of the Octoechos.*

*It is needful to know: That from this 11th day the Sunday of the Forefathers can begin, and it extends in this same December unto the 17th day. And it happens thus: If the Nativity of Christ fall on a Sunday:*[^89]

*Then the Sunday of the Forefathers is on the 11th day of December; and the Sunday of the Holy Fathers, which is before the Nativity of Christ, is on the 18th day of December.*

*If the Nativity of Christ fall on a Monday:*

*Then the Sunday of the Forefathers is on the 17th day of December; and the Sunday of the Holy Fathers, which is before the Nativity of Christ, is then on the 24th day of December.*

*If the Nativity of Christ fall on a Tuesday:*

*Then the Sunday of the Forefathers is on the 16th day of December; and the Sunday of the Holy Fathers, which is before the Nativity of Christ, is on the 23rd day of December.*

*If the Nativity of Christ fall on a Wednesday:*

*Then the Sunday of the Forefathers is on the 15th day of December; and the Sunday of the Holy Fathers is on the 22nd day of December.*

*If the Nativity of Christ fall on a Thursday:*

*Then the Sunday of the Forefathers is on the 14th day of December; and the Sunday of the Holy Fathers is on the 21st day of December.*

*If the Nativity of Christ fall on a Friday:*

*Then the Sunday of the Forefathers is on the 13th day of December; and the Sunday of the Holy Fathers is on the 20th day of December.*

*If the Nativity of Christ fall on a Saturday:*

*Then the Sunday of the Forefathers is on the 12th day of December; and the Sunday of the Holy Fathers, which is before the Nativity of Christ, is on the 19th day of December.*[^90]

*Here observe the Sunday of the Holy Forefathers, on whichever date it happens to occur, whether before the 28th Sunday [after Pentecost] or after: at the Liturgy read the Gospel of the 28th Sunday, Luke, Pericope 76: "A certain man made a great supper." Without change, this one alone. And on the 28th Sunday read the sequential [Gospel], whichever of another Sunday happens to fall.*

*It is needful to know concerning the Sunday of the Holy Forefathers:*

*When the Sunday of the Holy Forefathers occurs, the office of the saint falling on that Sunday is omitted, and we sing it beforehand on Friday at Compline. On Saturday at Small Vespers we sing according to the custom.*[^91]

*At Great Vespers, on "Lord, I have cried," the Resurrection stichera, 3; and Anatolian, 3; and of the Holy Forefathers, 4, Tone 8, Podoben: "Those in Eden" (И҆́же во є҆де́мѣ):*

*Who before the Law:*
