*And Both now, Theotokion:*

*Behold, the prophecy of Isaiah hath been fulfilled:*

*At the Aposticha, the Resurrection stichera. Glory... of the Forefathers, Tone 3:*

*The assembly of the Forefathers:*

*And Both now, Theotokion:*

*Without seed, of the Holy Spirit:*

*At the Blessing of the Loaves, Troparion: "Birthgiver of God, Virgin," twice; and of the Forefathers, once, Tone 2:*

*Through faith Thou didst justify the Forefathers:*

*At Matins, on "God is the Lord," the Resurrection troparion, twice; Glory..., Both now, of the Forefathers. After the 1st and after the 2nd Kathisma, the Resurrection sessional hymns; and the reading in the Commentary Gospel, the sequence of the Sunday. Thereafter the Polyeleos; and the Resurrection troparia: "The angelic assembly." Then the Hypakoe of the Tone; and the Sessional Hymn of the Forefathers; and a reading. The Anavathmoi, and the Prokeimenon of the Tone. "Let every breath." The Resurrection Gospel; and "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ." Psalm 50. The Resurrection Sticheron.*

*The Resurrection Canon, with the Heirmos unto 4; and of the Children unto 4, Tone 8; and of the Forefathers unto 6, Tone 6. Katavasia: "Christ is born." After Ode 3, the Hypakoe of the Forefathers, once, Tone 2: "Into the dew for the children." After Ode 6, the Kontakion of the Forefathers, Tone 6: "Disdaining the image made by hands;" and the Ikos. After Ode 9, the Resurrection Exapostilarion; Glory... of the Forefathers; Both now, Theotokion. At the Praises, the Resurrection stichera, 4; and of the Holy Forefathers, 4, Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*

*Glory... of the Forefathers, Tone 7:*

*Come, all ye faithful:*

*And Both now: "Most blessed art thou." The Great Doxology; and the Dismissal. And we sing the Gospel Sticheron in the narthex; and the First Hour; and the final Dismissal.*

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Tone, unto 6; and of the Forefathers, Ode 3, unto 4. After the Entrance, the Resurrection troparion, and of the Forefathers; Glory..., Both now, Kontakion of the Forefathers. Prokeimenon, the Song of the Fathers, Tone 4: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our Fathers;" Verse: "For righteous art Thou." Epistle of the Forefathers, to the Colossians, Pericope 257. Alleluia, Tone 4: "Moses and Aaron." Gospel of Luke, Pericope 76. The sequence* of that Sunday is omitted. Communion Verse: "Praise the Lord;" another: "Rejoice in the Lord."[^92]

*SUNDAY OF THE HOLY FOREFATHERS:*

*At "Lord, I have cried," the Resurrection stichera, 3; and Anatolian, 3; and of the Forefathers unto 4, Tone 8, Podoben: "Those in Eden" (И҆́же во є҆де́мѣ):*

*Stichera of the Forefathers:*

Celebrating today the memory of the Forefathers, O ye faithful, let us hymn Christ the Redeemer, Who hath magnified them among all the nations, and the Lord Who hath faithfully wrought marvelous wonders, as One sovereign and mighty; and Who from them hath shown forth unto us a rod of strength: the only unwedded and pure Maiden of God, Mary, from whom blossomed forth Christ, Who sprouted forth life for all, and inexhaustible food, and eternal salvation.

O Master Who didst deliver the holy children from the fire, and Daniel from the lions' mouths; Who didst bless Abraham, and Isaac Thy servant, and his son Jacob; Who wast pleased to be born of their seed like unto us, that by Thy Cross and Resurrection Thou mightest save our forefathers who had slipped before, and having broken the bonds of death, didst raise up together all who from the ages were among the dead, worshiping Thee, O Christ, King of the ages.

As in coolness in the midst of the flame, rejoicing by the dew of the Spirit, the divine children walked, mystically prefiguring in it the Trinity and the Incarnation of Christ, and as wise ones through faith they quenched the power of the fire; and Daniel the righteous appeared as a bridler of lions: Entreated by their prayers, O Savior, Lover of mankind, deliver us also from unquenchable and eternal fire, and make us worthy of Thy kingdom, O Lord.

As if in dew, Thy faithful and holy children in the furnace of flaming fire mystically prepictured beforehand Thy coming from the Virgin, which hath shone forth unburnt upon us; and Daniel the righteous, marvelous among the prophets, clearly setting forth Thy divine second coming: I beheld until the thrones were placed, he says, and the Judge sat, and a river of fire flowed forth: from which may we be delivered, O Christ, by their prayers, O Master![^93]

*Glory..., Tone 6. By Anatolius:*

All the Fathers who were before the Law let us praise today, O ye faithful: Abraham the beloved of God, and Isaac who was born of promise, and Jacob, and the twelve Patriarchs; David the most meek, and Daniel the prophet of desires, glorifying together with them the three children who turned the furnace into dew, asking forgiveness from Christ God, Who is glorified in His saints.

*Both now, 1st Theotokion of the Tone. At the Litiya, the sticheron of the Temple. Glory..., Tone 1:*

The renowned prophets, having shone forth with the rays of divine speech, are ever called blessed; and bearing the fruit of the utterances of the Spirit, they proclaimed unto all the ineffable Nativity of Christ God, having legally accomplished their end after living a most marvelous life.

*Both now, Theotokion:*

Behold, the prophecy of Isaiah hath been fulfilled:

*At the Aposticha, the Resurrection stichera. Glory..., Tone 3. By Germanus:*

Come, ye feast-lovers, let us praise the choir of the Forefathers in psalms: Adam the forefather, Enoch, Noah, Melchizedek, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; under the Law, Moses and Aaron, Joshua, Samuel, and David; with them Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, and Daniel, and the Twelve; together with Elijah, Elisha, and all; Zechariah and the Baptist, and those who proclaimed Christ as the life and resurrection of our race.

*Both now, Theotokion: "Without seed."*

*The Resurrection Troparion. Glory..., Both now, of the Forefathers, Tone 2:*

Through faith Thou didst justify the Forefathers, having through them betrothed the Church of the Gentiles beforehand: The saints boast in glory, for from their seed is the blessed Fruit: she that bare Thee without seed. By their prayers, O Christ God, have mercy on us.

*At Matins, on "God is the Lord," the Resurrection troparion, twice; Glory..., Both now, of the Forefathers. After both Kathismata, the Resurrection sessional hymns with their Theotokia. After the Polyeleos, the Hypakoe of the Tone, and the Sessional Hymn of the Forefathers, Tone 8, Podoben: "Guiding unto wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*

Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob let us all praise in hymnody: David the meek, Joshua, and the twelve Patriarchs, together with the three youths who quenched the fiery flame by the power of the Spirit, crying aloud unto them: Rejoice, ye who valiantly exposed the delusion of the senseless king, and entreat Christ to grant the remission of sins unto those who celebrate your holy memory with love.

*Glory..., Both now, Theotokion:*

A thankful praise, as is due, like the widow with those two mites, do I offer unto thee, O Sovereign Lady, for all thy gifts; for thou hast been shown forth as both a protection and help, ever delivering me from perils and afflictions; therefore, as one delivered from the midst of the burning furnace of those who afflict me, from my heart I cry unto thee: O Birthgiver of God, help me, entreating Christ God to give me the remission of sins; for I, thy servant, have thee as my hope.

*Three Canons: the Resurrection Canon unto 4; and of the Three Holy Children unto 4; and of the Forefathers unto 6.*

*Canon of the Three Holy Children, whose acrostic is:*[^94]

I sing of the three youths and of great Daniel. By Theophanes. Tone 8.

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

Having traversed the water as dry land, and escaped the Egyptian evil, the Israelite cried aloud: Let us sing unto our Redeemer and God!

*Troparia:*

Let us glorify the unoriginate Word, Who was divinely born of the Father before all ages, Who was seen in the furnace in a figure by the youths.

The noble children, having patiently spat upon the heads of the impious tormentor, refused to be defiled by the meats of the lawless Chaldeans.

Ye were indeed nourished spiritually by the Word, and carnally by vegetables that grow of themselves, and ye appeared unto the king with countenances fairer than those who were nourished on rich fare.

*Theotokion:*

The serpent's poison that was bitterly poured into Eve's ears dost thou heal, O Maiden who didst sprout forth from David, having borne the Redeemer.

*Another Canon of the Holy Forefathers, whose acrostic is:*

To the Fathers I fittingly now offer praise. By Joseph. Tone 1.

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

Christ is born, glorify Him! Christ from heaven, go forth to meet Him! Christ on earth, be ye lifted up! Sing unto the Lord, all the earth, and with gladness sing praise, O ye people, for He hath been glorified!

*Troparia:*

Let us offer hymnody unto the Fathers who shone forth before the Law and in the Law, and who with an upright will were well-pleasing unto the Lord and Master Who hath shone forth from the Virgin, and who now enjoy the unwaning illumination.

Let us honor Adam the first [man],[^95] honored by the hand of the Creator, who became indeed the forefather of us all, and who rests in heavenly tabernacles with all the elect.

God and Lord of all accepted Abel, who brought gifts with a most noble soul; and him, slain again by a foul and murderous hand, He brought unto the light, as a divine martyr.

*Theotokion:*

Let us give ear unto the divine sayings proclaiming Christ's manifestation: for behold, He is born in a cave of an unwedded Maiden, Whose awesome Nativity the star that appeared announces unto the astrologers.

*Katavasia:*

*Christ is born:*

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

Thou art the confirmation of those who flee unto Thee, O Lord; Thou art the light of the darkened, and my spirit hymns Thee.

*Troparia:*

Having acquired godly-taught understanding, O Master, the youths, David's descendants, godly-wisely kept the ancestral laws.

The fire burned not the most pure bodies of the pious, for they were nourished by soul-nourishing fasting.[^96]

The three youths sing a worldwide and manifold praise, marvelously dew-sprinkled in the midst of the vapor.

*Theotokion:*

That Thou mightest show us, O Master, the Childbirth from a virginal body, Thou dost save the youthful bodies in the furnace.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

Unto the Son begotten of the Father incorruptibly before the ages, and in these latter days incarnate without seed of the Virgin, unto Christ God let us cry aloud: Thou Who hast exalted our horn, holy art Thou, O Lord!

*Troparia:*

Seth's burning love toward the Creator is sung in the world; for in blameless life and soul's love he was truly well-pleasing unto Him; and now in the land of the living he cries: Holy art Thou, O Lord!

With lips and tongue and heart, Enos the marvelous, godly-wise, hoped in spirit to call upon the Master and God of all; and having lived well-pleasingly on earth, he received glory.

With sacred hymns let us call Enoch blessed; for having been well-pleasing unto the Lord, he was translated in glory, appearing better than death, as it is written, having been God's most sincere servant.

*Theotokion:*

Now the Expectation of the nations comes forth from the Virgin; and closed Bethlehem brightly opens Eden, receiving the Word incarnate, and reclining in the flesh in a manger reclining in the flesh.[^97]

*Katavasia:*

*Before the ages:*

*And the Hypakoe, Tone 2:*

The fire was turned into dew for the children, and weeping was turned into joy for the women; for an angel ministered in both wonders: changing the furnace into rest for the former, and proclaiming the three-day Resurrection unto the latter. O Author of our life, Lord, glory to Thee!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

I have heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation; I have considered Thy works, and glorified Thy divinity.

*Troparia:*

Daniel the most wise, divinely illuminated in mind, resolved the dreams of sovereigns by divine grace.

The suffering of the children in the furnace shines with wonders; for they caught the tormentor unto the knowledge of Thee, O Almighty One.

The harmony of organs and all-melodious musical songs drew not the valiant ones, nor did they bow down to the golden image.

*Theotokion:*

With songs, O all-hymned one, the children in Babylon honor Thy super-divine Son, Whom they recognized in the furnace.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

A rod from the root of Jesse, and a flower from it, O Christ, hast Thou blossomed forth from the Virgin; from the mountain praised and overshadowed in the thicket hast Thou come, incarnate of her that knew not a husband, O immaterial One and God: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^98]

*Troparia:*

Let us offer praise unto God, honoring with songs Noah, truly the sacred righteous one; for adorned in all the divine commandments he appeared as one well-pleasing unto Christ; unto Whom we, the faithful, sing: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

God, beholding the nobility and simplicity of thy character, and in all things perfect, clearly shows thee as the leader of the second world, having saved for it every kind of human seed from the deluge, as He Himself commanded.

Noah, who kept the law of God uninjured, and was found then righteous in his generation, and of old saved the kinds of brute beasts in an ancient ark by the all-effective command, let us piously call blessed with hymns.

The wine of compunction gushes forth unto us who honor thee, O blessed Noah; thy memory ever gladdening both souls and hearts of those who purely call blessed thine honorable virtues and godly manner of life.

*Theotokion:*

Now our Deliverance reclines in a manger, and in swaddling bands is wrapped like an infant; and the Eastern kings, the Magi, come to behold Him as God and King born of the pure one, and to worship Him with gifts in faith.[^99]

*Katavasia:*

*A rod from the root of Jesse.*

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

Why hast Thou cast me away from Thy presence, O Light unwaning, and a strange darkness hath covered me, the wretched one? But turn me back, and guide my paths toward the light of Thy commandments, I pray Thee.

*Troparia:*

Having been taught the Law, O Savior, Thy favored ones did not reject it: great Daniel with the three godly-wise youths; but having received strength from Thee, the Benefactor, they manfully conquered the tormentor.

Spiritually was Daniel instructed in Thy mysteries, O Lover of mankind; for on a cloud he beheld Thee coming as the Son of Man, as Judge and King of all nations, through the purity of his mind.

Your assembly, O children, was adorned more than a sapphire stone, as a golden ray rekindled by zeal for piety, walking with gladness in the furnace, and gathering a worldwide chorus.

*Theotokion:*

Daniel manifestly portrayed thee beforehand as a divine mountain, O Virgin; and the three youths, seeing the flame dew-sprinkled, hymn thy divine childbirth in song, as Savior, Creator, and Lord.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

O God of peace and Father of mercies, Thou hast sent unto us the Angel of Thy Great Counsel, Who grants peace; therefore, guided toward the light of the knowledge of God, watching early from the night, we glorify Thee, O Lover of mankind.

*Troparia:*

With divine praises let Shem be honored, having yielded his father's blessing; and he appeared well-pleasing before God, was numbered among the choirs of the Forefathers, and rests joyfully in the land of the living.

Abraham, as a friend of God, was accounted worthy to see the day of his Creator, and is filled with spiritual joy; honoring him with uprightness of mind, let us all call him blessed, as the divine forefather of Christ.

Thou didst behold the Trinity as far as it is possible for man to see, and didst entertain It as a true friend, O thrice-blessed Abraham; therefore thou hast received the reward of hospitable entertainment: that thou shouldest be by faith the father of countless nations.

*Theotokion:*

He Who is full empties Himself in the flesh for our sake, and He Who is without beginning receives a beginning receives a beginning; and the Rich One makes Himself poor, and God, being the Word, reclines in a manger of brute beasts like an infant, working the restoration of all who are from the ages.[^100]

*Katavasia:*

*God being of peace:*

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

The abyss of sins and the storm of transgressions troubles me, and drags me into the depth of violent despair; but stretch forth Thy strong hand unto me, as unto Peter, O Helmsman, and save me!

*Troparia:*

Having mastered the passions of the soul by the power of reason, ye became rulers of the land of the Chaldean nations; for virtue knows how to grant honor unto those who have acquired it, O wise grandsons of David.

Daniel, having of old clothed himself in life-bearing mortification, slew by food the manifest dragon that was impiously deemed a god by the Chaldeans; and he wisely slew the impious priests.

*Theotokion:*

Entreat Thy Son, O Virgin Birthgiver of God, to be a merciful Judge unto me in the day of judgment, through thy prayers, and a Deliverer from cruel things, O Mother; for in thee alone do I place my hope.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

From the belly the sea monster vomited Jonah like an infant, such as it had received; and the Word, having dwelt in the Virgin and taken flesh, came forth, having preserved her incorrupt; for He suffered no corruption, and kept her who bare Him uninjured.

*Troparia:*

Manifestly wast thou a figure of Christ's Passion, O thrice-blessed Isaac, being led up by thy father with obedience to be slaughtered; therefore thou hast been called blessed, and hast truly appeared as God's close servant, rejoicing with all the righteous.

He appeared as the most faithful servant of the God of all; therefore he also wrestled with an angel, and was called a mind that sees God; and while sleeping he beheld the divine ladder, upon which God was established, clad in flesh out of lovingkindness.

Loving obedience unto his father, Joseph was cast into a pit; for he was sold, a figure of Christ Who was slain and placed in a tomb; and he became the wheat-provider of Egypt, having been chaste and righteous, and a most true king of passions.

*Theotokion:*

A young child is made known on earth: the Son Who is ever with the Father and the Spirit; and He is wrapped in swaddling bands Who manifestly wraps the earth in mist, and reclines in a manger of brute beasts; let us who rejoice now celebrate beforehand His seedless Nativity.[^101]

*Katavasia:*

*From the belly Jonah:*

*Kontakion, Tone 6:*

Disdaining the image made by hands, but protected by the uncircumscribed Essence, O thrice-blessed ones, ye were glorified in the ordeal of fire; and standing in the midst of unbearable flame, ye called upon God: Make haste, O Compassionate One, and speed, as Thou art merciful, to our help; for Thou canst do so if Thou willest!

*Ikos:*

Stretch forth Thy hand, whereby of old the Egyptians who fought against them and the Hebrews who were fought against received trial; leave us not, lest death that thirsts for us devour us, and Satan who hates us; but draw near unto us, and spare our souls, as Thou didst once spare Thy children who were in Babylon, who unceasingly glorified Thee, and who for Thy sake were cast into the furnace, and from it cried aloud unto Thee: Make haste, O Compassionate One, and speed, as Thou art merciful, to our help, for Thou canst do so if Thou willest!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

The pious children in Babylon bowed not down to the golden image, but dew-sprinkled in the midst of the fiery vapor, they sang a hymn, saying: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers and of us, Who art supremely exalted!

*Troparia:*

A godly voice was recognized from the midst of the fire unto the Almighty; for Azariah, having formed a divine choir, sang a hymn, saying: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

The four youths theologize the God of all and the Almighty, Who clearly appeared unto them in the furnace; and they sang a hymn, saying: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

Beholding the three cast into the furnace, when the king saw the appearance of the fourth, he named Him beforehand the Son of God, and cried aloud unto all: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*

Having a mind illuminated with divine radiance, O godly-blessed Daniel, thou didst clearly foresee the Virgin's Childbirth, depicted by mystical figures, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

The youths reared together in piety, having disdained the impious command, feared not the fiery threat, but standing in the midst of the flame, they sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

Let Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, together with Daniel, be hymned, who quenched the fiery furnace, and bridled the assaults of the lions, and sang harmoniously unto Christ: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^102]

*Troparia:*

Having lawfully suffered in temptations and unremitting afflictions, Job was truly called the servant of God: meek, guileless, upright, perfect, blameless, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

In faith let us honor Moses and Aaron, and Hur, praising Joshua, and most sacred Levi, Gideon, and Samson, and let us cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*

Behold, as the Prophet foretold, the unwedded one hath conceived God in her womb, and clearly goes to give birth in the cave of Bethlehem; unto Whom we all sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Katavasia:*

*The youths reared together in piety:*

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

Sevenfold did the Chaldean tormentor furiously kindle the furnace for the godly ones; but seeing them saved by a higher power, he cried aloud unto the Creator and Redeemer: Youths, bless; priests, hymn; people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparia:*

Striving to preserve the nobility of Abraham, ye acquired the foundation of faith that is proper unto him, and hope, O venerable ones, endurance, and awaiting of tribulations, crying aloud: Priests, bless the Master; people, supremely exalt Him unto the ages!

Having shone forth like luminaries, and gone through the earth, and illuminated it with the enlightenment of piety, having formed a worldwide chorus, they sing unto the Master Who saved them from tribulations: Youths, bless; priests, hymn; people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

Having youthfully quenched the burning furnace, and shut the jaws of the lions, the grandsons of David now rejoicing sing of Thee, the Benefactor, King of all: Youths, bless; priests, hymn; people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*

The most wise Daniel mystically instructs, O most pure one, and the three godly-wise youths depict beforehand thy Childbirth, seeing in figures Him Who ineffably came forth from thy womb; Whom the children bless, the priests hymn, and the people supremely exalt unto all ages.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

The dew-bearing furnace portrayed the image of a wonder beyond nature; for it burns not the youths whom it received, even as the fire of the Godhead burned not the Virgin's womb into which It entered. Therefore chanting let us sing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages![^103]

Today we celebrate the divine memory of the honorable fathers who have been from the ages: of Adam, and Abel, Seth, and Noah, and Enos, and Enoch, and Abraham; Melchizedek, and Job; Isaac, and faithful Jacob: crying aloud: Let creation bless the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

Let us praise the godly-fair band of divine fathers: Barak, and Nadab, and Eleazar; Josiah, and David; Jephthah; and Samuel, looking upon things to come with honor, and crying aloud: Let all creation bless the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto the ages![^104]

Let us offer praise in song unto God's prophets, praising Joel, and Micah, Zephaniah, and Habakkuk; Zechariah, and Jonah; Haggai, and Amos; and with Obadiah, Malachi, and Nahum; Isaiah, and Jeremiah, and Ezekiel; together with Daniel, Elijah, and Elisha.

With Trinitarian utterances let us, the faithful, hymn the all-holy Trinity: the unoriginate Father, the Son, and the right Holy Spirit: a single three-hypostatic Unity; Whom every breath glorifies, calling aloud: Let all creation bless the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages![^105]

Thou hast appeared, O Christ, taking flesh from virginal blood through the ineffable Word, and being born as a perfect infant in a cave, O Jesus, through the abundance of Thy tender compassion; and the star from afar announced Thee unto the astrologers, who cried aloud: With faith sing, and supremely exalt Christ unto the ages!

*Katavasia:*

*Of a wonder beyond nature:*

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

Truly we confess thee as Birthgiver of God, being saved through thee, O pure Virgin, magnifying thee with the bodiless choirs.

*Troparia:*

Ye have attained the desired end, and ye stand before the Utmost of desires, in the heavenly chambers, O all-blessed youths!

Rejoicing, ye received the sheaves that sprang from tears, the good husbandry of your tilling, bearing the fruit of the ear of grain of incorruption.

Brightness hath now worthily shone forth unto you, and joy of heart hath blossomed, for ye have taken up dwelling where grief hath fled away.

*Theotokion:*

Thou hast halted the pasture of death, O Virgin, having given birth unto the Giver of life and the Lord, Who quickens those who magnify thee in faith.[^106]

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

A strange and most glorious mystery do I behold: heaven is the cave; the cherubic throne, the Virgin; the manger, the receptacle wherein reclined the Uncontainable Christ God, Whom chanting we magnify!

*Troparia:*

By Thy power of old, daughters wrought deeds of strength, O Lord: Hannah, and Judith, and Deborah, Huldah, and Jael; Esther, Sarah; Miriam the sister of Moses; Rachel, and Rebekah, and Ruth, the great-minded.

As those who quenched the holy furnace, let us sacredly honor the children, together with Daniel the prophet, and with all the righteous manifestly, who shone forth well before the Law, and were well-pleasing unto the Master under the Law.

The most wise divine prophets, being grandsons of Abraham, proclaimed by the Spirit the Word of God born of Abraham and Judah; by their entreaties, O Jesus, have compassion upon all!

All creation is sanctified by your memory, and keeping festival, calls aloud, crying as servants: Bring prayer unceasingly unto the Lord, O blessed ones, that they who praise you well may obtain eternal good things!

*Theotokion:*

Clad in me, the Word of the Father comes forth from the Virgin, and is ineffably born in a cave. Leap for joy, O creation, magnifying with voices of thanksgiving His all-holy condescension for the sake of infants!

*Katavasia:*

*A strange mystery:*

*Resurrectional Exapostilarion:*

*Glory... of the Forefathers, Tone 2, Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Же́ны оу҆слы́шите):*

Let us praise Adam, Abel, Seth, and Enos, Enoch, and Noah; Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; Moses, Job, and Aaron; Eleazar, and Joshua; Barak, Samson, and Jephthah; David, and the rest.

*Both now:*

The great Sun, the Creator, hastens into Bethlehem to enlighten from the unwedded Virgin those who are descended from Adam; therefore the all-radiant memory of the Forefathers announces the wonder.[^107]

*At the Praises, the Resurrection stichera, 4; and of the Holy Forefathers, 4, Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*

*Stichera of the Forefathers:*

Today we celebrate * the memory of the honorable Forefathers, * hymning their life * well-pleasing unto God, * whereby they were magnified. *Twice.*

*Verse:* Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers, and praised and glorified is Thy name unto the ages!

The youths quenched * the power of fire, * dancing in the midst of the furnace, * and singing * of the almighty God.[^108]

*Verse:* For righteous art Thou in all that Thou hast done for us!

Shut up in a pit, * a dweller with wild beasts, * Daniel the prophet * was shown forth untouched * by their malice.

*Glory..., Tone 7. By Germanus:*

Come, all ye faithful, let us celebrate in faith the yearly memory of the fathers before the Law: of Abraham and those with him. Let us worthily honor the tribe of Judah; the youths in Babylon who quenched the fiery flame of the furnace, as a figure of the Trinity, let us praise together with Daniel; holding firmly to the prophetic utterances, let us cry aloud with a loud voice together with Isaiah: Behold, the Virgin shall receive in her womb, and shall bear a Son, Emmanuel, which is: God with us!

*Both now:*

*Most blessed art thou:*

*The Great Doxology. Litanies, and the Dismissal; and the Gospel Sticheron. The First Hour; and the final Dismissal.*

*Prokeimenon, the Song of the Fathers, Tone 4:*

Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers, and praised and glorified is Thy name unto the ages!

*Verse:* For righteous art Thou in all things. *The Apostle of the Forefathers, to the Colossians, pericope 257.*

*Alleluia, Tone 4:*

Moses and Aaron among His priests, and Samuel among them that call upon His name.

*Gospel of Luke, pericope 76.*

*Communion Verse:* Praise the Lord from the heavens!

*Another:* Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous!

*In the same month, on the 12th day:*[^109]
*Of our venerable Father Spyridon the Wonderworker, Bishop of Trimythous.*

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 6, Tone 2, Podoben: "Rejoice" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ):*

*Stichera:*

Rejoice, rule of hierarchs, unshakable foundation of the Church, glory of the Orthodox, fountain of wonders; inexhaustible stream of love, all-radiant luminary, instrument of the Spirit, divine mind, meek and guileless, adorned with true simplicity: heavenly man, earthly angel, husbandman of the vineyard, sincere friend of Christ! Pray Him to grant great mercy unto those who honor thee!

Meek and truly an heir of the land of the meek wast thou shown forth, O Spyridon, glory of the fathers; who by the sinews of thy wise and simple words, through divine grace, didst strangle the all-malicious and most senseless enemy Arius; and having clarified the divine decree unto all, didst make it manifest unto the faithful, elevating the saving [faith] by the Spirit; and having most clearly enlightened all the Orthodox to glorify the one Word, as truly consubstantial with the pre-unoriginate Father, Who grants great mercy unto the world!

Having mortified the passions of the flesh, by the grace of God thou didst raise the dead, and didst transform a serpent into gold; and by thy prayer, O father, thou didst bridle the rush of the river; and appearing at night unto the emperor who was in peril, thou didst heal him by drawing near unto his heart, when the Lord had most gloriously glorified thee. Therefore with a loud voice we honor thy memory, and revere the divine and sacred reliquary of thy relics, from which gushes forth a divine stream of healings, and great mercy!

*Glory..., Tone 4:*

O venerable father, blessed and wise Spyridon, for the sake of the love of God thou didst question a dead woman as if alive; and thou didst turn a serpent into gold for one held fast by poverty; and thou didst hold back the flow of the river, having compassion upon the people; and thou didst appear as a physician unto the emperor by the providence of God; and again the dead hast thou raised as His disciple; and thou didst explain the faith in the midst of many fathers, being able to do all things in Christ Who strengthens thee. Pray Him now that our souls may be saved!

*Both now, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 4, Podoben: "All-lauded martyrs" (Всехва́льнїи мч҃ницы):*[^110]

Beholding Thy unjust slaughter, O Christ, * the Virgin weeping cried aloud unto Thee: * O sweetest Child, * how dost Thou die without cause? * How dost Thou hang upon the Tree, * Who suspended all the earth upon the waters? * Leave me not alone, O Benefactor rich in mercy, * me, Thy Mother and handmaid, I pray!

*At the Aposticha, from the Octoechos.*

*Glory of the Saint, Tone 2:*

An honest, divine vessel, O venerable father, wise Spyridon, wast thou shown forth by thy virtues. Therefore, having become a champion of the Church, thou didst drive out the heresiarchs, and didst cast down Arius' blasphemy conciliar-wise unto the earth. Therefore, working wonders in deed and word, entreat the Savior that our souls may be saved!

*Both now, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*

Beholding Thee nailed unto the tree of the Cross, O Jesus, she that knew not wedlock weeping said: O sweet Child, why hast Thou left me who bare Thee alone, O unapproachable Light of the pre-unoriginate Father?[^111] Make haste and be glorified, that they who glorify Thy divine passions may receive divine glory!

*Troparion, Tone 4:*

A rule of faith and image of meekness, a teacher of abstinence hath the truth of things revealed thee unto thy flock; therefore by humility thou hast acquired exalted things, by poverty riches: O father Spyridon, entreat Christ God that our souls may be saved!

*Or this one, Tone 1:*

Thou wast shown forth as a champion of the First Council and a wonderworker, O God-bearing father Spyridon our father! Therefore thou didst call out unto a dead woman in the tomb, and didst transform a serpent into gold; and when thou chantedst holy prayers, thou hadst angels ministering with thee, O most sacred one! Glory to Him Who gave thee strength! Glory to Him Who crowned thee! Glory to Him Who works healings for all through thee!

*Glory..., Both now, Theotokion:*

*At Matins, both canons of the Octoechos, without the martyria; and the canon of the Saint, on 6.*

*A composition of Theophanes. Tone 2.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

In the deep of old, the overwhelming power laid low the whole host of Pharaoh; and the incarnate Word destroyed all-wicked sin, the most glorious Lord, for gloriously is He glorified![^112]

*Troparia:*

Having reached the land of the meek, O father, as thou wast meek, merciful, and pure, calm the present storm of my heart, that being in divine stillness, I may hymn thee in song!

Having cleansed thy soul with divine gifts, O father, thou wast a God-seer, O Spyridon, and wast enriched with the most radiant illumination of the Divine Spirit; therefore thou dost purely enlighten those who call thee blessed.

Taking thee from the sheepfolds as David, the Creator established thee as a most excellent shepherd of His rational sheepfolds, radiant in simplicity and meekness, and adorned with guilelessness, O venerable shepherd.

*Theotokion:*

All-holy pure Virgin, illuminate and sanctify my thought and my soul, I pray, destroying the clouds of my ignorance, and taking away the darkness of sin, that as is meet I may call thee blessed.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

Having established me upon the rock of faith, Thou hast enlarged my mouth against mine enemies; for my spirit rejoices when singing: There is none holy as our God, and none righteous above Thee, O Lord!

*Troparia:*

Having enlightened thy mind with dispassion, and adorned thyself with divine humility, thou didst receive the gifts of the Spirit, to drive away spirits, and to resolve the diseases of those who faithfully honor thee, O most sacred one.

Having slain the serpent, the beginner of evil, and trampled upon the disposition to love of money, having mercy on him who was in need, O hierarch, thou didst turn a serpent into a golden ornament, by thy sacred prayers, O venerable father.

Thou hast ascended the mountain of dispassion, thou hast entered into the darkness of the vision of God, and upon the tablets of thy heart thou didst receive the saving law, as a most sacred one and an unbroken servant of thy Master.

*Theotokion:*

Heal the wounds of my soul, O Bride of God; enlighten my mind darkened by negligence, that I may sing: There is none blameless above thee, O blameless one, and none pure above thee, O Birthgiver of God!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*

Being entrusted to champion the Church of Christ from the pastures of sheep, thou didst shine forth as a shepherd brought forth by God, O Spyridon; thou didst drive away the wolves of evil belief by thy words, having nourished her upon the pastures of piety. Therefore in the midst of the God-bearing fathers thou didst confirm the faith by the wisdom of the Spirit, O blessed hierarch! Entreat Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who celebrate thy holy memory with love! *Twice.*[^113]

*Glory..., Both now, Theotokion, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*

As the all-blameless bride of the Creator, as the unwedded Mother of the Deliverer, as the receptacle of the Comforter, O all-hymned one, make haste to deliver me, who am a foul dwelling-place of lawlessness and have consciously become a plaything of demons, from their evildoing, and make me a radiant dwelling-place of virtues, O radiant and incorrupt one; drive away the cloud of passions, and vouchsafe me communion on high and the unwaning light, by thy prayers!

*Stavrotheotokion:*

Beholding the Lamb, Shepherd, and Deliverer upon the Cross, the ewe-lamb exclaimed weeping, and bitterly lamenting cried aloud: The world indeed rejoices, receiving deliverance through Thee, but my womb burns, beholding Thy Crucifixion, which Thou endurest for the sake of the tender compassion of mercy, O long-suffering Lord, abyss of mercy and inexhaustible fountain! Have mercy and grant remission of transgressions unto those who sing with faith of Thy divine passions!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

Thou hast come from the Virgin, not an ambassador, nor an angel, but the Lord Himself incarnate, and hast saved me, the whole man; therefore I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparia:*

Kindled with the coals of the honorable Spirit, thou didst burn up the easily consumed matter of the passions, O all-blessed one; and with the fiery-radiant rays of thy virtues, O Spyridon, thou didst enlighten the world.

Having mortified thy bodily motions, O God-inspired one, thou didst raise the dead by thy life-creating utterance. Therefore I pray thee: Quicken my deadened soul, O father!

In obedience unto thee, the dead woman gave voice, O father; and the rushing waters of the river were held back by thy commands; for thou wast shown forth as a wonderworker, O blessed one, having received divine grace.

*Theotokion:*

The prophets announced beforehand the unsearchable depth of thy mystery incomprehensible depth; for thou alone, O pure one, didst give birth unto the Incomprehensible One, incarnate for the sake of ineffable tender compassion.[^114]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

O Christ my Savior, illumination of them that lie in darkness, salvation of the despairing: rising early unto Thee, O King of peace, enlighten me with Thy radiance; for I know no other God besides Thee!

*Troparia:*

The river of sacred gifts in Thee waters every heart, O venerable one, and richly grants health unto all; it rouses all unto the glory of God Who glorified Thee, and honored Thee with all manner of wonderworking.

The earthly king, O blessed one, clearly recognized thee as a sincere servant of the Heavenly King, and full of divine gifts, when thou camest unto him, proclaiming a great physician unto God.

Having emulated the hospitable disposition of Abraham, thou didst open the entrances of thy house unto all, and wast all things unto all, providing for those in distress, O blessed Spyridon.

*Theotokion:*

A new Infant hast thou borne unto us, O Maiden, born before the ages of the unoriginate Father; entreat Him as thy Son and God, O all-pure one, to have compassion upon those who proclaim thee with a pure soul.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

Wallowing in the abyss of sin, I call upon the unfathomable abyss of Thy tender compassion: lead me up from corruption, O God!

*Troparia:*

Gold was accounted as dirt unto thee, shining brighter than gold with dispassion, and enriched with the all-golden gifts of the Spirit, O venerable one.

Purely serving thy Master, thou hadst a multitude of the angelic hosts obeying thee, O venerable one, with invisible voices, O most sacred one.

Thy most glorious life, O all-wise one, made thee most glorious unto the world, O father. Therefore, rejoicing, we celebrate thy divine memory, chanting unto thee.

*Theotokion:*

Wider than the heavens was thy womb shown forth, O unwedded one, having contained God Who is nowhere containable, O all-holy Virgin, Bride of God.

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*

Wounded with the love of Christ, O most sacred one, having given wings unto thy mind with the ray of the Spirit, by thy active contemplation thou didst find practice, O God-receiver, having become a divine altar, asking divine radiance for all.

*Ikos:*

Let us now praise the Lord's hierarch Spyridon, sanctified from the womb Spyridon, who received the tablets of the grace of divine glory, and who is most glorious in wonders unto all creation; and as a fervent eyewitness of divine radiance; as a champion of the poor, and a guide of souls for them that sin. For he became a divine sacrifice at the throne of Christ, asking divine radiance for all.[^115]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

The contrary command of the lawless tyrant raised up a high flame; but Christ spread out spiritual dew unto the pious youths: He Who is blessed and supremely glorified!

*Troparia:*

Having acquired the guilelessness of Moses, the meekness of David, and the blamelessness of Job of the land of Uz, thou wast a dwelling-place of the Spirit, chanting, O most sacred one: Blessed and supremely glorified art Thou!

Dewdrops falling from heaven upon thy head at harvest time portended what was to come; for God, as He said, glorified thy divine memory, O venerable one, sanctifying the faithful through thy mediation.

In the council of the fathers God glorifies thee; at the trial they preserved thy words, O blessed one, which thou didst bring forth with faith, rebuking the most senseless Arius, and bringing his opposition to naught.

*Theotokion:*

As a vine, O Virgin, thou hast brought forth by the ineffable Word a cluster of grapes: the only uncultivated One, gushing forth wine that makes all glad, sanctifying all earthly ones, and taking away all drunkenness of cruel things.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

The fiery furnace of old in Babylon divided its operation by the command of God, burning the Chaldeans, but dew-sprinkling the faithful who sang: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparia:*

By the divine downpours of the Divine Spirit, thou didst quench the furnace of passions, and didst pour forth dew that takes away the burning heat of diseases, O father, of those who ever faithfully come unto thee, O blessed, exceedingly rich Spyridon.

Guileless, upright, meek, and merciful, and bearing no malice wast thou; loving, hospitable, a most sacred hierarch, adorned with the wisdom of Orthodoxy, O venerable one; therefore we honor thee in faith.

Of old the dead woman gave voice unto thee as alive when thou questionedst her, O father! O marvelous wonder! O most glorious mystery! O grace which thou didst receive, being worthily adorned with an angelic life O worthy of wonder![^116]

*Theotokion:*

Heal the passions of my heart by thy mercy, O all-hymned one; calm my mind, and enlighten my soul, and direct me beneficially unto the saving paths, that I may ever hymn thee, O all-hymned one.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

The Son of the unoriginate Begetter, God and Lord, incarnate of the Virgin, hath appeared unto us, to enlighten them that are darkened, and to gather together the scattered; therefore the all-hymned Birthgiver of God do we magnify.

*Troparia:*

Clearly didst thou proclaim the Son of the unoriginate Begetter, consubstantial with the Father and co-eternal, being magnified in the midst of the God-bearing fathers; and thou didst stop the mouths of the lawless, O all-blessed hierarch.

O all-radiant sun, adornment of fathers, glory of priests, companion of angels: vouchsafe the unwaning light by thy prayers unto those who now joyfully celebrate thy light-bearing memory.

The divine habitations, the heavenly city, the fair choir of them that keep festival, received thy sanctified soul, adorned with virtues, O all-blessed one, in the voice of rejoicing.

*Theotokion:*

The great mystery of thy childbirth beyond understanding astonishes the angels, O thou full of God's grace, delights the assembly of the venerable, and gladdens the sacred fathers who divinely hymn thee, the hope of our souls.

*Exapostilarion of the Octoechos.*

*Glory of the Saint, Podoben: "He Who adorned the heaven" (Не́бо ѕвѣзда́ми):*

From the irrational pastures the Spirit led thee unto the rational flock, O God-bearer, even as Moses and David, whose disposition thou didst emulate, O Spyridon, light of the universe!

*Theotokion:*

Thou wast the cause of the good things given from God unto the world, O Birthgiver of God; but even now entreat the easily reconciled God for our common salvation.

*At the Aposticha, from the Octoechos.*

*Glory of the Saint, Tone 4:*

O venerable father, all-lauded hierarch, having been filled with apostolic teaching, and shown forth as a dwelling-place of the Divine Spirit on account of thy virtuous life, thou didst drive away the wolves of the Church by thy teachings, and didst explain the faith of the Orthodox. A pillar and champion of piety wast thou shown forth; therefore thou didst work wonders in the ends [of the earth]: thou didst turn a serpent into gold, and didst raise a dead woman to question her. But, O worthy of wonder among fathers, and companion of teachers, entreat the Savior save our souls!

*Both now, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 4, Podoben: "As noble" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*[^117]

Beholding Christ put to death, * the all-pure Mistress, * seeing Him Who puts the deceiver to death, * cried out bitterly exclaiming: * and marveling at Him Who came forth from her womb * and at His long-suffering, * she cried aloud: * O my most beloved Child, * forget not thine handmaid, * tarry not, O Lover of mankind, * my consolation!

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Octoechos, and Ode 3 of the Saint.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 1:*

My mouth shall speak of wisdom, and the meditation of my heart shall be of understanding.

*Verse:* Hear this, all ye nations.

*The Apostle to the Hebrews, pericope 335.*

*Alleluia, Tone 2:*

The mouth of the righteous shall meditate on wisdom.[^118]

*Verse:* The law of His God [is in His heart].

*Gospel of Luke, pericope 24.*

*Communion Verse:* In everlasting remembrance shall the righteous be.

*In the same month, on the 13th day:*
*Of the Holy Martyrs Eustratius, Auxentius, Eugenius, Mardarius, and Orestes; and the Holy Virgin Martyr Lucia.*

*Be it known that if the memory of these saints happen on the Sunday of the Forefathers, the office of the martyrs is sung together with it.*

*At Great Vespers, Blessed is the man. At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 6, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*

*Stichera:*

The memory of Thy passion-bearer Eustratius, O Lord, * shines like the sun in brightness, * who hid polytheism with invincible words, * as unradiant shadow done away by faith, * and made four fellow sufferers * and companions, * for whose sake grant us cleansing, * as Thou art the Lover of mankind.

Eustratius made rational stones * to know Thy dominion, * who compelled them to feel the power in his flesh * suddenly to put away the wounds from frightful torments, * and destroying falsehood, * to bless Thee with their mouths, * O all-powerful Jesus, * Savior of our souls.

By words and sufferings, * and manifold deprivations of life, * the holy ones showed their perfect, unshakable love * unto Thee: * Orestes and Mardarius * with glorious Eugenius, * having contended together with wise Eustratius * and Auxentius: * by their prayers, O Lord, save our souls.[^119]

*Other Stichera, in the same Tone, Podoben: "As noble" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*

As having nobly soldiered for the King of hosts, * thou, Eustratius, * didst willingly give thyself over unto torment, * and violent death, * bringing with thyself a choir of martyrs, O blessed one, * with whom thou didst suffer, * and didst receive the crowns of victory: * with them pray thou * for us, O all-glorious one.

God-wise Eustratius, * noble Auxentius, * glorious Eugenius, * and Mardarius, * with Orestes acted valiantly, * having conquered the enemies, * and having shone forth manifestly like all-radiant stars, * they illuminated the hearts of the faithful, * and drove away the darkness of delusion * by the radiance of the Spirit.

Unsparingly beaten, * and exhausted with fire, * and nailed in iron boots, O all-wise one, * and driven along the paths, * shut up in prison, * and as a pure sacrifice in an oven, * thou wast offered unto Him Who was sacrificed for thy sake, * as a sweet-smelling burnt offering * unto the banquet on high, * O martyr Eustratius.

*Glory..., Tone 6:*

Come, ye lovers of the martyrs, in hymns let us honor Christ's sufferers: Eustratius the invincible martyr, Auxentius, and Eugenius, and Mardarius, and Orestes, the fivefold-radiant choir of martyrs; who nobly contended against the invisible enemy, and bound with crowns of victory, pray unto Christ for those who celebrate their memory with faith and love.

*Both now, Theotokion: "Who will not call thee blessed:"*

*The Prokeimenon of the day, and three readings.*

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 43):*[^120]

Thus says the Lord: Let all the nations be gathered together, and their princes shall be gathered from them. Who among them will declare these things? Or who will make known unto you the things from the beginning? Let them bring forth their witnesses, and let them be justified, and let them give ear, and speak the truth. Be ye My witnesses, and I too am a witness, says the Lord God, and the Servant Whom I have chosen; that ye may know, and believe Me, and understand that I am He: before Me there was no other God, and after Me there shall be none I am God, and besides Me there is no savior. I have declared, and have saved, I have brought to reproach, and there was no strange god among you. Ye are My witnesses, and I am the Lord God, and even from the beginning I am He, and there is none that delivers from My hands; I will work, and who shall turn it back? Thus says the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel Who delivers you.[^121]

*Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon (Chapter 3):*

The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment shall touch them. In the eyes of the foolish they seemed to die, and their departure was accounted to be hurt, and their journeying from us to be utter destruction; but they are in peace. For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality. And having been a little chastened, they shall be greatly rewarded; for God proved them, and found them worthy for Himself. As gold in the furnace hath He tried them, and received them as a burnt offering. And in the time of their visitation they shall shine forth, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble. They shall judge nations, and have dominion over peoples, and the Lord shall reign in them unto the ages. They that put their trust in Him shall understand the truth, and such as be faithful in love shall abide with Him; for grace and mercy is in His holy ones, and visitation in His elect.

*Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon (Chapter 5):*

The righteous live unto the ages, and their reward is in the Lord, and the care of them with the Most High. Therefore shall they receive a kingdom of majesty, and a crown of beauty from the hand of the Lord; for with His right hand shall He cover them, and with His arm shall He protect them. He shall take to Him His jealousy for complete armor, and make the creature His weapon for the revenge of His enemies. He shall put on righteousness as a breastplate, and true judgment instead of a helmet. He shall take holiness for an invincible shield. His severe wrath shall He sharpen for a sword, and the world shall fight with Him against the unwise. Then shall the right-aiming thunderbolts go abroad, and from the clouds, as from a well-drawn bow, shall they fly to the mark. And hailstones full of wrath shall be cast as out of a stone bow, and the water of the sea shall rage against them, and the rivers shall cruelly drown them. A spirit of power shall stand up against them, and like a whirlwind shall sift them out. Thus lawlessness shall lay waste the whole earth, and evildoing shall overthrow the thrones of the mighty. Give ear therefore, O ye kings, and understand; learn, ye that be judges of the ends of the earth. Give ear, ye that rule multitudes, and that glory in the multitudes of the nations: for dominion is given you from the Lord, and power from the Most High.[^122]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "Rejoice" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ):*

*Stichera:*

Radiant pillar, O passion-bearer, filled with the brightness of wisdom, thou didst lift thyself up unto the height of endurance, O wise one, and directedst thyself unto the light of understanding; illuminating us with thy divine, bright, and wise words, O glorious Eustratius, who are given wings by thy love, O blessed one. Therefore, honoring thy memory with praises out of love, O martyr, we ask to obtain divine lovingkindness through thy prayers, and that great mercy be granted unto the world.

*Verse:* The righteous cried, and the Lord gave ear unto them.

Filled with beauty and true sweetness is the cup of thy wisdom; wine of piety in sweetest and abundant words hast thou poured forth, O wise one; being delighted wherewith, we are mystically led up into the silent and sweet divine knowledge of the Master, truly, O Eustratius. Therefore, honoring thy sufferings with praises in faith and love, we ask to obtain divine lovingkindness through thy prayers, and that great mercy be granted unto the world.

*Verse:* Many are the afflictions of the righteous, and the Lord shall deliver them out of them all.

Let the light-bearing, victorious, radiant, and fivefold choir of martyrs be honored with praises: having acquired as a radiant leader truly Eustratius, who warmly rebuked the Hellenic sacrifices, and confirmed the teachings proclaimed by God unto Christians with spoken commands. Let us therefore praise him who poured out the cup of wisdom, and spiritually gladdens us, praying unto Christ Who grants great mercy unto the world.

*Glory..., in the same Tone:*

Not having feared the savageness of the tormentors, but rather clearly proclaiming the faith of Christ, ye endured many scrapings and torments, O Eustratius, Auxentius, Eugenius, and Orestes, and glorious Mardarius; therefore pray unto the King and God for us who celebrate your memory in faith.

*Both now, Theotokion:*

We call thee blessed, O Virgin Birthgiver of God, and we, the faithful, glorify thee as is meet: the unshakable city, the impregnable wall, the firm protectress and refuge of our souls.

*Troparion, Tone 4:*

Thy martyrs, O Lord, through their sufferings received incorruptible crowns from Thee, our God. For having Thy strength, they laid low the tormentors, and crushed the powerless audacities of the demons; through their prayers save our souls.[^123]

*Glory..., Both now, Theotokion:*

The mystery hidden from the ages.

*At Matins, after the first Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*

Having clothed thyself in the breastplate of the courage of faith, and piously armed thyself with divine wisdom, O glorious Eustratius, thou didst conquer all the regiments of the devil, and didst expose the powerless audacity of the godless. As one having boldness before God, pray that we be saved. *Twice.*

*Glory..., Both now, Theotokion:*

Having darkened my prodigal mind with many sins, I cry unto thy firm protection: enlighten the eyes of my soul, O Birthgiver of God, shine forth upon me the radiant beam of repentance, and clothe me in the armor of light, O pure Virgin Mother of God.

*After the second Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4:*

With the weapon of thy words thou didst wound the tormentor, having become the general of the Christ-bearing people, O God-wise Eustratius; thou didst shine forth upon the world with the rays of wonders, and a crown was woven for thy head from on high. Therefore also in thy memory we glorify Christ. *Twice.*

*Glory..., Both now, Theotokion:*

We sing of thee, O Bride of God, Mother of Christ God, glorifying thy incomprehensible childbirth, through which we were delivered from the delusion of the devil, and from all misfortunes, O Lady Birthgiver of God; and in faith we cry aloud: Have mercy upon thy flock, O only all-lauded one.

*After the Polyeleos, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom and Word" (Премꙋ́дрости):*

Strengthened by faith in the Trinity, armed with the sling of truth, thou didst cast down the alien audacity of deceit, and didst seize the enemy's sword of words, wherewith thou didst cut down lying opposition. Therefore, having exposed deceit by thy victories, thou didst die in the body, but wast made alive in the spirit, O passion-bearer Eustratius; pray unto Christ God that He grant forgiveness of sins unto those who celebrate thy holy memory with love. *Twice.*

*Glory..., Both now, Theotokion:*

Having fallen into multifaceted temptations from enemies visible and invisible, held fast by the tempest of my countless transgressions, and as unto my warm protection and to my covering, O pure one, I flee unto the haven of thy goodness. Therefore, O all-pure one, pray fervently unto Him Who was incarnate of thee without seed, for all thy servants who unceasingly pray unto thee, O all-pure Birthgiver of God; ever praying Him to grant forgiveness of transgressions unto those who worthily hymn thy glory.[^124]

*The Graduals, the first Antiphon of Tone 4. Prokeimenon, Tone 4:*

The righteous cried, and the Lord gave ear unto them. *Verse:* Many are the afflictions of the righteous, and the Lord shall deliver them out of them all. *Let every breath:*

*Gospel according to Matthew, pericope 36 (10:16-22).*

*After Psalm 50, Sticheron, Tone 1. Idiomelon:*

Let us, O peoples, praise the fivefold choir of the saints, singing praise unto the Savior Christ: Eustratius the long-suffering and steadfast passion-bearer; with him Auxentius, Eugenius, Mardarius, and Orestes. For having suffered for the faith, they trampled upon the enemy's sacrifices; and they pray unto the Savior to grant cleansing and forgiveness of sins unto those who celebrate their memory in faith.

*Canon of the Birthgiver of God with the Heirmos to 6; and two canons of the saints, to 8.*

*The first Canon of John the Monk, Tone 4.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

Israel of old, traversing the deep of the Red Sea with dryshod feet, conquered the power of Amalek in the wilderness by Moses' hands stretched out in the form of a cross.

*Troparia:*

Christ the Institutor of the contest, Who distributes gifts in the heavens unto the sufferers who are upon the earth, sits, extending divine crowns with His all-holding right hand unto those who are on both sides of Eustratius.

Come, let us behold the fivefold choir of martyrs, shining with most radiant light, having as divine leader Eustratius, who is crowned with divine grace.

Having disbanded the regiment[^125] of earthly warfare, thou dost bring an offering unto the true King, having received the token of suffering for Christ through Auxentius, O Eustratius.

*Theotokion:*

Thou wast a spacious dwelling-place of the divine nature, O pure Birthgiver of God. Therefore Lucia, having longed for thee, was led virginally after thee unto thy Son.

*The second Canon, Tone 6.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

Israel, traversing the deep with their feet as on dry land, and beholding Pharaoh the pursuer drowned, cried aloud: Let us sing a song of victory unto God![^126]

*Troparia:*

Christ the King, the Giver of the heavenly spheres, sits presiding, extending crowns of victory unto those who suffered upon earth with Eustratius.

Let us the faithful praise the hymn-singing, God-crowned choir of the fivefold martyrs, having precious Eustratius as their faithful, divine leader in Christ.

Longing for the heavenly hosts, and having symbolically given up earthly honor, O Eustratius, thou didst offer thy life unto God, O wise one, sacredly cleansed.[^127]

*Theotokion:*

The choir of well-victorious martyrs,[^128] which received the crown of victory, rejoicing sings of thee, O pure one; for through thee heaven became accessible unto men, because thou didst bear the Creator of heaven beyond comprehension.

*Katavasia: "Christ is born:"*

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

Thy Church rejoices in Thee, O Christ, crying aloud: Thou art my strength, O Lord, and my refuge, and my foundation!

*Troparia:*

By the hope of martyrdom, as of an immaterial treasure, thou wast filled beyond nature with all joy, O all-blessed Eustratius.

With spiritual zeal, and by the endurance of tribulations, thou didst expose the tormentors' godlessness, O Auxentius, martyr of Christ.

As the most radiant beauty of the Church of the faithful, O martyrs, ye were adorned with Christ's wounds as with flowers.

*Theotokion:*

In truth and properly we the faithful honor thee as the Birthgiver of God; for thou, O all-immaculate one, didst bear God Who became flesh.

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*

There is none holy as Thou, O Lord my God, Who hast exalted the horn of Thy faithful, O Good One, and hast established us upon the rock of Thy confession.

*Troparia:*

With steadfastness of mind, having placed all thy hope in God on high, O blessed one, thou wast wholly filled with the comfort of the hope of wounds.

Thou didst blossom with the love of Christ and with divine wisdom; and by endurance of torments, O Auxentius, thou dost expose the madness, insolence, and cruelty of the persecutors.

The untamed wrath of the fierce ones, and the fire of violent torments, was accounted by thee as a dream, O wise martyr; for being strengthened in Christ, thou didst despise them as though another were suffering.

*Theotokion:*

With sacred words and voices, O Virgin Mother of God, we the faithful, singing in a manner befitting God, call thee blessed, who art the cause of Him Who is the Cause of all becoming like us.

*Katavasia:*

*Katavasia: "Before the ages:"*[^129]

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "In prayers" (Въ моли́твахъ):*

Thou didst appear as a light-bearing luminary unto those sitting in the darkness of ignorance, O passion-bearer; for having arrayed thyself with faith as with a spear, thou didst not fear the audacities of the enemies, O Eustratius, who art the most eloquent of orators.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom and Word" (Премꙋ́дрости):*

Neither sword, nor wild beasts, nor fire, nor anything else of terrifying tangible things could at all frighten thy steadfastness; for having trampled underfoot the enemy's power by the course of thy life, thou didst pass through life as one dispassionate and bodiless. Therefore thou dost dispense healings unto the faithful who flee with love unto thy memory, O holy passion-bearer Eustratius; pray unto Christ God that He grant forgiveness of sins unto those who celebrate thy holy memory with love. *Twice.*

*Glory..., Both now, Theotokion:*

When the Master and Creator of all shall come to judge all the earth, count me, the condemned one, among the sheep at His right hand, and rescue me, thy unprofitable servant, I pray, from the outer darkness and every torment: that I may gratefully magnify the riches of thy goodness, O all-immaculate Birthgiver of God, and cry aloud unto thee: Rejoice! Pray unto Christ God to grant forgiveness of sins, for I, thy servant, have thee as my hope.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

For the sake of love of Thine image, O Compassionate One, Thou didst stand upon Thy Cross, and the nations melted away: for Thou, O Lover of mankind, art my strength and praise!

*Troparia:*

Together with the wounds of thy flesh, thou didst lay aside the defilements of the soul: thou didst crush the arrows of the deceitful serpent by faith, O Eustratius.

The King of glory was glorified by thy wounds, O passion-bearer; and Eustratius filled those wounds with the power of wonders of ineffable glory.

Having emulated the audacity against the devil, by the net of martyrdom thou dost openly bring the wise Eugenius, having caught him, O Eustratius.

*Theotokion:*

O all-immaculate one, who wast shown forth as the only one more radiant than the Cherubim, save our souls from every adversity, who hymn thee in faith.

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*

Christ is my power, God and Lord, the honorable Church sings in a manner befitting God, crying out from a pure mind: feasting in the Lord!

*Troparia:*

The Almighty, having kindled a divine desire in thy soul showed forth marvelous deeds preeminently, making the wounds of thy flesh healed.[^130]

Having caught the wise Eugenius with the spiritual net of the fishermen, O wise one, thou dost bring him unto the King: whom having caught, thou didst bring unto Christ, O Eustratius.

Thy feet being pierced with nails, O all-wise one, by the torment of iron boots, thou didst wholly redden thyself, conforming thyself unto the passion of Christ the King.

*Theotokion:*

The uncontainable and immutable Word of God the Father, having changed by outward appearance, O all-immaculate one, being incarnate of thee, deifies me, a human, in His love for mankind.

*Katavasia: "A rod from the root:"*

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

Thou, O my Lord, hast come into the world as a Light, a holy Light turning from the gloomy darkness of ignorance those who hymn Thee in faith.

*Troparia:*

Thou, as a light-bearing star, hast shone forth far-shining among the regiment of martyrs, O invincible Eustratius.

O good lot! O God-given portion! O most excellent of women, who by counsel didst conquer the ancestral deceit!

Thou didst account all fair things as refuse, O Mardarius, having conquered the laws of nature by the love of suffering.

*Theotokion:*

An earthly mind cannot comprehend thy conception which is beyond mind, O Virgin Maiden Mother; for thou didst bear God.

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*

With Thy divine light, O Good One, illuminate, I pray, the souls of those who awake early unto Thee with love, to know Thee, O Word of God, as the true God, Who callest us from the gloom of sin.

*Troparia:*

Having become marvelous as a star of the Church, from afar in the midst of the martyrs thou didst shine forth, O Eustratius, illuminating the world with rays of martyrdom more than the sun.

Having seen thee casting forth a beam with radiant splendors, God-proclaiming Mardarius, innocent as a lamb unto the shepherd, followed thee with simplicity of heart.

The woman, masculine in mind, prudent, and Christ-loving, rose above her kindred nature: she preeminently and perfectly conquers beforehand, having anointed her husband for martyrdom.

*Theotokion:*

Save those who from the soul confess thee as the Birthgiver of God and Sovereign Lady of the world, O good one; for we have acquired thee as an invincible protectress, the holy Birthgiver of God.

*Katavasia: "God of peace:"*

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord, the Church cries aloud unto Thee, having been cleansed from the blood of demons by the blood which flowed from Thy side for mercy's sake.[^131]

*Troparia:*

Christ is in place of all things unto me, Mardarius cried with a loud voice, both fatherland, and honor, and name: for of thee was I taught this, O Eustratius.

Thy tongue cut out ceases not from hymns, and thy sacred hands are lifted up unto God, O Eugenius, asking salvation for those who hymn thy memory.

With thy feet bored through, thou wast hung head downwards, and scorched along the shoulders with red-hot spits; thou didst surrender thy spirit unto the Master, O Mardarius.

*Theotokion:*

Having found thee to be strength and a fortress, O Virgin, the female passion-bearer valiantly endures wounds; and rejoicing she is led after thee unto the Master of all.

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*

Beholding the sea of life surging with the tempest of temptations, I flee unto Thy calm haven, crying unto Thee: Lead up my life from corruption, O Most Merciful One!

*Troparia:*

Christ Himself is in place of all ancestral things unto me, crying aloud, O Mardarius: thy heel being crushed with red-hot spits of fire, and thy shoulders with arrows, rejoicing thou didst finish thy course.

Thy tongue being cut out, O Eugenius, it ceases not to hymn Christ; and thy sacred hands are lifted up unto God, O blessed one, asking deliverance for those who hymn thee.

How praiseworthy is thy courageous soul, O all-noble Eugenius! For thy shins having been violently broken, rejoicing thou didst surrender thy spirit into the hands of the Master of all.

*Theotokion:*

All-pure Lady, who didst bear the Helmsman of the earthly and the Lord: still the unstable and fierce disturbance of my passions, and grant tranquility unto my heart.

*Katavasia: "Out of the belly, Jonah:"*

*Kontakion, Tone 6, Podoben: "Fulfilling the dispensation for our sake" (Е҆́же ѡ҆ на́съ):*

Thou didst shine forth before the most lawless with divine things, and didst endure beatings with a most courageous heart; thou didst shine forth with God-given signs most marvelously, and didst quench the lofty flame of delusion; therefore we honor thee, O all-blessed one, martyr of Christ, Eustratius.

*Ikos:*

The Church today sacredly accomplishes a mystery-filled feast brightly proclaiming thy valiances, sicknesses, and labors; the divine contests which are beyond nature, and the wounds everywhere, wherewith he cast down the manifold-scheming one. Great glory and praise of the sufferers! Pillar of courage! Luminary of all who piously honor thee! Treasure of healings! Enricher of the poor, first-victorious one[^133] of the honorable martyrs, all-blessed martyr of Christ, Eustratius.[^132]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

In the Persian furnace the Abrahamic youths, inflamed rather by love of piety than by the flame, cried aloud: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

*Troparia:*

Having the unchanging disposition of confession to honor the one God in Trinity, thou didst despise torments, crying: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

As one blessed thou didst walk in the blameless way, and with good discernment didst bend the knee unto the Deliverer; and having surrendered thy soul into the hands of the Master as a most sweet-smelling sacrifice, O Auxentius.

God Who grants food unto Elijah through ravens, He also working wonders concerning thy honorable head, revealed it unto those who desired it: as a much-desired banquet unto the world, O Auxentius.

*Theotokion:*

Purely, O Mother, as one pure and incorruptible, the pure Word loved thee, and having been incarnate of thee, He reconstituted all mankind, Who glorified Lucia with wonders.

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*

The angel made the furnace dew-bearing unto the pious youths, but the command of God burning the Chaldeans persuaded the tormentor to cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparia:*

As a victor thou hast ascended unto the heavenly Kingdom, O Auxentius; for after trial of multifaceted torments, confessing Christ God, thou didst finish thy course for His sake, beheaded in the head.

Most marvelous is thy prudent courage, O Orestes; for upon the tribunal thou dost show forth understanding, and having pierced the soul of Lysias with the Cross, singing: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

Having Orestes as a fellow-traveler along the path of martyrdom, and an ally running with thee, and a fellow-sufferer, thou didst enrich thyself, singing with him: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*

The furnace burned not the three youths, prefiguring thy childbirth; for the divine Fire burned thee not, having taken up His dwelling in thee, and He enlightened all to cry: Blessed is the God of our fathers![^134]

*Katavasia: "The youths reared in piety:"*

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

Daniel, stretching out his hands, stopped the mouths of the lions in the pit; and the youths, lovers of piety, girded with virtue, quenched the power of the fire, crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparia:*

Having opened thy lips purely, thou didst draw in the divine Spirit, O Eustratius, and didst expose the weakness of soul-destroying services; and thou didst cry aloud to honor God in Trinity: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

The invincible Orestes, having strengthened his mind by thy wise instructions, O martyr Eustratius, being stretched out upon the iron bed, cried unto the destroyers of the flame, resembling the Children: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

Having patiently stretched out thy body upon the red-hot bed, O glorious martyr Orestes, thou wast numbered among the martyrs, rejoicing in the Lord; and thou hast rested in the heavenly tabernacles, crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Theotokion:*

Thou wast shown forth higher than the heavens, having borne the God of all: Who heavenized all the mixture of the earthborn, O all-honorable one, and Who made radiant the honorable memory of Lucia; unto Whom we ever cry aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*

Out of the flame Thou didst pour forth dew unto the pious, and didst consume the sacrifice of the righteous with water: for Thou dost all things, O Christ, only by willing: Thee do we supremely exalt unto all ages!

*Troparia:*

Boldly proclaiming the boundless power of the Trinity of one nature, thou didst speak theology, O Eustratius; and thou didst expose the snare-like service of idols, O all-wise and God-wise one.

The persecutor, not knowing thy endurance, showed himself intending to terrify thee with fiery appearance; but thou, having spat upon his cruelty, rejoicing didst hymn the Master, O Eustratius.

Instructed by thy divine utterances, God-wise Orestes leaped forth upon the bed made ready, as an immaculate lamb offered as a whole burnt-offering, crying unto God the Crown-Giver: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Theotokion:*

All-pure Virgin, save me; be help unto my weakness: deliver me from many and fierce afflictions, that I may glorify thee, the only Birthgiver of God.

*Katavasia: "A marvelous wonder:"*

...the Creator and Deliverer.[^135]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

The cornerstone unhewn by hands was cut off from thee, O unwrought mountain, Virgin: Christ Who joined together the sundered natures. Therefore, rejoicing, we magnify thee, O Birthgiver of God!

*Troparia:*

Longing to partake of the divine Mysteries, O passion-bearer, and to be accounted worthy of radiant theophany, O blessed Eustratius, thou didst draw near unto Christ, Who called thee to the heavens, Whom thou desiredst.

Greatly rejoicing at the joyful condemnation of the tormentor's supreme madness, O passion-bearer Eustratius, thou didst magnify thy Institutor of the contest, hymning Christ, the Destroyer of death.

Come, all ye lovers of the martyrs, with sacred songs let us magnify Eugenius, the destroyer of deceit; the wise Orestes and Mardarius; and with them Auxentius together with Eustratius.

*Theotokion:*

Light shone forth upon us from thy unwedded womb, O Virgin, with whose divine splendors having been divinely illumined, marvelous Lucia also became light, O Virgin Mother, Birthgiver of God.

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*

It is not possible for men to see God, upon Whom the angelic ranks dare not gaze; but through thee, O all-pure one, the incarnate Word was manifested unto men: Whom magnifying, together with the heavenly hosts, we call thee blessed!

*Troparia:*

Singing praise unto the Desired One, O Eustratius, and having become a partaker of the divine Mysteries, thou wast accounted worthy of His theophany in prison, O blessed one, calling thee unto the heavenly life of His Kingdom.

Strengthened by the power of Christ, O martyr Eustratius, thou didst laugh at the flatteries of the persecutors, glorifying Christ with songs, O glorious one; for as the youths of old into the furnace, rejoicing as into a fair paradise, O blessed one, thou didst enter within.

With hymns and songs let us all the faithful praise the divine warriors: Auxentius, Eugenius, together with Mardarius, glorious Orestes; and the leader and fellow-sufferer, and instructor, wise Eustratius.

*Theotokion:*

Thou wast the temple of Christ Who reigns together with the Father and the Spirit: for thy sake, O pure one, having become temples by grace, we were accounted worthy of His adoption through baptism.

*Katavasia: "A strange and marvelous mystery:"*

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "In the Spirit in the sanctuary" (Дх҃омъ во ст҃и́лищи):*

Thou didst accomplish the marvelous course of martyrdom, O blessed Eustratius; and having brought together with thee the honorable Eugenius, and the wise Auxentius, and Mardarius with Orestes; at whose faith and audacity the assemblies of men and angels were amazed. *Twice.*[^136]

*Glory..., Both now, Theotokion:*

Thou wast the all-immaculate bride of Thine ineffable childbirth, as a most sacredly revered temple, O Birthgiver of God; for thou didst bear the pre-eternal Word of God Who took up His dwelling in thee. Therefore, hymning thy childbirth, we magnify thee, O all-immaculate Maiden.

*At the Praises, Stichera, 4. Tone 5. By Germanus:*

With rhetorical words, terrifying unto the lawless, the soldier of Christ, and with suffering wounds, manfully conquered the enemy's powers: the glorious Eustratius, the steadfast sufferer, who traversed the narrow and sorrowful path, and reached into the land of eternal life, in which also he prays Christ to grant us great mercy.

Let us crown with suffering praises the philosopher who was revealed in divine wisdom, and the orator who was shown forth in the goodness of words, Eustratius the great among witnesses. For having assembled this pious regiment, the soldier of Christ, in the time of battles unto the furious contests of suffering, having seized the enemy's sword, therewith he wounded him. Unto whom let us cry aloud: Most excellent of martyrs, with those who suffered with thee, pray Christ God for those who celebrate thy all-honorable memory in faith.

*Tone 4. By John the Monk:*

Let the well-victorious witnesses of the truth be crowned with praises by us: Eustratius the accuser of Hellenic babbling, and preacher of Christian God-wisdom; Auxentius who by wisdom of words and endurance of deeds exposed the tormentors' godlessness; unto them Eugenius, acceptable unto God, and unprofitable unto the tormentors for the sake of the saving confession; and Orestes, the true and marvelous soldier of the King of all; with them also Mardarius, the innocent dove, who put to shame the crafty serpent by the grace of Christ God, and Savior of our souls.

*By Kassia the Nun:*

Above Hellenic teachings, the holy martyrs preferred apostolic wisdom, having left the oratorical books, and learned the fishermen's; for there indeed was eloquence of words, but in the unlettered, God-proclaiming [writings] they learned Trinitarian knowledge of God. In which pray that our souls be preserved in peace.

*Glory..., Tone 4. By the same Kassia:*
