Let us name-fittingly hymn and piously praise the God-bearing martyrs, the five-stringed lyre and five-fold luminary of the Church of God:[^137] Rejoice, thou who wast well-enlisted by God in the heavenly host,[^138] and who didst please Him Who enlisted thee, orator among orators, God-wise Eustratius! Rejoice, thou who didst multiply the talent entrusted unto thee by God many times over for the better, O blessed one! Rejoice, most fair branch of divine nobility, God-wise Eugenius! Rejoice, fair in form, most excellent in character, and ambidextrous,[^139] who didst dwell wholly in the divine mountains, all-blessed Orestes! Rejoice, holy, translucent pearl, who didst joyfully endure bitter torments, invincible Mardarius! Rejoice, choir equal in number to the wise virgins! Whom we pray to deliver from every wrath and affliction, and to make partakers of your ineffable glory, those who honor your yearly memory.

*Both now, Theotokion:*

Having thee, O Birthgiver of God:

*Great Doxology, and Dismissal.*

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the first Canon, Ode 3, on 4; and of the second, Ode 6, on 4.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 4:*

Unto the saints who are on His earth, the Lord hath made marvelous all His desires in them. *Verse:* I foresaw the Lord before me continually. *Epistle to the Ephesians, Pericope 233 [6:10-17]. Alleluia, Tone 4:* The righteous cried, and the Lord heard them. *Verse:* Many are the afflictions of the righteous. *Gospel according to Luke, Pericope 106 [21:12-19]. Communion Verse:* Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous.

*On the 14th Day of the Same Month. Holy Martyrs Thyrsus, Leucius, Philemon, and those with them. Alleluia.*

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*

Marvelous Thyrsus, God-wise Callinicus, and glorious Leucius, confessing the uncreated Trinity in dangers, with a most courageous mind endured most grievous sicknesses and unremitting torments and received crowns of victory as victors, having become fellow-citizens of the immaterial hosts.[^140]

Great Philemon, exceedingly rich Arianus, and wise Apollonius, with streams of blood quenched the flame of polytheism; they watered all the earth with divine currents of the knowledge of God, and with showers of healings dry up rivers of passions by divine grace, as fervent protectors.

As most fair flowers blooming in a floral garden, the glorious martyrs, emitting the divine fragrance of the Spirit, sweetly scent the thoughts of those who faithfully honor their yearly memory, their sufferings and contests, and their blessed end; for which sake they dwell rejoicing in the unwaning light.

*Other Stichera, to the Most Holy Birthgiver of God, in the same Tone and Podoben (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*

Rain down upon me, O Birthgiver of God, the abyss of thy mercy, and as compassionate, water my heart scorched by the burning heat of passions, O Maiden; and make me to pour forth drops of compunction unceasingly, I pray: whereby I may be accounted worthy of consolation, O pure one, which those who have sincerely wept are to receive.

Shaken by assaults of prison,[^141] and cast into the pit of destruction: take pity, O tenderhearted Birthgiver of God, and establish me upon the rock of virtues; and having destroyed the counsels of the enemies, account me worthy to do the commandments of Thy Son and our God, that I may obtain remission in the day of judgment.

I have fallen among foul, murderous robbers, O all-immaculate one, and through their onsets I was stripped of the incorruptible garment of ethereal brightness, O Maiden; and by them was unmercifully wounded, and cast down into a place of affliction, scarcely alive; but make haste and stretch out thy hand, and raise me up, I pray.

*Glory..., Both now, in the same Tone and Podoben (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*

I lie upon the bed of despondency, O all-immaculate one, and sluggishly pass my life, and I am terrified of the end of my time, O Birthgiver of God: lest as a lion the all-evil serpent mercilessly tear my humble soul. Therefore by thy goodness, hastening before the end, raise me up unto repentance.

*Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "As one valiant" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*

Beholding Christ, the Lover of mankind, crucified, O all-pure one, and His side pierced with a spear, weeping she cried aloud she cried aloud: What is this, O my Son? What have the ungrateful people rendered unto Thee for the good things which Thou didst for them? And art Thou hasty to leave me childless, O most dearly beloved? I marvel, O Tenderhearted One, at Thy voluntary crucifixion.[^142]

*At the Aposticha, from the Octoechos.*

*At Matins, both Canons from the Octoechos, and the Canon of the Saints, on 4.*

*Tone 6. By Theophanes.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

Traversing the deep on foot as if upon dry land with footsteps, Israel, beholding Pharaoh the persecutor drowning, cried aloud: Let us sing a song of victory unto God!

*Troparia:*

Standing before the divine throne in martyr splendors, and shining with divine brilliances, O passion-bearers, enlighten us who sing of your memory.

Desiring divine beauties, ye accounted the fair things of life as nothing, O passion-bearers of Christ; and having died in the body, ye were accounted worthy to find endless life.

Having in a manner befitting God exposed the deceit of godlessness, O passion-bearing martyrs, ye endured the fiery burning of many afflictions, and now have received painless life.

*Theotokion:*

The uncircumscribable Word, circumscribed in the body, thou didst bear, O pure one; Whom pray to deliver from afflictions and from the onset of passions those who glorify thee.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

There is none holy as Thou, O Lord my God, Who hast exalted the horn of Thy faithful, O Good One, and established us upon the rock of Thy confession.

*Troparia:*

The champions of darkness, cruelly scraping thy body, did not weaken the steadfastness of thy thought, O Thyrsus, who wast mightily strengthened with divine love toward [God's] love.

Truly sudden was thy faith toward the Lord, O marvelous martyr, wherewith thou didst put to shame the malice of the enemies, crying, O Philemon: I am a servant of Christ!

Unto the struggle with the enemy thou didst boldly go forth, O martyr, not with shield nor spear, but divinely protected by steadfast faith, and manfully didst cast him down unto the ground.

*Theotokion:*

One of the Holy Trinity in two natures, incarnate of thy pure blood, in a manner befitting God came forth, saving by goodness those descended from Adam, O all-pure one.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph was amazed" (Оу҆диви́ся і҆ѡ́сифъ):*

Protected by the shield of piety well covered,[^143] and having firmly clothed yourselves in the armor of the Cross, ye cast down the hosts of the tormentor, O praiseworthy martyrs of Christ, and having been crowned with crowns of victory by Him, ye dance unceasingly with the celestial hosts, and pray the Savior to save our souls.

*Glory..., Both now, Theotokion:*

Tossed by passionate surges, I, senseless, O pure one, cry unto thee fervently: Let me not, accursed, perish, O thou who didst bear the abyss of compassion, for beside thee I have no hope; lest I, who have trusted in thee, appear as an object of rejoicing and mockery unto enemies; for thou canst do whatsoever thou desirest, as thou art the Mother of the God of all.

*Stavrotheotokion:*

The Virgin and Ewe-lamb, beholding upon the Cross the Lamb Who was born of her without seed, and pierced with a spear, wounded with the arrows of grief, cried out, painfully exclaiming: What is this new mystery? How dost Thou die, Who art the only Lord of life? Therefore arise, raising up the fallen forefather.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

Christ is my power, God and Lord, the honorable Church sings in a manner befitting God, crying out from a pure mind: feasting in the Lord!

*Troparia:*

The martyrs, having desired to confess the only Tenderhearted One, the only Lord and God of all, through torments received His Kingdom.

Bodily scrapings, fiery assaults, and wild beasts and the sea, thou didst youthfully endure, O exceedingly rich one, strengthened by the power of the Cross, O martyr Thyrsus.

Adorned with wounds of contests, thou didst make thy soul brighter than the radiance of the sun, as a soldier of Christ, O passion-bearing martyr Leucius.

*Theotokion:*

A husbandless Mother, an immaculate Virgin, an undefiled Maiden, we know thee alone among women: O blessed Mary, the restoration of men.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

With Thy divine light, O Good One, illuminate, I pray, the souls of those who awake early unto Thee with love, to know Thee, O Word of God, as the true God, Who callest us from the gloom of sin.

*Troparia:*

Illumined with most divine, God-shining rays, O all-praised martyrs, ye traversed the unstable surge of godlessness, and passed over unto divine tranquility.

Cruelly dragged along the earth, O all-praised martyrs, and wounded with torments, ye received the honors of heaven ye received the honors of heaven, having now become fellow-citizens of the angels.[^144]

Loving to die for Christ Who openly loved thee, O martyr Philemon, thou didst account the wounds brought upon thy body as the shooting of arrows of infants, O God-blessed one.

*Theotokion:*

Save those who from the soul piously confess thee as the Birthgiver of God: for we have acquired thee as an invincible protectress, the true Birthgiver of God.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

Beholding the sea of life surging with the tempest of temptations, I flee unto Thy calm haven, crying unto Thee: Lead up my life from corruption, O Most Merciful One!

*Troparia:*

Moved by the winds of the divine Spirit, O wise ones, ye joyfully saved the spiritual desires unto noetic havens, O martyrs, together enjoying deification.[^145]

Having mounted a fiery chariot, O sufferers, by shed blood ye were caught up unto the heavens; and ye obtained divine glory, having received crowns of victory from Him.

Philemon and Leucius, Apollonius together with ever-memorable Thyrsus, the divine and light-bearing four, were enriched with Trinitarian[^146] illumination through immaterial communion.

*Theotokion:*

He Who is higher than all noetic, as God, and visible creation, being incarnate came forth from thy womb, having preserved thee incorruptible, as thou wast before childbirth, O Virgin Mother.

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "The firm and God-proclaiming" (Тве́рдыя):*

Champions of the pious faith, having spat upon the wicked tormentor, ye exposed his beast-like bloodshed; and ye conquered his furious opposition, strengthened by the help of Christ, O Thyrsus and Leucius, praying for us with those who suffered with you.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

The angel made the furnace dew-bearing unto the pious youths, but the command of God burning the Chaldeans persuaded the tormentor to cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparia:*

By divine showers ye quenched the furnace of polytheism, having joyfully ignited with divine love; and now ye sing, O sufferers: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

Having caught the persecutor with the divine net, O praiseworthy ones, ye drew him out of the deceitful depths ye drew him out of the deceitful depths, and brought him unto Christ, warmly singing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^147]

Ye shook the foundations of deceit, showing forth an unshakable resolve and a courageous mind, O sufferers; and now ye piously sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*

Beyond word is thy conception, O Bride of God, for thou didst bear God the Word, Who delivers every man from irrationality, and grants a word to cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

Out of the flame Thou didst pour forth dew unto the pious, and didst consume the sacrifice of the righteous with water: for Thou dost all things, O Christ, only by willing: Thee do we supremely exalt unto all ages!

*Troparia:*

Protected by the shield of piety, and having taken up the Cross as a spear, thou didst cut down the regiments of invisible enemies, O courageous-minded Thyrsus, divine glory of martyrs.

Inflamed with love of the Almighty, thou didst enter courageously into the martyr tribunal, and having patiently suffered, thou didst tear apart the great serpent, O sufferer Philemon.

Having shown forth the enemy's power sunken by the depth of thy courage and endurance, O Arianus, thou wast accounted worthy of an unshakable Kingdom unto all ages.

*Theotokion:*

Confessing thee as the true Birthgiver of God, as the angel we cry unto thee: Rejoice! For thou alone didst bear joy upon the earth, O rejoiced one, pure, blessed.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

It is not possible for men to see God, upon Whom the angelic ranks dare not gaze; but through thee, O all-pure one, the incarnate Word was manifested unto men: Whom magnifying, together with the heavenly hosts, we call thee blessed!

*Troparia:*

Representing Christ's Passion, ye endured the trial of many torments, O blessed ones; and having been beheaded in the heads, ye were numbered with the heavenly ranks, shining with glory and adorned with divine beams.

With thy blood thou didst dye a purple robe, O wise Thyrsus, and didst gloriously clothe thyself therein; and holding the Cross as a divine scepter, rejoicing with all the passion-bearers, now thou reignest together with Christ, O God-blessed one.

The angelic hosts marvelled at your contests, O blessed ones, your wounds, opposition, and violent death: with whom living with whom, make remembrance of those who celebrate your memory, O all-praised ones.[^148]

*Theotokion:*

In the likeness of human flesh, from thy womb the Word appeared being born, and drew a multitude of martyrs, having endured passions, the All-Good One, O pure Virgin Mary, rejoiced of God.

*On the 15th Day of the Same Month. Holy Hieromartyr Eleutherius; and our Venerable Father Paul of Latros. If thou wilt, sing Alleluia. At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Hieromartyr, 3; and of the Venerable, 3.*

*Stichera of the Hieromartyr, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*

Thou wast a most sacred vessel of the divine Spirit, having purified thy soul from passions most sacredly; thence thou didst receive holy divine anointing, having become a hierarch and a God-wise instructor of the people, and an invincible martyr of Him Who endured passions for our sake and poured forth dispassion, O sufferer Eleutherius.

Seeing thee having well finished the contest, she who had well borne thee, desiring to run a course equal unto thee, embracing thee in the midst of the stadium, O wise one, is slain like a heifer; with whom we pray thee, O Eleutherius: pray the Savior and Lord for us, O all-blessed one.

Thou didst despise the body wounded with beatings and approaching unto fire; for thou didst give wings to thy mind with invincible desire, by the most fair beauty of the divine Lover, wounded with Whose sweet longing: adornment of martyrs, ornament of hierarchs, O sufferer Eleutherius, converser with angels!

*Stichera of the Venerable, Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*

O Paul, beauty of monastics, fair blossom of the wilderness, praise of the venerable, glory of Latros, fortress of the faithful: those who with love celebrate thy all-honorable memory and embrace the shrine of thy relics the shrine of thy relics, deliver from every distress and fiery condemnation, by thy prayers unto the Sovereign Lady.[^149]

Having made thyself a temple of the Trinity, O God-blessed father, thou didst erect a church in Her name; and having entered into the impassable deserts of Latros, as Moses into Mount Sinai, thou didst settle there: where having received the divine Law, truly thou dost instruct the multitudes of monastics in the most excellent things, O all-marvelous one.

Having boldness toward God, and having subdued the members of the flesh with many labors,[^150] pray that we be preserved from temptations of the enemy, and incursions of heathens, and fire, and the sword, and every assault of the evil one's malice; for having thee as city-defender and protection, with God we have acquired our hope in thee, O blessed one.

*Glory..., Both now, Theotokion, in the same Podoben (Подо́бенъ то́йже):*

Thou alone, in an unconfined manner, didst bear in thy womb the uncontainable God, Who became man for His goodness, O most holy Bride of God; therefore I pray thee, alter the passions that afflict me: that having walked the narrow and right path, I may reach that which leads unto life, O Virgin.

*Stavrotheotokion:*

When the undefiled Ewe-lamb beheld her Lamb being led to slaughter as a man of His own will, weeping she said: Art Thou now hasty to leave me childless, O Christ, who bore Thee? What is this Thou hast done, O Deliverer of all? Yet I hymn and glorify Thy extreme goodness which is beyond mind and word, O Lover of mankind.

*Troparion, Tone 4:*

Having been a partaker of the characters and a successor to the thrones of the Apostles, thou didst find action an ascent unto contemplation, O God-inspired one; therefore, rightly dividing the word of truth, thou didst suffer for the faith even unto blood, O hieromartyr Eleutherius: pray Christ God that our souls be saved.

*Glory..., of the Venerable, in the same Tone:*

As a fellow-converser with the bodiless hosts, and a companion of all the venerable, O all-glorious Paul, we hymn thee, and pray thee: pray ever for us, that we may find mercy. *Both now, Theotokion.*

*At Matins, one Canon from the Octoechos, and two of the Saints.*

*Canon of the Hieromartyr, whose Acrostic is:* Show me free from passions, O all-blessed one. *By Joseph. Tone 4.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

Let us all sing a song of victory unto God Who wrought marvelous wonders with a high arm, and saved Israel, for He hath been glorified!

*Troparia:*

By thy radiant prayers, O martyr Eleutherius, now free him who is enslaved by the darkening of passions, that as a servant of Christ I may hymn thee with divine songs.

Thou didst shine forth with the purest rays of suffering, O most sacred one, and didst dye thy sacred vestment with blood, and wast made light-like by the Spirit.

Cleaving unto God with the purest mind from youth, thou didst distance thy soul from carnal wisdom, and wast enriched with abundant grace of wonders.

*Theotokion:*

As a fiery throne thou bearest the Creator; as an animate bridal chamber and a fair palace thou containest the King, Who became that which we are, without alteration or confusion.

*Another Canon, of the Venerable, in the same Tone.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

Christ is born, glorify Him! Christ from heaven, meet Him! Christ on earth, be ye exalted! Sing unto the Lord, all the earth, and with gladness sing praises, O ye people, for He hath been glorified!

*Troparia:*

As I strive to bring a new hymn of praise unto thee with the opening of my lips, O God-bearing Paul: by thy prayers, O venerable one, grant me grace to speak, that we may hymn thy honorable contests.[^151]

Having taken up the yoke of the Lord from youth, O venerable one, and sown spiritual wheat in the furrows of thy heart, thou didst reap an ear of grain that strengthens souls, O God-blessed one.

By most numerous labors thou didst obtain the Kingdom on high, living as one bodiless upon earth, and in the body living an angelic life; and now standing in the highest before the Trinity, remember us.

*Theotokion:*

Taking my corruptible flesh from thy blood, O Bride of God, the Bodiless One of His own will lay in a manger: this flesh which He assumed, the All-Good One, God's Mother, deifies through His union therewith.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

Let my heart be established in Thy will, O Christ God, Who didst establish the second heaven above the waters, and founded the earth upon the waters, O Almighty One!

*Troparia:*

Having chosen to suffer for Christ, thou dost endure bodily wounds, sweetening thyself, O wise one, with illnesses with illnesses and afflictions; for which sake thou hast now received painless life.[^152]

Held fast by fervent desire for the Creator, O God-wise sufferer, thou didst cast down the fiery cunning of the body,[^153] bedewed with the fire of the Spirit, O Eleutherius.

Shown forth as the most sacred among priests, and the most steadfast martyr among martyrs, thou didst receive a double crown, O blessed one, ever beholding the face of God.

*Theotokion:*

Thou didst bud forth Christ as the rod of strength, wherewith we are established: for the rod of Aaron that once budded prefigured thee, O unwrought earth, pure dove, ever-virgin.

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*

Unto the Son begotten of the Father incorruptibly before the ages, and in the last times incarnate of the Virgin without seed, unto Christ God let us cry aloud: Thou Who hast exalted our horn, holy art Thou, O Lord!

*Troparia:*

O thy courage! O thy spiritual valiance, O glorious one! For desiring to crush the jaw-teeth of the invisible lions, thou didst carry two exceedingly great stones during the night, a heavy weight upon thy shoulders.

Who can worthily recount thy contests? For treading the ways of life in the wilderness, thou didst eat raw acorns, having learned to sweeten thy tasting with the afflictions of abstinence.

Of old Moses the God-seer was accounted worthy of a mystical vision in the bush; but all-honorable Paul, when fire appeared from on high, knew himself to be ignited without being consumed.

*Theotokion:*

Being without beginning and by nature God, the Word co-honored with the Father: Thou didst receive a beginning in time, being born of the Virgin; Thou wast revealed as a man by nature, and didst become an infant, as a child wrapped in swaddling bands, O Christ Thou wast shown forth.

*Kontakion of the Venerable, Tone 8, Podoben: "To thee, the champion leader" (Въ збра́нной):*

From youth, O wise Paul, having manfully desired the things that are beyond understanding, thou didst leave worldly turmoil, and for the sake of divine life becamest an abode of the Trinity, and didst enlighten those who approach thee in faith; therefore we cry: Rejoice, O exceedingly rich Paul!

*Sessional Hymn of the Hieromartyr, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thy tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й сп҃се):*

Having acquired a mind free from passions, thou wast a most sincere servant of God, and didst free from deceit those who well gave ear unto thee. And having suffered as a priest and a martyr, O Eleutherius, thou hast received a twofold crown; pray that we may be saved.

*Glory to the Venerable Father, Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom and Word" (Премꙋ́дрости):*[^154]
Steered by the all-effective power and winged by the sail of the Cross, thou didst easily sail across the tempest of this life, and didst truly reach the divine havens. Having amassed a great merchandise of virtues, which thou didst offer unto the Birthgiver of God of all, and didst hear: "Good servant," and those things that follow thereupon. Therefore, O blessed Paul, pray to Christ God that He grant remission of sins unto those who with love honor thy holy memory.

*Both now, Theotokion:*
Having fallen into manifold tribulations from enemies visible and invisible, being seized by the tempest of mine unnumbered offenses, and as unto a warm defense and my shelter, O pure one, I flee unto the haven of thy goodness. Therefore, O most pure one, fervently pray to Him Who was incarnate of thee without seed for all thy servants who unceasingly pray unto thee, O most pure Birthgiver of God, ever beseeching Him to grant remission of sins unto those who worthily sing praises to thy glory.

*Stavrotheotokion:*
The Virgin and Mother of the Redeemer, standing at the Cross in affliction, mother-like cried out weeping: "What strange and most glorious thing is this, O Son? Who gushest forth passionlessness unto all men, to be crucified in the midst of condemned ones upon the Cross, pierced in the ribs and given gall to drink by the hands of those whom Thou didst create! But arise, and grant remission of offenses unto those who sing with faith of Thy divine sufferings."

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Foreseeing in the Spirit the incarnation of the Word, O Prophet Habakkuk, thou didst preach, crying out: When the years draw near, Thou shalt be known; when the time is come, Thou shalt be shown. Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Neither the gaping of lions, nor the boiling of fire, nor the threats of the cruel, weakened the strength of thy endurance, O sacred initiate; but as adamant thou didst take sweetness in torments, being inflamed with divine zeal.

*Troparion:*
Thy lips, filled with life-flowing streams, gushed forth rivers of divine teachings, O hieromartyr, drowning the mockery of the lawless, and watering the hearts of those who have recognized Christ God.

*Troparion:*
Greatly glorifying thee, thy Creator, for Whose sake thou wast zealous to suffer, O passion-bearer, sends unto thee a dove bringing food angelic, who didst become equal to the angels, shining with most radiant sufferings.

*Theotokion:*
The angelic hosts were struck with awe, beholding how the One invisible in appearance became visible from thee in the likeness of our nature, O Virgin Mother of God; beseech Him to grant salvation unto all who with faith glorify thee.

*Another [Canon], Ode 4. Heirmos:*
A rod from the root of Jesse, and a blossom from it, O Christ, Thou didst sprout forth from the Virgin; from the mountain praiseworthy and overshadowed grove Thou didst come, incarnate from the unwedded one, O immaterial One and God: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
When once in the time of youth thou wast overcome by sleep and didst grow slack during the all-night standing, thy venerable teacher Peter, seeing this, struck thee upon the face, O father; and having given thee forgetfulness, straightway he grants thee healing.

*Troparion:*
Conversing privately[^155] with God, and having drawn near unto Him immediately, Paul our father remained never overcome by sleep after the teacher's strike, but as though bodiless, was ever vigilant.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst appear as a most sacred vessel, and didst receive the heavenly myrrh, Christ, within Thy heart; and having brightly kindled the lamp of Thy patient endurance through a virtuous life, thou hast ascended unto the divine bridal chamber.

*Theotokion:*
Having heaven as Thy throne, O Word, and earth as Thy footstool, Thou didst enter into the womb of the Virgin, being incarnate, and wast contained in a poor cave; and from the Magi, Persian kings, Thou didst receive gifts as King and God-man.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Grant us Thy peace, O Son of God; for beside Thee we know no other God; we name Thy Name, for Thou art the God of the living and of the dead.

*Troparion:*
Craftily seeking to rob thee with deceitful words, O martyr, the all-wicked enemy is seen as an object of laughter, the wise one in malice being outwitted by thy wisdom.

*Troparion:*
Borne upon the chariot of divine virtues, O glorious one, thou didst reach the height of martyrdom, and cast down the exalted pride of the wicked demons.

*Troparion:*
Desiring to see the beauty of Jesus, O venerable one, thou didst adorn thyself with the beauty of martyrdom, and hast passed over unto Him, crowned with a radiant crown.

*Theotokion:*
Thy wonder amazes every mind, O pure one; for thou dost bear God in the flesh, and nourishest the Nourisher with milk, having known no trial of man, as He alone knows.

*Another [Canon], Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Being God of peace and Father of compassions, Thou hast sent unto us the Angel of Thy Great Counsel, Who grants peace; therefore, guided unto the light of the knowledge of God, watching early out of the night, we glorify Thee, O Lover of mankind.

*Troparion:*
Having cleansed thy mind of the mire of passions, thou wast an undefiled mirror, ever receiving the illuminations of the Spirit. Therefore the tempter, having assailed thee, was put to shame, having learned the weakness of the judgment of malice.

*Troparion:*
Having acquired Christ God, Who is Wisdom, dwelling within thy heart, thou didst cast down with thy fair feet the foolish sage of malice, who attempted to deceive thee, O divinely wise Paul, with manifold craftinesses.

*Troparion:*
Being a receptacle of the Light, a son of the day, thou didst foil the ruler of darkness, who plotted against thee like a lion, terrifying thee, O Paul, with earthquakes and shaking of stones, with flight and savage phantoms.

*Theotokion:*
Adam the first-formed having been cast out of Eden, O ever-virgin maiden, Bride of God, the pre-eternal Word, incarnate of thee and rocked in the manger of dumb beasts as an infant, delivered our race from irrationality.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Imitating the Prophet Jonah, I cry aloud: Deliver my life from corruption, O good One, and save me, O Savior of the world, who cry: Glory to Thee!

*Troparion:*
A distinguished ram of the flock of Christ, a most rational shepherd, is glorified along the pathway of ascetic struggles, having glorified God in his members.

*Troparion:*
Having been moved to compunction by gazing unto God, O wise one, thou didst firmly deprive the manifoldly crafty enemy of life, O ever-memorable one, glory of martyrs, rule of the priesthood.

*Troparion:*
Enduring wounds and going voluntarily unto the fire, thou didst put to sleep the onrushes of fierce wild beasts, having unslackening love toward the Creator.

*Theotokion:*
Having appeared as the tabernacle of salvation, O Mary, cleanse my wretched soul defiled by pleasures, and make me a partaker of divine glory and make me a partaker of divine glory.

*Another [Canon], Ode 6. Heirmos:*
The sea monster spat forth Jonah from its belly like an infant, just as it had received him; and the Word, having dwelt within the Virgin and taken flesh, came forth, having preserved her incorrupt; for of that corruption whereof He suffered none, He preserved the one who bore Him uninjured.

*Troparion:*
Even as the Savior Christ our God satisfied a numerous multitude with few loaves, so also Paul, the initiate of Christ's mysteries, gladdened multitudes unto satiety with the small water of a very small vessel; and the satiety shows forth abundance.

*Troparion:*
Thou dost stay the heat by thy prayers, O marvelous one, and loosenest the threatening famine; and with waters poured out from above thou dost soak the earth and water its dry furrows, causing rich gifts to sprout forth and multiplying its cultivation.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst receive painless life amid afflictions, and dost stay the distress of grievous illnesses for those who with faith ask to receive healings from thee, O all-honored one, beauty of the fathers. Therefore loosen my diseases of soul and body, I pray.

*Theotokion:*
O Word of the Father, timeless Son of God, and pre-eternal Offspring of the pure Mother and Maiden of God: as God and as man, being an infant, Thou Who art uncontainable wast contained in a cave; therefore, marveling, we all worship the great mystery.

*Kontakion of the Hieromartyr, Tone 2, Podoben: "The firm and God-proclaiming" (Тве́рдыѧ):*[^156]
As the embellishment of priests, O venerable one, and forerunner of suffering among the passion-bearers, we all praise thee and entreat thee, O hieromartyr Eleutherius: Free from manifold tribulations those who celebrate thy memory with love, praying unceasingly for us all.

*Ikos:*
Overlook the darkening of my soul, O compassionate Giver of life, as the only Lover of mankind and merciful God, and by Thy all-powerful right hand, O Word, free me from the assault of passions, that I may sing of Thy hierarch Eleutherius; for he was truly known unto Thee from the womb, and was sanctified and dedicated unto Thee, the Creator, like Samuel by a holy mother, praying unceasingly for us all.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The fire neither touched nor troubled Thy children in the furnace, O Savior. Then the three, as with one mouth, sang and blessed, saying: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
"Let Christ now be magnified in my flesh," thou didst cry aloud, O wise one, when being torn to pieces; "for I am not terrified by the heating of cauldrons, nor do I fear death, nor the rushes of wild beasts, for the sake of the life that truly is."

*Troparion:*
"Seeking the beauty of God alone, I desire to obtain His glory alone: let my whole body be torn to pieces and burned," thou didst cry aloud, O glorious one: "...of Christ Who frees the world from enslavement."

*Troparion:*
Beholding the future life, O blessed one, thou wast truly dead unto the world; and like gold refined by trials of wounds, thou didst shine forth, and wast laid up in the treasury of heavenly mansions.

*Theotokion:*
Having found thee alone most pure, O all-immaculate one, the most pure Word of God was born from thy womb, cleansing the faithful, O Bride of God, from defilement that hath accrued unto us from lack of restraint in passions.

*Another [Canon], Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The youths nurtured together in piety, disregarding the command of the impious one, feared not the threat of fire, but standing in the midst of the flame, they sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Shining forth as the sun, straightway thou didst enlighten the East; and having ascended the pillar, as though standing in the midst of heaven, thou didst gladden the whole inhabited earth with teachings, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst depart afar off, fleeing the turmoils of the world, and didst take up thy dwelling in the wilderness psalm-like,[^157] O divinely blessed one; thou didst receive God within thy heart, Who preserved thee by angelic custody.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst behold the torments of the world beyond with the eyes of the mind, and grieving in heart through thy soul that loves mankind, thou didst ever wash thyself with tears, not only like David his bed by night.

*Theotokion:*
The bodiless One is incarnate, and the timeless One comes into time; and He Who swaddles the earth with darkness, the Lord, is swaddled in bands for our sake, having Himself ineffably appeared in flesh, beyond comprehension, from the unwedded one.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Him at Whom the angels and all the hosts are struck with awe as Creator and Lord: praise, ye priests; glorify, ye children; bless, ye people, and exalt Him above all unto all ages.

*Troparion:*
Having flourished, thou didst blossom forth as a fair garden by the brightness of thy sufferings, O beauty of martyrs; and now ye have appeared as flowers of paradise, divinely pouring forth divine fragrance.

*Troparion:*
With the sprinklings of thy blood, who wast born of her, the mother unites her own blood; for when thy body was beheaded, O wise one, she is finished by the sword, and lives unto the ages.

*Troparion:*
Waters of healings and rivers of wonders does thy shrine pour forth unto those in need, O wise one, washing away the defilements of soul-destroying passions, O martyr and hierarch, unto all ages.

*Theotokion:*
As rain Christ came down into thy womb, and truly watered all creation, having dried up, O Virgin, the muddy rivers of the madness of idolatry, being the only Benefactor.

*Another [Canon], Ode 8. Heirmos:*
The dew-bearing furnace portrayed the image of a supernatural wonder; for it burned not the youths whom it had received, just as the fire of the Godhead burned not the womb of the Virgin into which It entered. Therefore, singing, let us chant: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages.

*Troparion:*
In harmony with David, thou didst chant a sweet-voiced, all-tuneful song, saying: "Thy consolations, O King of all, by a divinely fitting and man-befriending nod, have gladdened my soul." Therefore rejoicing thou didst cry aloud: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages.

*Troparion:*
The Creator, Who from youth preserved thee by His right hand, rewarded thee in accordance with thy love; and He nourishes thee divinely with three plants,[^158] as having from infancy trampled underfoot every lustful desire; and He gives these by the hand of an angel unto thee who didst emulate the angelic life, O all-glorious and God-bearing Paul.

*Troparion:*
Three condemned bound men were able to escape condemnation, because they turned aside from common servitude; for they were invisibly loosed from bonds by thy name, O all-glorious father. Deliver the bound from tribulations, as those who are borne by the one hand of the Upholder.

*Theotokion:*
She who bore the Sun of Righteousness, with a star summons the Magi with gold and myrrh and frankincense, marvelously worshiping Him Who unwedded became a Mother; Whom the shepherds magnified, and a multitude of angels praised and glorified, as God by essence and man by nature.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
The life-receiving and ever-flowing fountain, the light-bearing lamp of grace, the animate temple, the most pure tabernacle, the most pure one, wider than the heavens and the earth, we the faithful magnify the Birthgiver of God.

*Troparion:*
Having become the mouth of God, snatching vain-minded people from the mouth of the stranger, thou didst show them forth as heirs of grace; and having suffered valiantly, thou dost live with priests and sufferers, O Eleutherius.

*Troparion:*
The pure repository of the myrrh of the Spirit, the fair dwelling of virtues, the guileless lamb, the never-setting beacon, the degree and praise of hierarchs and martyrs, let Eleutherius be faithfully praised!

*Troparion:*
Thou dwellest truly in the unwaning Light, having become a light brighter than the sun. Therefore deliver from the gloom of passions those who celebrate today thy light-bearing memory, by thy prayers unto God, O Eleutherius.

*Theotokion:*
Spare us who sing of Thine ineffable Nativity from the Virgin, O Lord, delivering Thy servants from tribulations, passions, and sorrows through her supplications, as Benefactor and the only Lover of mankind.

*Another [Canon], Ode 9. Heirmos:*
I behold a strange and most glorious mystery: heaven is the cave; the Cherubic throne is the Virgin; the manger is the receptacle, wherein lay Christ God, Whom nothing can contain: Whom singing, we magnify.

*Troparion:*
Thy boldness before God, and the marvelous works which Thou didst perform after thy departure unto Him, proclaim the same; for by the oil of thy lamp-lighting Thou didst deliver many from diverse diseases.

*Troparion:*
Having an enlightened soul, O venerable one, as one wholly imbued with the myrrh of grace: with oil thou dost drive away demons, cleansing the lepers, and checking the sicknesses of bitten heads and fierce scabs.

*Troparion:*
The all-wicked Satan, having fallen apart in the form of an all-fierce beast, fell down, seeing thee pouring out the oil of thy lamp as myrrh for the healing of diverse diseases, and seized with fear, he vanished.

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst conceive in the latter times in thy womb the Son Whom the Father begot incorruptibly before the ages, O unwedded Mother. Him the heavens show forth with a star, and the earth with an earthly cave.

*Exapostilarion of the Oktoechos:*
*Glory to the Venerable Father, Podoben: "With the disciples let us go up" (Со оу҆чени́ки взы́демъ):*[^159]
David-like thou didst flourish in the house of the Lord like a palm tree, O venerable father, having now multiplied an hundredfold the fruits of thy labors;

therefore, O blessed Paul, having drowned the host of demons by the torrents of thy tears, thou hast received from Christ the prize and the crown of victory, and, O all-wise one, an enviably rich grace of miracles.

*Theotokion:*
He Who on high is divinely glorified by angels, without leaving the Father's bosom, O pure one, ineffably dwelt with those below; and thou wast the cause of this salvation, having beyond word lent flesh unto Him from thy pure blood, O pure one. Pray Him to grant unto thy servants deliverance from offenses.

*At the Aposticha, from the Oktoechos.*

*On the 16th Day of the Same Month. The Holy Prophet Haggai:*
*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera, Tone 8, Podoben: "O Lord, Thy martyrs" (Мч҃нцы твоѝ гдⷭи):*[^160]
Having become a dwelling place of thy Lord and an animate temple by the brightness of thy life and thy conversation, thou didst raise up of old the fallen inanimate temple, O all-honored one, unto Him Who reigns over the universe; entreat Him with fervent prayers that He grant great mercy unto all.

*Sticheron:*
Thou didst appear as a vessel of the Spirit, receiving the light-pourings given unto thee from the heavens, and receptive of splendors; therefore thou dost foretell the saving deliverance for all men; beseech Him by thy prayers that He grant great mercy unto all.

*Sticheron:*
Shining with ray-bearing dawn, and vouchsafed visions, thou didst appear full of the purest and unwaning enlightenment, O blessed one; preserve those who sing of thee, entreating the only Lord to give great mercy unto all.

*Other Stichera to the Most Holy Birthgiver of God, Tone and Podoben the same (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*
Snatch me away, O compassionate one, from the hand of the man-slaying serpent who wars against me to swallow me up completely by deceit; shatter his jaws, I pray thee, and destroy his craftinesses; that, having been delivered from his claws, I may magnify thy power.

*Theotokion:*
I am an unfruitful tree, O all-immaculate one, bearing no fruit of salvation; therefore I tremble at being hewn down, lest I be cast into the unquenchable fire, wretched one that I am; therefore I fall down before thee: deliver me from this, and by thy mediation, O pure one, show me forth as fruitful unto thy Son.

*Theotokion:*
My thoughts are unclean, my lips deceitful, and all my deeds defiled; and what shall I do? How shall I meet the Judge? O good Virgin, pray to thy Son and Creator and Lord, that He receive my spirit in repentance, as the only compassionate One.

*Glory... Both now, Theotokion:*
Woe unto him who hath provoked his God to wrath—woe is me!—in ignorance, and who abides in despondency and slothfulness, as do I! O good Virgin, help me who am darkened, and pray to thy Son and Creator that He grant me forgiveness of offenses.

*Stavrotheotokion:*
The spotless heifer, beholding the Calf willingly nailed upon the Tree, weeping piteously, cried aloud: "Woe is me, O most beloved Child! What hath the thankless Hebrew assembly rendered unto Thee, wishing to make me childless of Thee, O all-beloved One?"

*At Matins, both Canons from the Oktoechos; and of the Prophet, on 4, whose acrostic is: "We sing the God-given words of Haggai." By Theophanes, Tone 2:*[^161]
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Unto God Who delivered Israel from the Red Sea, let us sing a song of victory, for He is glorified!

*Troparion:*
Standing before God as a most clear seer of God and a true prophet, remember those who sing of thy honored memory, O blessed one.

*Troparion:*
Having built up thyself upon the firm foundation of virtues, thou didst dedicate thyself as an animate temple, O divinely blessed one.

*Troparion:*
Thy most pure mind, ever beholding God as far as is possible, shone forth far-beaming with gifts from on high, O blessed one.

*Theotokion:*
Having conceived in the womb according to the flesh the Word of God Who was formerly without a mother, the Virgin gave birth to a Son without a father.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
The Church of Christ is established in faith; for unceasingly with hymns she cries aloud, chanting: Holy art Thou, O Lord, and my spirit sings of Thee!

*Troparion:*
Having loosed us from the grievous captivity of demons by divine power, show us forth as Thy precious temples, O Savior, who cry unto Thee: "Holy art Thou!", saving our souls.

*Troparion:*
He Who dwells in the highest and fills the universe with holiness, O prophet, shows thee forth as a temple, saving our souls who cry: "Holy art Thou!"

*Troparion:*
The divine Spirit, distributing grace unto all, made His abode within thy heart, teaching thee to cry: "Holy art Thou, O Lord, Who savest our souls!"

*Theotokion:*
He Who by the Word wisely created all creation is formed from thee in our likeness, O Birthgiver of God, having become man out of tender mercy, the Lover of mankind.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 3, Podoben: "Of the divine faith" (Бж҃твенныѧ вѣ́ры):*[^162]
Having a mind enlightened by the divine Spirit, O prophet, thou dost foretell the mysteries of God, revealing the manifestation of things to come, and declaring the fulfillment of events, O all-blessed Haggai: pray to Christ God that He grant us great mercy.

*Glory... Both now, Theotokion:*
He departed not from the divine nature, having become flesh in thy womb; but being God, He became man and so remained, the only Lord, Who after childbirth preserved thee an all-immaculate Virgin Mother, even as before childbirth; beseech Him fervently to grant us great mercy.

*Stavrotheotokion:*
The spotless ewe-lamb of the Word, the incorrupt Virgin Mother, beholding Him Who sprang forth from her without pain suspended upon the Cross, lamenting mother-like, cried aloud: "Woe is me, O my Child! How dost Thou suffer willingly, desiring to deliver man from shameful passions?"

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I heard report of Thee, O Lord, that Thou hast appeared on earth in order to save us; therefore we cry: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst show forth unto Thy prophet, O Christ, the animate house received from the Virgin for Thyself; with whom we cry: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Thou hast gathered together the outcasts, O Lord, freeing us from the bondage of the enemy, as says the God-accepted prophet.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst reveal the future salvation of the nations in the latter days unto Thy prophet, O Christ, who cries unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst turn the curse of Adam into a blessing, O good one, having born Christ for us, unto Whom we cry: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Unto Thee I rise early and unto Thee I cry, O compassionate Lord: enlighten my soul, darkened by sins, with the light of Thy commandments, and guide me.

*Troparion:*
Vouchsafe that those who celebrate thy light-bearing feast may be temples of the living God, O blessed one, having established them upon the rock of thy dogmas by thy prayers.

*Troparion:*
As Benefactor, grant us Thy peace, O Lord, which is unto edification, peace of soul, which the divine Haggai foretold by the divine Spirit.

*Troparion:*
Great in truth shall be the renown of the Church, beyond the former congregation of Israel, for the Word became incarnate and was reconciled unto men.

*Theotokion:*
O blessed and all-glorified Mother who knewest not man, quicken my soul which is slain by sins and buried by the passions of intemperance.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Jonah cried aloud from the belly of hades: Lead up my life from corruption! And we cry aloud unto Thee: O almighty Savior, have mercy upon us!

*Troparion:*
Teaching piety with youthful vigor, O blessed one, thou didst raise up a consecrated temple unto the Master of all, promising an abundance of good things.

*Troparion:*
Thou hast led up man from earthly captivity, O Savior, out of the lowest depths, and hast brought him unto the celestial city, as Lover of mankind.

*Troparion:*
Rejoicing in the rays of the Spirit, O prophet, thou didst utter words of deeds, and instructed us in the ordinances of piety.

*Theotokion:*
Having fallen by his own will, Adam was cast out of paradise; but the Word, having taken flesh from the Virgin, calls him back and leads him up to celestial sweetness.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
Cast into the fiery furnace, the venerable youths changed the fire into dew, singing and crying aloud thus: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Having purified thy mind, O prophet, thou didst openly receive the radiance of the Spirit, clearly prophesying and crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Seeing thee leading a holy life, God appointed thee as a prophet of His coming, crying aloud unto all: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
He Who saved the three youths in the fiery furnace, O Virgin, dwelt within thy womb; He saves those who put their trust in Him, who cry aloud: Blessed is the fruit of thy womb, O all-immaculate one!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Him Who alone is the unoriginate King of glory, Whom the heavenly hosts bless and the angelic ranks tremble before: praise Him, O priests; let the people exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
We hymn Thee in song, O Master of all, Whom the prophet and God-seer Haggai showed forth, that we should worship and chant: Praise Him, O priests; let the people exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
That the unoriginate Word should appear in the latter times, O prophet and God-seer, thou didst proclaim, clearly crying aloud: Praise Him, O priests; let the people exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
He Who before was invisible and uncontainable by nature, being contained within thy womb became visible, O all-immaculate one, unto Whom we cry aloud with faith: Praise Him, O priests; let the people exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
O radiant one, higher than the heavens, who didst conceive without seed the unoriginate Word, and didst bear the incarnate God for men, therefore we all magnify thee.

*Troparion:*
Having laid hold of the vision of God which is beyond words, O prophet, thou didst shake off earthly cares, and didst stand worthily before the all-glorified God; therefore we all, the faithful, call thee blessed.

*Troparion:*
Thy divine and marvelous life, O blessed one, showed thee forth as an intercessor before God, O God-wise one; and thou dost rejoice eternally with the bodiless choirs; therefore we all ever call thee blessed.

*Troparion:*
It was fitting for thee, as a teacher of piety, to be with God, and to partake of His most pure light; Whom do thou now beseech, O blessed one, to deliver our souls from temptations.

*Theotokion:*
Supernaturally, O Mother of God, thou wast in truth the dwelling-place of the King of all, and the golden Ark, holding within Christ, the only Lawgiver, Who was incarnate.

*In the same month, on the 17th day: The Holy Prophet Daniel, and the Three Holy Children: Ananias, Azarias, and Misael.*
*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Prophet, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*[^163]
The marvelous Daniel, having acquired a pure heart as a dwelling of the Spirit, and enlightened by Him, clearly foretells the revelation of future things, adorned with the brightness of prophecy, and lucidly interpreting the hidden dreams of mighty, iniquitous kings.

Having strengthened thy body beforehand with unyielding fasting, thou didst shut the mouths of the lions; for standing in the midst of them, O marvelous prophet, and looking unto the good God, thou didst remain unharmed by the ineffable power of Him Who gloriously works all things, the Deliverer of our souls.

Sitting upon a throne, encompassed by angels, thou didst behold the unsearchable Judge, the righteous Lord, O marvelous prophet; and being astonished at the dreadful and fearful vision, thou didst mark out for all who should come after, describing the second coming of our God Who was incarnate.

*Other Stichera of the Holy Children, in the same tone, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*[^164]
Holding fast unto the God-given laws, O all-blessed ones, ye were not defiled by abominable foods; but having preserved the incorrupt beauty of your souls, ye kept the unharmed and unfading marvelous bloom of your flesh and its fair comeliness, while the Master glorified His servants.

Enkindled with divine fire, the youths disregarded the physical fire; and being bedewed therein, the honorable ones formed a most radiant choir, and set themselves to singing a hymn of much praise; for Daniel, seeing the unending Kingdom of Christ, rejoiced as a most preeminent prophet.

At the words of thy wisdom, O Daniel worthy of wonder, the torturers marvelled, and at the understanding of the children; and they appointed you honorable ones to govern and rule over the land of the Chaldeans; for even the adversary knows how to marvel most clearly at virtue and at the brightness of life; for having mastered the passions, ye became masters.

*Glory... Tone 2 (By Anatolios):*
Spiritually has the prophet Daniel gathered us, the faithful, together today, and set forth an abundant table of virtues for the rich and the poor, for strangers and household members, and a chalice that pours forth the water of piety for the minds, gladness for the hearts of the faithful, and provides the grace of the Holy Spirit. For this prophet, shining forth as a most bright luminary in the world, cast down all the Assyrian worship, and stopped the mouths of untamed beasts; and with him let the three children be praised, who, not being gold by nature, showed themselves to be more tried than gold; for the fire of the furnace did not consume them, but preserved them whole.

whom the naphtha, pitch, and brushwood crowned. And may the Lord Who brought us through the revolution of the year make us worthy to attain also unto the Lord's own honorable day of the Nativity of Christ, Who grants us through their prayers cleansing of sins and great mercy.

*Both now, of the Forefeast, the same tone (By Andrew of Pyrgos):*[^165]
Come, all ye faithful, let us keep the Forefeast of the Nativity of Christ in faith, and intellectually offer our chanting as a star; with the doxologies of the Magi, let us cry aloud with the shepherds: The deliverance of mankind has come from virginal loins, calling the faithful!

*At the Aposticha, from the Oktoechos:*
*Glory... Both now, Tone 6:*
Daniel, a man of desires, having seen Thee, O Lord, as a stone cut out without hands, foretold Thee as an Infant born without seed, the incarnate Word from the Virgin, the unchangeable God, and the Savior of our souls.

*Troparion, Tone 2:*
Great are the achievements of faith! In the fountain of the flame, as upon the waters of rest, the three holy children rejoiced; and the prophet Daniel was shown forth as a shepherd unto the lions, as though unto sheep. By their prayers, O Christ God, save our souls!

*At Matins, one canon from the Oktoechos, and two of the saints. Canon of the Prophet, whose acrostic is: "With songs I crown the wise Daniel." The composition of Theophanes. Tone 8.*[^166]
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Let us send up a song, O ye people, unto our marvelous God, Who freed Israel from bondage, singing a song of victory and crying aloud: We sing unto Thee, the only Master!

*Troparion:*
O Savior and Benefactor, Cause of all good things, with Thy light-bearing radiance enlighten my mind, O Lover of mankind, that I may praise the glorious memory of Thy prophet.

*Troparion:*
Having shone forth like the dawn of chastity, O wise one, thou didst save the chaste Susanna who was in mortal peril; for God, Who knows all corrupt things, raised thee up to convict the cruel elders.

*Troparion:*
Strengthened by the fear of God, the grandsons of Abraham manfully cast away the iniquitous food, and being fed by the divine desire for piety, they were raised unto the greatest glory.

*Theotokion:*
A noetic mountain didst thou behold, O most holy Daniel: the one all-immaculate ever-virgin Maiden, from whom was cut out without hands the cornerstone, which shattered the deception of the adversary entirely.

*Another Canon of the Three Holy Children, whose acrostic is: "I sing the three children, and the great Daniel." The composition of Theophanes. The same tone [Tone 8].*[^167]
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Having passed through the water as through dry land, and escaped the Egyptian malice, the Israelite cried aloud: Let us sing unto our Deliverer and God!

*Troparion:*
The unoriginate Word begotten of the Father before all ages in a manner befitting God, Who was seen in the furnace in a figure by the youths, let us glorify.

*Troparion:*
Having patiently spat upon the blasphemies of the impious tyrant, the noble youths would not defile themselves in the Chaldean manner with the foods of the iniquitous.

*Troparion:*
They were fed spiritually by the word, and bodily with wild pulse; and they appeared unto the king more fair in countenance than those who fed on rich dainties.

*Theotokion:*
Thou, O Maiden who didst sprout forth from David, dost heal the poison of the serpent that was bitterly poured into the ears of Eve, having given birth to the Deliverer.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Thou art the affirmation of those who run unto Thee, O Lord; Thou art the light of the darkened, and my spirit sings of Thee.

*Troparion:*
Having received understanding and wisdom from God, thou didst clearly interpret the shadowy dreams unto kings.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst put to death the visible serpent, casting food unto it, O glorious one; for first thou didst conquer the invisible demons.

*Theotokion:*
Enlightened by the dawn, in a vision thou dost behold the blessed mountain of God, O glorious one, the adornment of men.

*Ode 3 (Canon 2). Heirmos [The same]:*
*Troparion:*
Having acquired a God-inspired understanding, O Master, the Davidic youths wisely observed the laws of their fathers.

*Troparion:*
The fire burned not the most pure bodies of the pious, for they were bedewed by soul-nourishing fasting.

*Troparion:*
A universal hymn of much praise do the three children sing, being marvelously bedewed in the midst of the furnace.

*Theotokion:*
That Thou mightest show forth unto us Thy birth, O Master, from a virginal body, Thou didst save the virginal bodies in the furnace.

*Kontakion of the Prophet, Tone 3, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дв҃а дне́сь):*[^168]
Thy pure heart, enlightened by the Spirit, became the receptacle of most clear prophecy; for thou didst see things far off as though present; and cast into the den, thou didst tame the lions; therefore do we honor thee, O blessed prophet, glorious Daniel!

*Ikos:*
Pray unceasingly unto Jesus Christ our true God, Whose divine coming into the world thou didst proclaim, that those who celebrate this thy divine memory with gladness, and who honor thee with faith, may be saved from all temptations, and sins, and tribulations, since thou hast boldness, O God-wise one; and grant unblameworthy speech unto the opening of my lips to chant of thee, and by no means abhor me, O blessed prophet, glorious Daniel!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*[^169]
Prophetically, with the reed of faith, the youths depicted the image of the Trinity in the flame with immaterial colors; and mystically they saw the supreme descent of the Word to the earth, and proclaimed it unto all; therefore, having received spiritual dew from heaven, they pour forth gifts unto the faithful who cry aloud unto Thee in concord: Grant remission of transgressions, O Christ God, as Thou art compassionate, unto those who celebrate with love your holy memory.

*Glory... Another Sessional Hymn, the same model:*
Enriched with the grace of prophecy, thou didst sacredly describe the Virgin's childbirth, and clearly interpret dreams unto kings; and cast into the den as a martyr, O glorious and blessed one, thou didst miraculously teach the lions to fast; therefore thou didst tear down the service of the godless, and having manfully slain the serpent, O Daniel worthy of wonder, shone most radiantly; pray to Christ God that He grant remission of sins unto those who celebrate with love thy holy memory.

*Both now, Theotokion:*
Rejoice, fiery throne of God! Rejoice, O Maiden, royal seat, couch adorned with dazzling splendor, golden-purple bridal chamber, scarlet-gleaming robe, adorned temple, lightning-bearing weapon, most radiant lampstand! Rejoice, O Birthgiver of God, city of ninety walls,[^170] golden-wrought door, bright-formed bridal chamber, table gilded with splendor, God-adorned tabernacle! Rejoice, glorious Bride dripping sunshine! Rejoice, thou alone the beauty of my soul!

*Stavrotheotokion:*
The ewe-lamb, beholding the Lamb and Shepherd and Deliverer upon the Cross, cried aloud weeping, and bitterly lamenting cried out:

The world rejoices, receiving redemption through Thee; but my womb burns, beholding Thy Crucifixion, which Thou dost endure in Thy merciful compassion, O longsuffering Lord, Abyss of mercy and inexhaustible Fountain! Have compassion, and grant remission of transgressions unto those who chant with faith of Thy divine Passions!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
From the overshadowed mountain, O Word, even from the only Birthgiver of God, the prophet with divine vision perceived that Thou wouldst become incarnate, and with fear he glorified Thy power.

*Troparion:*
Having piously kept the Law, O prophet, thou didst know the Giver of divine wisdom, Who taught thee mystical and deep things, and enlightened thee in things that were in darkness.

*Troparion:*
Having lived a holy life, O God-manifest one, thou wast called a man of desires; for having manfully trampled down the passions, thou didst pass over unto the unaging life.

*Troparion:*
The grace of the Comforter which made its dwelling in thee, O Daniel, shows thee forth as light-bearing, a conqueror of tyrants and kings, and a dwelling-place of wisdom.

*Theotokion:*
As a stone cut out without hands from the mountain, from the Virgin Birthgiver of God, did the prophet Daniel behold Thee, O Word, crying aloud and hymning Thy divinity.

*Ode 4 (Canon 2). Heirmos:*
I have heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation; I have considered Thy works, and glorified Thy divinity.

*Troparion:*
Daniel the most wise, enlightened by divine understanding, interpreted the dreams of the autocrats by divine grace.

*Troparion:*
The suffering of the children in the furnace shines with miracles, for they caught the tyrant unto the knowledge of Thee, O Almighty One.

*Troparion:*
Instruments of harmony and all-musical songs drew not the valiant ones, and they bowed not down unto the golden image.

*Theotokion:*
With hymns, O all-hymned one, the children in Babylon honor Thy most divine Son, Whom they recognized in the furnace.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Out of the night of ignorance, having enlightened the ends of the earth with the knowledge of God, enlighten me in the morning of Thy love for mankind, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Having illuminated the ascetical struggles of the prophets by thy preaching, thou shinest with both, being filled with divine inspiration.

Thou wast shown to be all-wise, O blessed one, by the radiances of wisdom which surpasses the mind, O most great and God-speaking Daniel, and thou didst enlighten all things.

*Theotokion:*
The glorious prophet Daniel mystically guided the images of the ineffable incarnation of Him Who came forth from thee, O pure one.

*Ode 5 (Canon 2). Heirmos:*
Why hast Thou cast me off from Thy face, O unwaning Light, and an alien darkness has covered me, the wretched one? But turn me back, and direct my paths toward the light of Thy commandments, I pray Thee!

*Troparion:*
Having been instructed in the Law, O Savior, Thy servants apostatized not: the great Daniel with the three God-wise youths; but having received strength from Thee, the Benefactor, they manfully conquered the torturers.

*Troparion:*
Intellectually was Daniel instructed in Thy mysteries, O Lover of mankind; for he beheld Thee in the purity of his mind coming on the clouds as the Son of Man, the Judge and King of all nations.

*Troparion:*
Adorned, O children, beyond the sapphire stone was your gathering; for enkindled with zeal for piety like a golden radiance, ye walked with joy in the furnace, forming a universal choir.

*Theotokion:*
Daniel clearly depicted thee beforehand as the divine mountain, O Virgin; and the three children, seeing the flame become dew, praise in song thy divine childbirth, as of the Savior, Creator, and Lord.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
As Thou didst deliver the prophet out of the lowest depths, O Christ God, deliver me also from my sins, as Lover of mankind, and direct my life, I pray Thee!

*Troparion:*
Beholding the angelic choirs in the most bright light, thou wast a most preeminent imitator of them, enjoying the splendors of the King of all.

*Troparion:*
Proclaiming the saving coming of the Word, thou didst foretell also the destruction of the temple, the fulfillment of the Law, and the bestowing of grace that passes understanding.

*Theotokion:*
Behold, the Virgin clearly conceives in her womb Christ God, having been overshadowed by the Spirit, whose prefiguration the glorious Daniel foresaw.

*Ode 6 (Canon 2). Heirmos:*
The abyss of sins and the tempest of transgressions troubles me, and drags me into the deep of grievous despair; but stretch forth Thy strong hand unto me, as unto Peter, O Pilot, and save me!

*Troparion:*
Having mastered the natural passions by the power of the Word, ye became rulers in the land of the Chaldean nations; for virtue knows how to grant honor unto those who have acquired it, O wise grandsons of David.

*Troparion:*
Having clothed himself in life-bearing mortification of old, Daniel slew with food the most evil dragon which the Chaldeans impiously considered a god; and he wisely put to death the impious priests.

*Theotokion:*
Beseech Thy Son and Judge, O Virgin Birthgiver of God, to be merciful unto me in the day of judgment through thy prayers, and to deliver me from cruel evils, O Mother; for in thee alone do I place my hope.

*Kontakion [of the Three Children], Tone 6:*[^171]
Not honoring an image made by hands, but shielded by the uncircumscribed Essence, O thrice-blessed ones, ye were glorified in the ordeal of fire; and standing in the midst of the unbearable flame, ye called upon God: Make haste, O Compassionate One, and speed to our help as Thou art merciful, for Thou art able, if Thou wilt!

*Ikos:*
Stretch forth Thy hand, wherewith the contending Egyptians and the battling Hebrews received trial of old; forsake us not, lest death which thirsts after us and Satan who hates us swallow us up; but draw near unto us and spare our souls, even as Thou didst spare of old Thy youths who were in Babylon, who unceasingly glorified Thee, and who were cast for Thy sake into the furnace, and cried unto Thee from it: Make haste, O Compassionate One, and speed to our help as Thou art merciful, for Thou art able, if Thou wilt!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The Hebrew children in the furnace boldly trampled on the flame, and changed the fire into dew, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Fortified by the Law, O prophet, thou didst not accept to be defiled unlawfully; but enlightened in mind in a divine manner, thou didst cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Thy wonder astonishes all; for as a prophet unto a prophet, [Habakkuk] stood before thee carried by an angel, bringing thee food and singing: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Shut within the den and set forth as food for the lions, thou wast saved, for God sheltered thee, O blessed one, as thou didst cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
Thou pourest forth an unstinting stream of healings, O Virgin Mother of God!

for Daniel clearly beheld thee as a mountain, from which shone forth the Savior, the God of our fathers!

*Ode 7 (Canon 2). Heirmos:*
The pious children in Babylon bowed not down unto the golden image, but bedewed in the midst of the fiery furnace, they sang a hymn, saying: Blessed art Thou, O supremely exalted God of our fathers and our God!

*Troparion:*
A God-pleasing voice was sung from the midst of the fire unto the Almighty; for Azarias, having formed a divine choir, sang a hymn, saying: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
The pipe of the youths theologized God and Almighty Ruler of all, Who clearly appeared unto them in the furnace, and they sang a hymn, saying: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Seeing three cast into the furnace, when the king beheld the form of a fourth, he named Him the Son of God, and cried aloud unto all: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
Having a mind enlightened with divine radiance, O divinely blessed Daniel, thou didst clearly foresee the Virgin's childbirth figured by mystical images, crying aloud: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
The God-proclaiming children in the furnace, trampling the flame together with the fire, sang: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Thou wast shown to be consecrated, O prophet, and through active vision thou didst chant with the bodiless hosts: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Thee, O all-blessed one, do we all praise with blessings, and in thy venerable festival we cry aloud rejoicing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Theotokion:*
Having perceived the most marvelous Maiden through prefigurative types, O God-proclaimer, thou didst cry aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Ode 8 (Canon 2). Heirmos:*
The Chaldean tyrant furiously kindled the furnace sevenfold for the godly ones; but seeing them saved by a higher power, he cried unto the Creator and Deliverer: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Striving to preserve the noble birth of Abraham, ye acquired the foundation of faith kindred unto him, and the hope, O venerable ones, of endurance and expectation in tribulations, crying aloud: Ye priests, bless the Master; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Having shone forth as luminaries, and made the earth heavenly, and having appeared enlightened with the radiance of piety, having formed a universal choir, they sing unto the Master Who saved them from tribulations: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Having youthfully quenched the kindled furnace, and having bound the jaws of lions, the descendants of David now rejoicing sing unto Thee, the Benefactor, the King of all: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
The most wise Daniel mystically instructs, and the three God-wise children depict beforehand thy childbirth, O most pure one, beholding through types Him Who ineffably came forth from thy womb; Whom the children bless, the priests hymn, and the people supremely exalt unto all ages.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Truly we confess thee as the Birthgiver of God, being saved through thee, O pure Virgin, magnifying thee with the bodiless choirs.

*Troparion:*
Thou hast reaped the fruit of thy labors, ever keeping festival in the heavens with the prophets around the most high throne of the Almighty; crowned with the thrice-sunlit light, thou now standest before the Utmost of desires, rejoicing with the bodiless choirs.

*Theotokion:*
Beauteous is thy glory, which thou now dost enjoy; for thou, O venerable prophet, wast vouchsafed to proclaim the all-hymned Maiden unto all through types.

*Another [Canon], Heirmos the same:*
Ye have attained the desired end, and stand before the Utmost of desires in the heavenly chambers, O all-rich children.

*Troparion:*
Rejoicing, ye received the sheaves that sprang from tears, the fruit of your good labor, having borne the ear of incorruption.

*Troparion:*
Radiance has now worthily shone forth upon you, and gladness of heart has blossomed; for from whence sorrow has fled away, rejoice ye!

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst halt the burden of death, O Virgin, having given birth unto the Giver of life and the Lord, Who quickens all things.

*Exapostilarion of the Oktoechos:*
*Glory to the Prophet:*
Let Daniel, the greatest among the prophets, now be honored; for he beheld Christ our God as a stone cut out without hands from the mountain, the pure Birthgiver of God.[^172] With him let the three children also be praised, whom He saved from the furnace of fire unharmed, the divine and ineffable image of the Virgin, whereby the world was saved.

*Both now:*
The most wise Daniel mystically instructs through the divine Spirit, O all-pure one, and the three Abrahamic children depict by faith thy seedless childbirth; for the Son, the Word uncircumscribed in divinity, desiring to be circumscribed in flesh from thee, O Birthgiver of God, is born in Bethlehem unto the salvation of mankind.

*At the Aposticha of the Oktoechos:*
*Glory, and both now:*
*Tone 6, by Malaxos:*[^173]
When the noetic Sun of righteousness was about to shine forth from a virginal womb, like bright stars the children, equal in number to the Trinity, shone beforehand upon us from the furnace of fire, prefiguring the strange mystery in themselves. With them also Daniel, the most radiant prophet, illuminates the ends of the earth with the light of prophecy, preaching Christ the stone cut out without hands, proceeding from the Virgin, the overshadowed mountain, unto the salvation of our souls.

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes from the Canon of the Prophet, Ode 3; and of the Children, Ode 6.*
*Prokeimenon, Tone 4:* God is wonderful in His saints, the God of Israel. *Verse:* In the congregations bless ye God, the Lord from the springs of Israel. [Ps. 67:36, 27] *Epistle to the Hebrews, Pericope 331 [Heb. 11:33–40].* *Alleluia, Tone 4:* The righteous cried, and the Lord gave ear unto them. [Ps. 33:18] *Gospel according to Luke, Pericope 72 [Luke 13:19–29].* *Communion Hymn:* Rejoice: [Ps. 32:1]

*It should be known: If the commemoration of the Holy Prophet Daniel and the Three Holy Children coincides with the Sunday of the Holy Forefathers:*
*Their office is sung together with the Sunday service thus: At Small Vespers: at "Lord, I have cried," the Sunday stichera and of the Birthgiver of God, according to custom. At Great Vespers, at "Lord, I have cried," Sunday stichera, 3; and of the Forefathers, 3; and of the Prophet Daniel, 2, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ); and of the Children, 2, in the same Tone, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе); Glory of the Forefathers, Tone 6: "He that before the Law" (И҆́же пре́жде зако́на); Both now, the first Theotokion of the Tone. Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day. At the Litya, the sticheron of the temple; and of the Prophet Daniel, Tone 4: "Upon the throne sitting" (На прⷭ҇то́лѣ сѣдѧ́щаго), written last in order at "Lord, I have cried"; and of the Children, in the same Tone: "By the word of Thy wisdom" (Словесѝ премꙋ́дрости твоеѧ̀), written last at the same "Lord, I have cried"; and Tone 2: "Spiritually hath crowned us" (Дꙋхо́внѡ на́съ вѣ́нча); Glory of the Forefathers, Tone 1: "Radiant with beams" (Лꙋча́ми ѡ҆блиста́вшеся); Both now, Theotokion: "Behold, fulfilled is" (Сѐ и҆спо́лнися). At the Aposticha, the Sunday stichera; Glory* of the Forefathers, Tone 3: "The assembly of the Forefathers" (Пра́ѻ҆тєцъ собо́ръ); Both now, of the Prophet, Tone 6: "Daniel, a man of desires" (Данїи́лъ мꙋ́жъ жела́нїй). And at the blessing of the loaves, Troparion: "O Birthgiver of God and Virgin," twice; and of the Forefathers, once. And "Blessed be the Name of the Lord," thrice. Psalm 33: "I will bless the Lord," and a reading from the Apostolic Epistles.*

*And where a vigil does not take place, at Compline we say after "It is truly meet," and after the Trisagion, the Kontakion of the Holy Forefathers. At Matins, at "God is the Lord," the Sunday troparion, twice; Glory, of the Children; Both now, of the Forefathers. After the Kathismata, the Sunday Sessional hymns with their Theotokia; and a reading in the Commentary Gospel, the Sunday in course. After the Polyeleos, the troparia: "The angelic assembly" (А҆́гг҃льскїй собо́ръ); the Hypakoe of the Tone, and the Sessional hymn of the Forefathers. And a reading in the Gospel, the Sunday of the Holy Forefathers. The Hymns of Ascent and the Prokeimenon of the Tone. The Sunday Gospel. Psalm 50. The Sunday Sticheron, and the rest. The Sunday Canon with its Heirmos on 4; of the Prophet, and of the Children, both canons on 6. And we sing at each ode: three troparia of the Prophet, the Theotokion is omitted; and of the Children the first two troparia for one, then one troparion, and the Theotokion; and of the Forefathers on 4; and we keep 12 verses besides "Glory" and "Both now"; all together on 14. Katavasia: "Christ is born."*

*After Ode 3, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Prophet, and his Sessional hymn; Glory, of the Children; Both now, the Hypakoe of the Forefathers; and a reading. After Ode 6, the Kontakion of the Forefathers, and the Ikos; and we read the Prologue. After Ode 9, the Sunday Exapostilarion, and of the Forefathers; Glory, of the Prophet; Both now, the Great Doxology. At the Praises, Sunday stichera, 4; and of the Holy Forefathers on 4, with the refrains: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers," "For Thou art righteous." Glory of the Forefathers, Tone 7: "Come, all ye faithful, let us keep festival" (Прїиди́те всѝ вѣ́рнѡ торжествꙋ́емъ); Both now: "Most blessed art thou" (Пребл҃гослове́нна є҆сѝ); Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, the Sunday troparion. Litanies, and dismissal, and the customary procession; Glory, and both now, the Gospel Sticheron; and the First Hour. At the First Hour, the Sunday troparion; Glory, of the Forefathers; Both now, the Theotokion of the Hours. After the Trisagion, the Kontakion of the Forefathers, and the rest; and the complete dismissal. At the Third Hour, the Sunday troparion; Glory, of the Prophet; Both now, the Theotokion of the Hours. After the Trisagion, the Kontakion of the Forefathers. At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Tone on 4; and of the Forefathers, Ode 3, on 4; and of the Prophet, Ode 6, on 4. After the Entrance, the Sunday troparion, then of the saints. Glory, the Kontakion of the Prophet; Both now, of the Forefathers. Prokeimenon, the Hymn of the Fathers; and the saints' Epistle and Gospel of the Sunday of the Forefathers, and of the saints. The reading in course of the Sunday is omitted. Communion Hymn: "Praise ye the Lord," [Ps. 148:1] Another: "Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous." [Ps. 32:1]*

*Note: Thus do we sing the service of a great celebrated saint also, if one should fall on this Sunday: only after the Polyeleos, Both now, the Sessional hymn of the Forefathers. At the Liturgy, the Prokeimenon of the Forefathers and of the saint; and the entire service as was set forth before.*

*On the 18th Day of the Same Month. The Holy Martyr Sebastian and his Companions:*

*It should be known: That the Sunday before the Nativity of Christ, of the Holy Fathers, begins to be sung from the 18th day of this month, and extends up to the 24th day.*

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera, Tone 1, Podoben: "O all-praised martyrs" (Всехва́льнїи мꙋ́ченницы):*
With the dyed stainings of thy precious blood, O martyr, thou didst fashion for thyself a purple robe of great price, and having clothed thyself therein, thou truly dwellest in the supreme Kingdom, standing before God, the King of all; Him beseech thou, that He grant unto our souls peace and great mercy.

O invincible martyrs, having forsaken the earth and earthly things, ye ascended unto the heavens, adorned with your wounds and brightly variegated with venerable sufferings, O blessed ones; therefore pray ye, that He grant unto our souls peace and great mercy.
