With Sebastian suffers Zoe,[^174] Marcus and Marcellinus, and the God-wise Tiburtius, having endured the threefold anguish of tortures; and now they have settled into painless and divine repose, wherein they pray that He grant unto our souls peace and great mercy.

*Stichera of the Birthgiver of God, in the same Tone and Podoben (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*
Incorruption didst thou bear in giving birth unto God, Who destroyed corruption and gushed forth incorruption, O incorrupt and immaculate one; therefore I pray thee: renew me, who have decayed through grievous sins, by thy prayers, O pure one, that I may glorify thee, that with love I magnify thee, who hast magnified our race.

All-hymned Birthgiver of God, hope and establishment of the faithful, our haven and help: we pray thee, preserve thy servants from all tribulations, who with faith bow down before thy childbirth; beseech Christ that He grant unto our souls peace and great mercy.

Woe is me! What shall become of me, having defiled mind and soul and body with offenses? What shall I do? How shall I escape the unquenchable flame, the bonds unloosed and eternal? But O all-immaculate one, before the end beseech thy Son, that He grant me remission.

*Glory, and both now, Theotokion:*
Thou didst bear within thy womb Christ, the Fire of divinity; Whom now beseech, O all-pure one, to quench all the easily-kindled substance of my passions, and to deliver me from eternal fire, and to vouchsafe me the radiance of the righteous when He comes to judge all things.

*Stavrotheotokion:*
The undefiled Lamb, when once she beheld Him upon the Tree, Whom she bore from a seedless womb, unable to endure the wounding of her inward parts, tearing her hair, cried aloud: "O Thou Who upholdest all creation by Thy beckoning, how art Thou lifted up upon the Cross as one condemned, desiring in every way to save mankind?"

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their sufferings received incorruptible crowns from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength, they cast down the tormentors, and crushed the powerless boldness of the demons; by their supplications save Thou our souls.

*At Matins, both canons of the Oktoechos; and the canon of the saints on 4, whose acrostic is: "Divinely do I wisely give honor unto thee, O martyr." A composition of Joseph.[^175] Tone 4.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Thy victorious right hand is divinely glorified in strength; for it, O immortal One, as all-powerful shattered the adversaries, fashioning anew for the Israelites a path through the deep.

*Troparion:*
Enlightened by the divine radiances of the precious Trinity, O ever-memorable one, by thy prayers show forth as partakers of the light those who with faith honor thy radiant and sacred festival.

*Troparion:*
Possessing a mind full of light and receptive of precious illumination, thou didst truly desire the One Who alone exists, as an understanding and wise martyr, O passion-bearer; and having obtained Him through faith thou hast obtained.

*Troparion:*
With divine sweat thou didst truly darken the carnal mind, and with the blood of suffering thou didst dry up the turbid streams of polytheism, O God-wise and most rich martyr.

*Troparion:*
Through thy divine teachings Thou didst lead a company of sufferers unto the Creator, casting down all the wickedness of the persecutors by the grace of the Holy Spirit, with whom pray Thou that we may be saved.

*Theotokion:*
A youthful Son didst thou bring forth, Who existed before the ages with the Father, Who renewed the laws of nature, O pure one, immaculate Virgin Mother, by thy supernatural, honorable, and divine childbirth.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
O Thou Who alone knowest the weakness of human nature, and didst mercifully take form therein: gird me with power from on high, that I may cry aloud unto Thee, O Holy One: Living temple of Thine ineffable glory, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
Leading an honorable host established by the divine armor of faith, O invincible martyr, ye cast down all the battle arrays of the adversary and the wiles of the torturers by the power of the Spirit.

*Troparion:*
Having established the ascents of thy heart upon the noetic Rock, O much-suffering martyr of pious mind, thou wast not turned aside by the wiles of the deceitful serpent, but by deed didst become an establishment of piety unto all.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst endure the grievous piercing of thy members while bound and stretched upon the tree, O martyr; but through the divine power of God, O glorious one, thou wast straightway shown forth unharmed and whole, putting to shame the wiles of the enemy.

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast shown to be the noetic sanctuary of Him Who sanctifies all things, and a pure dwelling, O all-immaculate one; for from thee God appeared incarnate, known unto the world as twofold in nature in one hypostasis, O Bride of God.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast raised up upon the Cross" (Вознесы́йсѧ на крⷭ҇тъ):*
In the dye of thy blood thou didst steep the garment of suffering, and didst clothe thyself as with a precious purple robe, O Sebastian; therefore thou didst also enter with Christ into the supreme, endless Kingdom together with those who suffered with thee, and received crowns, O wise one; with whom keeping festival, ever remember us.

*Glory, and both now, Theotokion:*
He Who He Who sits upon the throne of the Cherubim and abides in the bosom of the Father: as upon His holy throne, O Sovereign Lady, He sits within thy bosom; for God truly incarnate reigned over all the nations, and with understanding do we now chant unto Him; Whom beseech thou to save thy servants.

*Stavrotheotokion:*
She that in the latter days bore Thee in the flesh Who wast begotten of the unoriginate Father, beholding Thee hanging upon the Cross, O Christ, cried aloud: "Woe is me, O most beloved Jesus! How art Thou, Who art glorified as God by the angels, now of Thine own will crucified by lawless men, O Son? I hymn Thy longsuffering!"

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Habakkuk with foresighted eyes having perceived thee as the mountain overshadowed by the grace of God, foretold that from thee should come forth the Holy One of Israel, unto our salvation and restoration.

*Troparion:*
The Lord grants thee power, O Tiburtius, to overcome the enemy through bodily weakness; for when the fire was kindled, thou didst youthfully and most valiantly step into it, O martyr, and didst receive heavenly dew.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst join the ministers on high, O Tiburtius, as an obedient servant of Christ, and didst offer up pure sacrifices in deeds, O sacred celebrant, glory and boast of martyrs; therefore with gladness do we honor thee.

*Troparion:*
Suspended upright, scraped with sharp irons, and compassed about by the violent rush of wounds, and buried in a pit, and receiving therein a divine end, the valiantly-minded Castulus[^176] rejoiced.

*Troparion:*
Performing healings in the holy work, O blessed one, unto the illumination of the people that look piously upon them, thou, O Sebastian, didst magnificently proclaim salvation, and in a martyr's manner didst finish thy course.

*Theotokion:*
The transcendent God chose thee alone out of all generations, and having shared our substance for our sake, He became man, the Creator of human nature, O all-immaculate Sovereign Lady, Mother of God.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
O Christ Who didst enlighten the ends of the world with the radiance of Thy coming and illuminated them with Thy Cross: enlighten the hearts of those who orthodoxly sing praises unto Thee with the light of Thy divine knowledge.

*Troparion:*
Thy paths and courses leading unto the Lord alone avoided the trackless ways of the enemies, and became a straight and steadfast path unto many, O all-honored martyr of Christ. Marcellinus and the most wise Mark speak eloquently before the tribunal of Christ's saving coming; and having been bound together, their feet are pierced through with spikes, and in a martyr's manner are they adorned.[^177]

*Troparion:*
Powerfully portraying the suffering of Him Who put our passions to death, Marcellinus and Mark were pierced with a lance, and crowned with wreaths, were joined unto the choirs of the sufferers.

*Theotokion:*
O all-immaculate one, most radiant cloud of the Sun: drive away the clouds of my soul by thy prayers, and enlighten my mind which is darkened through negligence, that I may hymn thee, O all-praised one.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
The uttermost abyss has compassed us about, and there is none to deliver; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter; save Thy people, O our God, for Thou art the strength of the ailing and their restoration.

*Troparion:*
By steadfastness of mind, O most honorable one, thou wast shown to be invincible when they beat thee unsparingly with cudgels and shot at thee with many arrows; therefore rejoicing didst thou pass over unto the never-waning Light, O martyr.

*Troparion:*
Christ quickened thee when thou didst struggle and war against demons, and shared in grievous wounds, O invincible martyr Sebastian, gazing unto Him with the eyes of the heart.

*Troparion:*
By the firm ramparts of thy most wise words thou didst shatter delusion, and didst pull down the shrines of the enemies; and having destroyed the temples of the idols, thou didst raise up thyself as a temple of the Divine Spirit.

*Theotokion:*
Thou hast renewed our nature which wasted away from transgression, having given birth unto Him Who renews all things by His divine will, O only blessed and grace-filled among women.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
We the faithful perceive thee, O Birthgiver of God, as a noetic furnace; for even as the Supremely Exalted One saved the three children, so the God of our fathers, supremely praised, renewed the world wholly within thy womb.

*Troparion:*
Strengthened by Thy mighty power, O Christ, Thy passion-bearers overcame the enemy; they trampled delusion underfoot, delivering their bodies unto wounds, singing: Praised and supremely glorified is the God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
The God-beholding passion-bearing martyrs having fought the good fight—Marcellinus, and Mark, and Tiburtius, and all-wise Castulus all-wise, passed over unto heaven, chanting unto the praised and supremely glorified God.

*Troparion:*
Youthfully, O sufferer Tiburtius, like the children didst thou noetically tread upon the flame, receiving the dew of the Spirit from above, and singing fervently: Praised and supremely glorified is the God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Suspended like a glorious ewe-lamb, thou didst choke the enemy by the sinews of thy patient sufferings, O all-praised one; and after death thou livest, O martyr Zoe, chanting: Praised and supremely glorified is the God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
A golden jar, an all-holy table of the divine Bread of life do we call thee, O pure one; a place of sanctification, a throne most high, whereon God rested: the praised and supremely glorified God of our fathers.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
In the furnace the children of Israel, as in a crucible, shone more purely than gold with the beauty of piety, saying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; hymn and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Desiring to die unto the world and unto all that are in the world, thou wast vouchsafed true life, O all-honored one, crying aloud most fervently: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; hymn and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
The lawless ones cruelly cast thee into a deep pit, throwing earth upon thee and putting thee to death as thou didst warmly sing, O ever-memorable Castulus: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; hymn and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst attain the blessed life, even as thou wast namesake thereof;[^178] for by violent suffocation thou didst depart from corruptible life, singing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; hymn and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast adorned in giving birth unto God, fair and good, Who illuminates the human race with divine beauties, O pure one; unto Whom we cry aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; hymn and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
The burning bush showed forth unconsumed the type of thy pure childbirth; and now we pray thee to quench the furnace of tribulations raging against us, that we may unceasingly magnify thee, O Birthgiver of God.

*Troparion:*
That thou mightest be vouchsafed divine radiance and eternal glory and beauty, O all-blessed Sebastian: torments, afflictions, and death and didst manfully endure death; therefore we all magnify thee.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst appear as a sun in the midst of the stars of those suffering with thee, O martyr; and now by your sacred sufferings and precious radiances ye illuminate the divine establishment of the Church, and destroy all the scheming of the devil.

*Troparion:*
Loving Christ, Tiburtius, Marcellinus, Mark, Zoe, and Castulus suffered with Sebastian, their guide and God-wise leader; and they receive equal crowns of victory, ever praying for us.

*Troparion:*
Settled in the dwellings full of light, the divine choir of martyrs was taken up, and traverses heaven rejoicing, ever beseeching the Lover of mankind for all of us who ever bless them.

*Theotokion:*
The noetic hosts are struck with awe, visibly beholding the Divine Radiance ineffably held in thy arms and possessing thy likeness, that He might deify earthly beings, O Virgin all-immaculate Mother.

*Note: Saturday before the Nativity of Christ:*
*At the Liturgy, the Prokeimenon, Alleluia, and Communion Hymn of the day. And if a celebrated saint should occur, we also sing the other Prokeimenon. Likewise read two Epistles: first for the Saturday before the Nativity of Christ, and the one in course under the same pericope, and thereafter of the saint, if there is one. Likewise also two Gospels. Epistle to the Galatians, Pericope 202 [Gal. 3:8–12]. Gospel according to Luke, Pericope 75 [Luke 14:1–11]. Communion Hymn: "Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous;" [Ps. 32:1] then of the saint.*

*Sunday before the Nativity of Christ, of the Holy Fathers:*
*It should be known: If it falls outside the 20th of December of this month, that is to say, on the 18th or on the 19th day:[^179] The Sunday service and that of the Holy Fathers is sung thus: On Saturday evening at Small Vespers, the Sunday stichera and of the Birthgiver of God, according to custom. At Great Vespers, at "Lord, I have cried," Sunday stichera, 3; and Anatolian stichera, 3; and of the Holy Fathers, 4, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having laid all aside" (Всѐ ѿло́жше); Glory of the Fathers, Tone 6: "Daniel, a man of desires" (Данїи́лъ мꙋ́жъ жела́нїй); Both now, the first Theotokion of the Tone. And three readings: 1st, of Genesis: "When Abram heard;" [Gen. 14:14–20] 2nd, of Deuteronomy: "Moses said unto the sons of Israel;" [Deut. 1:8–17] 3rd, of Deuteronomy: "Moses said unto the sons of Israel: Behold, the heaven of the Lord thy God;" [Deut. 10:14–21] At the Litya, the sticheron of the temple; and of the Fathers, Tone 1: "Radiant with beams" (Лꙋча́ми ѡ҆блиста́вшеся); Glory, Tone 3: "The assembly of the Forefathers" (Пра́ѻ҆тєцъ собо́ръ); Both now, Theotokion:* without seed of the Divine Spirit:

*(On the 18th day)*

*At the Aposticha, Sunday stichera in alphabetical order. Glory of the saints, Tone 2: "Rejoice, ye venerable prophets" (Ра́дꙋйтеся проро́цы честні́и); Both now: "O new wonder!" (Чу́десе нова́гѡ!). At the blessing of the loaves, the troparion: "O Birthgiver of God and Virgin," twice; and of the Fathers, Tone 2: "Great are the achievements of faith," once. And: "Blessed be the name of the Lord," thrice. Psalm 33: "I will bless the Lord," unto: "shall not be deprived of any good thing." And a reading in the Commentary on the Apostolic Epistles. At Matins, at "God is the Lord," the Sunday troparion twice; Glory, of the Fathers: "Great are the achievements of faith;" Both now, Theotokion: "All beyond comprehension." After the Kathismata, the Sunday Sessional Hymns with their Theotokia. And a reading in the Commentary Gospel for the Sunday before the Nativity of Christ, according to Matthew: "The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ;" Polyeleos, and the troparia: "The angelic choir." Litany; and the Sessional Hymn of the Fathers, Tone 8: "Of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob;" Glory, Both now, Theotokion: "A song of thanksgiving;" and we read the Sunday Gospel in course. Gradual, and the Prokeimenon of the Tone. "Let every breath." The Sunday Gospel. And "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ." After Psalm 50, the Sunday sticheron.*

*The Sunday Canon with the Heirmos to 4; and the Cross-Resurrection to 2; and of the Birthgiver of God to 2; and of the Fathers to 6, Tone 6. Katavasia: "Christ is born." After Ode 3, the Hypakoe, Tone 8; and a reading. After Ode 6, the Kontakion, Tone 6: "The handwritten image." After Ode 9, the Sunday Exapostilarion; Glory, of the Fathers; Both now, Theotokion.*

*At the Praises, the Sunday stichera, 3; and Anatolian, 1; and of the Fathers, to 4, Tone 5, Podoben: "Rejoice" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ); with their refrains: 1st: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers;" 2nd: "For Thou art righteous." Glory of the Fathers, Tone 8: "The concord of lawful teachings" (Зако́нныхъ ꙋ҆че́нїй согла́сїе); Both now: "Thou art supremely blessed;" The Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, the Sunday troparion; litanies, and the dismissal. But the Gospel Sticheron we sing in the narthex. And the First Hour, and the final dismissal. At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Tone to 6; and of the Fathers, Ode 3, to 4. After the Entrance, the Sunday troparion, and of the Fathers; Glory, Both now, Kontakion of the Fathers. Prokeimenon, Tone 4, Song of the Fathers: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers." Epistle to the Hebrews, Pericope 328 [Heb. 11:9–10, 17–23, 32–40];[^180] Gospel according to Matthew, the first pericope [Matt. 1:1–25]; and the one in course is omitted. Communion Hymn: "Praise the Lord from the heavens;" another: "Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous."*

*Sunday before the Nativity of Christ, of the Holy Fathers:*
*At Small Vespers, the Sunday stichera, and of the Birthgiver of God, according to custom. At Great Vespers, after the Introductory Psalm, we sing "Blessed is the man," the entire kathisma. At "Lord, I have cried," Sunday stichera, 3; and Anatolian, 3; and of the Fathers, 4.*
*If it falls within the 20th of the month:[^181] we sing the stichera: Sunday, 3; and Anatolian, 1; and of the Forefeast, three; and of the Holy Fathers, three.*
*Stichera of the Forefeast, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having laid all aside" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*

The unwaning Sun goes forth to shine from the virginal loins, to enlighten all that is beneath the sun. With pure eyes and pure deeds let us hasten to meet Him, and let us prepare ourselves in spirit now to receive Him Who comes unto His own by a strange birth, even as He was well pleased, that as the Compassionate One He might lead us back who were alienated from the life of Eden: He is born in Bethlehem.

Borne upon the cherubic shoulders, God the Word, having united Himself with the flesh according to hypostasis, dwelt in the all-immaculate womb, and became man; and He comes upon earth to be born of the tribe of Judah. O holy cave, adorn thyself well for the King of all, as a most magnificent palace! And ye, O manger, as a fiery throne! In which the Virgin Mother lays the Infant, for the renewal of creation, the Uncircumscribed One.

In a manger of dumb beasts the Virgin lays Thee, O beginnerless Word of God, Who didst receive a beginning beyond comprehension; for Thou comest to loose my irrationality which I incurred through the envy of the serpent. And to be wrapped in swaddling bands, that Thou mightest shatter the bonds and fetters of my transgressions, O only Good and Lover of mankind! Therefore do I glorify Thee, and sing, and joyfully bow down before Thy coming in the flesh, whereby I was set free.

*Stichera of the Holy Fathers, to the same melody:*

The memory of the Forefathers, which extends unto the ends of all the world, is truly full of light and shines with the rays of grace; for Christ, the bright Sun, having shone from on high from afar, leads the choir of stars that shone forth with Him; and the divine-human Birth is shown to take place within Bethlehem. Therefore in faith do we piously applaud and dance, offering praise unto the Forefeast.

Adam, rejoicing today, is adorned with the glory of divine communion, as the foundation and confirmation of the wise Forefathers; and Abel leaps for joy, and Enoch is glad, and Seth dances, and Noah together with them; and Abraham, the all-lauded, sings with the patriarchs; and Melchizedek now beholds from on high the birth without father. Therefore, we also, celebrating the divine memory of the Forefathers of Christ, pray that our souls may be saved.

The choir of God-wise children in the furnace shone brightly, and proclaims the Birth of Christ upon earth; for even as the Lord, descending as precious dew, saves the woman who gave Him birth unconsumed, preserves her immaculate, and enriches her with divine gifts. Therefore the God-pleasing Daniel also rejoices and is glad, for having clearly foreseen the Stone cut from the mountain without hands, he now with boldness prays for our souls.

*Glory of the Fathers, Tone 6:*
Daniel, a man of desires, having seen Thee, O Lord, as a Stone cut out without hands, foretold Thee as an Infant born without seed, the Word incarnate of the Virgin, the immutable God and Savior of our souls.

*Both now, of the Forefeast, the same Tone, by Byzantios (Бѷза́нтїево):[^182]*
O cave, adorn thyself well; for the Ewe-lamb comes, bearing Christ in her womb. And O manger, receive Him Who by a word has loosed us earthborn from irrational deed. Ye shepherds, piping, bear witness to the fearful miracle; and ye Magi from Persia, bring gold, frankincense, and myrrh unto the King; for the Lord has appeared from the Virgin Mother. Before Whom the Mother also bowed down as a servant, and addressed Him held in her arms: How wast Thou sown in me? Or how didst Thou sprout forth within me, O my Deliverer and God?

*If outside the 20th of the month, Both now, Theotokion of the current Tone.*
*Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day. Three Readings.*
*A Reading from Genesis [Chapter 14:14–20]:*
When Abram heard that his brother's son Lot was taken captive, he numbered his own household servants, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued them even unto Dan. And he fell upon them by night, he and his servants with him, and smote them, and pursued them unto Hobah, which is on the left of Damascus. And he brought back every horse of Sodom, and brought back Lot his brother's son, and all his goods, and the women, and the people. And the king of Sodom went out to meet him, after he returned from the slaughter of Chedorlaomer and of the kings that were with him, to the valley of Shaveh; this was the king's vale. And Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth loaves and wine; and he was the priest of the Most High God. And he blessed Abram, and said: Blessed be Abram of the Most High God, Who created heaven and earth; and blessed be the Most High God, Who delivered thine enemies into thy hands.

*A Reading from Deuteronomy [Chapter 1:8–17]:*
In those days, Moses said unto the sons of Israel: Behold, I have delivered the land before your face; go in and inherit it, which the Lord swore unto your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give unto them and to their seed after them. And I spoke unto you at that time, saying: I am not able to bear you alone. The Lord your God has multiplied you, and behold, ye are this day as the stars of heaven for multitude. May the Lord God of our fathers add unto you a thousandfold as many more as ye are, and bless you, even as He has spoken unto you! And I took from among you wise men, and understanding, and prudent, and set them to rule over you, rulers of thousands, and rulers of hundreds, and rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens, and officers unto your judges. And I charged your judges at that time, saying: Hear the causes between your brethren, and judge righteously between a man and his brother, and between his stranger. Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; thou shalt hear the small as well as the great, and thou shalt not be afraid of the face of man, for the judgment is God's.

*A Reading from Deuteronomy [Chapter 10:14–21]:*
In those days, Moses said unto the sons of Israel: Behold, the heaven and the heaven of heavens belong to the Lord thy God, the earth and all that is therein. Yet the Lord preferred your fathers, to love them, and He chose their seed after them, you above all nations, as at this day. Circumcise therefore the hardness of your heart, and stiffen your neck no more. For the Lord your God, He is the God of gods and Lord of lords, a great God, mighty, and terrible, Who regards not persons, nor takes a bribe. He executes judgment for the stranger, the orphan, and the widow, and loves the stranger, to give him food and raiment. Love ye therefore the stranger, for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God, and Him alone shalt thou serve, and unto Him shalt thou cleave, and swear by His name. He is thy boast, and He is thy God, Who has done for thee these great and glorious things, which thine eyes have seen.

*At the Litya, the sticheron of the temple.*
*And of the Fathers, Tone 1:*
Illumined with the rays of God-inspired speech, the renowned prophets are ever called blessed; and bearing the fruit of the utterances of the Spirit, they proclaimed unto all the ineffable Birth of Christ our God; and having lived a most marvelous life, they received a lawful end.

*Glory, Tone 3, by Germanus (Ге́рманово):[^183]*
Come, ye that love the feasts, let us psalmody-wise praise the assembly of the Forefathers: Adam the forefather, Enoch, Noah, Melchizedek, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; under the Law, Moses, and Aaron, and Joshua, Samuel, and David; with them Elijah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, and Daniel, and the Twelve; together with them Elisha, and all: Zechariah, and the Baptist, and those who proclaimed Christ, the Life and Resurrection of our race.

*Both now, of the Forefeast, the same Tone:*
Adorn thyself, O Bethlehem, for Eden is opened; make ready, O Ephrathah, for Adam is renewed, and Eve with him; for the curse is loosed, salvation has blossomed for the world, and the souls of the righteous are adorned: bearing gifts as a dowry, offering hymnody instead of myrrh, receiving spiritual salvation and incorruption. For behold, He lies in a manger, and commands us to complete spiritual singing, who unceasingly cry aloud: O Lord, glory to Thee!

*If outside the 20th of December, Both now, Theotokion: "Without seed of the Divine Spirit."*
*At the Aposticha, the Sunday sticheron, and in alphabetical order. But if on the 24th day, of the Forefeast, samopodoben, Tone 2:*
O House of Ephrathah, holy city, glory of prophets: adorn the house in which the Divine One is born.
*Verse: God shall come from Theman, and the Holy One from a mountain shadowed and densely wooded [Hab. 3:3].*
*Idiomelon:*
O Bethlehem, land of Judah, prepare the divine cave for Him Who has a bright dwelling according to the flesh, in which God is born in the flesh of the Holy Virgin who knew not wedlock, that He might save our race.
*Verse: O Lord, I have heard Thy report, and was afraid; O Lord, I considered Thy works* Thy works, and was astonished.

Come, all ye faithful, let us keep the Forefeast of the Nativity of Christ, and offer noetic hymnody as a star: let us cry aloud with the shepherds the doxology of the Magi: Salvation has come unto men from the virginal loins, summoning the faithful.

*Glory, the same Tone. Idiomelon, by Cyprian (Кѵпрїа́ново):[^184]*
Rejoice, ye venerable prophets, who having well ordered the Law of the Lord, and by faith were shown to be invincible and immovable pillars; for ye also appeared as mediators of the New Covenant of Christ. And having passed over unto heaven, pray Him to bring peace unto the world, and to save our souls.

*Both now, of the Forefeast, the same Tone, by Cyprian (Кѵпрїа́ново):*
Behold, the time of our salvation is drawn near: make ready, O cave, the Virgin draws near to give birth. O Bethlehem, land of Judah, be glad and rejoice, for our Lord has shone forth from thee! Give ear, ye mountains and hills, and the surrounding regions of Judea, for Christ comes to save man whom He fashioned, as the Lover of mankind!

*If outside the 20th, Both now, Theotokion: "O new wonder!"*
*At the blessing of the loaves, the troparion: "O Birthgiver of God and Virgin, rejoice," twice; and the troparion of the Fathers, Tone 2: "Great are the achievements of faith," once. In the fountain of flame, as upon the water of rest, the holy three children rejoiced; and the prophet Daniel appeared as a shepherd unto the lions as unto sheep. By their prayers, O Christ God, save our souls!*
*And if it falls on the 24th day: At the blessing of the loaves, troparia: of the Fathers, "Great are the achievements of faith," twice; and of the Forefeast: "Once were inscribed," once. And a reading.*
*At Matins, at "God is the Lord," the Sunday troparion, twice; Glory, of the Fathers; Both now, Theotokion, or of the Forefeast; and the customary Kathismata; and the Sunday Sessional Hymns, and their Theotokia; and a reading in the Commentary Gospel. But if on the 24th day, we sing the following Sessional Hymns:*
*After the 1st Stychology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph marveled" (Оу҆диви́ся І҆ѡ́сифъ):*
Concerning the Fathers, O God, Thou didst mysteriously proclaim beforehand the divine manifestation that was mystically to take place on earth of Thine eternal Son from the Virgin, in Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, Judah and the rest, Jesse, and David, and all the prophets, by the Spirit foretelling Christ Who appeared in Bethlehem Who appeared, delivering all that are in the world.

*Glory, Both now, the same.*
*After the 2nd Stychology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
Let us the faithful celebrate the feast of the divine Fathers with joy, honoring Adam, Abel, blessing Seth, Enos, Enoch, Noah; let us sing praises unto Shem and Japheth. Let us praise Abraham who shone forth through faith before the Law, and divine Isaac, Jacob, and Judah, Levi, and chaste Joseph, and faithfully cry aloud: O God-bearing Forefathers, pray unto Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who celebrate your holy memory with love!

*Glory, Both now, the same.*
*After the Blameless, their troparia; and the Sessional Hymn of the Fathers, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
Let us all praise in hymns Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, meek David, Joshua, and the twelve patriarchs, together with the three youths who quenched the flaming fire by the power of the Spirit, crying aloud unto them: Rejoice, ye who valiantly rebuked the delusion of the foolish king! And pray unto Christ to grant remission of offenses unto those who celebrate your holy memory with love!

*Glory, Both now, another, the same melody:*
Thou didst descend from the Father's bosom, and by an ineffable emptying didst take upon Thyself our poverty beyond nature, O Lover of mankind! Thou wast pleased, O Lord, to dwell in a cave, and art nourished at the breast as an infant, the Creator and Lord! Therefore the Magi, guided by a star, bring gifts unto Thee as unto the Master of creation; shepherds and angels were astonished, crying aloud: Glory to God in the highest, Who comes upon earth to be born as a man!

*And if outside the Forefeast, say this Theotokion:*
A dutiful praise of thanksgiving, even as that widow her two mites, do I offer unto thee, O Birthgiver of God, for all thy gifts; for thou wast shown to be both a protection and help, ever delivering me from temptations and tribulations. Therefore, as delivered from the midst of the burning furnace of those that afflict me, from my heart do I cry aloud unto thee: O Birthgiver of God, help me, praying unto Christ God to grant me remission of transgressions, for I thy servant have thee as my hope!

*Gradual, and the Prokeimenon of the Tone.*

*Two Canons, of the Fathers to 8; the Heirmoi twice, troparia to 6; wherein two Sunday troparia precede. Therefore, if on the 24th day, it is not sung in the Octoechos, and of the Forefeast to 6.*
*The Sunday Canon, Tone 6. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Unto Him Who of old hid the pursuer and tyrant with the wave of the sea, the children of the saved hid beneath the earth; but let us, as maidens, sing unto the Lord, for He is gloriously glorified.

The gates of death are opened unto Thee with fear, and the eternal bars are shattered; for by Thy precious descent the ancient dead arose, singing with gladness: O Christ, Thy Resurrection!

He Who is the Judge stands willing before Pilate's tribunal, unto unlawful judgment as one condemned; and God, before Whom earthly and heavenly beings tremble, is struck in the face by an unjust hand.

*Canon of the Fathers. If the Sunday of the Holy Fathers falls outside the 20th, the Canon of the Octoechos is Sunday with the Heirmos to 4; and Cross-Resurrection to 2; and of the Birthgiver of God, 2; and of the Fathers is read from here to 6. Likewise also in the other odes of the Fathers.*
Today the assembly of the divine Fathers keeps the Forefeast of the Nativity of Christ brightly, and this the most glorious grace delineates beforehand; for Abraham is an image of the Law, and the children also.

Of old, sacred Abraham received the one Tri-hypostatic Godhead; and now the Father's co-enthroned Word, gloriously praised, comes unto the children by the Divine Spirit.

Having cast down godlessness by the number and faith of the Holy Trinity, the children in the furnace clearly showed forth the hidden mysteries of God unto the world by sensible types.

Abraham was delivered from the hand of the unrighteous, and of old the divine children from the furnace flame; and the prophet Daniel was saved from the beasts and the pit. Therefore do we now keep the Forefeast of Christ's Nativity.

*Theotokion:*
O Mother who knewest not wedlock, Virgin incorrupt, graced of God, we bless thee; for from the race of Abraham and the tribe of David didst thou blossom forth; and thou gavest birth unto Christ Who was foretold of old by the prophets.

*Canon of the Forefeast. (If outside the 20th of the month, it is omitted.) Tone 1. Ode 1. Heirmos: "Christ is born"* Christ is born, give ye glory! Christ comes from heaven, meet ye Him! Christ is on earth, be ye exalted! Sing unto the Lord, all the earth, and praise Him with gladness, O ye people, for He is glorified!

Christ Who was an infant in the flesh, Christ Who became poor willingly, Christ Who became visible, the Virgin comes now to give birth in Bethlehem: let heaven and earth rejoice!

Ye mountains and hills, leap for joy; ye God-proclaiming prophets, dance; ye people and nations, applaud: the salvation and illumination of all is at hand, being born in the city of Bethlehem!

*Theotokion:*
The Rich One becomes poor, enriching those who were impoverished by malice; God is known as man from the Virgin who knew not wedlock, without change: let us all praise Him in hymns, for He is glorified!

*Katavasia: "Christ is born..."*
*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Beholding Thee hanging upon the Skull, Who suspended the whole earth without support upon the waters, creation was shaken with great awe, crying aloud: None is holy save Thee, O Lord!

Having remained three days in the tomb, Thou didst raise up the dead of ages by Thy life-giving rising; and loosed from condemnation, they rejoiced with gladness, crying aloud: Behold, Thou art come, our Deliverance, O Lord!

Glory to Thy rising, O our Savior, for as the Almighty Thou didst deliver us from the corruption and death of hades; and singing praises, we say: None is holy save Thee, O Lord, Lover of mankind!

*Of the Fathers:*
Faithfully preserving the glory according to the image and according to the likeness of God, the children quenched the flame of the golden image with spiritual fire in a martyr's manner, singing: We know the one Lord!

Girded with wisdom and the power of the Spirit, the children, captive in Babylon, put the wise men to shame, and boldly cried aloud: None is holy save Thee, O Lord, Lover of mankind!

The Law rejoices and dances with the children and prophets, and plays before the divine coming of the Lord today; and Abraham is glad, that from his seed he saw the Lord taking flesh.

*Theotokion:*
Conception without passion, reception beyond words was the manner of thy childbearing, O Birthgiver of God; for the mystery beyond nature, proclaimed by the prophets, was revealed unto us as God the Word God the Word, the Son of God.

*Another. Heirmos:*
Unto the Son begotten of the Father without corruption before the ages, and in the latter days incarnate without seed of the Virgin, let us cry aloud unto Christ God: Thou Who hast lifted up our horn, holy art Thou, O Lord!

He Who before the ages was begotten of the Father beyond understanding, in the end took flesh from the Virgin as He Himself knows, desiring to renew mankind, which had decayed through the counsel of the deceitful serpent.

He Who sits on high with the Father and the Spirit, seeing human nature humbled, the beginnerless Son of God receives a beginning, and wills to be born in the flesh as man.

*Theotokion:*
Holier than the angels and all creation, she now bears in the flesh without seed the Angel of Great Counsel,[^185] for the restoration of all who unceasingly sing unto Him: Holy art Thou, O Lord!

*Katavasia: "Before the ages..."*
*Hypakoe, Tone 8:*
An angel bedewed the furnace of the children; and now he loosed the weeping of the women, saying: Why do ye bring myrrh? Whom seek ye in the tomb? Christ God is risen, for He is the life and salvation of the human race.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Foreseeing Thy divine emptying upon the Cross, Habakkuk cried aloud in terror: Thou didst cut off the power of the mighty, O Good One, joining Thyself unto those in hades, as the Almighty!

Thy divine descent into hades, O Christ God, appeared as life unto the dead; for Thou, O Good One, didst bind below the dominion of the enemy, and opened a path to heaven unto men.

The all-pure body of the Deliverer lying in the tomb decayed not; but as the Mighty One, He broke the bars of hades, and arose in glory on the third day, O Christ!

*Of the Fathers:*
Let us honor the beginning of the Fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: for from their seed shone forth Christ, incarnate of the Virgin as the Almighty!

Daniel, delineating the future coming of Christ beforehand, clearly showed the beasts to all as sheep; for as a prophet of God he foresaw what was to come.

Unenticed by the poison of sin, ye children were delivered from the flame; for being wiser and purer than gold, ye were not consumed in the furnace of delusion.

*Theotokion:*
The Expectation of the nations and the salvation of the world is loudly proclaimed the salvation of the world, thy childbearing beyond nature, O all-pure, honored one, which the memory of the Fathers sings today.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*
A rod from the root of Jesse, and a flower from it, O Christ, Thou hast budded forth from the Virgin; from the praised mountain, the overshadowing forest, Thou art come, incarnate of her that knew not man, O immaterial God: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

As a rod from the root of Jesse, O Virgin, thou hast budded forth, having blossomed with the unfading flower, the Creator of all, Who adorns the whole earth with flowers as God, while it cries aloud unto Him: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

Stripped by the deceitful eating, and having slipped in understanding, and become like the irrational beasts, O Word of God, Thou art come to rebuild me, having become an Infant, and laid in the manger of irrational beasts: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Theotokion:*
From the overshadowing mountain, the Virgin, Habakkuk foresaw Thee incarnate, O Jesus, crushing the evil mountains and hills, and delivering unto destruction the pride of the crafty one and the haughtiness of the demons.

*Katavasia: "A rod from the root..."*

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Foreseeing Thy theophany, O Christ, which mercifully came to pass toward us, Isaiah, having beheld the unwaning light, rising early out of the night, cried aloud: The dead shall rise, and they that are in the graves shall arise, and all earthborn shall rejoice!

Shining brilliantly, visibly depicting joy, the angel appears in the tomb radiant with light, proclaiming the resurrection to the women; and leaving behind their weeping, they rejoiced, Christ being risen, from Whom also they received unending joy.

Out of compassion, O Good One, having taken our form upon Thyself, Thou wast nailed to the Cross of Thine own will for my sake, who had previously cast off Thy holy commandment for the sake of food in paradise; and Thou diest in Thy love for mankind, granting me life.

*Of the Fathers:*
Let us today honor the firstfruits of the Fathers, as leader and chief of the Law and of grace, the divine Daniel from the lineage of Abraham: for as a prophet of God he foretold Christ from the Virgin, and goes before to meet His divine birth.

Having clearly prefigured the coming of the Lord unto us, by the descent of the angel the Abrahamic children quenched the furnace; and having made the fire dew-bearing, therein by faith they destroyed the glory of the golden image the glory of the golden image.

Daniel shut the mouths of the beasts in the den by the Spirit; and the Abrahamic children quenched the power of the fire by grace; and being saved from corruption, they foretold Christ born of the Virgin, entreating Him as the Deliverer of our salvation.

*Theotokion:*
Revealed by the Divine Spirit, Isaiah cried aloud of Thine impassible assumption of our nature, O Lord, keeping vigil by the law of grace: From the lineage of Abraham, and from the tribe of Judah according to the flesh, the Virgin comes bringing forth without seed.

*Another. Heirmos:*
Being the God of peace and Father of compassions, Thou hast sent us the Angel of Thy Great Counsel, Who grants peace; therefore, guided to the light of the knowledge of God, rising early out of the night, we hymn Thee, O Lover of mankind!

Master by nature, fully among servants, the all-perfect Son of God, having willed out of compassion to be called also Son of Man, O all-bountiful One; therefore having voluntarily become impoverished in a cave, Thou art coming to be born, O all-blessed One.

Incomprehensible by nature, O Christ the King, how shall a small cave receive Thee? How shall a manger be able to contain Thee, Who for our sake comest in the flesh from a Mother that knew not wedlock into Thine own? That Thou mayest save those who have become estranged, O Lord!

*Theotokion:*
The ewe-lamb is come to give birth to the Shepherd: make ready, O holy cave! Make haste, ye shepherds, to behold the Shepherd and Lamb that is born! Ye Magi, prepare with gifts to worship Him as King in the flesh!

*Katavasia: "Being the God of peace..."*

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Beholding the sea of life surging with the tempest of temptations, fleeing to Thy calm haven, I cry unto Thee: Lead up my life from corruption, O Greatly-merciful One!

Thou hast wrought the slaying of death and the destruction of hades, O Good One, by Thy three-day burial; and having risen in God-befitting manner, Thou hast poured forth life unto those in the world, O good Jesus. *Twice.*

*Of the Fathers:*
Hospitable was the character and exalted the faith of Abraham the forefather; therefore receiving the divine mystery prefigured, he rejoiced; and running before Christ, he now is glad.

Faith now subdued creation unto the children by the gift of the Creator; for the all-devouring and shameless fire was put to shame before those who honor Christ the Maker of fire The savagery of the world forgot to rage together, yielding to profound peace in God-befitting manner at the coming of Christ; even as Daniel the prophet once stopped the mouths of the lions in the pit.

*Theotokion:*
From virginal loins thou hast given birth to Christ, O Mary, unwedded Mother, Whom the prophets beholding in the Spirit, the Fathers now dance beforehand for His nativity.

*Another. Heirmos:*
The sea beast vomited forth Jonah from its belly like a newborn babe, even as it received him; and the Word having dwelt in the Virgin and taken flesh, came forth preserving her incorrupt; for suffering no corruption Himself, He kept her that bore Him unharmed.

Being a new heaven, O Sovereign Lady, from thy womb as from a cloud, thou art coming to bring forth in the flesh in a cave Christ the Sun of glory: Who wills by His beams brightly to illumine all the fullness of the earth, out of boundless compassion.

Thou didst behold our affliction and distress, O bountiful Christ, and didst not despise us; but Thou didst empty Thyself, without departing from the Father. And Thou didst take up Thine abode in the womb that knew not wedlock, which goes forth without sorrow to bring Thee forth in the flesh in a cave.

*Theotokion:*
Ye mountains and hills, valleys and glens, peoples and tribes, nations and every breath, shout aloud, being filled with divine gladness: the Deliverance of all is come and draws near, the Word of God without beginning, Who under time is come to be out of compassion.

*Katavasia: "The sea beast vomited forth Jonah..."*

*If outside December 20, Kontakion of the Fathers, Tone 6:*[^186]
Having not worshipped the image made by hands, but defended by the uncircumscribed Essence, O thrice-blessed ones, ye were glorified in the ordeal of fire; and standing in the midst of the unbearable flame, ye called upon God: Make haste, O Bountiful One, and hasten as the Merciful to our help, for Thou art able, if Thou willest!

*Ikos:*
Stretch forth Thy hand, of which of old the warring Egyptians and the combating Hebrews received trial. Leave us not, lest death that thirsts for us and Satan that hates us swallow us up. But draw near unto us, and spare our souls, even as Thou once didst spare Thy children in Babylon, who unceasingly glorified Thee, and who were cast for Thy sake into the furnace, and from it cried aloud unto Thee: Make haste, O Bountiful One, and hasten as the Merciful to our help, for Thou art able, if Thou willest!

...Make haste, O Bountiful One, and hasten as the Merciful to our help, for Thou art able, if Thou willest!

*If inside the Forefeast, Kontakion, Tone 4, Podoben: "The angelic choir" (Ли́къ а҆́гглскїй):*
Be glad, O Bethlehem! Ephrathah, prepare thyself! For behold, the ewe-lamb, carrying the Great Shepherd in her womb, hastens to bring Him forth. Beholding Whom, the God-bearing Fathers rejoice, singing with the shepherds of the Virgin nursing.

*Ikos:*
Beholding the radiance of thy childbearing shining forth, O Virgin, Abraham the friend of God, Isaac ever-memorable, Jacob, and the whole God-assembled choir of the saints rejoice; and creation was led to meet thee with joyful utterances. For thou hast appeared as the Mediatress of joy unto all, having conceived in thy womb Him Who of old was seen in Babylon, Who preserved unburnt the children unjustly cast into the furnace, and Who revealed thee beyond all understanding. Therefore they hymn Him Who is beheld in the arms of the Heifer, singing of the Virgin nursing.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
An ineffable wonder! He Who delivered the venerable children from the flame in the furnace is laid in the tomb a breathless corpse, for the salvation of us who sing: Blessed art Thou, O God our Deliverer!

O strange wonder! The Lord Who sits upon the throne in the highest, the same endured death through the assumption of flesh; but He arose by the might of His Godhead, raising with Himself the dead of ages.

Thou didst shatter the power of death and arise, giving resurrection unto those who truly glorify Thee as Lord, and cry unto Thee with Orthodox faith: Blessed art Thou, O God our Deliverer!

*Of the Fathers:*
Having brought forth Christ in the flesh, by faith, O forefather Father Abraham, thou wast shown to be the father of many nations in the Spirit, for the salvation of us who sing: Blessed art Thou, O God our Deliverer!

The song of the separate ones put to shame the lifeless sound shouting in vain; for the children, trampling unharmed the furnace burning with fire with their bodies, sing to the Deliverer: Blessed art Thou, O God!

Having looked with spiritual vision of old, Daniel the prophet revealed Christ's Second Coming, and foretells the fearful things therein, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God our Deliverer!

*Theotokion:*
A strange wonder, recounted among the prophets, and unto the Fathers revealed of old, the pure Virgin comes willing to give birth, for the salvation of us who sing: Blessed art Thou, O God our Deliverer!

*Another. Heirmos:*
The children brought up together in piety, disdaining the ungodly command, feared not the threat of fire, but standing in the midst of the flame, they sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our Fathers!

The divine vine, having ripened the incorrupt cluster, draws near to bring forth Him Who distills the wine of gladness and gives drink unto us who cry unto Him: Blessed art Thou, O God of our Fathers!

The divine alabaster box bearing within the fragrant myrrh comes to pour it out in the cave of Bethlehem, filling with mystical fragrance those who sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our Fathers!

*Theotokion:*
The Tongs which Isaiah the prophet foresaw of old comes bearing in her womb Christ the Divine Coal,[^187] Who burns up all sinful matter and enlightens the souls of the faithful.

*Katavasia: "The children brought up together in piety..."*

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Be astonished and tremble, O heaven, and let the foundations of the earth be shaken! For behold, He that dwells in the highest is numbered among the dead, and is sheltered as a stranger in a small tomb! Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

O Thine ineffable condescension for the sake of us humble ones, O Christ! For behold, having tasted death, being immortal God, Thou wast laid in the tomb as man; but Thou didst arise, O Word, raising Adam with Thyself, who supremely exalts Thee unto all ages!

Every ear was astonished, that the Most High willingly came upon the earth to destroy the power of hades by the Cross and burial, and raised all with Himself to cry aloud: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Of the Fathers:*
Abraham prefigured Thy slaying, O Christ; the son whom he begot, obedient unto Thee, O Master, he went up upon the mountain willing by faith to sacrifice as a ram; but he returned rejoicing with him, glorifying and supremely exalting Thee, the Deliverer of the world.

Clothed with an untiring flame as with a divine garment, O Christ, the fire of Thy holy children quenched exceedingly and dew sounded forth unto those who sang through Thy descent: Ye priests, hymn, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

Daniel the prophet was given to the lions for food by an unjust judgment; but he held restraint over them by Thy command, fasting piously with the beasts in the depth of the pit. By his prayers, and of Abraham and the children, save in peace, O Christ, those who sing of Thee!

*Theotokion:*
Whom the prophetic voices faithfully foretold, Jesus Emmanuel, coming in human form: the Son and co-beginnerless Word of God the Father, the Virgin Mary bears without knowing man from the Holy Spirit, in the city of Bethlehem.

*Another. Heirmos:*
The dew-bearing furnace prefigured the image of a wonder surpassing nature; for it burnt not the youths whom it received, even as the fire of the Godhead burnt not the Virgin's womb into which It entered; therefore in hymns let us sing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

Glory to God in the highest, let us cry aloud with the angels in gladness: the Savior is born, the Master comes! Whom the star shows forth, and the Magi hasten to behold Him in the manger: Let all creation bless the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

Thou wast enrolled with servants of Thine own will, O Master, obeying Caesar's decree; that Thou, O God, mightest free mankind from the bondage of the crafty one, O Greatly-merciful One; therefore rejoicing, we hymn: Let all creation bless the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
As a newborn Infant I carry Thee, O Word without beginning, yet experience of man I have not known at all, the Virgin said in wonder. Whom upon earth shall I call Thy father? I know not. Therefore with all I sing to Thee: Let all creation bless the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Katavasia: "The dew-bearing furnace prefigured the image..."*

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Lament Me not, O Mother, beholding in the tomb the Son Whom thou didst conceive in thy womb without seed; for I shall arise and be glorified, and as God I shall endlessly exalt in glory those who magnify thee with faith and love.

Why dost thou weep, O creation, beholding upon the Cross and in the tomb the Giver of life as an earthly mortal? For He Who brightly renews thee shall arise, casting down hades by His three-day resurrection, and raising the dead with Himself unto those who hymn Him.

Though Thou didst descend into the tomb as a corpse, O Giver of life, yet Thou didst destroy the power of hades, O Christ, raising with Thyself the dead whom it had previously swallowed; and Thou didst grant resurrection as God unto those who magnify Thee with faith and love.

*Of the Fathers:*
Celebrating the feast of the Fathers who were before the Law, let us honor Christ from them in God-befitting manner; for Abraham, together with Isaac and Jacob, were shown as the foundation of the prophets and the Law, and preachers of grace by faith in the Spirit.

God, Who by fire in the bush showed the mystery surpassing understanding unto Moses the beholder of God, the very same, having descended into the fire unto the children, by the uncreated fire of His Godhead made the flame of the furnace into dew.

Coming together with Abraham, the most holy children, and Daniel the marvelous prophet of God, Isaac and Jacob, with Moses and Aaron, faithfully dance before the nativity of Christ, praying unceasingly that we may be saved.

*Theotokion:*
All creation rejoices at thy childbearing, O Virgin; for Bethlehem opened Eden unto us; and behold, all enjoying the Tree of Life, faithfully cry aloud with fervor: Fulfill our prayers, O Sovereign Lady!

*Another. Heirmos:*
A strange and most glorious mystery do I behold: the cave is heaven, the Virgin the cherubic throne, the manger the place wherein the uncontainable Christ God lay: Whom hymning, we magnify.

Strange, fearful, and most glorious mysteries! The Lord of glory came upon the earth, and being impoverished, entered a cave in the flesh: seeking to recall Adam, and to deliver Eve from sorrows.

By Thy swaddling clothes Thou loosest the bonds of transgressions; and by Thine abundant poverty Thou enrichest all, O Bountiful One; laid in the manger of irrational beasts, Thou alterest men from irrational malice, O Word of God, pre-beginnerless!

*Theotokion:*
The prophetic preachings have received their fulfillment; for He Whom they said would come at the end of the ages is come, and appeared taking flesh from the pure Virgin: let us receive Him with pure praise.

*Katavasia: "A strange and most glorious mystery..."*

The chosen of the patriarchs and the fathers before the Law by faith shone forth beforehand, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, as luminaries; for all the prophets and righteous ones shone forth from them as radiant torches, and enlightened all creation with the rays of honored prophecy; and they entreat God fervently for the world.

*Both now:*
The undefiled ewe-lamb, who in the latter times brought forth the Lamb, the Word pre-beginnerless: marvelous was this, the granddaughter of Adam and daughter of David worthily, whose ineffable childbearing the multitude of the Fathers worthily celebrate in advance.

From the seed of Abraham and of the divine David the Ancestor of God, the pre-beginnerless Word is brought in, Who of old miraculously saved the youths equal in number to the Trinity from the flame by the descent of the angel, and turned the weeping of the women into joy.

Whose divine nativity Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, all the patriarchs and prophets brightly celebrate in advance, and men with the angels.

*At the Praises, Sunday stichera, 4; and of the Fathers, 4. Stichera of the Fathers: Tone 5, Podoben: "Rejoice, [thou fair dwelling-place] of the ascetics" (Ра́дꙋйся по́стникѡвъ):*
Lift up thy voice truly, O Zion, divine city, and proclaim the divine memory of the Fathers, honoring with Abraham Isaac and ever-glorious Jacob; for behold, with Judah and Levi we magnify Moses the great and Aaron the marvelous; and with David we all honor Jesus [son of Nun] and Samuel: clapping hands in divine songs for the divine praise of the Forefeast of Christ, wherein we ask to obtain grace from Him, and that great mercy be granted to the world. *Twice.*

*Verse: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers, and praised and glorified is Thy name unto all ages.*

*Verse: For Thou art righteous in all that Thou hast done for us.*
She that from the ages was proclaimed on earth by the prophets in their utterances, the Virgin Birthgiver of God, is revealed; whom the wise patriarchs and the assemblies of the righteous proclaim; with whom the beauty of the women dances in company: Sarah, Rebecca, Rachel, and Anna, and the glorious Miriam of Moses together; with them the ends of the world rejoice; all creation pays honor, for the Creator of all and God comes to be born in the flesh, and to grant us great mercy.

The concord of the teachings of the Law:

A great voice is fulfilled: for behold, the Virgin carries the Uncontainable One circumscribed in the flesh in her womb, and comes most gloriously to bring Him forth. O cave acceptable to God, adorn thyself! Bethlehem, make ready! For the King willed thee as His dwelling. The radiant and animate cloud, carrying the heavenly rain, now goes forth to pour it out upon the earth, that It may water the face of the earth; the spring of grace, the spiritual swallow, holding Him within her womb, by the ineffable Word gives birth, destroying the winter of godlessness: the pure and undefiled palace brings the incarnate King into the cave!

Therefore, as a mediatorship unto the change from corruption, they proclaimed beforehand unto the souls held fast in hades, by reason of the resurrection: Lord, glory to Thee!

*In the Same Month, on the 19th Day: The Holy Martyr Boniface. Alleluia, or Troparion:*
*At "Lord, I have cried," stichera of the Martyr, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*
Thou didst desire the good calling appointed for martyrs, O much-suffering passion-bearer, and didst endure afflictions with a courageous mind, awaiting departure unto painless rest, and seeking to receive heavenly honors, O all-blessed one, and the paradise dwelling, the unwaning light, and life eternal.

Tearing by iron claws, cruel piercings, the boiling of lead, the severing of thy head, and the most ferocious pains didst thou endure, and wast joined rejoicing unto the choir of passion-bearers, O much-suffering one; therefore we celebrate thy yearly festival, O sufferer Boniface, companion of the angels!

Having sent thee forth as a servant, Aglaida received thee as a divine master, O Boniface,[^190] who didst master the passions, rule over the tormentors, cast down the foes, and wast arrayed with the crown of victory; therefore having built a holy and magnificent temple to thee, wherein she sacredly laid thee, she praises thee.

*Other Stichera to the Most Holy Theotokos, Tone and Podoben the same (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*
Rain down upon me, O Theotokos, the abyss of thy mercy, and my heart, scorched by the heat of passions, as the Mother of God water it, O Maiden; and make me unceasingly pour forth drops of compunction, I pray, whereby I may be accounted worthy, O pure one, of the consolation that they shall receive who weep sincerely.

Shaken by demonic assaults and cast into the pit of destruction, take pity [on my soul], O Theotokos, and establish me upon the rock of virtues; and having destroyed the counsels of the enemies, make me worthy to do the commandments of Thy Son and our God, that I may obtain remission in the day of judgment.

I have fallen among foul, murderous thieves, O all-undefiled one, and of the incorruptible garment of upper brightness have I been stripped by their incursions, O Maiden, and by them was pitilessly wounded, and was cast down into a place of affliction, scarcely alive; but do thou anticipate and stretch forth thy hand, and raise me up, I pray.

*Glory, both now, Tone and Podoben the same (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*
Upon the bed of despondency I lie, O all-undefiled one, and slothfully do I pass my life, and I am terrified at the end of my time, O Theotokos, lest like a lion the all-evil serpent mercilessly tear apart my humble soul. Therefore, through thy goodness anticipating before the end, raise me up unto repentance.

*Stavrotheotokion, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́бля):*
Seeing Christ, the Lover of mankind, being crucified, and His ribs pierced with a spear, the all-pure one weeping cried out: What have the ungrateful people rendered unto Thee for the good things Thou didst do for them? And dost Thou hasten to make me childless, O most beloved One? I marvel, O Tender-hearted One, at Thy voluntary crucifixion!

*At Matins, both canons of the Octoechos, and of the Saint to 4, whose acrostic is: "Faithfully I sing to thee, O most radiant martyr." A composition of Joseph. Tone 4.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
The mighty captains, O Thou Who wast born of the Virgin, in the abyss of dispassion drown the three parts of my soul, I pray, that unto Thee, as upon a timbrel, in the mortification of the body, I may chant a song of victory.

*Troparion:*
With fervent mind, having emulated the struggles of the noble sufferers, thou didst suffer stoutly, and didst put to death the serpent by thy life-bearing sufferings, O sufferer Boniface, companion of the holy angels.

*Troparion:*
Having seen the deceit of the enemy cruelly poured out upon the earth, O valiant sufferer, thy soul inflamed with most divine desire, thou didst enter into the arena with painless mind, O most blessed one.

*Troparion:*
Illumined with divine wisdom, O blessed one, thou didst make foolish the unwise enemies, proclaiming Christ, Who was likened to the grossness of the flesh, wherein He willed to appear, O Boniface, much-suffering martyr.

*Theotokion:*
The mountain of God which Daniel foresaw, the spiritual tabernacle, Mary the pure, the sanctuary of glory, the table that contained the divine Bread, let us all the faithful with one accord hymn.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
As the barren church of the Gentiles hath brought forth, and the assembly abundant in children hath grown weak, unto our marvelous God let us cry aloud: Holy art Thou, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
As thou didst desire the higher freedom, O glorious one, being delivered from the yoke of servitude, having emulated the honored passions of Him Who out of tender mercy became a servant...

*Troparion:*
Having been an initiate of carnal thoughts, by a divine change thou didst suddenly endure with joy every assault of cruel torments, O martyr Boniface.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst deny thyself, and didst go forth unto long struggles and contests, strengthened by the weapon of the Cross, and having become a victor, thou wast glorified, O martyr Boniface.

*Theotokion:*
The most radiant God, emptying Himself, not emptying the paternal bosom, was in thy womb, and became thy Son, O all-undefiled one, saving mankind.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up" (Вознесы́йся):*
Sent unto the assembly of the martyrs, thou becamest a true martyr, having suffered for Christ most stoutly, O all-praised one; and as a burden [of holy relics], O blessed one, thou wast given back unto her who in faith glorified thee, O blessed Boniface;[^191] but diligently pray that all may receive the complete forgiveness of transgressions.

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*
Being a lover of sin, I pray thee who didst bear the sinless God Who takes away the sins of the world, O all-pure one, to have compassion on my most sinful soul and to cleanse my many sins; for unto sinners thou art the cleansing, and salvation unto the faithful, and protection.

*Stavrotheotokion:*
She that bare Thee in the flesh in the last times, Who wast begotten of the unoriginate Father, seeing Thee hanging upon the Cross, O Christ, cried out: Woe is me, O most beloved Jesus! How is it that Thou, Who art glorified as God by the angels, art now voluntarily crucified by lawless men, O Son? I hymn Thee, O Long-suffering One!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
For love of Thine image, O Compassionate One, Thou didst stand upon Thy Cross, and the nations melted away; for Thou, O Lover of mankind, art my strength and praise.

*Troparion:*
Blessing the endurance of those who suffer, by the likeness of the honored sufferings, O martyr, thou didst assimilate thyself unto them, O God-wise and most rich one.

*Troparion:*
Going in faith unto the divine company of the martyrs, O blessed one, thou didst give back the bodily, right marvelous burden unto her that desired it, O God-wise one.

*Troparion:*
Purified like gold, O martyr, in the furnace of wounds, thou didst appear most pure, bearing the representation of the Creator's passions.

*Theotokion:*
Knowing thy virginity sealed after childbirth, O Maiden, thou didst faithfully magnify the Word ineffably born from thy womb.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Send down Thy light upon us, O Lord, and loose us from the gloom of transgressions, O Good One, granting Thy peace.

*Troparion:*
As a light-bearing star thou didst rise from the west, and didst set patiently through sufferings, O martyr; and straightway thou didst shine forth unto the west, illumining the ends of the earth.

*Troparion:*
Martyrlike didst thou struggle, pierced with sharp reeds during the tearing by claws, O martyr, and the stings of the evil one didst thou faithfully blunt by grace.

*Troparion:*
The enemy's wiles against thee grew weak, O God-wise one; for with steadfast gazing unto God, thou didst endure bodily wounds as one incorporeal.

*Theotokion:*
Wash my soul clean from every defilement, O Virgin, I cry unto thee; and save me, O pure one, who didst give flesh upon earth to the true God the Savior.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Prefiguring the three-day burial, the Prophet Jonah cried out, praying in the sea-monster: From corruption deliver me, O Jesus, King of hosts!

*Troparion:*
Beaten with bodily wounds, thou didst wound the godless who were incurably ailing with ignorance the descent of the Spirit that made wise the disciples of the Lord hath fulfilled thy God-proclaimed words.[^192]

*Theotokion:*
Delivered, O all-pure one, from the dark depths of hades by thy divine childbirth, we call thee blessed.

*Another Canon [of the Martyr]. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Christ is my power, God and Lord: the venerable Church chants in godliness, crying out from a pure mind, feasting in the Lord.

*Troparion:*
Adorned with holy wounds, thou didst appear most beauteous, O right marvelous one, and wast seen beloved by God Who crowned thy head.

*Troparion:*
Stretched out upon the tree, O glorious one, and scraped upon the earth, thou didst endure cruel tortures. Therefore rejoicing thou didst inherit the painless life.

*Troparion:*
Lawfully seeing thee suffering, O blessed one, the divine martyrs strengthened thee with words of endurance; with whom having completed long struggles, thou wast blessed.

*Troparion:*
With praises we crown the divine martyrs, whom divine grace hath crowned with divine chaplets, who cast down the lofty conceits of the enemy.

*Theotokion:*
[O Virgin,] deliver me from the vile passions and passionate thoughts that alienate me from God, the Only Pure One, that in faith I may call thee blessed.

*Ode 5 [of the Prophet]. Heirmos:*
The night is past, the day is at hand, and the light hath shone forth unto the world. Therefore the angelic ranks praise Thee, and all things glorify Thee.

*Troparion:*
The divine Joel clearly foretold unto all the coming of Christ, that He will come and save the human race from the delusion of idols.

*Troparion:*
Thou entirely didst mount, O glorious prophet, unto the transcendent light beyond all thought, and from thence didst draw forth the grace of prophecy, and didst proclaim righteousness.

*Troparion:*
Pray that those who hymn thee be saved from all affliction, O most rich Joel, and entreat that they may be accounted worthy of divine grace and radiance.

*Theotokion:*
O most holy Virgin, Mother of God of the world, pray that those who confess thee as Birthgiver of God be saved from countless sins and worldly tribulations.

*Another Canon [of the Martyr]. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
With Thy divine light, O Good One, illumine, I pray, with love the souls of those who dawn early unto Thee, that they may know Thee, the Word of God, as the true God, crying out from the darkness of sin.

*Troparion:*
Strengthened by divine nods and with steadfast mind, O Varus, thou didst tear the heart of the proud one that wrought evil.

*Troparion:*
The glorious martyr, seeing his own flesh falling away to the earth, rejoiced, with the brightness of his mind foreseeing eternal life and divine rewards.

*Troparion:*
"I hymn Thee, O Lord God, and glorify and worship Thee, having been accounted worthy of the good things prepared for those that love Thee!" the martyr fervently cried out in his suffering.

*Theotokion:*
Thou hast appeared truly holier than the cherubim and seraphim, O all-undefiled one; sanctify all who now faithfully glorify thee, and save them by thine intercession.

*Ode 6 [of the Prophet]. Heirmos:*
A great abyss of sin surrounds me, and imitating the prophet, I cry unto Thee: From corruption raise me up, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
The springs of thy words drip, welling forth God-proclaimed and soul-nourishing sweetness, O glorious one, watering those who faithfully approach. *Twice.*

*Troparion:*
We know thee, O God-proclaiming prophet, as a mountain of prophecy welling forth sweetness, and as a preacher of godliness, O all-wise Joel.

*Theotokion:*
O thou that didst give birth to the unsetting Light, illumine the hearts of those who faithfully glorify thee, O all-pure and compassionate one, and Him Who was ineffably born of thee.

*Another Canon [of the Martyr]. Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Seeing the sea of life surging with the tempest of temptations, fleeing unto Thy calm harbor, I cry unto Thee: Raise up my life from corruption, O Greatly Merciful One!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst disregard the words of the most lawless foe, and didst patiently endure the flame of intolerable tortures, O much-suffering Varus, intercessor for those who praise thee in faith.

*Troparion:*
The most senseless tormentor ceased not mercilessly crushing thee with wounds, until into the hands of God thou didst surrender thy holy soul, radiant with the beauties of thy struggles.

*Troparion:*
Thou wast lifted up in likeness upon the tree unto Christ, and hanging thereon, thou didst yield thy soul unto God, Who crowns thee, O passion-bearer, who didst lawfully struggle with valor.

*Theotokion:*
Direct, O Theotokos, my humble soul, ever storm-tossed in the deep of cruel things, and guide it unto a calm harbor, as with undoubting mind I call thee blessed.

*Kontakion of the Martyr, Tone 4:*
Following Christ, O martyr Varus, and having drunk of His cup, thou wast bound with the crown of martyrdom, and dancest with the angels; pray unceasingly for our souls.

*Ode 7 [of the Prophet]. Heirmos:*
Thou Who of old didst extinguish the all-burning furnace, and didst bedew the children with spiritual dew: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
The fountain proceeding from the house of the Lord and watering [the valley], even as thou didst foretell, came forth, O right honorable prophet.[^193]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst make the fountain a torrent of delight, wheat-bearing and nourishing, even as Joel foretold: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
He that made all things, being born of the Virgin, saved the world that piously sings: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Another Canon [of the Martyr]. Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The angel made the furnace bedewing for the venerable children, but the command of God burning the Chaldeans persuaded the tormentor to cry out: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Forefiguring thee radiant through the addition of thy struggles, Cleopatra,[^194] O Varus, bathed thee; having found glory through thee, a worthy reward of faith, which she showed warmly at thy death.

*Troparion:*
Pouring tears upon thee and anointing thee with honorable myrrh, the all-honored woman hid thee beneath the earth, who didst bury the evil delusion and dost illumine us from the tomb with splendors.

*Troparion:*
The ever-memorable woman ceased not, O venerable one, pleasing thee, the favorite of Christ, until thou didst appear as an intercessor for her, O wise one, of the heavenly kingdom; which she was accounted worthy of through thee, together with her most beloved son.

*Theotokion:*
Crushed by countless transgressions, O Virgin, renew me by thine intercession, healing my soul, and granting me the word to cry aloud: Blessed is she that bare God in the flesh!

*Ode 8 [of the Prophet]. Heirmos:*
Him Who of old bedewed the Hebrew children in the flame, and wonderfully burned the Chaldeans in it, let us hymn as Lord, saying: Bless and exalt Him supreme unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Thou hast shown me, O glorious one, images of repentance of the compassionate Lord Who accepts in faith those who approach Him in faith and sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Having become a minister of the Lord, O prophet Joel, thou wast entrusted to prophesy His mysteries unto the people who praise and sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
The Jordan rivers of wonders well forth remission, which are the most glorious apostles of the Lord, even as Joel prophesied, watering those who cry aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Theotokion:*
A composite Hypostasis in two essences, Christ, O all-undefiled one, hast thou brought forth, remaining a pure Virgin; unto Whom singing we cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Another Canon [of the Martyr]. Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Out of the flame Thou didst pour dew for the venerable ones, and didst burn the sacrifice of the righteous one with water; for Thou, O Christ, doest all things merely by willing: Thee do we exalt supreme unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Having given ear unto a mother's prayers, O martyr, thou didst gloriously enlist a noble youth into a certain army,[^195] and didst show him to be an inseparable companion of thy glorious praise, by thine ineffable tender mercy.

*Troparion:*
Having grown rich, Cleopatra brought thee as a precious treasure of Egypt, O martyr, with costly gifts, healing all Palestine which loves and honors thee.

*Troparion:*
Thou hast completed all thy struggles, O valiant soldier of the Almighty; and as a victor wast crowned by Him, O all-blessed Varus, great glory of martyrs!

*Theotokion:*
I add sins unto sins, and fear not the coming fearful judgment; take pity, O pure one, on the blindness of my soul, and having turned me by thy prayer, save me!

*Ode 9 [of the Prophet]. Heirmos:*
O blessed in the heavens and glorified upon the earth: Rejoice, O Bride unwedded!

*Troparion:*
With the prophets as a prophet, thou now dost joyfully rejoice in the heavenly mansions.

*Troparion:*
From on high thou dost now watch over us who devoutly glorify thee, O God-proclaiming and most rich one.

*Troparion:*
Having shortened the path of salvation, Joel showed it God-wisely through repentance.

*Theotokion:*
Thou hast raised us up who were fallen, O Mother of God, having given birth to the compassionate God and Savior.

*Another Canon [of the Martyr]. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
It is not possible for men to see God, upon Whom the ranks of angels dare not gaze; but through thee, O all-pure one, the Word made flesh appeared unto men; Whom magnifying, with the heavenly hosts we call thee blessed.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst overthrow the strength of the warrior-enemy, having girded thyself with divine power, O valiant sufferer Varus. Therefore we praise thee, as we the faithful draw abundant healing from thy relics.

*Troparion:*
Like light, like the dawn, like a great sun hath thy memory spread abroad unto the ends of the earth, illumining all with the light-bearing splendors of thy venerable struggles, O all-praised one, and driving away the gloom of hearts.

*Troparion:*
Seeing her son shining with thee in great glory, the child-loving mother magnified the God of all, and more sincerely glorified thee, O martyr, as the greatest protector, having been richly rewarded in her dwelling.

*Troparion:*
The earth wherein thy most patient body lies, O wise one, is divinely sanctified; but grant us by thy prayers remission of sins, amendment of life, O Varus, and deliverance from all unknown perils.

*Theotokion:*
The Lord appeared from thee, O Virgin, as a light cloud, and delivered over the idols of Egypt by His divine flesh; and He accounted the multitude of passion-bearers worthy to bear this, through this imitator's venerable sufferings.

*In the Same Month, on the 20th Day: The Holy Great-Martyr Artemius.*[^196]
*At "Lord, I have cried," stichera, to 6, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́бля):*
Giving over thy much-suffering and most patient body to be punished with manifold tortures of cruel wounds, O God-wise Artemius, Thou didst not deny Christ, nor didst Thou sacrifice to the idols; but Thou didst endure as though another were suffering, awaiting future recompense and immortal glory.

Hung up, scraped, crushed with stones, pierced through on every side with iron, and severed by the sword, thou didst remain unshaken having established the steps of thy soul upon the spiritual Rock, O glorious one. For the sake of this victory, thou wast joined unto the angels and martyrs, filled with the ineffable light.

Thy relics ever well forth the grace of healings unto those who love thee, O glorious Artemius, drowning passions and diseases, and driving away hosts of evil demons; and they water the hearts of the faithful, causing the divine fruits of virtues and the knowledge of piety to blossom forth.

*Glory, Tone 2, by Studites:*
Let us honor Artemius, the spiritual light of the faith, for he denounced the abominable emperor, and with the blood of his martyrdom God purpled the Church. Therefore he received unstinting grace of healings, to heal the infirmities of those who faithfully approach the shrine of his relics.

*Both now, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*
When the undefiled Ewe saw her Lamb voluntarily led to the slaughter as a man, weeping she said: Dost Thou now hasten to make me childless, O Christ, who bare Thee? What is this that Thou hast done, O Deliverer of all? Yet do I hymn and glorify Thy supreme goodness beyond mind and word, O Lover of mankind!
