*At the Aposticha, of the Octoechos.*
*Glory, Tone 6:*
Having lawfully suffered for Christ, O Artemius, and having overthrown the spiritual enemy together with the earthly emperor, thou didst worthily receive from the Savior, the Master of the contest, the crown; and now in the heavens thou dost rejoice with the angelic ranks, clearly enjoying the celestial illumination, and richly partaking of the tri-hypostatic and primal Light. Therefore we also, the faithful people and choir of martyrs, cry unto thee in hymns: Rejoice, O adamant unconquerable in soul, and stout armor-bearer of Christ! Rejoice, destroyer of the delusion of idols, and radiant champion of truth! But pray to the Lord, that we also, through a life beloved of God, may obtain with thee a place before the throne of His majesty!

*Both now, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 6, Podoben: "On the third day" (Трїдне́венъ):*
Seeing Thee crucified, O Christ, she that bare Thee cried out: What is this strange mystery that I see, O my Son? How is it that Thou, the Giver of life, diest hanging in the flesh upon the tree?

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
Thy martyr O Lord, Artemius, in his suffering received an incorruptible crown from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength, he cast down the tormentors, and crushed the powerless insolence of the demons. By his prayers save our souls!

*Glory, both now, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion.*
*At Matins, both canons of the Octoechos, without martyr troparia; and the canon of the Saint, to 6, whose acrostic is: "Grant me Thy rich grace, O blessed one. Joseph." Tone 2.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
In the deep of old, the all-powerful force overwhelmed the whole army of Pharaoh; and the incarnate Word destroyed all-wicked sin, the most glorified Lord, for gloriously is He glorified.

*Troparion:*
Having struggled with the good fight, O martyr, and having received radiant crowns, thou standest illumined before the Light by immaterial participation; therefore we pray thee: Illumine us by thy prayers!

*Troparion:*
Thy radiant festival, O martyr, hath summoned all today joyfully to the banquet, setting forth the burning of thy sufferings, thy courage and resistance, wherewith being filled, we call thee blessed in faith and love.

*Troparion:*
Bowled down, having understood the incomprehensible Lord Who was put to death upon the Cross in the flesh, the Author of life, thou didst love the voluntary deadness of suffering; therefore thou didst obtain immortal glory.

*Theotokion:*
The bodiless Word was divinely enfleshed of thee, O all-pure one, through an abundance of love for mankind, and drew near unto passions, and the most glorified Lord welled forth dispassion unto men, for gloriously is He glorified.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
The desert blossomed like a lily, O Lord, the barren church of the Gentiles, at Thy coming, wherein my heart hath been established.

*Troparion:*
Desiring to be adorned with martyr crowns, O glorious one, thou didst bear wounds and the tearings of bitter tortures, through divine grace.

*Troparion:*
The most cruel assault of torments shook not the pillar of thy heart, O all-wise one, for it was established upon the immovable spiritual Rock.

*Troparion:*
Hung upon the tree, and surrounded on every side with the tearings of parts [of thy flesh] -ful renewal in the Spirit.[^197]

*Troparion:*
Gazing upon Christ Who humbles Himself, let us be raised up from base passions; and with good zeal having learned not to mind high things in faith, let us humble ourselves in the Virgin, that we may exalt Him Who is born by lofty-working deeds.

*Another Canon. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
*He Whom God cannot contain:*

*Troparion:*
Unto those of godly wisdom, Christ commands to watch, who hope for His coming from the Virgin; for behold, He comes to be born.

*Troparion:*
At Thy second coming, O Christ, number me as a dweller among the sheep at Thy right hand, who honor Thy coming in the flesh.

*Heirmos:*
O Theotokos and Virgin, who containedst in thy womb God Whom nothing can contain, and didst bear Joy unto the world: we hymn thee.

*And a metania.*

*At Matins, at "God is the Lord", the Troparion of the Forefeast twice; Glory, of the Saint; Both now, of the Forefeast.*

*After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 1, Podoben: "Thy tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й сп҃се):*
Rejoice, O Bethlehem! Ephratha, make ready! For behold, the Ewe-lamb, carrying the great Shepherd in her womb, hastens to give birth; and seeing beforehand the divine star, the Magi rejoice, singing with the shepherds in uprightness of heart.

*Glory, both now, Tone and Podoben the same (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*
He Who bowed the heavens and dwelt in the Virgin comes forth in the flesh to be born in the cave of Bethlehem, as it was written; and He is seen as a babe, Who gives life to babes in the womb. Rejoicing at this, let us all now go to meet Him in uprightness of heart.

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*
O virgins, lead the maidenly rejoicing! O mothers, praise the approach of the Mother of Christ our God! Magi with the angels, shepherds with us: for the Virgin comes into the city of Bethlehem to give birth to the Son of the pre-eternal God, Who saves the world from corruption.

*Glory, both now, Tone the same:*
Rejoice, O Zion! Bethlehem, adorn thyself! The Sustainer of all, having sent forth a star beforehand, has announced His immeasurable condescension; Whom the heavenly powers tremble before, truly born of the Virgin without change, the only Lover of mankind.

*After the Kathismata, we read the Martyrdom of the holy Ignatius in two sections; and the Homily of Chrysostom on the Blessed Philogonius, in two sections.*[^198]

...in two sections. Psalm 50.

*Be it known that from this day forward, we do not say (*"Господеви поем"*) in the Odes, until the feast of the Holy Theophanies is given back.*[^199]

*Two canons: of the Forefeast with the heirmos to 8, and of the Saint to 6. The Canon of the Forefeast, whose acrostic is: "We sing these songs of the forefeast." A composition of Joseph. Tone 4.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos (twice):*
Let us all chant a song of victory unto God, Who wrought marvelous wonders with a high arm, and saved Israel, for gloriously is He glorified.

*Troparion:*
Let us today begin to celebrate the forefeast of the Nativity of Christ, Who is born in the flesh of the Virgin Mother in the cave of Bethlehem, because of His great tender mercy.

*Troparion:*
Loosing me from the bonds of sins, He is wrapped in swaddling clothes and laid in a manger, seen as a babe, the pre-eternal God: glory to His dominion!

*Theotokion:*
Eden is opened unto Thee, Who art born in the flesh of the Virgin Maiden of God in the city of Bethlehem, O Master: we sing the praises of Thy fearful dispensation.

*Another Canon of the Holy Ignatius, Tone and Heirmos the same. A composition of Andrew of Crete:*
*Troparion:*
Brightly celebrating, let us make banquet! The martyr Ignatius sacredly summons the Church of Christ unto his much-hymned suffering.

*Troparion:*
Being a most radiant luminary of the Church, O Ignatius, thou dost illumine all the ends of the earth and enlighten the west, having come from the east.

*Troparion:*
Emulating the perils of Paul from place to place, O Ignatius, and being a son of the nations, thou wast not dismayed, establishing by honored writings the churches of Christ.

*Troparion:*
We all hymn thy glorious memory, O all-blessed Ignatius, and with songs we honor Him Who crowned thy most honored head, O divinely-blessed one.

*Troparion:*
"Let my flesh be scraped, let my blood be poured forth! With desire I hasten; for the beasts I am ready, prepared for grinding, for the fire, for the sword, for eating!" the martyr cried aloud.

*Theotokion:*
O Eden, adorn thyself! For Ephratha, make ready for the Creator Who wills to be born of the Virgin Mother in the cave of Bethlehem, because of His great tender mercy.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
The Stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner: this is the Stone upon which Christ established the Church, which He redeemed from the nations.

*Troparion:*
Let all creation chant a forefeast song unto Him Who before the morning star was begotten of the Father, and now has ineffably shone forth from the Virgin, and is born in the flesh in Bethlehem because of His great tender mercy.

*Troparion:*
The star has already shone forth from the tribe of Judah, which the kings having recognized, make their journey from the East, and hasten to arrive, that they may behold Christ born in the flesh in Bethlehem.

*Theotokion:*
Behold, having known the Incarnation of Christ, Isaiah clearly foretells by the Holy Spirit: A child is born the Lord from the Virgin for our regeneration, Whose rule is upon His shoulder.

*Canon of the Saint, Tone and Heirmos the same:*
*Troparion:*
Thou didst appear, O father, as an image of sacred suffering, a pillar of endurance, and a rule of courage, and a pillar of the Church, and confirmation of the faith, and an exemplar of virtue, having been crowned in Christ by honored sufferings.

*Troparion:*
Truly according to thy name wast thou called God-bearer, O father; for while yet an infant in age, carried in the arms of the Lord, thou wast set forth by Him Who cries aloud unto us: "Become ye unto Me like this little child!"[^200]

*Troparion:*
"I am the pure wheat of God," criedst thou, O father; "I hasten to be ground by wild beasts! Let my body be crushed, let my limbs be eaten, and let me be food for the beasts, that I may appear pure bread unto God!"[^201]

*Troparion:*
The strange arena of martyrdom thou didst patiently complete; marvelously beyond all who suffered before thee didst thou show forth courage, inflamed by the love of unflagging longing; for like a fire it kindled thy soul.

*Troparion:*
Burning ever in spirit, the hieromartyr called aloud with love in the midst of perils: "I pursue Christ rejoicing, I am crucified with Christ; and I live, yet no longer I, but Christ alone," says he, "lives in me!"

*Theotokion:*
Come, O Isaiah, cry aloud: Behold, the Virgin shall conceive in her womb the Redeemer of the world, and shall bear Him in the cave; and the name of Him Who is born shall be Jesus, God with us, Emmanuel Sabaoth.

*Kontakion of the Forefeast, Tone 3, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дѣ́ва дне́сь):*
Today the Virgin comes to the cave to give birth ineffably to the pre-eternal Word: dance, O inhabited earth, when thou hearest it; glorify with the angels and with the shepherds, Him Who wills to appear as a young child, the pre-eternal God.

*Ikos:*
O truly fearful wonder surpassing speech! He Who gives being unto all, for the sake of goodness entered into the womb of the holy Virgin, and comes to be born in a cave, and to be laid in a manger. And a star announces Him from on high to the Magi, who come to worship Him with gifts, drawing them from afar as they eagerly follow the prophecy of Balaam, who said: "A star shall proclaim a young Child, the pre-eternal God."[^202]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 3, Podoben: "The beauty of virginity" (Красотѣ̀ дѣ́вства):*
Ordained by Christ God, thou didst illumine thy sacred vesture, truly having received testimony, O God-bearer; for thou didst incite the beasts to separate thee from the world, emulating the marvelous Apostle Paul. Therefore also in Rome didst thou worthily finish martyrdom, O father.

*Glory, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
Shining forth from the east like a star, and illuminating with the rays of thy words, thou didst enlighten the world and drive away darkness, and like Paul thou didst valiantly finish the course, having endured perils among nations and cities; whence also, like wheat, by the teeth of beasts wast thou ground, O blessed one, an offering unto thy Lord, O God-bearer Ignatius. Pray to Christ God to grant remission of transgressions unto those who with love honor thy holy memory!

*Both now, Tone and Podoben the same (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*
The Word of God, having shone forth unsown from the Father's bosom before the ages, without seed comes forth from thy womb, O all-undefiled one, in the last times: to renew him who of old fell grievously, and raising him up to his ancient beauty, as He is merciful; before Whose Nativity the hosts of the bodiless go forth, mystically sending up songs of victory unto men, crying: "Glory to God Who has granted us peace, Who has broken down the middle wall of enmity as He willed!"

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Foreseeing in the Spirit the Incarnation of the Word, O Prophet Habakkuk, thou didst proclaim, crying aloud: "When the years draw nigh, Thou shalt be known; when the time is come, Thou shalt appear! Glory to Thy power, O Lord!"

*Troparion:*
O mountains, hills, and forest trees, rivers and seas, and every breath: leap for joy in gladness! Now salvation, Jesus, draws near to be born of the Virgin in the city of Bethlehem!

Take up the Psalter, O Prophet David, and clearly sing in the Holy Spirit: for of the Virgin is born, Who unsown before the morning star shone forth from the womb of the Father, the Lord of glory, Christ God!

*Troparion:*
How shall the cave, so tiny and exceedingly poor, receive Thee born in the flesh, O Word? How shalt Thou be wrapped in swaddling clothes, Who deckest the heavens with clouds? How in a manger of dumb beasts shalt Thou recline like a babe?

*Canon of the Saint, Tone and Heirmos the same:*
*Troparion:*
Thou didst strike the earth with awe by the radiance of thy sufferings, O holy Ignatius, having appeared as a prisoner; for traversing like the sun with the rays of martyrdom, thou didst enlighten the whole fearful west from the east.

*Troparion:*
Bound like Paul by verbal beasts, thou didst hasten to Rome, O wise Ignatius; yet even though bound, thou didst not cease establishing the churches, sending word to all the cities unto all the hierarchs of Christ to be of good courage.

*Troparion:*
"I strive to be Christ's, Christ alone do I desire; for I am wholly Christ's," criedst Thou, O sufferer; "Him do I pursue, Him do I go to attain! And for this cause, fire and sword and beasts do I endure, all things, that I may attain life!"

*Troparion:*
"Sweet to me is affliction, welcome are the bonds for the sake of the Beloved," criedst thou, O sufferer; "persecutions are sweeter to me than native lands, and my grinding more than all gladness, pains more than all bodily health!"

*Troparion:*
"Let the beasts be unto me mouths of slaying and bellies of graves," criedst thou, O sufferer; "let no one trouble me, let no one crush my strength; for I hasten to be ground like wheat, and to be found pure bread unto God!"

*Theotokion:*
Being God, Thou wast well-pleased to be born for our sake in an earthly cave, O Good One, having become poor with our poverty because of tender mercy; and having come forth incarnate from the Virgin, Thou didst abide one Son from the Father and from the Mother.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Grant us Thy peace, O Son of God, for other than Thee we know no God; we call upon Thy name, for Thou art the God of the living and of the dead.

*Troparion:*
Let the clouds rejoicing drop down sweetness; for already the Lord draws near, to be born like a babe from the pure Virgin in a humble cave.

*Troparion:*
Leap for joy now, O divine prophets of God; for Christ the Truth comes, to fulfill the proclamations of your divine tongue, being born like a babe.

*Theotokion:*
O Eden, that wast shut against me of old, be opened henceforth, seeing Christ becoming an infant in the flesh, and as He was well-pleased, in the city of Bethlehem born of the Virgin Maiden!

*Canon of the Saint, Tone and Heirmos the same:*
*Troparion:*
"Such a high priest became us," crying aloud, Paul beforehand wrote the sacred image of thy holy ways: holy, faithful, undefiled, harmless.

*Troparion:*
Bound and led away to suffer as high priest, a prisoner of Christ, O Ignatius, thou didst write unto churches and cities, establishing all in the confession.

*Troparion:*
Zealously emulating the achievements of Paul in godly manner, thou didst endure all his perils, O hieromartyr worthy of marvel, radiance of the East and evening star!

*Troparion:*
Striving with the desire of Paul, having bonds upon thy hands, thou didst traverse the world, O hieromartyr, that well-pleasing by thy sacred sufferings thou mightest appear unto all.

*Troparion:*
We sing of thy contests, we honor thy bonds with incensings and psalms; we honor the dust of thy relics, as an aromatic ointment-anointed earth, O martyr, by thy sacred sufferings!

*Theotokion:*
God, having become like men from thee, is born a babe for our sake, O Bride of God, and abides wholly unchanged, and in the flesh is seen God Who became man.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Emulating the Prophet Jonah, I cry aloud: Deliver my life from corruption, O Good One, and save me, O Savior of the world, who cry: Glory to Thee!

*Troparion:*
A heaven upon earth shows forth the heavenly King, Who for our sake is born, by a radiant star unto the astrologers now in the city of David.

*Troparion:*
The prophet clearly testifies and cries aloud: "Thou house of Ephratha, Bethlehem, wherein God shall appear from the Virgin, dance and leap for joy!"

*Troparion:*
In the cave of Bethlehem the Virgin manifestly gives birth to the Lord, the Creator of all; and having swaddled Him like a man in swaddling clothes, she now lays Him to rest in a manger.

*Canon of the Saint, Tone and Heirmos the same:*
*Troparion:*
As one who truly loved the Beloved without wavering, and having spiritually kindled the fire toward Him, O Ignatius, thou didst have living water within thee, and speaking.[^203]

*Troparion:*
Fulfilling the testimony of thy conscience, thou wast not content, looking upon the onrush of the beasts [of the beasts,] thou wast not terrified, as wheat desiring to be ground in every limb.

*Troparion:*
Thy harsh persecutions and indissoluble bonds, and then the tearings in Rome, and the fire of the persecutors, didst thou count as nothing, O hieromartyr, for the sake of thy Beloved!

*Troparion:*
Burning with the charcoal of Christ's love, O sufferer, Thou didst run to the fire of trial as unto the morning dew, to attain that Beloved Who truly is!

*Troparion:*
Even though thou didst drink the cup of Christ thirsting, yet didst thou ever remain choosing rather to suffer than to live, and criedst aloud: "None of these things are anything to me compared with attaining Him Who is life!"

*Theotokion:*
Adorn thyself, O Bethlehem! Ephratha, prepare! For without mother from the Father, and without father from a mother He is carried in the womb, and is born saving us.

*Kontakion of the Saint, Tone 3, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дѣ́ва дне́сь):*
The light-bearing day of thy radiant contests pre-proclaims unto all Him Who is born in the cave; for thirsting with love to enjoy Him, thou didst hasten to be eaten by wild beasts; therefore also wast thou called God-bearer, O all-wise Ignatius!

*Ikos:*
Abraham of old offered up his son, prefiguring the slaughter of Him Who holds all things, Who now hastens to be born in a cave. And thou, O divinely-wise one, didst offer up thine entire self as a sacrifice, and having become the food of wild beasts, thou didst appear as pure wheat unto thy Creator, truly enduring forever in the heavenly granaries and enjoying thy Beloved; for Whose sake having forsaken the whole world, thou wast called God-bearer, O all-wise Ignatius!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
Unto Thy children in the furnace, O Savior, the fire touched not neither troubled them. Then the three as with one mouth chanted and blessed, saying: "Blessed is the God of our fathers!"

*Troparion:*
Showing forth the manifestation of Christ in the flesh, Jeremiah cried aloud: "Incarnate upon earth God hath appeared, and hath found out every way of knowledge, born in Bethlehem of a Mother!"

*Troparion:*
Behold, from the root of Jesse a rod hath sprouted forth, blossoming with Christ the flower; and upon Him, now born in the cave, rests the Spirit of wisdom and counsel, and of divine knowledge.

Let us give ear unto the sacred words: The Lord is born, a Child for our sake, Whose principality is upon His shoulder, and He is called the Angel of great counsel of the Father, the Prince of peace, Christ!

*Canon of the Saint, Tone and Heirmos the same:*
*Troparion:*
Thou hadst not in thee a fire of material love, O Ignatius, but rather living and speaking water, water calling: "Come unto the Father!", water flowing from life and leading us unto life!

*Troparion:*
"Let the teeth of the beasts," says he, "be unto me a sword and weapons and slaughter; and let the dear bellies be my tomb! Let fire devour me before corruption, the remnants of skin!"

*Troparion:*
"To me sweet is death," says he; "sweet to me are all painful labors! Beasts are joyful; this fire is dew unto me, if only I lay hold of life! Therefore also I hasten to die, that I may live with Christ!"

*Troparion:*
"Living to me is not desirable in the flesh, for in the spirit do I desire to live! To me to live is Christ, divine love; unto Him do I go, Him," says he, "do I love; to attain Him do I hope!"

*Theotokion:*
He Who of old was foretold by the prophets draws near to me, a Child born of the Virgin: Adam rejoices, and the foremother Eve is loosed from birth-pangs; and David, the father of the Birth-giver, bears witness.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Him of Whom the angels and all the hosts are in awe, as Creator and Lord: praise, ye priests; glorify, ye youths; bless, ye peoples, and supreme-exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
The Lord comes by a strange Nativity manifestly unto His own; let us receive Him, that us who had become estranged from the delight of Paradise, He may again adopt unto Himself, being born in a cave!

*Troparion:*
Behold, our Calling comes; let us raise joyful songs with diligence, and let us sing forefeast hymns unto Him Who is contained in a most tiny cave!

*Troparion:*
As the Lord swore, so hath He now fulfilled, having given us from the seed of David His Mother the Virgin, of whom a Child was born in the flesh in the city of Bethlehem, surpassing speech!

*Canon of the Saint, Tone and Heirmos the same:*
*Troparion:*
Hymned be Ignatius, the divine priest, doubly crowned as martyr and shepherd; for having suffered for the love of God, desiring to be beloved, he refused not to suffer.

...[he refused not] to suffer.

*Troparion:*
In the course of faith like the sun, valiantly didst Thou traverse the earth from the ends of heaven; and setting never to set from the earth unto Christ, Thou shinest forth upon the world the light of incorruption.

*Troparion:*
Thirsting for the cup of Christ's passion, bound didst Thou run, O wise Ignatius; and having reached the arena, Thou didst not cease crying aloud: "I thirst to thirst for Christ unto the ages!"

*Troparion:*
O love and warmth of divine longing! With desire to be crucified, and that he may live unto the Beloved: he thirsts to be thirsted for, and loves to be loved, choosing to die that he may live again!

*Troparion:*
Having cast off the dust, immaterially didst thou wing thy mind unto the Truly Existing, longing for the Beloved; for He is the eternal Desire, and truly the Wisdom and Life of all things that have been made.

*Theotokion:*
A star hath shone forth, Christ from Jacob, and the Magi hasten unto the city of Bethlehem, to hymn, honor, and worship Him, Who is born from the womb of the pure Theotokos.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
The life-receiving ever-flowing fountain, the light-bearing lamp of grace, the living temple, the tabernacle all-pure, more spacious than the heavens and the earth: the Theotokos do we the faithful magnify.

*Troparion:*
With the patriarchs and all the righteous, and with the holy prophets, let us leap for joy: the Lord Jesus, redemption, enlightenment, life, and salvation, is now born of the Virgin in the city of David!

*Troparion:*
Already the portals of the divine Word's Incarnation are manifestly opened unto all! Ye heavens, rejoice; ye angels, leap for joy; and let the earth be glad with men, with the shepherds and the Magi in the Spirit!

*Troparion:*
The Virgin, a spiritual alabaster jar, carries Christ like inexhaustible myrrh, and comes to pour it out manifestly in the Spirit within the cave, that His fragrance may fill our souls!

*Canon of the Saint, Tone and Heirmos the same:*
*Troparion:*
Ignatius, looking upon lowly things and minister of heavenly mysteries, fulfilling an undefiled service and being perfected, sacredly offers himself through martyrdom, and prepares for the beasts and the fire.

*Troparion:*
Loving to put on that which is according to the image, thou didst exchange the old images; therefore, having received through newness and not oldness the primal beauty of the Archetypal form, thou art settled together with Christ!

...thy sacred vesture, O most sacred one, thou didst make even more sacred by thy sufferings. Therefore, having received a double crown, thou singest with martyrs and pastors, O hieromartyr of Christ our God!

*Troparion:*
"I am the pure wheat of God," saidst Thou, "and by the teeth of beasts am I ground, that I may be bread sacredly consecrated unto the Beloved and God, purified; for love of Whom I refuse not to die!"

*Troparion:*
Illumined by unapproachable Light, and settled in the mansions on high, O holy Ignatius: pray unceasingly unto God and thy Creator for this thy flock, we pray thee!

*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, O pure living city of God, wherein God was well-pleased to be contained! For leaving not the heights, He came down unto thee like rain upon the earth, O Birth-giver of God, and in the city of Bethlehem is born a babe!

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "In spirit in the sanctuary" (Дꙋ́хомъ во ст҃и́лищи):*
The pre-unoriginate Word, the Wisdom of God, having shared with earthly men through ineffable goodness, teaching the people of old, held thee in His arms, O God-bearer Ignatius; and living in God, thou didst pass through the martyrdom of suffering rejoicing!

*Glory, both now, of the Forefeast, Podoben: "Make ready beforehand" (Предꙋгото́висѧ):*
Adorn thyself, O Bethlehem, the new dwelling, the manger and cave! O company of shepherds, Magi from the east, anticipate entering into it by the brightness of the star; for the Virgin now bears within it as a babe Him Who is all-perfect!

*At the Praises, Stichera of the Forefeast, Tone 6, to 4, alphabetically. A composition of Romanos the Melodist. Automelon:*[^204]
Go before, ye angelic hosts! Ye in Bethlehem, make ready the manger! For the Word is born, Wisdom comes forth, the Church receives greeting unto the joy of the Theotokos! Ye peoples, let us say: Blessed art Thou Who art come, our God, glory to Thee!

*Troparion:*
Let the mountains drop down sweetness, for behold, God comes from the south: ye nations, submit! Rejoice, ye prophets; leap for joy, ye patriarchs; ye men, clap your hands! Christ, the mighty and great Prince, is born; the King of the heavens comes upon earth!

*Troparion:*
Raising up humanity from the earth, the Creator is come, renewing again the royal image. Rejoice together, ye powers of the heights, and sing: The middle wall of enmity is broken down! He is come unto Whom it pertained; for God becomes man, Christ the King of Israel Christ our God.

*Troparion:*
Come, O hard-hearted Israel, cast off the cloud that hangs over thy soul; recognize the Creator Who is born in the cave! He is the Expectation of the nations; He shall dissolve thy feasts. For thou refusest to cry aloud: Christ the King of Israel comes!

*Glory, Tone and Podoben the same (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*
Christ draws near; O Bethlehem, make ready beforehand! Already the salvation of the nations shines forth; adorn the manger; assemble the shepherds; summon the Magi from Persia! Ye hosts of the bodiless intellects, cry aloud: [unto Him Who cannot be contained by all!] And the manger prepares to receive the Eternal Life. Unto Him let us all sing, and let us cry aloud: Save our souls, O Jesus our God, Who wast incarnate for our sake!

*Both now, Tone and Podoben the same (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*
Truly envy and fire shall consume thee, O foolish deceiver, and the curse of the Law: for behold, the Virgin, as Isaiah foretold, has conceived in her womb, and shall lay the King to recline in the manger; by Whom all the mighty of the tribe of Judah shall be brought to nought.

*At the Aposticha, Stichera Idiomela, Tone 4:*
Adorn thyself, O Bethlehem! Sing praises, O city of Zion! Rejoice, O wilderness, betrothing joy beforehand! For the star goes before into Bethlehem, proclaiming Christ Who wills to be born; and the cave receives Him Whom nothing can contain. And the manger prepares to receive the Eternal Life. Unto Him let us all sing, and let us cry aloud: Save our souls, O Jesus our God, Who wast incarnate for our sake!

*Verse: God shall come from Theman, and the Holy One from a mountain shadowed and densely wooded.*[^205]
Christ our God Who comes manifestly, shall come and shall not delay; He shall appear from the unwedded Maiden, and He rests now in the cave, and in a manger of dumb beasts, Whom the heaven cannot contain; receive Him Who wills to be wrapped in swaddling clothes in thee, Who by His Word has loosed us from irrationality. The star announces Him, the Magi worship, the shepherds play their pipes, beholding the fearful wonder. And the angels sing on earth, seeing the redemption of our race.

*Verse: O Lord, I have heard Thy report, and was afraid; O Lord, I considered Thy works, and was amazed.*[^206]
Rejoice, O heaven, having received the Word of God; prophesy unto the Maiden Mary, the bush that burns and is not consumed by fire through the radiance of the Godhead. Adorn thyself, O Bethlehem; open thy gates, O Eden; and go, ye Magi, to behold Salvation wrapped in swaddling clothes in the manger; Whom the star showed above the cave, the Lord the Giver of life, Who saves our race.

*Glory, of the Saint, Tone 4. By Studites:*[^207]
A living pillar and ensouled icon, thy yearly festival is arrived, O God-bearer Ignatius, proclaiming thy mystagogy and thy valiance, even thy resistance for the faith unto blood, and that blessed and ever-memorable voice saying: "I am the wheat of God, and by the teeth of beasts am I ground." Therefore, having become an emulator of the passions of Christ thy God, pray that our souls may be saved!

*Both now, Tone 6:*
O cave, adorn thyself, for the Ewe-lamb comes carrying Christ in her womb; and ye mangers, receive Him Who by His Word has loosed us earthborn from irrational deeds! Ye shepherds, piping on your flutes, bear witness to the fearful wonder; and ye Magi from Persia, bring gold and frankincense and myrrh unto the King, for the Lord has appeared from the Virgin Mother. Before Whom also, bowing low like a handmaid, the Mother worshipped, and spoke unto Him Whom she held in her embrace: "How wast Thou sown in me? Or how didst Thou sprout forth within me, my Redeemer and my God?"

*At the Hours: Troparion of the Forefeast. Glory, of the Saint; Both now, Theotokion of the Hours. After the Our Father, the Kontakion of the Forefeast alone at all the Hours.*

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes from the Canon of the Forefeast, Ode 3 with the heirmos to 4; and of the Saint, Ode 6 to 4. Prokeimenon: The righteous man shall be glad in the Lord: Verse: Give ear, O God, unto my voice: Epistle to the Hebrews, Pericope 331 [Heb. 10:32–38]. Alleluia, Tone 4: The righteous man shall flourish like a palm tree: Verse: Planted in the house of the Lord: Gospel of Mark, Pericope 47 [Mark 10:32–45]. Communion Hymn: In everlasting remembrance shall the righteous be.*

*If the Sunday of the Holy Fathers falls in the Forefeast, within the 20th day, that is to say: on the 20th, the 21st, the 22nd, or the 23rd day:*[^208]
*The service is celebrated thus: At Small Vespers, the resurrectional Stichera and of the Theotokos, according to custom. At Great Vespers, at "Lord, I have cried", Stichera: Resurrectional 3, and Anatolian 1; and of the Forefeast 3, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having laid aside all" (Всѐ ѿло́жше); and of the Fathers 3, Tone and Podoben the same: Glory, Tone 6: Daniel, a man of desires: Both now, of the Forefeast, Tone the same: O cave, adorn thyself. Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day. And the three readings of the Fathers. At the Litiya, Stichera of the Forefeast in order, on whichever day this Sunday is chanted, from the Aposticha. And of the Fathers, Tone 1: Shining with rays: Glory, Tone 3: The assembly of the Forefathers: Both now, of the Forefeast, Tone the same: Adorn thyself, O Bethlehem. At the Aposticha, the Resurrectional Stichera: Glory, Tone 2: Rejoice, ye prophets: Both now, of the Forefeast, Tone the same: Behold, the time draws near. At the Blessing of the Loaves, Troparion: O Theotokos and Virgin, twice; and of the Fathers: Great are the achievements of faith: once. Blessed be the name of the Lord, thrice. And a reading from the commentaries on the Epistles. At Matins, at "God is the Lord", the Resurrectional Troparion, twice: Glory, of the Fathers, Tone 2: Great are the achievements of faith: Both now, of the Forefeast, Tone 4: Make ready, O Bethlehem. And the usual Kathismata, and the Resurrectional Sessional Hymns, and their Theotokia, and a reading from the Commentary on the Gospel of Matthew, at the very beginning:* "The book of the generation of Jesus Christ." *After the Evlogetaria (Amomos), the troparia "The angelic council", the Hypakoe, and a reading from the Commentary on the Gospel appointed in order: The Hymns of Ascent of the Tone: Prokeimenon: Let every breath: The Resurrectional Gospel. And "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ": After Psalm 50, the Resurrectional Sticheron. The Resurrectional Canon with the heirmos to 4; and of the Forefeast to 4; and of the Fathers to 6: Katavasia: Christ is born: After Ode 3, the Hypakoe of the Fathers, Tone 8: The angel bedewed the furnace for the youths: and a reading. After Ode 6, Kontakion, Tone 1, Podoben: "The angelic choir" (Ли́къ а҆́ггльскїй): Be glad, O Bethlehem: and the Ikos. And we read the Prologue. After Ode 9: Holy is the Lord our God: Resurrectional Exapostilarion, Glory, of the Fathers, Both now, of the Forefeast. At the Praises, Resurrectional Stichera 4; and of the Fathers 4, Tone 5, Podoben: "Rejoice" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ): Glory, of the Fathers, Tone 8: Of the lawful teachings: Both now: Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos: The Great Doxology. Resurrectional Troparion, Litanies. And the Dismissal. The Gospel Sticheron in the narthex. And the First Hour. And the final Dismissal. At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Tone to 4; and of the Fathers from the Canon, Ode 3 to 4; and of the Forefeast, Ode 6 to 4. After the Entrance, the Resurrectional Troparion, and of the Fathers, and of the Forefeast. Glory, Kontakion of the Fathers, and Both now, of the Forefeast. Prokeimenon, the Hymn of the Fathers, Tone 4: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers, and praised and glorified is Thy name unto the ages.*[^209] *Epistle to the Hebrews, Pericope 328 [Heb. 11:9–10, 17–23, 32–40]. Alleluia, Tone 4: O God, with our ears have we heard:*[^210] *Gospel of Matthew, Pericope 1 [Matt. 1:1–25]. The regular Sunday reading of the cycle is omitted. Communion Hymn: Praise the Lord: Another: Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous.*

*Concerning the Forefeast of the Nativity of Christ, it is fitting to know:*
*Note: From the 20th day the Forefeast begins. There is indeed fasting, yet prostrations are not made in the church.*[^211]

*The 21st Day of the Same Month:*

*The Forefeast of the Nativity of Christ; and the Holy Virgin Martyr Juliana of Nicomedia.*[^212]

*At "Lord, I have cried", Stichera of the Forefeast, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*
"This is our God, and none other shall be accounted of beside Him," the prophet cried aloud in the Spirit; "and He hath found out every way of knowledge." And after these things He shall be made like unto men, having clothed Himself in the flesh: for of the Virgin Maiden of God He comes to be born, having become accessible unto me, Who by nature art inaccessible![^213]

Thy womb, O all-undefiled Theotokos, is shown forth as a threshing-floor stack, carrying ineffably beyond mind and speech the unplowed Ear of corn; Whom thou shalt bring forth in the cave of Bethlehem, Who wills to nourish the whole creation with divine understanding by grace, and to deliver mankind from soul-corrupting famine.

The undefiled Heifer, carrying the fatted Calf in her womb, comes unto the holy cave, by a most marvelous word to give birth unto Him, and to swaddle Him like a man, and to lay Him in a manger like a babe. O creation, celebrate the forefeast, joyfully magnifying Him Who has wrought such glorious things upon the earth!

*And of the Saint, Tone the same, Podoben: "As one valiant" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*
Having dyed for thyself the garment of salvation in the purple of thy blood, O all-praised one, and having been enlightened by the Spirit, thou wast betrothed unto the Lord, the immortal King, Who preserves thee undefiled and uncorrupted unto ages of ages in the manifest bridal chambers, as a maiden adorned and incorrupt.

Sharing in wounds and wrestling with fire, having endured the tearing of thy flesh and valiantly borne terminal beatings, thou wast not vanquished in thy mind, [unto the idols] thou didst not sacrifice unto idols; but bowing thy neck unto God, through the beheading of the sword thou didst ascend into the heavens as a crown-bearer!

Adorned with drops of blood, thou didst shine forth manifestly like the sun; and thou didst drive away the darkness of godlessness by grace, O all-praised one, O martyr Juliana, and didst enlighten the faithful who honor thy valiant contests and thy bright and light-bearing memory, which is in all things saving!

*Glory, both now, of the Forefeast, Tone 6:*
Triumph, O Zion! Be glad, O Jerusalem, city of Christ God: receive the Creator Who is contained in the cave and in the manger! Open unto me the gates, and having entered into them I shall behold Him swaddled in swaddling clothes like a babe, Who holds creation in His palm; Whom the angels hymn with unceasing voice, the Lord the Giver of life, Who saves our race!

*At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Forefeast, Tone 2, Podoben: "House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
The prophecies of all the prophets are fulfilled: for Christ is born in the city of Bethlehem of the pure Maiden of God!

*Verse: God shall come from Theman, and the Holy One from a mountain shadowed and densely wooded.*
The glory, rejoicing, and praise of the earthborn, O honored Bethlehem: divine metropolis, receive thy Creator!

*Verse: O Lord, I have heard Thy report, and was afraid; O Lord, I considered Thy works, and was amazed.*
The Father's Word, by Whom all things were made, passionlessly and incorporeally, is seen as one hypostasis in two natures!

*Glory, both now, Tone 6. By Byzantios:*[^214]
O unwedded Virgin, whence art thou come? Who was he who begot thee? And who is thy mother? How dost thou carry the Creator upon thine arms? How wast thou not corrupted in thy womb? O the great, glorious, and fearful mysteries accomplished in thee upon the earth, which we ever behold! And we prepare a worthy debt for thee: on earth a cave; and from heaven we ask to grant a star. And the Magi also come from the east of the earth unto the west, to behold the salvation of mankind, swaddled in swaddling clothes in the manger!

*Troparion of the Saint, Tone 4:*
Thy lamb, O Jesus, Juliana, cries with a great voice: "Thee, my Bridegroom, do I love, and seeking Thee I endure suffering, and am crucified and with Thee am I buried in Thy baptism, and I suffer for Thy sake, that I may reign in Thee; and I die for Thee, that I may also live with Thee; but as an undefiled sacrifice receive me who have sacrificed myself unto Thee with love." By her intercessions, as Thou art merciful, save our souls!

*Glory, both now, Tone the same:*
Make ready, O Bethlehem! Be opened unto all, O Eden! Adorn thyself, O Ephratha, for the Tree of Life has blossomed forth in the cave from the Virgin: for her womb appeared as a noetic Paradise, wherein is the divine Garden; eating of which we shall live, and shall not die as did Adam. Christ is born, to raise up the image that had fallen of old!

*At Compline, Triodion, the heirmos twice, troparia to 6; and again at the end the heirmos by both choirs together. The acrostic whereof is: "I sing to the fourth."*[^215]
*Tone 2. Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Having established me upon the rock of faith, Thou hast enlarged my mouth against mine enemies. For my spirit rejoiced when singing: There is none holy as our God, and none righteous beside Thee, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
The assembly of Herod gathers together in vain and willingly, defiled with murder, to slay the Lord Christ Who is born; unto Whom we sing: Thou art our God, and there is none righteous beside Thee, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
The harsh counsel of Herod is concealed, that son of a God-fighting soul, to slay the Master Christ with the infants; unto Whom we sing: Thou art our God, and there is none righteous beside Thee, O Lord!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
When the decree of the tyrant prevailed, the furnace was heated sevenfold of old; wherein the youths were not burned, trampling underfoot the king's decree, but cried aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and supreme-exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Pouring forth tears like myrrh unto Christ Who for our sake is born in the flesh, wherewith let us cleanse our defilements, approaching purely unto the Most Pure, and crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and supreme-exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
With tears of compunction, let us sinners flee the weeping of future fearful torments, embracing the steps of Christ, laid in swaddling clothes like a babe, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and supreme-exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Knowing that redemption is sacredly ministered from the fountain of their own inmost hearts and tears, having washed beforehand through confession unto Christ having washed beforehand through confession, ye faithful, let us approach in the flesh unto Him Who is born in the cave, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and supreme-exalt Him unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
With pure souls and undefiled lips, come, let us magnify the undefiled and all-pure Mother of Emmanuel; through whom offering supplication unto Him Who is born of her: Spare our souls, O Christ God, and save us!

*Troparion:*
Let no one be without understanding, nor deceitful in the image of envy, among those who now bring gifts acceptable unto God. Instead of myrrh, and gold, and frankincense, let there be the anointing of virtues, of those who sing unto Christ Who is born: Spare our souls, O Christ God, and save us!

*Troparion:*
Herod said unto the wise Magi who had come: "Go and seek out the King Who is now born, and having found Him, bring me word"; the harsh one was plotting murder with a murderously-defiled heart: Spare our souls, O Christ God, and save us!

*Troparion:*
O blindness of murderously-defiled all-daring, whereby thou didst receive oblivion, in that no one can lay hold of God with his hands to slay Him! Yet inflamed with fury, thou savagely slaughterest the infants, O Herod: Spare our souls, O Christ God, and save us!

*At Matins, after the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn of the Forefeast, Tone 2, Podoben: "The noble Joseph" (Бл҃гообра́зный):*
The inaccessible God, having voluntarily become accessible unto me for the sake of tender mercy, comes to be born in the flesh like a man, in the city of Bethlehem of the Virgin Maiden: Whom let us diligently hasten to receive, crying aloud with fear: Lord, glory to Thee!

*Glory, both now, Tone 1, Podoben: "Thy tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й сп҃се):*
He Who bowed the heavens and dwelt in the Virgin comes forth in the flesh to be born in the cave of Bethlehem, as it was written; and He is seen as a babe, Who gives life to babes in the womb. Rejoicing at this, let us all now go to meet Him in uprightness of heart!

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 2, Podoben: "The Word Who is pre-unoriginate" (Собезначáльное):*
O Bethlehem, make ready to meet the Virgin Mary and Mother of God; for behold, she comes unto thee carrying as a babe Christ, Who is ever co-unoriginate with the Father and the Spirit; Whom she brings forth in the cave, and after childbirth is shown forth a virgin again!

*Glory, both now, Tone 3, Podoben: "The beauty of virginity" (Красотѣ̀ дѣ́вства):*
A most marvelous wonder is beheld today, for our Savior is born in the flesh for our sake of the Virgin in the cave and hastens now to be born. And the Magi worship Him with gifts as King; and the shepherds with the angels glorify Him. With them let us also cry aloud: Glory to Him Who was made man for our sake!

*Canons: of the Forefeast with the heirmos to 8; and of the Saint to 4.*
*Canon of the Forefeast, whose acrostic is according to the alphabet. A composition of Joseph. Tone 4:*[^216]
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
O Thou Who wast born of the Virgin, drown, I pray Thee, the tripartite power of my soul in the depth of dispassion, as of old Thou didst drown the mighty captains; that as upon a timbrel, in the mortification of the body I may sing unto Thee a song of victory!

*Troparion:*
Rejoice, O heaven, and be glad, O earth: for our God, having become flesh, is born of the Virgin Maiden, and is wrapped in swaddling clothes; and as He is merciful, He looses the bonds of my transgressions!

*Troparion:*
The pure Queen brings forth beyond understanding the King of all, Who opens the heavenly Kingdom unto the faithful, and utterly abolishes sin which ever tyrannously reigned within us!

*Troparion:*
The prophetic scriptures attain their fulfillment: for behold, Christ Whom they foreannounced appears in the city of Bethlehem, becoming incarnate; let us hasten today to celebrate the forefeast of His Nativity with uprightness of mind!

*Another Canon of the Saint, whose acrostic is: "May God add grace to sing of thee, O martyr." A composition of Joseph. Tone the same:*[^217]
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Israel of old, having traversed the Red Sea's deep with unwetted feet, by Moses' hands stretched out crosswise vanquished the power of Amalek in the wilderness.

*Troparion:*
Radiant manifestly with the brightness of martyrdom, thou dancest before God, sacredly deified, O all-praised one, and by thy supplications thou grantest enlightenment unto those who hymn thee!

*Troparion:*
Thou wast wounded with the sweetest longing for Christ, O all-praised one, and having forsaken carnal pleasures and a corruptible bridegroom, thou wast betrothed, O undefiled pure virgin, unto Him Who made thee!

*Troparion:*
The Creator of all and God, having shone upon thy mind with light-revealed beauties, accounted thee worthy of the heavenly bridal chambers, dancing maidenly, O divinely-wise martyr!

*Theotokion:*
The Virgin goes to bring forth in the cave the Creator of nature, Who ineffably and supernaturally took flesh from her according to hypostasis!

...that He may deify mankind.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
As the barren Church of the nations hath brought forth, and the synagogue great in children hath grown weak, unto our marvelous God let us cry aloud: Holy art Thou, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Daniel beholds Thee, O Word, as the Stone cut out without hands from the virginal mountain, crushing the idol temples by Thy power; therefore do we glorify Thee with fear!

*Troparion:*
Guided by the star, the Magi from the east bring gifts unto Thee, the King of all, O Christ: myrrh, gold, and frankincense, marveling at Thine extreme condescension!

*Troparion:*
Mary, the unplowed field, carries the life-bearing Ear of corn, to bring Him forth in the city of Bethlehem, Who nourishes the souls of all who cry: Holy art Thou, O Lord!

*Canon of the Saint. Heirmos:*
Thy Church rejoices in Thee, O Christ, crying aloud: Thou art my strength, O Lord, and my refuge, and my confirmation!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst make thy soul an all-holy temple of God, O glorious one, ever attending the divine temples with hymns and prayers!

*Troparion:*
Longing to attain the greatest gifts, O all-honored one, thou didst endure bodily pains as though in an alien body!

*Troparion:*
With the drops of thy blood thou didst extinguish the fire of godlessness, and didst water the minds of the faithful, O Juliana!

*Theotokion:*
The Redeemer Who delivers mankind is born in Bethlehem of the Pure One, receiving swaddling clothes like a babe!

*Kontakion of the Saint, Tone 2, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дв҃а дне́сь):*
Purified with the beauties of virginity, O maiden, and crowned now with the wreaths of martyrdom, O Juliana: thou grantest healing and salvation unto those who are in needs and infirmities, who draw near unto thy shrine; for Christ pours forth divine grace and life eternal!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*
Having loved the Bridegroom, the Creator and God, thou didst forsake a corruptible bridegroom, O honored martyr, and rejoicing didst endure torments and tearings, and the burning of fire. Therefore, crowned with wreaths, thou didst ascend unto the divine bridal chamber, entreating forgiveness of transgressions for all!

*Glory, both now, of the Forefeast, Tone 3, Podoben: "The beauty of virginity" (Красотѣ̀ дѣ́вства):*
[Joy...] Be filled with joy, all ye ends of the earth! For the Theotokos draws near to give birth unto the King of all. O ineffable wonder! The Pre-unoriginate begins, and the Bodiless is incarnate: the cave receives Him Who holds all things. Rejoice, O Bethlehem; and O creation, dance in celebration on this forefeast day!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Jesus, Who is surpassing God, Who sits in glory upon the throne of the Godhead, came upon a light cloud, and with His incorruptible palm saved those who cry: Glory to Thy power, O Christ!

*Troparion:*
The holy alabaster jar of honored purification comes into the city of Bethlehem to pour forth this ointment, granting sanctification unto us all who cry: Glory to Thy power, O Christ!

*Troparion:*
O divinely-speaking Isaiah, seeing thy honored proclamations accomplished in deeds, rejoice and dance: for without seed the Virgin brought forth in the flesh within the cave of Bethlehem Him Whom nothing can contain!

*Troparion:*
The One born in the flesh, and He Who is timeless in time, is seen as a babe, loosing my temporal transgressions, and by His ineffable poverty ever enriching me, who had become impoverished through corruptive transgressions!

*Canon of the Saint. Heirmos:*
Beholding Thee, the Sun of Righteousness, lifted up upon the Cross, the Church stood in her place, worthily crying aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Having stretched out thy mind unto the Lord of all, when stretched out in the flesh and grievously wounded, thou didst take no heed thereof, O good maiden Juliana!

*Troparion:*
The longings of the flesh were unable to darken the Master's love, O all-praised martyr; therefore didst thou despise both riches and bridegroom, and manifold torments!

*Troparion:*
Tearing thee, the undefiled ewe-lamb, with wounds like wolves, O martyr, the torturers completed the holy whole sacrifice and divine slaughter of an undefiled sheep of God!

*Theotokion:*
Seeing virginity sealed after childbirth, O Theotokos, possessed with awe, she cried aloud: "O Child, how shall I now swaddle Thee, Who swaddlest the sea with sand?"[^218]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
The ungodly shall not see Thy glory, O Christ; but we, who wake at dawn from the night, hymn Thee, the Only-begotten, the Radiance of the Father's glory of the Godhead, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
God Emmanuel is born of the Virgin, and reclining in the manger reclining in the manger, He willingly works our restoration; let us piously celebrate His Nativity beforehand!

*Troparion:*
Being the Word before all beginning, consubstantial with the Father, reclining in the manger of mute beasts, Thou hast loosed us from irrationality, as we piously celebrate beforehand Thy Nativity!

*Troparion:*
Blessed was the root of Jesse, having sprouted a branch bearing the divine Flower, Christ the Lord,[^219] Whose Nativity we celebrate beforehand, rejoicing!

*Canon of the Saint. Heirmos:*
Thou, my Lord, hast come into the world as a Light, a holy Light, turning those who hymn Thee in faith back from dark ignorance!

*Troparion:*
With streams of thy blood shed unjustly, O martyr, thou didst dry up the flood of evil godlessness, and didst quench the fire of delusion!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst offer thyself consecrated unto God Himself, having made the scarlet robe of virginity more radiant with the purpling of thy blood!

*Troparion:*
Having wounded her soul with Thy beauty, the good maiden outran visible beauties, shining with suffering!

*Theotokion:*
A novel and seemly marvel: the all-pure Virgin goes into the cave of Bethlehem, to give birth unto God incarnate!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
I am come into the depths of the sea, and the tempest of my many sins has drowned me; but as God, lead up my life from the depth, O most merciful One![^220]

*Troparion:*
He Who shone forth ineffably from the Father before all ages is born unto us a new babe upon earth, and delivers all from the ancient transgression, as He is compassionate!

*Troparion:*
Strange and glorious things were heard in the city of Bethlehem when Thou wast born, O unoriginate Word; for the shepherds with the angels thus offered a song unto Thee!

*Troparion:*
The Star of Righteousness proclaims the Sun born ineffably in a lowly place; Whose honored Nativity we now celebrate beforehand, rejoicing!

*Canon of the Saint. Heirmos:*
I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord, the Church cries aloud unto Thee, cleansed from demonic blood by the blood that flowed through mercy from Thy side!

*Troparion:*
Wounded with divine longing, thou didst cry aloud: "I seek to attain Christ, Who is fair in beauty; therefore I endure torments, rejoicing with an unyielding mind!"

*Troparion:*
The deceitful persecutor commanded that the Lord's ewe-lamb, whose mind was extended unto Christ, be mercilessly stretched out and crushed with rods!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst wake at dawn unto Christ, the never-setting Sun, and with His splendors, O divinely-wise maiden, thou didst illumine thy soul and heart, and didst pass over unto the ever-existing Light!

*Theotokion:*
The Creator, Who wrapped the sea with mist, is born willingly of the Virgin maiden, and receives swaddling clothes like an infant, delivering the world!

*Kontakion of the Forefeast, Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Въ вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*[^221]
Beholding in Bethlehem Him Who holds all the earth in His hand wrapped in swaddling clothes, we offer forefeast hymns unto her who gave Him birth; for she rejoices maternally, holding the Son of God in her bosom!

*Ikos:*
The Virgin, holding the Son of God in her embrace, kissing Him with maternal caresses, spoke: "I knew no seed in conception, and yielded no corruption in birth; and now I am pure as before, likewise even after childbirth. Therefore, O Child, I proclaim Thy great compassion and incomprehensible majesty, which Thou hast shown upon me. Therefore I also rejoice, holding the Son of God in my bosom!"

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The three youths in Babylon, turning the tyrant's command into folly, cried aloud in the midst of the flame: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers![^222]

*Troparion:*
How shall the cave contain Thee, the uncontainable One, Who comest to be born for our sake? How shall the Virgin suckle Thee, the Nourisher of all, O compassionate Jesus, Son of God?

*Troparion:*
Following the angels, the Magi, the boast of the sorcerer Balaam,[^223] hasten with gifts to worship Christ, understanding by divine inspiration that He reigns as King!

*Troparion:*
Rejoice and dance, O human nature that had been barren of all virtue; for Christ comes to be born in the flesh of the Virgin, that He may show thee to be fruitful in good things!

*Canon of the Saint. Heirmos:*
In the Persian furnace, the Abrahamite youths, consumed by love of piety rather than by flame, cried aloud: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
In his folly, O martyr, the judge cast thee mercilessly into a glowing cauldron; but the Lord saved thee unharmed by an angel, as thou didst venerate Him!

*Troparion:*
Not terrified, with manly wisdom, but rather, O all-honored martyr thou didst go unto the fire, feeling refreshment, and crying aloud: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
As a dowry unto the Bridegroom, thou didst bring a people and nation that came to believe in Him; and by thy luminous wonderworkings thou didst drive away the gloom of delusion!

*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, O dwelling place of the Uncontainable, O Virgin Mother; for thou art about to give birth in the flesh within the cave unto Him Who restores the creation of His hands, O all-pure one!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
O almighty Redeemer of all, having descended into the midst of the flame, Thou didst bedew those who acted piously, and didst teach them to sing: All ye works, bless the Lord, and praise Him!

*Troparion:*
Seeing that I through my many transgressions had become a den of robbers, O Christ, out of Thine ineffable compassion Thou hast saved me, and wast pleased to be born in a cave of the pure Virgin!

*Troparion:*
Subscribing full remission unto me, Thou, the Creator of creation, wast enrolled with servants by the decree of Caesar; I sing of the boundless abyss of Thy compassion, O Master!

*Troparion:*
O radiant palace of the Master: how didst thou enter into a most tiny cave, to give birth unto the King and Lord incarnate for our sake, in truth, O Virgin Bride of God?

*Canon of the Saint. Heirmos:*
Daniel, stretching out his hands, stopped the mouths of the lions in the pit;[^224] and the youths, lovers of piety, girded with virtue, quenched the power of fire, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Having thine eye and mind directed on high unto God Who is able to save, by the grace of the Holy Spirit thou didst calm the agitations of the flesh, singing in faith the song of the youths, O martyr: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Serving the command of the evil tyrant, vain-minded men worthy of fire cast thee alive into the fire, O martyr; but thou wast unburned by the fire, bedewed with the love of the Bridegroom, O God-bearer, as thou didst revere Him!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst stand before the judgment seat, proclaiming Christ, the immortal God, Who endured crucifixion, and slew delusion, and grants immortal life unto the faithful who cry aloud: All ye works, praise the Lord!

*Theotokion:*
The Lord Who makes the clouds His ascent[^225] comes to be born for us of the Virgin Cloud, that He may dispel the dark cloud of sin from those who cry aloud unto Him: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Eve indeed, through the disease of disobedience, brought in a curse; but thou, O Virgin Theotokos, through the blossoming of thy childbearing, didst make blessing bud forth for the world. Therefore we all magnify thee!

*Troparion:*
Let us all, the faithful, dance, leap for joy, and cry out in unison: The salvation of all draws near! The Lord comes to be born, to save those who wisely celebrate His Nativity!

*Troparion:*
Take up the psalter and harp, O holy forefather, and sing a hymn: Rejoice, O house of Ephratha! For He Whom the Father begat from the womb is born unto thee most radiantly, becoming incarnate of the Virgin!

*Troparion:*
Like a shower, like a great rain, the Master descended into thy womb, O Mother of God, Virgin Mother, and watered the parched earth darkened by godlessness, and dried up the seas of delusion!

*Canon of the Saint. Heirmos:*
A stone cut without hands from an unhewn mountain was cut off from thee, O Virgin, even Christ the cornerstone,[^226] Who joined together the severed natures. Therefore, rejoicing, we magnify thee, O Theotokos!

*Troparion:*
The angels marveled at the contests for the faith of God-bearing Juliana: how in a woman's nature she trampled down him who put her foremother to death in Paradise!

*Troparion:*
As a most noble passion-bearer and an exquisite maiden, thou didst lawfully receive the crown of righteousness, having trampled down the bodiless foe with thy flesh, and becoming victorious!

*Troparion:*
We venerate thee as a spiritual swallow and an incorrupt turtledove and dove, whose wings were gilded by martyrdom, and who didst fly unto God and find rest!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst blossom in the valleys of martyrdom like a lily, O passion-bearer Juliana, and wast like a fragrant rose by thy virginity, becoming a divine fragrance unto thy fair Bridegroom!

*Theotokion:*
Bearing Him Who bears all things, the Virgin comes unto Bethlehem, both to give Him birth and to recline Him in a manger like a babe, Who excellently accomplishes the restoration of men!

*Exapostilarion of the Forefeast, Podoben: "He has visited us" (Посѣти́лъ ны̀ є҆́сть):*[^227]
Come, all ye faithful, let us bring forefeast hymns of the Nativity: Christ already comes unto Bethlehem to be born, to save the universe, as He alone loves mankind!

*Glory, both now:*
 O Bethlehem, land of Judah, adorn thine entrances:[^228] for unto thee the Virgin and Theotokos already comes to give birth, in a cave and manger, unto my God and Lord!

*At the Praises, Stichera on 4, Tone 6, Podoben: "Ye angelic hosts, go before" (А҆́ггелскїѧ пред̾иди́те):*
Creative Wisdom now comes forth: the prophetic clouds are opened, grace blossoms, truth hath shone forth; shadow-like riddles cease, the door of Eden is opened! Dance, O Adam; God our Creator hath created a greater work!

*Sticheron:*
Fulfilling the prophetic utterances and visions, the Word is born in the flesh and takes on gross substance, and having been born, reclines in the manger of mute beasts. This is the utmost condescension! This is the awesome dispensation, on account of which we sing: Christ, the King of Israel, comes!

*Sticheron:*
Behold, the Pure One, beyond mind and word, gives birth unto the Son of God, Whom the prophets proclaimed of old, foreseeing by the Holy Spirit: Who preserves thee undefiled, and looses Adam from sin. Let us people say: Christ our King comes in the flesh!

*Sticheron:*
Without leaving the Father's bosom, Thou hast appeared as man; and held by maternal hands, Thou hast called the Magi from Persia by a star, who worship Thee as King and God. By the breath of Thy lips Thou shalt destroy the impious pagan princes, and shalt shepherd Thy chosen people!

*Glory, in the same Tone and Podoben (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*
The Word Who is consubstantial with the Father, having received a mingling of pure blood from virginity, is fashioned, and grows by the space of pregnancy; and moreover He is born in a cave. Great is the awe! Angels sing praises, and men clap their hands: Christ, the King of Israel, comes!

*Both now, in the same Tone and Podoben (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*
The prophecies of the sorcerer Balaam receive fulfillment; for illumined by Persian wonders and by the radiance of an unusual star, being illumined by Christ, the never-setting Sun, they denote with gifts the incarnate God and King in Bethlehem, and the voluntary dead One.

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O house of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
The star shines forth, signifying Him Who is already being born in the cave: ye shepherds with the angels, and ye Magi with gifts, hasten to go before Him!

*Verse: God shall come from Theman, and the Holy One from a mountain shadowed and densely wooded.*[^229]

*Sticheron:*
That He may fulfill the prophetic utterances, the Lord is born in Bethlehem and opens Eden unto those of Adam's race!

*Verse: O Lord, I have heard Thy report, and was afraid: O Lord, I considered Thy works, and was amazed.*[^230]

*Sticheron:*
Anoint with myrrh, O Bethlehem, the holy manger; for within thee the Master is about to extend the rays of His Godhead!

*Glory, both now, in the same Podoben (Подо́бенъ то́йже):*
Come, ye earthborn, let us unceasingly hymn the Virgin, Mary the Theotokos, with one accord; for from her Christ is born!

*On the 22nd Day of the Same Month. Forefeast of the Nativity of Christ: And the Holy Great Martyr Anastasia, Pharmakolytria, which is the Deliverer from Bonds:*[^231]

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Forefeast on 3; and of the Saint on 3.*

*Stichera of the Forefeast:*
*Tone 1, Podoben: "O praised martyrs" (Восхвале́нїи мꙋ́нцы):*
All the earth, beholding the divine condescension, rejoices: the Magi bring gifts unto Me, heaven from above proclaims by a star, the angels give glory, the shepherds pipe and marvel, the manger receives Me as a throne of fiery appearance; rejoice, O Mother, beholding these things!

*Sticheron:*
As a Light for the revelation of the Gentiles, Thou hast come clothed in the likeness of my form, O my unoriginate Son, ineffable Offspring of the Father before all beginning; for Thou comest to enrich impoverished mankind through the poverty wherewith Thou art clothed; I hymn Thy compassion, O Lord!

*Sticheron:*
Beholding Me as a babe resting upon thy hands, O Mother, rejoice; for I am come to take away all the pain of Adam, which he suffered through the serpent's most evil counsel of old, having tasted and been cast out from paradise's delight, and having become corrupt!

*Other Stichera of the Holy Martyr, Tone 4, Podoben: "What shall we call you" (Что́ вы нарече́мъ):*
Having despised the beauties of the world, and moreover not having spared thy flesh not having spared thy flesh, O pure one: thou didst give over thine entire self to minister in godly manner unto the saints, most patiently in their sufferings; wiping away their purulent matter, and most wisely strengthening them unto bravery with wise words: pray that our souls may be saved!

*Sticheron:*
Thou didst disperse thy temporal wealth unto the needy, O honored one, fervently seeking that which is eternal; and following the divine footsteps of Christ with unwavering faith, Thou didst cry aloud: "I am wounded with longing for Thee, O immortal One! Make me conformable unto Thy sufferings, and show me to be a partaker of Thy divine glory, as Thou art compassionate and the Lover of mankind!"

*Sticheron:*
Having endured blessed suffering, O Anastasia, thou truly washest away our passions with the streams of thy healings evermore; therefore we worthily call thee blessed, and celebrate thy memory with love, and bow down before thy relics, drawing forth sanctification: pray that our souls may be saved!

*Glory, of the Saint, Tone 2:*
Thou didst receive the gift of resurrection, O all-praised Anastasia, having suffered at the judgment seat; for having destroyed a multitude of demons, thou didst consign them to the sea, O praiseworthy martyr and passion-bearer!

*Both now, of the Forefeast, Tone 4:*
Adorn thyself, O Bethlehem; sing, O city of Zion; rejoice, O wilderness, confirming joy beforehand! For the star goes before into Bethlehem, proclaiming Christ Who is about to be born; and the cave receives Him Whom nothing can contain, and the manger is made ready to receive eternal Life. Let us all hymn Him and cry aloud: Save our souls, O Jesus our God, Who wast incarnate for our sake!

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O house of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
Christ comes to crush the deceitful one, to enlighten those who are in darkness, and to loose those who are bound, unto those who go before to meet Him!

*Verse: God shall come from Theman, and the Holy One from a mountain shadowed and densely wooded.*

*Sticheron:*
Dance, O Zion; adorn thyself well, O cave; be prepared, O Bethlehem: for behold, the Virgin comes to give birth unto Christ!

*Verse: O Lord, I have heard Thy report, and was afraid: O Lord, I considered Thy works, and was amazed.*

*Sticheron:*
Sing praise and glory, ye families of the nations: ye Magi with gifts, and ye shepherds playing upon pipes, make haste with diligence!

*Glory, of the Saint, Tone 4. By the Studite:*[^232]
 Being named after the life-bearing Resurrection of Christ, through an honorable life Thou didst excellently follow thy calling; and having strengthened thy nature, and having shown courage in mind, Thou didst weave a purple robe with the dyeing of thy blood. And holding the Cross in Church like a sceptre, Thou reignest with God and the Savior, O all-blessed Anastasia! Pray unto Him to illumine us also with His divine glory!

*Both now, in the same Tone:*
Dance, O Isaiah, receiving the Word of God: prophesy unto the Virgin Mother that the bush burns with the radiance of the Godhead and is not consumed by fire! Adorn thyself well, O Bethlehem; open thy gates, O Eden; and ye Magi, go to see salvation swaddled in a manger! Whom the star showed above the cave, the Lord and Giver of life, Who saves our race!

*Troparion of the Martyr, Tone 4:*[^233]
Thy ewe-lamb Anastasia, O Jesus, cries aloud with a great voice: "I love Thee, my Bridegroom, and seeking Thee I endure suffering, and am crucified with Thee, and am buried with Thy baptism; and I suffer for Thy sake, that I may reign in Thee, and I die for Thee, that I may also live with Thee: but receive me as a spotless sacrifice, offered with love unto Thee!" By her prayers, as Thou art merciful, save our souls!

*Glory, both now, of the Forefeast:*
"Make ready, O Bethlehem: Written on the twentieth day."

*At Compline, the Canon, Tone 2, whose acrostic is: "I sing the long song of Great Thursday."*[^234] *Heirmos twice, troparia on 6. And again the heirmos at the katavasia.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
The parted Red Sea is cleft asunder, and the wave-nourished deep is dried up; the same becoming passable for the unarmed, and a grave for those in full armor; and a divinely fair song was sung: Gloriously hath Christ our God been glorified![^235]

*Troparion:*
Prosperously praised and all-ruling Life, the boundless Wisdom of God, built a house for Herself from the pure Mother who knew not man; for having clothed Himself in the bodily temple, Christ our God hath been gloriously glorified!

*Troparion:*
The Wisdom of God, initiating the Magi, gathers them as firstfruits from the nations; to mystically nourish beforehand those who are irrational, the mystical table lies in the manger of mute beasts; unto which they hasten, journeying with gifts, as the star goes before them!

*Troparion:*
Let us now proclaim the prophetic voices being fulfilled by the Spirit voices: for the Virgin, having conceived in her womb, comes to give birth unto the most holy One; Whom heaven showed unto the Magi, and the angels unto the shepherds, as a babe being carried!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Being Lord of all, and Creator God, the Passionless One, having become poor, united creation unto Himself; and being carried in the flesh as a babe, He is worshipped in a poor manger: "Eat, O friends, My Body, and be established by faith!"

*Troparion:*
As Christ comes to pour out His blood as redemption for the world, Herod rages to slay Him before the time, raging before Pilate's madness; therefore, with murderous savagery, he slaughtered a multitude of babes!

*Troparion:*
The foolish man said: "There is no God." Having been filled with utter frenzy, he is sick with the murder of Christ; and having fallen away by the audacity of his mind, he armed himself wholly to slaughter innocent babes, and defiled the earth with blood!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Foreseeing Thy ineffable mystery, O Christ, the prophet cried aloud: Thou hast set firm the love of Thy strength, O compassionate Father; for, O Good One, Thou hast sent Thine Only-begotten Son into the world as a cleansing![^236]

*Troparion:*
Having descended like rain upon the fleece, and like a drop upon the earth, onto her who gave Thee birth, O Lord,[^237] Thou comest mercifully to be born, and to live with men; for the Father hath sent Thee, the Only-begotten, into the world as a cleansing!

*Troparion:*
Thou hast partaken of human flesh, O Christ, from the seed of Abraham; and Thou comest to grant grace for grace, and to save and make incorrupt the image; for the Father hath sent Thee, the Only-begotten, into the world as a cleansing!

*Troparion:*
The new drink, which anciently David thirsted and desired to drink,[^238] proceeds to flow forth in the cave of the Bethlehemite, and to quench the enduring spiritual thirst of Adam and David, from whom Christ is born according to the flesh!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Bound by the bond of love as lovers of the brethren, let us give glory unto Him Who rules over all, Who loved the world exceedingly, and gave His beloved Son as redemption, Who grants peace unto all!

*Troparion:*
The Wisdom of God, holding the uncontainable and high waters in the air, bridling the abysses, and restraining the seas, having descended like rain upon a fleece, dwelt in the womb of the Virgin!

...By a star Christ calls the Magi, the disciples of the sorcerer Balaam, unto understanding. And He Who clothes the heavens with clouds is wrapped in swaddling clothes, and reclines in a manger, before Whom the cherubim tremble; and He Who fills all things is contained within a cave!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
The bottommost abyss of sins hath encompassed me, and no longer enduring the tempest, like Jonah I cry aloud unto the Master: Lead me up from corruption![^239]

*Troparion:*
The heavens, knowing Thee to be the Lord, proclaim Thy glory, O Savior; now calling the Magi with gifts by a star unto knowledge of Thee, and unto divine worship!

*Troparion:*
Having wiped away defilement, let each renounce it, and thus pure let him touch pure Christ, the Babe lying in the manger, Who cleanses the depth of hearts!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The youths in Babylon feared not the flame of the furnace; but cast into the midst of the flame, being bedewed they sang: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Shaking his head, foreseeing evil things, Herod was moved, seeking an opportune time to slay the God of life and death, Who is Lord of all and Master of creation!

*Troparion:*
As many of you as are Christ's friends, flee with Him Who flees into Egypt; and worthily worshipping Him, cry out in a godly manner and glorify Him with one accord!

*Troparion:*
"He who is not with Me does against Me," Christ says: "and he who gathers not with Me is likened unto him who scatters."[^240] Therefore let us fear His bodily descent!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
In Babylon the blessed youths, braving dangers for the laws of their fathers, spat upon the mad command of the king, and joined together, not scorched by the fire, worthily sang a song unto the Ruler: All ye works, praise the Lord, and exalt Him above all forever!

*Troparion:*
Ye divinely-wise foster-children who have gone before the Word unto Bethlehem, let us behold the marvel with the angels and shepherds, sending up glory unto God in the highest, Who gives goodwill and peace unto men: All ye works, praise the Lord, and exalt Him above all forever!

*Troparion:*
Holding fast to the law of love, let us embrace brotherly love, living at peace one with another, and being of one mind; for Christ, the Giver of peace, comes, reconciling all things, and saving those who cry aloud: All ye works, praise the Lord, and exalt Him above all forever!

*Refrain instead of "Glory": Bless* we the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*

*Troparion:*
With deceitful words lawless Herod honors Christ Who is being born, and bowed down to the Magi as though he himself also would worship Him; but he was not ashamed, persecuting Christ Who hid Himself, nor did he have mercy on the infants. And he knew not how to cry aloud: All ye works, praise the Lord, and exalt Him above all forever!

*Then both choirs sing together:*
*We praise, we bless, we worship the Lord, singing and exalting Him above all forever.*

*And we sing the heirmos:*
*For the laws of their fathers...*

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Come, O faithful, with minds on high let us enjoy the Master's hospitality and the immortal table in the lowly cave, having ineffably known the incarnate Word, Whom we magnify!

*Troparion:*
"Go," said Herod unto the leaders of the Magi, "search for the young Child; and when ye have found Him, bring me word quickly," devising deceit in his heart. But the deceiver was exposed, in vain acting lawlessly!

*Troparion:*
The Creator, begotten of the Father before the ages, is born of the Virgin, being the Wisdom, Word, and Power of God. Therefore, knowing Him to be the only Son, the God-man, the Lord, we magnify Him!

*Troparion:*
As man Thou appearedst in essence, not in phantasm; so as God by character of creation, in nature, O Savior, which Thou hast assumed. Therefore, honoring Thy divine coming from the Virgin, we magnify Thee!

*We sing the heirmos. And a prostration.*

*At Matins. After the first stichology, sessional hymn, Tone 1:*
*Tone 1, Podoben: "While the stone was sealed" (Ка́мени запеча́тану):*
Be enlightened, O creation, for the Creator comes forward to be born in the cave on account of His ineffable mercy! Ye shepherds, go forth to meet Him with diligence, beholding a fearsome marvel! Come, ye Magi, holding gifts in your hands, and saying: Glory to the born King, glory to Him Who guided us on the way! Let us worship Him in the flesh as King of all!

*Glory..., both now... Tone 4:*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*
Divinely does all creation rejoice today; for Christ the Lord, the Son of God, is born of the pure Virgin, making all the human race immortal; and she has annulled the curse of our foremother Eve. Therefore, as unto our Benefactor, let us offer up a song!

*After the second stichology, sessional hymn, Tone 6:*
*Tone 6, Podoben: "Hope of the world" (Оу҆пова́нїе мі́ра):*

The kings from Persia of old brought gold, myrrh, and frankincense unto the born King and God; but we who now keep the forefeast of His Nativity with godly mind from the soul, let us bring Him hope, faith, and love, singing praises unto the Virgin!

*Glory..., both now... Tone 3:*
*Tone 3, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дв҃а дне́сь):*
Singing praise unto the Virgin who gives birth to the pre-eternal Word, righteous Joseph cried aloud: I behold thee who hast become the temple of the Lord, bearing Him Who has come to save all men, and Who, on account of His tender mercy, shows forth as divine temples those who hymn Him!

*Two canons: of the Forefeast, to 8; and of the saint,[^241] to 6. Canon of the Forefeast, Tone 6:*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
When Israel walked on foot across the deep as on dry land, seeing the persecutor Pharaoh drowned, he cried aloud: Let us sing a song of victory unto God!

*Troparion:*
From the virginal cloud the great Sun, Jesus, our enlightenment, has shone forth unto us; let us who are in darkness sing unto Him, being brightly illumined by His radiance!

*Troparion:*
The Expectation of Jacob, the King of peace comes to slay the adversary! Let us hasten to meet Him Who is being born in Bethlehem for our salvation!

*Troparion:*
The divine voices of the prophecies are fulfilled, having signified the fearsome manifestation of Christ; for the ewe-lamb draws near to give birth to the Lamb and Redeemer and Lord of all!

*Theotokion:*
