Thee, the pure, sweet-smelling dove, honorable, undefiled, and fair among women, as having given birth to the God of all, we the faithful call blessed, O divinely-blessed maiden!

*Canon of the Saint, whose acrostic is: "I sing of thee, O Martyr Anastasia, with love. Joseph."[^242] Tone 8:*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Let us send up a song, O ye peoples, unto our marvelous God, Who freed Israel from bondage, singing a song of victory and crying aloud: Let us sing unto Thee, the only Master!

*Troparion:*
Let us send up a hymn unto God, Who goes forth to be born in the flesh of the Virgin in the city of Bethlehem, and as a Child to be laid in a manger as an infant, that He may save the human race!

*Troparion:*
Seeking the sole desired beauty of Christ, O glorious Anastasia, thou hast surpassed worldly beauties through firmness of disposition, and hast been accounted worthy of an immortal inheritance, O martyr!

*Troparion:*
Illumined by the enlightenment of the Spirit, O honorable one, thou didst prudently pass through the night of deceitful darkening, and now hast taken up abode where the divine radiance of the uncreated Trinity shines!

*Theotokion:*
The invisible God appeared, being born supernaturally of thee, O Virgin Mother, because of His great tender compassion; He Who is rich became poor, that by immortality He might enrich the human race!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
There is none holy like Thee, O Lord my God, Who hast exalted the horn of Thy faithful, O Good One, and established us upon the rock of Thy confession!

*Troparion:*
He Who stretched out the heavens by His word enters into the cave, and Christ goes to recline in the manger of brute beasts, desiring in His tender mercy to deliver us from irrationality!

*Troparion:*
The prophet cries aloud divinely: "This is our God, and none other shall be accounted of in comparison with Him! He found out every way of knowledge, having united Himself with men."[^243]

*Troparion:*
The cherubim cannot bear to gaze upon Him; and how shall the manger there endure Him Who is uncontainable by nature, being born for our sake of the Virgin according to His great tender mercy, O Lord, Lover of mankind!

*Theotokion:*
Daniel the prophet of old foresaw thee as the mountain from which the stone was cut, O Theotokos; and having truly destroyed the idol shrines, O all-pure Bride of God!

*Another [Canon]. Ode 3. Heirmos:*
O Lord, Supreme Creator of the celestial vault and Builder of the Church, establish me in Thy love, O summit of desires, firm support of the faithful, O only Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
Wrapped in swaddling clothes as a young Child, the intangible Lord desires to be seen reclining in a manger! Ye mountains, leap for joy, and ye hills, shine with divine joy, being filled with light!

*Troparion:*
With pious boldness thou hast blunted the fiery arrow-words of the persecutors, O Anastasia, having enriched thyself with the saving word and guided the stirrings of thy soul with divine love!

*Troparion:*
Continually, O martyr, didst thou cry aloud: "I seek the Lord; unto His love alone have I bound my soul! In the most honorable radiance of His splendors do I walk richly, in simplicity of manner!"

*Theotokion:*
O maiden uncontainably formed, in thy womb thou bearest in the flesh Him Who bears all creation in His hand; Whom also, when He is born, thou layest in a manger, the pre-eternal One seen as an infant!

*Kontakion of the Forefeast, Tone 3:*
*Tone 3, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дв҃а дне́сь):*
Today the Virgin comes to the cave to give birth ineffably to the pre-eternal Word; rejoice, O universe, having heard it, glorify with the angels and the shepherds Him Who desires to appear as a young Child, Who is God before the ages!

*Ikos:*
Of a truth, a fearsome wonder passing understanding! He Who gives being unto all on account of His goodness, has entered into the womb of the holy Virgin, and comes to be born in the cave, and to be laid in a manger! And the star proclaims Him from on high unto the Magi going to worship Him with gifts, arriving from afar with diligence, following the prophecy of Balaam, who said: A star desires to announce the young Child, Who is God before the ages![^244]

*Sessional Hymn [of the Saint], Tone 4:*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "Thy tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й сп҃се):*
As the bride of Christ we praise thee, O virgin; as an honorable maiden we worthily revere thee. Therefore also in thy memory rivers of healings pour forth; for thou hast received grace, keeping the commandments of the Lord by the power of the Spirit!

*Glory..., both now..., of the Forefeast, Tone 8:*
*Tone 8, Podoben: "That which was commanded mystically" (Повелѣ́нное та́йнѡ):*
Celebrating the forefeast of the Nativity of Christ, let us the faithful keep festival; and let us all worthily go forth to meet Him, bringing the virtues like gifts, as did the Magi: to sing a new angelic song unto our God, born in Bethlehem without seed of the Virgin Handmaiden of God, Whom all creation glorifies!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
"Christ is my power, God and Lord," the honorable Church sings in a manner befitting God, crying aloud from a pure mind, keeping festival in the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Lo, the star has shone forth from afar, which was foretold of old out of Jacob! The uncontainable God has become man, and is seen wrapped in swaddling clothes!

*Troparion:*
Lo, the Lord and Deliverance of all is seen as an infant, seated in virginal arms, Who as the Son reposes in the bosom of the Father!

*Troparion:*
O Eden, which of old wast closed unto me by the theft of food, open thou! For now in Bethlehem He is born, having clothed Himself in me, Who estranged me from thy painless enjoyment!

*Theotokion:*
The prophet Habakkuk, in the Spirit, foresaw thee, O Virgin, as the mountain of God overshadowed with virtues, from which He Who enlightens our souls has appeared unto us!

*Another [Canon]. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I have heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation; I considered Thy works, and glorified Thy divinity!

*Troparion:*
The utterances of those who prophesied by the divine Spirit are now being fulfilled; for the Virgin goes into the cave to give birth unto the All-perfect One!

*Troparion:*
Having sought with love the martyr's glorious blessing, thou hast obtained it, having firmly suffered with steadfast will, O patient-minded one!

*Troparion:*
With the robe woven from on high by grace hast thou truly been clothed through the stripping off of the body, O passion-bearer, all-praised martyr!

*Theotokion:*
Bearing fruit, the heavenly King comes forth from thy light-bearing womb, O all-pure one, reclining in a manger as upon a throne!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
With Thy divine light, O Good One, enlighten with love the souls of those who rise early unto Thee, I pray, that they may know Thee, O Word of God, as true God, calling them out from the darkness of sin!

*Troparion:*
From the cities, O house of Bethlehem, the Ruler shall come forth out of thee in Israel, calling the cast-off nations, even as Micah foretold of old, illumined by the Spirit![^245]

*Troparion:*
To shepherd His flock, Jesus alone in strength shall be born of the Virgin, and He shall be magnified unto the ends of the earth, as the inspired prophet proclaimed of old!

*Troparion:*
The Spirit of wisdom, the Spirit of God, the Spirit of counsel and strength, of knowledge and understanding, the Spirit of the divine fear has filled Thy Son, incarnate of thy womb, O Virgin![^246]

*Theotokion:*
All the weapons of the enemy, O all-pure, all-immaculate, and chaste one, thou hast truly brought to an end; for thou hast given birth unto the God of all, Who with a spear cast down his fury!

*Another [Canon]. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Rising early, we cry aloud unto Thee, O Lord, save us; for Thou art our God, besides Thee we know no other!

*Troparion:*
The star of Judah has shone forth from the land of the Chaldeans, moving the astrologers unto worship, as it was written!

*Troparion:*
Lawfully didst thou contend, having overcome the lawless, O all-glorious martyr, by the power of the Spirit!

*Troparion:*
Thou dost prefigure the divine Resurrection by thy naming, putting to shame the invisible enemies, O all-praised one!

*Theotokion:*
In a cave beneath the earth Christ comes to be born of the Virgin, that all creation may rejoice!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Beholding the sea of life surging with the tempest of temptations, fleeing to Thy calm haven I cry aloud unto Thee: Lead up my life from corruption, O greatly merciful One!

*Troparion:*
For lo, Christ comes unto His own; let us the faithful make ourselves His own by grace through divine virtues, and let us receive Him, being enlightened in souls and hearts!

*Troparion:*
The root of Jesse has sprouted, and from it has come forth our God, the Hope of the nations, rest and honor, even as Isaiah, divinely enlightened, foretold of old!

*Troparion:*
By Thy swaddling clothes Thou hast broken the chains of my many sins, and enriched me who was grievously impoverished through wickedness, O my Jesus, Who hast impoverished Thyself by Thine incarnation!

*Theotokion:*
The winter of hostile thoughts overwhelms my lowly heart through the assaults of evil spirits, O blessed Lady; subdue it by thy mediation!

*Another [Canon]. Ode 6. Heirmos:*
I pour out my prayer unto the Lord, and unto Him will I declare my sorrows, for my soul is filled with evils, and my life draws nigh unto hades; and like Jonah I pray: Lead me up from corruption, O God!

*Troparion:*
Having assumed the nature that is from us, the Compassionate One is seen as an infant, Who fashions infants in the womb; and He is wrapped in swaddling clothes and lies in a manger, and by His goodness looses the many-tangled chains of my passions!

*Troparion:*
Patiently following the contests of the holy martyrs for Christ's sake, and ministering to their needs, and wiping away their festering wounds, O venerable one, thou hast been most brightly enriched, shining with their glorious praise!

*Troparion:*
Thou pourest forth drops of healings with showers of divine gifts, and restrainest the rivers of passions, and helpest those who are in sore peril, O all-glorious martyr of Christ, named after the divine Resurrection!

*Theotokion:*
Healing human nature, which had corrupted through the ancient transgression, without corruption a new infant is born; and He sits in thy bosom as upon a throne, O unwedded Maiden, without leaving His co-enthronement with the Father in His divinity!

*Kontakion [of the Saint], Tone 2:*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*
Those who are in temptations and afflictions, fleeing unto thy temple, receive honorable gifts from the divine grace that dwells within thee, O Anastasia; for thou ever pourest forth healings for the world thou pourest forth healings!

*Ikos:*
Being named after Christ's Resurrection, resurrect me who am now fallen, by thy prayers, O martyr, dropping a drop of thy wonders upon my soul and quenching the flame of grievous sin! For thou ever savest the world from manifold passions, by which I also am tempted; for granting all things unto all, thou pourest forth healings for the world!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The Angel made the furnace dew-bearing for the venerable youths, while the command of God, consuming the Chaldeans, persuaded the tyrant to cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
The All-perfect One is born as an infant, wrapped in swaddling clothes, and the Unoriginate takes a beginning from the Virgin, seeking to deify our nature which He assumed: let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth be glad!

*Troparion:*
Clothed in the flesh as in a royal purple robe, now from thy womb, O Maiden, comes forth the King of peace, having crushed the enemies as mighty, and having brought peace unto our life that was formerly embattled!

*Troparion:*
God with us shall appear incarnate! Understand, ye adversary nations, and submit yourselves, ye who have estranged yourselves from our life: lo, our Restoration, an infant, desires to recline in the manger of Bethlehem!

*Theotokion:*
Out of all generations, the King Who dwelt within thy womb, O Maiden, chose thee as an undefiled palace; unto Whom we now sing in a godly manner: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Another [Canon]. Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The Hebrew youths in the furnace boldly trampled upon the flame, and turned the fire into dew, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, forever!

*Troparion:*
The heavenly choirs of the bodiless hosts sing praises, while we on earth worship, beholding Thee, O Christ, God of all, Who hast made Thyself like unto us earthly ones, and liest in a manger!

*Troparion:*
Thou hast reduced the deceitful fire to ashes, having shared in the flame as did the children; thou didst show forth fervent longing, O divinely-wise one, which thou didst acquire for thy Master and Bridegroom!

*Troparion:*
Thou pourest forth showers of healings, quenching the burning of diseases, and ever directest the people to sing: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, forever!

*Theotokion:*
A marvel astonishing to the mind is accomplished in thee, O Virgin Mother: to give birth thou art to give birth unto God, and to recline in a manger Him Who is unapproachable unto the cherubim, and uncontainable by nature!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
From the flame Thou didst pour forth dew for the venerable youths, and the sacrifice of the righteous one Thou didst consume with water; for Thou doest all things, O Christ, merely by willing them! Thee do we exalt above all forever!

*Troparion:*
The utterances of the inspired prophets are now fulfilled: the Virgin draws near to give birth unto the Lord! Let all the earth make merry, keeping festival, and let it rejoice forever!

*Troparion:*
Beaming with the rays of divine grace, putting aside the shadow of the law, Jesus the Giver of light has shone forth: ye that are darkened, behold a great light!

*Troparion:*
Make me, who have become a den of thieves, O Lord born in a cave, a temple of Thyself, and of the Father, and of Thy Holy Spirit, that I may glorify Thee forever!

*Theotokion:*
The heavenly star has shone forth from thy womb; the astrologers were moved to see it, being enlightened with the knowledge of it by the Spirit, O all-pure Virgin, ever blessed!

*Another [Canon]. Ode 8. Heirmos:*
The divinely-inspired youths in the furnace, trampling upon the flame with the fire, sang: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Unto Whom thousands and myriads of angels stand before on high, the cave bears Him Who is born, Whom we, His works, ceaselessly praise as Lord!

*Troparion:*
Thou hast shown thyself to be a temple of the Trinity in the divine temples, O Anastasia, occupying thyself with prayers and fastings, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Having strengthened thyself with most powerful words, O pleasing unto Christ, O passion-bearer, thou didst trample down the feeble fury of the idols, having suffered valiantly!

*Theotokion:*
O Maiden who contained God, in the city of Bethlehem, on account of His ineffable mercy, thou shalt give birth as an infant unto the Creator of the ages and immutable Lord!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
It is not possible for men to see God, upon Whom the ranks of angels dare not gaze; but through thee, O all-pure one, the Word incarnate appeared unto men: Whom magnifying, together with the heavenly hosts, we call thee blessed!

*Troparion:*
Lo, the Calling of all has arrived, Christ our Cleansing, Salvation, and Power! The priceless Treasure is hidden within the cave, wherewith the Magi having enriched themselves, bring gold as unto the King!

Ye shepherds of Christ, keep vigil, and come in mind unto the city of Bethlehem, and cry aloud unto God in the highest: Glory and majesty unto Him Who was well-pleased to appear as an infant for our sake, on account of His goodness!

*Troparion:*
Wrapped in swaddling clothes in the flesh, Thou Who wrappest the earth in mist and the sea in sand, hast broken the bond of my sins, and by righteousness hast bound together all things that were weakened by the assaults of the adversary!

*Theotokion:*
O chamber and throne of the reigning King, mountain of God, chosen city, paradise, and all-radiant cloud of the Sun, enlighten my soul, driving away the cloud of my many transgressions, O thou who hast found favor with God!

*Another [Canon]. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Truly we confess thee to be the Theotokos, who are saved through thee, O pure Virgin, magnifying thee with the bodiless choirs!

*Troparion:*
Leap, ye mountains, in gladness, and ye hills, gird yourselves with joy, for now the Virgin draws near to give birth unto the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Creation brings a day of gladness unto thee, O Anastasia, glorifying thy memory, which thou hast glorified by thy blood for the Word!

*Troparion:*
Now illumined with the purest light, by thy prayers ask from on high that we all may be enlightened, O grateful martyr!

*Theotokion:*
Let all creation now rejoice brightly: the Theotokos comes to give birth unto God the Word from God, Who has become man!

*Exapostilarion [of the Saint]:*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "In the spirit in the sanctuary" (Дх҃омъ во ст҃или́щи):*
Unto marvelous Chrysogonus shut up in prison Thou didst minister, O glorious Anastasia; and having obeyed his words, in God didst Thou finish the course of martyrdom; from Whom receiving the grace of healings, Thou healest infirmities![^247]

*Glory..., both now..., of the Forefeast, the same Podoben (Подо́бенъ то́йже):*
Let heaven rejoice and let the earth be glad! Be enlightened, O cave, and receive, O manger, Him Who created man with His hand, being born as an infant of the Virgin! Ye multitude of angels, cry aloud clearly: Glory to God in the highest!

*At the Praises, stichera to 4, Tone 6:*
*Tone 6, Podoben: "Angelic hosts, go before" (А҆́гглскїѧ предвари́те):*
Now the ancient visions are fulfilled; for the Virgin has conceived in her womb: for the stone was cut from the mountain, and the rod of Jesse has blossomed, and the dew of Gideon has now poured forth upon the earth! O ye peoples, let us cry aloud: Christ the King of Israel comes!

At the strange Nativity, strange things are seen: how does He Who sits with the Father on high, voluntarily recline in the manger of dumb beasts? How is the untouchable wrapped in swaddling clothes? How is He Who is everywhere contained in a cave? O ye peoples, let us cry aloud: Christ the King of Israel comes!

He Who worked wonders, striking Egypt, and rained down manna upon the senseless people, becomes incarnate and is nourished with milk! And seen as a young Child, He flees from the persecutor Herod, borne as upon a cloud by the Virgin Mother, even as the most divinely-sighted Isaiah foresaw![^248]

He Who is from before, the Child, the King of the ages, is born willingly, and a Son is given unto us! Give ear, ye nations, and hear; understand, and submit yourselves: for God is with us, Who shall crush and destroy from the earth every kingdom and principality that has not obeyed Him![^249]

*Glory..., the same Podoben (Подо́бенъ то́йже):*
With a rod of iron shalt thou be pastured, O Judea, because thou hast not submitted, nor believed the prophets; for unto the begotten Son the Father gives the nations for an inheritance, and the possession of all the earth; but thee He shall cast away, O defiled murderer, because thou hast not submitted to cry aloud: Christ the King of Israel comes![^250]

*Both now..., the same Podoben (Подо́бенъ то́йже):*
Leap for joy, O David, for Christ comes from thy loins! Rejoice, O Jesse, for thy root has blossomed! From thy thigh, O Judah, the Lord comes, according to the prophecy of Balaam! Behold, ye nations, according to great Isaiah: Lo, the all-pure Virgin shall bring forth the Child Emmanuel![^251]

*At the Aposticha, stichera, Tone 2:*
*Tone 2, Podoben: "O house of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
Christ draws near, the star has foretold Him; the heavenly multitude of the host of intelligent powers looks down!

*Verse: God shall come from Theman, and the Holy One from the mountain overshadowed and densely forested.*
Rejoice, O Bethlehem, that shepherdest us, saving Israel: no longer shalt thou be least among the princes of Judah!

*Verse: O Lord, I have heard Thy report, and was afraid; O Lord, I considered Thy works, and was astonished.*
Come, ye earthborn, let us also join the choir with the angels: Glory to God in the highest, let us cry aloud!

*Glory..., of the Saint, Tone 5:*
*By Byzantios:*
Today the forefeast day of the incarnation of Christ our God and the feast of the all-praised martyr Anastasia have shone forth together! Lo, the Virgin draws near unto Bethlehem, to recline the young Child wrapped in swaddling clothes [in a manger]!

to recline in the manger of dumb beasts Him Who freed us from the ancient curse and saves our souls!

*Both now..., of the Forefeast, the same Tone:*
Grieve not, O Joseph, beholding my womb; for thou shalt see Him Who is born of me, and shalt rejoice, and worship Him as God: so said the Theotokos unto her betrothed, being about to give birth unto Christ. Let us sing praise unto her, saying: Rejoice, thou that art full of grace, the Lord is with thee, and through thee, with us!

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Forefeast, Ode 3; and of the Saint, Ode 6. Prokeimenon, Tone 4: God is marvelous in His saints, the God of Israel. *In the same month, on the 23rd day:*
*Forefeast of the Nativity of Christ; and the holy Ten Martyrs who were in Crete.*
*At Vespers, on "Lord, I have cried," stichera of the Forefeast, 3; and of the Saints, 3. Stichera of the Forefeast, Tone 4:*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant" (Я҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*
With uprightness of mind, let us herald the forefeast hymns of the Nativity of Christ: for He Who is equal in honor with the Father and the Spirit, having clothed Himself in our mortal nature through tender mercy, is about to be born in the city of Bethlehem, Whose ineffable Nativity the shepherds sang with the angels!

Let us sound aloud with cymbals, let us shout with songs: the manifestation of Christ has appeared! The prophetic proclamations have reached their fulfillment; for He Whom they foretold would appear unto men in the flesh, is born in the holy cave, and reclines in a manger as a young Child, and is wrapped in swaddling clothes as an infant!

O Bethlehem, prepare thyself; O Eden, now be opened; the all-holy Virgin comes to give birth! Let the heavens be glad, let men leap for joy:

Life is in the manger, the Rich One is in the cave; He comes for the sake of the multitude of His mercy, having assumed the poverty of Adam, without change or confusion!

*Other Stichera, of the Holy Martyrs, in the same Tone and Podoben (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant" (Я҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*
The divinely-called decade and ten-branched lamp, illuminating the fullness of the Church with divine radiance, unshakable pillars, radiant stars, who have made the earth heavenly by the splendors of greatest struggles: let them be praised with loud voice today with sacred praises!

Let Theodulus be praised, with Zoticus and Pompeius, Basilides, Euporus, Agathopus, and Saturninus, Gelasius, and divine Evarestus, and with them let Eunician now be honored with hymns: all-calm havens for those in tempest, who have exposed deceit and received the crown of victory!

Offshoots of Crete, confirmations of the Church, and unfading adornments of the faithful, honorable, sweet-breathing flowers of paradise, acceptable and fair slaughterings for Christ, and dedications of the heavenly temple: let us honor the decade of passion-bearers of the Holy Trinity!

*Glory..., Tone 8:*
Today the forefeast of the martyrs has arrived, prefiguring for us the day of the Nativity, proclaiming the Sun from the Sun, God Who has appeared in the flesh from the Virgin; the decade of martyrs having suffered steadfastly in Crete have received crowns of victory from heaven! Unto them let us cry aloud: O choir divinely chosen, pray unto Christ, ye holy martyrs, for those who in faith celebrate your all-holy memory!

*Both now..., in the same Tone:*
Make thyself fair, O Bethlehem, for Eden is opened! Prepare thyself, O Ephratha, for Adam is renewed, and Eve with him; for the curse is destroyed, and salvation has blossomed in the world, and the souls of the righteous are adorned: offering hymnody instead of myrrh as an oblation-gift, and receiving spiritual salvation and incorruption! For lo, He reclines in the manger, commanding beforehand that spiritual song be made by those who cry aloud ceaselessly: Glory to Thee, O Lord!

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 6:*
*Tone 6, Podoben: "Having risen on the third day" (Трїдне́венъ):*
The immeasurable Wisdom of God, Christ, beyond understanding has built Himself a house from the Virgin; and in the cave and the manger of dumb beasts He wills to be born in the flesh beyond comprehension![^253]

beyond comprehension!

*Verse: God shall come from Theman, and the Holy One from the mountain overshadowed and densely forested [Hab. 3:3].[^254]*
Thou didst appear unto the prophets, O Christ, so far as it was possible to see Thee, the Creator; and in the last times Thou hast shown Thyself unto all men in the city of Bethlehem, having become man!

*Verse: O Lord, I have heard Thy report, and was afraid; O Lord, I considered Thy works, and was astonished [Hab. 3:2].*
The star ran together, heralding Christ the Sun of righteousness unto the astrologers in the city of Bethlehem; and the angels now announce good tidings unto the shepherds: with them let us run, O divinely-wise ones!

*Glory..., Tone 2:*
Today Crete celebrates the forefeast of the Nativity of Christ in the memory of the passion-bearers; therefore by their prayers, O Lord, save our souls!

*Both now..., in the same Tone:*
Behold, the time of our salvation draws near: prepare thyself, O cave! The Virgin draws near to give birth! O Bethlehem, land of Judah, adorn thyself and be glad, for out of thee has shone forth our Lord! Give ear, ye mountains and hills, and the surrounding regions of Judea: for Christ comes, that as the Lover of mankind He may save man whom He created!

*Troparion of the Martyrs, Tone 4:*
Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their sufferings received incorruptible crowns from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength, they cast down the tormentors and crushed the powerless audacities of the demons: by their prayers, save our souls!

*Glory..., both now..., of the Forefeast, in the same Tone:*
Make ready, O Bethlehem; Eden is opened unto all; adorn thyself, O Ephratha, for the Tree of Life has blossomed in the cave from the Virgin! For her womb was shown to be a spiritual paradise, wherein is the divine Garden, eating from which we shall live, and not die as did Adam! Christ is born, to raise up the image that fell of old!

*At Compline, the tri-ode canon, whose acrostic is: "The Forefeast." The heirmos twice; troparia to 6; the last heirmos by both choirs together. Tone 6.*[^255]
*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Unto Thee I rise early, Who through tender mercy didst immutably empty Thyself and didst bear the form of a servant from the Virgin, O Word of God: grant peace unto me who am fallen, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
Having washed our thoughts and cleansed ourselves beforehand through communion in the mysteries of the awesome dispensation, let us ascend in body and soul unto the city of Bethlehem, to behold the Master being born!

*Troparion:*
Behold, O friends, and fear not; for senseless Herod still rages, seeking to slay the born Creator; but He, holding life and death, lives and shall save the world as the Lover of mankind!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
The pillar of godless malice the godly children exposed; but Herod raging against Christ grows fierce, taking counsel in vain, plotting to slay Him Who holds life in His palm: Whom all creation blesses, glorifying Him unto ages![^256]

*Troparion:*
Let all us faithful shake off the sleep of sluggishness from our eyelids, and keep vigil in prayer, repelling the temptations that come from the evil one, and with the shepherds let us appear as beholders of the glory of Christ Who is born: Whom all creation blesses, glorifying Him unto ages!

*Troparion:*
Who among men can search out the depths of the wisdom and understanding of the Creator? What wise man can attain unto the abyss of God's judgments? For whose sake, having bowed the heavens, He lived with men bearing flesh: Whom all creation blesses, glorifying Him unto ages!

*Troparion:*
Let us the faithful forbid the defilement of words to go forth from our lips; and having meditated upon divine words, let us now bring them unto Him Who wills to loose us from irrationality, Who lies in the manger of dumb beasts: Whom all creation blesses, glorifying Him unto ages!

*Troparion:*
Let us make haste to cleanse ourselves of fleshly passions and the beauties of the world, and let us hold fast unto spiritual concerns, O divinely-wise ones, presenting ourselves worthy through deeds unto the Master Who is born: Whom all creation blesses, glorifying Him unto ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
More honorable than the cherubim, and beyond compare more glorious than the seraphim, who without corruption gavest birth unto God the Word, very Theotokos, thee do we magnify!

*Troparion:*
The ruinous command of the adversary, troubled by the strange Nativity, wrought the slaughter of the guileless infants; but let us honor with faith Him Who is born!

*Troparion:*
Contemning the laws of nature and casting aside the divine covenants, cruel Herod unlawfully bereaved mothers of their children, and slew the innocent infants for the sake of the Life of all!

*Troparion:*
Unto the nations the gate of Eden was opened, when the Redeemer was born in the cave; and the Lord of glory pours forth a spring of immortality unto those who thirst: Whom we magnify!

*Troparion:*
The angels surrounded the manger as a cherubic throne; for they beheld the cave as heaven, while the Master lay within it; and they cried aloud: Glory to God in the highest!

*Then the heirmos. And a prostration.*
