*Tone 4, Podoben: "The divine faith" (Бж҃е́ственныя вѣ́ры):*
Today the Church rejoices, sings, is adorned, and truly celebrates beforehand the Savior's Nativity; for the all-holy solemnity is accomplished, and she clothes herself in the glory of the Lord! Let us all cry aloud unto Christ God: O Lover of mankind, have mercy upon us who sing unto Thee!

*Glory..., both now..., the same.*
*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8:*
*Tone 8, Podoben: "Of wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
From the bosom of the Father Thou didst descend, and through ineffable emptying didst take upon Thyself our poverty beyond nature, O Lover of mankind! In a cave Thou wast well pleased to dwell, O Lord, and as an infant art nourished at the breast, O Creator and Lord! Therefore the Magi, guided by a star, bring gifts unto Thee as Master of creation; the shepherds and angels were astonished, crying aloud: Glory to God in the highest, Who comes to be born on earth as man!

*Glory..., both now..., the same.*
*Canon of the Forefeast with the heirmos to 8; and of the Saints to 6.*
*Canon of the Forefeast:*
*Whose acrostic is: According to the Alphabet. By Joseph.*[^257]
*Tone 6. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Him Who of old covered the persecuting tormentor beneath the wave of the sea, Herod seeks to slay as He is hidden in the manger; but with the Magi we sing: Let us sing unto the Lord, for He is gloriously glorified!

*Troparion:*
The ruler from Judah has already ceased; for He unto Whom it was promised, as was written beforehand, the Expectation of the nations, Jesus Christ, has come, and is born in the cave for the sake of supreme goodness![^258]

*Troparion:*
O Bethlehem, be glad with joy: for in thee Christ the Lord is born! Let the universe leap for joy, receiving redemption; let all creation keep festival and rejoice!

*Troparion:*
Desiring to save the human race, the All-good One dwelt within the womb of the Virgin who knew not wedlock; and lo, He comes to be born! Unto Him let us bow down, for He is gloriously glorified!

*Another Canon, of the Saints:*
*Whose acrostic in the Theotokia is: "Of George." Tone 2.*[^259]
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Come, ye peoples, let us sing a hymn unto Christ God, Who divided the sea and guided the people whom He brought forth out of the bondage of Egypt, for He is glorified!

*Troparion:*
All-radiant rays have shone forth today, heralding unto all the spiritual Sun, His shining forth and manifestation in the flesh in the world!

*Troparion:*
A spiritual forefeast banquet have the passion-bearers set forth unto all today, mystically nourishing us with the graces of Christ Who is born!

*Troparion:*
Having shone forth as radiant stars, O holy ones, ye followed the spiritual Sun of glory in the time of your struggles; and having obtained this, ye are now enlightened!

*Troparion:*
The martyrs, being of one mind, destroyed the hostile battle-lines, and ineffably received the prizes of victory from Christ Who is born in the cave!

*Theotokion:*
The human race brings unto thee a forefeast praise, O Bride of God; for they glorify the Lover of mankind born of thee as the Mediator and Author of common joy!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Beholding Thee Who didst suspend all the earth upon the waters without restraint, being born in a cave, creation, trembling in astonishment, cried aloud: There is none holy save Thee, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Thou wast well pleased to clothe Thyself in the form of a servant, that Thou mightest deliver me from the bondage of the evil one; I hymn Thy tender mercy, O Word, co-unoriginate with the Father and co-ever-existing: Glory to Thy dispensation!

*Troparion:*
The Virgin comes to give birth unto the Lord in the cave! Come beforehand, ye Magi; come now, ye shepherds; cry aloud a hymn from on high, ye angels: the Redemption of men has appeared!

*Troparion:*
Seeking me who had gone astray, O Lover of mankind, who through unfruitful deeds was shown to be a den of thieves, Thou hast now come into a cave, O Master, to be born of the Virgin today: Glory, O Word, unto Thy coming!

*Another [Canon]. Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Establish us in Thee, O Lord, Who by the tree didst put sin to death; and plant Thy fear in the hearts of us who sing unto Thee!

*Troparion:*
Having been wrapped in swaddling clothes, the Word born in the flesh tore asunder the garments of ancient condemnation, and clothed us in incorruption!

*Troparion:*
Ye destroyed the gathering of godlessness, O all-wise ones, by the power of Christ God Who appeared in the flesh, and were bound unto His love!

*Theotokion:*
We have been loosed from the bonds of condemnation, since the Creator was wrapped in swaddling clothes; and we have been clothed, O Theotokos, in the garment of pristine beauty!

*Kontakion of the Forefeast, Tone 3:*
*Tone 3, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дв҃а дне́сь):*
Today the Virgin comes to the cave to give birth ineffably unto the pre-eternal Word; rejoice, O universe, having heard this, and glorify with angels and shepherds Him Who wills to appear, the young Child, the pre-eternal God!

*Ikos:*
O marvel truly awesome and beyond word! He Who gives existence unto all, for the sake of His goodness comes to enter the womb of the holy Virgin, and to be born in the cave, and to be laid in the manger! And a star announces Him from on high unto the Magi coming to worship Him with gifts, drawing near from afar with diligence, following the prophecy of Balaam who said: A star is about to announce the young Child, the pre-eternal God![^260]

*Sessional Hymn of the Saints, Tone 1:*
*Tone 1, Podoben: "Thy tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й сп҃се):*
The radiant and honorable governors of Crete, having suffered steadfastly, by faith conquered the primordial evil serpent, and were lawfully crowned! Today we celebrate their praiseworthy memory, with loud voice glorifying the Lord of all! *Twice.*

*Glory..., both now..., of the Forefeast, in the same Tone and Podoben (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*
Rejoice, O Zion; adorn thyself, O Bethlehem: the Sustainer of all, having sent a star beforehand, has announced His immeasurable descent; for He Whom the heavenly powers tremble before, is born of the Virgin without change, our only God!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Foreseeing Thy coming from the Virgin, Habakkuk was astonished and cried aloud: Incarnate from the south, Thou art come, O Redeemer, to call back Adam who was cast away![^261]

*Troparion:*
The light-bearing cloud comes, to cause Christ the Sun of righteousness to shine forth from the maternal womb, illuminating all the earth with divine rays!

*Troparion:*
God was seen like unto men, and becomes poor in the flesh, that He may enrich us; and He is born in the cave! Him let us the faithful receive with a pure heart!

*Troparion:*
Lo, Christ is born in the city of Bethlehem, that He may open Eden unto us, which was closed of old through disobedience by the deception of the serpent; let us feast in a godly manner!

*Another [Canon]. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I have heard Thy report, O Lord, and was afraid; I considered Thy works, and was astonished, and cried aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^262]

*Troparion:*
Let the heavens be glad, let the earth be filled with mystical joy: for Christ is come to renew all things!

*Troparion:*
The decade of passion-bearers, heralding the birth of the Creator, rejoices with us and makes merry!

*Troparion:*
The coming of Christ divinely exalted the valiant martyrs unto heaven through their suffering!

*Theotokion:*
As common joy, O Theotokos, all creation honors thee with hymns, celebrating beforehand!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Unto Thee I rise early, Who through tender mercy didst immutably empty Thyself and didst bear the form of a servant from the Virgin, O Word of God: grant peace unto me who am fallen, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
Let every heart of the earthborn leap for joy, let creation be glad: the Lord is born of the pure Maiden in the cave of Bethlehem, and the Magi bring worthy gifts unto Him!

*Troparion:*
Ye people who sat of old in the shadow of death, behold the Light that has shone forth unto you from the Virgin, and be filled with much sweetness of soul, ever magnifying the Word Who has impoverished Himself![^263]

*Troparion:*
In a small cave Thou comest to be contained, Who art uncontainable by nature, that Thou mayest magnify me who was diminished through transgression, for the sake of Thine immeasurable mercy: I worship Thy tender mercy, O long-suffering One!

*Another [Canon]. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
O Giver of light and Creator of the ages, O Lord, guide us in the light of Thy commandments: for besides Thee we know no other God![^264]

*Troparion:*
Let us the faithful bring faith unto Christ as gold, and hymnody as acceptable frankincense, and pure love as myrrh, unto Him Who was well-pleased to be born in the flesh for our sake!

*Troparion:*
The defense of the passion-bearers, having gathered together today in one accord of Christ, cast down the manifold wiles of the enemies, and worthily received the honors of victory!

*Troparion:*
Having perceived the coming of Christ in the flesh, the all-wise martyrs cast away fleshly love; therefore for the sake of His love they also suffered!

*Theotokion:*
Having been delivered from idolatrous deceit, O pure one, through thee we have known the Creator and only Savior; therefore at His Nativity we honor thee with love, O all-pure one!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
The uttermost abyss of sins has surrounded me, and no longer able to endure its tempest, like Jonah I cry unto Thee, O Master: Lead me up from corruption![^265]

*Troparion:*
Without fleshly laws, O Lord, the Virgin comes to give birth unto Thee in the cave, and to recline Thee in the flesh in the manger as an infant!

*Troparion:*
Unto me who was estranged from God through transgressions, the supremely divine One, born of the Maiden who knew not wedlock for the sake of His mercy, reveals me to be a citizen of heaven!

*Troparion:*
Be glad, ye mountains and hills and valleys: for the Lord is born in the flesh, renewing creation that was corrupted by evil transgressions!

*Another [Canon]. Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Wallowing in the abyss of sin, I call upon the unsearchable abyss of Thy tender mercy: Lead me up from corruption, O God!

*Troparion:*
The eastern star that shone upon us from on high through ineffable mercy, having welcomed, announces illumination unto those in the world!

*Troparion:*
Shining in the night of life, by the light of Christ direct ye men unto Him, who walk in the deep of deceit, O all-glorious ones!

*Troparion:*
He Who for the sake of ineffable mercy was born in the cave, as the Lover of mankind drew up the martyrs from the depth of godlessness unto the height of divine knowledge!

*Theotokion:*
Through Christ God born of thee in the flesh beyond comprehension, O Bride of God, we the earthborn have been granted divine rebirth and honor!

*Kontakion [of the Martyrs], Tone 4:*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared today" (Я҆ви́лся є҆сѝ дне́сь):*
The morning star has shone forth, the honorable contest of the martyrs, pre-illuminating for us Him Who is born in the cave: Whom the Virgin seedlessly brought forth!

*Ikos:*
The warriors, loving Christ the Life-giver, born of the Virgin in a cave for our sake, raised up a radiant army against Belial; and having manifestly conquered, they cast him down unto the earth, who boasted immeasurably of old. Therefore they shine unto those in darkness, being luminaries of the spiritual Sun Christ our God: for a star indeed stood beforehand before the Magi, leading the way unto Bethlehem, the city of Judah; while these men proclaim Him unto us through their torments: Whom the Virgin seedlessly brought forth!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The children in Babylon feared not the flame of the furnace, but cast into the midst of the flame, being bedewed, they sang: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers![^266]

*Troparion:*
How shall the small cave contain Thee, O Word, Who hast clothed the poverty of Adam with much poverty, and hast enriched men with the wealth of divine grace?

*Troparion:*
The shepherds, having heard strange words, made haste to see Bethlehem, and Him Who reclines in the manger of dumb beasts, loosing all men from irrationality!

*Troparion:*
With lips and heart let us make haste to hymn Christ Who comes to be born in the flesh in the cave of the Virgin Maiden, and let us faithfully worship Him!

*Another [Canon]. Ode 7. Heirmos:*
Unto the golden image worshipped in the plain of Dura, Thy three children took no heed of the godless command; but cast into the midst of the fire, being bedewed, they sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^267]

*Troparion:*
Having become poor in the flesh, Christ showed forth the wealth of His ineffable love for mankind; for having become man, He opened the abundance of good things unto those who cry aloud without ceasing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Having been spiritually sweetened with the divine fragrance of Christ, O passion-bearers, ye abhorred all delightful beauties, and followed Him through suffering, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Ye were shown forth as a forefeast sacrifice unto Christ, O wise ones; ye brought the fragrance of suffering unto Him as myrrh; therefore by the sweet-smelling myrrh of wonders He glorified you, who cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
By thy prayer grant unto us who faithfully hymn thee, with pure eyes of the mind to behold the divine glory and splendor of our God born of thee in the flesh in the cave, O all-pure one!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
In Babylon the blessed youths, contending for the ancestral laws, spat upon the senseless decree of the king; and joined together in the fire wherein they were not consumed, they sang unto the Sovereign Lord:

-unto the Sovereign Lord they sang a worthy hymn: Hymn the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages![^268]

*Troparion:*
Holding in thy hands, O Maiden, the one Lord Who is incarnate beyond word and clothed in human likeness, and worshipping and kissing Him maternally, thou saidst: O sweetest Child, how do I hold Thee thus, Who holdest all creation in Thy hand, and deliverest it from the hand of bondage?

*Troparion:*
Prepare yourselves, O divine angels, to hymn Him Who is born upon earth! Ye Magi, guided by the star, bring your gifts! Ye shepherds, hasten to see Him, sitting as an infant in His Mother's embrace, crying aloud: Hymn the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
O unwedded cloud of the Light, how dost thou wrap with swaddling bands Him Who clothes the heavens with clouds by His ineffable beckoning? How dost thou lay down in a manger of dumb beasts the Master Who delivers men from irrationality through His boundless mercy? Unto Whom all creation bows down in fear, hymning Him unto all ages!

*Another [Canon]. Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Unto God Who descended into the fiery furnace unto the Hebrew children, and turned the flame into dew: hymn the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages![^269]

*Troparion:*
All creation prepares firstfruits for Thee, O Christ, Who art to be born in a cave of the pure Virgin; and it sings a forefeast hymn of praise, glorifying Thee, the only Benefactor.

*Troparion:*
Following Christ Who was born upon earth, O passion-bearers, having faith as a radiant guiding star, ye beheld Him, and brought unto Him divine gifts through suffering.

*Troparion:*
Strengthened by the power of Christ, O all-wise passion-bearers, ye conquered the oppression of the enemy and showed him to be powerless, hymning Christ unto all ages.

*Theotokion:*
He Who is in the bosom of the Father, having been born in the cave, reclined in thy maternal arms, O Birthgiver of God; and unto all who faithfully hymn thee, He opens the Kingdom in the heavens.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Marvel not now, O Mother, seeing as an infant Him Whom the Father begot from the womb before the morning star; for I have manifestly come to raise up and glorify together with Myself fallen human nature, which magnifies thee with faith and love.[^270]

*Troparion:*
Rejoice, O all-pure receptacle of ineffable joy; for behold, thou comest to give birth ineffably in a cave unto the Master, Who desires truly to renew all creation that was corrupted of old by transgression: hymning Him with faith, we magnify thee.

*Troparion:*
All ye souls of the righteous, and ye nethermost places together, rejoice! For behold, the Deliverance of all has appeared, being born in the city of Bethlehem; and the star proclaims Him unto the Magi who piously seek Him: who also, having seen Him in the cave, were filled with awe.

*Troparion:*
As another heaven we hymn thee, O Virgin, who art about to cause the morning Sun of Righteousness to dawn upon us from thy most pure womb, illuminating those who are in the darkness of death and corruption: therefore as is meet, with praises we magnify thee.

*Another [Canon]. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
God the Word of God, Who by ineffable wisdom came to renew Adam, who had fallen grievously into corruption through eating, and for our sake was ineffably incarnate of the Holy Virgin: with one mind, ye faithful, in hymns we magnify Him.[^271]

*Troparion:*
The army of sufferers, having run before the divine coming of the King of all, proclaims a banquet of joy unto all creation, and receives all the faithful, having set forth their own valiant deeds as food.

*Troparion:*
Beholding faith as a star, O passion-bearers of the Lord, and holding it fast, unto the never-setting Sun, unto Christ, ye were guided without stumbling because of it, O wise ones; and ye brought your blood unto Him as gifts.

*Troparion:*
Having reaped the flowers of the knowledge of Christ from imperishable meadows, O passion-bearers, ye were filled with His sweet fragrance having suffered; and through martyrdom ye yourselves brought the sweetest-smelling myrrh unto Him.

*Theotokion:*
Grace has been poured forth, O Virgin Birthgiver of God, among all generations of earth-born men, and the wealth of thy wonders flows abundantly in the radiant joy of thy giving birth, and enriches those who glorify thee with faith and love.

*Exapostilarion, Tone 2, Podoben: "With the disciples let us go up" (Со оу҆чени́ки взы́демъ):*
With Theodulus let us crown Zoticus, Agathopus, and Saturninus, Pompeius, together with Eunician, glorious Basilides, divine Euporus, glorious Gelasius, and Evarestus, joyfully with hymns: that through their prayers we may be delivered from transgressions, and receive crowns from Christ the Savior.

*Glory, both now, of the forefeast, Tone 2, Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Же́ны оу҆слы́шите):*
The mystery hidden and untold unto the angels is about to be accomplished by the good pleasure of the Father and the cooperation of the Spirit; let us make haste: for the Word Who is without beginning, having taken a beginning as man, is born of the Virgin for the salvation of the world.

*At the Praises, Stichera on 4, Tone 6, Podoben: "Ye angelic hosts, go before" (А҆́ггелскїя предиди́те):*
Foreordained by the Father before the ages, and foreannounced by the prophets in the latter times, the mystery has appeared, and God is made man: having taken flesh from the Virgin, the Uncreated is willingly created; He Who is becomes what He was not; Christ the King of Israel comes!

I sing to Thee, O King, wrapped in swaddling bands, for Thou loosest the bonds of my sinful falls; and having honored me with immortal and incorruptible glory, Thou hast made me wholly Thine own unto the Father, fashioning and rebuilding me. Therefore I cry aloud unto Thee: Christ the King of Israel comes!

The Light that proceeded from Light and shone forth from the Virgin unto those upon earth: the astrologer Magi, having seen Him by a star, cast off the Persian darkness and all starry delusion, and in joy sang unto God Who was born: Blessed is our God Who is come, glory to Thee!

The infant crop does Herod frantically reap, having been mocked by the wise Magi; and he thought to raise a vile and murderous hand against Thee: but Thou hast come unto the Egyptians, driving away the deepest darkness. With them we sing: Blessed is our God Who is come, glory to Thee!

*Glory, the same Tone and Podoben (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*
Sing, O new Israel, a new song; sing that heavenly hymn: rejoice and be glad with joy, and dance! Bring brightly the things of the feast: God has appeared in the flesh from the south![^272] The Same desires to be washed in the streams of the Jordan as man.

*Both now, the same Podoben (Подо́бенъ то́йже):*
Thou hast appeared upon earth, and hast dwelt with men; by the decrees of Caesar Thou wast enrolled with servants: not being changed from Thy created nature, Thou didst remain unaltered, being wholly God, even though Thou wast incarnate. Glory to Thy dispensation, honor, praise, and majesty, both now and unto the ages. Amen.

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O house of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
Pour forth fragrance, O Zion, * the holy manger; * for in thee the Master * is about to stretch forth * the rays of His Divinity.

*Verse:*

God shall come from the south, and the Holy One from a mountain overshadowed and densely wooded.[^273]

*Sticheron:*
Faith instead of gold, * and love as myrrh: * as frankincense of good deeds * let us bring unto the Creator, * Who comes unto His own.

*Verse:*
O Lord, I have heard Thy report, and was afraid; O Lord, I considered Thy works, and was astonished.[^274]

*Sticheron:*
Christ draws near, * the star shines forth beforehand. * A heavenly multitude * of the army of noetic powers * stoops down.

*Glory, Tone 3. By Theodore the Studite:*
O valiant martyrs of truth, neither the tyrant's duress, nor alluring flattery, nor the severing of limbs, nor threats of death availed to separate you from the love of God. Therefore, having boldness before Christ, Who is God over all: as a recompense for your painful sufferings, ask of Christ that through your prayers we may receive great mercy.

*Both now, of the forefeast, Tone 8. By Anatolius:*
In Bethlehem the Creator of all is born, and the eternal King opens Eden: the fiery sword turns back; the middle wall of partition is broken down; the heavenly powers are joined with earthly beings; angels with men establish a mighty celebration; the pure bring a hymn unto the Pure One. We behold the Virgin as the Cherubic throne of glory, containing God Whom nothing can contain, and bearing Him Whom the Seraphim glorify with fear: that He may grant great mercy unto the world.

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the forefeast, Ode 3; and of the martyrs, Ode 6. Prokeimenon, Tone 4:*
Unto the saints that are in His earth, marvelous has the Lord made all His desires in them.[^275] *Verse:* I beheld the Lord ever before me, for He is at my right hand, that I should not be moved.[^276] *The Epistle to the Ephesians, section 233.*[^277] *Alleluia: The righteous cried aloud.*[^278] *The Gospel according to Luke, section 106.*[^279] *Communion Hymn:*
Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous![^280]

*The same month, on the 24th day: Forefeast of the Nativity of Christ; and the memory of the Holy Nun-martyr Eugenia.*

*At "Lord, I have cried", stichera of the forefeast, Tone 5, Podoben: "Rejoice" (Ра́дꙋйся):*
Thou bearest Adam's form, being all-perfect in the image of God; and Thou desirest to be held by hands, Who by Thy power holdest all things in Thy hand! The pure and all-immaculate one spoke, saying: How shall I wrap Thee with swaddling bands as an infant? How shall I nourish Thee at the breast, Who nourishest all things? How shall I marvel at Thy poverty which is beyond comprehension? How shall I call Thee my Son, who am now Thy handmaid? I hymn and bless Thee, Who grantest great mercy unto the world!

Beholding the eternal God as an infant incarnate of her, holding Him with her hands and kissing Him often, and filled with joy, the all-immaculate one spoke unto Him: O Most High God, invisible King! How do I look upon Thee, and yet am unable to comprehend the mystery of Thy boundless poverty? For a very small cave, and that belonging to another, contains Thee within it, Who art born, and hast preserved the womb, leaving virginity unloosed, as before giving birth: and Who grantest great mercy!

While the pure one spoke these things as a servant in awe, she heard the Magi standing together before the cave, and said unto them: Whom seek ye? For I see that ye have come from a foreign land, having Persian appearance and wisdom. A strange departure and journey have ye made; and having come with haste to worship Him Who journeyed from on high and strangely dwelt in me as He knows: Who grants great mercy unto the world!

*Other stichera of the saint, Tone 8, Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (Ѡ҆ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*
Having forsaken the beauty of the world, * by grace from on high * with virtues thou didst make clear * the nobility of thy soul, * O all-praised Eugenia. * Having preserved the grace of the image untroubled by thy manner of life, * O invincible martyr, * God-like rampart of virginity, * and most noble flower of nature!

By appearance, and life, and grace, * and by the endurance of thy soul thou adornedst thyself; * thou didst lead armies of sufferers * and an assembly of virgins * unto Him Who shone forth from the Virgin, * and Who manifestly opened the entrance of martyrdom unto all, * O all-wise Eugenia. * Together with them do thou now implore Him, * that He may save thy flock.

The Disposer of Righteousness, * as a pure virgin * and as a glorious martyr, * adorned thee splendidly with twofold crowns: * having granted thee a fair bridal chamber, * illuminated with manifestations of light: * wherein having taken up thy dwelling, * O bride of Christ, * with eternal blessedness * Thou hast now manifestly been enriched.

*Glory, both now, of the forefeast, Tone 2:*
Behold, the time of our salvation is drawn near; * make ready, O cave, the Virgin draws near to give birth! * O Bethlehem, land of Judah, dance and be glad, * for out of thee our Lord has shone forth![^281] * Give ear, ye mountains and hills, * and ye surrounding regions of Judea, * for Christ comes: * that as Lover of mankind * He may save man whom He fashioned!

*At the Aposticha, stichera of the forefeast, Tone 4, Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Всехва́льнїи мꙋ́ченицы):*
Bringing gifts unto Thee, O Son, * the eastern kings came, * knowing Thee to be born a King: * frankincense, and myrrh, and gold: * and behold, they stand before the doors. * Command them * to see Thee as an infant * held in my arms, * Who art older than ancient Adam.

*Verse:*
God shall come from the south, * and the Holy One from a mountain overshadowed and densely wooded.[^282]

Come, see with diligence, * the Virgin of old said unto the Magi: * and behold the Invisible One, * Who has manifestly appeared as visible, * and become an infant! * And they with zeal * entered and worshipped, * and brought gifts: * fulfilling the divine prophecy.

*Verse: O Lord, I have heard Thy report, and was afraid; O Lord, I considered Thy works, and was astonished.*[^283]

I bear Thee as an infant in my hands, * Who bearest all things; * and I am astonished, said the unwedded one: * how shall I nourish Thee with milk, * Who nourishest all? * O my Son and my Creator, * I glorify Thine immeasurable condescension * unto men: * whereby Thou wilt save the perishing world!

*Glory, both now, of the forefeast, Tone 6:*
Triumph, O Zion; be glad, O Jerusalem, city of Christ God: receive the Creator contained in the cave and manger. Open unto me the gates, and having entered therein I shall see wrapped in swaddling bands as an infant Him Who holds holding creation in His palm: Whom the angels hymn with unceasing voice, the Life-giving Lord Who saves our race.

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
Once, Mary was enrolled with the elder Joseph in Bethlehem, as being of the seed of David, bearing in her womb the seedless Offspring; and the time came for the birth, and there was no place in the inn: but as a beautiful palace, the cave was shown unto the Queen. Christ is born, to raise up the image that had fallen of old!

*At Compline, the Canon, whereof the acrostic is: "Today I hymn the Great Sabbath."*[^284]
*The Heirmoi are sung twice, and the Troparia unto 6. Tone 6.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Him Who covered the pursuing tyrant in the surge of the sea of old, Herod seeks to slay as He is hidden in a manger; but let us sing with the Magi: Let us sing unto the Lord, for He is gloriously glorified![^285]

*Troparion:*
O Lord my God, a nativity hymn and a forefeast song shall I sing unto Thee, Who by Thy divine birth grantest rebirth unto me, and leadest me back unto the original nobility.

*Troparion:*
Knowing Thee on high upon the throne and below in the manger, O my Savior, celestial and earthly beings marveled at Thy dominion; for Thou wast marvelous beyond understanding, two-fold in nature, God-man!

*Troparion:*
That Thou mightest fill all things with Thy glory, having bowed the heavens, Thou camest down upon the earth;[^286] as rain upon the fleece didst Thou descend into the virginal womb,[^287] from whence Thou comest now to be born twofold, both God and man.

*And at the end, the Heirmos is sung by both choirs together.*
*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Beholding Thee Who suspended all the earth unheld upon the waters born in the cave, creation was shaken with awe, crying aloud: There is none holy save Thee, O Lord![^288]

*Troparion:*
Manifesting the types of Thine ineffable incarnation, O Compassionate One, Thou didst multiply visions and inspire prophecies: which having now come Thou hast fulfilled, being born in the flesh of the pure Maiden in the city of David.

*Troparion:*
The earth spread out its shoulders and receives the Creator, Who receives glory from the angels, a star from the heavens, praise from the shepherds, gifts from the Magi, and acknowledgment from all the world.

*Troparion:*
The riddles of the astrologer-magus Balaam are now fulfilled: for a star has shone forth out of Jacob, and guided the kings, the Magi from Persia, bringing gifts unto the Sun of Glory.[^289]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Foreseeing Thy coming from the Virgin, Habakkuk cried aloud in awe: Becoming incarnate from the south, Thou art come, O Deliverer, to recall banished Adam![^290]

*Troparion:*
Now the Lord draws near and comes, the Expectation of the nations and the Salvation of the world:[^291] prepare the cave, O city of Bethlehem; and ye shepherds, running together with the Magi, sing praises!

*Troparion:*
By the power of the Godhead Thou hast commingled Thyself with men in an unconfused union: in the likeness of flesh, O Savior, Thou renewest Adam, and by Thine assumption dost save him.

*Troparion:*
The Word, being manifested, clothes Himself in flesh, and dwells among us by ineffable providence; come, ye faithful, let us behold His glory, as of the Only-begotten from God the Father![^292]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Seeing the never-setting light of Thy divine manifestation, O Christ, which graciously came to pass unto us, Isaiah, rising early from the night, cried aloud: Behold, a Virgin shall conceive in the womb, and bring forth the incarnate Word, and all earth-born men shall rejoice![^293]

*Troparion:*
Thou makest new things for the earth-born, having become dust, O Creator! The manger, the swaddling bands, and the cave are symbols of Thy humility; and the betrothed of Thy Mother, Thy reputed father according to the flesh, now accomplishes the counsel of the Father Who begot Thee.

*Troparion:*
By myrrh they foreshadow death, by gold royal dominion, and by frankincense the pre-eminence of the Godhead: the kings of the Gentiles, offering firstfruits of gifts unto Thee, born in the Bethlehem cave of an unwedded Mother.

*Troparion:*
Having come forth from an unwedded one, O Word co-eternal with the Father, Thou didst dwell bodily in the cave, accounting the manger as a throne: and by Thy fearful dispensation Thou astonishest the Magi and shepherds, and didst fill the angels with awe: glory to Thy dominion!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Jonah was swallowed but not held fast in the belly of the sea-monster; for bearing the image of Thee Who wast born and manifested in the flesh, he came forth from the beast as from a bridal chamber! For being born now in the flesh, Thou didst will to enter into the tomb and death, and to rise again on the third day.[^294]

*Troparion:*
Perished now and broken down is the middle wall of the ancient enmity by Thy coming in the flesh, O Christ, and the fiery sword turns its back unto all;[^295] and faithfully partaking of the life-bearing Tree of Eden, I am straightway shown forth as a cultivator of the gardens of immortality!

*Troparion:*
Hades reigned together with sin from Adam even unto Thee;[^296] but their shameless tyranny is brought to ruin, as Thou art born in the flesh, O Deliverer, of the tribe of David, and as Thou sittest upon the throne of his kingdom in the latter times, reigning unto the ages!

*Troparion:*
Cruel Herod was shown to be a slayer of children, but not a slayer of Christ; for though he bitterly mowed down the infants as grass, he was not able to seize and slay the Ear of Life; for being the Giver of life, He hid Himself as God from the pursuer by divine power.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
An ineffable wonder! He Who delivered the holy children from the flame in the furnace reclines as an infant in a poor manger, for the salvation of us who sing: Blessed art Thou, O God our Deliverer![^297]

*Troparion:*
The deceitful enemy was wounded, seeing God lying as an infant in a humble manger, and is slain by the mighty divine hand, for the salvation of us who sing: Blessed art Thou, O God our Deliverer!

*Troparion:*
Blessed is the manger! For having received the Creator into itself as an infant, it was shown to be as the Cherubic throne, for the salvation of us who sing: Blessed art Thou, O God our Deliverer!

*Troparion:*
By human law Thou acceptest to be laid in swaddling bands, having appeared as an infant: whereby Thou loosest the bonds of our transgressions, granting freedom unto those who cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God our Deliverer!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Be astonished and tremble, O heaven, and let the foundations of the earth be shaken! For behold, He that holds all things in His palm is wrapped in swaddling bands, and is sheltered as a stranger in a small manger! Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages![^298]

*Troparion:*
Bound Adam is loosed, and freedom is granted unto all the faithful, as Thou, O Savior, art wrapped in swaddling bands, and laid in a small cave and in a manger of dumb beasts. Therefore rejoicing, with faith we offer a forefeast hymn unto Thee at Thy birth!

*Troparion:*
The Persian delusion has ceased; for the eastern kings, the star-gazers, bring gifts unto Christ the King of all Who is born: gold and myrrh with frankincense: * Whom ye children, bless; * ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
O new wonders! O goodness! O ineffable forbearance! For behold, He that dwells in the highest is accounted as an infant; and God willingly flees from Herod: Whom ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Marvel not now, O Mother, seeing as an infant Him Whom the Father begot from the womb before the morning star; for I have manifestly come to raise up and glorify together with Myself fallen human nature, which magnifies thee with faith and love.[^299]

*Troparion:*
In Thy strange birth, having escaped pangs supernaturally, I was called blessed, O Son without beginning; but now seeing Thee fleeing from Herod, I am troubled in soul by the sword of sorrow, crying aloud: Save those who honor Thee![^300]

*Troparion:*
Into the land of Egypt I indeed go, but the hand-made idols of Egypt, O Mother, I will cast down with an earthquake;[^301] and all the enemies that seek My life I will send into hades; as the only Sovereign One, I will exalt and save those who honor thee!

*Troparion:*
Let creation rejoice, for the Creator is being created, and He Who was before is now known as the new God! Let the Magi come to meet Him with gifts; let the shepherds clap their hands in faith at the wonder; and let men be glad with the angels!

*At Matins, on "God is the Lord", the Troparion of the forefeast, thrice. After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 6, Podoben: "The angelic hosts" (А҆́ггелскїя си́лы):*
The prophetic utterances are now fulfilled: for our God is born on the morrow of the Virgin Mary, beyond word, and remains as He was before giving birth! The Magi gather together, bringing gifts; the shepherds play their pipes: let us also sing in accompaniment: O Lord Who wast born of the Virgin, glory to Thee! *Glory, both now, the same.*

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8:*
Transforming the songs of the shepherds' pipes, the angelic army cried aloud, saying unto them: Cease playing your pipes, ye leaders over the flocks of the pastured; cry aloud, singing: For Christ the Lord is born, Who as God was well pleased to save the human race! *Glory, both now, the same.*

*Canon of the forefeast with the Heirmos unto 8, and of the saint unto 4. Canon of the Forefeast.*

*The acrostic whereof is:*
*According to the alphabet.*[^302]
*A composition of Joseph. Tone 2.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
*The exceedingly equipped power of old overwhelmed the Pharaoh-led host in the deep; and the Word made flesh has consumed all-malicious sin; the all-glorified Lord, for He is gloriously glorified.*[^303]
*Troparia:*
*Thou wast enrolled by Caesar's decree, O Sovereign King, wishing to enroll man in the book of life;[^304] for marvelously Thou hast come unto Thine own, calling unto Heaven him who had been bitterly estranged from Paradise.*
*Receive Christ, O Bethlehem, for He who is incarnate comes unto thee, opening Eden unto me. Make ready, O cave, for thou shalt see the Incomprehensible One contained within thee most gloriously, now impoverished through the wealth of His tender mercy.*
*Christ comes to be born, as God granting marvelous rebirth unto those sprung from Adam. Rejoice, O barren wilderness, the whole nature of earthborn men; for the Master is come to make thee fruitful with many children.*[^305]
*Canon of the Saint.*
*A composition of Theophanes.*
*The acrostic whereof is:*
*I sing outstandingly in hymns the great glory of Eugenia.*[^306]
*Ode 1. The same Heirmos:*
*Troparia:*
*O Eugenia, martyr of Christ, now dancing joyfully with the angelic hosts, as a virgin undefiled and as an all-rich, crown-bearing martyr, pray that grace be granted unto those who hymn thee with love.*
*Having listened to the divine chanting, O bride of Christ, Thou wast winged toward exalted nobility; for like light the theology of the Spirit's songs shone in thy heart, driving away all godlessness.*
*Thy mind, having forgotten female nature, ran toward manly deeds, having grown courageous through grace; and being guided providently unto God, O martyr Eugenia, who art the namesake of divine nobility.*[^307]
*Illumined with spiritual light, O divinely wise maiden, thou didst make thyself partaker of a more abundant radiance; whereof do thou now, by thy supplications, deem worthy those who hymn thee, delivering them from sin, O all-blessed martyr Eugenia.*
*Theotokion:*
*Having been slain by the orchard of knowledge, O pure Virgin, by the Tree of Life, Christ God, Who sprouted forth from thee beyond understanding, O Theotokos, we faithful have been called back unto life; unto Whom with boldness pray with boldness that our souls be saved.*
*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
*The wilderness has blossomed like a lily, O Lord, the barren Church of the Gentiles, by Thy coming, wherein my heart is established.*[^308]
*Troparia:*
*Delivering me from evil bonds, O Lord, Thou comest as an infant wrapped in swaddling bands, O Lover of mankind; I bow down before Thy divine condescension.*
*The Virgin comes to give birth unto Thee, Who art outside of time and hast timelessly shone forth from the Father, releasing the temporal passions of our souls.*
*Seeking me, who had strayed through transgression, Thou hast made a cave Thy dwelling as Heaven, preparing for me the mansions yonder, O compassionate and most merciful One.*[^309]
*Another. Heirmos:*
*Having established me upon the rock of faith, Thou hast enlarged my mouth against my enemies. For my spirit rejoiced in singing: None is holy as our God, and none is righteous beside Thee, O Lord.*[^310]
*Troparia:*
*As a blameless sacrifice unto the Master thou didst offer thyself, with most perfect mind, and didst cast away corruptible wealth, crying out, O all-wise maiden: Thou art our God, and none is holy beside Thee, O Lord.*
*Bright was thy purity made known, and the strength of thy sufferings shone forth; for thou didst make action the ascent unto contemplation,[^311] crying out: Thou art our God, and none is holy beside Thee, O Lord.*
*Possessed with desire for chastity, thou didst preserve the boast of purity; thou wast a dwelling acceptable unto Wisdom, crying out unto Christ: Thou art our God, and none is holy beside Thee, O Lord.*
*Theotokion:*
*Let us hymn the all-pure Mother, the Theotokos, who appeared as the mediatress of salvation, O divinely wise, and let us cry out: None is pure as thou art, O all-pure one, and none is blameless beside thee, O Theotokos.*
*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8. Podoben: "Of Wisdom:" (Премꙋ́дрости:)*
*Having practiced self-control in the labors of ascetical struggle, thou wast glorified by martyrly contests, having led many who are saved unto thy Creator. For having forsaken temporal things through divine love, thou didst accomplish manly feats, O glorious maiden. Therefore after thy repose thou didst find endless life, ever abiding with thy Bridegroom, O Eugenia equal to the angels. Intercede with Christ God that He grant remission of transgressions unto those who honor with love thy most holy memory with love.*
*Glory..., Both now...:*
*The earth was shown unto me today as Heaven, for upon it the Creator is born and reclines in a manger, in Bethlehem of Judah. With the angels the shepherds sing unceasingly: "Glory in the highest, peace on earth;"[^312] for they saw the star traveling with the Magi, who ran swiftly to offer gifts: gold, myrrh, and frankincense, as unto God Who is over all, the eternal King, and the Creator of all things, Who through tender compassion is born in a cave.*
*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
*Thou hast come from a Virgin, not an intercessor nor an angel, but Thyself, O Lord, incarnate, and hast saved the whole of me, man. Therefore I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lord.*[^313]
*Troparia:*
*O creation, cast off now all growing old, seeing thy Creator created and renewing thee, having become an infant, and leading thee back unto thy first beauty.*
*The Magi hastened,[^314] guided by the divine star, and saw the Sun rising from the virginal cloud, and offered gifts unto Him.*
*Behold, the Virgin comes as a heifer, bearing in her womb the fatted Calf,[^315] Who takes away the sins of the world; let creation rejoice, keeping feast.*
*The proclamations of the prophets announcing Christ's manifestation have received today a saving fulfillment; for He is come in the flesh to enlighten those who are in distress in darkness.*
*Another. The same Heirmos:*
*Troparia:*
*Thou hast come, incarnate from a Virgin, O Most High, having betrothed unto Thyself the assemblies of virgins who have loved Thee alone, the renowned virginal Bridegroom.*
*Thou didst strip off the veil of carnal birth; and in baptism, O all-glorious martyr, thou didst radiantly put on the incorruptible garment of regeneration.*[^316]
*A light-bearing ray shone in thy heart, driving away the outpoured darkness of deception by the flash of grace, O martyr of Christ Eugenia, noble virgin.*
*Splendidly and beautifully didst thou illuminate thy life, first having withered the carnal passions by self-control, and thereafter shining most radiantly by suffering, O Eugenia.*
*Theotokion:*
*Thou hast become higher than the angels, O all-immaculate maiden, having given birth unto the Angel of Great Counsel of the Father,[^317] Who became man through His abundant tender mercy, the Lover of mankind.*
*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

*Thou hast become a Mediator between God and men, O Christ God; for through Thee, O Master, we have access unto Thy Father, the Source of Light, out of the night of ignorance.*[^318]
*Troparia:*
*Let the people who once sat in darkness see the unwaning Light that has shone forth;[^319] Whom the star of old announced unto the kings from Persia who worshiped fire.*
*The great King hastens to enter a small cave, that He might magnify me who was abased, and through His immeasurable wealth might enrich me who was impoverished, being pre-eminently divine.*
*Now from Jacob, as Balaam said, Christ is born;[^320] He instructs the Gentiles, and by grace His Kingdom shall be exalted, abiding without succession.*
*Another. Heirmos:*
*The illumination of those lying in darkness, the salvation of the despairing, O Christ my Savior: unto Thee do I rise early, O King of peace; illumine me with Thy radiance, for beside Thee I know no other God.*[^321]
*Troparia:*
*Seeing thy course directed toward salvation, O passion-bearer, the soul-destroying serpent raised diverse temptations against thee, attempting to weaken thy strength. But him, O divinely wise and pure maiden, thou didst trample down.*
*All-fair didst thou appear unto the Giver of good things and Benefactor, and the Bridegroom of souls, Christ, adorned among ascetics with self-control, and radiant with martyrly suffering, O martyr Eugenia of Christ, noble virgin.*
*A crown of graces was placed upon thy head, for thou didst honor wisdom with divine understanding; having despised ancestral wealth and glory, and with fortitude thou didst follow thy beloved Bridegroom, O all-honored maiden.*
*Theotokion:*
*Life having shone forth unto the world from thee, O Parent of God, calls back unto everlasting life by communion those who were formerly held by death, who cry in faith: Beside Thee we know no other God.*
*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
*Wallowing in the abyss of sin, I call upon the unfathomable abyss of Thy tender mercy: lead me up from corruption, O God.*[^322]
*Troparia:*
*In marvelous manner Christ comes unto His own;[^323] let us estrange ourselves from sins and receive Him Who dwells in meek souls.*
*In no wise shalt thou be least among cities, O Bethlehem;*[^324]

*...for in thee is born the King and Lord, to shepherd a rich people.*
*How shall a small cave receive Thee, Whom the world cannot contain, O Incomprehensible One? How shalt Thou be seen as an infant, Who art co-unoriginate with the Father?*
*Another. The same Heirmos:*
*Troparia:*
*Thou didst give no slumber unto thine eyelids, until thou hadst quenched all voluptuousness,[^325] and didst make thyself a pure dwelling for thy Creator.*
*Having rivaled the Egyptian woman in disposition, she who was blackened in deed and name rushed to slander thy honorable life, O all-honored maiden.*[^326]
*Having displayed steadfast brightness, and having been enriched with the grace of healings through the wealth of faith, thou didst become the teacher of an assembly of monastics.*
*Theotokion:*
*Mystically were all the prophets taught concerning thine ineffable giving of birth, O all-pure one, prefiguring it spiritually and foretelling future things unto all.*
*Kontakion, Tone 3. Podoben: "Today the Virgin:" (Дв҃а дне́сь:)*
*Today the Virgin comes to give birth ineffably in a cave unto the pre-eternal Word: rejoice, O inhabited world, having heard it; glorify with the angels and the shepherds Him Who desires to appear, a young Child, the pre-eternal God.*[^327]
*Ikos:*
*The sacred utterances of the prophets have received their end: for behold, the Virgin gives birth unto the All-perfect One in the city of Bethlehem, within the cave. Let all creation be made new, rejoice and dance: the Master of all is come to dwell with servants, delivering us who were brought down by corruption from an alien dominion; and He is seen as an infant, wrapped in swaddling bands in a manger: a young Child, the pre-eternal God.*
*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
*The God-opposing command of the lawless tyrant raised a high flame, but Christ spread out spiritual dew unto the pious youths, He Who is blessed and all-glorious.*[^328]
*Troparia:*
*Let the clouds drop down water from above,[^329] for He Who makes the clouds His chariot is borne by the Virgin as a cloud: the unwaning Light comes to shine upon those formerly darkened and in distress.*
*The host of divine angels is made ready to hymn the ineffable condescension of the Lord: overtake Him, O Magi; hasten, O shepherds; He is come unto Whom it pertained,[^330] Christ, the Expectation of the nations and their deliverance.*
*What is this strange and most great wonder? How shall I carry Thee, Who upholdest all things by Thy word?[^331] O ineffable birthgiving, O my unoriginate Son, said the all-pure Virgin, holding Christ in her hands with awe.*
*Another. The same Heirmos:*
*Troparia:*
*Thou didst explain unto all the truth of the divinely inspired Scriptures, having made thy female nature manly, and most gloriously didst astonish all, O honored maiden: who didst lead brightly unto Christ those who believed, O all-rich one.*
*Plainly didst thou refute idolatrous frenzy, O all-praised maiden, by thy divine teachings; and having betrothed an unnumbered, radiant multitude of virgins unto Christ Who reigns over all, through martyrly blood.*
*Seeing thy light-bearing life, the glorious Basilla divinely emulated it and betrothed herself unto Christ, forsaking all carnal voluptuousness; and now she has been deemed worthy of martyrly joy.*[^332]
*Theotokion:*
*Thou hast healed the deadly pasture,[^333] having seedlessly given birth unto hypostatic Life, O all-immaculate Virgin, pure Parent of God. Therefore rejoicing we call thee the fountain of immortality.*
*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
*The fiery furnace of old in Babylon divided its operation by divine command, consuming the Chaldeans, but bedewing the faithful, who sang: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord.*[^334]
*Troparia:*
*The undefiled Virgin, beholding the truly ineffable height of the mystery of Him Who covered the heavens with understanding,[^335] marveled and said: The heavenly throne that holds Thee is flaming, and how, O my Son, shall I carry Thee?*
*Bearing the Father's likeness, O my Son, how hast Thou impoverished Thyself and taken the likeness of a servant?[^336] How shall I lay Thee down in a manger of dumb beasts, Who deliverest all from irrationality? I hymn Thy tender mercy.*
*Rejoice, all the earth! Behold, Christ draws near to be born in Bethlehem; let the sea be glad, let the choir of prophets leap for joy, seeing today the fulfillment of their words, and rejoice, all ye righteous!*
*Another. Heirmos:*
*Unto Him Who descended into the fiery furnace unto the Hebrew youths, and changed the flame into dew Who changed the flame into dew: hymn the works of the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.*[^337]
*Troparia:*
*In the river youthfully, and in the fire patiently wast thou tried;[^338] for with fortitude thou didst pass through contrary elements, crying: Hymn Christ, ye works of the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.*
*Appearing marvelously unto Thee when thou wast kept in prison, Christ fed Thee abundantly; and through His Nativity He united Thee unto the heavenly hosts as thou glorifiest Him unto the ages.*[^339]
*Thy Bridegroom gorgeously adorns thee with twofold crowns, O divinely wise Eugenia; and as the Righteous One He justly grants thee a radiant bridal chamber. Supremely exalt Him unto all ages.*
*The divine grace, having shone upon thee with light, now illumines thee in heavenly mansions; do thou unceasingly pray, O divinely wise maiden, that those who celebrate thy memory be filled therewith.*
*Theotokion:*
*We know thee, O Theotokos, as the fountain of immortal dawn, as having given birth unto the Word of the immortal Father, Who delivers from death all those who supremely exalt Him unto the ages.*
*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
*The Son of the unoriginate Begetter, God and Lord, incarnate of the Virgin, has appeared unto us, to enlighten those in darkness, to gather the dispersed; therefore the all-hymned Theotokos do we magnify.*[^340]
*Troparia:*
*Let all earthly kingdoms sing, rejoicing, and let the tribes of the nations be glad; let the mountains and valleys and hills, the rivers, the sea, and all creation magnify the Lord now born.*[^341]
*Thou wast seen as far as it was possible for the prophets to see Thee; and in the last times, having become man, Thou hast appeared unto all men in the city of Bethlehem of Judah, the star revealing Thee ineffably unto the astrologers.*
*"O sweetest Child, how shall I nourish Thee Who nourishest all? How shall I hold Thee Who holdest all things by Thy beck? And how shall I wrap Thee in swaddling bands, Who wrappest the whole earth in mist?"[^342] cried the all-pure Sovereign Lady, whom unceasingly we magnify.*
*Another. The same Heirmos:*
*Troparia:*
*Dwelling in the heavenly mansions, O glorious maiden, now hast thou plainly been deemed worthy of the sweetness of Paradise with the virgins, as a most true martyr; and with the martyrs as an all-immaculate virgin, O all-blessed Eugenia.*

*Thou hast obtained thy desire beyond mind and understanding, standing radiantly before the Utmost of desires;[^343] and shining clearly with the light-beaming rays of the Source Trinity, O divinely wise Eugenia, noble virgin.*
*Holding the unquenchable lamp of virginity,[^344] thou wast adorned with a martyr's crown; and now cease not to pray, that those who piously honor thee with love be saved through thy prayers, O all-glorious Eugenia.*
*Thou hast now gone forth unto divine refreshment, O all-valiant maiden, having passed through the intolerable fire of wounds, and the surging water of temptations, O martyr Eugenia;[^345] intercede therefore with Christ that He save our souls.*
*Theotokion:*
*Having conceived in thy womb the heavenly rain as a fleece, O all-immaculate maiden, thou didst give birth unto Him Who grants immortality unto us who piously hymn Him and magnify thee, the all-immaculate Theotokos.*[^346]
*Exapostilarion of the Forefeast. Podoben: "With the Disciples:" (Со оу҆чн҃ки:)*
*He Who dwells in unapproachable light, and upholds all things, through His ineffable tender mercy is born of a Virgin, and is wrapped in swaddling bands as an infant, and reclines in a cave and in a manger of dumb beasts;[^347] let us hasten with speed to come unto Bethlehem to worship Him with the Magi, bearing as gifts the fruits of outstanding deeds.*
*Glory..., Both now...:*
*Let us faithful offer singing unto the Virgin Mary; for behold, she now comes into the city of Bethlehem to give birth unto Christ the Savior. Therefore, O Magi, run with gifts and with the star, and worship with us; O shepherds, hasten to cry out with the angels unto Him Who is born: Glory to Thee Who liest in the cave and the manger!*
*At the Praises, Stichera, Tone 6. On 4. Podoben: "Go before, ye Angelic Powers:" (А҆́гг҃льскїя предиди́те:)*
*A star has shone forth from Jacob in the cave;[^348] come, let us also, celebrating the forefeast, run with the Magi, let us go with the shepherds and see God in swaddling bands, let us see the Virgin suckling Him. O awesome sight! Christ the King of Israel comes!*
*With hymns the angelic choir now honors thee, the radiant and unwedded Mother, and rejoicing dances at thy childbearing, O all-pure one. Rejoice, hope of the Orthodox; rejoice, protection of those who hymn thee. Therefore let us say: Blessed is He Who is come, our God, glory to Thee!*

*"A Flower shall come forth from the root of Jesse,"[^349] was proclaimed by the radiant prophet; for we see the Virgin who through the Spirit has supernaturally given birth in a cave unto the lovely Rose, Who is co-enthroned with the Father in the highest. Ye peoples, let us say: Blessed is He Who is come, our God, glory to Thee!*
*Today Adam is called back from deception, and from the gloomy deceit of the adversary; for Christ is incarnate of the Virgin as man, Who having renewed Adam has taken away the curse through the Virgin. Ye peoples, let us say: Blessed is He Who is come, our God, glory to Thee!*
*Glory..., Tone and Podoben: the same (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*
*Build, O Bethlehem, prepare the things of the Nativity; come, O Joseph, be enrolled with Mary; O all-honored manger, O God-bearing swaddling bands! Wherein Life, having wrapped Himself, shall burst the bonds of death, binding men unto incorruption, Christ our God.*
*Both now..., Podoben: the same (Подо́бенъ то́йже):*
*O blessed womb of the Maiden of God, which was mentally shown to be greater than Heaven! For Him Whom the heavens cannot contain, thou dost contain, carrying Him within thyself. O blessed breasts of the Virgin, which Christ sucks, He Who nourishes every breath,[^350] having fashioned flesh for Himself in the husbandless womb of the Maiden!*
*At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Forefeast, Tone 2. Podoben: "O House of Ephratha:" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ:)*
*Thou hast been shown to be the house of the Creator of all, O Virgin, for having made His abode in thee, the Lord of glory now comes forth to be born.*
*Verse: God shall come from Theman, and the Holy One from the mountain overshadowed and dense.*[^351]
*A young Child in Bethlehem from the Virgin, the pre-eternal God, is born in a manger of dumb beasts: O wonder!*
*Verse: O Lord, I have heard Thy report, and was afraid; O Lord, I considered Thy works, and was astonished.*[^352]
*Ye noetic angelic ranks, with the shepherds and with the Magi, sing unto God in the highest, unto Him Who is born: Glory to Thee!*
*Glory..., Podoben: the same (Подо́бенъ то́йже):*
*Glory to Thee, Father, Son, and Spirit, by Whom an awesome mystery was arranged, for the rebirth of men.*
*Both now..., Podoben: the same (Подо́бенъ то́йже):*
*Rejoice, O Virgin Theotokos, who hast given birth unto the Life of the world from the Holy Spirit, unto the deliverance of all.*
*It is fitting to know: If the Sunday before the Nativity of Christ, of the Holy Fathers, falls on the 24th day of December.*[^353]

And a combined tone is performed.*[^358] *Glory..., of the Fathers, Tone 8: "Of legal teachings;" Both now..., "Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos:"*
