Communion hymn: "Praise the Lord from the heavens;"*[^364] *Another: "Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous."*[^365]
*It is fitting to know concerning the Hours on the Eve of the Nativity of Christ. Note:*
*If the Nativity of Christ falls on a Sunday or on a Monday, we sing the Hours beforehand on Friday. But if the Nativity of Christ falls on a Tuesday, on a Wednesday, on a Thursday, on a Friday, or on a Saturday, we sing the Hours on the Eve.*[^366]

*The Order of the Hours Sung on the Eve of the Nativity of Christ.*
*At the beginning of the second hour,*[^367] *the bell is sounded. And when we have assembled in church, the priest vests in phelonion, and the deacon in sticharion. And the paraecclesiarch places an analogion, adorned, opposite the holy doors, and lights a candle upon the candle-stand. The priest goes forth with the Gospel into the nave, or into the trapeza, through the holy doors, the deacon preceding him with the censer. And the priest places the Holy Gospel upon the analogion, and standing before the analogion he makes the beginning according to custom. And after the beginning, the reader:*
*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee. O Heavenly King... and the rest. And after the exclamation, the priest censes the Holy Gospel upon the analogion round about, and the other icons, and the whole temple, and the superior, and the brethren.*
*And the reader reads Psalm 5:*
*Give ear to my words, O Lord; consider my cry. Attend to the voice of my supplication, my King, and my God; for unto Thee will I pray, O Lord. In the morning Thou shalt hear my voice; in the morning I will stand before Thee, and shalt look up. For Thou art not a God that willest iniquity; neither shall the evil-doer dwell with Thee, nor shall the transgressors remain before Thine eyes. Thou hast hated all that work iniquity; Thou shalt destroy all that speak lies. The Lord abhors the man of blood and deceit. But as for me, in the multitude of Thy mercy I will enter into Thy house; I will worship toward Thy holy temple in Thy fear. Lead me, O Lord, in Thy righteousness; because of mine enemies, make straight my way before Thee. For there is no truth in their mouth; their heart is vain. Their throat is an open sepulchre; with their tongues they have dealt deceitfully. Judge them, O God; let them fall from their counsels. Cast them out according to the multitude of their ungodliness, for they have provoked Thee, O Lord. And let all that put their trust in Thee rejoice; they shall exult unto ages, and Thou shalt dwell among them. And all that love Thy name shall boast in Thee; for Thou shalt bless the righteous man. O Lord, as with a shield of good will hast Thou crowned us.*[^368]
*Psalm 44:*[^369]
*My heart has poured forth a good word; I speak of my works unto the King. My tongue is the pen of a swiftly writing scribe. Thou art comely in beauty beyond the sons of men; grace has been poured forth upon Thy lips;*

*therefore God has blessed Thee unto ages. Gird Thy sword upon Thy thigh, O Mighty One, in Thy comeliness and in Thy beauty; and bend Thy bow, and prosper, and reign, for the sake of truth, and meekness, and righteousness; and Thy right hand shall guide Thee wonderfully. Thine arrows are sharp, O Mighty One—the peoples shall fall under Thee—in the heart of the enemies of the King. Thy throne, O God, is unto ages of ages; a sceptre of uprightness is the sceptre of Thy kingdom. Thou hast loved righteousness and hated iniquity; therefore God, Thy God, has anointed Thee with the oil of gladness above Thy companions. Myrrh and stacte and cassia exhale from Thy garments, out of the ivory palaces, whereby the daughters of kings have made Thee glad in Thine honor. At Thy right hand stood the queen, arrayed in vesture of inwrought gold, adorned in varied colors.*
*Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline thine ear; and forget thine own people, and thy father's house; and the King shall greatly desire thy beauty; for He is thy Lord, and thou shalt worship Him.*[^370] *And the daughter of Tyre shall worship Him with gifts; the rich among the people shall entreat thy face. All the glory of the King's daughter is within, clothed in gold-fringed garments, adorned in varied colors. The virgins that follow after her shall be brought unto the King; those near unto her shall be brought unto Thee. They shall be brought with gladness and rejoicing; they shall be led into the King's temple. Instead of thy fathers, sons have been born to thee; thou shalt make them princes over all the earth. I will remember thy name in every generation and generation; therefore shall the peoples confess Thee unto ages, and unto ages of ages.*[^371]
*Psalm 45:*[^372]
*God is our refuge and strength, a helper in afflictions that have found us exceedingly. Therefore we will not fear when the earth is troubled, and when the mountains are removed into the heart of the seas. Their waters roared and were troubled; the mountains were troubled by His might. The rushings of the river make glad the city of God; the Most High has sanctified His tabernacle. God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; God shall help her right early in the morning. The nations were troubled, the kingdoms leaned aside; the Most High uttered His voice, the earth was shaken. The Lord of hosts is with us; our helper is the God of Jacob. Come and behold the works of God, what wonders He has wrought upon the earth, taking away wars unto the ends of the earth. He will shatter the bow, and break the weapon, and burn the shields with fire. Be still, and know that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted upon the earth. The Lord of hosts is with us;*

*...with us; our helper is the God of Jacob.*
*Alleluia, thrice.*
*Lord, have mercy, thrice.*
*Glory..., Troparion of the Forefeast, Tone 4:*
*Enrolled was He of old with the elder Joseph, as being of the seed of David in Bethlehem, Mary bearing in her womb the seedless conception. And the time of birth was at hand, and there was no room in the inn; but as a delightful palace, the cave was shown unto the Queen. Christ is born, to raise up the image that before was fallen.*
*Both now..., Theotokion:*
*What shall we call thee, O full of grace? Heaven, for thou hast made the Sun of Righteousness to shine forth; paradise, for thou hast blossomed the Flower of incorruption; virgin, for thou hast remained undefiled; pure Mother, for thou hast held in thy holy embrace a Son, the God of all: Him do thou entreat, that He save our souls.*
*Then we sing these troparia twice.*
*The composition of Sophronius, Patriarch of Jerusalem.*[^373] *Tone 8:*
*Bethlehem, prepare thyself, let the manger make itself ready; cave, receive, the Truth has come! The shadow has passed away, and God has appeared unto men from the Virgin, having been formed as we are, and having deified the flesh. Therefore Adam is renewed with Eve, crying out: Glory..., Both now..., Good will has appeared on earth to save our race.*
*The second choir sings the same troparion, without refrain.*
*Then this verse:*
*Verse: God shall come from Theman, and the Holy One from the mountain overshadowed and dense.*[^374]
*Tone 3:*
*Now the prophetic foretelling comes to be fulfilled, which mysteriously says: And thou Bethlehem, land of Judah, art by no means the least among rulers, preparing the cave; for out of thee shall come forth for Me a Leader of the nations in the flesh, from the Virgin Maiden, Christ God, Who shall shepherd His people, the new Israel. Let us all give Him majesty!*[^375]
*Verse: O Lord, I have heard Thy report, and was afraid; O Lord, I considered Thy works, and was astonished.*[^376]
*Again the same troparion.*
*Then Glory..., Tone 8:*
*These things Joseph says unto the Virgin: O Mary, what is this matter that I behold in thee? I am at a loss and marvel, and in my mind I am terrified: therefore depart from me in secret quickly! O Mary, what is this matter that I see in thee? Shame instead of honor, sorrow instead of gladness; instead of praise, thou hast brought me reproach. No longer do I endure the reproaches of men; for I received thee blameless from the priests of the temple of the Lord, and what is this that is seen?*
*Both now..., again the same troparion.*
*Then the Prokimenon, Tone 4:*
*The Lord said unto Me: Thou art My Son, this day have I begotten Thee.*[^377]
*Verse: Ask of Me, and I will give Thee the nations for Thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for Thy possession.*[^378]
*Then the Paremia.*
*The Reading from the Prophecy of Micah (Chapter 5):*[^379]
*Thus says the Lord: And thou, Bethlehem, house of Ephratha, art thou very small to be among the thousands of Judah? For out of thee shall come forth for Me One to be a Ruler in Israel; and His goings forth have been from the beginning, from the days of eternity. Therefore shall He give them up until the time that she who is in travail has brought forth; then the rest of His brethren shall return unto the children of Israel. And He shall stand, and see, and shepherd His flock in the strength of the Lord; and they shall abide in the glory of the name of the Lord their God; for now shall they be magnified unto the ends of the earth.*
*Deacon: Wisdom!*
*The Reading from the Epistle of the Holy Apostle Paul to the Hebrews (Pericope 309):*[^380]
*Brethren, in many and various ways God spoke of old to our fathers by the prophets; but in these last days He has spoken unto us by a Son, Whom He appointed the heir of all things, through Whom also He made the worlds; Who, being the brightness of His glory and the express image of His person, and upholding all things by the word of His power, when He had by Himself made purification of our sins, sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high; having become so much better than the angels, as He has inherited a more excellent name than they. For to which of the angels did He ever say: "Thou art My Son, today I have begotten Thee"? And again: "I will be to Him a Father, and He shall be to Me a Son"? And again, when He brings the firstborn into the world, He says: "Let all God's angels worship Him." And of the angels He says: "Who makes His angels spirits, and His ministers a flame of fire." But to the Son He says: "Thy throne, O God, is unto ages of ages; a sceptre of righteousness is the sceptre of Thy kingdom. Thou hast loved righteousness and hated iniquity; therefore God, Thy God, has anointed Thee with the oil of gladness beyond Thy companions." And: "Thou, Lord, in the beginning didst lay the foundation of the earth, and the heavens are the works of Thy hands. They will perish, but Thou remainest; and they will all grow old like a garment; like a cloak Thou wilt fold them up, and they will be changed; but Thou art the same, and Thy years will not fail."*

*Deacon: Wisdom, upright, let us hear the Holy Gospel.*
*Priest: The Reading from the Holy Gospel according to Matthew (Pericope 3):*[^381]
*The birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as His mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Spirit. Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a public example, was minded to put her away privily. But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife; for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit. And she shall bring forth a Son, and thou shalt call His name JESUS; for He shall save His people from their sins." Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a Son, and they shall call His name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us." Then Joseph, being raised from sleep, did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife; and knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn Son; and he called His name JESUS.*
*We sing the Troparion:*
*Order my steps according to Thy word, and let no iniquity have dominion over me. Deliver me from the slander of men, and I will keep Thy commandments. Make Thy face to shine upon Thy servant, and teach me Thy statutes. Let my mouth be filled with Thy praise, O Lord, that I may sing of Thy glory, and of Thy majesty all the day long.*[^382]
*Then the Trisagion; and after the "Our Father":*
*Kontakion, Tone 3:*
*The Virgin this day comes to the cave to give birth ineffably unto the pre-eternal Word. Dance, O universe, having heard this; glorify with angels and shepherds Him Who is pleased to be revealed as a young Child, the pre-eternal God.*[^383]
*Lord, have mercy (40 times). And the Prayer:*
*Thou Who at all times and at every hour, in heaven and on earth, art worshipped and glorified, O Christ God, Who art long-suffering, plenteous in mercy, and most compassionate; Who lovest the righteous and hast mercy on sinners; Who callest all men to salvation through the promise of good things to come: do Thou, the same Lord, receive also our supplications in this hour, and direct our life in Thy commandments. Sanctify our souls, purify our bodies, correct our thoughts, cleanse our minds, and deliver us from all tribulation, evils, and distress;*

*...and sicknesses; hedge us about by Thy holy angels, that guarded and guided by their encampment, we may attain unto the unity of the faith, and unto the comprehension of Thine unapproachable glory. For blessed art Thou unto ages of ages. Amen.*
*Lord, have mercy (thrice).*
*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.*
*More honorable than the Cherubim, and beyond compare more glorious than the Seraphim, thee who without corruption gavest birth to God the Word, the very Theotokos, thee do we magnify.*
*In the name of the Lord, bless, father.*
*The Priest exclaims:*
*God be merciful unto us, and bless us, and cause His face to shine upon us, and have mercy on us.*[^384]
*Then this Prayer:*
*O Christ, the true Light, Who enlightenest and sanctifiest every man that comes into the world: let the light of Thy countenance be signed upon us, that in it we may see the unapproachable light; and direct our steps unto the doing of Thy commandments, by the prayers of Thy most pure Mother, and of all Thy saints. Amen.*
*THE THIRD HOUR.*
*Come, let us worship... (thrice).*
*Then Psalm 66:*[^385]
*God be merciful unto us, and bless us; cause His face to shine upon us, and have mercy on us; that we may know Thy way upon earth, Thy salvation among all nations. Let the peoples confess Thee, O God; let all the peoples confess Thee. Let the nations be glad and rejoice, for Thou shalt judge the peoples with uprightness, and shalt guide the nations upon earth. Let the peoples confess Thee, O God; let all the peoples confess Thee. The earth has yielded her increase. Bless us, O God, our God; bless us, O God, and let all the ends of the earth fear Him.*
*Psalm 86:*[^386]
*His foundations are in the holy mountains; the Lord loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob. Glorious things are spoken of thee, O city of God. I will make mention of Rahab and Babylon to them that know me. And behold, the foreigners, and Tyre, and the people of the Ethiopians: these were born there. A man will say: Mother Zion, and: A man was born in her, and: The Most High Himself has founded her. The Lord shall recount it in the books of the peoples and of the rulers, of these that were born in her. For as of them that rejoice, all our dwelling is in thee.*[^387]
*Psalm 50:*[^388]
*Have mercy on me, O God, according to Thy great mercy; and according to the multitude of Thy compassions blot out my transgression. Wash me thoroughly from mine iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin. For I know mine iniquity, and my sin is before me continually. Against Thee only have I sinned, and done evil before Thee; that Thou mightest be justified in Thy words, and conquer when Thou art judged. For behold, I was conceived in iniquities, and in sins did my mother bear me. For behold, Thou hast loved truth; the hidden and secret things of Thy wisdom hast Thou revealed unto me. Thou shalt sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed; Thou shalt wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow. Thou shalt make me to hear joy and gladness; the bones that are humbled shall rejoice. Turn away Thy face from my sins, and blot out all mine iniquities. Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within my inward parts. Cast me not away from Thy face, and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me. Restore unto me the joy of Thy salvation, and uphold me with Thy governing Spirit. I will teach transgressors Thy ways, and the ungodly shall turn back unto Thee. Deliver me from blood-guiltiness, O God, Thou God of my salvation; my tongue shall rejoice in Thy righteousness. O Lord, Thou shalt open my lips, and my mouth shall declare Thy praise. For if Thou hadst desired sacrifice, I would have given it; with whole-burnt offerings Thou wilt not be pleased. A sacrifice unto God is a broken spirit; a broken and a humbled heart God will not despise. Do good, O Lord, in Thy good pleasure unto Zion, and let the walls of Jerusalem be built. Then shalt Thou be pleased with a sacrifice of righteousness, with oblation and whole-burnt offerings; then shall they offer bullocks upon Thine altar.*
*Glory..., Both now..., Alleluia (thrice).*
*Lord, have mercy (thrice).*
*Glory..., Troparion, Tone 4:*
*Enrolled was He of old with the elder Joseph, as being of the seed of David in Bethlehem, Mary bearing in her womb the seedless conception. And the time of birth was at hand, and there was no room in the inn; but as a delightful palace, the cave was shown unto the Queen. Christ is born, to raise up the image that before was fallen.*
*Both now..., Theotokion:*
*O Theotokos, thou art the true vine that hast budded forth for us the Fruit of life: we entreat thee, intercede, O Sovereign Lady, with the holy apostles, that He have mercy on our souls.*
*Then we sing these troparia twice.*
*Tone 6:*
*This is our God, no other shall be compared unto Him, Who was born of the Virgin and dwelt among men! In a poor manger, the only-begotten Son is seen lying as a man, and the Lord of glory is wrapped in swaddling clothes, and a star announces Him unto the Magi to worship Him; and we sing: O Holy Trinity, save our souls! (Twice).*
*Then we sing, Tone 8:*
*Verse: God shall come from Theman, and the Holy One from the mountain overshadowed and dense.*[^389]
*Before Thy Nativity, looking with trembling upon Thy mystery, O Lord, the intelligent hosts were astonished; for Thou Who hast adorned the heavens with stars wast well pleased to be born as an infant, and in a manger of dumb beasts Thou dost recline, Who holdest all the ends of the earth in Thy hand! For by such a dispensation Thy tender compassion has been made known, O Christ: Great is Thy mercy, glory to Thee!*
*Verse: O Lord, I have heard Thy report, and was afraid; O Lord, I considered Thy works, and was astonished.*[^390]
*And again we sing the same troparion.*
*Then Glory..., Tone 3:*
*Tell us, Joseph, how is it that from the Holy of Holies thou bringest a Virgin not barren into Bethlehem? I, he said, have searched the prophets, and having received a message from an angel, I have been assured that Mary shall give birth ineffably unto God; and to worship Him the Magi shall come from the east, serving Him with precious gifts. O Thou Who wast incarnate for our sake: Lord, glory to Thee!*
*Both now..., again the same troparion.*
*Prokimenon, Tone 4:*
*Unto us a Child is born, a Son, and unto us is given.*[^391]
*Verse: Whose government is upon His shoulder.*[^392]
*The Reading from the Prophecy of Jeremiah (Baruch, Chapter 3):*[^393]
*This is our God, and no other shall be compared unto Him. He found out all the way of knowledge, and gave it unto Jacob His servant, and unto Israel His beloved. Afterward He appeared upon earth, and conversed with men. This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endures unto ages. All they that hold it fast shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die. Turn thee, O Jacob, and take hold of it; walk in the presence of the light thereof, unto its brightness. Give not thine honor to another, nor the things that are profitable unto thee to a strange nation. O Israel, happy are we, for things that are pleasing unto God are made known unto us.*[^394]
*Then the Apostle:*
*The Reading from the Epistle of the Holy Apostle Paul to the Galatians (Pericope 208):*[^395]
*Brethren, before faith came, we were kept under guard by the law, shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed. Therefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith. But after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster. For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus. For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female; for ye are all one in Christ Jesus. And if ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise.*
*Deacon: Wisdom, upright, let us hear the Holy Gospel.*
*Priest: The Reading from the Holy Gospel according to Luke (Pericope 5):*[^396]
*In those days, there went out a decree from Caesar Augustus, that all the world should be taxed. (And this taxing was first made when Cyrenius was governor of Syria.) And all went to be taxed, every one into his own city. And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judea, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem (because he was of the house and lineage of David), to be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child. And so it was, that, while they were there, the days were accomplished that she should be delivered. And she brought forth her firstborn Son, and wrapped Him in swaddling clothes, and laid Him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn. And there were in the same country shepherds abiding in the field, keeping watch over their flock by night. And lo, the angel of the Lord came upon them, and the glory of the Lord shone round about them, and they were sore afraid. And the angel said unto them: "Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people. For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Savior, Which is Christ the Lord. And this shall be a sign unto you: Ye shall find the Babe wrapped in swaddling clothes, lying in a manger." And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host praising God, and saying: "Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men." And it came to pass, as the angels were gone away from them into heaven, the shepherds said one to another: "Let us now go even unto Bethlehem, lehem, and see this thing that is come to pass, which the Lord has made known unto us." And they came with haste, and found Mary and Joseph, and the Babe lying in a manger. And when they had seen it, they made known abroad the saying which was told them concerning this Child. And all they that heard it wondered at those things which were told them by the shepherds. But Mary kept all these things, and pondered them in her heart. And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things that they had heard and seen, as it was told unto them.*[^397]
*Then:*
*Blessed be the Lord God, blessed be the Lord day by day; may the God of our salvation prosper us; our God is the God of salvation.*[^398]
*Then the Trisagion. And after the Our Father:*
*Kontakion, Tone 3:*
*Today the Virgin comes to the cave to give birth ineffably unto the pre-eternal Word: dance, O universe, having heard it, glorify with the angels and the shepherds Him Who is well pleased to appear as a young Child, God before the ages.*
*Lord, have mercy (40 times).*
*And the Prayer:*
*Thou Who at every time and every hour...*
*Lord, have mercy (3 times).*
*Glory..., Both now...:*
*More honorable than the cherubim, and more glorious beyond compare than the seraphim, without defilement thou gavest birth unto God the Word: true Theotokos, thee do we magnify. In the name of the Lord, bless, father.*
*Priest: Through the prayers of our holy fathers...*
*Then the Prayer:*
*O Sovereign God, Father Almighty, O Lord the Only-begotten Son, Jesus Christ, and Holy Spirit, one Godhead, one Power: have mercy on me a sinner; and by the judgments which Thou knowest, save me Thine unworthy servant: for blessed art Thou unto ages of ages. Amen.*
*At the Third and Sixth Hours, the deacon censes the Gospel and the icons, and the superior, and the choirs only. And we say:*
*THE SIXTH HOUR.*
*Come, let us worship (3 times).*
*And Psalm 71:*
*Give the king Thy judgment, O God, and Thy righteousness unto the king's son: to judge Thy people in righteousness, and Thy poor in judgment. Let the mountains take up peace for the people, and the hills righteousness. He shall judge the poor of the people, and shall save the children of the needy, and shall humble the false accuser. And He shall abide with the sun, and before the moon, for generations of generations. He shall come down like rain upon a fleece, and like drops*[^399] *dropping upon the earth. In His days shall righteousness flourish, and abundance of peace, until the moon be taken away. And He shall have dominion from sea to sea, and from the rivers unto the ends of the inhabited earth. Before Him shall the Ethiopians fall down, and His enemies shall lick the dust. The kings of Tarshish and the islands shall offer gifts; the kings of the Arabians and Saba shall bring presents. Yea, all the kings of the earth shall worship Him; all nations shall serve Him: for He has delivered the needy from the mighty, and the poor that had no helper. He shall spare the poor and needy, and shall save the souls of the needy. He shall redeem their souls from usury and injustice; and precious shall His name be in their sight. And He shall live, and unto Him shall be given of the gold of Arabia; and they shall pray for Him continually: all the day long shall they bless Him. There shall be a firm support on the earth upon the tops of the mountains; the fruit thereof shall be exalted above Lebanon; and they of the city shall flourish like grass of the earth. His name shall be blessed unto the ages; before the sun His name abides. And in Him shall all the tribes of the earth be blessed; all nations shall call Him blessed. Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, Who alone does marvelous deeds! And blessed be the name of His glory unto the age, and unto ages of ages; and all the earth shall be filled with His glory. So be it, so be it.*[^400]
*Psalm 131:*
*Remember David, O Lord, and all his meekness: how he sware unto the Lord, and vowed a vow unto the God of Jacob: Surely I will not enter into the tabernacle of my house, nor go up into the bed of my repose; I will not give sleep to mine eyes, or slumber to mine eyelids, or rest to my temples, until I find a place for the Lord, a habitation for the God of Jacob. Lo, we heard of it in Ephrathah; we found it in the fields of the wood. We will go into His tabernacles; we will worship at the place where His feet stood. Arise, O Lord, into Thy resting place: Thou, and the ark of Thy holiness. Thy priests shall be clothed with righteousness, and Thy righteous ones shall rejoice with joy. For Thy servant David's sake, turn not away the face of Thine anointed. The Lord has sworn in truth unto David, and He will not turn from it: Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne. If thy children will keep My covenant and these My testimonies which I shall teach them, their children also shall sit upon thy throne unto the age. For the Lord has chosen Zion; He has desired it for a habitation for Himself:*[^401]

*This is My rest unto ages of ages; here will I dwell, for I have chosen it. I will abundantly bless her provision; I will satisfy her poor with bread. I will clothe her priests with salvation, and her righteous ones shall rejoice with joy. There will I make the horn of David to bud; I have prepared a lamp for Mine anointed. His enemies will I clothe with shame, but upon Him shall My holiness flourish.*[^402]
*Psalm 90:*
*He that dwells in the help of the Most High shall abide in the shelter of the God of heaven. He shall say unto the Lord: Thou art my protector and my refuge: my God, and I will hope in Him. For He shall deliver thee from the snare of the hunters, and from troubling words. With His shoulders shall He overshadow thee, and under His wings shalt thou trust; His truth shall encompass thee with a shield. Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night, nor for the arrow that flies by day, nor for the thing that walks in darkness, nor for mishap and the noonday demon. A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand, but it shall not come nigh thee. Only with thine eyes shalt thou behold, and see the reward of sinners. For Thou, O Lord, art my hope; Thou hast made the Most High thy refuge. No evils shall come upon thee, and no scourge shall draw near unto thy dwelling. For He shall give His angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways. In their hands they shall bear thee up, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone. Thou shalt tread upon the asp and basilisk, and thou shalt trample the lion and the dragon. Because he has set his hope on Me, therefore will I deliver him; I will protect him, because he has known My name. He shall call upon Me, and I will hear him; I am with him in affliction; I will deliver him, and glorify him. With length of days will I satisfy him, and show him My salvation.*[^403]
*Glory..., Both now...: Alleluia (3 times).*
*Lord, have mercy (3 times).*
*Glory..., Troparion, Tone 4:*
*Mary was once inscribed with the aged Joseph as being of the seed of David in Bethlehem, bearing in her womb the seedless Conception; and the time of the birth was at hand, and there was no room in the inn; but as a fair palace, the cave showed itself unto the Queen. Christ is born to raise up the image that before was fallen.*
*Both now..., Theotokion:*
*Because we have no boldness by reason of our many sins, do thou beseech Him Who was born of thee, O Virgin Theotokos; for a mother's prayer avails much toward the good-will of the Master. Despise not the supplications of sinners, O all-pure one; for merciful is He, and able to save, Who was well pleased even to suffer for our sake.*
*Then we sing these troparia, Tone 1:*
*Come, ye faithful, let us be lifted up divinely, and let us behold the divine condescension from on high, manifestly appearing unto us in Bethlehem; and having purified our mind, let us bring a life of virtues, preparing faithfully the entrances of the Nativity instead of myrrh, crying out from the treasures of the soul: Glory in the highest unto God Who is in Trinity, for Whose sake good-will has appeared among men, delivering Adam from the primal curse, as He loves mankind! (Twice).*
*Verse: God shall come from Theman, and the Holy One from the mountain overshadowed and dense.*[^404]
*Tone 4:*
*Hear, O heaven, and give ear, O earth: let the foundations be shaken, let the underworld take trembling! For God and Creator has clothed Himself in a bodily creature, and He Who fashioned creation with a mighty hand is seen as a creature of the womb. O the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are His judgments, and His ways past finding out!*
*Verse: O Lord, I have heard Thy report, and was afraid; O Lord, I considered Thy works, and was astonished.*[^405]
*And again we sing the same troparion.*
*Glory..., Tone 5:*
*Come, Christ-bearing people, let us behold a wonder that astonishes and takes hold of every mind; and singing piously, ye faithful, let us worship: today the Maiden great with child comes unto Bethlehem to give birth unto the Lord, and the angelic choirs run before. And seeing this, Joseph the Betrothed cried out: "What is this strange mystery in thee, O Virgin? And how art thou about to give birth, O Heifer that hast not known the yoke?"*
*Both now..., again the same troparion.*
*Then the Prokimenon, Tone 4:*
*From the womb before the morning star have I begotten Thee; the Lord has sworn and will not repent.*[^406]
*Verse: The Lord said unto My Lord: Sit Thou at My right hand.*[^407]
*And the Paroemia.*
*The Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 7):*[^408]
*The Lord spoke again unto Ahaz, saying: "Ask thee a sign of the Lord thy God, in the depth or in the height." And Ahaz said: "I will not ask, neither will I tempt the Lord." And Isaiah said: "Hear ye now, O house of David: Is it a small thing for you to weary men, but will ye weary my God also? Therefore the Lord Himself shall give you a sign: Behold, a Virgin shall conceive in her womb, and shall bring forth a Son, and they shall call His name Emmanuel. Butter and honey shall He eat, before He knows or chooses the evil, He shall choose the good: for before the Child shall know good or evil, He refuses evil, to choose the good. And the Lord said unto me: "Take thee a great new scroll, and write in it with a man's pen concerning the making speed unto the spoil of prey: for it is at hand." And take unto me faithful men as witnesses, Uriah the priest, and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah. And I went unto the prophetess, and she conceived, and bare a son. And the Lord said unto me: "Call his name: Spoil quickly, plunder swiftly. For before the child shall know how to cry: My father, or: My mother, he shall take the power of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria before the king of Assyria. God is with us: understand, O ye nations, and submit yourselves! Give ear, even unto the ends of the earth! Ye mighty ones, submit yourselves: for if ye again wax strong, again shall ye be conquered! And whatever counsel ye take, the Lord shall scatter it; and whatever word ye speak, it shall not remain among you: for God is with us!"*[^409]
*The Reading from the Epistle of the Holy Apostle Paul to the Hebrews (Pericope 304):*[^410]
*Thou, Lord, in the beginning hast laid the foundation of the earth; and the heavens are the works of Thine hands. They shall perish, but Thou remainest; and they all shall wax old as doth a garment; and as a vesture shalt Thou fold them up, and they shall be changed: but Thou art the same, and Thy years shall not fail. But to which of the angels said He at any time: "Sit on My right hand, until I make Thine enemies Thy footstool"? Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation? Therefore we ought to give the more earnest heed to the things which we have heard, lest at any time we should let them slip. For if the word spoken by angels was steadfast, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompense of reward: how shall we escape, if we neglect so great a salvation; which at the first began to be spoken by the Lord, and was confirmed unto us by them that heard Him?*
*Deacon: Wisdom, upright, let us hear the Holy Gospel.*
*Priest: The Reading from the Holy Gospel according to Matthew (Pericope 3):*[^411]
*Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem, saying: "Where is He that is born King of the Jews? For we have seen His star in the east, and are come to worship Him." When Herod the king had heard these things, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him. And when he had gathered all the chief priests and scribes of the people together, he demanded of them where Christ should be born. And they said unto him: "In Bethlehem of Judea: for thus it is written by the prophet: And thou Bethlehem, in the land of Judah, art not the least among the princes of Judah: for out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule My people Israel." Then Herod, when he had privily called the wise men, enquired of them diligently what time the star appeared. And he sent them to Bethlehem, and said: "Go and search diligently for the young Child; and when ye have found Him, bring me word again, that I may come and worship Him also." When they had heard the king, they departed; and lo, the star, which they saw in the east, went before them, till it came and stood over where the young Child was. When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceeding great joy. And when they were come into the house, they saw the young Child with Mary His mother, and fell down, and worshipped Him: and when they had opened their treasures, they presented unto Him gifts: gold, and frankincense, and myrrh. And being warned of God in a dream that they should not return to Herod, they departed into their own country another way.*[^412]
*Then:*
*Let Thy tender compassions speedily prevent us, O Lord, for we are brought very low; help us, O God our Savior, for the glory of Thy name: O Lord, deliver us, and purge away our sins, for Thy name's sake.*[^413]
*Then the Trisagion. And after the Our Father:*
*Kontakion, Tone 3:*
*Today the Virgin comes to the cave to give birth ineffably unto the pre-eternal Word: dance, O universe, having heard it, glorify with the angels and the shepherds Him Who is well pleased to appear as a young Child, God before the ages.*
*Lord, have mercy (40 times).*
*And the Prayer:*
*Thou Who at every time and every hour...*
*Lord, have mercy (3 times).*
*Glory..., Both now...:*
*More honorable than the cherubim, and more glorious beyond compare than the seraphim, without defilement thou gavest birth unto God the Word: true Theotokos, thee do we magnify. In the name of the Lord, bless, father.*
*Priest: Through the prayers of our holy fathers...*
*Then the Prayer of Saint Basil the Great:*
*O God and Lord of hosts, and Maker of all creation, Who through the tender compassion of Thine incomparable mercy didst send down Thine Only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, for the salvation of our race, and by His precious Cross didst tear up the handwriting of our sins, and thereby didst triumph over the principalities and powers of darkness: do Thou Thyself, O Master, Lover of mankind, receive also from us sinners these thanksgivings and entreating prayers, and deliver us from every all-destructive and dark transgression, and from all them that seek to do us harm, visible and invisible enemies. Nail our flesh with Thy fear, and incline not our hearts unto words or thoughts of malice, but with Thy love wound our souls: that looking ever unto Thee, and guided by the light that is from Thee, beholding Thee, the unapproachable and everlasting Light, we may send up unceasing confession and thanksgiving unto Thee, the Father without beginning, with Thine Only-begotten Son, and Thine all-holy and good and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.*
*Then:*
*THE NINTH HOUR.*
*Come, let us worship (3 times).*
*And Psalm 109:*
*The Lord said unto my Lord: Sit Thou at My right hand, until I make Thine enemies Thy footstool. The Lord shall send Thee the rod of Thy power out of Zion: and rule Thou in the midst of Thine enemies. With Thee is dominion in the day of Thy power, in the splendors of Thy saints: from the womb before the morning star have I begotten Thee. The Lord has sworn, and will not repent: Thou art a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek. The Lord at Thy right hand has broken kings in pieces in the day of His wrath. He shall judge among the nations, He shall fill them with fallings; He shall crush the heads over many lands. He shall drink of the brook in the way: therefore shall He lift up the head.*[^414]
*Psalm 110:*
*I will confess Thee, O Lord, with my whole heart, in the counsel of the upright, and in the congregation. Great are the works of the Lord, sought out in all the things that He wills. Confession and majesty are His work, and His righteousness abides unto ages of ages. He has made a remembrance of His wonders; merciful and gracious is the Lord: He has given food unto them that fear Him. He will be mindful forever of His covenant; He will declare unto His people the power of His works, to give them the heritage of the nations. The works of His hands are truth and judgment; all His commandments are faithful, established unto ages of ages, done in truth*[^415] *and uprightness. He sent redemption unto His people; He has commanded His covenant forever; holy and terrible is His name. The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom; a good understanding have all they that do it: His praise abides unto ages of ages.*[^416]
*Psalm 85:*
*Bow down Thine ear, O Lord, and hear me: for I am poor and needy. Preserve my soul, for I am holy: O my God, save Thy servant that trusts in Thee. Have mercy upon me, O Lord: for I will cry unto Thee all the day long. Rejoice the soul of Thy servant: for unto Thee have I lifted up my soul. For Thou, Lord, art good and longsuffering, and plenteous in mercy unto all them that call upon Thee. Give ear, O Lord, unto my prayer; and attend to the voice of my supplication. In the day of my trouble I called upon Thee: for Thou hast heard me. Among the gods there is none like unto Thee, O Lord; neither are there any works like unto Thy works. All nations whom Thou hast made shall come and worship before Thee, O Lord; and shall glorify Thy name. For Thou art great, and doest marvelous deeds: Thou art God alone. Teach me Thy way, O Lord, and I will walk in Thy truth; let my heart rejoice to fear Thy name. I will confess Thee, O Lord my God, with my whole heart, and I will glorify Thy name forever. For great is Thy mercy toward me, and Thou hast delivered my soul from the lowest hell. O God, the proud are risen against me, and the assemblies of violent men have sought after my soul, and have not set Thee before them. But Thou, O Lord my God, art a God full of compassion, and gracious, longsuffering, and plenteous in mercy and truth. O look upon me, and have mercy upon me; give Thy strength unto Thy servant, and save the son of Thine handmaid. Show me a token for good, that they which hate me may see it and be put to shame: because Thou, Lord, hast helped me and comforted me.*[^417]
*Glory..., Both now...: Alleluia (3 times).*
*Lord, have mercy (3 times).*
*Glory..., Troparion, Tone 4:*
*Mary was once inscribed with the aged Joseph as being of the seed of David in Bethlehem, bearing in her womb the seedless Conception; and the time of the birth was at hand, and there was no room in the inn; but as a fair palace, the cave showed itself unto the Queen. Christ is born to raise up the image that before was fallen.*
*Both now..., Theotokion:*
*O Thou Who for our sake wast born of the Virgin, and didst endure crucifixion, O Good One, Who by death didst despoil death, and manifest the Resurrection as God: despise not them whom Thou hast fashioned with Thine hand. Show forth Thy love for mankind, O Merciful One; accept the Theotokos who bare Thee, as she intercedes for us; and save, O our Savior, a despairing people.*
*Then we sing these troparia, Tone 7:*
*Herod was astonished, beholding the piety of the Magi; and overcome with wrath, he diligently enquired after the space of years. Mothers were made childless, and the untimely age of babes was bitterly reaped down; breasts grew dry, and fountains of milk were stayed. Great was the calamity! Therefore, ye faithful, having assembled piously, let us worship the Nativity of Christ! (Twice).*
*Then the verse: God shall come from Theman, and the Holy One from the mountain overshadowed and dense.*[^418]
*Troparion, Tone 2:*
*When Joseph was wounded with sorrow, O Virgin, going unto Bethlehem, thou didst cry out unto him: "Why art thou downcast and troubled, beholding me with child, knowing not at all the dreadful mystery that is in me? Lay aside all fear henceforth, coming to know what is most glorious. For God, for the sake of mercy, comes down upon earth in my womb now, though He has taken flesh; Whom thou shalt see when He is born, according as He has been well pleased, and filled with joy shalt thou worship Him as thy Maker, Whom angels unceasingly praise and glorify with the Father and the Holy Spirit."*
*Verse: O Lord, I have heard Thy report, and was afraid; O Lord, I considered Thy works, and was astonished.*[^419]
*And again we sing the same troparion.*
*Then the canonarch, standing in the midst of the church, proclaims with a loud voice this entire sticheron.*
*Glory..., Tone 6:*
*Today He Who holds the whole creation in His hand is born of the Virgin; He Whose essence cannot be touched is wrapped in swaddling clothes like a mortal; God Who established the heavens by His word in the beginning lies in a manger; He Who rained down manna upon the people in the wilderness is nourished with milk from the breasts; the Bridegroom of the Church calls the Magi; the Son of the Virgin accepts their gifts. We worship Thy Nativity, O Christ! We worship Thy Nativity, O Christ! We worship Thy Nativity, O Christ! Show us also Thy divine Theophanies!*
*Both now..., again the same troparion.*
*And we make three prostrations.*

*At the Ninth Hour, the deacon censes the entire church.*
*Then the Prokimenon, Tone 4:*
*A man shall say: Mother Zion; and a Man was born in her.*[^420]
*Verse: His foundations are in the holy mountains.*[^421]
*The Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 9):*[^422]
*Unto us a Child is born, and unto us a Son is given, Whose government was upon His shoulder: and His name is called the Angel of Great Counsel, Marvelous Counselor, the Mighty God, the Ruler, the Prince of Peace, the Father of the age to come. For He shall bring peace upon the rulers, and His health. And His government is great, and of His peace there is no bound, upon the throne of David and upon his kingdom, to establish it and to support it with judgment and with righteousness from henceforth and forever. The zeal of the Lord of hosts will perform this.*
*The Reading from the Epistle of the Holy Apostle Paul to the Hebrews (Pericope 306):*[^423]
*Brethren, both He that sanctifies and they who are sanctified are all of one: for which cause He is not ashamed to call them brethren, saying: "I will declare Thy name unto My brethren, in the midst of the church will I sing praise unto Thee." And again: "I will put My trust in Him." And again: "Behold I and the children which God has given Me." Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, He also Himself likewise took part of the same; that through death He might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil; and deliver them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage. For truly He took not on Him the nature of angels; but He took on Him the seed of Abraham. Therefore in all things it behoved Him to be made like unto His brethren, that He might be a merciful and faithful High Priest in things pertaining to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people. For in that He Himself has suffered being tempted, He is able to succour them that are tempted.*
*Deacon: Wisdom, upright, let us hear the Holy Gospel.*
*Priest: The Reading from the Holy Gospel according to Matthew (Pericope 4):*[^424]
*When the wise men were departed, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying: "Arise, and take the young Child and His mother, and flee into Egypt, and be thou there until I bring thee word: for Herod will seek the young Child to destroy Him." When he arose, he took the young Child and His mother by night, and departed into Egypt: and was there until the death of Herod: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying: "Out of Egypt have I called My Son." Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked of the wise men, was exceeding wroth, and sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men. Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremiah the prophet, saying: "In Rama was there a voice heard, lamentation, and weeping, and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not." But when Herod was dead, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt, saying: "Arise, and take the young Child and His mother, and go into the land of Israel: for they are dead which sought the young Child's life." And he arose, and took the young Child and His mother, and came into the land of Israel. But when he heard that Archelaus did reign in Judea in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither: notwithstanding, being warned of God in a dream, he turned aside into the parts of Galilee: and he came and dwelt in a city called Nazareth: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophets, "He shall be called a Nazarene."*[^425]
*Then:*
*Forsake us not utterly, for Thy holy name's sake, and make not void Thy covenant, and take not away Thy mercy from us, for the sake of Abraham beloved of Thee, and for the sake of Isaac Thy servant, and Israel Thy holy one.*[^426]
*Then the Trisagion, through Our Father.*
*Kontakion, Tone 3:*
*Today the Virgin comes to the cave to give birth ineffably to the Pre-eternal Word. Dance, thou inhabited earth, hearing thereof; glorify with the angels and the shepherds Him Who is willed to appear: a young Child, the Pre-eternal God.*
*Lord, have mercy (40 times). And the prayer:*
*Thou Who at all times and at every hour...*
*Lord, have mercy (3 times).*
*Glory..., Both now...*
*More honorable than the Cherubim...*
*In the name of the Lord, bless, father.*
*Priest: Through the prayers of our holy fathers, O Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us.*
*Then the Prayer of Saint Basil the Great:*
*Master, Lord Jesus Christ our God, Who hast been long-suffering toward our sins, and hast brought us even unto the present hour, wherein, hanging upon the life-giving tree, Thou didst open unto the wise thief the entrance into Paradise, and by death didst destroy death: cleanse us, Thy sinful and unworthy servants; for we have sinned and committed iniquity, and are not worthy to lift up our eyes and look upon the height of heaven: for we have forsaken the path of Thy righteousness, and have walked in the desires of our hearts. But we entreat Thy boundless goodness: spare us, O Lord, according to the multitude of Thy mercy, and save us for Thy holy name's sake; for our days have vanished in vanity. Pluck us from the hand of the adversary, and forgive us our sins, and mortify our carnal mind: that putting off the old man, we may put on the new, and may live unto Thee, our Master and Benefactor; and thus, following Thy commandments, we may attain unto eternal rest, where is the dwelling place of all that rejoice. For Thou art truly the true rejoicing and joy of them that love Thee, O Christ our God; and unto Thee do we send up glory, with Thine unoriginate Father, and Thy most-holy and good and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.*
*After this, Psalm 102:*[^427]
*Bless the Lord, O my soul, and all that is within me, bless His holy name. Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all His benefits. Who is gracious to all thine iniquities, Who heals all thine infirmities. Who redeems thy life from corruption, Who crowns thee with mercy and compassion. Who satisfies thy desire with good things; thy youth shall be renewed like an eagle's. The Lord performs deeds of mercy, and brings judgment for all that are wronged. He made known His ways unto Moses, His will unto the sons of Israel. Compassionate and merciful is the Lord, long-suffering and plenteous in mercy. He will not be wroth unto the end, neither will He keep His anger forever. He has not dealt with us according to our iniquities, nor rewarded us according to our sins. For according to the height of heaven from the earth, the Lord has confirmed His mercy over them that fear Him. As far as the east is from the west, so far has He removed our iniquities from us. Like as a father pities his children, so has the Lord pitied them that fear Him. For He knows our frame, He remembers that we are dust. As for man, his days are as grass; as a flower of the field, so shall he flourish. For the wind passed over him, and he shall not be; and shall know his place no more. But the mercy of the Lord is from everlasting to everlasting upon them that fear Him. And His righteousness is upon sons of sons, unto such as keep His covenant, and remember His commandments to do them. The Lord has prepared His throne in heaven, and His kingdom rules over all. Bless the Lord, all ye His angels, mighty in strength, that perform His word, to give ear unto the voice of His words. Bless the Lord, all ye His hosts, His ministers that do His will. Bless the Lord, all His works, in every place of His dominion; bless the Lord, O my soul.*[^428]
*In every place of His dominion, bless the Lord, O my soul.*
*Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.*
*Psalm 145:*[^429]
*Praise the Lord, O my soul. I will praise the Lord in my life, I will chant unto my God as long as I have my being. Trust not in princes, nor in the sons of men, in whom there is no salvation. His spirit shall go forth, and he shall return unto his earth; in that day all his thoughts shall perish. Blessed is he of whom the God of Jacob is his help, whose hope is in the Lord his God, Who made heaven and the earth, the sea, and all things that are therein; Who keeps truth forever, Who executes judgment for the wronged, Who gives food to the hungry. The Lord looses the fettered; the Lord makes wise the blind. The Lord sets upright the fallen; the Lord loves the righteous. The Lord preserves the proselytes; He shall adopt the orphan and widow, and the way of sinners He shall destroy. The Lord shall reign forever; thy God, O Zion, unto generation and generation.*
*Both now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.*
*O Only-begotten Son and Word of God, Who art immortal, and didst deign for our salvation to become incarnate of the Holy Theotokos and Ever-Virgin Mary, and without change didst become man; and wast crucified, O Christ God, trampling down death by death, Who art One of the Holy Trinity, glorified together with the Father and the Holy Spirit: save us.*
*Then:*
*In Thy kingdom when Thou comest, remember us, O Lord.*[^430]

*Blessed are they that mourn, for they shall be comforted.*
*Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth.*

*Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.*

*Blessed are they that are persecuted for righteousness' sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.*

*Rejoice, and be exceeding glad, for great is your reward in heaven.*
*We say not the canticles upon the Beatitudes which are in the Menaion, neither the Epistle nor the Gospel. Glory..., Both now...*
*Remember us, O Lord, when Thou comest into Thy kingdom.*
*Remember us, O Master, when Thou comest into Thy kingdom.*
*Remember us, O Holy One, when Thou comest into Thy kingdom.*
*The heavenly choir chants unto Thee and says: Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord of Sabaoth, heaven and earth are full of Thy glory.*
*Verse: Come unto Him, and be enlightened, and your faces shall not be ashamed.*[^433]
*The heavenly choir chants unto Thee and says: Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord of Sabaoth, heaven and earth are full of Thy glory.*
*Glory...*
*The assembly of holy angels and archangels, with all the heavenly hosts, chants unto Thee and says: Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord of Sabaoth, heaven and earth are full of Thy glory.*
*Both now...*
*The Confession of the Orthodox Faith, of the First and Second Councils. (If there be Liturgy, here we say it not, but after "Both now...", we say: Remit, forgive, and the rest.):*
*I believe in one God, the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth, and of all things visible and invisible. And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, begotten of the Father before all ages; Light of Light, true God of true God; begotten, not made, of one essence with the Father, by Whom all things were made; Who for us men, and for our salvation, came down from the heavens, and was incarnate of the Holy Spirit and the Virgin Mary, and became man; and was crucified also for us under Pontius Pilate, and suffered, and was buried; and the third day He arose again, according to the Scriptures; and ascended into heaven, and sits at the right hand of the Father; and He shall come again, with glory, to judge both the quick and the dead, Whose kingdom shall have no end. And in the Holy Spirit, the Lord, the Giver of life, Who proceeds from the Father and the Son,[^434] Who with the Father and the Son together is worshipped and glorified, Who spoke by the prophets. And in one, holy, catholic, and apostolic Church. I confess one baptism for the remission of sins. I look for the resurrection of the dead, and the life of the world to come. Amen.*

*Then the prayer:*
*Remit, forgive, pardon, O God, our offenses, voluntary and involuntary, in word and in deed, in knowledge and in ignorance, in mind and in thought, by day and by night; forgive us all things, for Thou art good and the Lover of mankind.*
*And after Our Father:*
*Kontakion, Tone 3:*
*Today the Virgin comes to the cave to give birth ineffably to the Pre-eternal Word. Dance, thou inhabited earth, hearing thereof; glorify with the angels and the shepherds Him Who is willed to appear: a young Child, the Pre-eternal God.*
*Lord, have mercy (40 times).*
*Then this prayer:*
*All-Holy Trinity, consubstantial dominion, undivided kingdom, the cause of all good things: be favorably inclined even toward me a sinner. Establish and give understanding to my heart, and take away all my defilement. Enlighten my mind, that I may ever glorify, chant, worship, and say: One is Holy, One is Lord: Jesus Christ, to the glory of God the Father. Amen.*
*Then: It is truly meet... And the dismissal of the day.*
*And there is departure until the evening hour.*
*And Vespers is celebrated with the Liturgy of Basil the Great in its proper time. And the Psalm: I will bless the Lord:*
*We say at the Liturgy after the prayer behind the ambon.*
*But if there be no Liturgy, we say here:*
*Blessed be the name of the Lord from henceforth and forever (3 times).*
*Glory..., Both now... Psalm 33:*[^435]
*I will bless the Lord at all times; His praise shall continually be in my mouth. My soul shall make her boast in the Lord; let the meek hear thereof, and be glad. O magnify the Lord with me, and let us exalt His name together. I sought the Lord, and He gave ear unto me, and delivered me from all my afflictions. Come unto Him, and be enlightened, and your faces shall not be ashamed. This poor man cried, and the Lord gave ear unto him, and saved him out of all his afflictions. The angel of the Lord shall encamp round about them that fear Him, and deliver them. O taste and see that the Lord is good; blessed is the man that trusts in Him. O fear the Lord, all ye His saints; for there is no want to them that fear Him. The rich have become poor and hungry; but they that seek the Lord shall not want any good thing. Come, ye children, give ear unto me: I will teach you the fear of the Lord. Who is the man that desires life, that loves to see good days? Keep thy tongue from evil, and thy lips from speaking guile. Turn away from evil, and do good; seek peace, and pursue it. The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and His ears are open unto their prayer. But the face of the Lord is against them that do evil, to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth. The righteous cried, and the Lord gave ear unto them, and delivered them out of all their afflictions. The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart, and will save such as be of a humble spirit. Many are the afflictions of the righteous; but the Lord delivers them out of them all. The Lord keeps all their bones; not one of them shall be broken. Evil shall slay the wicked; and they that hate the righteous shall be desolate. The Lord redeems the soul of His servants; and none of them that trust in Him shall be desolate.*[^436]
*It is truly meet... And the dismissal.*
*Note:*[^437] *It is fitting to know: if the Paramon fall on a Saturday or on a Sunday, the Liturgy of Chrysostom is chanted; but the Liturgy of Basil the Great is chanted on the feast itself. In like manner do we also on the feast of the Holy Theophanies. Take heed: when it is not a Saturday or Sunday on the Paramon, then is the Liturgy of Basil the Great celebrated, and on the day of the feast the Liturgy of Chrysostom is celebrated; likewise also for the feast of Theophany.*
*Note:*[^438] *Be it also known concerning this: that from the Nativity of Christ until the Holy Theophanies, there is no fast in any wise, nor do genuflections take place, neither in church nor in cells.*
*Be it known:*[^439] *If the Nativity of Christ or Theophany fall on a Sunday, we chant nothing of the Resurrection.*

*On the 25th day of the same month: The Nativity According to the Flesh of our Lord, God, and Savior Jesus Christ.*
*At the 7th hour of the day, they strike the great bell, and all the heavy bells; and having assembled in the church, we begin Vespers according to custom:*
*Deacon: Bless, master.*
*Priest: Blessed is the kingdom...*
*And after the Amen, the Superior: Heavenly King, the Trisagion, and after Our Father, Lord, have mercy (12 times). Glory..., Both now... O come, let us worship (3 times), and the Psalm: Bless the Lord, O my soul.*[^440]
*After this, the deacon says the Great Litany.*
*And if it be on Saturday evening, we chant: Blessed is the man, the entire Kathisma.*[^441]
*If on Sunday evening, we chant only the 1st Antiphon.*
*If on another day, there is no Psalter reading; but after the Litany, we immediately chant: Lord, I have cried unto Thee, in Tone 2.*
*The priest performs the Proskomedia.*
*Then the deacon censes the church according to custom, and the choirs chant the Stichera of the feast, on 8, Tone 2, Idiomela. By Germanus:*
*O come, let us rejoice in the Lord, proclaiming the present mystery! The partition wall of separation is broken down; the flaming sword turns back, and the Cherubim withdraws from the tree of life, and I partake of the food of Paradise, whence I was cast out because of disobedience. For the unchangeable Image of the Father, the Expression of His eternity, takes the form of a servant, having come forth from an unwedded Mother, having suffered no change; for what He was, He remained, being true God; and what He was not, He took upon Himself, having become man for love of mankind. Unto Him let us cry aloud: O God, Who wast born of the Virgin, have mercy on us! (Twice)*
*By Anatolius:*
*When the Lord Jesus was born of the Holy Virgin, all things were enlightened; for while the shepherds were piping, and the Magi were worshipping, and the angels were singing praises, Herod was troubled, because God had appeared in the flesh, the Savior of our souls. (Twice)*
*Thy kingdom, O Christ God, is a kingdom of all ages, and Thy dominion in every generation and generation.[^442] Thou Who wast incarnate of the Holy Spirit, and became man of the Ever-Virgin Mary: a light has shone forth upon us, O Christ God, by Thy coming! Light of Light, the Father's effulgence, Thou hast enlightened all creation; every breath praises Thee, the Image of the Father's glory! Thou Who art, and Who wast before, and hast shone forth from the Virgin: have mercy on us! (Twice)*
*What shall we offer Thee, O Christ, because Thou hast appeared on earth as man for our sake? For each of the creatures made by Thee brings Thee thanksgiving: the angels, a hymn; the heavens, a star; the Magi, gifts; the shepherds, wonder; the earth, a cave; the wilderness, a manger; and we offer an unwedded Mother! O Pre-eternal God, have mercy on us! (Twice)*
*Glory..., Both now..., in the same Tone. By Kassia:*
*When Augustus reigned alone upon earth, the polyarchy of men came to an end; and when Thou wast made man of the pure Virgin, the polytheism of idols was brought to naught. Cities came under one earthly kingdom, and nations believed in one dominion of the Godhead. The peoples were enrolled by the decree of Caesar; we the faithful were enrolled in the name of the Godhead, of Thee our God Who became man. Great is Thy mercy, O Lord, glory to Thee!*
*Entrance with the Gospel.*
*O Joyful Light:*
*Prokimenon of the day:*
*And the readings according to their order, with their troparia and their verses.*
*If the Eve of the Nativity of Christ fall on a Friday, the Prokimenon is chanted:*
*Who is a great god like our God?*[^443]
*With its verses.*
*And that of the day is omitted.*
*The Reading from Genesis (Chapter 1):*[^444]
*In the beginning God made the heaven and the earth. But the earth was invisible and unformed, and darkness was upon the abyss; and the Spirit of God was borne upon the face of the water. And God said: "Let there be light," and there was light. And God saw the light, that it was good; and God divided between the light and the darkness. And God called the light Day, and the darkness He called Night. And there was evening, and there was morning, the first day. And God said: "Let there be a firmament in the midst of the water, and let it divide between water and water." And it was so. And God made the firmament, and God divided between the water which was under the firmament, and the water which was above the firmament. And God called the firmament Heaven. And God saw that it was good. And there was evening, and there was morning, the second day. And God said: "Let the water which is under the heaven be gathered together into one place, and let the dry land appear." And it was so. And the water which was under the heaven was gathered into its gatherings, and the dry land appeared. And God called the dry land Earth, and the gatherings of the waters He called Seas. And God saw that it was good. And God said: "Let the earth bring forth the herb of grass, yielding seed according to its kind and according to its likeness, and the fruit tree yielding fruit whose seed is in itself, according to its kind upon the earth." And it was so. And the earth brought forth the herb of grass, yielding seed according to its kind and according to its likeness, and the fruit tree yielding fruit whose seed is in itself, according to its kind upon the earth. And God saw that it was good. And there was evening, and there was morning, the third day.*[^445]
*The Reading from Numbers (Chapter 24):*[^446]
*The Spirit of God came upon Balaam; and he took up his parable, and said: "How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Israel! As shady valleys, and as gardens by the river side, and as tents which the Lord has pitched, and as cedar trees beside the waters. There shall come forth a Man of his seed, and He shall rule over many nations, and His kingdom shall be exalted, and it shall increase. God guided Him out of Egypt; He has as it were the glory of a unicorn: He shall consume the nations of His enemies, and shall drain their marrow, and shall shoot the enemy through with His arrows. He couched, He lay down as a lion, and as a young lion: who shall stir Him up? Blessed are they that bless thee, and cursed are they that curse thee. A Star shall shine out of Jacob, and a Man shall rise out of Israel, and shall shatter the princes of Moab, and spoil all the sons of Seth; and Edom shall be a possession, and Esau His enemy shall be a possession, and Israel did valiantly."*
*The Reading from the Prophecy of Micah (Chapters 4 and 5):*[^447]
*In those days, says the Lord: "I will gather her that was crushed, and will receive her that was cast off, whom I rejected; and I will make her that was crushed a remnant, and her that was rejected a strong nation; and the Lord shall reign over them in mount Zion from henceforth, even forever. And thou, Bethlehem, house of Ephratha, art thou little among the thousands of Judah? For out of thee shall He come forth unto Me to be a Ruler in Israel, Whose goings forth have been from the beginning, from the days of eternity. Therefore shall He give them up until the time of her that brings forth, she shall bring forth; and the remnant of His brethren shall return unto the sons of Israel. And He shall stand, and shall see, and shall shepherd His flock in the strength of the Lord; and in the glory of the name of the Lord their God shall they abide, for now shall He be magnified unto the ends of the earth."*[^448]
*Then the reader proclaims in Tone 6, and as we stand, he says this Troparion:*
*Thou wast born secretly in a cave, but heaven proclaimed Thee unto all, using the star as a mouth, O Savior, and it brought Thee the Magi worshipping Thee with faith; with them have mercy on us!*
*Verse 1:*[^449] *His foundations are in the holy mountains; the Lord loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob. Glorious things are spoken of thee, O city of God. I will make mention of Rahab and Babylon to them that know me.*
*And we chant the conclusion:*
*And it brought Thee the Magi worshipping Thee with faith; with them have mercy on us!*
*Verse 2:*[^450] *Behold the foreigners, and Tyre, and the people of the Ethiopians, these were there. Mother Zion, a man shall say, and a Man was born in her, and the Most High Himself has established her.*
*And again:*
*And it brought Thee the Magi worshipping Thee with faith; with them have mercy on us!*
*Verse 3:*[^451] *The Lord shall tell it in the scriptures of the peoples, and of these princes that were born in her: for the dwelling of all that rejoice is in thee.*
*And it brought Thee the Magi worshipping Thee with faith; with them have mercy on us!*
*Then, Glory..., the right choir chants the conclusion of the Troparion.*
*Both now..., the left choir likewise chants the conclusion.*
*After this, the reader says the entire Troparion,*
*And himself chants the conclusion thereof:*
*Thou wast born secretly in a cave, but heaven proclaimed Thee unto all, using the star as a mouth, O Savior, and it brought Thee the Magi worshipping Thee with faith; with them have mercy on us!*
*And these readings are read again according to custom:*
*The Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 11):*[^452]
*Thus says the Lord: "There shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a blossom shall grow out of his root. And the Spirit of God shall rest upon Him: the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and might, the Spirit of knowledge and piety. The Spirit of the fear of God shall fill Him. He shall not judge according to appearance, neither reprove according to speech; but with righteousness shall He judge the judgment of the humble, and shall reprove with equity the glorious of the earth; and He shall strike the earth with the word of His mouth, and with the breath of His lips shall He slay the ungodly. And righteousness shall be the girdle of His loins, and truth the belt of His ribs. Then the wolf shall feed with the lamb, and the leopard shall rest with the kid; and the calf and the bull and the lion shall feed together, and a little child shall lead them. And the ox and the bear shall feed together, and their young shall be together; and the lion shall eat chaff like the ox. And a little child shall put his hand over the hole of the asp, and over the lair of the offspring of asps. And they shall not hurt, nor shall they have power to destroy anyone upon My holy mountain; for the whole earth is filled with the knowledge of the Lord, as much water covers the seas. And in that day there shall be a Root of Jesse, and He Who arises to rule over the Gentiles: in Him shall the Gentiles hope, and His rest shall be honor."*[^453]
*The Reading from the Prophecy of Jeremiah (Chapter 3):*[^454]
*"This is our God; no other shall be accounted of in comparison with Him. He found out every way of discipline, and gave it unto Jacob His servant, and unto Israel His beloved. Thereafter He appeared upon earth, and dwelt among men. This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that exists unto ages. All they that hold it fast are unto life, but they that forsake it shall die. Turn thee, O Jacob, and take hold of it; walk towards the radiance before the light thereof. Give not thine honor unto another, nor the things that are profitable unto thee to a strange nation. Blessed are we, O Israel, for the things that are pleasing to God are made known unto us."*
*The Reading from the Prophecy of Daniel (Chapter 2):*[^455]
*Daniel said unto Nebuchadnezzar: "Thou, O king, sawest, and behold, a statue: that great statue, and its appearance was round, standing before thy face, and the sight thereof was fearful. As for this statue, its head was of pure gold; its hands and chest and arms of silver; its belly and thighs of brass; its legs of iron; its feet partly of iron, and partly of clay. Thou sawest till a stone was cut out from a mountain without hands, and it struck the statue upon its feet of iron and clay, and broke them completely to pieces. Then were the clay, the iron, the brass, the silver, and the gold broken to pieces together, and became like dust from the summer threshing-floor; and the rush of the wind carried them away, and no place was found for them. And the stone that struck the statue became a great mountain, and filled all the earth. This is the dream, and we will tell the interpretation thereof before the king.*
*The God of heaven shall set up a kingdom which shall never be destroyed unto ages, and His kingdom shall not be left to other people. It shall crush and consume all kingdoms, and it shall stand unto ages. Forasmuch as thou sawest that the stone was cut out of the mountain without hands, and that it crushed the clay, the iron, the brass, the silver, and the gold; the great God has made known to the king what must come to pass hereafter: and the dream is true, and the interpretation thereof sure."*
*Then the reader says this Troparion, Tone 6:*
*Thou hast shone forth from the Virgin, O Christ, Thou spiritual Sun of righteousness, and a star showed Thee in the cave, Who cannot be contained, yet art contained. Thou hast guided the Magi to worship Thee, with whom we magnify Thee: O Giver of life, glory to Thee!*
*Verse 1 (Psalm 92):*[^456] *The Lord reigns, He is robed in majesty; the Lord is robed in strength, and has girded Himself. For He has established the world, which shall not be shaken. Thy throne is prepared from of old; Thou art from everlasting.*
*Then again:*
*Thou hast guided the Magi to worship Thee, with whom we magnify Thee: O Giver of life, glory to Thee!*
*Verse 2:*[^457] *The rivers have lifted up, O Lord, the rivers have lifted up their voices. The rivers shall lift up their waves, with the voices of many waters.*
*Then again:*
*Thou hast guided the Magi to worship Thee, with whom we magnify Thee: O Giver of life, glory to Thee!*
*Verse 3:*[^458] *Marvelous are the surges of the sea, marvelous is the Lord on high. Thy testimonies are made exceedingly sure; holiness becomes Thy house, O Lord, unto length of days.*
*Glory..., the conclusion of the Troparion:*
*Both now..., again the conclusion.*
*Then the entire Troparion:*
*Thou hast shone forth from the Virgin, O Christ, Thou spiritual Sun of righteousness, and a star showed Thee in the cave, Who cannot be contained, yet art contained. Thou hast guided the Magi to worship Thee, with whom we magnify Thee: O Giver of life, glory to Thee!*
*And the reader himself chants the conclusion of the Troparion, and thereafter reads:*
*The Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 9):*[^459]
*"For unto us a Child is born, a Son is given unto us, Whose government was upon His shoulder: and His name is called the Angel of Great Counsel, Marvelous Counselor, Mighty God, Potentate, Prince of Peace, Father of the age to come; for He shall bring peace upon the rulers, and His health. And great is His government, and of His peace there is no end. Upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with righteousness from henceforth and forever. The zeal of the Lord of hosts shall perform this."*
*The Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapters 7 and 8):*[^460]
*The Lord spoke again unto Ahaz, saying: "Ask thee a sign of the Lord thy God, in the depth, or in the height." And Ahaz said: "I will not ask, neither will I tempt the Lord." And Isaiah said: "Hear now, O house of David! Is it a small thing for you to cause trouble for men, and how do you cause trouble for the Lord? Therefore the Lord Himself shall give you a sign: Behold, a virgin shall conceive in the womb, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call His name Emmanuel. Butter and honey shall He eat, before He knows or chooses evil, He shall choose good; for before the child knows good or evil, he refuses evil, and chooses good."*
*And the Lord said unto me: "Take thee a new, great scroll, and write in it with a man's pen: Concerning making a speedy plunder of spoils; for it is at hand." And I took unto me faithful men as witnesses: Uriah the priest, and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah. And I went unto the prophetess, and she conceived in her womb, and bore a son. And the Lord said unto me: "Call his name: Hasten-to-Plunder, Swift-to-Spoil. For before the child shall know how to call his father or his mother, one shall take away the power of Damascus, and the spoils of Samaria before the king of Assyria."*
*God is with us; understand, O Gentiles, and submit yourselves! Give ear, even unto the ends of the earth; submit yourselves, O mighty ones! For even if you gain strength again, again shall you be conquered. And whatever counsel you take, the Lord shall destroy it. And whatever word you speak, it shall not abide in you; for God is with us!*
*After this, the Little Litany, and after the exclamation, the Trisagion:*
*And the Prokeimenon, Tone 4:* *The Lord said unto Me: "Thou art My Son, this day have I begotten Thee."* *Verse:* *Ask of Me, and I will give Thee the heathen for Thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for Thy possession.*[^461]
*The Epistle to the Hebrews, Pericope 303 (Hebrews 1:1–12): God, Who at sundry times and in divers manners... The end:* *And Thy years shall not fail.*
*Alleluia, Tone 5:* *The Lord said unto my Lord: "Sit Thou on My right hand, until I make Thine enemies the footstool of Thy feet."*[^462]
*Verse:* *The Lord shall send the rod of Thy strength out of Zion.*
*Verse:* *Out of the womb before the morning star have I begotten Thee.*

*The Gospel from Luke, Pericope 5 (Luke 2:1–20): In those days there went out a decree from Caesar Augustus... The end:* *As it was told unto them.*
*[And the appointed daily Prokeimenon, Epistle, and Gospel on the eve of the Nativity of Christ and Theophany are not read.]*
*And in order, the Divine Liturgy of Basil the Great. Instead of "It is truly meet," we chant:* *All of creation rejoices in thee...* *Communion Hymn alone:* *Praise the Lord from the heavens...* *Alleluia (thrice).* *And after the dismissal of the Liturgy, the paraecclesiarch lights a candle-stand and places it in the midst of the church. And the clergy, both choirs standing together, chant aloud the Troparion of the feast, Tone 4:* *Thy Nativity, O Christ our God...*
*Glory..., Both now...: Kontakion, Tone 3:*
*Today the Virgin brings forth Him Who is transcendent in essence...*
