*And upon the conclusion of the Kontakion, we enter the refectory and eat cooked food with oil; but we do not eat fish, yet we drink wine, giving thanks unto God.*
*Be it known:*
*Take note: If the eve of the Nativity of Christ occurs on a Saturday or a Sunday:* *There is no fast, and the troparia of the Imperial Hours with their readings are not chanted on Saturday and Sunday; but we chant the Imperial Hours beforehand on Friday according to custom, as indicated in order.*[^463] *And we say:* *I believe in one God...* *and Psalm 33:* *I will bless the Lord...* *and the dismissal. And Liturgy is not celebrated on that day, but we chant Vespers at its proper time. On Saturday and Sunday, the Liturgy of Chrysostom takes place at its proper time. After the dismissal, we eat a piece of bread, and partake of a little wine, and depart to our cells.*
*At the seventh hour of the day, we begin Vespers. If on Saturday evening, we chant:* *Blessed is the man...* *and cense the entire church. If on Sunday evening, the first antiphon.*[^464] *Thereafter, at "Lord, I have cried," we chant 8 stichera, Tone 2, Idiomela:* *Come, let us rejoice...* *and the rest. Glory..., Both now..., in the same Tone:* *When Augustus reigned alone upon the earth...* *Entrance with the Gospel; "O Joyful Light"; Prokeimenon of the day. If on Saturday evening, we chant the Prokeimenon:* *The Lord reigns...* *and the readings according to their order. Upon the conclusion of the readings, we do not chant the Trisagion, but after the Old Testament readings there is a Little Litany. And after the exclamation, the Prokeimenon, Tone 4:* *The Lord said unto Me: "Thou art My Son..."* *Verse:* *Ask of Me...* *Epistle to the Galatians, Pericope 207 (Galatians 3:15–22):* *Brethren, I speak after the manner of men...* *Alleluia, Tone* 5:* *The Lord said unto my Lord...* *Verse:* *The Lord shall send the rod of Thy strength...* *Verse:* *Out of the womb before the morning star have I begotten Thee.*
*The Gospel from Matthew, Pericope 53 (Matthew 13:31–36):* *The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed...* *After this, the Litany:* *Let us all say...* *Then:* *Vouchsafe, O Lord...* *and:* *Let us complete our evening prayer...* *and the exclamation. And after this the deacon says:* *Wisdom!* *The choir:* *Bless!* *and the rest according to custom, and the dismissal. And after the dismissal, we light a candle-stand in the midst of the church, and both choirs standing together chant the Troparion of the feast; Glory..., Both now..., the Kontakion. And we enter the refectory, and eat a full meal. But we do not eat fish, but with tree-oil, and boiled wheat,*[^465] *or kolyvo with honey. And we drink wine unto the glory of God; and in regions where there is none, we drink beer. And there is set forth also a reading: the Instruction of Cyril, Archbishop of Jerusalem, the beginning of which is:* *As we hope in Jesus Christ...*
*It is proper to know that on whatever day the feast of the Nativity of Christ falls, Great Compline is chanted thus:*
*Take note: At the tenth hour of the night there is the ringing of the bell, and then a chime on all the bells; and the priest with the deacon having vested make the beginning, as on all vigil feasts. The deacon says:* *Bless, master!* *The priest:* *Blessed is our God...* *And while the priest censes, we say Great Compline from the beginning:* *Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee. O Heavenly King...* *Trisagion, and the rest. "God is with us" we chant with melody. And instead of the customary troparia:* *Enlighten mine eyes...* *we say the Troparion of the feast; and instead of:* *Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us...* *we chant the Kontakion of the feast.*
*After "Glory to God in the highest," we go forth into the narthex, chanting:*
*At the Litiya, Idiomelon Stichera, Tone 1. By John the Monk:*
*Let heaven and earth prophetically rejoice today, let angels and men spiritually keep festival! For God has appeared in the flesh unto those who sit in darkness and the shadow; born of the Virgin, the cave and the manger received Him; shepherds proclaim the marvel; Magi from the east bring gifts to Bethlehem. And let us, with unworthy lips, offer praise to Him like the angels:* *Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace;* *for the Expectation of the nations has come! Having come, He has saved us from the bondage of the enemy.*
*Heaven and earth are joined together today, Christ being born! Today God has come upon the earth, and man has ascended into the heavens! Today He is seen in the flesh, Who is invisible by nature, for the sake of man! Therefore we also, glorifying Him, cry out unto Him:* *Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace;* *for Thy coming has granted this, O our Savior, glory to Thee!*
*Glory to God in the highest, hear I today in Bethlehem from the bodiless hosts, upon earth peace unto Him Who is well-pleased to be! Now the Virgin is wider than the heavens, for light has shone forth upon those in darkness, and has exalted the humble, who chant like the angels:* *Glory to God in the highest!*
*Having seen him who was in the image and likeness corrupted through transgression, Jesus bowed the heavens and came down, and dwelt unchanged in the virginal womb, that in her He might renew fallen Adam, who cries:* *Glory to Thine epiphany, O my Redeemer!*
*Glory..., Tone 5. By John the Monk:*
*The Magi, Persian kings, clearly recognizing the heavenly King born upon earth, being led by the radiant star, arrived in Bethlehem, bearing chosen gifts: gold, and frankincense, and myrrh; and falling down they worshipped, for they beheld the ageless Infant lying in the cave.*
*Both now..., Tone 6. By Germanus:*
*All the angels in heaven dance, and men rejoice today; and all creation leaps for joy on account of the Savior and Lord born in Bethlehem: for all idol delusion has ceased, and Christ reigns unto ages!*
*At the Aposticha, Idiomelon Stichera, Tone 2. By Germanus:*
*A great and most glorious marvel is accomplished today: a Virgin gives birth, and her womb suffers no corruption; the Word is incarnate, yet is not separated from the Father! Angels with shepherds give glory, and we with them cry out:* *Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace!*
*Tone 3. Verse:* *Out of the womb before the morning star have I begotten Thee; the Lord has sworn, and will not repent.*[^466]
*Today the Virgin brings forth the Creator of all: Eden offers a cave, and a star reveals Christ the Sun unto those in darkness; with gifts the Magi worshipped, being enlightened by faith. And the shepherds beheld the marvel, while the angels chanted and said:* *Glory to God in the highest!*
*Tone 3. Verse:* *The Lord said unto my Lord: "Sit Thou on My right hand..."*[^467]
*By Anatolius:*
*When the Lord Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea, Magi having come from the east worshipped God Who was made man; and opening their treasures eagerly, they offered precious gifts: refined gold, as to the King of ages; and frankincense, as to the God of all; and as to a three-days-dead corpse, myrrh unto the Immortal One! All you nations, come, let us worship Him Who was born to save our souls!*
*Glory..., Tone 4. By John the Monk:*
*Rejoice, O Jerusalem, and keep festival, all you that love Zion! Today the burdensome bond of Adam's condemnation is loosed; paradise is opened unto us; the serpent is brought to naught: for her whom he deceived of old, he now sees become the Mother of the Creator! O the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God! The sinful vessel that brought forth death unto all flesh has become the beginning of salvation unto all the world, for the sake of the Theotokos! For an Infant is born of her, all-perfect God, and by His birth He seals her virginity, loosing the bonds of sin by swaddling bands, and through His infancy healing the sorrows of Eve unto health! Therefore let all creation dance and leap for joy, for Christ has come to renew it and to save our souls!*
*Both now..., in the same Tone:*
*Thou hast dwelt in a cave, O Christ God; a manger received Thee, and shepherds and Magi worshipped Thee! Then truly the prophetic preaching was fulfilled, and the angelic powers marvelled, crying out and saying: Glory to Thy condescension, O only Lover of mankind!*
*Then: "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart"; Trisagion; after "Our Father":*
*Troparion, Tone 4:*
*Thy Nativity, O Christ our God, has shone upon the world the light of wisdom; for by it, those who served the stars were taught by a star to worship Thee, the Sun of righteousness, and to know Thee, the Orient from on high: O Lord, glory to Thee! (Thrice).*
*Then:* *Blessed be the name of the Lord... (thrice).* *And Psalm 33:* *I will bless the Lord at all times... The end:* *Shall not lack any good thing.*
*Then, the reading of the feast in the Commentary on Matthew, Homily 4.*
*Thereafter: "Glory to God in the highest," in all the psalms, according to custom. At Matins, at "God is the Lord," the Troparion of the feast, thrice; and the customary Kathisma chanting.*

*In a manger for our sake, who were devoid of reason, Thou wast laid, O long-suffering Savior, having willed to become an Infant; and the shepherds sang Thy praise with the angels, crying: Glory and praise unto Him Who is born upon earth, and Who has deified the nature of earth-born men, Christ our God!*
*Glory..., Both now..., the same; and a reading.*
*After the 2nd Kathisma Chanting, Sessional Hymn, Tone 3, Podoben: "The beauty of virginity" (Красотѣ дѣвства):*
*The eternal and incomprehensible One, co-eternal with the invisible Father, thou didst carry bodily in thy womb, O Theotokos, the one and unmingled Divinity of the Trinity, praying that thy grace may shine forth upon the world. Therefore we unceasingly cry out: Rejoice, O pure Virgin Mother!*
*Glory..., Both now..., the same; and a reading.*
*After the Polyeleos, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph was amazed" (Оудивися їѡсифъ):*
*Come, let us behold, O faithful, where Christ is born! Let us follow where the star goes with the Magi, kings of the east, Whom angels unceasingly praise there, and shepherds pipe a worthy hymn, saying:* *Glory in the highest unto Him Who today is born in the cave of the Virgin and Theotokos in Bethlehem of Judea!*
*Glory..., Both now..., the same.*
*The Graduals: the 1st Antiphon of the 4th Tone. Prokeimenon, Tone 4:* *Out of the womb before the morning star have I begotten Thee; the Lord has sworn, and will not repent.* *Verse:* *The Lord said unto my Lord: "Sit Thou on My right hand, until I make Thine enemies the footstool of Thy feet."*[^468]
*Let every breath praise the Lord. Verse:* *Praise God in His saints.*
*The Gospel from Matthew, Pericope 2 (Matthew 1:18–25): Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise...*
*After Psalm 50, instead of "Through the intercessions of the Theotokos," we chant:*
*Glory:* *All things are filled with joy today: Christ is born of the Virgin!*
*Both now:* *All things are filled with joy today: Christ is born in Bethlehem!*
*Then:* *Have mercy on me, O God...*
*And the Sticheron, Tone 6:*
*Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace! Today Bethlehem receives Him Who sits ever with the Father; today the angels divinely glorify the swaddled Infant: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men!*[^469]

*Acrostic:*[^470] *Christ having become man remains what He was: God.*
*Canon of the Nativity. Tone 1. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
*Christ is born, give glory! Christ from heaven, meet Him! Christ on earth, be lifted up! Sing unto the Lord, all the earth, and praise Him with joy, O you peoples; for He has been glorified!*
*Troparia:*
*The wise Creator renews him who was made according to the image of God, but was corrupted through transgression and fallen from the better, divine life, being completely subject to corruption; for He has been glorified!*
*The Creator, seeing man perishing, whom He had fashioned with His hands, bowed the heavens and came down; and taking all his substance from the pure, divine Virgin, He is truly incarnate; for He has been glorified!*
*Wisdom, Word, and Power, the Son and Radiance of the Father, Christ God, hidden from the powers both supra-mundane and on earth, having become man has renewed us; for He has been glorified!*
*Another Canon, iambic. By Lord John of Damascus. In the same Tone. Heirmos:*
*The wonder-working Master saved the people, drying up the wet surge of the sea of old; and having willingly been born of the Virgin, He sets before us a traversable path to heaven; Whom, equal in essence to the Father and to men, we glorify.*
*Troparia:*
*The womb bore the consecrated Word, clearly depicted beforehand unconsumed by the bush, God mingled with human form, releasing the wretched womb of Eve from the bitter ancient curse; Whom we earth-born glorify.*
*Before the sun, the star showed the Word to the Magi, Who came to put an end to sins, clearly in the lowly cave, Thee, the Merciful One, wrapped in swaddling clothes, Whom rejoicing they beheld, Himself both man and Lord.*
*Katavasia: the Heirmos of the first Canon, and the second Heirmos is the Katavasia of the second Canon.*
*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
*Unto the Son begotten incorruptibly of the Father before the ages, and in these last times incarnate without seed of the Virgin, Christ God, let us cry aloud: Thou Who hast exalted our horn, holy art Thou, O Lord!*
*Troparia:*
*Earth-born Adam, having partaken of the better breath of life, yet slipping into corruption through the woman's deceit, beholding Christ born of a woman, cries aloud: Thou Who for my sake hast become like unto me, holy art Thou, O Lord!*
*Conformed to the lowly clay, mingled having become, and through communion with the baser flesh imparting of the Divine nature, having become earthly yet remaining God, and having exalted our horn: holy art Thou, O Lord!*
*Rejoice, O Bethlehem, being king of the princes of Judah; for He Who shepherds Israel, riding upon the shoulders of the Cherubim, has manifestly come forth from thee, even Christ; and having exalted our horn, He reigns over all!*
*Another Canon, iambic. Heirmos:*
*Look down upon the hymns of Thy servants, O Benefactor, abasing the exalted pride of the enemy; and do Thou, O all-seeing One, Who art high above sin, unshakably establish Thy singers, O Good One, upon the foundation of faith.*
*Troparia:*
*The choir of pipers was accounted worthy to behold the most rich birth of the all-pure Bride, passing understanding, being bowed down in strange manner: the choir of the bodiless singing of Christ the King, incarnate without seed.*
*Reigning on high over the heavens, He achieves in mercy for our sake, from the unwedded Maiden, being immaterial before; but in the end the Word took on the density of flesh, that He might draw the fallen first-created man unto Himself.*
*Hypakoe, Tone 8:*
*The heaven brought Thee the first-fruits of the Gentiles as Thou wast lying in the manger, calling the Magi by a star; whom neither scepters nor thrones astounded, but the uttermost poverty: for what is poorer than a cave? and what is more humble than swaddling clothes? wherein shone forth the riches of Thy Divinity: O Lord, glory to Thee!*[^471]
*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
*Rod of the stem of Jesse, and blossom from it, O Christ, Thou hast budded forth from the Virgin; from the mountain overshadowed and dense with woods, Thou hast come, incarnate from her that knew not man, O Immaterial One and God: glory to Thy power, O Lord!*
*Troparia:*
*Whom Jacob foretold of old, the Expectation of the nations, O Christ, Thou hast shone forth from the tribe of Judah, and hast come to overthrow the power of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria, transforming delusion into divinely-fitting faith: glory to Thy power, O Lord!*
*Thou hast filled with joy the wise stargazers, disciples of the words of the prophet Balaam of old: having shone forth as a star out of Jacob, O Master, and bringing in the first-fruits of the Gentiles, Thou hast manifestly received them: glory to Thy power, O Lord!*
*As rain upon the fleece didst Thou descend into the womb of the Virgin, O Christ, and as drops dropping upon the earth; Ethiopia and Tarshish, and the Arabian islands, Sheba, and they that hold all the land of the Medes fell down before Thee fell down before Thee, O Savior: glory to Thy power, O Lord!*
*Another Canon, iambic. Heirmos:*
*Singing of old the renewal of the human race, the Prophet Habakkuk foretold it, having been accounted worthy to behold the type ineffably: for the young Child, the Word, came forth from the Mountain, the Virgin, unto the renewal of the peoples.*
*Troparia:*
*Equal to men came forth the Most High, willingly taking flesh from the Virgin, to cleanse the venom from the serpent's head, leading all unto the life-bearing light, being God, from the sunless gates.*
*The nations that of old were plunged in corruption, having escaped the destructive ruin of the enemy, lift up their hands with hymns of praise, honoring Christ alone as the Benefactor Who has mercifully come unto us.*
*Having grown up from the root of Jesse, O Virgin, thou hast surpassed the bounds of human nature, having given birth to the pre-eternal Word of the Father, as He Himself was well pleased to pass through a sealed womb by a strange emptying.*
*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
*Being the God of peace and Father of mercies, Thou hast sent unto us the Angel of Thy Great Counsel, Who gives peace; therefore, guided to the light of the knowledge of God, watching early out of the night, we glorify Thee, O Lover of mankind.*[^472]
*Troparia:*
*Enrolled among the servants in obedience to Caesar's decree, Thou hast set free us who were slaves of the enemy and of sin, O Christ; and becoming wholly poor according to our condition, Thou hast made the earthly man divine through Thine own union and communion with him.*
*Behold, the Virgin, as was said of old, having conceived in her womb has given birth to God made man, and remains a Virgin; through whom we sinners having been reconciled to God, let us, the faithful, praise her as truly the Theotokos.*
*Another Canon, iambic. Heirmos:*
*Out of the night of the dark works of delusion, come Thou unto us as purification, O Christ, who now vigilantly offer a hymn unto Thee as Benefactor, granting an easy path, ascending along which we may find glory.*
*Troparia:*
*The Master, cutting off again the bitter enmity against us by His coming in the flesh, that He might destroy the soul-destroying ruler, joined peace with the immaterial essences, making Him Who begot Him accessible to creation.*
*The people who were darkened of old beheld by day the light of the brightness from on high; and the Son brings the nations as an inheritance unto God, granting ineffable grace there where sin flourished most abundantly.*

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
*The sea beast cast forth Jonah from its belly as an infant, just as it had received him; and the Word, having dwelt within the Virgin and taken flesh, came forth, having preserved her incorrupt; for He suffered no corruption, and kept her who bore Him unharmed.*
*Troparia:*
*Christ our God has come, incarnate from the womb, Whom the Father begot before the morning star; and holding the governance of the immaculate powers, He lies in a manger of beasts and is wrapped in swaddling clothes; and He looses the many-tangled bonds of transgressions.*[^473]
*A young Son is born from Adam's clay, the offspring of mingling, and is given to the faithful: He is the Father and Ruler of the age to come, and is called the Angel of Great Counsel; He is the mighty God, and rules over all creation with power.*[^474]
*Another Canon, iambic. Heirmos:*
*Jonah, dwelling in the ocean depths, prayed that he might come forth and calm the tempest; but I, pierced by the dart of the tormentor, sing unto Christ, the Destroyer of evils, that Thou mayest come swiftly to my sluggishness.*
*Troparia:*
*The God-Word, Who was in the beginning with God, now confirms what was strong of old, having seen fit to preserve our human substance, whereby through a second communion with Himself He immediately shows it forth free of passions.*
*He Who dwells in light and now by His condescension has been well pleased to lie in a manger for man's salvation, comes for our sake from Abraham's loins, to raise up from the depths the sons cast down in the dark gloom of transgressions.*
*Kontakion, Tone 3. Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дѣ́ва дне́сь):*
*Today the Virgin gives birth to the Transcendent One, and the earth offers a cave to the Unapproachable One. Angels with shepherds give glory, and Magi journey with a star; for for our sake is born a young Child, the pre-eternal God.*
*Ikos:*
*Bethlehem has opened Eden, come let us behold; we have found food in secret; come, let us receive the things of paradise within the cave: there an unwatered root has appeared, budding forth forgiveness; there an undug well is found, from which David longed to drink of old. There the Virgin, having given birth to the Child, has quenched immediately the thirst of Adam and David. Therefore let us go unto Him where He is born, a young Child, the pre-eternal God.*[^475]
*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
*The youths brought up together in piety, [despising] the command of the ungodly command [of the ungodly], were not terrified by the threat of fire; but standing in the midst of the flame, they sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!*
*Troparia:*
*The shepherds playing on their pipes received an awe-inspiring vision of light, for the glory of the Lord shone round about them; and the angel cried out: "Sing praise, for Christ is born, the blessed God of our fathers!"*[^476]
*Suddenly, with the word of the angel, the heavenly hosts cried out: "Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men; Christ has shone forth, the blessed God of our fathers!"*[^477]
*"What is this word?" said the shepherds. "Let us go and see that which has come to pass, the divine Christ." And coming unto Bethlehem, they fell down before Him together with her who bore Him, singing: "Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!"*[^478]
*Another Canon, iambic. Heirmos:*
*The youths caught by love for the King of all disdained the wicked blasphemy of the tyrant raging beyond measure, before whom the great fire yielded, as they said unto the Master: "Blessed art Thou unto the ages!"*
*Troparia:*
*The flame indeed furiously burned up the servants, but with awe spared the youths, though heightened by a sevenfold kindling; and it crowned them without begrudging, as the Lord granted them dew because of their piety.*
*O Christ, the Helper of men, having an ineffable incarnation, Thou hast put to shame the opposing reproach; bearing the riches of deification, Thou art now formed, for the hope of which we came from above into the nether darkness.*
*Thou hast all-powerfully overthrown sin, which was wickedly and unrestrainedly lifted up and impiously raged from the perversion of the world, which it formerly drew unto itself; and today, incarnate of Thine own will, O Benefactor, Thou savest from its snares.*
*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
*The furnace moist with dew prefigured the type of a supernatural wonder; for it did not burn the youths whom it received, just as the fire of the Godhead did not consume the womb of the Virgin into which It entered. Therefore, singing praise, let us sing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!*
*Troparia:*
*The daughter of Babylon drags unto herself the captive youths, the sons of David from Sion; but she sends forth the Magi bearing gifts as children to pray unto David's divinely-welcomed daughter. Therefore, singing praise, let us sing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!*
*The instruments of grief were put aside, for they sang no for the youths of Sion did not sing songs of lamentation in a strange land; and Christ, having shone forth in Bethlehem, destroys the Babylonian delusion and their musical instruments. Therefore, singing praise, let us sing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!*[^479]
*Troparia:*
*Babylon received the spoils of the kingdom of Sion and its captive wealth; but Christ leads to Sion the treasures thereof, and the kings, stargazers, guiding them by a star. Therefore, singing praise, let us sing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!*
*Another Canon, iambic. Heirmos:*
*The youths burned in the furnace under the Old Law prefigure the unburnt womb of her who supernaturally gave birth, remaining sealed. Grace, accomplishing both by a single wonder, raises up the peoples unto hymnody.*
*Troparia:*
*Having escaped the ruin of claiming deification through delusion, all creation, with youthful awe, unsatiatedly praises the Word Who poured Himself out, fearing to offer inglorious blasphemy, being corruptible, though enduring wisely.*
*Thou comest, returning the strayed human nature from the desert hills unto the flower-bearing pasture, to quench the violent power of the manslayer, having been revealed as man and God by Thy providence, O Uprising of the nations!*
*At Ode 9, the brethren light candles.*
*We chant not "More honorable than the Cherubim," but we chant the refrains of the feast:*
*Magnify, O my soul, her who is more honorable and more glorious than the heavenly hosts, the all-pure Virgin Theotokos.*
*And the Heirmos:*
*A strange and most glorious mystery do I behold: the cave is heaven; the Virgin, the Cherubic throne; the manger, the receptacle wherein is reclined the Incontainable Christ God, Whom singing praise we magnify.*
*Then the second choir chants the same refrain and Heirmos.*
*And we chant the remaining six refrains, once for each troparion.*
*Magnify, O my soul, God born in the flesh of the Virgin.*
*Magnify, O my soul, the King born in the cave.*
*Troparion:*
*Beholding the extraordinary course of an unfamiliar new star newly shining, illuminating the heavens and signifying Christ the King born on earth in Bethlehem for our salvation.*
*Magnify, O my soul, [the God worshipped] by the Magi.*

*...[worshipped] as God by the Magi.*
*Magnify, O my soul, Him Who was announced to the Magi by a star.*
*Troparion:*
*When the Magi said: "Where is the new-born Child-King, Whose star has appeared? For we are come to worship Him," Herod, raging, was troubled and, contending against God, was frantic to slay Christ.*[^480]
*Magnify, O my soul, the pure Virgin and only Theotokos who gave birth to Christ the King.*
*The Magi and the shepherds came to worship Christ born in the town of Bethlehem.*
*Troparion:*
*Herod inquired the time of the star by whose guidance the Magi worshipped Christ with gifts in Bethlehem; and being guided by it back to their own country, they left the cruel slayer of children mocked.*[^481]
*Then the first choir chants the refrain of the second Canon:*
*Today the Virgin gives birth to the Master within the cave.*
*And the Heirmos:*
*It is easier for us to choose silence through fear, as being without peril; yet through love, O Virgin, it is hard to weave harmoniously composed hymns; but do thou, as Mother, grant us power equal to our desire.*[^482]
*The second choir chants the same Heirmos:*
*It is easier for us...*
*And to the remaining troparia we chant the refrains:*
*Today the shepherds behold the Savior wrapped in swaddling clothes and lying in a manger.*
*Today the Master, the Intangible One, is wrapped in swaddling clothes as an infant.*
*Today all creation rejoices and is glad, for Christ is born of the Virgin Maiden.*
*Troparion:*
*Beholding dim types and shadows passed away, O pure Mother, and the Word having appeared anew from the shut gates, and deeming Him to be the true Brightness, worthily we bless thy womb.*
*The heavenly hosts announce to the world the Savior, Lord, and Master Who is born.*
*Instead of "Glory":*
*Magnify, O my soul, the dominion of the Tri-hypostatic and Undivided Godhead.*
*Instead of "Both now":*
*Magnify, O my soul, her who has delivered us from the curse.*
*Troparion:*
*Having obtained their desire and been accounted worthy of God's coming, the people adorned with Christ now take comfort in the renewal of life, as thou, O pure Virgin, impartest life-bearing grace to worship His glory.*
*Then both choirs, having come together, chant the first refrain of the feast of the feast, and the Heirmos:*
*A strange and most glorious mystery do I behold...*
*We chant the refrain of the second Canon, and the Heirmos:*
*It is easier for us to choose silence...*
*And a prostration. Exapostilarion:*
*Our Savior, the Dayspring from the Orient, has visited us from on high, and we that were in darkness and the shadow have found the truth; for the Lord is born of the Virgin. (Thrice)*[^483]
*At the Praises, we chant 4 idiomelic Stichera, of Andrew of Jerusalem, Tone 4:*
*Rejoice, O you righteous; be glad, O heavens; leap for joy, O mountains, at the birth of Christ! The Virgin sits resembling the Cherubim, bearing in her bosom God the Word incarnate; the shepherds marvel at Him Who is born; the Magi offer gifts to the Master; the angels sing praise, saying: "O Incomprehensible Lord, glory to Thee!"*
*O Virgin Theotokos, who hast given birth to the Savior, thou hast abolished the first curse of Eve; for thou wast the Mother of the Father's good pleasure, bearing in thy bosom the incarnate Word of God. The mystery endures no searching out: by faith alone do we all glorify it, crying out with thee and saying: "O Ineffable Lord, glory to Thee!"*
*Come, let us praise the Mother of the Savior, who after childbirth was still shown to be a Virgin: Rejoice, O living city of our King and God, wherein Christ dwelt and wrought salvation! With Gabriel let us sing; with the shepherds let us give glory, crying aloud: "O Theotokos, pray unto Him Who was incarnate of thee, that our souls may be saved!"*
*The Father was well pleased; the Word became flesh, and the Virgin gave birth to God made man: a star announces Him; the Magi worship; the shepherds marvel, and creation rejoices.*
*Glory, Tone 6. By Germanus:*
*When it was time for Thy coming upon earth, the first enrollment of the world was made; then wast Thou pleased to register the names of men who believe in Thy Nativity. Therefore such a decree was proclaimed by Caesar; for the unoriginate eternity of Thy kingdom was renewed by Thy Nativity. Therefore, above all tribute of worldly taxes, we also offer unto Thee the theology of the Orthodox riches, as unto our God and the Savior of our souls.*[^484]
*Both now, Tone 2. By John the Monk:*
*Today Christ is born of the Virgin in Bethlehem; today He Who has no beginning begins to be, and the Word becomes incarnate; the powers of heaven rejoice, and the earth makes glad with men; [the Magi offer gifts to the Master...]*[^485] *offer gifts; the shepherds marvel at Him Who is born; and we unceasingly cry aloud: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men!*[^486]
*Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, the Troparion of the feast; litanies, and dismissal.*
*And the hegumen anoints the brethren with the holy oil from the holy lamp that hangs before the festal icon, while we chant the idiomelic Sticheron of the feast; and the First Hour. At the First Hour, the Troparion of the feast; after the Our Father, the Kontakion of the feast, and the rest; and the complete dismissal.*
*Be it also known: that if the Eve of Christ's Nativity falls on a Saturday or Sunday, there is no fasting; the Liturgy of Chrysostom is celebrated at its usual time; and on the feast day itself the Liturgy of Basil is sung without fail. The same is done on the feast of Theophany.*[^487]
*Instead of "All of creation rejoices in thee," we chant the Heirmos of Ode 9.*
*On this day the Liturgy is celebrated early in the morning, because of the labor of the vigil.*
*At the Liturgy: First Antiphon, Psalm 110. Tone 2:*
*I will give thanks unto Thee, O Lord, with my whole heart; I will speak of all Thy marvelous works.*[^488]
*Refrain:*
*Through the intercessions of the Theotokos, Savior, save us.*
*Verse 2:* *In the council of the upright and in the congregation, great are the works of the Lord.*
*Through the intercessions of the Theotokos, Savior, save us.*
*Verse 3:* *Sought out in all things according to His will.*
*Through the intercessions of the Theotokos, Savior, save us.*
*Verse 4:* *Thanksgiving and majesty are His work, and His righteousness endures unto ages of ages.*
*Through the intercessions of the Theotokos, Savior, save us.*
*Then both choirs, Glory, Both now:* *Through the intercessions of the Theotokos...*
*Second Antiphon, Psalm 111. Tone 2:*
*Blessed is the man that fears the Lord; in His commandments he will delight exceedingly.*[^489]
*Refrain: Save us, O Son of God, born of the Virgin, who sing unto Thee: Alleluia.*
*Verse 2:* *Mighty upon earth shall be his seed; the generation of the upright shall be blessed.*
*Save us, O Son of God...*
*Verse 3:* *Glory and riches shall be in his house, and his righteousness endures unto ages of ages.*
*Save us, O Son of God...*
*Verse 4:* *There has arisen in darkness a light for the upright; he is merciful, and full of compassion, and righteous.*
*Save us, O Son of God...*
*Then both choirs together, Glory, Both now:*
*Only-begotten Son and Word of God Third Antiphon, Psalm 109. Tone 4:*
*The Lord said unto my Lord: "Sit Thou on My right hand."*[^490]
*Troparion:*
*Thy Nativity, O Christ our God, has shone forth upon the world the light of understanding; for thereby they that served the stars were taught by a star to worship Thee, the Sun of Righteousness, and to know Thee, the Dayspring from on high: O Lord, glory to Thee!*
*Verse 2:* *Until I make Thine enemies the footstool of Thy feet.* *Troparion: Thy Nativity, O Christ our God...*
*Verse 3:* *The Lord shall send Thee a rod of power out of Sion; and rule Thou in the midst of Thine enemies.* *Thy Nativity, O Christ our God...*
*Verse 4:* *With Thee is the beginning in the day of Thy power, in the splendors of Thy saints.* *Thy Nativity, O Christ our God...*
*Introit:*
*Out of the womb before the morning star have I begotten Thee; the Lord has sworn, and will not repent: "Thou art a priest unto the age according to the order of Melchizedek."*[^491]
*The Troparion in the loudest voice:*
*Thy Nativity, O Christ our God...*
*Glory, Both now:*
*Kontakion: Today the Virgin...*
*Instead of the Trisagion:*
*As many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Alleluia.*[^492]
*Prokeimenon, Tone 8:*
*Let all the earth worship Thee, and sing unto Thee.*[^493]
*Verse:* *Shout with joy unto the Lord, all the earth.*
*The Epistle to the Galatians, Pericope 204 (Galatians 4:4–7): But when the fullness of the time was come...*
*Alleluia, Tone 1:*
*The heavens declare the glory of God.*[^494]
*Verse:* *Day unto day pours forth speech.*
*The Gospel from Matthew, Pericope 3 (Matthew 2:1–12): Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea...*
*Communion Hymn:*
*The Lord has sent redemption unto His people. Alleluia. (Thrice)*[^495]
*At the table there is great consolation for the brethren; and we read the homily of Chrysostom, whose incipit is: "Of old indeed the patriarch..."*
*Note: If the feast of the Nativity of Christ happens to fall on a Wednesday or a Friday: we grant dispensation, namely, for laymen to eat meat, and for monks cheese and eggs. And we eat, from the Nativity of Christ every day until the Eve of Holy Theophany, laymen indeed meat, and monks cheese and eggs.*[^496]

*In the same month, on the 26th day:*
*The Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos; and the memory of the Holy Hieromartyr Euthymius, Bishop of Sardis.*
*His service is chanted at Compline.*
*At Vespers there is no stichology, except on Sunday.*
*At "Lord, I have cried," the Stichera of the feast, on 6:*
*Tone 2. Idiomela:*
*Come, let us rejoice in the Lord, proclaiming the present mystery: the middle wall of partition has been destroyed; the flaming sword turns back, and the Cherub withdraws from the tree of life; and I partake of the food of paradise, from which I was driven out through disobedience; for the unchanging Image of the Father, the Expression of His eternity, takes the form of a servant, having come forth from an unwedded Mother, suffering no change. For He remained what He was, being true God; and He took what He was not, having become man for love of mankind. Unto Him let us cry aloud: "O God born of the Virgin, have mercy on us!" (Twice)*[^497]
*When the Lord Jesus was born of the holy Virgin, all things were enlightened; for while the shepherds were piping, and the Magi were worshipping, and the angels were singing praise, Herod was troubled, because God had appeared in the flesh, the Savior of our souls. (Twice)*
*Thy kingdom, O Christ God, is a kingdom of all the ages, and Thy dominion is throughout every generation and generation. Incarnate of the Holy Spirit, and made man of the Ever-Virgin Mary: a light has shone upon us, O Christ God, even Thy coming. Light of Light, the Brightness of the Father, Thou hast enlightened all creation. Let every breath praise Thee, the Image of the Father's glory: O Son, Who art before all, and hast shone forth from the Virgin, O God, have mercy on us!*[^498]
*What shall we offer Thee, O Christ, because Thou hast appeared on earth as man for our sake? For every creature made by Thee offers Thee thanksgiving: the angels, a hymn; the heavens, a star; the Magi, gifts; the shepherds, wonder; the earth, a cave; the wilderness, a manger; and we, a Virgin Mother: O pre-eternal God, have mercy on us!*
*Glory, Both now, Tone 2:*
*Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace! Today Bethlehem receives*[^499] *the Sun of Righteousness, holy in her order, worthily crying aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!*[^500]
*Troparia:*
*Covered on the face, he was enlightened by divine grace; and in the wisdom of his words, he was a partaker with Christ, all-blessed one, Who for our sake was clothed with flesh.*
*The mindless ones were not ashamed before the honor of the priesthood, nor did they respect his venerable gray hairs; and showing no reverence for thy old age, they mercilessly wounded thee.*
*Unto the Deliverer wrapped in swaddling clothes and lying in the manger, O father Euthymius, thou hast offered as a costly gift thy precious blood, poured out in love for Him.*
*Theotokion:*
*The Creator of immaterial essence is born today in the flesh from thee as man, O Mother of God. Unto Him let us sing: Glory in the highest to Christ God!*
*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
*Thou, my Lord, hast come as a light into the world, a holy light turning from dark ignorance those who sing Thy praise in faith.*
*Troparia:*
*Unto Thee, O Savior, a living image is offered, which honored the image of Thy precious body and Thy bodily representation; unto Thee, O Master, the shepherd whose name signifies good cheer is offered, bearing in his own body the wounds of Thy body.*[^501]
*Thou hast quenched the fire of the rage of the lawless, O Euthymius, by the shedding of thy blood unjustly poured out, O most sacred and all-blessed one.*
*Theotokion:*
*The course of corruption has ceased, for the Virgin has incorruptibly given birth to Him Who delivers from corruption the corrupted nature of man.*
*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
*I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord, the Church cries unto Thee, having been cleansed from the demonic blood by the blood that flowed in mercy from Thy side.*[^502]
*Troparia:*
*Conformed unto the Savior's stripping and wounds by the stripping of all things, O father, having endured afflictions, thou hast shed thy blood along with His blood.*
*Having enriched thyself through virtues with love, and hope, and divinely-wise faith that abides unto the ages, thou offerest them as gifts unto Him Who was born of the Virgin, O all-blessed Euthymius.*
*Having lawfully served Christ in the divine sacred ministry of the Word, thou hast received the reward thereof, O divinely-speaking father: even to finish thy course in blood.*
*Theotokion:*
*He Who created* He Who created man according to His own image, for His great compassions renews him; for from thee, O Mother of God, He was perfectly clothed in him.[^503]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thy tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й сп҃се):*
Thou hast offered unto Christ, Who was born of the Virgin, O wise Euthymius, as godly gifts, having suffered most patiently, O hierarch, thy blood. Therefore, thou hast received a double crown of victory, and thou standest before the All-Holy Trinity, praying that we may be saved.[^504]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The Abrahamic youths in the Persian furnace, inflamed with love of piety rather than with the flame, cried aloud: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord![^505]

*Troparion:*
Having mingled the divinely-given anointing of the priesthood with thy blood, O most sacred one, thou hast shown it forth sacredly: Blessed art Thou, my God, crying aloud, in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Having set thy feet upon the rock of the faith, O all-blessed one, thou hast remained unshaken by all the assaults of temptations: Blessed art Thou, my God, crying aloud, in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord![^506]

*Troparion:*
Thou hast drawn upon thyself the grace of the divine Protomartyr, of whom thou hast shown thyself to be an exquisite emulator, giving blessings as a recompense unto those who unmercifully killed thee, O all-blessed Euthymius.[^507]

*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, O sanctified divine dwelling-place of the Most High; for through thee joy was given, O Mother of God, unto those who cry: Blessed art thou among women, O all-immaculate Lady![^508]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Stretching out his hands, Daniel stopped the mouths of the lions in the pit; and having girded themselves with virtue, the youths, lovers of piety, quenched the power of the fire, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^509]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst stand at the tribunal, valiantly struggling, O father Euthymius; for thou wast instructed in the most perfect limit of love, so that thou didst choose to die for thy friends, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^510]

*Troparion:*
Bright both in word and mind, thou hast possessed a radiant soul, a radiant countenance, and yet more radiant wast thou even unto blood, O Euthymius, resisting the God-hating emperors, and crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
The mighty ones of the earth fell upon thee, O blessed one, doing most lawless things to put thee to death; but thou, having reached out unto Him Who was born *unto the Deliverer born of the pure Virgin, thou didst cry aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!*
*Theotokion:*
*Behold, now the prince and governor from the tribe of Judah has failed of late; for thou, O all-immaculate one, hast given birth to the Expectation of the nations, Christ, Who was prepared beforehand for this, unto Whom we sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!*[^511]
*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
*A cornerstone was cut out without hands from the unquarried mountain, which is thee, O Virgin, even Christ, Who has joined together separated natures. Therefore, rejoicing, we magnify thee, O Mother of God.*[^512]
*Troparia:*
*Unto the most tranquil harbor hast thou departed from those here below, O father; for as a sparrow thou hast been delivered from the snare of those hunting thee, blessing with a courageous spirit Him Who delivered thee, O hieromartyr.*[^513]
*When the Light of the Dayspring from on high appeared, being enlightened, and having shone forth preternaturally from Judah, O hierarch, unto the radiant star of illumination, thou hast gone forth unto the Lady.*[^514]
*Thou hast been counted worthy now to join the choral dance in the expanses of paradise, where is the brightness of the blessed and the rejoicing of the saints, for they received thee, O Euthymius, as a victorious sufferer.*
*Having boldness toward God, as both a hierarch and a martyr, ask now for tranquility for the Church from the present winter, and forgiveness of transgressions for those who sing thy praise, O all-blessed one.*
*Theotokion:*
*A rod hast thou budded forth from the root of Jesse, O Parent of God, having today given birth unto the Flower of Divinity, Christ, for us, O all-pure one, as God Whom naught can contain, and now swaddled as an infant.*[^515]
*Stichera, Tone 8. Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder!" (Ѽ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*
*Still dripping with blood and crimsoned with warmth, and thy wounds full of blood, thou hast stood before Christ, O divinely-speaking Euthymius. Stretching out the marks of thy wounds, O father, in place of prayers, pray unto Him for those who sing thy praise, and fervently, O blessed one, pray for thy flock.*
*Thou hast offered a gift, O venerable one, unto Christ Who was born and became an infant in the flesh: venerable gray hairs, adorned with the gifts of the hierarchy, O father, and reddened with the blood of thy suffering; orthodox faith, and fervent and truly incorrupt hope, and unshakable love, O venerable one.*
*A tongue moved by the Spirit, and uttering the teachings of truth of long ago, by God-given grace, beautifully distilling the sweetness of piety a God-proclaiming pipe of piety, an immovable foundation of Orthodoxy, honey-streaming lips, a treasury of wisdom, a loud-voiced trumpet of the Church hast thou shown thyself to be, O venerable one.*
*Theotokion:*
*Having taken flesh from thy blood, the pre-eternal God showed thee forth as an intercessor for mankind, O pure one; therefore, deliver thy servants from every necessity and distress, and from the snares of the all-evil enemy, and grant that all who praise and worship thee may share in the judgment of the elect.*
*Note. It should be known:*
*That in the afterfeast of the Nativity of Christ and of the Theophany, Small Compline is sung without the Theotokion Canon. At Compline for the 26th day, after "It is truly meet" and after the Trisagion, we say the Kontakion of the Mother of God, for the Synaxis: "He Who before the morning star..."*
*At Midnight Office we say the usual kathisma. After the 1st Trisagion, instead of "Behold, the Bridegroom," we say the Troparion of the Feast: "Thy Nativity, O Christ our God..." After the 2nd Trisagion, we say the Kontakion of the Mother of God: "He Who before the morning star..." Then "Lord, have mercy," 12 times, and the Dismissal. But the prayer "Remember, O Lord," we do not say.*[^516]
*At Matins, at "God is the Lord," the Troparion of the Feast, thrice. After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 1. Podoben: "The stone having been sealed" (Ка́мени запеча́танꙋ):*
*When Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea, creation was enlightened, having recognized the Creator. The choirs of angels marvelled, beholding the Master upon earth having taken the form of a servant, yet being inseparable from the Father. Glory to the incarnate God! Glory to Him Who was born upon earth! Glory to Him Who was well pleased to save our race!*[^517]
*Glory, Both now, the same.*
*And we read the homily of Epiphanius of Cyprus, in praise of the Most Holy Mother of God, in three parts. After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4. Podoben: "Joseph marvelled" (Оу҆диви́сѧ І҆ѡ́сифъ):*
*"Why art thou astonished, O Mary? Why art thou struck with awe at that which is within thee?" "Because I have given birth in time unto the timeless Son," she said. "Not having known the conception of Him that is born, I am unwedded, and how shall I bear a Son? Who has ever seen a seedless birth? For where God wills, the order of nature is overcome," as it is written: Christ is born, to raise up the previously fallen image.*[^518]
*Glory, Both now, the same.*
*Canons of the Feast: the heirmoi of both canons twice; the troparia on 12. Katavasia: the heirmoi of both canons. After Ode 3 After Ode 3, Kontakion of the Feast: "Today the Virgin..." And the Ikos, and the Hypakoe.*
*After Ode 6, Kontakion, Tone 6:*
*He Who before the morning star was begotten of the Father without mother, on earth without father was incarnate today from thee. Therefore, a star brings good tidings unto the Magi, and the angels with the shepherds sing of Thy unutterable nativity, O full of grace!*[^519]
*Ikos:*
*Having budded forth the untilled cluster of grapes, O mystical vineyard: bearing Him in thy arms as upon branches, she spoke: "Thou art my fruit; Thou art my life! Whence I have known that I remain what I was: Thou art my God; for beholding the seal of my virginity unbroken, I proclaim Thee to be the immutable Word become flesh. I know no seed; I know Thee to be the destroyer of corruption, for I am pure, since Thou hast come forth from me; for just as Thou didst find my womb, Thou hast left it intact, beholding it whole. Therefore, all creation keeps festival together with me, crying aloud: Rejoice, O full of grace!"*[^520]
*And we read the Prologue.*
*At Ode 9 we do not sing "More honorable," but we sing the refrains as on the feast itself.*
*Exapostilarion:*
*Our Savior, the Dayspring of daysprings, has visited us from on high, and those in darkness and the shadow of death have found the truth; for the Lord was born of the Virgin. (Thrice)*[^521]
*At Lauds, Stichera on 4, Tone 4. Automela:*
*Rejoice, ye righteous; heavens, be glad; leap for joy, ye mountains, for Christ is born! The Virgin sits resembling the Cherubim, bearing in her bosom God the Word incarnate; the shepherds marvel at Him Who is born; the Magi offer gifts unto the Master; the angels singing praise say: Incomprehensible Lord, glory to Thee!*[^522]
*O Virgin Theotokos, who didst bear the Savior, thou hast abolished the first curse of Eve, for thou wast the Mother of the Father's good pleasure, bearing in thy bosom God the Word incarnate. The mystery does not endure searching out. By faith alone do we all glorify it, crying with thee and saying: Ineffable Lord, glory to Thee!*
*Come, let us hymn the Mother of the Savior, who after childbirth is again shown to be a Virgin: Rejoice, living city of the King and God, in which Christ having dwelt accomplished salvation! With Gabriel let us sing, with the shepherds let us glorify, crying aloud: O Mother of God, pray unto Him Who was incarnate of thee, that our souls may be saved!*

*The Father was well pleased; the Word became flesh; the Virgin gave birth to God made man; the star proclaims it; the Magi worship; the shepherds wonder; and creation rejoices.*
*Glory, Tone 2:*
*Today the invisible nature is united unto men from the Virgin; today the boundless essence is wrapped in swaddling clothes in Bethlehem; today God leads the Magi by a star unto worship, prefiguring His three-day burial, as in gold, and myrrh, and frankincense, unto Whom we sing: O Christ God, Who wast incarnate of the Virgin, save our souls!*[^523]
*Both now, Tone 2. By John the Monk:*
*Today Christ is born in Bethlehem of the Virgin; today He Who has no beginning begins, and the Word is incarnate. The heavenly powers rejoice, and the earth makes glad with men. The Magi offer gifts unto the Master. The shepherds wonder at Him Who is born. And we unceasingly cry aloud: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will among men!*[^524]
*Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, the Troparion of the Feast, and the litanies, and the Dismissal. And the First Hour, and the final Dismissal. At the Hours, the Troparion of the Feast. Kontakion of the Mother of God: "He Who before the morning star..." At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes from the Canons of the Feast, Odes 3 and 6. After the Entrance: "O Son of God, born of the Virgin, save us who sing unto Thee: Alleluia!" This we sing until the Apodosis of the Feast. Troparion of the Feast: "Thy Nativity, O Christ our God..." Glory, Both now, Kontakion: "He Who before the morning star..." Then the Trisagion. Prokeimenon, Tone 3, the Hymn of the Mother of God: "My soul doth magnify the Lord..." Verse: "For He hath regarded the lowliness of His handmaiden." Epistle to the Hebrews, section 302 [Heb 2:11–18]. Alleluia, Tone 8: "Arise, O Lord, into Thy rest..." Verse: "The Lord hath sworn in truth unto David, and He will not turn from it." Gospel according to Matthew, section 4 [Mt 2:13–23]. Communion verse: "The Lord hath sent redemption unto His people."*[^525]
*Note. It should be known: That if the Nativity of Christ falls on Sunday, we do not celebrate the memory of the Holy God-ancestors on the coming Sunday, because the month of January will already begin, and the feast of Christ's Nativity will already be concluded; but we celebrate this Sunday on the 26th of December, on the day after the feast, on Monday. And we sing thus: On Sunday evening at "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 6: of the feast, 3, Tone 2: "Come, let us rejoice in the Lord..." and of the saints, 3, Tone 1. Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Небє́сныхъ чинѡ́въ):*

*...Joy of the heavenly ranks: "Let us all praise the God-ancestor..." Glory, of the Stichera, Tone 6: "The memory we celebrate..." Both now, of the Feast, the same tone: "Glory in the highest..." Entrance. Great Prokeimenon, Tone 7: "Who is a great god like our God?" with its verses, and litanies. At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Feast, Idiomela, 3, Tone 8, with their refrains. Glory, Tone 6: "The memory of the sacred ones..." Both now, of the Feast. Troparion of the Saints, Tone 2: "Proclaim good tidings, O Joseph..." Glory, Both now, of the Feast. At Compline, after the Trisagion, Kontakion of the God-ancestors. Glory, Both now, of the Mother of God: "He Who before the morning star..." At Matins, at "God is the Lord," Troparion of the Feast, twice; Glory, of the Saints; Both now, of the Feast. After the kathismata, Sessional Hymn of the Feast. And we read in the Gospel Commentary for the Sunday after the Nativity of Christ. First Canon of the Feast with the heirmos on 6: heirmos twice, troparia on 4; and the other Canon of the Feast on 4; and of the Saints on 4. Katavasia: the heirmoi of both canons. After Ode 3, Kontakion of the Mother of God, Tone 6: "He Who before the morning star..." and its Ikos; Sessional Hymn of the Saints; Glory, Both now, of the Feast. And reading. After Ode 6, Kontakion of the Saints: "Today David is filled with joy..." and Ikos. And we read the Prologue. At Ode 9 we do not sing "More honorable," but we sing the refrains of the Feast. Exapostilarion of the Saints, twice; Glory, Both now, of the Feast. At Lauds, Stichera of the Feast on 4, Tone 4, Idiomela; Glory, of the Saints, Tone 8: "Blood and fire..."; Both now, of the Feast, Tone 2: "Today Christ..." Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, Troparion of the Saints; Glory, Both now, of the Feast. Litanies, and Dismissal. And the First Hour, and the final Dismissal. At the Hours, Troparion of the Feast; Glory, of the Saints; Both now, Theotokion of the Hours. After "Our Father," Kontakion of the Mother of God: "He Who before the morning star..." and Kontakion of the Saints, saying them alternately. At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes from the Canon of the Feast, Ode 3, on 4; and of the Saints, Ode 6, on 4. After the Entrance, Troparion of the Feast, and of the Saints; Glory, Kontakion of the Saints; Both now, of the Mother of God: "He Who before the morning star..." Prokeimenon, the Song of the Mother of God, Tone 3: "My soul doth magnify the Lord..." Verse: "For He hath regarded the lowliness of His handmaiden." Another of the Saints, Tone 4: "Marvelous is God in His saints, the God of Israel." Epistle to the Hebrews, section 302 [Heb 2:11–18]; another Epistle of the Saints, to the Galatians, section 200 [Gal 1:11–19]. Alleluia of the Mother of God, Tone 8: "Arise, O Lord, into Thy rest..." Verse: "Remember, O Lord, David..." The Gospel is one, of the Mother of God and of the Saints: Matthew, section 4 [Mt 2:13–23]. Communion verse: "The Lord hath sent redemption"*[^526] *sent redemption unto His people. Another: Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous.*[^527]
*Saturday after the Nativity of Christ. At the Liturgy, Prokeimenon, Tone 4: "I will make mention of Thy name in every generation and generation." Verse: "Give ear, O daughter, and behold." Epistle to Timothy, section 288 [1 Tim 6:11–16]. Alleluia, Tone 8: "Arise, O Lord, into Thy rest." Gospel according to Matthew, section 46 [Mt 12:15–21]. Communion verse: "I will take the cup of salvation."*[^528]
*Sunday after the Nativity of Christ. We celebrate the memory of the holy and righteous Joseph the Betrothed, and David the King, and James the Brother of the Lord.*[^529]
*It should be known: If this Sunday occurs after the Nativity of Christ on the 26th, or the 27th, or the 28th, or the 29th, or the 30th [of December], we sing thus:*
*On Saturday at Little Vespers according to custom. At Great Vespers, after the kathisma, at "Lord, I have cried," Resurrection Stichera, 3; and of the Feast, 4; and of the Saints, 3, Tone 1. Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Небє́сныхъ чинѡ́въ): "Let us all praise the God-ancestor..."; Glory, Tone 6: "The memory we celebrate..."; Both now, Theotokion of the tone. Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day. At the Litiya, Stichera of the Feast: those sung on the feast itself; Glory, Both now, of the Feast. At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Octoechos, in alphabetical order; Glory, Tone 6: "The memory of the sacred ones..."; Both now, of the Feast. At the blessing of loaves, Troparion of the Feast: "Thy Nativity, O Christ our God...", twice; and of the Saints, once, Tone 2: "Proclaim good tidings, O Joseph..."; and reading. But where there is no All-Night Vigil: at Compline after "It is truly meet" and after the Trisagion, Kontakion of the God-ancestors; Glory, Both now, of the Feast. At Matins, at "God is the Lord," Resurrection Troparion, twice; Glory, of the Saints; Both now, of the Feast. After the usual kathismata, Resurrection Sessional Hymns, with their Theotokia. And reading in the Gospel Commentary, Matthew, Sunday after the Nativity of Christ. After the Polyeleos, their troparia. Hypakoe of the tone. And reading in the Gospel Commentary, Sunday in course. Gradual Antiphons and Prokeimenon of the tone. "Let every breath praise the Lord." Resurrection Gospel, and "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ." After Psalm 50, Resurrection Sticheron. Resurrection Canon with the heirmos on 4; and of the Mother of God on 2; and of the Feast on 4; and of the God-ancestors on 4. [If it be on the 26th day, we sing the Resurrection Canon with the heirmos on 4; and both Canons of the Feast on 6; and of the God-ancestors on 4.] Katavasia of the Feast: "Christ is born." After Ode 3, Kontakion and Ikos of the Feast; and Sessional Hymn of the Saints, Tone 3. Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дв҃а дне́сь): "Of Joseph the righteous..."; Glory, same tone: "The Virgin gave birth to the Creator"; Both now: "The choir of the prophets..."; and reading.*

*...reading. After Ode 6, Kontakion of the Saints, Tone 3. Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дв҃а дне́сь): "Today David is filled with joy..."; and the Ikos. And we read the Prologue. At Ode 9 we sing "More honorable." Resurrection Exapostilarion; Glory, of the Saints. Podoben: "With the disciples" (So ucheniki): "With James let us sing..."; Both now, of the Feast. At Lauds, Resurrection Stichera, 4; and of the Feast, Idiomela, 4, Tone 4: "Rejoice, ye righteous...", with their refrains; Glory, of the Saints, Tone 8: "Blood and fire..."; Both now: "Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos..." Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, Resurrection Troparion. Litanies, and Dismissal, and the Gospel Sticheron according to its order; and the First Hour, and the final Dismissal. At the Hours, Resurrection Troparion; Glory, of the Feast; Both now, Theotokion of the Hours. But the Troparion of the Saints and that of the Feast we say alternately. After "Our Father," the Kontakion of the Feast and that of the Saints we say alternately. At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the tone on 4; and the appointed Ode of the Feast on 4; and of the Saints, Ode 6, on 4. After the Entrance, Resurrection Troparion, and of the Feast, and of the Saints; Glory, Kontakion of the Saints; Both now, of the Feast. Prokeimenon of the tone; and of the Saints, Tone 4: "Marvelous is God in His saints, the God of Israel." Epistle to the Galatians, section 200 [Gal 1:11–19]. Alleluia, Tone 4: "Remember, O Lord, David..." Gospel according to Matthew, section 4 [Mt 2:13–23]; and then the Sunday in course. Communion verse: "Praise the Lord from the heavens." Another: "Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous."*[^530]

*Sunday after the Nativity of Christ. We celebrate the memory of the holy and righteous Joseph the Betrothed, and David the King, and James the Brother of the Lord.*
*It should be known: If this Sunday occurs after the Nativity of Christ on the 26th, or the 27th, or the 28th, or the 29th, or the 30th day:*
*On Saturday at Little Vespers, the Resurrection Stichera and of the Mother of God, according to custom.*
*At Great Vespers, after the usual Psalm [Ps 103], we sing the 1st Kathisma entirely. At "Lord, I have cried," Resurrection Stichera, 3; and of the Feast, 4: those sung on the feast itself; and of the Saints, 3, Tone 1. Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Небє́сныхъ чинѡ́въ):*
*Let us all praise the God-ancestor, David the king; for from him came forth the rod, the Virgin, and from her blossomed forth the flower, Christ, and He recalled Adam from corruption, as He is compassionate.*[^531]
*In old age Joseph the Betrothed clearly saw the prophetic predictions manifestly fulfilled; for he received in truth a strange revelation, having received the angels who cry aloud: Glory to God, Who has sent down peace upon the earth!*[^532]
*Let us all praise the Brother of the Lord, as a hierarch, who again shone forth valiantly through hieromartyrdom. By his prayers, O Jesus our God, Who wast swaddled in swaddling clothes in the cave, save all who sing Thy praise!*[^533]
*Glory, Tone 6:*
*We celebrate the memory of David and James, the pious king-prophet and the apostle, the first bishop; for having been delivered from delusion by their teachings, we hymn Christ, Who shone forth and was incarnate of the Virgin to save our souls.*[^534]
*Both now, Theotokion of the tone.*
*Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day. At the Litiya, Stichera of the Feast, those sung on the feast itself. Glory, Both now: "The Persian Magi..." At the Aposticha, Resurrection Stichera. Glory, Tone 6:*
*The memory of the sacred ones and the dominion of kings and gladness was Thy Nativity; and boasting therein we say: Our Father, Who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name, O Lover of mankind!*[^535]
*Both now, the same tone:*
*Today the invisible nature is united unto men from the Virgin; today the boundless essence boundless essence is wrapped in swaddling clothes in Bethlehem. Today God leads the Magi by a star unto worship, prefiguring His three-day burial, as in gold, and myrrh, and frankincense, unto Whom we sing: O Christ God, Who wast incarnate of the Virgin, save our souls!*
*At the blessing of loaves, Troparion: "Thy Nativity, O Christ our God...", twice; and of the Saints, Tone 2, once: "Proclaim good tidings, O Joseph, unto David the God-ancestor of the wonders: thou hast seen a Virgin giving birth; with the shepherds thou hast given glory; with the Magi thou hast worshipped; having received the news from an angel, entreat Christ God to save our souls!"*[^536]
*And where there is no All-Night Vigil: At Compline, after the Trisagion, Kontakion of the God-ancestors; Glory, Both now, of the Feast. At Matins, at "God is the Lord," Resurrection Troparion, twice; Glory, of the Saints; Both now, of the Feast. After the kathismata, Resurrection Sessional Hymns, with their Theotokia. And reading in the Gospel Commentary, from Matthew, for the Sunday after the Nativity of Christ; or the Homily of Gregory of Nyssa on the Holy Trinity and on Abraham, in two parts. And we sing the Blameless [Psalm 118] and their troparia. Hypakoe of the tone. Gradual Antiphons and Prokeimenon of the tone. Resurrection Gospel. "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ." After Psalm 50, Resurrection Sticheron. Resurrection Canon with the heirmos on 4; and unto the Theotokos on 2; and of the Feast on 4; and the present Canon on 4: the work of Cosmas the Monk, Tone 4.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
*I will sing unto Thee, O Lord my God, for Thou hast led Thy people out from Egyptian bondage, and Thou hast overwhelmed Pharaoh's chariots and might.*[^537]
*Troparia:*
*Having formed Christmas dances unto Him Who was incarnate for our sake, with joy let us hymn James the Brother of the Lord, and David the God-ancestor.*
*The angelic choirs in Bethlehem stood before Joseph, singing "Glory in the highest," saying: With them let us hymn Him Who was well pleased to be incarnate!*[^538]
*O David, God-ancestor, with harps, having drawn along James the righteous, sing unto the Lord Who was incarnate from the root of Jesse.*[^539]
*Theotokion:*
*I will sing unto Thee, O Lord my God, for Thou wast born from a pure Virgin Mother, and hast shown her forth as the hope of our souls.*
*Katavasia: "Christ is born."*
*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
*O Christ God, the Confirmation of those who hope in Thee, establish us in Thy orthodox faith!*

...establish us, as Thou art the Lover of mankind.

Unto Christ God Who was born in the flesh from the Virgin without seed, let us all sing with the angels, crying aloud: Glory to God in the highest!

With David and James, O ye faithful, let us worthily honor with hymns the co-celebrated feast of Him Who emptied Himself for our sake.

As a bridegroom from his bridal chamber, from His Mother's womb David said that the Lord should come forth; Whom now with James let us hymn.[^540]

*Theotokion:*

Let us honor the unwedded Mother of God Mary, for through her the Sun of righteousness has shone forth upon us.

*Kontakion of the Feast, Tone 3:*

Today the Virgin gives birth unto the Transubstantial One, and the earth offers a cave unto the Unapproachable One; the angels with the shepherds give glory, and the Magi journey with the star; for for our sake is born a young Child, the Pre-eternal God.[^541]

*Ikos:*

Bethlehem has opened Eden, come let us behold; we have found food in secret; come let us receive the things of paradise within the cave: there the unwatered root has appeared, budding forth forgiveness; there the undug well has been found, from which David of old longed to drink; there the Virgin, having given birth unto the infant, has quenched straightway the thirst of Adam and David. Therefore let us go unto Him where He was born: a young Child, the Pre-eternal God.[^542]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 3, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дв҃а дне́сь):*

Unto righteous Joseph the Betrothed of the Virgin, and with David unto James, let us sing as is fitting; for having walked in a righteous path, they worthily attained the heavenly mansions, dancing with the angels, and they ask for us the forgiveness of sins.

*Glory, in the same tone and podoben (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*

The Virgin has given birth unto the Creator of all things, and the Magi come to worship Him in the flesh; men with the angels give glory; the cave and the manger offer gifts, hymning the One born: a young Child, the Pre-eternal God.[^543]

*Both now, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph marveled" (Оу҆диви́сѧ і҆ѡ́сифъ):*

The prophetic choir celebrates divinely; for the wonder that came to pass in thee, O Virgin: for thou hast borne upon earth God incarnate. Therefore the angels sing with the shepherds, and the Magi with faith cry aloud with Joseph: Wonders unto David the God-ancestor![^544]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

Preaching Thy coming, Thy manifestation on earth, O Christ God, the prophet cried aloud with gladness: Glory to Thy power,[^545] O Lord!

With the Magi let us worship Him Who was born, and with the angels and Joseph let us rejoice, crying aloud in a manner befitting God: Glory in the highest to Christ God!

Christ Who reigns over all kings, being born in the flesh from the seed of David, took chosen James as His brother, as He was well pleased.

The Lord Who appeared in the flesh from the Virgin has glorified together your memory, O holy ones: James, best among the apostles, and all-blessed David.

*Theotokion:*

Surpassing the ranks of the Cherubim, and having borne in the flesh God Who is carried in hands: Rejoice, unwedded Mother of God!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

O Thou Who hast shone forth light, and illuminated the morning, and displayed the day: Glory to Thee, glory to Thee, O Jesus, Son of God![^546]

*Troparia:*

O God incarnate Who wast well pleased to be born of a pure Virgin: Glory to Thee, glory to Thee! Joseph cried aloud.

O Thou Who wast born of the Virgin and hast made radiant the memory of David and James: Glory to Thee, glory to Thee, O Jesus, Son of God!

Him Whom the prophet David divinely inspired called the rain upon the fleece, James preached as Jesus, the Son of God.[^547]

*Theotokion:*

With unceasing voice creation offers the angel's greeting unto thee, O Virgin: Rejoice, pure Mother of Jesus, Son of God!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

Prefiguring the three-day burial, the prophet Jonah cried aloud, praying in the whale: Deliver me from corruption, O Jesus, King of hosts![^548]

*Troparia:*

The bodiless ranks stood in awe before the cave, and unceasingly sang of the most pure Nativity: Glory in the highest unto God Who was born!

Thou hast sat upon the throne, as Thou didst swear, O Master, unto the prophet David, having come forth from the fruit of his loins; and unto James Thou hast delivered the throne of the Church, O Christ.[^549]

David was marvelous as king and prophet, and was shown forth as forefather of the divine Incarnation; but James was the disciple of Jesus, more than the singer.[^550]

*Theotokion:*

We pray for thy servants, O Virgin Mother of God: entreat Him Who was incarnate of thee, for we know thee to be our only intercessor.

*Kontakion, Tone 3, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дв҃а дне́сь):*

Today the divine David is filled with gladness, and Joseph with James offers praise; for having received a crown through kinship with Christ, they rejoice, and they hymn Him Who was ineffably born upon earth, and they cry aloud: O Compassionate One, save those who honor Thee![^551]

*Ikos:*

By an ineffable counsel the Bodiless One is born in the flesh; the Uncircumscribed One is now circumscribed by a body, and He preserves both essences without change; He Who is by nature without beginning and alone eternal receives a beginning; He Who is all-perfect is seen as an infant; He Who carries all things is carried in hands. Therefore as God He crowns by His Nativity those honored through kinship with Him; and glorifying them in faith, we cry aloud unceasingly: O Compassionate One, save those who honor Thee![^552]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

The Abrahamic children of old in Babylon trampled down the furnace flame, crying aloud with hymns: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^553]

*Troparia:*

Marveling at the Nativity of the Mother of God Mary beyond expression, the angelic choirs cried aloud unto Joseph: Glory in the highest, and peace on earth!

David being the leader of the bride, and James the chamberlain of the divine Church, said: Blessed art Thou, O God, Who wast incarnate for our sake![^554]

The king among prophets and prophet among kings, with godly-wise James, cries aloud also with us: Blessed art Thou, O Christ, Who wast incarnate for our sake!

*Theotokion:*

In the unburnt bush and in the dew-giving furnace thou wast prefigured, O most pure Mother; without seed thou hast given birth unto God incarnate, O ever-blessed one.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

Christ the King, Whom the captive youths confessed, speaking in the furnace with a great voice: Praise the Lord, all ye works![^555]

*Troparia:*

Christ incarnate, Whom the heavenly powers glorified, and Joseph the Betrothed unceasingly hymns: Praise the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

Christ incarnate, Whom David the ancestor of God foretold, and James preached unto the peoples, crying: Praise the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

Unto Christ Who was born of the Virgin, and Who magnified the memory of David, and the hierarchic memory of James, as of His friends: Praise the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*

Christ the King, Whom the Mother of God Mary bore for us, and remained a pure Virgin after childbirth: Praise the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*At Ode 9, we sing: More honorable than the Cherubim.*
*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

Moses saw the unburnt bush upon the mountain; Joseph heard the ineffable birth within the cave, O undefiled Virgin, unwedded Mother; with hymns we magnify thee, O Mother of God![^556]

*Troparia:*

Unto Him Who was born of the Virgin all creation served with trembling: the heavens indeed with a star, and the earth with the manger; the mountain with the cave; the Magi with gifts; the shepherds with wonders; and the angels: Glory to God in the highest!

David of old was a king taken from the shepherds; and thou, O James, from the tribe of Judah and of the Church, wast shown forth as the shepherd of the flock of the incarnate One, the Lamb on high and the Son of God.

Rejoice now, O Bethlehem, having become the city of the new David; and Zion, proclaim the primacy of the churches, the common joy, having now received the King of all and His pleased servants!

*Theotokion:*

The angelic assemblies glorify thee, O Parent of God, and the human race unceasingly honors thee with hymns; for by thy divine childbirth thou hast united earthly things with the heavenly. Therefore we honor thee.

*Resurrection Exapostilarion. Glory, of the Saints, Tone 2, Podoben: "With the disciples let us go up" (Со ꙋ҆чн҃ки):*

With glorious James, the Brother of the Lord, let us hymn David the ancestor of God, and divine Joseph the Betrothed of the Mother of God; for they served Christ's divine Nativity in the city of Bethlehem in a manner befitting God, with angels, Magi, and shepherds, singing hymns unto Him as God and unto the Mother of God.[^557]

*Both now, of the Feast.*
*At the Praises, Stichera: Resurrection Stichera, 4; and of the Feast, 4, Tone 4, with the refrains of the Feast.*
*Glory, Tone 8:*

Blood, and fire, and vapor of smoke: the wonders on earth which Joel foresaw: blood, the Incarnation; fire, the Godhead; and the vapor of smoke, the Holy Spirit Who came upon the Virgin and filled the world with sweet fragrance. Great is the mystery of Thine enfleshment! O Lord, glory to Thee![^558]

*Both now: Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Mother of God...*
*Great Doxology. Resurrection Troparion, and dismissal. Evangelical Sticheron, First Hour, and final dismissal. At the Hours, Resurrection Troparion; Glory, of the Feast, and Both now, Theotokion; and Troparion of the Saints, alternating. After the Our Father, Kontakion of the Feast, and of the Saints, alternating. At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the tone on 4, and of the Feast on 4, and of the Saints, Ode 6 on 4. After the Entrance, Resurrection Troparion, and of the Feast, and of the Saints; Glory, Kontakion of the Saints;*

*...and Both now, of the Feast.*
*Prokeimenon of the tone; and of the Saints, Tone 4:* Marvelous is God in His saints, the God of Israel.[^559] *Verse:* In congregations bless ye God, the Lord from the springs of Israel. *Epistle to the Galatians, Pericope 200 [Gal 1:11–19]. Alleluia, Tone 4:* Remember, O Lord, David and all his meekness. *Gospel from Matthew, Pericope 4 [Mt 2:13–23]. Communion Hymn:* Praise the Lord... *Another:* Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous...

*Instruction concerning the Epistles and Gospels which occur on the Saturday and Sunday after the Nativity of Christ, and the other Saturday and Sunday before the Theophany:*

It should be known that if the Nativity of Christ occurs on a Sunday: then between the Nativity of Christ and the Theophany there is only one Saturday and Sunday; and we sing the Sunday after the Nativity of Christ on the day following the feast of the Nativity of Christ on Monday, December 26, as was indicated in sequence on Monday, the day following the feast. At the Liturgy we read the Epistle and Gospel of the Sunday after the Nativity of Christ. And for the Saturday after the Nativity of Christ, we read the Epistle and Gospel on Saturday at the Apodosis of the feast of the Nativity of Christ first; then of the Saturday before the Theophany; and the Prokeimenon, Alleluia, and Communion Hymn are of the Feast. And on January 1, we read the Prokeimenon, Epistle, and Gospel of the Sunday before the Theophany, as will be set forth in sequence in the present chapter.[^560]

*If the Nativity of Christ occurs on a Monday:*

Then between the Nativity of Christ and the Theophany there is one Saturday and one Sunday; and the Saturday after the Nativity of Christ occurs on December 30. At the Liturgy we read the Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, Gospel, and Communion Hymn first of the Saturday after the Nativity of Christ; then the Epistle and Gospel of the Saturday before the Theophany. And for the Sunday after the Nativity of Christ, we read at the Liturgy on the Apodosis of the feast of the Nativity of Christ the Epistle and Gospel as indicated in sequence. And for the Sunday before the Theophany, we read the Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel on January 1 as will be shown in sequence, when Circumcision and Basil occur on a Sunday.[^561]

*If the Nativity of Christ occurs on a Tuesday:*

Then between the Nativity of Christ and the Theophany there are two Saturdays. But only one Sunday, and the Saturday after the Nativity of Christ then occurs on December 29.

At the Liturgy we read the Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, Gospel, and Communion Hymn first of the Saturday after the Nativity of Christ, and thereafter of the Innocents. And of the Sunday after the Nativity of Christ, we sing the service on December 30, as indicated in sequence. And for the Sunday before the Theophany, we read the Matins Gospel, and at the Liturgy the Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel first on January 1, and thereafter of the Circumcision and of Basil together. *Communion Hymn:* Praise the Lord... *Another:* In everlasting memory...[^562]

*If the Nativity of Christ occurs on a Wednesday, or on a Thursday, or on a Friday:*

Then between the Nativity of Christ and the Theophany there are two Saturdays and two Sundays. On the first Sunday, the Epistle and Gospel are read for the Saturday and the Sunday after the Nativity of Christ. And on the second Saturday and Sunday, the Epistle and Gospel are read for the Saturday and the Sunday before the Theophany.[^563]

*If the Nativity of Christ occurs on a Saturday:*

Then between the Nativity of Christ and the Theophany there are two Sundays, but only one Saturday. And for the Sunday after the Nativity of Christ, we sing the service on the day following the Nativity of Christ on Sunday, as indicated in sequence. And the Apodosis of the Nativity of Christ then occurs on Friday; and we sing the service of the Apodosis of the Nativity of Christ, as indicated in sequence. Only at the Liturgy the Prokeimenon, Alleluia, and Communion Hymn are of the Feast; but the Epistle and Gospel are of the Saturday after the Nativity of Christ. And on the Saturday before the Theophany, at the Liturgy we read the Epistle and Gospel on January 1, first of the Circumcision, and thereafter of the Saturday before the Theophany.
