And on the morrow, on this present Sunday, at Matins we read the Gospel of the Sunday first, and thereafter in sequence. And at the Liturgy, the Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel are first of the Sunday before the Theophany; then of the Saint. And we read the daily reading combined under one pericope, if there be no postponement. *Communion Hymn:* Praise the Lord... *And of the Saint.*[^564]

*In the same month, on the 27th day: The Holy Apostle, Protomartyr, and Archdeacon Stephen; and our Venerable Father and Confessor Theodore the Branded, brother of Theophanes the Hymnographer.*
*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Apostle, 3; and of the Venerable One, 3.*
*Stichera of the Apostle, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́бля):*

Having illuminated thy mind with the grace of the Spirit, thou didst appear with an angelic countenance, O Stephen; for thy body shone with inner brightness, and revealed the dawn of thy soul unto those who beheld it; because of which thou didst also attain the vision of the light, the heavens having been gloriously opened unto thee, O beginning and boast of martyrs![^565]

As steps and a ladder unto the heavenly ascent were the stones cast at thee; ascending upon them thou didst behold the Lord standing at the right hand of the Father, stretching forth a crown that answers unto thy name with His life-bearing right hand; near Whom thou standest as a noble confessor and the chief of sufferers.[^566]

Shining with signs and wonders, and with dogmas, thou didst quench the council of the lawless; and being slain by them, and pelted with stones, thou didst pray for forgiveness for those who slew thee, imitating the voice of the Savior, into Whose hands thou didst commit thy spirit, O sacred Stephen.[^567]

*Other Stichera of the Venerable One, in the same tone and podoben (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*

Unto the wounds of wandering were added wounds unto thee, most grievous exiles, O venerable one, when he who unlawfully held the lawful throne fiercely troubled the laws of the faith and cast down the Savior's most pure icon; whom by divine grace thou didst put to shame, O pleased servant of Christ.[^568]

Neither prison nor confinement, nor dismal darkness, nor wounds nor beatings, O father, were able to separate thee from the love of God, O Theodore; neither a severe, lingering, and intolerable sickness, nor lack of food, O divinely speaking one; but thou didst endure steadfastly, foreseeing the reward of thy labors.[^569]

Instead of sorrow, relief; instead of pains, delight instead of darkness, illumination has the righteous Arbiter of the contest granted unto thee; and instead of the brand engraved upon thy face, thou hast been written in the book of life, and enrolled in the Church of the firstborn in the highest, and hast come with great joy unto the festal assembly of the angels.[^570]

*Glory, Tone 2. By Anatolius:*

Unto the King and Master of all born upon earth, a most radiant crown is offered: fashioned not from precious stones, but blossomed from his own blood. But, O ye lovers of the martyrs, come, taking flowers of song, let us crown our heads, and singing hymns let us say: O thou who didst enlighten thy soul with wisdom and grace, protomartyr of Christ God, ask peace for us, and great mercy![^571]

*Both now, in the same tone:*

A great and most glorious wonder has been accomplished today: the Virgin gives birth, and her womb suffers no corruption; the Word is incarnate, and is not separated from the Father. The angels with the shepherds give glory, and with them we cry aloud: Glory to God in the highest, and peace on earth!

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Не́бныхъ чинѡ́въ):*

Him Who shone forth from the Father before the ages, and Who as the Son is ever in the Father's bosom; and again in the latter times sits upon His Mother's arms as upon a throne, and is now worshipped by angels, shepherds, and Magi: let us hymn Him![^572]

*Verse:* From the womb before the morning star have I begotten Thee.

Coming together in Bethlehem, O ye faithful, let us behold the Creator of all lying in the manger, unto Whom those from the Chaldean land brought a chosen three-part gift: as unto King, and God, and One Who for our sake would be three days dead.[^573]

*Verse:* The Lord said unto my Lord: Sit Thou at My right hand.

Thou wast born of the Virgin in a cave, and the angelic hosts standing around cried aloud: Glory in the highest to Thee, O God, Who wast born in the form of a servant and hast renewed the world in the womb of the Virgin, an unwedded Mother!

*Glory, Tone 6. By Anatolius:*

Thou wast shown forth as the first among martyrs and among deacons, O Stephen the apostle, adornment of sufferers, confirmation of the faithful, glory of the righteous: as thou standest before the throne of Christ the King of all, ask for those who celebrate thy honorable memory cleansing of transgressions, and vouchsafing of the Heavenly Kingdom.[^574]

*Both now, in the same tone. By Germanus:*

All the angels make merry in heaven, and men rejoice today; and all creation leaps for joy for the sake of the Savior and Lord born in Bethlehem; for all deceit of idols has ceased, and Christ reigns unto the ages![^575]

*Troparion of the Saint, Tone 4:*

Thou didst fight the good fight, O protomartyr of Christ and apostle, and didst expose the impiety of the torturers; for being stoned by the hands of lawless men, thou didst receive a crown from the right hand on high, and didst cry out unto God, saying: Lord, lay not this sin to their charge![^576]

*Glory, of the Venerable One, Troparion, Tone 8:*

Guide of Orthodoxy, teacher of piety and purity, light of the universe, divinely inspired adornment of monastics, all-wise Theodore: by thy teachings thou hast enlightened all, O spiritual pipe; entreat Christ God that our souls may be saved![^577]

*Both now, of the Feast: Thy Nativity, O Christ our God...*
*At Matins, at "God is the Lord," Troparion of the Feast, twice; and of the Apostle, once; Glory, of the Venerable One; Both now, of the Feast.*
*After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 3, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дв҃а дне́сь):*

The seedless conception brings forth the Deliverer; and the Magi come to worship the Life; men with the angels give glory; the cave and the manger bring gifts, hymning the One born: a young Child, the Pre-eternal God.[^578]

*Glory, Both now, the same.*
*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph marveled" (Оу҆диви́ся і҆ѡ́сифъ):*

How was the Incomprehensible One everywhere contained in a womb? How was He Who is in the Father's bosom held in a Mother's arms? Entirely as He knows, as He willed, and as He was well pleased! For being bodiless He was incarnate voluntarily, and He Who is became what He was not for our sake; and without departing from His nature He partook of our compound nature. In twofold nature Christ was born, desiring to fulfill the world on high.[^579]

*Glory, Both now, the same.*
*First Canon of the Feast, with the heirmos on 6; and of the Saints, two canons, on 8.*
*Canon of the Feast, Tone 1. Ode 1. Heirmos:*

Christ is born, glorify Him! Christ from heaven, go ye forth to meet Him! Christ upon earth, be ye lifted up! Sing unto the Lord, all the earth, and praise Him with gladness, O ye peoples, for He has been glorified![^580]

*Troparia:*

Him who was made according to the image of God, corrupted through transgression and become wholly of corruption, fallen from the better divine life, the wise Creator renews again, for He has been glorified.

Beholding man perishing, whom He had created with His hands, the Maker bowed the heavens and came down; and He took substance wholly from the divine and pure Virgin, being truly incarnate, for He has been glorified.

The Wisdom, Word, and Power, being the Son and Radiance of the Father, Christ God, hidden from the powers both of heaven and earth, and having become man, has renewed us, for He has been glorified.

*Canon of the Apostle. The work of John of Damascus, Tone 5. Ode 1. Heirmos:*

The horse and his rider into the Red Sea, He Who shatters wars with a high arm, Christ shook out; but He saved Israel, singing a song of victory.[^581]

*Troparia:*

Come, let us gloriously crown with crowns of hymns the protomartyr of Christ of the Church; and being crowned by Stephen's divine grace, let us sing a song of victory.[^582]

Bearing the Teacher's meek disposition, and the deifying humility born of love, thou wast worthily, O Stephen, the elder among deacons, and the protector of widows.[^583]

Thou wast worthily summoned to the assistance of the apostles of Christ, and wast a faithful deacon, O Stephen who bearest the name of crown, having passed by blood to where Christ is.

*Theotokion:*

Thou indeed for men's sake, O Christ, having assumed humanity from the Virgin, wast swaddled as an infant; and Thy protomartyr, assailed by the hurling of stones, hastens to strip off the body.[^584]

*Another Canon of the Venerable One, the acrostic of which is: "I weave close praises for thee, my brother. Theophanes." Tone 4. Ode 1. Heirmos:*

Israel of old traversed the Red Sea's deep with unwetted feet, and by Moses' arms outstretched in the form of a cross, overcame the power of Amalek in the wilderness.[^585]

*Troparia:*

Beholding the inscription upon thy honorable face, the Cherubim step back from the Tree of life, and the flaming sword most reverently turns its back to thee, O all-wise Theodore![^586]

The title lay above the head of Christ the King, written upon the wood of the Cross; and thine inscription, O all-wise one, was traced upon thy face, written in a manner befitting God.[^587]

The Lord indeed was lifted up upon the Cross, and was pierced in His side; and thou, stretched out upon a bench *patiently didst endure the scourgings, marked out like a chosen ram, O initiate of sacred mysteries.*[^588]
*Adorned with all wisdom, O Father Theodore, thou didst refute the leader of the beast-like heresy; and by the endurance of thy deeds thou didst strike terror into his presumptuous conceit.*[^589]
*Theotokion:*
*Thou wast the receptacle of transcendent Wisdom, O all-pure Mother of God, sole salvation and song of the faithful; for today thou hast borne for us the divine Redemption.*
*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
*Unto the Son begotten of the Father before the ages without corruption, and in these last days incarnate without seed from the Virgin, unto Christ God let us cry aloud: Thou Who hast exalted our horn, holy art Thou, O Lord!*[^590]
*Troparia:*
*Earthy Adam, who partook of the superior inbreathing and slipped into corruption through womanly deceit, beholding Christ born of woman, cries out: O Thou Who for my sake becamest as I am, holy art Thou, O Lord!*
*Conformed to our clayey lowliness, O Christ, by the commingling, and through partaking of the inferior flesh having imparted of the divine nature; having become earthly while remaining God, and having exalted our horn, holy art Thou, O Lord!*
*Rejoice, O Bethlehem, being king among the princes of Judah; for He Who shepherds Israel upon the shoulders of the Cherubim has come forth openly from thee, Christ; and having exalted our horn, He has reigned over all.*
*Another [Canon of the Protomartyr, Tone 5]. Ode 3. Heirmos:*
*Thou Who by Thy command didst establish the earth upon nothing, and didst suspend its weight unrestrained, establish Thy Church upon the immovable rock of Thy commandments, O Christ, Who alone art good and the Lover of mankind!*[^591]
*Troparia:*
*Lawfully arrayed as a soldier of Christ against the God-slayers, and clad in His unconquerable power, Stephen refuted all the crafty opposition of the lawless.*
*Kindled with the zeal of Christ's love and stripped for the contests, filled with faith and the divine Spirit, O protomartyr, thou didst most bravely expose to all their God-slaying preaching.*
*As a preacher truly of the hidden and divine life, as though forgetting the present one, the protomartyr showed forth openly to all by deeds the victorious truth, having chosen death.*
*Theotokion:*
*For our sake the Good One entered into the cave of this life by the manner of His descent; and Stephen, the leader of the martyrs, departs from human heaviness, overcome by loving-kindness.*

*Another [Canon of the Venerable One, Tone 4]. Ode 3. Heirmos:*
*Thy Church rejoices in Thee, O Christ, crying aloud: Thou art my strength, O Lord, and my refuge and foundation!*[^592]
*Troparia:*
*Having nothing wherewith to contradict thy teachings, O venerable one, he who was full of pagan fury turned to inflicting wounds.*
*Thou didst patiently surrender thyself, O divinely inspired one, to wounds upon thy shoulders and chest for Christ's sake, and to blows upon the head.*
*By spiritual wisdom and fervency of mind, thou didst put to shame the wicked and lawless one through thy most sacred dogmas.*
*Theotokion:*
*David, as an ark in Bethlehem, with prophetic eyes, O Mother of God, sees thee bearing the super-divine Infant.*[^593]
*Kontakion of the Feast, Tone 3:*
*Today the Virgin gives birth to the Transcendent in essence, and the earth offers a cave to the Unapproachable; angels with shepherds give glory, and the Magi journey with a star; for for our sake is born a young Child, the pre-eternal God.*[^594]
*Ikos:*
*Bethlehem has opened Eden, come, let us behold; we have found food in secret; come, let us receive the things of paradise within the cave: there the unwatered root appeared, blossoming forth forgiveness; there was found the undug well from which David of old longed to drink; there the Virgin, having brought forth an Infant, quenched the thirst of Adam and David. Therefore let us go unto Him where He was born: a young Child, the pre-eternal God.*
*Sessional Hymn of the Protomartyr, Tone 1. Podoben: "Thy tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й сп҃се):*
*Apostle of Christ, first among deacons, wise protomartyr, crown of the martyrs, thou didst sanctify the ends of the world by thy sufferings, and by miracles thou didst enlighten the souls of men: deliver from all tribulations those who honor thee, O all-praised Stephen.*
*Glory... Sessional Hymn of the Venerable One, Tone 3. Podoben: "Of the divine faith" (Бж҃е́ственныѧ вѣ́ры):*
*Thou wast a mouth of boldness, having high-mindedly put to shame the pride of the torturers by the endurance of thy sufferings; for having been wounded in thy face, O Theodore, for the most honorable icon of Christ, thou didst proclaim unto all to honor and glorify it, asking for us great mercy.*
*Both now... Theotokion:*
*Beholding the seedless Nativity, the all-undefiled one in wonder spoke unto Him Who was born of her: Though Thou art clothed in human form yet the elements proclaim Thee as God, O Child without beginning, co-beginningless with the Father without beginning: grant Thou great mercy unto all!*
*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
*A rod from the root of Jesse, and a blossom therefrom, O Christ, Thou hast budded forth from the Virgin; from the praised mountain overshadowed by the forest Thou hast come, incarnate from her that knew not man, O Immaterial One and God: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!*[^595]
*Troparia:*
*He Whom Jacob of old foretold, the Expectation of the nations, O Christ, Thou hast shone forth from the tribe of Judah, and Thou hast come to plunder the power of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria, transforming deceit into divine faith: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!*
*By the words of Balaam the soothsayer of old, Thou didst fill the wise stargazers with joy, O Master, having shone forth as a Star out of Jacob; and Thou didst openly receive the firstfruits of the Gentiles being brought in: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!*
*As rain upon the fleece didst Thou descend into the Virgin's womb, O Christ, and like drops falling upon the earth; Ethiopia and Tarshish, the Arabian islands, Sheba, and they that rule the whole land of the Medes fell down before Thee, O Savior: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!*
*Another [Canon of the Protomartyr, Tone 5]. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
*Perceiving Thy divine self-emptying foresightly, O Christ, Habakkuk cried out to Thee with trembling: For the salvation of Thy people, to save Thine anointed ones, art Thou come!*[^596]
*Troparia:*
*Having emulated the angelic zeal, thou wast brightly adorned with an angelic countenance, and thou beholdest the divine glory and its illumination.*
*The slanderer, judge, and torturer shows himself to be a murderer and the father of lies, O Stephen; yet he defeats himself, spreading nets against his own self.*
*As the first of the martyrs, having opened for us the entrance to martyrdom, Stephen dances crowned with the victor's wreath, crowned with the wreath of martyrdom.*
*Theotokion:*
*Having shone forth from the Virgin like the sun, O Christ, Thou dost adorn with Thine own brightness the glorious memory of the protomartyr, which has shone forth together with Thee like the daystar.*
*Another [Canon of the Venerable One, Tone 4]. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
*Beholding Thee lifted up upon the Cross, O Sun of righteousness, the Church stood in her station, worthily crying aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!*[^597]
*Troparia:*
*Stretched out upon a board, thou wast inscribed, O Theodore, as a venerator of the icon of Christ and of the Mother of God, through insolent ferocity and barbaric cruelty.*[^598]
*Having served the Master from thy youth, O blessed one, and possessing unceasing desire for Him, through self-mastery thou wast forthwith most brightly adorned with martyric blood.*
*Radiant as the sun, O God-bearer, Thou didst hasten from the East, emitting the beams of thy confession and of thy high-minded and most valiant resistance.*
*Theotokion:*
*Blessed is God the Word Who comes into Bethlehem, being compassionate, from thy womb that knew not wedlock, O all-pure one; beseech Him now to save those who flee unto thee.*
*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
*Being the God of peace and Father of mercies, Thou hast sent unto us the Angel of Thy great Counsel, granting peace; therefore, guided to the light of the knowledge of God, watching early from the night, we glorify Thee, O Lover of mankind!*[^599]
*Troparia:*
*Among servants by Caesar's decree didst Thou submit to be enrolled, and Thou hast freed us who were slaves of the enemy and of sin, O Christ; and having become entirely poor for our sake, Thou hast deified the earthy one through the very union and communion.*
*Behold, the Virgin, as was said of old, having conceived in her womb, has given birth to God incarnate, and she remains a virgin; through whom we sinners having been reconciled unto God, let us the faithful hymn her as truly the Mother of God.*
*Another [Canon of the Protomartyr, Tone 5]. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
*O Thou Who clothest Thyself with light as with a garment, unto Thee I rise early, and to Thee I cry: Enlighten my darkened soul, O Christ, for Thou alone art compassionate!*[^600]
*Troparia:*
*Thy protomartyr shone like an angel, having surpassed the beauty of the blameless, O Christ, and being filled with Thine ineffable glory, O Lover of mankind.*
*By the downpours of his divinely eloquent lips, the protomartyr cast down the defiled murderers, by whose countless downpours of stones he was crowned as a victor.*
*How unconquerable was the boldness of the protomartyr's divine zeal! For even unto blood he manly arrayed himself against the God-slayers.*
*Theotokion:*
*The protomartyr beheld Him Who came forth from the unwedded Mother standing in the heavens in the unchangeable divinity and glory of the Father.*
*Another [Canon of the Venerable One, Tone 4]. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
*Thou, my Lord, hast come into the world as a light, a holy light turning those who hymn Thee in faith from the dark gloom of ignorance.*[^601]
*Troparia:*
*Dwelling in a strange land, thou didst patiently submit to wandering, affliction, wounds, banishments, and the cruellest of prisons.*
*Now truly rejoicing, having received the victorious crowning on the bright and light-bearing day of the divine protomartyr.*
*The promise of piety which thou didst have from childhood, thou didst keep even unto the end, remaining uncorrupted, O invincible Theodore.*
*Theotokion:*
*Thee do we set forth as an invincible weapon against enemies; thee have we gained as the helper and hope of our salvation, O Bride of God!*
*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
*From the belly the sea monster vomited forth Jonah like an infant, just as it had received him; and the Word, having dwelt in the Virgin and taken flesh, came forth keeping her incorrupt; for He suffered not corruption, and preserved unharmed her that bore Him.*[^602]
*Troparia:*
*Christ our God has come, having become incarnate, Whom the Father begat from the womb before the daystar; holding the governance of the undefiled hosts, He lies in a beasts' manger and is wrapped in swaddling bands, yet looses the tangled bonds of our transgressions.*
*As a young child of our human compound, from Adam a Son was born and given unto the faithful; He is the Father and Ruler of the age to come, and is called the Angel of Great Counsel; He is the mighty God, holding all creation in His power.*
*Another [Canon of the Protomartyr, Tone 5]. Ode 6. Heirmos:*
*Raging with a soul-corrupting tempest, O Master Christ, calm the sea of passions, and bring me up from corruption, for Thou art compassionate!*[^603]
*Troparia:*
*The glorious leader of the martyrs' choir, Stephen, O ye faithful, having surpassed the laws of nature by grace, is illuminated with divine glory.*
*Having become the most excellent emulator of Thy honorable passions, O Master Christ, Stephen avenged himself upon his murderers with a blessing.*
*Preserve us free from any part in defiled murderous deeds, O Christ, and vouchsafe Thy singers the heritage of the protomartyr, for Thou art compassionate.*
*Theotokion:*
*Thy nativity, O Master Christ, became the beginning of the world's salvation, and the foundation of the divine confession for the martyrs.*
*Another [Canon of the Venerable One, Tone 4]. Ode 6. Heirmos:*
*I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord, the Church cries aloud unto Thee, having been cleansed from demonic blood through the blood that flowed from Thy side for mercy's sake.*[^604]
*Troparia:*
*Still dripping with the sweat of contests thou didst stand before the Contest-master, Who governs all creation with righteous judgment, O God-bearing and all-blessed Theodore.*
*Nothing separated thee from the love of Christ: neither the wounding of the body, nor the menace of the sentence of death, nor the vain threats of the assessors, O all-blessed Theodore.*
*Being a son both of the light and of the most radiant day, full of light thou didst pass away, ever advancing towards the divine radiance, failing not day and night, O God-accepted one.*
*Theotokion:*
*Finding thee alone in the midst of thorns, as a most pure lily and a flower of the valley, O Mother of God, the spiritual Bridegroom dwelt in thee.*
*Kontakion of the Protomartyr, Tone 3. Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дв҃а дне́сь):*
*Yesterday the Master came to us in the flesh, and today the servant departs from the flesh; yesterday the King was born in the flesh, today the servant is stoned with stones: therefore also is perfected the protomartyr and divine Stephen.*[^605]
*Ikos:*
*Like a radiant star today, the protomartyr Stephen shone forth together with the Nativity of Christ; shining upon and enlightening the ends of the earth, he confounded all the Jewish wickedness alone; having refuted them by the wisdom of his word, reasoning from the Scriptures and persuading them that Jesus, born of the Virgin, is the Son of God and God: thus the protomartyr and divine Stephen put to shame their impious villainy.*
*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
*The youths reared together in piety, disdaining the ungodly decree, were not afraid of the threat of fire; but standing in the midst of the flame, they sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!*[^606]
*Troparia:*
*The shepherds piping their pipes received an awe-inspiring radiance of light, for the glory of the Lord shone round about them, and the angel cried aloud: Sing ye, for Christ is born, the blessed God of our fathers!*
*Suddenly, at the angel's word, the heavenly hosts cried aloud: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will among men! Christ has shone forth, the blessed God of our fathers!*
*What is this saying? said the shepherds; let us go over and see what has come to pass, the divine Christ! And having reached Bethlehem, they worshipped together with her that bore Him, singing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!*
*Another [Canon of the Protomartyr, Tone 5]. Ode 7. Heirmos:*
*The supremely exalted Lord of our fathers quenched the flame and bedewed the youths who sang in unison: Blessed art Thou, O God!*[^607]
*Troparia:*
*Gnashing their teeth murderously, the lawless ones, having seized Stephen like beasts, killed him as he divinely sang: Blessed art Thou, O God!*
*As with variegated and fair flowers, O Stephen, being adorned with stones, thou didst offer thyself unto Christ the Life-giver, singing: Blessed art Thou, O God!*
*How unconquerable was Paul's resistance, who at first persecuted the servants of God, yet now leads the Gentiles unto Christ unto ages!*[^608]
*Held fast by the Holy Spirit, O Stephen, thou didst ineffably behold the Son with the Father, crying to the Trinity: Blessed art Thou, O God!*
*Theotokion:*
*Unto Thee Who didst shine forth from the divine pure Virgin, a living wreath was offered as unto a King, divinely singing hymns unto Thee: Blessed art Thou, O God!*
*Another [Canon of the Venerable One, Tone 4]. Ode 7. Heirmos:*
*In the Persian furnace, the Abrahamic children, consumed rather by the love of piety than by the flame, cried aloud: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!*[^609]
*Troparia:*
*Kindled with Orthodox zeal, O all-wise one, thou didst boldly cast away the communion of the foul and bitter heresy, crying: Blessed art Thou, O my God and Lord!*
*The word of wisdom, the word of dogmas, the word of knowledge, the word of teachings most pious, O Father, God the Word granted unto thee, as thou didst cry: Blessed art Thou, O my God and Lord!*
*Having shone forth from the East like the sun, thou didst sow upon the earth the ray of piety, the veneration of Christ's icon, illuminating and teaching all, O Father Theodore.*
*Theotokion:*
*Adorned and supremely glorified, radiant with the light of virginity, thou wast revealed as the Mother, having borne God in the body and swaddled in swaddling bands Him Who visibly wraps all things.*
*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
*The dew-bearing furnace portrayed the image of a supernatural wonder; for it burned not the youths whom it received, even as the fire of the Godhead burned not the Virgin's womb into which He entered. Therefore singing hymns let us sing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!*[^610]
*Troparia:*
*The daughter of Babylon draws unto herself from Sion the captive children of David but she sends the Magi children as gift-bearers, entreating David's God-accepted daughter. Therefore singing hymns let us sing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!*
*The instruments of music turned aside mournful songs, for Sion's children sang not in a strange land; but Christ, having shone forth in Bethlehem, looses all Babylonian deceit and musical bands. Therefore singing hymns let us sing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!*
*Babylon took the spoils of Sion's kingdom and its captive wealth; but Christ draws unto Sion the treasures thereof, and its kings, the stargazers, guided by a star. Therefore singing hymns let us sing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!*
*Another [Canon of the Protomartyr, Tone 5]. Ode 8. Heirmos:*
*Unto Thee, the Creator of all, the children in the furnace, having formed a universal choir, sang: Praise the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!*[^611]
*Troparia:*
*Come, illuminated in mind with Stephen's glory, let us sing unto God Who was incarnate: Praise the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!*
*For thee, O Stephen, as victor over exceeding lawless deceit, the crown of sufferings was woven; therefore thou didst cry aloud: Praise the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!*
*Christ appeared unto thee in the Father's glory, openly proclaiming unto thee the rewards of thy sufferings; therefore thou didst cry aloud: Praise the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!*
*The bountiful Nativity and the memory of the protomartyr have woven for us a festive choir; therefore unceasingly we praise the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!*
*Theotokion:*
*Thee Who beyond understanding didst divinely-humanly give birth to the Lord by the Word, and art suckling a child: all works bless thee, O Virgin, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!*
*Another [Canon of the Venerable One, Tone 4]. Ode 8. Heirmos:*
*Daniel stretched forth his hands and shut the lions' gaping mouths in the pit; and the children, lovers of piety, girded with virtue, quenched the power of fire, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!*[^612]
*Troparia:*
*Relying on firmness of soul like a lion, O all-blessed one, thou didst not fear the heretical onslaught, the frenzy of him whose name is rage; and having spat in his face, rejoicing thou didst cry aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!*[^613]
*Having adorned thy soul with courage, and thy desire with chastity, O blessed one, having acquired a mind full of understanding, thou didst accomplish thy course and having directed thy thoughts by righteousness, thou didst cry aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!*
*Thou didst dry up the impetuously flowing stream of heresy, O Father, by thy instructions, O venerable one, and by all-wise demonstrations tearing down the subtleties of the wicked, crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!*
*Theotokion:*
*God, Who created human nature in the beginning, clothes Himself therein from thy most pure and holy womb, O all-undefiled one, being born today prophetically in Bethlehem; therefore we all bless thee, O Mary, Bride of God!*
*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
*A strange and most glorious mystery do I behold: the cave is heaven; the Cherubic throne, the Virgin; the manger, the receptacle in which lay the uncontained Christ God, Whom praising we magnify!*[^614]
*Troparia:*
*Beholding the marvelous course of an unusual new star shining anew, enlightening the heavens, the Magi saw signified Christ the King upon earth, born in Bethlehem for our salvation.*
*When the Magi said: Where is the newborn Child King, Whom the star revealed? For we have come to worship Him: Herod was troubled and enraged, raging as a fighter against God to slay Christ.*
*Herod inquired the time of the star, through whose guidance the Magi in Bethlehem worshipped Christ with gifts; and being guided by it unto their own country, they left the cruel child-slayer mocked.*
*Another [Canon of the Protomartyr, Tone 5]. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
*Rejoice, O Isaiah: the Virgin has conceived in her womb and brought forth a Son, Emmanuel, God and man, Dayspring is His name; Whom magnifying, we call the Virgin blessed.*[^615]
*Troparia:*
*Thou hast surpassed every rank of praises, O Stephen, and in every word thou truly bearest the trophies of victory; for the human mind is unable to weave a crown of praises worthy of thee.*
*O thy blessed voice which thou didst utter, O Stephen, crying aloud: Lay not this sin to the charge of my murderers, O Master Christ; but as God and Creator, receive my spirit as a most sweet-smelling sacrifice!*
*Thou hast received the reward of thy sufferings, the victor's crown from the Almighty right hand; and now, O all-blessed one, standing before the King of all, do thou crown with glory and grace those who honor thee.*
*Theotokion:*
*The timeless Son of the Father received in the flesh from the Virgin the beginning of temporal existence; for Whose sake Stephen, the emulator of Christ, being slain has now inherited eternal life from the beginning.*
*Another [Canon of the Venerable One, Tone 4]. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
*A cornerstone was cut out from thee, O unquarried mountain, Virgin, even Christ, Who has united separated natures; therefore rejoicing, we magnify thee, O Mother of God!*[^616]
*Troparia:*
*Overcome by divine desire, thou didst easily endure the arrays of persecutions, O divinely wise one; and having cast down the persecutor's ferocity, thou didst receive the crown of contests, O Father.*
*Thou hast found heavenly wealth and an abiding dwelling place in exchange for bitter exile, wandering, and journeys, and now receiving the eternal delight that nourishes thee.*
*Offering hymns and supplications to the Master, O Father, cease not to pray for my weakness, and for our co-dwellers and thy brethren, that having lived together we may together attain deification.*[^617]
*Theotokion:*
*Thee Who beyond mind and word didst today bear God the Word in Bethlehem, O Virgin, and didst wrap Him in swaddling bands, as truly the Maiden of God and Mother of God we magnify!*
*Exapostilarion of the Protomartyr. Podoben: "In spirit in the sanctuary" (Дꙋ́хомъ во ст҃и́лищи):*
*Thou didst behold the Word without beginning standing at the right hand of the Father, and thou didst fill thy face with ineffable light, O praise of apostles and glory of martyrs; and thou wast adorned with a crown by the hurling of stones, and didst receive a divine end.*[^618]
*Glory, Both now... Exapostilarion of the Feast:*
*He was laid in a manger, having become an infant as a child; and a star summoned the trinity of Magi; the shepherds marveled at the wonder, and hastened to see God become man; and the angelic choirs marveled, crying aloud: Glory in the highest!*
*At the Praises, Stichera on 6, idiometic. Tone 1:*
*By Cyprian:*
*Let us the faithful weave a martyric crown for the protomartyr from spiritual flowers; for he prepared the way for the martyrs, and in joy cried aloud: Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of God standing at the right hand of the invisible Father!*[^619]
*Tone 2. By Anatolius:*
*First among deacons, first also among martyrs didst thou show thyself, O all-honorable Stephen; for thou wast the way for the saints, and didst bring many martyrs unto the Lord; therefore heaven was opened unto thee, and God appeared unto thee: beseech Him to save our souls.*[^620]
*Clothed in holiness, O blessed Stephen, protomartyr and apostle, protomartyr and archdeacon, partaker with the angels: intercede and pray for us unto the Savior, the sinless Lord.*
*Let us worthily honor Stephen, the protomartyr and good pleasing servant of Christ, the archdeacon; for he, standing in the midst of the lawless, beheld the Son at the right hand of the Father.*
*Tone 4. By John the Monk:*
*O glorious Stephen, citizen of heaven, blessed pleasing servant of Christ, make prayer for our souls.*
*Tone the same:*
*Stephen, the good beginning of the martyrs, full of grace and power, did signs and great wonders among the people; he was stoned with stones by the lawless, but he shone forth like an angel. And he beheld the glory of Thee Who wast crucified for our sake, at the right hand of Power; and by the Spirit of grace he was lifted up unto the heavens; and therefore, taking up his abode in the angelic choirs, he prays that our souls may be saved.*
*Glory... Tone 6. By Cyprian:*
*O protomartyr, apostle, and archdeacon, door of the martyrs, and glory of the righteous, boast of the apostles: standing in the judgment hall, thou didst behold the heavens opened, and the Son of God standing at the right hand of the invisible Father. Therefore, having shone forth in countenance like an angel, in joy thou didst cry aloud concerning those who stoned thee: Lay not this sin to their charge! And now, ask for those who praise thee in love the cleansing of sins and great mercy.*
*Both now... Tone the same. By John the Monk:*
*An incomprehensible mystery is accomplished today in Bethlehem: the Invisible is seen, the Incorporeal is incarnate, the Word becomes gross, and He Who is becomes that which He was not. The Virgin brings forth a young Child in the cave, the Creator of nature. For the manger prefigures the heavenly throne; the beasts prefigure the standing of the Cherubim; the shepherds marvel, the Magi offer gifts. The angels singing aloud say: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will among men, Emmanuel unchanging!*[^621]
*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2. Podoben: "Ye angelic forces" (А҆́ггельскїѧ си̑лы):*
*All creation keeps the feast of the Nativity with joy, and the heavens rejoice with us; for in the manger the Creator, being incarnate of the Virgin, was seen most gloriously as an Infant in Bethlehem of Judea. Ye peoples, let us say: Blessed art Thou Who wast born, O our God, glory to Thee!*

*Verse: From the womb before the morning star have I begotten Thee.*
*That Thou mightest make the earthly heavenly, Thou didst come upon the earth, incarnate of the Virgin, and wast seen as an Infant, being the pre-eternal Word. Thou didst stir up the Magi from Persia unto Thine adoration, O Compassionate One; with whom we cry aloud: Blessed art Thou Who wast born, O our God, glory to Thee!*
*Verse: The Lord said unto My Lord: Sit Thou at My right hand.*
*As a young Child for our sake didst Thou appear, O Jesus, having shone forth from the Father before the ages, desiring to renew all men grown old through transgression. Therefore unto Thee we all gratefully cry aloud: Blessed art Thou Who wast born, O our God, glory to Thee!*
*Glory... Tone 8. By Cyprian:*
*Rejoice in the Lord, O crown-bearer Stephen, imitator of the Master; for thou wast also the protomartyr of Christ our King, and didst abolish the deceit of the lawless Judeans, praying for us unto the Lord.*
*Both now... Tone the same. By John the Monk:*
*How shall I utter the great mystery? The Incorporeal is incarnate, the Word becomes gross, the Invisible is seen, and the Impalpable is touched; and He Who is without beginning begins; the Son of God becomes the Son of man: Jesus Christ, the same yesterday and today, and unto the ages.*
*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Feast, Ode 4, on 4; and of the Saint, Ode 6, on 4. Prokeimenon of the Feast, and until the Apodosis. And of the Apostle, Tone 8: Their sound is gone out into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world.*[^622]
*Verse: The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of His hands.*
*Epistle in the Acts, Pericope 17.*
*Alleluia, Tone 4: The heavens shall confess Thy wonders, O Lord.*
*Gospel according to Matthew, Pericope 87.*
*Communion Hymn of the Feast, and until the Apodosis; and of the Apostle: Their sound is gone out into all the earth In the same month, on the 28th day: The Holy Twenty Thousand Martyrs, burned in Nicomedia.*
*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Feast, Tone 5. Podoben: "Rejoice" (Ра́дуйсѧ):*
*Thou bearest Adam's form, being all-perfect in the form of God; and Thou desirest to be held by hands, Who by Thy hand holdest all things by Thy power. The pure, all-undefiled one spoke, saying: How shall I swaddle Thee with swaddling bands as an infant? How shall I suckle Thee, Who nourishest all things? How shall I marvel at Thy poverty passing understanding? How shall I call Thee my Son, being now Thy handmaid? I hymn, I bless Thee, Who grantest great mercy unto the world!*
*Beholding the pre-eternal God incarnate from her as an Infant, holding Him with her hands and kissing His humanity, and being filled with joy, the all-undefiled one spoke unto Him: O Most High God, invisible King, how do I behold Thee, and cannot comprehend the mystery of Thy boundless poverty? For a most humble cave, and this one belonging to strangers, contains Thee within, Who art born without breaking the seals of virginity, having preserved the womb as before birth, and Who grantest great mercy!*
*These things the pure one spoke as a handmaid, yet in awe; and she heard the Magi standing together before the cave, and said unto them: Whom seek ye? For I see that ye have come from a far-off land; having Persian appearance and wisdom, ye have made a strange departure and journey; and unto Him Who has sojourned from on high, and Who strangely dwelt within me as He alone knows, ye have come with diligence to worship Him, Who grants great mercy unto the world!*
*Other Stichera of the Saints, Tone 4. Podoben: "As noble" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*
*By divine power and firmly strengthened, and by the commands of Christ the Master, in natural weakness ye showed yourselves unconquerable, O passion-bearers, having vanquished the enemy in your struggles; and ye pray for those who celebrate your holy and light-bearing memory, O glorious great-martyrs.*[^623]
*Theophilus in words, Dorotheus in deeds, and Migdonius, together with Gorgonius, with Secundus also and Peter, and Indes, having shown valor, vanquished the enemy's battle arrays, rejoicing and they pray to deliver from all afflictions those who in faith celebrate their all-honorable memory.*
*Youths, virgins, elders, and infants showed one single valor; therefore by grace they received equal rewards, abiding together with their King and God; whom let us honor with sacred hymnody, as radiant luminaries of the universe, being twenty thousand.*
*Glory, Both now... Tone 5:*
*Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice; for today in truth there has become one flock of angels and men. O wonder! The Invisible is seen, the Incomprehensible is contained, the Word becomes gross, the Son of God becomes the Son of man; and the Virgin who knows not man is seen as the Mother of God, and after childbirth the Mother is found a virgin. The incarnate Word of the Father lies in the manger, and the shepherds as preachers become partakers of the mystery. The Magi from the east brought gifts, guided by a star, and worshipped the newborn Savior. With them also let us lovers of the feast, eagerly opening the treasures of our hearts, offer unto Him good deeds: faith, hope, and love, like gold, frankincense, and myrrh, crying aloud with the voice of the bodiless hosts unto Him: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will among men, Who hast come to save from deception all our race!*
*At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Feast, Tone 2. Podoben: "O house of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
*Purely and in a manner becoming God, having assumed the first Adam, O Christ, Thou wast born in the cave from the Virgin, and art swaddled in the manger.*[^624]
*Verse: From the womb before the morning star have I begotten Thee: the Lord has sworn, and will not repent.*
*Sing prophetically, O David, tuning the pipes; for from thy loins, from whom is the Mother of God, Christ is born today.*
*Verse: The Lord said unto My Lord: Sit Thou at My right hand.*
*With the shepherds and Magi let us the faithful offer praise becoming God, and glory with the angels, unto God Who has budded forth from the Virgin.*
*Glory, Both now... Tone 4:*
*Glory to God in the highest, I hear today in Bethlehem from the bodiless hosts, unto Him Who was well-pleased that peace should be on earth. Now the Virgin is wider than the heavens; for light has shone forth upon those in darkness, and has exalted the humble who sing in angelic manner: Glory to God in the highest!*
*Troparion of the Saints, Tone 2:*
*O passion-bearers of the Lord, blessed is the earth that was drenched with your blood with your blood, and holy are the dwellings that received your bodies; for in the stadium ye vanquished the enemy, and proclaimed Christ with boldness: beseech Him as the Good One, we pray, that our souls may be saved.*
*Glory, Both now... of the Feast:*
*Troparion of the Feast, Tone 4:*
*Thy Nativity, O Christ our God, has shone forth the light of reason upon the world; for thereby they that served the stars were taught by a star to worship Thee, the Sun of Righteousness, and to know Thee, the Dayspring from on high: O Lord, glory to Thee!*
*At Matins, the Troparion of the Feast, twice; Glory... of the Saints; Both now... of the Feast.*
*After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 1. Podoben: "The stone being sealed" (Ка́мени запеча́тану):*
*Sitting on the fiery throne in the highest with the unoriginate Father and Thy divine Spirit, Thou wast well-pleased to be born in the flesh from the Virgin who knew not man, O Jesus; therefore also a star showed Thee from Persia unto the Magi. Glory to Thy good counsel; glory to Thy manifestation; glory to Thine extreme condescension unto men!*
*Glory, Both now... the same.*
*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 3. Podoben: "The beauty of virginity" (Красотѣ̀ дѣ́вства):*
*The pre-eternal and incomprehensible One, co-ever-existing with the invisible Father, the one and unconfused Godhead of the Trinity, didst thou carry in the womb bodily, O Mother of God; thy grace has shone forth in the world, O all-hymned one. Therefore unceasingly we cry aloud: Rejoice, O pure Virgin-Mother!*
*Glory, Both now... the same.*
*Canon of the Feast with the Heirmos, on 8, Tone 1. A work of Cyr John:*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
*The Master, working wonders, saved the people, turning of old the wet wave of the sea into dry land; and being born willingly of the Virgin, He lays for us a passable path to heaven; Whom, equal in essence to the Father and to men, we glorify.*[^625]
*Troparia:*
*The sacred womb brought forth the Word, visibly depicted in the bush that was not burned with fire, mingling God with human form, releasing Eve's wretched womb from the bitter ancient curse; Whom we earthly ones glorify.*
*The star before the sun showed the Word Who came to make an end of sins, unto the Magi, visibly in the poor cave, Thee the Merciful One, wrapped in swaddling bands; Whom rejoicing they beheld as Himself both man and Lord.*
*And the Canon of the Saints, on 4; the acrostic whereof is: The multitude The multitude of victorious martyrs shall save me. By Joseph. Tone 4.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
*Let us all sing a song of victory unto God, Who has done marvelous wonders with a high arm, and has saved Israel, for He is glorified.*
*Troparia:*
*O numerous multitude of honorable martyrs, cleanse the multitude of my many transgressions by your intercession, and give me a word to sing of your triumph.*
*Most radiant luminaries of the Church, victorious martyrs, having glorified Christ with your members, be ye glorified now by your light-bearing memory.*
*The divine faith of the sufferers destroyed the godless tyranny of the unbelieving, and by grace consumed the crafty opposition of demons.*
*Having confessed Thee, the Almighty One Who didst take flesh and destroy death by death, the martyrs, having been put to death, received never-ending life.*
*Theotokion:*
*I hymn thee, all-praised and blessed one, who didst bear in the flesh the much-hymned God, Who magnifies the sufferers that vanquished the enemy.*
*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
*Look down upon the hymns of Thy servants, O Benefactor, bringing low the haughty pride of the enemy; and do Thou Who seest all, O Blessed One, bear up steadfastly above sin those who sing, established upon the foundation of faith.*[^626]
*Troparia:*
*The choir of pipers, having been counted worthy to behold passing understanding the most rich birthgiving of the all-pure Bride, bowed down in strange manner, and the rank of the bodiless hosts singing of Christ the King, seedlessly incarnate.*
*He Who reigns in the height of the heavens, out of tender mercy accomplishes our salvation from the unwedded Maiden, being formerly immaterial; but afterward the Word, having become gross with flesh, that He might draw the fallen first-formed man unto Himself.*
*Another [Canon of the Martyrs]. Heirmos:*
*Let my heart be established in Thy will, O Christ God, Who didst establish the second heaven above the waters, and didst found the earth upon the waters, O Almighty One.*
*Troparia:*
*Most brightly kindled with the love of Christ, O all-praised ones, when the fire was kindled ye feared not in any way; but having met your end therein, ye are glorified together.*
*Proclaiming God with a clear voice, they were not terrified by the threats of the godless; but with one mind crying aloud the voice of the children crying aloud, the all-praised warriors of Christ met their end.*
*Let us not fear the fire that is our fellow-servant, the noble ones cried aloud together, rejoicing in soul: For Thy sake we are put to death, Who didst die and didst abolish death, O Savior!*
*Theotokion:*
*That He might deify humanity, God became man from thee, O pure Virgin, beyond word and understanding; therefore with one accord we the faithful call thee blessed.*
*Kontakion, Tone 2. Podoben: "Firm in soul" (Тве́рдыѧ):*
*Firm in soul according to faith, the holy ones, two myriad sufferers, receiving suffering by fire, crying aloud unto Him Who was born of the Virgin: Receive our whole-burnt offerings for Thy sake, as the gifts of the Persian kings, gold, and myrrh, and frankincense, O pre-eternal God!*[^627]
*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4. Podoben: "Thy tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й сп҃се):*
*The army in number two myriad of martyrs, being honored, has shone forth unto us, enlightening the hearts and minds of the pious for the sake of the faith. For having been kindled with the divine love of the Master, the noble ones eagerly received a holy end by fire.*
*Glory, Both now... of the Feast, Tone and Podoben the same (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*
*In the manger of the irrational beasts wast Thou laid for our sake, O long-suffering Savior, having voluntarily become an infant; and the shepherds sang of Thee with the angels, crying aloud and the shepherds sang of Thee with the angels, crying aloud: Glory and praise unto Him Who is born upon earth, and Who has deified the nature of earthborn men, Christ our God!*
*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
*The renewal of the human race the Prophet Habakkuk foreshowed of old in song, having been accounted worthy ineffably to behold the type: for a young Child, the Word, came forth from the mountain, the Virgin, unto the renewal of the peoples.*[^628]
*Troparia:*
*Equal to men hast Thou come forth, O Most High, having willingly taken flesh from the Virgin, to purge the poison of the serpent's head, bringing all from the sunless gates unto the life-bearing light, being God.*
*The nations that of old were plunged in corruption, having escaped the exceedingly destructive ruin of the enemy, lift up their hands with hymns of praise, honoring Christ alone as Benefactor, Who has mercifully come unto us.*
*Having budded from the root of Jesse, O Virgin, thou hast surpassed the ordinances of human nature, having born the pre-eternal Word of the Father, as He Himself was well-pleased to pass through the sealed womb by a strange emptying.*
*Another [Canon of the Martyrs]. Heirmos:*
*I have heard Thy report, O Lord, and was afraid; I understood Thy works, the Prophet said, and I glorified Thy power.*
*Troparia:*
*Having bound their hearts to Thy love, O Word, the passion-bearers, being put to death for Thy sake like blameless lambs, showed themselves imitators of Thy passion.*
*Having guided your souls unto the haven of salvation by the Spirit, O holy ones, ye escaped the tempest of idol-madness, O blessed ones.*
*Unchangeable did ye show yourselves in the contest of martyrdom, unshakable and unswerving, having vanquished the opposition of the persecutors by divine faith.*
*Theotokion:*
*Having been delivered by thy childbirth from the first curse, O blessed one, we have received blessing, and life, and redemption, who glorify thee as the Mother of God.*
*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
*Out of the night of works of darkened deceit, do Thou, O Christ, come unto us who now watchfully perform a hymn unto Thee as Benefactor, bringing cleansing, granting an easy path, traversing which we may find glory.*[^629]
*Troparia:*
*Cutting off again the cruel enmity against us, the Master by His coming in the flesh, that He might destroy the soul-corrupting possessor, has joined the world with immaterial essences, making the Father accessible to creation.*
*The people that of old were darkened, after days have seen the light of the brightness from on high; and the Son brings the nations as an inheritance unto God, granting there ineffable grace, where sin flourished exceedingly.*
*Another [Canon of the Martyrs]. Heirmos:*
*Shine forth upon us Thy radiant, ever-existing light, who rise early unto the judgments of Thy commandments, O Master, Lover of mankind, Christ our God.*
*Troparia:*
*Light-manifesting is the memory of Thy passion-bearers, and it has enlightened the ends of the earth by the divine dispensations of wonders, O Christ our God.*
*The celebrants of holy things, offering sacrifice, were themselves offered up as whole-burnt offerings, perfect slaughters, with all the other exceedingly many martyrs, magnifying Christ.*
*Being temples of God by holy baptism, O holy ones, ye received together a holy end in the divine house, and were taken up unto the heavenly temple.*
*Theotokion:*
*That God might unite with those on high those who through transgression had slipped into a great pit, He took up His abode in thy womb, O all-undefiled one, and became flesh.*
*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

*Abiding in the depths of the sea, Jonah prayed to come forth and still the storm; and I, wounded by the arrow of the tormentor, sing unto Christ, the Destroyer of evils, that Thou mayest come quickly unto my slothfulness.*[^630]
*Troparia:*
*He Who was from the beginning with God, God the Word, now confirms that which was of old weak, having seen to preserve the nature that is like unto us, whereby revealing Himself free from passions by a second communion.*
*For our sake He comes from the loins of Abraham, to raise up as sons those who have fallen darkly into the gloom of transgressions, bowed down to the earth; He Who abides in light, and through condescension was well-pleased to dwell now in a manger for the salvation of mankind.*
*Another [Canon of the Martyrs]. Heirmos:*
*Emulating the Prophet Jonah, I cry aloud: Deliver my life from corruption, O Good One, and save me, O Savior of the world, who cry: Glory to Thee!*
*Troparia:*
*Thou wast the chief of the sacred people, and hast sent them before in joy unto heaven, having suffered, O glorious hieromartyr Anthimus.*[^631]
*Like pure gold in the midst of fire, your suffering piety was made known unto Jesus, shining more brightly than the sun.*
*Having been put to death in the flesh, ye inherited true life, O wise ones, abiding with Christ, Who showed you to be stronger than torments.*
*Theotokion:*
*After childbirth in truth, as before childbirth, O Mary, by the power of Jesus Who was incarnate from thee, thou didst remain a virgin: a wonder truly most glorious!*
*Kontakion of the Feast, Tone 3. Podoben: "The Virgin today" (Дв҃а дне́сь):*
*Today the Virgin gives birth to Him Who is transcendent in essence, and the earth offers a cave to the Unapproachable One; angels with shepherds give glory, and Magi journey with a star: for our sake is born a young Child, the pre-eternal God.*[^632]
*Ikos:*
*Bethlehem has opened Eden: come, let us behold; we have found delight in secret: come, let us receive the things of paradise within the cave! There the unwatered root has appeared, budding forth forgiveness; there has been found the undug well, of which David of old longed to drink. There the Virgin, having brought forth an Infant, straightway quenched the thirst of Adam and David. Therefore let us go unto Him where He is born: a young Child, the pre-eternal God!*
*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
*The youths caught in heart by love scorned the ungodly raging tyrant's blasphemous talk; to whom the great fire yielded, while they said unto the Blessed One: Blessed art Thou unto the ages!*

*...while they said unto the Blessed One: Blessed art Thou unto the ages!*
*Troparia:*
*The all-consuming furnace furiously burned the servants, but with fear saved the youths, being stoked sevenfold; whom the flame crowned without grudging, as the Lord granted them dew for their piety's sake.*
*O Helper of men, Christ, having an ineffable incarnation, an enigma to Thine adversary, Thou didst put him to shame; bearing the riches of deification, having now taken form; for the hope whereof we came down from on high into the nether darkness.*
*Thou hast mightily cast down sin, which was evilly and unrestrainedly exalted, raging ungodly from the corruption of the world, which it formerly drew down; and today Thou deliverest from snares, being willingly incarnate, O Benefactor.*
*Another [Canon of the Martyrs]. Heirmos:*
*When Thy children were in the furnace, O Savior, the fire touched them not neither distressed them; then the three, as with one mouth, sang and blessed, saying: Blessed is the God of our fathers!*
*Troparia:*
*Beholding the one thing that abides there, O blessed ones, by divine power, like the three divine youths in Babylon, ye were shown superior to the fire, enlightened by divine light.*
*Scorning the tyrant's irrational rage, O wise ones, with the holy women, and as an offering truly with the divine infants, ye were offered up as whole offerings unto the King of all.*
*The enlightenment of the knowledge of Christ standing within your souls in all piety, ye truly passed through the dark cloud of godlessness, O sufferers, and entered into eternal light.*
*Theotokion:*
*Higher than the heavens wast thou shown to be, having born the Master and God of all; Whom cease not fervently to beseech, O all-holy pure one, to save those who in warm faith hymn thee.*
*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
*The youths burning in the Old Covenant prefigured the unconsumed womb of the Maiden that brought forth supernaturally, being sealed; both accomplishing one single wonder, grace stirs up the people to song.*[^633]
*Troparion:*
*Having escaped the ruin of seeking to become gods through deception, all creation unceasingly sings in youthful manner with trembling of the poured-forth Word, offering unceasing praise fearing to offer inglorious praise, being corruptible, even though wisely enduring.*
*Thou comest turning the straying back unto pasture through flowering hills, the uprising of the nations, human nature, to quench the violent power of the manslayer; and Thou didst appear as man, and God by providence.*
*Another [Canon of the Martyrs]. Heirmos:*
*Praise Christ God and supremely exalt Him unto all ages, Who saved the children in the furnace, singing hymns, and turned the thundering flame into dew.*
*Troparia:*
*The relics of the martyrs pour forth an anointing of divine fragrance as from a bridegroom's myrrh, and take away the foul stench of passions from those who in faith hymn Thee, O Christ, unto the ages.*
*Ye appeared like most fair rosebushes,*[^634] *O sufferers, walking in the midst of the fire and fervently crying: Praise and supremely exalt Christ unto the ages!*
*Youths together and maidens, elders and the young, infants, and an innumerable multitude of women attained the choir on high, having suffered together.*
*Theotokion:*
*Ezekiel beholds thee as the sealed door, O Virgin, through which Jesus passed, Who dwelt within thy womb; and having ineffably assumed flesh from thy blood...*
*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
*It is easier for us, on account of fear, to love silence as free from peril; yet out of love, O Virgin, it is hard to weave songs harmoniously composed; but do thou, O Mother, give strength according as our desire is.*[^635]
*Troparia:*
*Having beheld dim types and shadows passed away, O pure Mother, of the Word newly revealed from shut gates, and thinking upon the true radiance, we worthily bless thy womb.*
*Having obtained their desire, and having been deemed worthy of the divine coming, the people adorned by Christ now take comfort in regeneration, since thou, O pure Virgin, givest life-bearing grace to worship His glory.*
*Another [Canon of the Martyrs]. Heirmos:*
*The radiant cloud, into which the Master of all came down like rain from heaven upon the fleece, and was incarnate for our sake, becoming man, He Who is without beginning: all of us magnify as the pure Mother of our God.*
*Troparia:*
*Like voluntary slain lambs ye were burned together, and like pure sacrifices ye were brought unto the Master Who was slain for us who are earthly-born, O noble-victorious martyrs; and worthily [ye received] crowns of victory glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace: for the expectation of the nations is come; having come He saved us from the enemy's bondage.*[^636]
*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes: Ode 4 of the Feast, on 6.*
*Prokeimenon of the Saints, Tone 4: Thou, O Lord, shalt keep us and preserve us. Verse: Save me, O Lord, for the godly man hath failed.*
*Epistle to the Romans, §96 [from the half; Rom. 8:28–39].*
*Alleluia, Tone 4: Shout with jubilation unto the Lord, all the earth.*
*Gospel from Luke, §51 [from the half; Lk. 10:19–21].*
*Communion Hymn: Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous.*
*In the same month, on the 29th day.*[^637]
*The Holy 14,000 Infants slain for Christ by Herod in Bethlehem of Judea; and our venerable father Marcellus, Abbot of the Monastery of the Unsleeping Ones.*
*At "Lord, I have cried," stichera of the Saints, Tone 1. Podoben: "As one valiant" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*
*Seeking the hidden Treasure, the lawless Herod slew the innocent infants today, and Rachel was inconsolable, seeing their unjust slaughter and untimely death, over whom she wept, aching in womb; but now she rejoices, beholding them in Abraham's bosom.*
*Seeking the ageless King Who had come under time, the lawless king, not finding Him to kill Him, reaped an ineffable multitude of infants; whom he made martyrs without intending it, and citizens of the Kingdom on high, forever reproaching his extreme madness.*
*When Thou wast born of the Virgin, O pre-eternal Lord, and for goodness' sake didst become an infant, a choir of infants was brought unto Thee by martyr's blood, having most righteously illumined their unclouded souls; whom Thou didst settle in the ever-living mansions, reproaching Herod's malice and most cruel madness.*
*Stichera of the Venerable Father, Tone and Podoben the same (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*
*An image of temperance An image of temperance hast thou shown thyself unto monastics, O God-bearing Marcellus: through temperance a pillar of fire, lifted up in spirit, O most wise one, from earth unto heaven; and companion of purity; a true keeper of silence in truth, and an animate pillar of courage, and a most certain rule unto virtue.*
*Thou didst wither the surgings of the passions, O venerable one, through rigorous vigilance and meditation upon the Scriptures, and through diligent prayer and the shedding of tears; therefore in truth thou didst appear as a worthy dwelling-place for the Master, and thou dispensest healings unto those who draw near in faith, being deemed worthy of immortal delight.*
*Delighting most clearly in the beauty of thy Master, the fleshly mirrors having been dissolved, O blessed one, and by His manifestation here below: pray for those who chastely praise thy most sacred memory, and honor it with psalms and hymns, that we may obtain mercy on the day of judgment.*
*Glory, of the Infants, Tone 8. By Andrew of Crete:*[^638]
*The lawless Herod, seeing a star brighter than all creation, was troubled, and snatched suckling infants from their mothers' embraces; but Elizabeth, taking John, besought the rock, saying: Receive a mother with her child! The mountain received the Forerunner; and the manger guarded the Treasure Whom the star proclaimed and the Magi worshipped: Lord, glory to Thee!*
*Now and ever, the same Tone:*
*A most glorious mystery is accomplished today: nature is renewed, and God becomes man; what He was, He remained; and what He was not, He assumed, having suffered neither confusion nor division.*
*At the Aposticha, stichera of the Feast, Tone 6. Podoben: "On the third day" (Трїдне́венъ):*
*I behold an awesome mystery: for God Who holds all creation in His fist is embraced in the flesh in a manger of brute beasts, and is wrapped in swaddling rags, He Who swaddles the sea with mist.*
*Verse: Out of the womb before the morning star have I begotten Thee; the Lord hath sworn and will not repent.*
*God Who is bodiless is incarnate, and He Who is without beginning begins; and He Who is full is now emptied, being an Infant fed with milk from the Virgin in a small cave, Who nourishes every breathing thing.*
*Verse: The Lord said unto my Lord: Sit Thou at My right hand.*
*They leap for joy The shepherds leap for joy at Christ's Nativity, and they give glory with the angels; and the star bears gifts, and the Magi worship; and men, having been saved, magnify the Theotokos.*
*Glory, of the Infants, Tone 8. By Andrew of Crete:*[^639]
*When Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea, the Jewish dominion was abolished: let the infants slain for Christ leap for joy; let Judea weep: for a voice was heard in Ramah, Rachel weeping wails, as it is written, for her children; for the lawless Herod, having slain the infants, fulfilled the Scripture, glutting Judea with innocent blood; and while the earth was indeed reddened with the blood of infants, the Church of the Gentiles is mystically cleansed and clothed in beauty. The Truth is come, God Who was born of the Virgin hath appeared unto those sitting in darkness, in order to save us.*
*Now and ever, the same Tone. By John the Monk:*[^640]
*O Lord, having come unto Bethlehem, Thou didst dwell in a cave; having heaven for a throne, Thou didst recline in a manger; whom hosts of angels surround, Thou didst descend unto shepherds: that Thou mightest save our race, as Thou art tenderhearted, glory to Thee!*
*Troparion of the Saints, Tone 1:*[^641]
*Be entreated, O Lord, by the sufferings which the saints endured for Thy sake, and heal all our sicknesses, O Lover of mankind, we pray Thee.*
*Glory, of the Venerable Father. Troparion, Tone 8:*
*In thee, O father, was preserved with certainty that which is according to the image; for taking up the cross, thou didst follow Christ, and by thy deeds didst teach us to overlook the flesh, for it passes away, and to care for the soul, a thing immortal. Therefore thy spirit rejoices with the angels, O venerable Marcellus.*
*Now and ever, of the Feast, Tone 4:*
*Thy Nativity, O Christ our God, hath shone upon the world the light of wisdom; for thereby those who served the stars were taught by a star to worship Thee, the Sun of righteousness, and to know Thee from the height of the Orient: Lord, glory to Thee!*
*At Matins, at "God is the Lord," the Troparion of the Feast, twice; and of the Infants. Glory, of the Venerable Father; Now and ever, of the Feast.*
*After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 5. Podoben: "Co-beginningless Word" (Собезна́чальное):*
*Illumined by the shining of the star, the Magi came from Persia unto the cave of Bethlehem, bringing choice gifts unto the King born of the Virgin and Mother bringing them gratefully, guided from among the Gentiles unto worshipping Him. Glory, and now and ever, the same.*
*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8. Podoben: "He is risen from the dead" (Воскре́се и҆з̾ ме́ртвыхъ):*
*The angelic host cries aloud the good song, having renewed the pastoral order, saying: Sing divine praise, ye that govern the sheep; cry aloud, singing: For Christ the Lord is born, Who was well pleased to save the human race as God!*
*Glory, and now and ever, the same Podoben (Подо́бенъ то́йже):*
*A most glorious mystery is this, O faithful: God was born of the Virgin as He knows; the angelic ranks, marveling at His condescension, cry aloud, singing: For Christ the Lord is born, Who was well pleased to save the human race as God!*
*Canon of the Feast, on 6; and of the Saints, two canons, on 8. Canon of Cyr Cosmas, Tone 1. Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^642]
*Christ is born, give ye glory! Christ from the heavens, meet ye Him! Christ on earth, be ye lifted up! Sing unto the Lord, all the earth; and in gladness sing, O ye people, for He is glorified!*
*Troparia:*
*Him that was made according to the divine image, having corrupted through transgression, being wholly of corruption, fallen away from the better divine life, the wise Creator renews again, for He is glorified!*
*Seeing man, whom He made with His hands, perishing, the Creator bowed the heavens and came down; and He completely assumed his essence from the divine pure Virgin, truly being incarnate, for He is glorified!*
*Wisdom, Word, and Power, being the Father's Son and Radiance, Christ God, hidden from the powers both as many as are transcendent and as many as are on earth, having become man, hath renewed us, for He is glorified!*
*Canon of the Holy Infants, on 4, Tone 4. Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^643]
*God, having cut through the Red Sea deep, Who drowned Pharaoh in it, having led Moses dry-shod into the wilderness, and having rained manna for food for the people of Israel, for He is mighty.*
*Troparia:*
*The star shone forth in Bethlehem, and delivered Eden from the dark curse; and the day of salvation is granted unto the ancestors of our race, Jesus having shone forth from the virginal cloud, the illumination of those in darkness.*
*Today the arena of the infants opened for the faithful for the sake of Christ and God, reproaching the principalities and powers of the enemies, and Herod's reproaching Herod's childish wrath manly and prudently.*
*Theotokion:*
*Divine confirmation, and unbroken wall, O pure one, and ever a noetic bridge, and unconquerable pillar, and foundation and shelter, through whom all of us are saved from dangers: thou art in truth!*
*Canon of the Venerable Father, Tone 6. Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^644]
*Traversing the deep on foot as on dry land, Israel, seeing the pursuer Pharaoh drowned, cried out: Let us sing a song of victory unto God!*
*Troparia:*
*Creation is renewed, and the nature of earthly beings is made new: Christ the Creator of all being born in the flesh beyond comprehension, from the pure and all-holy Mother.*
*Having received understanding from the God of truth, O father, and having unceasingly sought Him by a pure life, O Marcellus, thou didst please Him by divine virtues.*
*Theotokion:*
*Earth received deliverance from the ancestral curse that was in Eden, when the Deliverer was born upon it from thee, O pure one, Who renewed and sanctified it.*
*Ode 3. Heirmos:*[^645]
*Unto the Son begotten of the Father without corruption before the ages, and in these latter times incarnate of the Virgin without seed, unto Christ God let us cry aloud: Thou Who hast exalted our horn, holy art Thou, O Lord!*
*Troparia:*
*The earthly Adam, having partaken of the better inspiration, and having slipped into corruption by woman's deception, seeing Christ born of woman, cries out: Thou Who for my sake hast become like unto me, holy art Thou, O Lord!*
*Conformed unto our vile lowliness by mingling, O Christ, and having partaken of the baser flesh, imparting of the divine nature; having become earthly and remained God, and having exalted our horn: holy art Thou, O Lord!*
*Bethlehem, rejoice, being King of the princes of Judah; He that feeds Israel upon the cherubic shoulders, Christ, came forth openly from thee; and having exalted our horn, He reigned over all.*
*Another [Canon of the Infants]. Heirmos:*[^646]
*He Who establishes the thunder and builds the spirit, establish me, O Lord, that I may hymn Thee in truth and do Thy will; for there is none holy as Thou, our God.*
*Troparia:*
*Having passed through the virginal door, our Creator and God ineffably fashioned for Himself a fleshly house; and He became an Infant, and reclined in a manger.*
*Children of the same age, martyrs of Christ's incarnation, Herod's blinded Herod's foolish fury, and were shown forth as all-radiant eyes of the Church.*
*Theotokion:*
*From thee appeared the Fatherless, and Motherless before the ages, the Lord; and He is supernaturally formed, and grants the gift of deification unto those descended from Adam, O Virgin unacquainted with wedlock.*
*Canon of the Venerable Father. Heirmos:*
*There is none holy as Thou, O Lord my God, Who hast exalted the horn of Thy faithful, O Good One, and hast established us upon the rock of Thy confession.*
*Troparia:*
*Drop down upon the earth, O ye clouds, the sweetness of gladness; for from a radiant cloud Christ hath shone forth, born in the flesh in a cave beyond all thought.*
*Arming thyself with steadfastness of soul against the spiritual foes, O God-bearer, thou didst mightily cut down their ranks, and wast crowned with the wreath of victory.*
*Theotokion:*
*Having ineffably become incarnate from thy most pure and precious blood, O pure one, the Word of God showed thee to be the Mistress of all creatures.*
*Kontakion of the Feast, Tone 3:*[^647]
*Today the Virgin gives birth to Him Who is transcendent in essence, and the earth offers a cave to the Unapproachable One; angels with shepherds give glory, and Magi journey with a star: for our sake is born a young Child, the pre-eternal God.*
*Ikos:*
*Bethlehem has opened Eden: come, let us behold; we have found delight in secret: come, let us receive the things of paradise within the cave! There the unwatered root has appeared, budding forth forgiveness; there has been found the undug well, of which David of old longed to drink. There the Virgin, having brought forth an Infant, straightway quenched the thirst of Adam and David. Therefore let us go unto Him where He is born: a young Child, the pre-eternal God!*
*Sessional Hymn of the Infants, Tone 4. Podoben: "Thou hast appeared" (Ꙗ҆ви́лся є҆сѝ):*
*Unto Him Who is born today of the Virgin, the host of infants as unto Creator and King is offered as acceptable slaughter, laid before Christ for faith's sake.*
*Glory, of the Venerable Father, Tone 4. Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*[^648]
*Having pre-cleansed thy soul with the coals of purity, thou didst bridle the body unto incorruptible strength, O all-praised Marcellus; therefore thou wast shown to be a divine dwelling-place, driving away sicknesses, and enlightening by faith those who ever draw near unto thee and extol thee.*
*Now and ever, the same Tone. Podoben: "Joseph marveled" (Оу҆диви́ся і҆ѡ́сифъ):*[^649]
*Herod was astounded Herod was astounded, learning of it, the cruel king, seeking with rage to fight against the young King, Christ, born upon earth; and seized with trembling and great fear, he sends an army to kill with fury the babes in Bethlehem; attempting together with them to kill the Creator, Who became poor through tenderheartedness: for He came forth from a virginal womb, desiring to save our race.*
*Ode 4. Heirmos:*[^650]
*Rod of the root of Jesse, and flower from it, O Christ, Thou hast budded forth from the Virgin; from the mountain overshadowed and densely forested, Thou, the Praised One, art come, incarnate of her that knew not man, O Immaterial One and God: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!*
*Troparia:*
*Whom Jacob foretold of old as the expectation of the nations, O Christ, Thou hast shone forth from the tribe of Judah; and Thou art come to overturn the power of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria, changing error into faith befitting God: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!*
*Fulfilling the words of the sorcerer Balaam of old, Thou hast filled with joy the wise astrologers, his disciples; having shone forth as a star out of Jacob, O Master, and Thou hast openly received the first-fruits of the Gentiles that were brought in: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!*
*Like rain upon the fleece, and as drops falling upon the earth, Thou didst come down into the womb of the Virgin, O Christ; Ethiopia and Tarshish, and the Arabian isles, and Sheba, holding all the land of the Medes, fell down before Thee, O Savior: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!*
*Another [Canon of the Infants]. Heirmos:*[^651]
*I have heard Thy report, and was afraid, said the prophet; I considered Thy works and was amazed, and cried aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!*
*Troparia:*
*Earth and heaven, heavenly and earthly beings, having mediated by thy childbirth beyond comprehension, she reconciled, and tore down the middle wall of enmity.*
*The multitude of infants, having suffered martyr-like for the sake of the God of all, receives the honors of suffering from Him; on whose account Herod was utterly put to shame.*
*Theotokion:*
*Having conceived the Divine Word in thy womb by an awesome decree, beyond word thou didst bear Him in the flesh, O all-immaculate one. Therefore we glorify thee as the Theotokos.*
*Another [Canon of the Venerable Father]. Heirmos:*[^652]
*Christ is my power, God and Lord, the venerable Church sings in manner befitting God, crying out from a pure mind, feasting in the Lord.*
*Troparia:*
*Having seen Having seen Thy descent into the cave, O Lord, the spiritual ranks were seized with dread in fear; and they sang of Thine incomprehensible mercy, O Christ.*
*Thy sufferings and sweats, O venerable Marcellus, mixed with the bloody streams of the infants, were offered as precious gifts unto Him Who was born in the flesh.*
*Theotokion:*
*Seeing thee radiant, gleaming with beauty through the dawn of thy Son, O pure one, the gift-bearing Gentiles sang of a new and most glorious vision.*
*Ode 5. Heirmos:*[^653]
*As Thou art the God of peace and Father of mercies, Thou hast sent unto us the Angel of Thy great counsel, granting peace; therefore, guided unto the light of the knowledge of God, watching early out of the night, we glorify Thee, O Lover of mankind.*
*Troparia:*
*Numbered among the slaves by Caesar's decree, Thou wast obedient; and us who were slaves of the enemy and of sin Thou didst set free, O Christ; having become poor wholly like unto us, Thou didst deify the earthly nature from the very union and communion.*
*Behold, the Virgin, as was said of old, having conceived in her womb, hath brought forth God incarnate, and she remains a virgin; through whom we sinners, having been reconciled unto God, hymn the true Theotokos, O faithful.*
*Another [Canon of the Infants]. Heirmos:*[^654]
*Shine upon me, O Lord, the light of Thy commandments, for unto Thee my spirit seeks early and hymns Thee; for Thou art our God, and unto Thee I flee, O King of peace.*
*Troparia:*
*The sensible sun is covered with clouds, but the noetic and all-immaterial Sun, through boundless tenderheartedness clothed in flesh, is today wrapped in swaddling bands in a cave for our sake.*
*Herod is defiled with the blood of foul murder; for attempting to slay the Master of all, God and King, he rages against the babes, and is fiercely savage.*
*Theotokion:*
*With the dawn of thy prayer, O pure Mother of God, illumine the blindness of my heart; as thou didst shine forth Christ, the only Candlestick of the Lord and Sun of glory.*
*Another [Canon of the Venerable Father]. Heirmos:*[^655]
*By Thy divine light, O Good One, illumine, I pray, the souls of those who lovingly seek Thee early, that they may know Thee, O Word of God, as the true God, calling them out of the darkness of sins.*
*Troparia:*
*There overflows The cup of Thy tenderheartedness overflows, O Christ, unto all creations; and it abundantly filled these with mercy, when Thou didst appear in the flesh and wast born.*
*Having cleansed the essential darkening of the soul, and every earthly and corruptible beauty, by the sufferings of thy fasting, O Marcellus, thou wast shown to be an equal of the angels in the world.*
*Theotokion:*
