*He that was born of thee in the flesh in the cave, O pure one, poured forth spiritual streams of immortality, and gave human nature to drink, having enriched it with incorruption, as He is tenderhearted.*
*Ode 6. Heirmos:*[^656]
*The sea beast vomited forth Jonah from its belly like an infant, even as it had received him; and the Word, having dwelt in the Virgin and taken flesh, came forth, preserving her incorrupt; for He suffered not corruption, and kept her that bare Him unharmed.*
*Troparia:*
*Christ our God is come, incarnate, Whom the Father begets from the womb before the morning star; holding the reins of the pure powers, He reclines in a manger of beasts and is wrapped in swaddling bands, and He looses the tangled bonds of transgressions.*
*A young Child from Adam's mixture, a Son was born and given unto the faithful; He is the Father and Ruler of the age to come, and is called the Angel of great counsel; this is mighty God, holding all creation by His power.*
*Another [Canon of the Infants]. Heirmos:*[^657]
*The tempest of my many transgressions drowns me, and my spirit fails; but do Thou, O Lord, having descended as Thou art merciful, lead up my life.*
*Troparia:*
*The divine mystery of the incarnation of the Word is accomplished today, O Theotokos; for through thee the pre-eternal God hath appeared in the flesh, that He might deify that which He assumed.*
*Rachel, weeping for her children, of old foretold the infants that received untimely slaughter for Christ's sake; therefore refusing to be comforted, not desiring consolation.*
*Theotokion:*
*Thy divine childbirth, O all-pure one, cut off the curse that budded in paradise; and having opened unto men the ancient path of life, it poured forth blessing.*
*Another [Canon of the Venerable Father]. Heirmos:*[^658]
*Beholding the sea of life surging with the tempest of temptations, fleeing unto Thy calm haven, I cry unto Thee: Lead up my life from corruption, O Most Merciful One!*
*Troparia:*
*The earth brought forth the most fragrant myrrh within itself beyond comprehension, from the precious of His precious Body, pouring forth in the flesh, and filling men with divine fragrance.*
*Having wisely discerned the temporal and unstable nature of life, O Marcellus, thou didst lift up thy soul's desire unto the things that abide forever, which thou didst attain through the labors of asceticism.*
*Theotokion:*
*The Timeless One is born; for God the Word took flesh from thee, O all-pure Virgin, that He might grant unto men ageless life, an eternal inheritance, and incorruptible glory.*
*Kontakion, Tone 4. Podoben: "Thou hast appeared" (Я҆ви́лсѧ є҆сѝ):*
*A star sent the Magi unto Him that was born; and Herod sent an unjust army fiercely, supposing to slay Him lying as an infant in the manger.*
*Ikos:*
*While the things above and the things below now rejoice together at the manifestation of the King of all, Herod alone grieves with the prophet-slaying Jews; for it is fitting that they alone should weep, since henceforth they shall not reign; but the Kingdom of the Lord even now shall bear rule, repelling the audacity of enemies and summoning the multitudes of the faithful to look with the honored infants upon Him Who lies in the manger as a babe.*
*Ode 7. Heirmos:*[^659]
*The youths, reared together in piety, disdained the ungodly command and were not afraid of the threat of fire; but standing in the midst of the flame, they sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!*
*Troparia:*
*The shepherds playing their pipes received an awe-inspiring vision of light, for the glory of the Lord shone round about them; and the angel, crying aloud, said: Sing ye, for Christ is born, the blessed God of our fathers!*
*Suddenly with the angel's word the heavenly hosts appeared, crying: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will among men; Christ has shone forth, the blessed God of our fathers!*
*What is this saying? the shepherds said; let us go over and see this thing which has come to pass, the divine Christ; and having come and seen Him, they worshiped Him with Her that bare Him, singing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!*
*Another [Canon of the Innocents]. Heirmos:*[^660]
*The Abrahamic youths in the Persian furnace, burned rather by the love of piety than by the flame, cried out: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!*
*Troparia:*
*Bethlehem rejoices today with us, for it receives the Incomprehensible One in a cave, crying: Blessed art Thou, O only God of our fathers!*
*A blameless and unblemished sacrifice is slain beforehand for Thee, O Word of God, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!*
*Theotokion:*
*Rejoice, sure haven of repentance, unto which fleeing, O Theotokos, we cry: Blessed art thou alone, who didst bear the God of our fathers!*
*Another [Canon of the Venerable Father]. Heirmos:*[^661]
*The angel made the furnace pour forth dew for the venerable youths, but the command of God, consuming the Chaldeans, persuaded the tormentor to cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!*
*Troparia:*
*He that was born in the cave established anew by the knowledge of Himself all creation, which had been shaken by godlessness, as it unceasingly cries unto Him: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!*
*By the fire of fasting, O Marcellus, thou didst burn up carnal pleasures, and with the dew of dispassion thou didst refresh thy soul, crying radiantly unto Christ: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!*
*Theotokion:*
*All creation, O Bride of God, beheld thy divine majesty, when the God of all was born of thee in the flesh in the city of Bethlehem, and with the shepherds and the Magi praised thee.*
*Ode 8. Heirmos:*[^662]
*The furnace pouring dew prefigured the image of a supernatural marvel; for it burned not the youths whom it received, even as the fire of the Godhead burned not the womb of the Virgin into which It entered. Therefore singing, let us chant: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!*
*Troparia:*
*The deceit of Babylon drove the captive youths of David from Sion unto itself; but it sent the Magi, the children that bring gifts, to entreat the God-welcoming daughter of David. Therefore singing, let us chant: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!*
*The instruments laid aside mournful songs, for the children of Sion sang not in a strange land; but Christ, having shone forth in Bethlehem, dissolves all the delusion of Babylon and its musical harmonies. Therefore singing, let us chant: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!*
*Babylon took the spoils of the kingdom of Sion and its captive wealth; but Christ draws unto Sion the treasures thereof, and the kings, guiding the stargazers with a star. Therefore let us chant: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!*
*Another [Canon of the Innocents]. Heirmos:*[^663]
*O Master, by Thy wisdom Thou didst frame the universe, and didst establish the foundation of the earth, as Thou alone knowest, setting its foundations upon boundless waters. Therefore we all cry out, singing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, unceasingly!*
*Troparia:*
*Angels glorify the dominion of Him Who was born, shepherds marvel, and the Magi worship; the heavens proclaim the Creator by a star; with them we all sing, crying out: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!*
*The innocent multitude wages war today for the Master with blood, and is firmly armed against Herod, for Thou, O Christ, art born. Therefore we all cry out, singing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!*
*Theotokion:*
*O pure Virgin, the prophets of God proclaimed thee as temple, door, and cloud; the unburned bush, the jar of manna, the budding rod, the ark, the candlestick, the tablets of the covenant, and the holy mountain from which a stone was cut without hands.*
*Another [Canon of the Venerable Father]. Heirmos:*[^664]
*Thou didst shed forth dew from the flame for the venerable ones, and with water didst burn up the sacrifice of the righteous one; for Thou, O Christ, accomplishest all things by Thy mere willing: Thee do we exalt above all unto all ages!*
*Troparia:*
*Creation is clothed with a radiant garment, and has put away all its former mourning, now that the Renewer and Master is born on earth, Whom we exalt above all unto the ages.*
*Arming thyself with virtues, O venerable Marcellus, thou didst conquer the hosts of demons; and as a victor thou didst win trophies over them, and receivedst from God the grace of miracles.*
*Theotokion:*
*He that was born of thee in the cave, O all-immaculate one, prepared eternal habitations for men who sincerely sing unto thee, O Theotokos, and exalt thy ineffable childbearing above all.*
*Ode 9. Heirmos:*[^665]
*A strange and most glorious mystery do I behold: the cave is heaven, the Virgin the cherubic throne, the manger the place wherein Christ God lay, Whom nothing can contain; Whom praising, we magnify!*
*Troparia:*
*The Magi, beholding the extraordinary path of the unusual, new, newly-shining star that illumined the heavens, signified Christ the King born on earth in Bethlehem for our salvation.*

*When the Magi said: Where is the newborn Child-King, Whose star was shown? For we are come to worship Him: Herod was enraged and troubled; opposing God, he raged to slay Christ.*
*Herod inquired diligently the time of the star, by whose guidance the Magi in Bethlehem worshiped Christ with gifts; and being guided by it unto their own country, they left the cruel child-slayer mocked.*
*Another [Canon of the Innocents]. Heirmos:*[^666]
*For He that is mighty hath done to me great things, and holy is His Name; and His mercy is on them that fear Him, from generation to generation.*
*Troparia:*
*He that is in the bosom of the Father is wholly contained in thee; the Creator of heaven is formed, and empties Himself for my sake; and wrapped in swaddling bands, He looses the cords of transgressions.*
*From Ramah was heard Rachel's bitter weeping, mourning, woe, and contrition; for Herod the enemy was shown to be a foul murderer of the children of Bethlehem.*
*Theotokion:*
*By thy childbearing, O Virgin, we mortals were deified; for thou bearest and feedest with milk God, the Nourisher of all, Who shares equal glory with the Father. O marvelous wonder!*
*Another [Canon of the Venerable Father]. Heirmos:*[^667]
*It is impossible for men to see God, upon Whom the ranks of angels dare not gaze; but through thee, O all-pure one, the Word was made manifest incarnate unto men; Whom magnifying, together with the heavenly hosts, we bless thee.*
*Troparia:*
*The mercy of Thy love for mankind, which surpasses understanding, was made known unto the nations, O Christ; for Thou, O Master, didst become poor in the flesh, that Thou mightest make us partakers of the better riches, O Lord, as Thou art good and abundant in mercy.*
*Taking up the cross of Christ upon thy shoulders, O blessed one, and imitating His passions, thou wast wholly crucified unto the world, O Father Marcellus; for thou wast a partaker of divine deification and of the better glory, wherein remember us.*
*Theotokion:*
*God, born in the flesh from thee, O all-pure one, made us sons of God, and restored the former dignity unto those who receive Him, and who diligently glorify and magnify thee as Mother of God.*
*Exapostilarion of the Innocents. Podoben: "The Cross is the preserver" (Крⷭ҇тъ храни́тель):*[^668]
*Fighting against God, the accursed Herod sent forth and reaped the flourishing field of infants while yet unripe; and being unable to slay the newborn Lord, He is filled with divine shame.*
*Glory, and now and ever, of the feast:*
*Our Savior the Dayspring of daysprings from on high, has visited us; and we that were in darkness and shadow have found the truth: for of the Virgin the Lord is born.*
*At the Praises, Stichera of the Saints, on 4, Tone 1. Idiomelon: By Cyprian:*
*The infants were the first sacrifice for Thy most pure Nativity, O Christ God; for Herod, desiring to take Thee Who art uncontainable, knew not that he was bringing a choir of martyrs unto Thee. Therefore we pray Thee Who becamest man: Save our souls! (Twice)*
*Tone 2:*
*Your slaughter has entered into the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth, O honorable infants; for for His sake ye shed your blood, and ye rest in the bosom of Abraham, and ye cast away for ever the loathsome malice of Herod, by the power of Christ Who was born.*
*Tone 3:*
*Abominable is Herod's slaughter of children, because of his abominable murder; but pure is the sacrifice of the children, who, as contemporaries of Christ our salvation, were slain beforehand as a new sacrifice and sent on ahead. Weep not, Rachel, for thy children, mindful of the bosom of Abraham, where is the dwelling place of all who rejoice!*
*Glory, Tone 5:*
*Venerable father, thou gavest not sleep unto thine eyes, nor slumber unto thine eyelids, until thou didst free soul and body from the passions, and didst prepare thyself as a dwelling place of the Spirit; for Christ, coming with the Father, made His abode in thee; and having become a pleasing servant of the consubstantial Trinity, O our father Marcellus, great preacher, pray that our souls may be saved!*
*Now and ever, in the same tone:*
*Beholding Thee born in the flesh in Bethlehem, the Creator and Fashioner of all, all creation is made anew and renewed; the sun spreads forth its light, and the earth rejoices; the Magi from Persia bring gifts unto the King of all; the shepherds marvel with wonder, and worship God in the flesh with Her that bare Him. O marvel! The Nourisher is nourished by a tenderhearted mother, for the sake of the world's salvation and renewal!*
*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2. Podoben: "Angel-like" (А҆́ггелскїѧ):*[^669]
*The mountains, hills, valleys, and fields sang of Christ born of the Virgin; and the star from heaven showed Him unto the Magi, lying as an infant in a cave, clothed in a servant's body; unto Whom we cry: Blessed art Thou Who wast born, O our God, glory to Thee!*

*Verse: Out of the womb before the morning star have I begotten Thee.*
*What is Thy great and inscrutable poverty, for the sake of which Adam has been enriched with divine things? cried the Virgin, holding in her embrace Emmanuel, God and Creator, Who received flesh from her; unto Whom we cry: Blessed art Thou Who wast born, O our God, glory to Thee!*
*Verse: The Lord said unto my Lord: Sit Thou at My right hand.*
*As the noetic morning dawn, O Virgin, thou didst shine forth Christ the Sun, holding Him in thine embrace; by Whom the entire rational nature is enlightened with the brightness of perfect knowledge, and is counted worthy of incorruption, faithfully crying: Blessed art Thou Who wast born, O our God, glory to Thee!*
*Glory, in the same tone and podoben (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*
*Now is the Child revealed on earth, Who was begotten of the Father before the ages: let all creation rejoice, let the heavens be glad, beholding those who before were cast off now reunited unto God, and crying unto Him: Blessed art Thou Who wast born, O our God, glory to Thee!*
*Now and ever:*
*With fiery lips the transcendent powers on high praise Him that was born in the cave, for His ineffable mercy: may we also be counted worthy to praise Him with clay tongues, unceasingly crying unto Him: Blessed art Thou Who wast born, O our God, glory to Thee!*
*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes, from the canon of the feast, Ode 3; and of the holy infants, Ode 6.*
*Prokeimenon, Tone 6: Praise the Lord, O ye servants; praise ye the Name of the Lord. [Psalm 112:1]*
*Verse: He that makes the barren woman to dwell in a house, a mother rejoicing over children. [Psalm 112:9]*
*Epistle to the Corinthians, Pericope 180 [2 Corinthians 1:3–7].*
*Alleluia, Tone 5: They shed their blood like water. [Psalm 78:3]*
*Gospel according to Matthew, Pericope 4 [Matthew 2:13–23].*
*Communion Hymn: Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous. [Psalm 32:1] In the same month, on the 30th day.*[^670]
*The Holy Martyr Anysia; and our Venerable Mother Melania; and the Venerable Zoticus.*
*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Holy Anysia, 3, Tone 4. Podoben: "As noble" (Ꙗ҆́ко до́блѧ):*[^671]
*Enlightened by the splendor of virginity, O all-praised one, thou didst shine forth with the labors of martyrdom; for refusing to obey the command to worship the sun, thou didst endure unjust slaughter, and stained with blood, thou didst stand before the Sun of glory as a crown-bearer, illumined by the rays that stream forth from thence.*
*Showing forth the love of thy heart, O glorious one, with tears of compunction thou didst wet the earth, and with thy hair didst wipe the footstool of Christ, thinking of Him as present and foreseeing Him Whom thou didst desire; and touching His feet in thought, thou didst illumine thy soul with most divine visions.*
*Dispensing thy wealth and distributing it unto the poor, thou wast betrothed unto thine incorruptible Bridegroom; and as a bridal dowry, O all-glorious one, thou didst offer unto Him streams of blood and the imitation of His sufferings, which thou didst endure, O Anysia; and He alone settled thee in the bridal chamber on high, as a passion-bearer and martyr.*
*Other Stichera, of the Venerable Melania, in the same tone. Podoben: "Called from on high" (Зва́нный свы́ше):*[^672]
*Thou wast joined unto the angelic choirs when divine love set thee afire, moving thee to soar above visible things for the sake of dispassion and purity; then thou didst catch thy spouse with words submissive unto God, putting aside the unstable tumult of passing life. Therefore, having found eternal life and delight together with him, thou prayest the Master to save our souls.*
*Desiring the angelic life, when thou didst spit upon sweet food, exercising thyself in abstinence, vigilance, sleeping on the ground, and sackcloth, then thou wast a most pure vessel of the Divine Spirit, adorned with most bright gifts unto Him, O all-honored one; therefore thou didst draw people unto His divine zeal, and didst lead them unto the Mother of God, O Melania, for the salvation of our souls.*
*Adorned with the beauties of virtues, when thou didst fulfill the saving word, dispersing and giving ten thousands of thy gold unto the poor and destitute, then thou didst receive heavenly riches, being enriched with righteousness forever, and with incorruption and redemption. Therefore we honor thy dormition, and diligently entreat thee: Pray the Creator to enlighten our souls!*
*Glory, and now and ever, of the feast, Tone 1:*
*Glory to God in the highest, I hear today in Bethlehem from the bodiless hosts, unto Him Who has been pleased that peace should be on earth. Now is the Virgin more spacious than the heavens; for light has shone forth upon those in darkness, and has exalted the humble who sing in the manner of angels: Glory to God in the highest!*
*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2. Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*[^673]
*A Star from Jacob, Christ having shone forth, has enlightened the nations with the light of the knowledge of God: Him do we glorify!*
*Verse: Out of the womb before the morning star have I begotten Thee; the Lord hath sworn, and will not repent.*
*Rejoice, O Bethlehem, city of David! For from thee He Who is immortal and fatherless according to the flesh became incarnate of the pure Virgin, the Maiden of God.*
*Verse: The Lord said unto my Lord: Sit Thou at My right hand.*
*The Word of the Father, having received flesh, is born and wrapped in swaddling bands; He lies in a manger, releasing me from irrationality.*
*Glory, and now and ever, Tone 4:*
*Beholding him who was made according to the image and likeness corrupted through transgression, Jesus bowed the heavens and came down, and took up His abode without change in the virginal womb, that therein He might renew corrupted Adam, who cries: Glory to Thy manifestation, my Redeemer and my God!*
*Troparion of the Feast, Tone 4:*
*Thy Nativity, O Christ our God, hath shone forth the light of wisdom upon the world; for thereby they that served the stars were taught by a star to worship Thee, the Sun of righteousness, and to know Thee, the Dayspring from on high: O Lord, glory to Thee!*
*The service of Saint Zoticus is chanted at Compline.*
*Canon, Tone 8.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^674]
*Let us sing unto the Lord, Who led His people through the Red Sea; for He alone is gloriously glorified!*
*Troparia:*
*Entreat Christ, O Zoticus, that my darkened mind may be enlightened from on high, that I may worthily praise thee.*

*By thy life on earth, O God-wise one, thou didst show thyself emulating the angels, worthily abhorring the beauties of worldly life.*
*Theotokion:*
*The human race is built up through thee, O Virgin; for God, without leaving the heights, came down unto the earth.*
*Ode 3. Heirmos:*[^675]
*Thou art the foundation of those who flee unto Thee, O Lord; Thou art the light of the darkened, and my spirit sings of Thee!*
*Troparia:*
*Come today, ye strangers, let us joyfully lift up our voice in this radiant solemnity, blessing Zoticus!*
*Thou didst leave thy house, as Abraham left his tent of old, today receiving all the poor and richly feeding them.*
*Theotokion:*
*Thou didst quell every tempest in thy childbearing, O all-pure one; therefore kings vanquish enemies, exulting in peace.*
*Ode 4. Heirmos:*[^676]
*I heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation; I considered Thy works, and I glorified Thy Godhead!*
*Troparia:*
*Let us now glorify this radiant feast of the venerable Zoticus, which summons all to pass over unto the life of Christ.*
*Thou didst excel in miracles, and didst leave behind for us most glorious wonders, thy honorable deeds on earth, O most blessed one, as a divine pattern.*
*Theotokion:*
*We have found thee to be a place of propitiation, O Mother of God, and an unconquerable refuge in battles; and kings bear an honorable scepter.*
*Ode 5. Heirmos:*[^677]
*Enlighten us by Thy commandments, O Lord, and by Thy high arm grant us Thy peace, O Lover of mankind!*
*Troparia:*
*An adornment of virtue, O wonderful one, were thy honorable accomplishments shown to be: a divine home, a clothing for the naked.*
*Healing leprosy, O holy father, thou didst raise up thine honorable house as an infirmary, wherein every disease is worthily cured.*
*Theotokion:*
*Holy and honorable is the mystery that was revealed in thee, O Virgin Theotokos; for lo, truly we earthly ones have been reconciled unto God.*
*Ode 6. Heirmos:*[^678]
*The abyss of sins and the storm of transgressions trouble me, and drag me into the deep of grievous despair; but stretch forth Thy strong hand unto me, as unto Peter, O Pilot, and save me!*
*Troparia:*
*We, all the faithful, know thee to be a temple of the Spirit; for thou didst make thine house a most magnificent sanctuary, O most glorious one, wherein every disease is driven away by thy prayers.*
*Emulating Abraham, thou didst establish a hospice on earth, all-piously receiving the homeless, bringing in the naked, the wayfarers, the lame, the strangers, and the poor.*
*Theotokion:*
*He Who showed the cave to be heaven on earth, O Virgin, showed thee to be a heavenly temple adorned with angelic choirs, who faithfully cry unto Thy childbearing: Glory to God in the highest!*
*Sessional Hymn, Tone 5. Podoben: "The Word co-beginningless" (СобезначА́льное сло́во):*[^679]
*Thou didst quench the furnace of the passions with the dew of abstinence, O venerable one; and enriched with the gift of healings from God, O Zoticus, thou receivedst power to heal the grievous sicknesses of the faithful and to drive away the hosts of demons. Therefore with gladness we honor thee.*
*Ode 7. Heirmos:*[^680]
*The Hebrew children in the furnace boldly trampled upon the flame and changed the fire into dew, crying: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages!*
*Troparia:*
*Thou wast numbered among these venerable ones and with the divine choirs of the bodiless hosts, O most blessed Zoticus, with whom thou criest: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages!*
*By power and grace, O God-wise one, thou wast a helper of widows and the infirm, and wast shown to be a father of orphans, crying: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages!*
*Theotokion:*
*Destroy the strength of the barbarians, O Theotokos, and save thy people, and strengthen faithful kings who cry: Blessed, O all-pure one, is the fruit of thy womb!*
*Ode 8. Heirmos:*[^681]
*Sevenfold did the Chaldean tormentor furiously heat the furnace for the godly ones; but seeing them saved by a higher power, he cried unto the Creator and Deliverer: Ye children, bless; ye priests, praise; ye people, exalt Him above all unto all ages!*
*Troparia:*
*These victories, O wise one, these accomplishments, and the tears of the poor and of women, showed thy church to be higher than the heavens, and opened unto thee the entrances to the Kingdom; for in faith thou didst cry: Ye children, bless; ye priests, praise the Lord; ye people, exalt Him above all unto all ages!*
*Thou didst give no sleep unto thine eyes, O praiseworthy one, nor unto thine eyelids nor slumber unto thine eyelids, O God-pleasing one, until thou didst finish unto the end the divine work, the rational paradise of Christ, singing: Ye children, bless; ye priests, praise the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!*
*Theotokion:*
*Through the love for mankind of Thy mercy Thou camest unto us, Who for the sake of our salvation becamest as man, and didst dwell in a cave, wrapped in swaddling bands, and didst raise up the earthborn from the passions, as they sing in unison: Ye priests, praise the Lord; ye people, exalt Him above all unto all ages!*
*Ode 9. Heirmos:*[^682]
*Heaven was astonished at this, and the ends of the earth were amazed, that God has appeared unto men in the flesh, and thy womb became more spacious than the heavens. Therefore the hierarchs of angels and of men magnify thee, O Theotokos.*
*Troparia:*
*Grace was given thee by God, O father, to heal diseases: the poor, the withered, and the lame; receiving whom faithfully as the beloved of Christ, and rejoicing with them evermore, thou didst take up thy dwelling in the bosom of Abraham.*
*Thou didst richly feed every stranger, the naked, and the passerby, O father, ever rejoicing brightly with the patriarchs and with the righteous now, where is wealth and delight, where is the everlasting hope of the saved, where Christ is the wealth of all.*
*Theotokion:*
*As the true Mother of God, as the protectress and haven of those who honor thee, as the refuge of all who flee unto thee, O Virgin, as the joy of kings, and their glory, confirmation, and worthy crown: save thy people, O Theotokos!*
*Stichera, Tone 6. Podoben: "On the third day" (Тридне́венъ):*[^683]
*Like Abraham in thy ways, O wise one, thou wast shown to be in both things: thou didst open thine house as a sufficient abundance unto all, supplying those in need and granting mercy unto the poor.*
*Christ showed thee to be a receiver of garments and of the poor, a fervent champion of the afflicted, a defender in perils, a protector and deliverer of those who praise thee, O our father.*
*Glory, in the same tone:*
*Strengthened by the power and adorned by the grace of Him Who was born in the cave, O Zoticus: by fasting and abstinence thou didst conquer the passions, and didst receive the prizes of victory.*
*Now and ever, in the same tone:*
*As an infant in the manger did the Virgin who bare Thee without seed cradle Thee, O Christ God; and the choirs of the bodiless hosts cried aloud from on high cried aloud: Glory to the Creator and God of all!*
*At Matins, the Troparion of the Feast, thrice.*
*After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4. Podoben: "The stone being sealed" (Ка́мени запеча́танꙋ):*[^684]
*Being the Wisdom and Understanding before the ages, the Son consubstantial with the Father and the Spirit, Thou didst will in the latter times to be born of a Virgin for our sake, that He might save the world from the enemy's alien tyranny. Glory to Him that was born in the flesh! Glory to Him Who was well-pleased! Glory to Him Who has redeemed us by His Nativity!*
*Glory, and now and ever, the same.*
*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8. Podoben: "That which was commanded" (Повелѣ́нное):*[^685]
*Let heaven rejoice, let the earth be glad, for the Lamb of God was born on earth, granting deliverance unto the world; the Word Who is in the bosom of the Father came forth without seed from the Virgin. Beholding Whom, God in the flesh, the Magi marveled; and the shepherds cried aloud: Truly glory to the only God!*
*Glory, and now and ever, in the same tone. Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*[^686]
*O radiant and divine glory, Thou didst come forth from the virginal womb, and didst preserve the Virgin that bare Thee intact; and as a throne Thou didst show the manger wherein Thou didst rest when born, and the cave as a fair palace; the shepherds sang of Thee as King of all; and a star journeyed together with them, to show the divine light unto the Magi. Therefore we all cry unto Thee: O Master Christ God, send down the remission of transgressions unto those who celebrate Thy divine Nativity with faith!*
*Canon of the Feast, with the heirmos on 6: the composition of Lord John. Tone 1.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^687]
*The Master Who works wonders saved the people, turning the watery wave of the sea into dry land of old; and being born of the Virgin by His own will, He sets before us a passable path to heaven. Whom, equal in essence both to the Father and unto men, we glorify.*
*Troparia:*
*The sacred womb brought forth the Word, clearly prefigured unburned by the bush: God mingled with the human form, loosing the wretched womb of Eve from the ancient bitter curse; Whom we earthborn glorify.*
*The star showed unto the Magi the Word Who came before the sun to put an end to sins, manifest in a poor cave, wrapped in swaddling bands, Thee Who art merciful; Whom rejoicing they beheld as very Man and Lord.*

*Canon of the Holy Martyr Anysia. The composition of Theophanes. Tone 4.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^688]
*Traversing the Red Sea's deep with dryshod feet, ancient Israel of old, by Moses' hands stretched out in the form of a cross, conquered the power of Amalek in the wilderness.*
*Troparia:*
*As I sing of thy light-bearing memory, send down light unto me, O all-praised one, as thou standest in joy before the Father of lights, driving away the storm of my passions by thy prayers.*
*By abstinence thou didst renew the soul's field, O God-wise one, yielding the ear of martyrdom unto the Husbandman Who preserved thee and breathed strength into thee, O praiseworthy virgin-martyr.*
*Thy hands having most richly dispensed corruptible riches, thou didst acquire life that makes rich, which by no means passes away, and an inexhaustible treasure, O martyr, and incorruptible glory.*
*Theotokion:*
*From thee, O unwedded one, the Creator of all is born today in the flesh like unto us, and is wrapped in swaddling bands, He Who wraps the sea in mist, O Mother, Ever-Virgin.*
*Canon of the Venerable Melania. The composition of Theophanes. In the same tone [Tone 4].*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^689]
*I shall open my mouth, and it will be filled with the Spirit, and I shall utter a word unto the Queen Mother; and I shall appear, brightly celebrating, and rejoicing I shall sing of her wonders.*
*Troparia:*
*Illumining me who was blackened at the entrance by the darkening of passions, cleanse me by the light-bearing prayers of Thy venerable Melania, O Lover of mankind; and inspire a word in me who honor her.*
*Fervently didst thou follow Him Who for thy sake endured voluntary crucifixion: carrying thy cross upon thy shoulders, O all-blessed one, and diligently didst thou preserve His ordinances.*
*Thou didst wholly turn away from attachment unto parents and carnal pleasure, O God-wise one, desiring the beauty of Christ the only Lover, the glory of Whom all who partake of Him desire.*
*Theotokion:*
*The rich One becomes poor, enriching me with Godhead, who was evilly impoverished by lack of restraint of old; and the Beginningless One, lo, receives a beginning, being born of the Virgin, the Maiden of God.*
*Ode 3 [Canon of the Feast]. Heirmos:*[^690]
*Look down upon the singing of Thy servants, O Benefactor, humbling the exalted pride of the enemy; and, O all-seeing One, bearing the singers firm above sin, O Good One, establish them upon the foundation of faith.*

*Being counted worthy to behold beyond understanding the most rich childbearing of the all-pure Bride, the choir of the shining ones bowed down in strange manner, even the rank of the bodiless hosts who sing of Christ the King, Who took flesh without seed.*
*He that reigns on high over the heavens accomplishes in mercy for our sake, from the unwedded Maiden, being immaterial beforehand; but afterwards the Word having become gross in flesh, that He might draw unto Himself the fallen first-created man.*
*Another [Canon of the Holy Martyr Anysia]. Heirmos:*[^691]
*Thy Church rejoices in Thee, O Christ, crying aloud: Thou art my strength, O Lord, and refuge and confirmation!*
*Troparia:*
*Thy Creator, desiring thy soul's beauty, O martyr, betrothed thee unto Himself as a truly good and blameless bride.*
*Loving the death of the Passionless One Who was put to death for our sake, O honorable martyr, thou didst die a martyr's death.*
*As a spiritual slaughter, as a pure and perfect sacrifice, she that loved Thy Cross was offered unto Thee, O God.*
*Theotokion:*
*Thou wast a spacious dwelling for the uncontainable Creator, containing Him in the flesh, O full of grace, all-pure one.*
*Another [Canon of the Venerable Melania]. Heirmos:*[^692]
*Not in wisdom, nor in power, nor in wealth do we boast, but in Thee, the Father's hypostatic Wisdom, O Christ; for there is none holy save Thee, O Lover of mankind.*
*Troparia:*
*Forsaking the desires of lower things, O glorious one, thou didst piously direct thy whole desire by thy free will unto future and eternal things alone.*
*By diligent prayers thou didst adorn thy senses, and by the rays of the Spirit thou wast wholly luminous, imitating the immaterial life while in the body.*
*Fleeing and keeping silence, thou didst show forth instruction, the strengthening of the unsteady, the pattern of monastics, O God-wise Melania; therefore we sing of Thee.*
*Theotokion:*
*He Who covers the heavens with clouds by His will is wrapped in swaddling bands, held by the Virgin's hands, snatching me from the hands of the adversary.*
*Sessional Hymn of Saint Anysia, Tone 4. Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up" (Вознесы́йсѧ на крⷭ҇тъ):*[^693]
*Reigning over carnal passions, thou didst arm thyself with life-creating sufferings, O honorable Anysia, having piously dyed an incorruptible purple robe from thy blood; therefore as a blameless bride of the King of all of the King of all thou wast shown to be; but deliver us from perils, who celebrate thy glorious memory.*
*Glory, of Venerable Melania, in the same tone. Podoben: "Thou didst quickly anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*[^694]
*Accomplishing the divine commandments with diligence, thou didst disperse and distribute ten thousands of thy gold unto the poor; and taking thy cross upon thy shoulders, O Melania, together with thy bridegroom thou didst follow in faith Christ, Who was crucified in the flesh, our only God.*
*Now and ever, of the Feast, in the same tone:*
*All creation now rejoices divinely, for the Lord is born, the Son of God, born of the pure Virgin, freeing the whole human race and loosing the curse of the ancestral mother Eve: therefore as unto our Benefactor let us offer up a song.*
*Ode 4 [Canon of the Feast]. Heirmos:*[^695]
*Singing of old, the Prophet Habakkuk foretells the renewal of the human race, being counted worthy to behold the image ineffably; for a young Babe has come forth from the mountain of the Virgin, the Word, for the renewal of the peoples.*
*Troparia:*
*Equal unto men came forth the Most High, willingly taking flesh from the Virgin, to purge the poison of the serpent's head, bringing all unto the life-bearing light, being God, from the sunless gates.*
*The nations that of old were sunken in corruption, having completely escaped the enemy's destruction, lift up their hands with songs of praise, honoring Christ alone as Benefactor, Who has mercifully come unto us.*
*Sprung from the root of Jesse, O Virgin, thou didst surpass the boundaries of human nature, bearing the Father's eternal Word, as He Himself was well-pleased to pass through the sealed womb, by a strange emptying.*
*Another [Canon of the Holy Martyr Anysia]. Heirmos:*[^696]
*Beholding Thee lifted up upon the Cross, O Sun of righteousness, the Church stood in her station, worthily crying aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!*
*Troparia:*
*Following Thy life-bearing steps, Thy handmaid is wounded in the side by a spear, and unswervingly passes through the turning sword, O Master Christ, as she sings of Thee.*
*Shining with the splendors of martyrdom and adorned with the crown of incorruption, rejoicing thou standest before Christ thy Bridegroom, O all-praised martyr Anysia.*
*Having conquered by the trials of martyrdom him who tripped up the first Eve by deceit, thou didst cast him down, showing him to be powerless, singing unto Christ: Glory to Thy power O Lord!*
*Theotokion:*
*He Who created immaterial beings is born today of thee in the flesh as man, O Mother of God; unto Him let us sing: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!*
*Another [Canon of the Venerable Melania]. Heirmos:*[^697]
*He Who sits in glory upon the throne of the Godhead, Jesus the most divine, came on a swift cloud, with incorruptible hand, and saved those who cry: Glory to Thy power, O Christ!*
*Troparia:*
*Having put to death carnal lusts through abstinence, thou didst have the Life of the living dwelling in thee, O all-honorable one; unto Whom departing from earth thou didst take up thy dwelling, delighting in the heavenly Kingdom.*
*Having distributed thy many ten thousands of gold unto the hungry, thou truly storest them in treasures that never grow old, which preserve for thee an abundant abiding unto the ages.*
*The wealth of thy compassion became like a river, watering every heart of the poor, O glorious one; washing away the defilement of poverty, procuring for thee an inexhaustible, unstealable wealth in the heavens.*
*Theotokion:*
*Having submitted to the lusts of passions, rational though I am, like an irrational beast have I become likened unto the cattle; but do thou who didst bear the Co-eternal Word, despise me not who am perishing continually.*
*Ode 5 [Canon of the Feast]. Heirmos:*[^698]
*Out of the night of works of darkened delusion, do Thou, O Christ, come as cleansing unto us who now vigilantly offer a song as unto our Benefactor, granting an easy path, traversing which we shall find glory.*
*Troparia:*
*The Master again cuts off the fierce enmity against us by His coming in the flesh, that He might destroy the soul-destroying ruler, uniting the world with immaterial essences, rendering the Father approachable unto the creation like unto Him.*
*The people that of old were darkened, after days beheld the light of celestial brightness; and as an inheritance unto God, the Son brings the nations, granting there ineffable grace, where sin did more abound.*
*Another [Canon of the Holy Martyr Anysia]. Heirmos:*[^699]
*Thou, my Lord, hast come into the world as light, a holy light turning from gloomy ignorance those who sing of Thee in faith.*
*Troparia:*
*Knowing Thee, O Lord, to be the fountain of salvation, with unwavering heart Thy martyr drank the cup of salvation.*

*Heifer of Christ, God-pleasing slaughter, God-offered sacrifice, passion-bearer of the Lord, pray that we may be saved!*
*Thou wast light, having clearly drawn near unto the great Light; and thou enlightenest those who celebrate thy light-bearing memory.*
*Theotokion:*
*Thee do we set forth as an unconquerable weapon against enemies; thee have we acquired as confirmation and the hope of our salvation, O Bride of God.*
*Another [Canon of the Venerable Melania]. Heirmos:*[^700]
*The ungodly shall not see Thy glory, O Christ; but we, rising early from the night, sing of Thee, the Only-begotten, the Radiance of the Father's glory of the Godhead, O Lover of mankind.*
*Troparia:*
*Having wholly scraped away from thy soul the unsightly forms of the passions, O pure one, with the paint of abstinence thou didst depict therein dispassion and unfeigned love.*
*Having become radiant as a mirror, O maiden, thou didst brightly receive the gifts of the Divine Spirit, O glorious one, and didst enlighten the faithful with the brightness of thy life.*
*Quenching the inflammation of the passions through abstinence, thou didst kindle the soul's fire, which shines throughout thy whole life and repels demonic darkness.*
*Theotokion:*
*The Virgin bare God Emmanuel in the city of Bethlehem, Who of old by mercy opens Eden, which was locked through lack of restraint in eating and the serpent's deceit.*
*Ode 6 [Canon of the Feast]. Heirmos:*[^701]
*Abiding in the depths of the sea, Jonah prayed that Thou wouldest come and calm the tempest; and I, pierced by the arrow of the tormentor, sing unto Christ, the Destroyer of evils, that Thou wouldest quickly come unto my sluggishness.*
*Troparia:*
*God the Word, Who was in the beginning with God, now establishes that which was weak of old, seeing to preserve our human nature; whereby in this second communion, He immediately shows Himself free from passions.*
*He Who dwells in light comes for our sake from the loins of Abraham, to raise up the sons who had fallen into darkness and bowed down low in the gloom of transgressions; and now beyond His dignity He has been well-pleased to be in a manger, for the salvation of mankind.*
*Another [Canon of the Holy Martyr Anysia]. Heirmos:*[^702]
*I shall sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord, the Church cries unto Thee, having been cleansed from the blood of demons by the blood that flowed for mercy's sake from Thy side.*
*Troparia:*
*Taking up a masculine mind in a woman's body, O martyr, thou didst go forth unto battle against the bodiless enemies and with the weapon of endurance thou didst put them to death.*
*By the floods of thy blood thou didst dry up the sea of false belief, and didst water the honorable Church of Christ, O passion-bearer Anysia, praise of virgins!*
*Dryshod and without drowning didst thou pass through the storm of trials; therefore without wavering didst thou hasten unto the haven, and delightest in true stillness, O all-glorious one.*
*Theotokion:*
*He Who created man according to His own image, for His great tenderheartedness builds him anew, having clothed Himself wholly in him from thee, O Virgin, Mother of God.*
*Another [Canon of the Venerable Melania]. The same Heirmos:*[^703]
*Dryshod didst thou pass through the tempest of life, guided by the nod of Him Who made all things by a word; and thou didst attain unto the haven of salvation, O Melania.*
*By the sparks of thy fervent love for the Lord, all the burning arrows of sin were consumed, and the demonic malice was utterly destroyed.*
*Thy mind being deified by union with the Better, was separated from love for the flesh by the almighty nod: therefore thou didst bear the labors of fasting.*
*Theotokion:*
*The Lord born of the Virgin deifies me, and is wrapped in swaddling bands, working the loosing of my transgressions; and He Whom nothing can contain is contained in a cave.*
*Kontakion of the Feast, Tone 3. Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дѣ́ва дне́сь):*[^704]
*Today the Virgin gives birth unto the Transcendent in essence, and the earth offers a cave unto the Inaccessible; angels with shepherds give glory, and the Magi journey with a star: for for our sake is born a young Child, the God before the ages!*
*Ikos:*
*Bethlehem has opened Eden, come let us see! We have found delight in secret: come let us receive the things of paradise within the cave! There an unwatered root has appeared, blossoming with remission; there is found an undug well, whereof David desired to drink of old; there the Virgin, having brought forth a babe, straightway quenched the thirst of Adam and of David. Therefore unto Him let us go, where is born a young Child, the God before the ages!*
*Ode 7 [Canon of the Feast]. Heirmos:*[^705]
*The youths caught by love in their hearts, disdained the impious blasphemous babbling of the tormentor who raged without measure unto them the mighty fire submitted, as they said unto the Master: Blessed art Thou unto the ages!*
*The all-consuming furnace, raised to sevenfold heat, fiercely burns the servants, but saves the youths who with fear stood within; whom the flame crowned without grudging, while the Lord granted dew for the sake of their piety.*
*O Christ, Helper of men, having ineffable incarnation, Thou didst put to shame the hostile riddle, bearing the wealth of deification, having taken form now; for Whose sake in hope we have come from on high into the nether darkness.*
*Thou didst mightily cast down sin that evilly and unrestrainedly lifted itself up and impiously raged through the corruption of the world, which it drew down before; but today Thou savest from the snares, having willingly become incarnate, O Benefactor.*
*Another [Canon of the Holy Martyr Anysia]. Heirmos:*[^706]
*Thou Who in the fire didst save Thy Abrahamic children, and slewest the Chaldeans, whom justice righteously snared, O all-hymned Lord God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!*
*Troparia:*
*The tormenting torrents, rushing against thy soul's dwelling, O martyr, which was mentally fortified by the confession of Christ, by no means shook her as she cried out: Blessed art Thou, O God!*
*Knowing Christ to be the Sun of righteousness, O martyr, thou didst not will impiously to sacrifice unto the sun, as the tormentor commanded; but thou didst sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!*
*Having dipped a purple robe for thyself from thy sacred blood, O martyr, thou didst crown thy head with a triumphal crown; and now thou standest rejoicing before God, the immortal King.*
*Theotokion:*
*He Who clothes heaven with clouds and the earth with mist, is born of thy womb, is wrapped in swaddling bands, and is laid in a manger, O all-immaculate Mother of God, saving those who know thee as Theotokos.*
*Another [Canon of the Venerable Melania]. The same Heirmos:*[^707]
*Bearing the yoke of Christ together with thy spouse, O God-bearer, ye renewed your souls with the plow of prayers; and having tilled the field of good deeds, ye delight forever in celestial glory.*
*Like an olive tree planted in the house of God, as the Psalmist says, thou mystically anointest the hearts and faces of those who faithfully praise thy labors with the oil of thy sufferings, O venerable one.*
*Having quenched the furnace of the passions with the bedewing of abstinence, by the raining down of prayers thou didst pour forth floods of healings, drowning the assaults of the passions drowning the assaults of the passions for those who honor thee, O Melania.*
*Theotokion:*
*David called thee a fleece, O pure one, as having received the heavenly rain, drying up the streams of iniquity, and watering the minds of the faithful that were dried up by sin.*
*Ode 8 [Canon of the Feast]. Heirmos:*[^708]
*The youths who were bedewed in the furnace of old prefigure the sealed womb of the Maiden that gave birth supernaturally; and grace, working one marvel in both, rouses the people to singing.*
*Troparia:*
*Having escaped the ruin of claiming deification through deception, with trembling all creation unceasingly sings like the youths of the Word poured forth; with fear it brings an unrenowned praise, being corruptible, though wisely it endured.*
*Thou comest to turn back the straying human nature unto the flower-bearing pasture, from the desolate hills the rising of the nations, to quell the violent power of the murderer of man, having appeared as a Man, and being God by providence.*
*Another [Canon of the Holy Martyr Anysia]. Heirmos:*[^709]
*Stretching forth his hands, Daniel shut the lions' mouths in the den; and the youths, lovers of piety, girt with virtue, quenched the power of the fire, crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!*
*Troparia:*
*Thou didst distribute thy wealth unto widows, orphans, and the poor, and unto all in need, loving without doubt the commandments of the Almighty; and thou didst seek the cup of martyrdom, O honorable virgin, drinking which, thou didst put an end to worldly desires.*
*As a bridal dowry thou didst bring unto Christ fasting and tears, the mortification of passions, the shedding of blood, and the piercing of thy side: therefore He Who never grows old grants thee a crown, an incorruptible bridal chamber, and heavenly glory.*
*Thou dwellest with angels in the light, celebrating with the ranks of virgins and the assemblies of martyrs: beholding the face of thy Bridegroom face to face, and partaking of radiant glory, and crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!*
*Theotokion:*
*Henceforth a prince and ruler has visibly failed from the tribe of Judah; for thou, O all-immaculate one, didst give birth unto Christ, the expectation of the nations, promised unto him of old; unto Whom we sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!*
*Another [Canon of the Venerable Melania]. Heirmos:*[^710]
*The childbearing of the Mother of God saved the pious youths in the furnace: then prefigured, but now* [then prefigured], but now active, raises up the entire inhabited world to sing unto Thee: Hymn the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him above all unto all ages.[^711]

Having perfected thy heart and body as a temple for the transcendent Trinity, thou didst build up divine temples, O glorious one, wherein thou didst assemble ranks of virgins and choirs of monastics, singing in concord and exalting Christ above all unto all ages.

Thou didst acquire a mother of constant steadfastness; dispersing thy goods, thou didst give unto the poor: thy righteousness endures unto the ages. And the acquisition gained therefrom, which grows not old, has accrued unto thee, O God-bearing Melania. Therefore we honor thee as a true victor.

Shining forth with prudence, courage, chastity, and divine righteousness, thou didst possess loftiness-working humility which lifted thee unto the heavenly height; whereby, O venerable one, thou didst cast down the haughty serpent. Therefore we revere thee as a true victor.

*Theotokion:*
The surges of the passions confound me, the depth of despair submerges me; save me, O all-immaculate Mother, and I shall be saved: for thou didst bear the Savior and Lord, laid as an Infant in a manger, Whom we exalt above all unto all ages.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
It is easier for us, on account of fear, to love silence as free from peril, whereas out of love, O Virgin, it is hard to weave harmoniously composed hymns; but do thou, O Mother, grant us power commensurate with our resolve.[^712]

Beholding the dim types and the shadows passed away, O pure Mother, through the Word newly appeared from the shut gates, and contemplating the true Radiance, we worthily bless thy womb.

Having obtained their desire and been accounted worthy of God's coming, the Christ-loving people are now comforted by regeneration, for thou, O pure Virgin, dost bestow life-bearing grace to worship His glory.

*Another Canon. Ode 9, Tone 4. Heirmos:*
A cornerstone was cut without hands from an uncut mountain—which art thou, O Virgin—even Christ, Who joined together the separated natures: therefore, rejoicing, we magnify thee, O Theotokos.[^713]

They who rendered honors unto stones rather than unto the Creator, unable to endure beholding thee devoted unto God, O glorious one, cut thee down with the sword, betrothing unto thee divine immortality through death.

The city of Thessalonica boasts of thy swaddling-bands and thy sufferings, O virgin martyr; and the Church of the firstborn possesses thy divine spirit rejoicing with the supremely blessed.

Frankincense, gold, and myrrh did the Magi bring in faith unto Him Who was born in Bethlehem; and the passion-bearer brings the shedding of the blood of martyrdom, entreating Him on our behalf.

*Theotokion:*
Thou hast budded forth as a rod from the root of Jesse, O Mother of God, having borne for us today the Flower of the Godhead, Christ, O all-pure one: Whom, as uncontainable God, and now as an Infant wrapped in swaddling-clothes, we magnify.

*Another Canon. Ode 9, Tone 4. Heirmos:*
Eve through the disease of disobedience brought in the curse; but thou, O Virgin Theotokos, through the budding of thy childbearing, didst cause blessing to blossom forth for the world: therefore we all magnify thee.[^714]

Unto the height of ultimate perfection thou didst manifestly ascend, O blessed one, and didst attain unto the ranks of the bodiless ones; having drawn near unto the true Desire, thou hast now received the fountain of good things: therefore we all call thee blessed.

Thou rejoicest with the choirs of fasters, having practiced abstinence and put the passions to death; with unveiled face thou beholdest the beauty of God, which thou didst acquire through chastity before its manifestation, O all-blessed Melania.

Having walked the narrow path, thou hast attained the broad spaces of paradise, where is the joy of those who keep festival, where the tree of life is, continually remembering us who honor thy dormition.

*Theotokion:*
He Who is dreadfully borne upon the shoulders of the Cherubim now sits upon the arms of the pure Maiden and is wrapped in swaddling-bands, loosing the bonds of our evils; and He is nourished with milk as an Infant, Who nourishes every breath.

*Exapostilarion of the Feast, Tone 3 (sung twice):*
Our Savior, the Dayspring from on high, the Orient of orients, has visited us; and we who were in darkness and shadow have found the truth, for the Lord was born of the Virgin.[^715]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 6. Podoben: "Angelic [hosts]" (А҆́гглскїѧ):*
Behold, the Lamb of God, Who as God takes away the sin of the world, lies in a manger as an Infant, desiring to deliver rational beings from all irrational passions and from eternal torment; unto Whom we cry: Blessed art Thou Who wast born! O our God, glory be to Thee![^716]

*Verse:* Out of the womb before the morning star have I begotten Thee; the Lord hath sworn and will not repent.[^717]

*Another Sticheron:*

O mysteries beyond understanding and ineffable! Out of tender mercy God is born upon earth, wrapping Himself in the form of a servant, that He might snatch from the bondage of the alien those who cry unto Him in faith: Blessed art Thou Who wast born! O our God, glory be to Thee!

*Verse:* The Lord said unto my Lord: Sit Thou at My right hand.[^718]

Let us assemble reverently at the house of the Lord, with acclamations let us sing in concord of His tender mercy and great condescension; for in Bethlehem of Judea He was pleased to appear as an Infant; and let us cry aloud: Blessed art Thou Who wast born! O our God, glory be to Thee!

*Glory, and now. Podoben the same (Подо́бенъ то́йже):*
O my Sun, how shall I wrap Thee in swaddling-bands? How shall I nourish Thee with milk, the Nourisher of all nature? How shall I hold Thee with my hands, Who holdest all things? How shall I look upon Thee without fear, upon Whom the many-eyed dare not look? Thus spoke the unwedded Maiden, holding Christ.

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the feast: Ode 8, on 6.*

*In the same month, on the thirty-first day: Memory of our Venerable Mother Melania the Roman.*[^719]

*Her service was prescribed on the thirtieth day, because the Apodosis of the feast falls on the thirty-first day, and the entire service of the feast alone is sung.*

*At Vespers, the customary Kathisma. On "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 6, sung as on the feast itself. Glory, and now: "When Augustus reigned alone..." Prokeimenon of the day. There is no entrance. We do not read the Paroemias. Then, "Vouchsafe, O Lord." And the Litany: "Let us complete our evening prayer." At the Aposticha, Stichera of the feast with their verses; Glory, and now, of the feast. After "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart" and the Trisagion, the Troparion of the feast. Then the Litany: "Have mercy on us, O God," and the dismissal. We commemorate the saint of the day at the dismissal. We sing Small Compline according to custom with a Kathisma, and we say the troparia of the day. And we say the prayer: "Remember, O Lord, in the hope of the resurrection," and the dismissal. At Matins, on "God is the Lord," the Troparion of the feast, thrice.*

*After the Kathismas, Sessional hymns of the feast, and a reading of the feast. First Canon with its heirmos on 8; second Canon with its heirmos on 6: the heirmoi of both canons twice. Katavasia: the heirmos of the first canon, at the descent. After Ode 3, Hypakoe, Tone 8: "The firstfruits of the Gentiles." After Ode 6, Kontakion of the feast, and Ikos. At Ode 9, we do not sing "More honorable," but we sing the refrains of the feast, as on the feast itself. Exapostilarion of the feast, once; Glory, and now, the same. At the Praises, Stichera of the feast, on 4; Glory, Tone 6: "When the time [was come]..." And now, Tone 2: "Today Christ in Bethlehem..." And the Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, Troparion of the feast, litanies, and dismissal. And the customary procession into the narthex. And the First Hour: Troparion and Kontakion of the feast. At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of both canons: Ode 4, on 8. We do not say the antiphons of the feast. After the entrance, Troparion of the feast; Glory, and now, Kontakion of the feast. Then the Trisagion. Prokeimenon, Alleluia, and Communion verse of the feast; the Epistle and Gospel of the day.*[^720]

*If the Apodosis of the Nativity of Christ should fall on a Sunday:*[^721]
*At Small Vespers, the resurrectional stichera, and of the Theotokos according to custom. At Great Vespers, Kathisma 1: "Blessed is the man." On "Lord, I have cried," resurrectional stichera 3; and of the feast 4, Tone 2: "Come, let us rejoice in the Lord"; and of the saints 3.[^722] Glory of the saints, Tone 6: "We celebrate the memory"; and now, of the feast, Tone 2: "When Augustus reigned alone upon the earth."[^723] Entrance, Prokeimenon of the day. At the Litiya, Stichera of the feast; Glory, Tone 5: "Persian Magi"; and now, Tone 6: "The angels dance."[^724] At the Aposticha, resurrectional stichera; Glory of the saints, Tone 6: "The memory of the sacred [fathers]"; and now, of the feast.[^725] At the blessing of the loaves, the Troparion, "O Theotokos Virgin," twice; and of the saints, once: "Proclaim the good tidings, O Joseph."[^726] Then a reading in the apostolic epistles. At Matins, on "God is the Lord," the resurrectional Troparion, twice; Glory of the saints; and now, of the feast. After the Kathismas, resurrectional Sessional hymns and their Theotokia. And a reading in the Commentary Gospel: the Sunday after the Nativity of Christ. Then the Blameless [Psalm 118] with their troparia. The Hypakoe of the Tone. And a reading of the feast. The Hymns of Ascent and the Prokeimenon of the Tone. And "Let every breath." The resurrectional Gospel. And "Having beheld the resurrection of Christ." After Psalm 50, the resurrectional sticheron. The resurrectional Canon with its heirmos on 4; and of the saints on 4; and of the feast, both canons on 6. Katavasia of the feast: the heirmos of the first canon. After Ode 3, Kontakion* of the saints, and Ikos, and their Sessional hymn; Glory, and now, of the feast. And a reading. After Ode 6, Kontakion of the feast, and Ikos. At Ode 9, we sing "More honorable." Resurrectional Exapostilarion; Glory of the saints; and now, of the feast. At the Praises, resurrectional stichera 4; and idiomel stichera of the feast 4, Tone 4: "Rejoice, ye righteous," with their refrains; Glory of the saints, Tone 8: "Blood and fire";[^727] and now: "Most blessed art thou..."[^728] The Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, the resurrectional Troparion, litanies, and dismissal. And the Catechesis of St. Theodore the Studite, and the customary procession. And we sing: Glory, and now, the Gospel sticheron. And the First Hour in the narthex.*

*At the First Hour: the resurrectional Troparion; Glory of the feast; and now, the Theotokion of the Hours. After the Our Father, Kontakion of the feast. At the Third Hour: the resurrectional Troparion; Glory of the saints; and now, the Theotokion of the Hours. We recite the Kontakia of the feast and of the saints alternating.*

*At the Liturgy: the Beatitudes of the Tone on 4; and of the feast, from the first canon, Ode 4 on 4; and of the saints, Ode 6 on 4. After the entrance, the resurrectional Troparion, and of the feast, and of the saints; Glory, Kontakion of the saints; and now, of the feast. Prokeimenon of the feast, and of the saints: "Marvelous is God in His saints." Epistle to the Galatians, section 200 [Gal. 1:11-19]; Alleluia of the feast. Gospel according to Matthew, section 4 [Matt. 2:13-23]; Communion verse: "Praise the Lord," and another of the feast.*[^729]

*Note: If the afterfeast or Apodosis of the Nativity of Christ should fall on a Saturday:*
*On Friday evening: On "Lord, I have cried," Glory, and now, of the feast; we do not sing the first Theotokion of the current Tone.*
