# CONCLUDING APPENDICES AND COLOPHON

*Service of the Holy Great Martyr Barbara.*[^730]
*At Small Vespers, on "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 4, Tone 4. Podoben: "As one noble" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*[^731]
Having adorned thyself with blood-dyed vesture, O glorious Barbara, holy great martyr, thou wast united unto the Bridegroom, Christ our God, Who is comely in beauty, O virgin maiden, Who preserves thy virginity undefiled in heavenly habitations, in the bridal chamber not made with hands, O martyr. *(Twice)*

Imperfect in body, yet perfect in mind, having conquered the great dragon, thou didst crush his head, O glorious one, by spiritual power, and didst show his might to be powerless. Therefore an unconquerable crown was given unto thee, O Barbara of great renown, champion of the Trinity.

Having whitened thyself with drops of blood, thou didst shine forth manifestly like the sun, O all-praised one, and didst drive away the darkness of paternal godlessness, and didst wash away from thyself its mire by the grace of Christ, O great martyr Barbara: save those who honor thy valiant exploits and who festively celebrate thy radiant memory.

*Glory, Tone 2:*
Having been richly enlightened by spiritual light, thou didst despise corruptible wealth, having loved that which is heavenly alone; and having manifestly put on the strength of martyrdom, thou didst eagerly bend thy neck unto the sword: therefore thou didst also put to shame the enemy—thy father who beheaded thee—being crowned with the wreath of victory, O most glorious great martyr Barbara; pray that we all may be saved.

*And now, Theotokion:*
Upon thee have we set our hope, O Theotokos: O pure one, let us not fall away; save us from perils, O helper of the perplexed, and scatter the counsels of our adversaries: for thou art our salvation, O blessed one.

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 1. Podoben: "Unto the heavenly ranks" (Не́бнымъ чинѡ́мъ):*[^732]
Having despised an impious father and mother, O Barbara, thou didst love God and the heavenly Jerusalem, in which thou now dwellest: entreat good Christ that we also may abide together with thee.

*Verse:* Marvelous is God in His saints, the God of Israel.[^733]
Neither affection for parents, nor pleasures, nor bodily beauty, nor wealth, nor torments tear thee away from the love of the Creator: Whom make merciful unto us, O great martyr.

*Verse:* Unto the saints that are in His earth.[^734]
Confessing one God in Trinity with boldness, O Barbara, and beheaded, thou didst receive from on high from Christ the crown of victory, with Whom thou now reignest: entreat peace for all.

*Glory, Tone 2:*
Like precious myrrh didst thou bring thy blood unto the Bridegroom Christ, O invincible martyr Barbara; and from Him thou didst receive an incorruptible crown as thy reward. Therefore, even after thy suffering, healings richly flow from thy precious relics unto those who approach with faith and honor thee; which pour forth unstintingly also unto us, and pray that our souls may be saved.

*And now:*
All my hope I place upon thee, O Mother of God: preserve me under thy shelter.

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
O all-blessed ewe-lamb Barbara, having been divinely illumined with the thrice-sunlit light of the Holy Trinity, and established in the font unto the defeat of paternal deception, thou didst confess the faith of Christ. Therefore, O honorable Barbara, grace was granted thee from on high to heal all sicknesses and diseases: by her prayers, O Christ God, save our souls.[^735]

*At Great Vespers:*
*We sing "Blessed is the man," Antiphon 1. And Stichera to the Saint on 8, Tone 2. Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*[^736]
When the all-blessed Juliana beheld the glorious martyr Barbara suffering with wounds at the dread tribunal, and her whole body cut to pieces with diverse tortures, she cried aloud with fervent tears: O Word of God, O Lover of mankind, account me now worthy to be a partaker with her!

One indeed in disposition toward piety was Barbara and Juliana, and by the power of the Holy Spirit they strove against the enemy, and having powerfully conquered him, were accounted worthy of glory from Christ God. Therefore, having destroyed the harm of destructive passions, they bestow healings upon all the faithful.

When sweet death was pronounced upon thee, O most honorable martyr Barbara, rejoicing and hastening thou didst finish thy course; and sacrificed by the all-lawless hands of an impious parent thou didst offer thyself as a fruit unto God; therefore, truly rejoicing with the wise virgins, thou beholdest the radiance of Christ thy Bridegroom.

*Glory, Tone 6:*
Having forsaken country, kindred, and possessions, O Barbara, and hated an impious father, thou didst love God, unto Whom thou wast betrothed, and wast named a great merchant: pray Him that our souls may be saved.[^737]

*And now, Theotokion:*
*Who would not call thee blessed...*[^738]

*Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day. And three readings:*

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 43):*[^739]
Thus says the Lord: All the nations were gathered together, and princes shall be gathered out of them. Who will declare these things among them? Or who will declare unto you things from the beginning? Let them bring forth their witnesses, and let them be justified; and let them hear, and let them speak the truth. Be ye My witnesses, and I too am a witness, says the Lord God, and the servant whom I have chosen: that ye may know, and believe Me, and understand that I am He. Before Me there was no other God, and after Me there shall be none. I am God, and beside Me there is no savior. I have declared, and have saved, I have brought reproach, and there was no strange god among you. Ye are My witnesses, and I am the Lord God; even from the beginning I am He, and there is none that can deliver out of My hands: I will work, and who shall turn it back? Thus says the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel Who delivers you.

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 62):*[^740]
Thus says the Lord: Upon thy walls, O Jerusalem, have I set watchmen all the day and all the night, who shall not hold their peace unto the end, making mention of the Lord; for there is none like unto you, if thou shalt establish and make Jerusalem a praise upon the earth. The Lord hath sworn by His glory and by the strength of His arm: I will no more give thy corn and thy provisions unto thine enemies, nor shall the sons of strangers drink thy wine, for which thou hast labored. But they that gather it shall eat it, and praise the Lord; and they that harvest it shall drink it in My holy courts. Go through, go through My gates; prepare the way, and make a path for My people; cast away the stones from the way, and lift up a standard for the nations. For behold, the Lord hath made it to be heard unto the ends of the earth. Say ye to the daughter of Sion: Behold, thy Savior comes, having His reward with Him, and His work before His face. And He shall call them a holy people, redeemed by the Lord; and thou shalt be called a sought-out city, and not forsaken.

*Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon (Chapter 5):*[^741]
The righteous live unto the ages, and their reward is with the Lord, and the care of them is with the Most High. Therefore shall they receive a kingdom of glory, and a crown of beauty from the hand of the Lord: for with His right hand shall He cover them, and with His arm shall He shield them. He shall take His zeal for complete armor, and shall make the creature His weapon for vengeance upon the enemies. He shall put on righteousness as a breastplate, and shall take unfeigned judgment instead of a helmet. He shall take holiness for an invincible shield: His severe wrath shall He sharpen for a sword, and the world shall fight with Him against the foolish. Right-aiming shafts of lightnings shall go forth, and from the well-rounded bow of the clouds shall they fly unto the mark. And from the stony-throwing fury shall hailstones full of wrath be cast; the water of the sea shall rage against them, and the rivers shall inundate them sharply. A spirit of power shall stand up against them, and like a whirlwind shall sift them: thus lawlessness shall make the whole earth a wilderness, and wrongdoing shall overthrow the thrones of the mighty. Hear therefore, O ye kings, and understand; learn, ye that are judges of the ends of the earth. Give ear, ye that rule multitudes, and that boast yourselves in the throngs of the nations: For power is given unto you from the Lord, and sovereignty from the Most High.

*At the Litiya, Stichera, Tone 2:*
Radiantly honoring the incorruptible bride who was adorned by the Holy Spirit, we keep thy radiant memory, O martyr passion-bearer; and through devout veneration of thy holy shrine of relics, continually drawing healing for our passions, O all-praised Barbara, we glorify thee in faith.

Sustained by the power of thy Creator, O all-praised one, thou didst depict His sufferings in the flesh, and didst endure all patient suffering of afflictions; and now thou dwellest on high, wearing painless glory and an unfading crown, and thou beholdest Him Whom the angelic ranks behold rejoicing, O God-inspired Barbara.

Behold, thou didst offer the severance of thy members unto thy Bridegroom, O most honorable one; therefore He accounted thee worthy of the heavenly bridal chamber, and enlightens thee with the ever-existing light of divine glory; before Whom thou standest rejoicing and entreating Him for us who celebrate thy memory in faith, O Barbara.

*Glory, Tone 2:*

The crafty enemy was put to shame, conquered by a woman, even as he had wielded power toward sin through the foremother; for the Father's Word, incarnate of the Virgin without change and without confusion, as He alone knows, loosed the curse of Eve and of Adam, even Christ Who worthily crowned the martyr Barbara, and for her sake grants unto the world cleansing and great mercy.[^742]

*And now, Theotokion:*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 5:*
Rejoicing, thou didst stand before the tormentor, O glorious martyr, clearly proclaiming the faith: many scourgings and torments didst thou endure, O passion-bearing Barbara; having put the tormentor to shame, thou wast betrothed unto Christ: pray Him on behalf of us who in faith celebrate thy memory.

*Verse:* Planted in the house of the Lord, in the courts of our God.[^743]
Beholding thee suffering valiantly for the sake of the true faith, the angels rejoiced with joy, glorifying the God of all Who strengthened thee; and men, worshipping Him, praise Him with hymns, Who gave thee, O virgin Barbara, victory over the enemy: pray Christ God that we also may conquer him, and that our souls may be saved.

*Verse:* With patience I waited for the Lord, and He gave ear unto me, and heard my prayer.[^744]
Fearing neither wounds nor afflictions, thou wast not terrified by the tormentor's fury, and thou didst disregard all things, O martyr Barbara; but rather didst choose the love of Christ, and having been betrothed unto Him, thou standest at His right hand, arrayed and adorned as a queen in gilded raiment, fervently praying for those who with faith and love celebrate thy memory.

*Glory, Tone 6:*
Walking by the path of suffering, thou didst escape ancestral counsel, O God-fearing Barbara; and as a wise virgin bearing a lamp, thou didst enter into the courts of thy Lord; and as a valiant martyr, thou didst receive grace to heal evil bodily passions. But deliver also from spiritual sicknesses us who praise thee, through thy prayers unto God.[^745]

*And now, Theotokion:*
No one that hastens unto thee turns away put to shame from thee, O most pure Virgin Theotokos; but he asks for grace, and receives a gift according to his profitable petition.[^746]

*At the blessing of the loaves: Troparion of the Saint, twice (look at Small Vespers); and "O Theotokos Virgin," once.*

*At Matins, after the first Kathisma: Sessional hymn, Tone 5. Podoben (Подо́бенъ): Tone 5, Podoben: "Co-unoriginate Word" (Собезначя́лное):*
Assembling in faith at the memory of the saints, we celebrate the memory of the passion-bearer; for by prayer she slew the author of evil, the enemy, who of old through deceit seduced Eve in incorruption, and she prays unto the Lord to have mercy on our souls.

*Glory, and now, Theotokion:*
Rejoice, O holy and God-trodden mountain! Rejoice, O animate and unburnt bush! Rejoice, O only bridge unto God for the world, leading mortals across unto eternal life! Rejoice, O incorrupt maiden, who without knowing man didst bear the Salvation of our souls!

*After the second Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4. Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up" (Вознесы́йсѧ):*
Having loved Christ Thy Bridegroom, and having brightly prepared Thy lamp, thou didst shine forth with virtues, O all-praised one; therefore thou didst enter with Him into the wedding, having received from Him the crown of suffering. Snatch us from perils, O Barbara, who celebrate Thy memory.

*Glory, and now, Theotokion:*
The Father's Word, Christ our God, Who was incarnate of thee, have we known, O Virgin Theotokos, alone pure and blessed; therefore we ever glorify thee, magnifying thee.

*After the Polyeleos, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4. Podoben: "Thou didst quickly anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*
Having forsaken paternal wealth, and having loved Christ divinely, thou didst find the wealth of heavenly glory, O martyr; and, wholly shielded by the prayer of grace and by the weapon of the Cross, thou didst trample down the tormentor. Therefore the angels, marveling at thy contest, said: "The enemy has fallen, conquered by a woman." Thou hast appeared as a crown-bearer, O martyr, since Christ has crowned thee, Who grants great mercy unto the world.

*Glory, and now, Theotokion:*
Having received the Word from the angel into thy womb, and having given birth to the incarnate God Emmanuel: O Theotokos, pray for our souls.

*The Graduals, the first Antiphon of Tone 4.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 4:* God is marvelous in His saints, the God of Israel.[^747] *Verse:* In the congregations bless ye God, the Lord.[^748]

*Let every breath:*

*Gospel according to Matthew, pericope 106.*[^749]

*After Psalm 50, Sticheron, Tone 6:*
Having forsaken country, race, and possessions... *(Look at Great Vespers, folio 205 on the reverse).*[^750]

*Canon of the Theotokos, Tone 8, with the Heirmos unto 6; and of the Saint, two Canons unto 8. Tone 2.*

*Ode 1, Tone 2. Heirmos:*
Of old, the overwhelmingly equipped power cast Pharaoh's whole host into the deep; and the incarnate Word destroyed all-wicked sin, the most glorious Lord, for gloriously has He been glorified.

*Troparion:*
O super-divine, venerable Trinity, Who above mind bestowest a gift upon Thy servants, breathe a radiant ray into my darkened mind, that I may praise Thy ever-memorable martyr Barbara. *(Twice)*

*Troparion:*
Truly the glory of Thy martyrs has surpassed every bound of praises, O Lover of mankind; but having accepted the praise from faith according to our strength, send down richly in return, O Master, a recompense.

*Troparion:*
From a thorny root sprang forth a most beautiful rose, perfuming the Church of Christ, and having reddened herself with the purple of suffering by blood, O glorious Barbara, whom we worthily hymn.

*Second Canon of the Saint, Tone 8. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Having traversed the water as dry land, and escaped Egyptian evil, the Israelite cried: "Let us sing unto our Deliverer and God!"

*Troparion:*
Having forsaken the mire-filled water of impiety, thou didst hasten unto the purifying water, O Barbara; do thou also purify our hearts, purely to sing of thy sufferings.

*Troparion:*
Having purified thyself with the water of baptism, O great-martyr, thou didst cleave unto the pure Bridegroom Christ; unto Whom do thou also purely unite us through thy prayers.

*Glory:*
Emulating Him Who drowned the crafty dragon in the water, by thy suffering blood thou didst submerge the enemy's power, O passion-bearer; pray the Savior that we also may be delivered from him.

*And now, Theotokion:*
Grant me, O all-pure one, the purifying water of tears, and having cleansed me from the mire of lawlessness, present me pure, O Bearer of God, unto Thy Son and God.

*Ode 3, Tone 2. Heirmos:*
The desert has blossomed as a lily, O Lord, the barren church of the nations, by Thy coming, wherein my heart has been established.

*Troparion:*
Wounded by Thy love as by a bridegroom's, O Master, with irrepressible longing the passion-bearer Barbara hated all her paternal godlessness.

*Troparion:*
Neither beauty of pleasure, nor flower of comeliness, nor wealth, nor youthful pleasures delighted thee, O glorious Barbara, who wast betrothed unto Christ, O good virgin.

*Troparion:*
In the face of perfect contests, nothing proved a hindrance to womanly weakness, nor youth of age, O Christ; for she was strengthened by Thy invisible power.

*Second Canon of the Saint, Tone 8. Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Celestial vault's supreme Creator, O Lord, and Builder of the Church, do Thou establish me in Thy love, O summit of desires, confirmation of the faithful, O only Lover of mankind.

*Troparion:*
Beholding the ornament of the celestial vault, O wise virgin Barbara, thou didst recognize the supreme Creator, and having loved Him, thou didst choose to serve Him: do thou also establish us in His love through thy prayers.

*Troparion:*
Depicting the all-radiant essence of the celestial Creator in Trinity, thou didst command three windows to be fashioned in thy father's bathhouse, teaching us to worship the Triune Godhead; vouchsafe that we also may worship Him eternally.[^751]

*Glory:*
Longing for the celestial bridal chamber, thou didst preserve the beauty of thy virginity for the heavenly Bridegroom, having despised the temporary: strengthen me also, O martyr, to serve Him in purity.

*And now, Theotokion:*
Having given birth to the celestial Creator, O all-hymned Theotokos, thou hast appeared more spacious than the heavens: having turned me away from the broad and ruinous path, guide me unto the heavenly path, I pray thee.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 5. Podoben: "The beauty of virginity" (Красотѣ̀ дѣ́вства):*
In thy suffering thou didst astonish all, in that thou didst endure the scourgings, bonds, torments, and prisons of the tormentors, O most praised Barbara; therefore Christ gave thee a crown from heaven. Unto Whom having longed, thou didst zealously hasten, and He bestowed grace upon thee, O martyr, to pour forth healings unto men.

*Glory, and now, Theotokion:*
Thou wast the divine tabernacle of the Word, O only all-pure Mother and Virgin, who by purity didst surpass the angels: me, who beyond all have become dust, defiled by fleshly trespasses, do thou purify with the divine waters of thy prayers, granting great mercy, O pure one.

*Ode 4, Tone 2. Heirmos:*
Thou didst come from the Virgin, neither mediator nor angel, but Thyself, O Lord, incarnate, and didst save me, whole man; therefore I cry unto Thee: "Glory to Thy power, O Lord!"

*Troparion:*
Born of the Virgin, Thou didst grant unto maidens by deed of martyrdom to cast down the deceiver; therefore the fair-victorious Barbara mocked his pride.

*Troparion:*
The foremother, deceived of old by the wiles of the deceiver, was cast out from the delight of paradise; but Barbara, having mocked him, now abides in the heavenly bridal chamber.

*Troparion:*
By Thy Cross Thou didst destroy the power of death; therefore, not sparing her body, O Christ, the maiden Barbara most valiantly endured wounds with a steadfast mind.

*Second Canon of the Saint, Tone 8. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation; I understood Thy works, and I glorified Thy Godhead.

*Troparion:*
Having heard the heavens declaring the glory of God, O Barbara, Thou didst desire to glorify God upon earth: vouchsafe that we also may share in His glory.

*Troparion:*
When thy father heard thee confessing the supreme Father, he pursued thee unto slaughter; yet he could not tear truth away from the true God.

*Glory:*
Hearing the paternal threats and enduring torments from him, O Barbara, thou didst remain unshaken: direct me also to be unshaken in virtues.

*And now, Theotokion:*
Give ear, O all-pure Lady, unto my supplication, and deliver me from evil things, and vouchsafe that I may hear the voice of the blessed calling into the Kingdom.

*Ode 5, Tone 2. Heirmos:*
Thou becamest a Mediator between God and men, O Christ God; for through Thee, O Master, we have access from the night of ignorance unto Thy Father, the Source of Light.

*Troparion:*
Having commanded the bathhouse to be illumined with three windows, thou didst mystically portray baptism, O Barbara, the soul's radiant, shining cleansing by the light of the Trinity.

*Troparion:*
Kindled with zeal for the holy God, the all-praised Barbara spat upon the defiled faces of the falsely named gods, as the maiden mocked the external ruler of the world.

*Troparion:*
Fleeing the fury of thy cruel father, O Barbara, the mountain straightway cleft asunder and received thee, even as of old it did the ever-memorable protomartyr Thecla, when Christ worked wonders.[^752]

*Second Canon of the Saint, Tone 8. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Illumine us with Thy commandments, O Lord, and with Thy high arm grant Thy peace unto us, O only Lover of mankind.

*Troparion:*
Having illumined thy lamp with faith, O martyr, thou didst surrender thy body to be burned with torches, desiring to enter brightly into the heavenly bridal chamber.

*Troparion:*
People darkened by unbelief were illumined with faith, beholding thee, O martyr, valiantly enduring burnings, beatings, and lacerations.

*Glory:*
Illumine me, O Barbara, who am darkened by the mist of sin and make me to be shone upon by the never-waning light, O radiant virgin, I pray thee.

*And now, Theotokion:*
Thou didst illumine darkened nature, O Theotokos, having given birth to the true Light; therefore, having illumined me with light, deliver me from dark enemies.

*Ode 6, Tone 2. Heirmos:*
Held fast in the depth of sins, O Savior, and tempest-tossed in the abyss of life, yet even as Thou didst Jonah from the beast, lead me also up from passions, and save me.

*Troparion:*
As Thou didst promise, O Savior, to grant wisdom in godly confidence unto those standing for Thy sake before the tribunal of the tormentors, with this wisdom the martyr Barbara was filled.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst refute the deceit of the godless by God-wise word, O glorious Barbara, and by the endurance of deeds thou didst strangle the vain thoughts of the tormentors.

*Troparion:*
To be scraped unsparingly with wounds, and her ribs to be severely rubbed with haircloth for Christ's sake, the blameless passion-bearer surrendered her body.

*Second Canon of the Saint, Tone 8. Ode 6. Heirmos:*
I will pour out my prayer unto the Lord, and unto Him will I declare my afflictions; for my soul is filled with evils, and my life has drawn near unto Hades, and I pray like Jonah: "Lead me up from corruption, O my God!"

*Troparion:*
Christ heard thy martyr's prayer, O Barbara: He visited thee shut up in prison, granted wholeness unto thy wounds, and strengthened thee for the contest; do thou also heal my sinful wounds, O martyr, I pray thee.

*Troparion:*
By thy prayer and steadfast martyr's endurance, and by marvelous healing, thou didst draw Juliana away from wickedness to suffer with thee for Christ; draw me also unto heavenly thoughts, O passion-bearer.

*Glory:*
Everyone who brings prayer with faith unto thee, O martyr, and hastens unto thy holy relics, quickly receives healing of soulful and bodily passions; grant this richly unto us also, we pray.

*And now, Theotokion:*
Receive our supplication, O all-pure one, and by thy all-powerful prayer pray the Lover of mankind, God Whom thou didst bear, that we may be delivered from enemies visible and invisible, from sins, and from every torment.

*Kontakion, Tone 4. Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up" (Вознесы́йсѧ):*
Having followed God piously hymned in Trinity, O passion-bearer, thou didst trample down the idol shrines; and having contested in the midst of the arena O Barbara, thou wast not terrified by the threats of the tormentors, O manly-minded one, ever singing with a loud voice: "I venerate the Trinity, the one Godhead!"

*Ikos:*
Assembling, let us worthily honor Barbara, who was betrothed unto Christ through martyrdom; that, having been delivered through her prayers from soul-corrupting pestilence, destruction, earthquake, and ruin,[^753] we may pass our life in peace, being vouchsafed with all the saints who from the ages have well-pleased God to walk in the light, and to sing with them: "Thou hast made marvelous Thy mercies, O Savior, unto all men who confess in faith: We venerate the Trinity, the one Godhead!"

*Ode 7, Tone 2. Heirmos:*
The God-opposing decree of the lawless tormentor raised a high flame; but Christ spread spiritual dew over the pious children, He Who is blessed and supremely glorified.

*Troparion:*
The tormentor who furiously raged to destroy the earth and consume the sea, lies at the end like a plaything beneath the feet of the maiden Barbara; for Christ trampled him down and bound him like a petty bird.

*Troparion:*
With unbearable wounds, while thy whole body was scraped and reddened with drops of blood, thou didst endure being burned with torches upon thy ribs, O all-praised martyr, thanking Christ, O glorious Barbara.

*Troparion:*
O inhuman and unmerciful cruelty of the tormentors, and surpassing godlessness! For as in a butchery they cruelly cut off the martyr's breasts with swords,[^754] while she fixed her mind upon Christ the Contender.

*Second Canon of the Saint, Tone 8. Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The Hebrew children boldly trampled upon the flame in the furnace, and changing the fire into dew, they cried: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages!"

*Troparion:*
The angel who preserved the Hebrew children unburnt from the fire, also protected thee from shame, O Barbara, as thou wast led naked, clothing thee with a raiment from on high, who sangest: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages!"

*Troparion:*
Counting torments as children's play, thou didst not spare thy body from being scraped and acutely rubbed for Christ's sake, O great-martyr, singing: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages!"

*Glory:*
The Hebrew children I also emulate, O Barbara: I praise Christ Who gave thee strength. Do thou strengthen me unto the contest of virtues, and vouchsafe that I may be clothed in the raiment of incorruption unto the ages.

...unto the ages.

*And now, Theotokion:*
At thy childbearing, who remained a virgin even after childbirth, I marvel, O Theotokos. Make marvelous therefore upon me also the mercy of thy Son, that, having found mercy through thee, I may sing: "Blessed is God Who blessed thee as His Mother unto the ages!"

*Ode 8, Tone 2. Heirmos:*
Of old, the fiery furnace in Babylon divided its operation by the divine command, burning the Chaldeans, but bedewing the faithful as they sang: "Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!"

*Troparion:*
Christ appeared unto thee in unapproachable light, O Barbara, when thou wast shut up in prison, commanding thee to be of good cheer, healing thy wounds, and granting joy; therefore thou wast winged with the desire for thy Bridegroom.

*Troparion:*
Clearly was Thy prophecy shown fulfilled, O Christ; for a father betrays his child unto death,[^755] and the wretched parent himself became the perpetrator of the slaughter of Thy martyr; therefore he was consumed by fire from heaven.

*Troparion:*
A radiant angel clothed thee, venerable Barbara, with light-bearing raiment when thou wast stripped naked for Christ's sake, as a bride going through passions; for thou didst strip off garments, O martyr, having received divine transformation.

*Second Canon of the Saint, Tone 8. Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Having become conquerors over the enemy and the flame by grace, the children, striving zealously for the commandment, sang: "Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!"

*Troparion:*
The tormentors, striving to conquer thy invincible faith, unsparingly cut off thy breasts; but thou, steadfastly enduring, didst nourish the bystanders with the milk of godly teaching, as they blessed Christ unto the ages.

*Troparion:*
By thy courage, O martyr Barbara, thou didst conquer all the subtle wiles of the tormentors: pray then the Master Christ, we pray thee, to grant victory over enemies unto all the faithful who sing: "Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!"

*Glory:*
Thou hast appeared as conqueress of thy cruel father, O martyr; for he was cast down by heavenly fire into hellish fire, while thou didst ascend into heaven: intercede that this may be granted unto me also, delivering me from the fire unto the ages.

*And now, Theotokion:*
Conquer, O all-pure one, the enemies visible and invisible who strive to cast us down, and deliver me from all passions, that I may celebrate and sing: "Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!"

*Ode 9, Tone 2. Heirmos:*
The Son of the unoriginate Father, God and Lord, having become incarnate of the Virgin, has appeared unto us, to illumine the darkened and gather the dispersed; therefore the all-hymned Theotokos do we magnify.

*Troparion:*
When thou wast about to receive a glorious end of thy martyrdom by the sword, O Barbara, being vouchsafed martyr's crowns together with Juliana, thou didst hear a divine voice fulfilling your petitions.

*Troparion:*
United now unto thy Bridegroom, Christ the King of all, and shining with the glory of divine light in heavenly chambers, O Barbara, look down upon those who sing of thee, delivering them from passions, and bringing them unto the living God.

*Troparion:*
Christ has fulfilled thy petition, O passion-bearer Barbara, granting healings unto those who celebrate thy annual memory with faith; for truly thy praised wonderworkings have surpassed the sand of the sea.

*Second Canon of the Saint, Tone 8. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Truly confessing thee as Theotokos, saved through thee, O pure Virgin, with the heavenly hosts do we magnify thee.

*Troparion:*
Truly confessing God, O martyr, thou didst inherit the heavenly bridal chamber; vouchsafe that we also may attain it, that with thee we may eternally magnify Christ.

*Troparion:*
Truly was Christ's prophecy fulfilled upon thee, O Barbara: "A father shall betray his child unto death,"[^756] through which death thou didst find eternal life.

*Glory:*
Truly no one who hastens unto thee, O passion-bearer, departs empty of thy grace; with which do thou fill me also, I pray thee.

*And now, Theotokion:*
Truly didst thou bear the true God in the flesh, O Theotokos; make Him merciful unto us in the day of judgment, that endlessly with Him we may magnify thee.

*Exapostilarion of the Saint. Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Жены́ ꙋ҆слы́шите):*
As a most beautiful rose didst thou spring forth from a thorny root, O virgin Barbara, having reddened thyself with the sacrifice of blood in holy suffering, O martyr; and now save from perils those who with love celebrate thy divine memory.

*Glory, and now, Theotokion:*
Truly do we confess thee as Theotokos, O Lady, who are saved through thee; for thou didst ineffably give birth to God, Who by the Cross destroyed death, and drew unto Himself the assemblies of the righteous, with whom we praise thee, O Virgin.

*At the Praises, Stichera of the Saint, Tone 1. Idiomela: By Anatolius:*
Having despised the enjoyment of earthly food, and having hated paternal wealth together with glory, thou didst love the heavenly Bridegroom, O all-praised Barbara. For having had thy head severed with the sword, thou didst enter with the wise virgins unto the Bridegroom Christ; therefore, driving away destructive diseases, thou healest the faithful by the operation of the Holy Spirit, and prayest unceasingly for our souls.

*Tone 2. By Byzantios:*
The crafty enemy was put to shame, conquered by a woman, even as he had wielded power toward sin through the foremother; for the Father's Word, incarnate of the Virgin without change and without confusion, as He alone knows, loosed the curse of Eve and of Adam, even Christ Who worthily crowned the martyr Barbara, and for her sake grants unto the world cleansing and great mercy.[^757]

*Sticheron:*
The God-called martyr Barbara, suffering at the tribunal, said: "Cruel indeed are the present torments, O tormentors, but joyous is the reception of eternal life! I will by no means prefer earthly things over heavenly; therefore cut, scrape my flesh, and surrender me to fire: rejoicing, I will go unto my Bridegroom Christ!" By her prayers, O Christ God, send down Thy mercies, and save us who faithfully celebrate her sufferings.

*Sticheron:*
Come, ye peoples, let us sing of the solemnity of the passion-bearer Barbara today; for neither sword, nor fire, nor other torment, nor the intricate snares of Belial conquered her. And in faith let us cry unto her: Pray Christ, O noble martyr all-glorious, to grant great mercy unto us!

*Glory, Tone 6. By John the Monk:*
Walking by the path of suffering, thou didst escape ancestral counsel, O all-venerable Barbara; and as a wise virgin bearing a lamp, thou didst enter into the courts of thy Lord; and as a valiant martyr, thou didst receive grace to heal fleshly passions. But deliver also from spiritual sicknesses us who sing of thee, through thy prayers unto God.[^758]

*And now, Theotokion:*
We have known God Who was incarnate of thee, O Virgin Theotokos: pray Him that our souls may be saved.

*At the Liturgy, Prokeimenon, Tone 4:* God is marvelous in His saints.[^759] *Verse:* In the congregations bless ye God, the Lord.[^760]
*Epistle to the Galatians, pericope 208.*[^761]
*Alleluia, Tone 1. Verse:* With patience I waited for the Lord.[^762]
*Gospel according to Matthew, pericope 104.*[^763]
*Communion Hymn:* Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous.[^764]

*Resurrectional Theotokia for the Eight Tones.*

*Tone 1. Theotokion:*
Let us hymn the Virgin Mary, the glory of the whole world, who sprang forth from mankind and bore the Master, the heavenly door, the song of the bodiless and the adornment of the faithful! For she appeared as heaven and temple of the Godhead; she, having broken down the barrier of enmity, brought in peace and opened the Kingdom. Having her, therefore, as the confirmation of faith, we have the Lord born of her as our Defender. Take courage, therefore, take courage, O people of God, for He will conquer the enemies, as He is all-powerful.[^765]

*At the Aposticha, Theotokion:*
Behold, Isaiah's prophecy is fulfilled: for thou, O Virgin, didst give birth, and after childbirth didst remain even as before childbirth, for God was He Who was born; therefore nature also was renewed.[^766] But O Mother of God, despise not the supplications of thy servants offered unto thee in thy temple; but as thou bearest the Merciful One in thy hands, have compassion on thy servants, and pray that our souls may be saved.[^767]

*Tone 2. Theotokion:*
The shadow of the law passed away when grace arrived; for even as the bush burned yet was not consumed, so as a virgin thou didst give birth, and a virgin thou didst remain. In place of the pillar of fire, the Sun of righteousness shone forth; in place of Moses, Christ, the salvation of our souls.[^768]

*At the Aposticha, Theotokion:*
O new wonder, surpassing all ancient wonders! For who ever knew a mother who gave birth without a man, and who carried in her arms Him Who upholds all creation? It is the divine will of Him Who was born. Whom as an Infant having borne in thy hands, O all-pure one, and possessing maternal boldness toward Him, cease not praying for those who honor thee, to have mercy and to save our souls.[^769]

*Tone 3. Theotokion:*
How can we not marvel at thy God-man childbirth, O all-pure one? For without receiving trial of man, O all-blameless one, thou didst bear without a father a Son in the flesh, Who before the ages was begotten of the Father without a mother, having undergone no change, nor confusion, nor division[^770] but preserved whole the properties of each nature. Therefore, O Lady Virgin Mother, pray Him to save the souls of those who in orthodox fashion confess thee to be the Mother of God.[^771]

*At the Aposticha, Theotokion:*
Without seed, of the divine Spirit, and by the Father's will, thou didst conceive the Son of God, Who before the ages was of the Father without a mother; and for our sake, having come from thee without a father, thou didst bear Him in the flesh and didst nourish the Infant with milk. Therefore cease not to pray, that our souls may be delivered from perils.[^772]

*Tone 4. Theotokion:*
David the ancestor of God, the prophet, through song proclaimed concerning thee unto Him Who hath done great things for thee: The Queen stood at Thy right hand.[^773] For God, Who was pleased without a father to become incarnate from thee, showed thee forth as Mother and Mediatress of life, that He might renew His own image, which was corrupted by passions; and having found the sheep that went astray in the mountains, taking it upon His shoulders, He might bring it unto the Father, and according to His own will might unite it with the heavenly powers, and save the world, O Theotokos, Christ Who hath great and rich mercy.

*At the Aposticha, Theotokion:*
Look down upon the entreaties of thy servants, O all-immaculate one, quenching the fierce uprisings against us, releasing us from every affliction. For thee alone have we as a firm and sure confirmation, and we have acquired thy protection, that we who call upon thee may not be put to shame, O Theotokos. Hasten to the supplication of those who cry faithfully unto thee: Rejoice, O Theotokos, help of all, joy and protection, and the salvation of our souls![^774]

*Tone 5. Theotokion:*
In the Red Sea, an image of the bride that knew not wedlock was inscribed of old. There Moses was the divider of the water; and here Gabriel was the minister of the wonder. Then Israel traversed the deep without being wetted; and now the Virgin gave birth unto Christ without seed. The sea after the passage of Israel remained impassable; the immaculate one after the childbirth of Emmanuel remained incorrupt. O God Who art and Who wast before, Who didst appear as man: have mercy on us![^775]

*At the Aposticha, Theotokion:*
Thou art temple and gate, palace and throne of the King, O all-honored Virgin, through whom my Deliverer, Christ the Lord, appeared unto those sleeping in darkness, being the Sun of righteousness, desiring to enlighten that which He fashioned according to His own image with His own hand. Therefore, O all-hymned one, as thou hast acquired maternal boldness toward Him, cease not[^776] cease not to pray that our souls may be saved.

*Tone 6. Theotokion:*
Who will not bless thee, O all-pure Virgin? Or who will not sing of thy childbirth free of defilement? For the only-begotten Son, Who shone forth timelessly from the Father, the Same came forth from thee, pure one, having been ineffably incarnate; being God by nature, and having become man by nature for our sake; not divided into two persons, but known in two natures without confusion. Him do thou beseech, O pure and all-blessed one, that our souls may find mercy.[^777]

*At the Aposticha, Theotokion:*
My Maker and Deliverer, O all-pure one, Christ the Lord, having come forth from thy womb, clothed in me, delivered Adam from the first curse. Therefore unto thee, O all-pure one, as the Mother of God and Virgin in truth, we cry unceasingly with the angelic salutation: Rejoice, O Lady; rejoice, O Theotokos: protection, shelter, and the salvation of our souls![^778]

*Tone 7. Theotokion:*
A Mother indeed wast thou known to be beyond nature, O Theotokos, and thou didst remain a virgin beyond word and understanding; and the wonder of thy childbirth no tongue is able to tell. For exceeding glorious was thy conception, O pure one; incomprehensible is the manner of thy childbirth; for where God wills, the order of nature is overcome. Therefore, knowing thee as the Mother of God, all of us pray thee earnestly: pray that our souls may be saved.[^779]

*At the Aposticha, Theotokion:*
Beneath thy shelter, O Theotokos, all we earthborn flee, crying unto thee: O our hope, deliver us from immeasurable transgressions, and save our souls.[^780]

*Tone 8. Theotokion:*
The King of heaven, for His love of mankind, appeared on earth and lived with men; for having taken flesh from the pure Virgin, and having come forth from her with that which He assumed, one Son is He, twofold in nature, but not in hypostasis. Therefore, truly proclaiming Him to be perfect God and perfect man, we confess Christ our God. Pray Him, O Mother unwedded, that our souls may find mercy.[^781]

*At the Aposticha, Theotokion:*
O unwedded Virgin, who didst ineffably conceive God in the flesh, Mother of God Most High: accept the supplications of thy servants, O all-immaculate one, granting unto all the cleansing of transgressions. Now receiving our entreaties, pray that we all may be saved.[^782]

*Theotokia of the Eight Tones, sung when there is "Glory..." to the Saint in the Menaion, and "Both now..." in the Tone of the Saint.*[^783]

*Tone 1.*

*On Sunday evening, Theotokion:*
The joy of the heavenly ranks, the firm protection for men upon earth, O all-pure Virgin: save us who flee unto thee, for upon thee after God have we placed our hope, O Theotokos.[^784]

*On Monday at Matins, Theotokion:*
Holier than all the holy powers, more honorable than all creation, O Lady Theotokos: having given birth to the Savior, save us from myriad transgressions and perils, as thou art good, through thy prayers.[^785]

*On Monday evening, Theotokion:*
O all-hymned Virgin, the mystery that was in thee Moses beheld with prophetic eyes: the bush burning and unconsumed; for the fire of the Godhead burned not thy womb, O pure one. Therefore we pray thee, as the Mother of our God, to ask peace for the world and great mercy.[^786]

*On Tuesday at Matins, Theotokion:*
The harlot, the prodigal, and the thief have I surpassed, and the publican, in my very many and countless transgressions. Woe is me! What shall become of me? How shall I escape torment, wretched that I am? Pure one, I fall down before thee: have compassion on me by thy mercy, even as thy Son saved them.[^787]

*On Wednesday evening, Theotokion:*
Rejoice, O joy of the forebears, delight of the apostles and martyrs, and shelter of us thy servants, O Virgin.[^788]

*On Thursday at Matins, Theotokion:*
Rejoice, O Virgin Theotokos; rejoice, praise of the whole universe; rejoice, O all-pure Mother of God, blessed one.[^789]

*On Friday evening, Theotokion:*
Truly marvelous beyond the mind are thy great wonders, O Bride of God, which all the prophets proclaimed, all exceeding glorious! Conception and childbirth, O all-hymned one, are past understanding and ineffable, whereby the world is saved, as He is merciful.[^790]

*On Saturday at Matins, Theotokion:*
Rejoice from us, O holy Virgin Theotokos, pure vessel of the whole universe, unquenchable lamp, container of the Uncontainable, unconquerable temple! Rejoice, thou from whom was born the Lamb of God, Who takes away the sins of the whole world.[^791]

*Tone 2.*

*On Sunday evening, Theotokion:*
Rejoice, O Mary Theotokos, indestructible temple, or rather holy one, as the prophet cries: Holy is Thy temple, marvelous in righteousness.[^792]

*On Monday at Matins, Theotokion:*
On thee have we placed our hope, O Theotokos: let us not fall away from our expectation; save us from perils, O helper of those in perplexity, and destroy the counsels of the adversaries: for thou art our salvation, O blessed one.[^793]

*On Monday evening, Theotokion:*
Impassable gate, mystically sealed, O blessed Virgin Theotokos: receive our entreaties, and offer them unto thy Son and God, that He may save our souls through thee.[^794]

*On Tuesday at Matins, Theotokion:*
Rejoice, O Mary Theotokos, indestructible temple, or rather holy one, as the prophet cries: Holy is Thy temple, marvelous in righteousness.[^795]

*On Wednesday evening, Theotokion:*
As a fruitful olive tree, O Virgin, didst thou bud forth the Fruit of life, to bring forth as fruit for the world great and rich mercy.[^796]

*On Thursday at Matins, Theotokion:*
All my hope I place upon thee, O Mother of God: preserve me beneath thy shelter.[^797]

*On Friday evening, Theotokion:*
Save thy servants from perils, O Virgin Theotokos, for after God we all flee unto thee, as unto an indestructible wall and protection.[^798]

*On Saturday at Matins, Theotokion:*
Come, let all of us glorify the Mother of the Light, calling upon her with unceasing hymns; for she gave birth unto our salvation. And let us bring unto her the salutation "Rejoice!", as unto her who alone gave birth to Him Who is before all things, God before the ages. Rejoice, thou who hast restored fallen Eve! Rejoice, O all-pure Virgin who knewest not wedlock![^799]

*Tone 3.*

*On Sunday evening, Theotokion:*
O Theotokos, protectress of all who pray unto thee: in thee do we take courage, and in thee do we boast, and upon thee is all our hope; pray Him Who was born of thee, on behalf of the unprofitable servants[^800] thy servants.[^800]

*On Monday at Matins, Theotokion:*
Thou hast stood forth, O all-pure one, being the boast of the heavenly ranks, the song of the apostles, and the fulfillment of the prophets: O Theotokos, receive our prayers.[^801]

*On Monday evening, Theotokion:*
O holy unwedded Mother and Theotokos among women: pray Him Whom thou didst bear, the King and God, that He may save us, as He loves mankind.[^802]

*On Tuesday at Matins, Theotokion:*
Without seed thou didst conceive of the Holy Spirit, and giving glory, we sing of thee: Rejoice, O all-holy Virgin![^803]

*On Wednesday evening, Theotokion:*
O Maiden, snatch me who have sinned greatly from the fierce flame by thy great mercy; and guide me, O pure one, by thy supplications, directing me unto saving paths by thy maternal prayers.[^804]

*On Thursday at Matins, Theotokion:*
Without seed thou didst conceive of the Holy Spirit, and giving glory, we sing of thee: Rejoice, O all-holy Virgin![^805]

*On Friday evening, Theotokion:*
O holy unwedded Mother and Theotokos among women: pray Him Whom thou didst bear, the King and God, that He may save us, as He loves mankind.[^806]

*On Saturday at Matins, Theotokion:*
Without seed thou didst conceive of the Holy Spirit, and giving glory, we sing of thee: Rejoice, O all-holy Virgin![^807]

*Tone 4.*

*On Sunday evening, Theotokion:*
Rejoice, cloud of light! Rejoice, radiant lampstand! Rejoice, jar wherein is the manna! Rejoice, rod of Aaron! Rejoice, bush unconsumed! Rejoice, bridal chamber! Rejoice, throne! Rejoice, holy mountain! Rejoice, refuge! Rejoice, divine table! Rejoice, mystical door! Rejoice, joy of all![^808]

*On Monday at Matins, Theotokion:*
O Theotokos, Queen of all, boast of the orthodox: destroy the insolence of heretics, and put to shame the faces of those who neither bow down before nor honor thine honorable icon, O all-pure one.[^809]

*On Monday evening, Theotokion:*
Deliver us from our necessities, O Mother of Christ God, who didst bear the Creator of all, that[^810] that we all may cry unto thee: Rejoice, the only protection of our souls![^810]

*On Tuesday at Matins, Theotokion:*
Preserve thy servants from all perils, O blessed Theotokos, that we may glorify thee, the hope of our souls.[^811]

*On Wednesday evening, Theotokion:*
Having thee, O Theotokos, as our hope and protection, we shall not fear the assaults of the enemy, for thou savest our souls.[^812]

*On Thursday at Matins, Theotokion:*
We have acquired thee as a wall, O all-pure Theotokos, and a calm haven and confirmation. Therefore I pray, tempest-tossed in this life: guide and save me![^813]

*On Friday evening, Theotokion:*
Unquenchable lamp, righteous throne, O all-pure Lady: pray that our souls may be saved.[^814]

*On Saturday at Matins, Theotokion:*
O only pure and all-immaculate Virgin, who didst bear God without seed: pray that our souls may be saved.[^815]

*Tone 5.*

*On Sunday evening, Theotokion:*
Dread, marvelous, and great is the mystery: the Incomprehensible was contained in a womb; and the Mother after childbirth remained again a virgin: for she bore God incarnate of her. Unto Him let us cry, unto Him let us say a hymn, singing with the angels: Holy art Thou, O Christ God, Who wast made man for our sake, glory to Thee![^816]

*On Monday at Matins, Theotokion:*
O thou who art full of grace, intercede by thy prayers, and ask for our souls a multitude of compassions and the cleansing of many transgressions, we pray thee.[^817]

*On Monday evening, Theotokion:*
Assuage the sicknesses of my much-sighing soul, O thou who didst wipe away every tear from the face of the earth; for thou drivest away the diseases of men and dost dissolve the sorrows of sinners: for thee have all of us acquired as our hope and confirmation, O all-holy Virgin Mother.[^818]

*On Tuesday at Matins, Theotokion:*
O thou who art full of grace, intercede by thy prayers, and ask for our souls a multitude of compassions and the cleansing of many transgressions, we pray thee.[^819]

*On Wednesday evening, Theotokion:*
We bless thee, O Virgin Theotokos, and we the faithful praise thee as is due: unshakable city, invincible wall, firm protectress, and refuge of our souls.[^820]

*On Thursday at Matins, Theotokion:*
We bless thee, O Virgin Theotokos, for from thee hath shone forth the Sun of righteousness, Christ, Who hath great mercy.[^821]

*On Friday evening, Theotokion:*
Thee we entreat as the Mother of God, O blessed one: pray for the salvation of our souls.[^822]

*On Saturday at Matins, Theotokion:*
O wretched soul of mine, what answer wilt thou give to the Judge at that hour, when the thrones are set for judgment, and the Judge comes from the heavens accompanied by myriad angels? When He sits upon the judgment seat to enter into controversy with unprofitable servants like unto me, what wilt thou answer? And what wilt thou bring forward then? Truly nothing, having defiled thy mind and body. Therefore fall down before the Virgin, and cry unceasingly, that He may richly grant thee forgiveness of sins.[^823]

*Tone 6.*

*On Sunday evening, Theotokion:*
Archangelically let us, the faithful, hymn the fiery bridal chamber and truly sealed gate: Rejoice, for whose sake Christ, the Giver of life and God, the Savior of all, sprang up for us! Cast down the tyrants, our godless enemies, O Theotokos, by thy hand, O all-pure one, the hope of Christians![^824]

*On Monday at Matins, Theotokion:*
Thou didst receive the Archangel's word, and appeared as the cherubic throne, and in thine arms didst carry the hope of our souls, O Theotokos.[^825]

*On Monday evening, Theotokion:*
None who runs unto thee, O all-pure Virgin Theotokos, departs from thee put to shame; but he asks for grace, and receives a gift according to his profitable request.[^826]

*On Tuesday at Matins, Theotokion:*
Of great gifts, O pure Virgin Mother of God, wast thou accounted worthy, for in the flesh thou didst bear One of the Trinity, Christ the Giver of life, unto the salvation of our souls.[^827]

*On Wednesday evening, Theotokion:*
The eye of my heart I direct unto thee, O Theotokos: despise not my small sighing in the hour when thy Son judges the world: be unto me shelter and helper.[^828]

*On Thursday at Matins, Theotokion:*
Transformation of the sorrowful, relief of the sick art thou, O all-hymned Theotokos: save the city and the people, O pacification of the embattled, stillness of the tempest-tossed, only protectress of the faithful.[^829]

*On Friday evening, Theotokion:*
Through the prayers of her who bore Thee, O Christ, of Thy martyrs, and apostles, and prophets, and hierarchs, of the venerable, and righteous, and all the saints: give rest to Thy departed servants.[^830]

*On Saturday at Matins, Theotokion:*
We have known God Who was incarnate of thee, O Virgin Theotokos: pray Him for the salvation of our souls.[^831]

*Tone 7.*

*On Sunday evening, Theotokion:*
The greeting "Rejoice!" we cry unto thee with the angel, O Bride of God, calling thee bridal chamber and door, and fiery throne, and unhewn mountain, and bush unconsumed.[^832]

*On Monday at Matins, Theotokion:*
Pacify our life through the prayers of the Theotokos, as we cry unto Thee: O Merciful Lord, glory to Thee![^833]

*On Monday evening, Theotokion:*
Rejoice, cloud of the noetic and ineffable Sun, O Lady; rejoice, all-radiant lamp; rejoice, lampstand all of gold: through thee, O all-pure one, Eve was delivered from the curse. But as thou hast boldness toward thy Son and God Who is easily reconciled, fail not to pray with thy maternal prayer, O all-pure one.[^834]

*On Tuesday at Matins, Theotokion:*
Thou hast caused Light to spring forth from the Virgin, O Christ, and hast enlightened the human race: O Lord, glory to Thee![^835]

*On Wednesday evening, Theotokion:*

*On Thursday at Matins, Theotokion:*
Thou wast born of the Virgin ineffably, O Christ, and hast enlightened those who were in darkness, as they cry: O Lord, glory to Thee![^837]

*On Friday evening, Theotokion:*
O thou who alone didst receive the Incomprehensible, and didst bear God the Word[^838] the Word incarnate: pray that our souls may be saved.[^838]

*On Saturday at Matins, Theotokion:*
Pray, O Virgin, with the apostles and martyrs, that those who have reposed may find great mercy at the Judgment.[^839]

*Tone 8.*

*On Sunday evening, Theotokion:*
Having received the voice of the Archangel Gabriel, let us say: Rejoice, Mother of God, who didst bear Christ the Giver of life unto the world![^840]

*On Monday at Matins, Theotokion:*
Heaven sings of thee, O mother unwedded, full of grace, and we glorify thine unsearchable childbirth, O Theotokos: pray that our souls may be saved.[^841]

*On Monday evening, Theotokion:*
Rejoice, praise of the universe! Rejoice, temple of the Lord! Rejoice, overshadowing mountain! Rejoice, refuge of all! Rejoice, golden lampstand! Rejoice, honorable glory of the orthodox! Rejoice, Mary, Mother of Christ God! Rejoice, paradise! Rejoice, divine table! Rejoice, tabernacle! Rejoice, vessel all of gold! Rejoice, hope of all![^842]

*On Tuesday at Matins, Theotokion:*
Thy shelter, O Virgin Theotokos, is spiritual medicine: for fleeing unto it, we are delivered from spiritual infirmities.[^843]

*On Wednesday evening, Theotokion:*
I, O holy Virgin Theotokos, flee unto thy shelter: I know that through thee I shall find salvation, for thou, O pure one, art able to help me.[^844]

*On Thursday at Matins, Theotokion:*
Snatch me, O Lady, from the hand of the man-slaying serpent who desires through cunning to swallow me up utterly: crush his jaws, I pray thee, and destroy his snares, so that having escaped from his claws, I may magnify thy protection.[^845]

*On Friday evening, Theotokion:*
O pure Virgin, gate of the Word, Mother of our God: pray that we may be saved.[^846]

*On Saturday at Matins, Theotokion:*

*Resurrectional Dismissal Theotokia of the Eight Tones.*[^848]

*Tone 1. Theotokion:*
When Gabriel said unto thee: Rejoice, O Virgin! with the voice the Master of all became incarnate in thee, the holy ark, as the righteous David said.[^849] Thou wast shown forth more spacious than the heavens, having borne thy Creator. Glory to Him Who dwelt in thee! Glory to Him Who came forth from thee! Glory to Him Who delivered us by thy childbirth!

*Tone 2. Theotokion:*
All thy mysteries are beyond comprehension, all thy mysteries are exceeding glorious, O Theotokos: sealed in purity and preserved in virginity, thou wast known to be a true Mother, having given birth unto the true God.[^850] Pray Him that our souls may be saved.

*Tone 3. Theotokion:*
Thee who didst mediate the salvation of our race we hymn, O Virgin Theotokos; for having accepted the Passion on the Cross in the flesh assumed of thee, thy Son and our God delivered us from corruption, as He loves mankind.[^851]

*Tone 4. Theotokion:*
The mystery hidden from the ages and unknown unto the angels was made manifest through thee, O Theotokos, unto those on earth: God incarnate in unconfused union, Who having willingly accepted the Cross for our sake, thereby resurrected the first-fashioned and saved our souls from death.[^852]

*Tone 5. Theotokion:*
Rejoice, impassable gate of the Lord! Rejoice, wall and protection of those who run unto thee! Rejoice, haven untroubled by storms, and unwedded bride who didst give birth in the flesh to thy Maker and God: fail not to pray for those who hymn and worship thy childbirth![^853]

*Tone 6. Theotokion:*
Having called Thy Mother blessed, Thou camest to the Passion by voluntary counsel, shining forth upon the Cross, desiring to seek out Adam, saying unto the angels: Rejoice with Me, for the lost coin is found![^854] O our God, Who hast wisely ordered all things, glory to Thee!

*Tone 7. Theotokion:*
As the treasury of our resurrection, O all-hymned one, lead up from the pit and depth of transgressions those who put their trust in thee[^855] for thou didst save those guilty of sin, having given birth unto our salvation: who before childbirth wast a virgin, and in childbirth a virgin, and after childbirth still remainest a virgin.[^856]

*Tone 8. Theotokion:*
O Thou Who for our sake wast born of a Virgin, and didst endure crucifixion, O Good One, Who by death didst overthrow death, and as God didst reveal the Resurrection: despise not those whom Thou hast fashioned with Thy hand; manifest Thy love for mankind, O Merciful One; accept the Theotokos who bore Thee, interceding for us, and save, O our Savior, a despairing people.[^857]

*Dismissal Theotokia,*[^858]
*sung after the troparia of the saints throughout the entire year, at Vespers, and at "God is the Lord" at Matins, and again at the end of Matins.*

*Tone 1.*
*On Sunday evening, and on Monday at "God is the Lord":*
Beholding in thee the miracle of miracles, O full of grace, creation rejoices; for thou didst conceive without seed, and didst bear ineffably Him Whom the ranks of the angels cannot behold: pray Him for our souls.[^859]

*At the end of Matins:*
O most pure Theotokos, blessed in the heavens and glorified on earth: rejoice, O Bride unwedded![^860]

*On Monday evening, and on Tuesday at "God is the Lord":*
Thou who didst unburnt conceive the divine Fire, and without seed didst give birth unto the Fountain of life, the Lord, O grace-filled Theotokos: save those who magnify thee.[^861]

*At the end of Matins:*
Him Who in heaven is without mother beyond understanding and hearing, thou didst bear on earth without father: pray Him, O Theotokos, for our souls.[^862]

*On Tuesday evening, and on Wednesday at "God is the Lord":*
Having thy protection, O most pure one, and being delivered from tribulations by thy prayers, preserved everywhere by the Cross of thy Son, we all dutifully and piously magnify thee.[^863]

*At the end of Matins:*
*O most pure Theotokos, blessed in the heavens...*

*On Wednesday evening, and on Thursday at "God is the Lord":*
*Thou who didst unburnt conceive the divine Fire...*

*At the end of Matins:*
*Him Who in heaven is without mother Him Who in heaven is without mother...*

*On Thursday evening, and on Friday at "God is the Lord":*
*Having thy protection...*

*At the end of Matins:*
*O most pure Theotokos...*

*On Friday evening, and on Saturday at "God is the Lord":*
When Gabriel said unto thee: Rejoice, O Virgin! with the voice the Master of all became incarnate in thee, the holy ark, as the righteous David said.[^864] Thou wast shown forth more spacious than the heavens, having borne thy Creator. Glory to Him Who dwelt in thee! Glory to Him Who came forth from thee! Glory to Him Who delivered us by thy childbirth!

*At the end of Matins:*
*Him Who in heaven is without mother...*

*Tone 2. On Sunday evening, and on Monday at "God is the Lord":*
Being a fountain of tender compassion, vouchsafe mercy unto us, O Theotokos: look down upon a people that has sinned; show forth as always thy power, for putting our trust in thee, we cry aloud unto thee: Rejoice! as once did Gabriel, the supreme commander of the bodiless hosts.[^865]

*At the end of Matins:*
O holy Mother of the ineffable Light, honoring thee with angelic hymns, we piously magnify thee.[^866]

*On Monday evening, and on Tuesday at "God is the Lord":*
Partakers of the divine nature have we become through thee, O Theotokos, Ever-Virgin: for thou didst bear unto us God incarnate. Therefore we all dutifully and piously magnify thee.[^867]

*At the end of Matins:*
We magnify thee, O Theotokos, crying aloud: Rejoice, cloud of the unwaning Light, who didst bear in thy bosom the Lord of glory![^868]

*On Tuesday evening, and on Wednesday at "God is the Lord":*
Exceeding glorious art thou, O Virgin Theotokos, we hymn thee: for by the Cross of thy Son Hades was cast down, and death was put to death; we who were slain are arisen, and have been counted worthy of life, and have received Paradise, the ancient enjoyment. Therefore giving thanks, we glorify Christ our God as mighty and alone plenteous in mercy.[^869]

*At the end of Matins:*
We magnify thee, O Theotokos, crying aloud: Rejoice, O rod from which without seed God budded forth, destroying death upon the Tree![^870]

*On Wednesday evening, and on Thursday at "God is the Lord":*
*Partakers of the divine nature have we become...*

*At the end of Matins:*
*We magnify thee, O Theotokos, crying aloud We magnify thee, O Theotokos, crying aloud...*

*On Thursday evening, and on Friday at "God is the Lord":*
*Exceeding glorious art thou, O Virgin Theotokos...*

*At the end of Matins:*
*We magnify thee, O Theotokos, crying aloud: Rejoice, O rod...*

*On Friday evening, and on Saturday at "God is the Lord":*
All thy mysteries are beyond comprehension, all thy mysteries are exceeding glorious, O Theotokos: sealed in purity and preserved in virginity, thou wast known to be a true Mother, having given birth unto the true God.[^871] Pray Him that our souls may be saved.

*At the end of Matins:*
*O holy Mother of the ineffable Light...*

*If Alleluia occurs in any Tone, these are said:*
*Troparion:*
Apostles, martyrs, and prophets, hierarchs, venerable ones, and righteous, who have well finished the course and kept the faith, having boldness before the Savior: pray Him as good on our behalf, that our souls, we pray, may be saved.[^872]

*Troparion:*
Remember, O Lord, as Thou art good, the souls of Thy servants, and forgive whatever they have sinned in life; for no one is sinless save Thee Who art able to grant rest also unto the departed.[^873]

*Theotokion:*
*O holy Mother of the ineffable Light...*

*Tone 3. On Sunday evening, and on Monday at "God is the Lord":*
Marveling at the beauty of thy virginity and the surpassing radiance of thy purity, Gabriel cried out unto thee, O Theotokos: What worthy praise shall I offer thee? And by what name shall I call thee? I am in perplexity and wonder. Therefore, as I was commanded, I cry unto thee: Rejoice, O full of grace![^874]

*At the end of Matins:*
Each one rightfully flees unto where he is being saved; and what other such refuge is there as thou, O Theotokos, sheltering our souls?[^875]

*On Monday evening, and on Tuesday at "God is the Lord":*
Our refuge and strength, O Theotokos, mighty help of the world, by thy prayers shelter thy servants from every necessity, O only-blessed one.[^876]

*At the end of Matins:*
*Each one rightfully flees unto where he is being saved...*

*On Tuesday evening, and on Wednesday at "God is the Lord":*
Having acquired the Cross of thy Son as a rod of strength, O Theotokos, thereby we cast down the insolence of the enemy, ceaselessly magnifying thee with love.[^877]

*At the end of Matins:*
*Our refuge and strength, O Theotokos Our refuge and strength, O Theotokos...*

*On Wednesday evening, and on Thursday at "God is the Lord":*
The prophets proclaimed, the apostles taught, the martyrs confessed, and we have believed that thou art truly the Theotokos; therefore do we also magnify thine ineffable childbirth.[^878]

*At the end of Matins:*
*Each one rightfully flees unto where he is being saved...*

*On Thursday evening, and on Friday at "God is the Lord":*
*Having acquired the Cross of thy Son as a rod of strength...*

*Our refuge and strength, O Theotokos...*

*On Friday evening, and on Saturday at "God is the Lord":*
Thee who didst mediate the salvation of our race we hymn, O Virgin Theotokos; for having accepted the Passion on the Cross in the flesh assumed of thee, thy Son and our God delivered us from corruption, as He loves mankind.[^879]

*At the end of Matins:*
*The prophets proclaimed, the apostles taught...*

*Tone 4. On Sunday evening, and on Monday at "God is the Lord":*
Unto thee who wast reared in the temple in the Holy of Holies, clothed with faith and wisdom and boundless virginity, the supreme commander Gabriel brought from heaven the salutation and the "Rejoice": Rejoice, O blessed one! Rejoice, O exceeding glorious one: the Lord is with thee![^880]

*At the end of Matins:*
As thou art higher than all creation, being in perplexity how to hymn thee worthily, O Theotokos, therefore we pray thee: have mercy on us.[^881]

*On Monday evening, and on Tuesday at "God is the Lord":*
Unto the Theotokos let us sinners and humble ones now earnestly run, and let us fall down in repentance, crying from the depth of the soul: O Sovereign Lady, help us, having tender compassion upon us; make haste, for we perish from the multitude of our transgressions; turn not thy servants away empty, for thee alone do we have as hope.[^882]

*At the end of Matins:*
We magnify thee, O Theotokos, crying aloud: Thou art the bush wherein Moses unburnt beheld as a flame the Fire of the Godhead.[^883]

*On Tuesday evening, and on Wednesday at "God is the Lord":*
O all-immaculate Virgin, Mother of Christ God, a sword pierced through thy most holy soul when thou didst behold thy Son and God voluntarily crucified: cease not, O blessed one, interceding with Him to grant us forgiveness of transgressions.[^884]

*At the end of Matins:*

*At the end of Matins:*
We magnify thee, O Theotokos, crying aloud: Thou art the mountain from which ineffably a stone was cut without hands, and crushed the gates of Hades.[^885]

*On Wednesday evening, and on Thursday at "God is the Lord":*
Christ our God, the Word of the Father, incarnate of thee have we known, O Virgin Theotokos, only pure one, only blessed one: therefore ceaselessly hymning thee, we magnify thee.[^886]

*At the end of Matins:*
*As thou art higher than all creation...*

*On Thursday evening, and on Friday at "God is the Lord":*
*O all-immaculate Virgin, Mother of Christ God...*

*At the end of Matins:*
*We magnify thee, O Theotokos, crying aloud: Thou art the mountain...*

*On Friday evening, and on Saturday at "God is the Lord":*
The mystery hidden from the ages and unknown unto the angels was made manifest through thee, O Theotokos, unto those on earth: God incarnate in unconfused union, Who having willingly accepted the Cross for our sake, thereby resurrected the first-fashioned and saved our souls from death.[^887]

*At the end of Matins:*
*We magnify thee, O Theotokos, crying aloud: Thou art the bush...*

*Tone 5. On Sunday evening, and on Monday at "God is the Lord":*
Invisible with the angels, earthly with men, with the voice of rejoicing we cry unto thee, O Theotokos: Rejoice, gate more spacious than the heavens! Rejoice, only salvation of the earthborn! Rejoice, pure and full of grace, who didst give birth unto God incarnate![^888]

*At the end of Matins:*
O Christ God, Who didst shine forth the Lights unto the world, Who through her didst reveal sons of the light: have mercy on us![^889]

*On Monday evening, and on Tuesday at "God is the Lord":*
Show forth thy speedy protection and help and mercy upon thy servants; and calm, O pure one, the waves of vain thoughts, and raise up my fallen soul, O Theotokos: for I know, yea, I know, O Virgin, that thou art able to do whatever thou dost will.[^890]

*At the end of Matins:*
O most pure Mother of God, rampart of Christians, deliver thy people as is thy wont, who earnestly cry unto thee: resist shameful and proud thoughts, that we may cry unto thee: Rejoice, Ever-Virgin![^891]

*On Tuesday evening, and on Wednesday at "God is the Lord":*

*On Tuesday evening, and on Wednesday at "God is the Lord":*
By the Cross of thy Son, O Theotokos divinely endowed with grace, all the deceit of idols has been abolished, and the power of demons has been trampled down; therefore we the faithful dutifully and ever hymn and bless thee, and truly confessing thee to be the Theotokos, we magnify thee.[^892]

*At the end of Matins:*
*O Christ God, Who didst shine forth the Lights unto the world...*

*On Wednesday evening, and on Thursday at "God is the Lord":*
The marvelous mystery of the Virgin was shown forth unto the world as saving: for of her Thou wast born without seed, and in the flesh Thou wast revealed without corruption, O Joy of all! O Lord, glory to Thee![^893]

*At the end of Matins:*
*O most pure Mother of God, rampart of Christians...*

*On Thursday evening, and on Friday at "God is the Lord":*
*By the Cross of thy Son, O Theotokos divinely endowed with grace...*

*At the end of Matins:*
*O Christ God, Who didst shine forth the Lights unto the world...*

*On Friday evening, and on Saturday at "God is the Lord":*
Rejoice, impassable gate of the Lord! Rejoice, wall and protection of those who run unto thee! Rejoice, haven untroubled by storms, and unwedded bride who didst give birth in the flesh to thy Maker and God: fail not to pray for those who hymn and worship thy childbirth![^894]

*At the end of Matins:*
*O Christ God, Who didst shine forth the Lights unto the world...*

*Tone 6. On Sunday evening, and on Monday at "God is the Lord":*
The beginning of salvation was Gabriel's greeting unto the Virgin; for she heard the "Rejoice", and was not afraid of the salutation; she doubted not like Sarah in the tent, but thus spoke: Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word.[^895]

*At the end of Matins:*
Thou didst receive the archangelic word, and wast shown forth as the cherubic throne, and in thine arms thou didst carry, O Theotokos, the Hope of our souls.[^896]

*On Monday evening, and on Tuesday at "God is the Lord":*
O good Virgin Theotokos, Hope of the world: we ask thy sole and sovereign protection; have tender compassion upon a people that has no helper; pray the merciful God that our souls may be delivered from every threatening, O only-blessed one.[^897]

*At the end of Matins:*
No one who flees unto thee departs from thee ashamed, O most pure Virgin Theotokos; but he asks for grace, and receives the gift the gift unto a profitable petition.[^898]

*On Tuesday evening, and on Wednesday at "God is the Lord":*
O Virgin Theotokos, pray thy Son, Who was willingly nailed upon the Cross, and delivered the world from deceit, Christ our God, to have mercy on our souls.[^899]

*At the end of Matins:*
Him Who before the ages was begotten of the Father without mother, the Son and Word of God, in these last times thou didst bear, incarnate of thy pure blood without man, O Mother of God: pray Him that forgiveness of sins may be granted us before the end.[^900]

*On Wednesday evening, and on Thursday at "God is the Lord":*
O holy, pure Sovereign Lady, Mother of our God, who didst ineffably bear the Creator of all: together with the holy apostles ever pray His goodness, to deliver us from passions, and to grant us remission of sins.[^901]

*At the end of Matins:*
Of great gifts hast thou been accounted worthy, O pure Virgin Mother of God: for in the flesh thou didst bear One of the Trinity, Christ the Giver of life, unto the salvation of our souls.[^902]

*On Thursday evening, and on Friday at "God is the Lord":*
*O Virgin Theotokos, pray thy Son...*

*At the end of Matins:*
*Him Who before the ages was begotten of the Father without mother...*

*On Friday evening, and on Saturday at "God is the Lord":*
Gideon foretold the conception, and David tells of thy childbirth, O Theotokos: for like dew upon the fleece, the Word descended into thy womb; and thou, O holy earth, without seed didst bud forth the salvation of the world, Christ our God, O full of grace![^903]

*At the end of Matins:*
*Him Who before the ages was begotten of the Father without mother...*

*Tone 7. On Sunday evening, and on Monday at "God is the Lord":*
O Virgin Theotokos [immaculate], pray thy Son together with the hosts on high, that forgiveness of transgressions may be granted us before the end, who faithfully glorify thee.[^904]

*At the end of Matins:*
Thou hast surpassed the heavenly hosts, for thou wast shown forth as the divine temple, O blessed Theotokos, having given birth unto Christ, the Savior of our souls.[^905]

*On Monday evening, and on Tuesday at "God is the Lord":*
The "Rejoice" we bring unto thee, O Theotokos for thou hast been shown forth higher than the angels, having given birth unto God.[^906]

*At the end of Matins:*
[Bring peace] by the prayers of the Theotokos unto our life, as we cry: O Merciful Lord, glory to Thee![^907]

Ceaselessly pray [O Virgin Theotokos], Christ our God Who was crucified for us and destroyed the power of death, that He may save [our] souls.[^908]

*Christ our God Who was crucified for us...*

*At the end of Matins:*
*Deliver us, O Theotokos...*

*On Friday evening, and on Saturday at "God is the Lord":*
As the treasury of our resurrection, O all-hymned one, lead up from the pit and depth of transgressions those who put their trust in thee; for thou didst save those guilty of sin, having given birth unto our salvation: who before childbirth wast a virgin, and in childbirth a virgin, and after childbirth still remainest a virgin.[^912]

*At the end of Matins:*
Rejoice, thou who didst contain in thy womb Him Whom the heavens cannot contain! Rejoice, O Virgin, proclamation of the prophets, through whom Emmanuel shone forth! Rejoice, Mother of Christ God![^913]

*Tone 8. On Sunday evening, and on Monday at "God is the Lord":*
Rejoice, thou who from the angels didst receive the joy of the world! Rejoice, thou who didst bear thy Creator and Lord! Rejoice, thou who wast accounted worthy to be the Mother of God![^914]

*At the end of Matins:*
Rejoice, gate of the King of glory, which the Most High alone passed through, and preserved sealed alone, unto the salvation of our souls.[^915]

*On Monday evening, and on Tuesday at "God is the Lord":*

*On Monday evening, and on Tuesday at "God is the Lord":*
The immovable confirmation of the faith, and precious gift of our souls, we the faithful magnify the Theotokos in hymns: Rejoice, thou who didst contain the Rock of life in thy womb! Rejoice, hope of the ends of the earth, protection of the afflicted! Rejoice, O Bride unwedded![^916]

*At the end of Matins:*
O most pure Virgin, save us by thy prayers, moving the maternal heart of thy Son and our God.[^917]

*On Tuesday evening, and on Wednesday at "God is the Lord":*
Beholding Thee, the Lamb and Shepherd and Savior of the world, upon the Cross, she who bore Thee said weeping: The world indeed rejoices, receiving redemption; but my heart burns within me, beholding Thy crucifixion, which Thou dost endure for all, O my Son and my God![^918]

*At the end of Matins:*
The Fruit of thy womb, O most pure one, is the fulfillment of the prophets and the Law: therefore glorifying thee, O Theotokos, with understanding, we piously magnify thee.[^919]

*On Wednesday evening, and on Thursday at "God is the Lord":*
O noetic gate of life, most pure Theotokos, faithfully deliver from tribulations those who run unto thee, that we may glorify thy most holy childbirth unto the salvation of our souls.[^920]
